session duplication is after successful child completion. Single recvmsg attempts hand EINTR back

## 2026-10-14 — Clipboard descriptor-transfer ownership

Previous goal turn is progress: 35f380ff removed twelve unsupported mount-setup wording checks,
preserved both executable byte-validator tests and two focused forbidden-operation scans, and
corrected the claimed evidence layer. User's pivot stays binding: audio, display-command launching,

Concrete next path at 35f380ff: fuse/mod.rs392-452 receives one SCM_RIGHTS buffer using flags0,
returns immediately on MSG_CTRUNC, accepts cmsg_len >= one-fd length, and owns only the first fd.
CMSG_SPACE padding can hold two descriptors on Linux x86_64. Kernel receipt installs the delivered
prefix before reporting truncation; only excess descriptors are automatically closed. Thus two
rights can be accepted with an unowned extra descriptor, and three-or-more rights can leave installed
handles after refusal. Separate post-receive F_SETFD and dup/F_SETFD expose inheritance windows.
This is a source-proven lifetime path; a deployed FUSE failure or exploit has not been demonstrated.

Authority model: the fixed validated helper remains the designated sender. The receiver owns every
kernel-installed descriptor before validating exact cardinality and truncation; success transfers
exactly one owned close-on-exec handle, and refusal releases every delivered handle. Receipt uses
MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC and retained-copy creation uses F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, with no nonatomic fallback.
Move only these operations into a private io::Result native module and keep caller error reporting.
The nine common tests perform real sendmsg/recvmsg, object roundtrips, exact peer EOF after refusal,
native flag observations, invalid duplication and an actual exec child with a positive inherited-
object control. The pinned former production functions run unchanged with only error construction
adapted to io::Error; one positive and three distinguishing negative cases share the exact tests.
The focused lane uses existing zero-NIC RAM admission and guest-only nonroot/capless/network-none
Docker, Rust1.75 and root-locked libc0.2.171. No host payload, Docker, FUSE device, service or foreign
memory user is touched. Edit lock45983 proves both marker sets idle while source is prepared.

## 2026-10-13 — Debian runner entry authority

Previous goal turn is progress: pushed97b2d70b, two concrete final-package ELF-role
defects corrected and actual archive/native-library comparison accepted. This turn

Source proof at97b: verify-debian-package-authority.py:544 parses `_entry` and
does not consult it; line597 discards each LOAD's permissions after checking W+X.
Thus a runner with no entry, a data-segment entry, or unmapped entry can pass its
production ELF identity predicate. Intended model: both closed runner paths must
have a nonzero entry within exactly one file-backed executable LOAD; shared
libraries remain permitted to have no entry. No fallback, alternate parser or
dependency is needed: keep LOAD permissions in the existing parsed record.
Research: ELF GABI e_entry defines process-start virtual address and zero means

configured connected kernel endpoint remains the exact owned endpoint. Every send
attempt returns its actual kernel outcome; queue backpressure never converts the
endpoint into absence, and a replacement bound at the same name is not adopted.
There is no reconnect, fallback or blocking wait. Existing aggregate shutdown
errors remain retained. Primary Linux send(2),
https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/send.2.html, defines nonblocking EAGAIN and
atomic datagram sends. Systemd v252's authoritative service contract,
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v252/man/systemd.service.xml, requires
extension receipt before the stop deadline and continued receipt thereafter;
send success alone is not a manager acknowledgement. Full installed failure and
permanent channel loss against the 30-second manager kill backstop remain open.

The previous `cs.rs:657` read chose a random32-bit ID once, queued up to eight responses and reissued the same request/ID after CB_RESPONSE_FAIL. - Official MS-RDPECLIP request/response documents specify the echoed unsigned32-bit streamId, maximum range size and OK1/FAIL2 result. Processing failure is an unsatisfied-request result, with no retry instruction. Removing automatic retries is our explicit lifetime-design choice inferred from that result model, not a claim that Microsoft literally prohibits all client retries. Primary sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rdpeclip/cbc851d3-4e68-45f4-9292-26872a9209f2 ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rdpeclip/df87c178-ab02-471a-acde-bb921aa1af85 ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rdpeclip/d19de33e-4027-43de-b150-668ee21bced8 . Source finding: Connection::send_login_error used enqueue-only FramedStream::send; the stale-generation on_message result breaks the connection loop, and FramedStream::drop aborts its writer before the queued rejection necessarily reaches the sink. The keyed drain has separate two-second enqueue and acknowledgment timeouts and poisons/retires the writer on failure; no credential lock spans it, and denied authorization remains denied. This reuses the existing close-reason boundary rather than changing normal traffic enqueue, crypto, policy or credential ownership. Native diagnostics now record the serving-identity/durable observations before semantic rejection; the required exact typed rejection and all earlier cases remain strict. Primary references: https://docs.rs/futures-util/0.3.31/futures_util/sink/trait.SinkExt.html#method.send (sink send completes including flush), https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/sync/mpsc/struct.Sender.html#method.send (channel enqueue success does not establish delivery). The queue/drop defect is inferred from repository source and the retained native failure; a fresh source-bound build and the unchanged installed race suite are still REQUIRED. - Relevant path: libs/hbb_common/src/fs.rs::TransferJob::write at pre-edit3522–3619 validates receive role/job/index, but3554 finalizes the previous file and3555 advances the file index;3571 opens the next destination claim. Only3587 then decodes compressed input and3596–3613 checks declared size and aggregate counters. finish_current_write_file3387–3445 flushes/synchronizes the current stream and publishes its exact claim; subsequent receive-error retirement cannot delete an already-visible final file. A malformed/truncated or excessive next-file block can therefore make an irreversible preceding-file publication before returning refusal. Initial malformed/excessive input can likewise create sidecars before rejection. This is receive-admission/finality correctness, not a demonstrated unauthenticated or ordinary-local privilege escalation.

- Intended model: the receive job remains the sole owner of its exact current stream, sidecars and destination lease. Role/job/index admission, bounded decoding, target-file offset/size checks and representable accounting must all succeed without mutating that ownership. Only admitted payload may finish the current file, advance the index, acquire the next claim and write bytes; counters publish after the write. A new-file offset is zero, while same-file/resume input uses the retained offset. This local ordering correction preserves the public API and the existing fallible filesystem/cleanup authority; no alternate mode, detached work, raw-decode fallback or generic transaction abstraction is needed. Filesystem failures after valid admission are still fallible and may have admitted effects; no multi-file atomicity claim is made. Rust rename's documented effect is https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/fn.rename.html; R-S11fi remains the governing exact cleanup/finality requirement.

## Objective

Audit beyond the completed R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC work for real and conceptual local privilege escalation paths across all desktop platforms and adjacent helper/service surfaces. Treat local IPC, helper IPC, service control, privileged packaging, filesystem writes, process spawning, registry/plist/systemd/polkit/Authorization Services actions, and privileged runtime cleanup/discovery as security boundaries.

## Ground Rules

- Evidence comes from current source and repo verification, not prior memory.
- Record every inspected surface with scope, code evidence, authority model, risk assessment, and follow-up.
- A finding is `OPEN` only when there is a concrete or defensible conceptual privilege path not already closed by source/gates.
- A surface is `CLOSED/NO FINDING` only when the relevant old path is absent or receiver-authorized and a gate prevents reintroduction.
- If a fix is needed, implement in-repo, verify with repo scripts, commit, and push.
- Build/compile claims must use the repo script layer:
  - `scripts/verify.sh` for the day-to-day source/compile/hardening gate.
  - `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` when Apple/macOS/iOS source paths are touched.
  - `scripts/verify-release.sh` for all source verification gates before release.
  - `scripts/build-release.sh` for artifact build proof; it orchestrates the slow release builds.
- Raw `cargo` commands are diagnostic only and do not prove this project builds correctly.

- Current relevant path: `TransferJob::new_read_with_budget` records each file's enumerated size and aggregate bytes. At the starting `libs/hbb_common/src/fs.rs:3884`, `set_stream_offset` checked `entry.size` only for Receive; Send used the retained file's current metadata length, then sought and incremented finished/transferred counters. A source admitted at five bytes could grow to twelve and admit offset six, even though the job still declared five. Both `src/server/connection.rs:9253` direct SendConfirm and `src/ui_cm_interface.rs:3019` generation-keyed CM SendConfirmForRead call this production admission method and retire the exact job/send a typed error on refusal. - Authority/model: the admitted entry defines the byte range a filesystem job may confirm; subsequent growth of its source does not expand that contract. Both roles reject an offset beyond that size before resolving a pathname, opening, seeking, changing accounting or publishing confirmation. Send independently requires the exact retained/provisional opened object's current length to admit the offset before seek. The existing send/receive API and role ownership are appropriate; moved the existing seven-line Receive bound into the shared admission path and removed its role-local duplicate. No new mode, dependency, fallback, snapshot claim, runtime or production unwrap/expect was added. ## 2026-10-10 — Send-job admission owns the exact enumerated index range

- Resumed the attachment/Ralph goal after an acknowledgment-only turn (NO PROGRESS), reread the attachment, complete Ralph/AGENTS, mandatory R-S11/a/b/c/R-S16/R-S19 and Appendix C #25-#29, and the current authority ledger. - One coherent product/native slice: filesystem send-job starting-index admission. Current `TransferJob::new_read_with_budget` (`libs/hbb_common/src/fs.rs:3232`) enumerates native paths but admits an arbitrary signed `file_num`; `open_data_stream` and `read` cast it to usize and treat every index at or beyond list length as successful EOF, and `handle_read_jobs` can report Done. CM `start_read_job` (`src/ui_cm_interface.rs:3100-3206`) and direct `create_and_start_read_job` (`src/server/connection.rs:11853-11909`) trust that constructor's Result before publishing/admitting the job. The network Send dispatcher already rejects negative indexes (`connection.rs:8991`) but not a positive index beyond the actual list. Thus an invalid positive request may masquerade as successful completion. This is a concrete finality/correctness defect, not demonstrated local privilege escalation or installed peer behavior.
- Intended model: the filesystem constructor owns the exact enumerated list and initial index. It admits `0 <= file_num <= files.len()`, where equality is the legitimate completed/empty resume state; rejection creates no transfer owner or data stream. Existing typed Result is the correct API; add admission at its source rather than scatter guards at callers or change the protocol, add a mode, fallback, or state replica. MemoryCursor's protocol ordinal is not a filesystem list index; the existing arbitrary positive ordinals and keyed receipt test remain in scope as unchanged neighboring behavior, not evidence of filesystem bounds.

Official Rust Reference numeric-cast semantics (`https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/operator-expr.html#numeric-cast`) confirm signed-to-unsigned casts are numeric casts rather than range validation; API admission must reject invalid indexes before those read paths. Consulted pinned Tokio 1.44.2 File source (`https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/blob/tokio-1.44.2/tokio/src/fs/file.rs`); this slice changes no OS file-open/read/durability operation. ## 2026-10-05 — Android controlled-CM admission result is not authoritative

- Read-only trace at clean `fdcb4cfb`: `CmClientRegistry::admit` commits the new
  `(id, registry_generation)` before `ConnectionManager::add_connection` invokes
  `FlutterHandler::add_connection` (`src/ui_cm_interface.rs:574-611,1004-1064`).
  The handler calls the Android Service through JNI and logs a JNI error, but then
  publishes the Flutter `add_connection` event regardless (`src/flutter.rs:3077-3093`).
- The generation-aware JNI wrapper checks that the MainService generation is
  activation-claimed, then calls `rustSetByName` with a `void` return signature
  (`libs/scrap/src/android/ffi.rs:738-770`). `MainService.rustSetByName` returns
  normally after refusing an add when controlled admission is closed, the type
  is unknown, or `ControlledCaptureOwnerState.upsert` rejects it
  (`MainService.kt:119-165`). JNI therefore cannot distinguish those refusals
  from committed Service admission. Existing Kotlin owner-state tests execute
  `upsert` but not this Service/JNI transaction.
- Classification: OPEN controlled-side lifecycle/coherence gap, not proof of an
  exploitable local privilege escalation or the user's outgoing-viewer screen
  hang. The receiver does fail closed for capture/input when it refuses, but
  the native registry/UI can temporarily claim an admitted connection that the
  persistent Service does not own. Do not simply turn the void callback into a
  Boolean while leaving partial capture/voice/notification side effects or
  rolling back a replaced owner incorrectly. Define atomic admission and exact
  rollback/finality across the registry, Service state, voice state, and UI
  publication; then exercise refusal and successor preservation in an installed
  APK with a real controlled-side peer. Until then, no native closure claim.

## 2026-10-04 — Desktop tab-to-window ownership: source mismatch, native OPEN

- Read-only trace at clean pushed `73d2703cbd701ed21992db6384b161c2e3fcacb3`
  while the same APK producer session31157 remains live. No repository source,
  instruction content, host service, or running-test input was changed.
- The ordinary Remote tab menu (`remote_tab_page.dart:272`) passes its existing
  connection UUID through the main-window dispatcher (`desktop_home_page.dart:650`)
  into `RustDeskMultiWindowManager.moveTabToNewWindow` (`utils/multi_window_manager.dart:69`).
  Parameters include session_id and tab_window_id but no display/displays or prior
  client-owner identity. New and reused windows both construct RemotePage with
  that UUID; RemotePage.initState creates FFI(widget.sessionId).
- FFI's constructor (`models/model.dart:4453`) deliberately creates a fresh desktop
  clientOwnerId even when reusing the connection UUID. FFI.start (`:5167`) regards
  tabWindowId as an existing peer, skips sessionAddSync, and calls
  sessionAddExistedSync only when display is non-null. For ordinary tab transfer,
  neither native admission nor native owner replacement occurs before sessionStart.
  Native session_start_ (`src/flutter.rs:2822`) checks the exact client owner and
  refuses the fresh owner; the old handler still belongs to the old FFI.
- This is a source-proved unhandled transfer case, not yet a measured native
  failure. The cached-state/old-tab-close continuation (`model.dart:4954`) requires
  an event on the new stream first, so it cannot supply the missing prior transfer.
  closeSession:false retires only Dart ownership and does not call native
  remove_session_by_exact_ui_owner. The separate monitor-window path supplies
  display/displays and a fresh connection UUID, so this finding does not claim
  that every existing-peer attachment is broken.
- Preserve Rust's fail-closed exact-owner check. A correction needs an explicit
  exact-old-owner to exact-new-owner transfer with captured peer/display state,
  stale-callback rejection and old-engine resource retirement; it must not grant
  authority from a reused bare UUID or merely suppress attachment errors. Before
  implementing, define a real isolated multi-window transfer/repeat/failure test
  that holds the authenticated peer connection constant, observes changing pixels,
  retires old engine-backed resources and rejects stale-owner actions. Current
  focused model and Linux peer schedules do not exercise this transfer surface.
- This is outgoing desktop correctness/lifetime work, not an established local
  privilege escalation, not the Windows focus-delay cause, and not the Android
  Force-Stop display-hang cause. Native evidence and exact failure/rollback design
  remain OPEN. No implementation or native-pass claim is made in this turn.
- Git provenance narrows the transfer regression: commit
  76bd45ee07731c8cf3df7e8783a0f5c03e0c1cbf ("Make desktop texture teardown
  exact-owner safe") changed desktop clientOwnerId from sessionId to a fresh
  UUID on2026-07-31; exact native ownership refusal already existed from
  813bc5cb3. These are source-history facts under the recorded Git author,
  not evidence of who operated a machine or a measured native transfer failure.
  The fix must complete the missing transfer, not revert independent UI ownership.
- A simpler correct direction is to give the replacement view a fresh UI-session
  UUID as well as a fresh client-owner UUID, while attaching it to the same retained
  authenticated peer Arc. Existing monitor-window attachment already supports
  fresh handler IDs; last/non-last exact close already preserves a peer with a
  surviving handler. Extend that attachment to prove the exact source handler
  and owner, carry its explicit display inventory, bind cached-state requests
  to that same source generation, and retire the old view through ordinary exact
  close only after replacement admission/readiness. This avoids preserving a
  bare reused UUID that older owner-less input/preferences APIs could target.
  The two remaining closeSession:false call sites are Remote/ViewCamera cached
  transfer cleanup; they are not a reason to maintain detached ghost handlers.
  This is design research, not an implementation claim. Failure-before-handoff
  must preserve the old view; changed source, failed replacement and stale cached

- Separate progress hypothesis, not an observed engine failure: the isolate-wide
  LatestFrameDrainPool correctly retains permits for uncancellable operations

  shows a newest queue waiting, then releases one before the newest can begin.

  not a reason to add retries, unbounded conversions or service death. Primary:

  and `flock(2)` at https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html (nonblocking advisory locks bind an
  open file description). Locks serialize cooperating publishers; hostile root/kernel or deliberately

## 2026-07-27 — Whiteboard helper closed protocol and terminal resource ownership

- Scope and existing authority:
  - Traced Remote-only `show_my_cursor` registration through per-connection token creation, helper launch,
    token-derived endpoint selection, platform parent admission, mutual role-bound HMAC, command dispatch,
    renderer state, connection teardown, helper event-loop cancellation, and transport failure.
  - The pre-slice path already used a fresh 32-byte launch token, a token-derived endpoint, exact launch-parent and
    `--whiteboard` role proof, and tokens minted only for Remote-authenticated connection IDs. The reviewed source
    did not show an ambient same-UID overlay-command bypass.
- Finding and classification:
  - All four proof messages and all four post-proof commands still lived in the cross-purpose `Data` union and used
    the default unlimited `BytesCodec`. The owner used an unbounded command queue and ignored stream-write errors.
    The helper detached each authenticated stream, continued accepting streams, retained an unbounded token map,
    parsed unrelated `Data` variants, and made disconnect cleanup depend on incidental active state.
  - Classification: local parser, memory-budget, lifecycle-finality, and future-reactivation debt. This is not
    evidence of exploitation, root acquisition, public listener exposure, host RustDesk/service/configuration
    mutation, firewall/network mutation, or compromise.
- Intended authority and resource model:
  - Preserve the existing conjunctive launch-parent, exact-role, mutual-HMAC, Remote-connection, and per-connection
    token proofs. Replace the shared parser with closed directional handshake and command protocols; cap every
    whiteboard stream before proof; bound the owner queue and both owner/helper connection state; propagate every
    transport write; and let the helper directly own one proved stream through one unconditional terminal overlay
    exit.
- Current implementation:
  - `src/ipc.rs` defines unknown-field-denying owner-handshake, helper-handshake, and command enums outside `Data`;
    applies a 64-KiB codec cap on both connecting and accepted streams; uses one-second proof/read/write deadlines;
    and treats post-proof read timeout only as a cancellation wake while preserving terminal reset/codec/schema
    errors.
  - `src/whiteboard/client.rs` retains at most 16 positive IDs with fresh 32-byte tokens, uses a nonblocking
    64-entry queue, drops lossy presentation events with a diagnostic on overflow, retires the stream owner on
    bind/close/shutdown overflow, drops its extra local sender, and propagates every actual IPC write failure.
  - `src/whiteboard/server.rs` independently validates token shape and the 16-entry ceiling, rejects unbound,
    wrong-token, and peer `Exit` commands, directly awaits the sole authenticated stream instead of detaching it,
    wakes once per second for event-loop cancellation, and sends terminal overlay `Exit` for shutdown,
    cancellation, peer closure, malformed traffic, or transport failure.

    checkers, and the independent workspace mutation catalog bind the new model. The active requirements hash is

## 2026-07-22 — Authenticated Unix incumbent-listener ownership

- Candidate reconciliation before the finding:
  - Traced the Linux root service's `ServiceRuntime`, `OwnedServiceChild`, pidfd-backed crash recovery,
    boot/start-time/UID/executable/role/generation revalidation, credential drop, `PDEATHSIG`, child bootstrap, and
    termination paths. Routine ownership uses the retained `Child`; recovery is pidfd-first and fail-closed; the
    protected IPC receivers independently prove root-service/direct-child ancestry. No surviving ambient signaling
    or service-child ownership defect was found. The only intentionally separate parent surface remains the exact
    cold `.deb` transaction, already excluded from routine runtime authority and still governed by R-B2.
  - The next unresolved recorded boundary was `src/ipc/fs.rs::probe_existing_listener`, so this slice stayed on that
    one local lifecycle-authority decision rather than expanding into unrelated service or Android work.
- Finding and classification:
  - The inherited default treated a successful Unix-socket connection as sufficient proof of a live RustDesk
    singleton. Linux `_cm` and `_pa` had stronger process proofs and `_service` performed a typed liveness exchange,
    but main, password, URL, and token-derived whiteboard endpoints did not prove peer UID, PID, or executable before
    allowing the incumbent to retain the pathname.
  - An unrelated same-UID executable could bind one of those user-owned paths first and hold local availability
    without passing the endpoint's independent accept-time authentication. Conversely, treating missing identity
    evidence as stale would authorize unlinking an ambiguous live endpoint and could create split-brain state.
  - Classification: deterministic local singleton-availability/lifecycle-authority ambiguity. It is not message
    authorization bypass, credential disclosure, LPE, remote reachability, exploitation evidence, host mutation, or
    evidence of compromise. Code already executing under the same UID retains the unavoidable residual ability to
    deny service by repeatedly mutating its own mode-0700 socket directory.
- Primary platform evidence:
  - Linux `unix(7)` documents `SO_PEERCRED` as the connected Unix peer credentials captured at connect/listen/socket
    creation time: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html.
  - Linux `proc_pid_exe(5)` documents `/proc/<pid>/exe` as the executed-program reference and the ptrace-governed
    read/dereference boundary: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html.
  - The design therefore treats a positive UID/executable mismatch as a foreign stale candidate, but treats missing
    credentials or unavailable executable proof as an error that preserves the namespace entry.
- Implemented the smallest source correction:
  - `probe_existing_listener` and `check_pid` are fallible. Remaining generic Linux/macOS endpoints require the
    connected socket's kernel peer UID/PID, current-effective-UID equality, and a positive peer/current executable
    match before an incumbent is retained. `new_listener` propagates ambiguous proof failure before cleanup/bind.
  - Linux `_cm`/`_pa` retain their stronger exact proof paths. `_service` additionally retains the typed bounded
    `Data::Test` exchange; a failed/malformed response after identity proof now preserves the ambiguous endpoint
    instead of becoming silent cleanup authority. Accept-time receiver authentication remains independent and no new
    message is admitted.
  - Added R-S11bs, Appendix C #212, R-S11e-85, a focused policy regression,
    `scripts/verify-unix-listener-incumbent.py` with 18 deliberate mutations, shared/Apple gate wiring, and independent
    workspace-verifier source/mutation bindings. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `19765e32030adbbb3c25b2f98ec28a09ba6f6bd8da2b95287911023b8797e120`.
- Verification evidence:

## 2026-07-23 — Debian vendor-unit package authority (R-S11by/R-S11e-91)

- Selected one release-relevant privileged-boundary slice after confirming that the previously considered Windows
  MSI cleanup surface was already closed: Debian package scripts treated `rustdesk.service` as script-created mutable
  state instead of a dpkg-owned vendor file.
- Current-path proof before the change:
  - `build.py` placed `res/rustdesk.service` at `/usr/share/rustdesk/files/systemd/rustdesk.service`.
  - `postinst` unconditionally deleted `/etc/systemd/system/rustdesk.service`,
    `/usr/lib/systemd/system/rustdesk.service`, and `/usr/lib/systemd/user/rustdesk.service`, then copied the private
    template into `/usr/lib/systemd/system`.
  - `prerm` deleted the same paths and reloaded systemd before dpkg's package-file removal phase.
  - The exact `/etc/systemd/system/rustdesk.service` object may be an administrator replacement or a `/dev/null`
    mask. The scripts could therefore erase administrator policy; the vendor unit also sat outside dpkg's normal
    file and digest ownership.
- Implemented authority model:
  - `build.py` now packages the byte-exact unit directly as the ordinary mode-0644
    `/usr/lib/systemd/system/rustdesk.service` data member. Exact package inventories include the vendor directories
    and file, exclude the old `/usr/share` template, and include the unit in `md5sums`.
  - Dpkg alone installs, replaces, and removes the vendor unit. `postinst`, `prerm`, and `postrm` contain no primary
    systemd unit path and never unlink administrator state. The exact `preinst` old-unit predicate remains read-only.
  - Configure retains checked enable/reload/start. `prerm` retains checked stop/disable and removes only the
    maintainer-created `/usr/bin/rustdesk` link. `postrm remove|purge` performs checked daemon reload after dpkg file
    removal; purge separately clears helper and root service-config state.
  - The emitted-artifact gate checks exact source bytes, current-user extracted ownership, mode 0644, one link, and
    legacy-template absence. The package authority validator independently binds archive bytes and exact md5sums.
  - Source/systemd and SysV lifecycle package fixtures now stage the unit at the vendor path. The disposable systemd
    fixture creates an administrator `/etc/systemd/system/rustdesk.service` link before installation and requires it
    to survive install, removal, and purge while the dpkg-owned target appears and disappears normally.
- Regression enforcement:
  - The maintainer-script validator permits systemd unit search paths only in the exact read-only `preinst` predicate
    and enforces the revised lifecycle ordering.
  - The package self-test mutates the constructor back to the legacy template, restores `/etc` deletion in
    `postinst`, restores vendor deletion in `prerm`, restores `/etc` deletion in `postrm`, removes the post-removal
    reload, corrupts unit bytes, and changes unit mode. All are rejected.
  - The shared verifier and independent workspace semantic/mutation matrix bind constructor placement, each script
    path absence, post-removal reload, focused gate internals, emitted artifact binding, installed administrator-link
    fixture, requirement R-S11by, Appendix C #218, hardening ledger R-S11e-91, and synchronized hash scope.
- Normative/ledger updates:
  - Added R-S11by and Appendix C #218; reconciled Appendix C #59; updated deployment documentation.
  - Requirements SHA-256 is `54d0f62a0a6e14b1ee4cadc660944bea16583d3c0ddf9678ae8b94e83a2a5f5a`, synchronized in
    `HARDENING_STATUS.md` and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`.
  - Primary contracts: Debian Policy §9.3 and §10.7, plus Debian's `systemd.unit(5)` unit load-path precedence.
- Confined verification:
  - In immutable image `sha256:6766564c65b0daead7d7031fcf0ff9ec8becab6ef9e3f9a7efd9f02f1b893776`,
    Bash syntax, in-memory UTF-8 Python compilation, maintainer-script semantic validation, and the complete Debian

- Audited the final RustDesk-authored Windows Installer custom action and all of its authority/build edges:
  - `Package/Components/RustDesk.wxs` passed `[App.InstallFolder]` through a type-51 setter into deferred
    `CustomActionData`, then scheduled `RemoveRuntimeGeneratedFiles` immediately before `RemoveFiles` on uninstall
    and old-product removal.

    `RuntimeBroker_rustdesk.exe` without following a final reparse point, and marked it for deletion. Earlier
    R-S11d-4/R-S11d-33 work correctly made that inherited path fail closed, but the sole operation was already
    represented by Windows Installer's standard fixed-file removal model.
- Primary contract and boundary evidence:
  - Microsoft defines the `RemoveFile` table for author-specified files not installed by `InstallFiles`, with each
    row controlled by the linked component's action state and `InstallMode=2` applying when the component is removed:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/msi/removefile-table.
  - Microsoft defines the `RemoveFiles` standard action as the action that removes those author-specified files:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/msi/removefiles-action.
  - WiX v4 maps that row to a `RemoveFile` child of `Component`, defaults the directory to the parent component, and
    maps `On="uninstall"` to removal when the component goes absent:
    https://docs.firegiant.com/wix/schema/wxs/removefile/.
  - WiX also documents that extensions typically combine compiler support with extension-owned implementation
    actions: https://docs.firegiant.com/wix/tools/wixext/. Therefore the exact source claim is that RustDesk authors
    no custom-action DLL or cleanup action; it is deliberately not a claim that the final MSI `CustomAction` table
    is empty. Native R-B2/R-B10 validation must enumerate and attribute any actions emitted by pinned typed WiX
    extensions.

## 2026-07-22 — Event-driven outgoing voice-call subscription ownership

- Candidate reconciliation before the finding:
  - The remaining Linux `check_process()` users were traced before selecting this slice. R-S11e-45 already
    removed their service-child/tray/CM signal and replacement authority. The surviving Linux tray calls are
    non-root receiver-side singleton/presence decisions; they do not select a process to signal. The
    `allow-only-conn-window-open` connection branch is unreachable under this fork's compile-pinned empty option,
    explicitly chosen to avoid headless self-denial. The Unix current-image `--server` UID scan is stable
    config-sync routing, while sensitive password channels and helper receivers independently authenticate the
    connected process. No new privilege or connection-authorization finding was attributed to those scans.
  - The audit then returned to the shared outgoing-viewer lifetime involved in the reported Android symptom and
    enumerated every worker creation/handle in `src/client/io_loop.rs`. Video/audio decode and voice capture now
    retain handles, but the outgoing voice-capture worker still had a separate live resource defect.
- Proven old path and scope:
  - `Remote::start_voice_call()` subscribed a synthetic `ConnInner` to the process-local audio service, created a
    standard-library stop channel, and launched a dedicated thread whose unconditional loop performed
    `rx.try_recv()` followed by `rx_audio_data.try_recv()`. When neither stop nor audio was ready there was no
    wait, yield, or blocking receive. Every active outgoing voice call could therefore hot-poll a CPU core while
    idle.
  - The stop sender was not ownership of the service subscription that kept the audio receiver open. The worker
    itself revoked that subscription only after its polling loop happened to observe stop. This mixed resource
    ownership and polling as a lifecycle substitute.
  - The path is compiled on Android and desktop and is absent on iOS, whose branch has no local audio-service
    voice-capture worker. Android's foreground service can retain the process after the Activity is swiped away,
    amplifying the lifetime of shared process state. This source defect is not an on-device reproduction or
    proved cause of the reported one-host screen-control hang; it is not evidence of host RustDesk mutation,
    listener/firewall changes, Docker privilege, exploitation, or compromise.
- Corrected ownership and wait model:
  - `VoiceCallThread` now owns one `Arc<AtomicBool>` durable stop flag, the exact subscribed synthetic
    `ConnInner`, and the exact worker `JoinHandle`. Its common `stop()` publishes retirement with Release ordering
    before taking and unsubscribing that exact connection. The service's sender and the owner's retained sender
    are then dropped, closing the receiver and waking an idle worker without polling.
  - The dedicated standard thread blocks in `UnboundedReceiver::blocking_recv()`; it does not sleep-poll, spawn a
    detached async task, or create a nested runtime. It checks retirement before blocking and again after wake,
    so a queued audio message cannot cross a concurrent stop. Worker exit idempotently unsubscribes by the exact
    synthetic ID and restores voice-input state.
  - Named-thread spawn failure rolls back the subscription and voice-input selection before returning `None`.
    Normal voice close, outgoing-round reconnect/final teardown, and hard `Drop` all use `stop()` and retain the
    existing fixed media-completion pool's exact handle join/handoff. The persistent incoming Android
    `MainService`, listener, projection owner, and controlled-side capture demand are unchanged.
  - Added R-S11bp, Appendix C #209, and R-S11bp/R-S11e-82. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `45f7f885e6a5392e479db8aeb6544f4b85bcd2d0080ef13033b4c169076287eb`, synchronized in the native-codec and
    hardening hash ledgers.

    `/nix/store`. macOS likewise accepted every string beginning with `/Applications/<app>.app`. These are ambient
    directory/bundle prefixes, not supported executable identities; they include sibling names, helper payloads,
    copied-bundle prefixes, and future files below those names.

    bundle/signature, and installed-helper proofs. A caller-side Boolean cannot replace those receiver checks.

    against trusting the returned path as unforgeable executable identity:

## 2026-07-22 — Shared outgoing-viewer reconnect round ownership

- Selection and scope:
  - The open R-S11/R-S11b/R-S11c ledger is source-implemented but still carries exact cold release-artifact,
    Apple/mobile artifact, live-device, external R-V3 crypto-review, and accepted native-decode residual evidence.
    The binding loop expressly excludes starting the long release build without a separate request. This slice
    therefore continued the adjacent Android/session resource-lifetime audit in shared viewer-core source.
  - Android's retained `MainService` makes process-static outgoing state survive task swipe/relaunch, but the
    concrete defect is shared by Android, desktop, iOS, and future macOS builds. File transfer remains independently
    usable because the worker table keys it under a separate `ConnType` session. No controlled-side listener,
    service, MediaProjection, capture, or file-transfer behavior is changed by this slice.
- Proven old path and authorship:
  - Imported baseline `c2abd3b3` explicitly implemented `ConnectionState::Connecting => return` in
    `Session::reconnect()`. An explicit user retry therefore did nothing while a retained outgoing start was stuck;
    that exact worker and its peer/type slot remained authoritative until it happened to complete or the process
    died.
  - Commit `907a3a8` correctly retained and joined exact outgoing I/O/media worker handles before replacement, but
    it preserved the inherited connecting-state early return. That correction removed detachment and exposed the
    remaining state-machine defect; it did not create the defect.
  - `Remote::io_loop()` raced `Client::start()` only against final close. A completed old start unconditionally
    changed the shared state to Connected and published `connection_ready`; establishment failure likewise
    published without proving its round still owned the session. A replacement notification alone would not be a
    durable cancellation fact because Tokio `Notify::notify_waiters()` does not store a permit for future waiters.
  - This is deterministic shared viewer-lifecycle/availability debt and a source-proven mechanism consistent with
    the Android report. It is not an on-device causal reproduction and is not evidence of host RustDesk
    modification, public exposure, firewall/UFW change, privilege escalation, root/container escape, exploitation,
    or compromise.
- Corrected owner model:
  - Each `Session` now owns one checked monotonic `ConnectionRoundOwner`: exact round, Connecting/Connected/
    Disconnected state, terminal-retirement bit, and a connection-start cancellation notifier. Counter exhaustion
    fails closed; retirement is irreversible and rejects both future rounds and late publications.
  - Explicit reconnect acquires the exact worker slot, publishes the replacement round first, wakes the old
    connecting start (or sends `Data::Close` to an established round), joins the exact old worker and all media
    children it owns, rechecks final retirement, and only then spawns the replacement. The former Connecting no-op
    is deleted.
  - `run_start()` constructs and enables final-close and round-replacement waiters before reading durable state.
    Replacement before waiter creation is caught by the round mismatch; replacement between registration and
    selection is caught by the enabled waiter. The locked state is reduced to a Boolean in a lexical scope before
    `tokio::select!`, so no `MutexGuard` crosses an await and the future remains `Send` on Rust 1.75.
  - Connection-start success/readiness and establishment error publication execute synchronously inside exact
    current-round admission. This linearizes publication against concurrent reconnect and final retirement. A stale
    successful start drops its peer, shuts down its owned workers, and cannot mutate the replacement. Final close
    marks the round owner retired before setting/notifying the existing close flag, closing the post-start/
    pre-publication retirement race.
  - Primary runtime references: Tokio 1.44.2 `Notify`/`Notified` semantics,
    https://docs.rs/tokio/1.44.2/tokio/sync/struct.Notify.html; Tokio `select!` cancellation behavior,
    https://docs.rs/tokio/1.44.2/tokio/macro.select.html; and Rust exact-thread `JoinHandle::join` synchronization,
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.75.0/std/thread/struct.JoinHandle.html.
  - R-T4 states replacement/cancellation/current-round admission and terminal-retirement requirements. Appendix C
    #206 and the R-D7a/R-T4 ledger record the inherited defect, correction, shared-platform scope, Android
    amplification, non-causal limitation, and remaining artifact/device obligations. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `d9512748e16a3995bb459e63dc3b8aa8084246de182a62e8e29cdc2acddf5ad4`, synchronized in both tracked ledgers.
- Verification evidence and boundary:

## 2026-07-21 — Android MediaProjection owner and live capture-demand finality

- Selection and scope:
  - The exact cold R-B2/R-B10 release transaction, APK/device execution, and R-V3 review remain open; the binding
    loop expressly excludes starting the long release build without a separate request. This slice therefore
    continued the adjacent Android resource-lifetime audit in source and did not claim device reproduction.
  - The original reported symptom was Android acting as an outgoing viewer after task swipe/relaunch. The source
    finding here is on Android's controlled side: the persistent `MainService` owns incoming direct service and
    screen capture. It is actionable but is not claimed as the source-proven cause of that outgoing-viewer symptom.
    File transfer remains independent of MediaProjection and is not changed.
- Proven old path and authorship:
  - Imported baseline `c2abd3b3` retained a `MediaProjection` but registered no `MediaProjection.Callback`.
    `createOrSetVirtualDisplay()` caught `SecurityException`, launched a new consent Activity, and returned `Unit`;
    `startCapture()` then unconditionally set `_isStart = true` and enabled raw video even if no VirtualDisplay had
    been created. Fresh consent overwrote the projection without an exact callback/owner replacement transition.
  - Commit `ec0fc853` correctly made service destruction and explicit Stop converge on complete capture-resource
    teardown, but it did not close revocation observation or false active-state commit. This slice does not blame
    that correction for the inherited defect; it completes the owner model that the earlier patch began.
  - Native `ConnectionManager::remove_connection` counted a connection by negative type checks only. It omitted
    view-camera and did not require the row to be authorized and non-disconnected. An unauthorized, stale, or
    non-desktop row could therefore retain desktop-capture demand after the last live Remote session ended.
  - Android's official API contract requires callback registration before `createVirtualDisplay`, defines
    `MediaProjection.Callback.onStop()` as the point after which the projection is invalid and resources must be
    released, documents a nullable VirtualDisplay result, and documents `SecurityException`/`IllegalStateException`
    failure for stopped/reused or callback-less projections. Primary references:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/projection/MediaProjection and
    https://developer.android.com/media/grow/media-projection.
  - This is controlled-side capture-lifecycle/correctness and availability debt. It is not evidence of a host
    RustDesk modification, public listener, firewall/UFW change, privilege escalation, root/container escape,
    exploitation, or compromise.
- Corrected owner and demand model:
  - `MainService` has one exact projection/callback owner. Installation fully retires the old owner while preserving
    only live capture demand, registers the exact callback before any display creation, and marks projection
    readiness only after registration succeeds. Callback replacement is ABA-safe: `onStop()` invalidates resources
    only when both the projection and callback identities still match; a delayed callback from a replaced owner is
    ignored.
  - Capture start is transactional. It snapshots the exact projection, rejects absence, creates/reattaches the
    VirtualDisplay through a Boolean result, and commits `_isStart`/raw-video enable only after a non-null display
    exists. Revoked/stopped/null state fully releases the failed owner while preserving demand and requests fresh
    consent. Optional audio failure is logged and does not turn an already-active display into false inactive state.
  - Exact projection stop clears readiness and fully releases VirtualDisplay, ImageReader, Surface, raw-video, and
    audio state. Full service teardown additionally unregisters and stops the exact projection. Explicit capture
    stop clears demand but keeps the reusable projection/display grant where Android permits reuse; system stop or
    failed ownership always uses full release.
  - Capture demand is set for every newly authorized Remote even when capture is already active, and is cleared
    only when no live authorized non-disconnected Remote remains. File-transfer, view-camera, terminal,
    unauthorized, and disconnected connections never create or retain demand. A delayed fresh-consent result
    resumes capture only if that demand still exists, so consent cannot revive capture after the last Remote leaves.
  - R-S14 now states the exact owner/callback, transactional-start, connection-demand, and delayed-consent rules.
    Appendix C #205 and the R-S14/R-T4 ledger record the defect, correction, non-causal limitation, and pending
    device evidence. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `0f19384a35720c2043ddd511b74c61e4ed3d42a2a1dbcfdfb081c2dd826c37b0`, synchronized in both tracked ledgers.

- Selection and disproved lead:
  - Re-read the binding loop, AGENTS.md, R-S11/R-S11a/R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19, Appendix C #25–#29,
    the complete current R-S11b/R-S11c/open-residual ledger, and the live IPC/resource paths. The exact clean cold
    R-B2/R-B10 transaction, final Debian artifact lifecycle marker, real-device behavior, and R-V3 review remain
    open; the loop expressly forbids starting the long release build without a separate request.
  - The initial Android CM-state suspicion did not survive source tracing. Every `Connection::start` constructs its
    own `rx_to_cm`/`tx_from_cm` channels and invokes Android `start_channel` separately, while file actions validate
    the embedded connection identity. The mutable `current_id` in that function is therefore per-channel task state,
    not a process-global session reused between hosts. No change or causal claim was made on that false lead.
  - The adjacent desktop audit did find a concrete, independently actionable lifecycle defect in Linux headless CM
    bootstrap. This is not claimed as the Android swipe/relaunch screen-control cause.
- Proven old path and authorship:
  - `try_start_cm_ipc()` moves the per-connection receivers into a Tokio bridge task. Normal bridged operation
    already terminates when the connection-owned command sender disappears, but bootstrap has waits before that
    receive loop.
  - Commit `98fc028f` introduced the logind-less `headless_service_user` selection loop around the imported
    prelogin sleep without observing command-channel closure. Once its connection owner disappeared, that task
    could remain in the one-second wait indefinitely.
  - Imported baseline `c2abd3b3` supplied the Linux empty-username loop and explicitly documented that a closed
    `_rx_desktop_ready` receiver returns `None` immediately and can spin. It nevertheless discarded the timeout/
    receive result and retained that behavior. `LinuxHeadlessHandle` owns the only readiness sender, so dropping the
    exact `Connection` permanently closes the receiver and makes this a deterministic CPU hot loop while username
    remains empty. The same task could proceed to CM launch or endpoint retries after owner loss.
  - This is local resource/lifecycle availability debt. It is not evidence of a host RustDesk modification, public
    listener, firewall/UFW change, privilege escalation, root/container escape, exploitation, or compromise.
- Corrected lifetime model:
  - Every desktop `Connection` owns the sole sender of a dedicated one-shot lifetime channel. The spawned task
    races bootstrap against its receiver, and `Connection::Drop` closes that sender before other cleanup. Owner
    loss therefore cancels any async pre-bridge wait independently of command traffic. Once authenticated bootstrap
    signals completion, biased selection drains the live bridge rather than cancelling it, preserving the queued
    graceful/hard-Drop CM close notification before command-receiver closure terminates the bridge.
  - The per-connection command receiver remains an additional fail-closed check before target/prelogin selection,
    each headless-user iteration, CM launch, and each endpoint retry. Once closure is observed, no further bootstrap
    work is admitted. A bounded synchronous launch already admitted before concurrent closure may finish before the
    outer future is polled; the next poll cancels the remainder.
  - A Linux-only `LinuxDesktopReadyWait` outcome makes the readiness protocol explicit: timeout and a delivered
    signal are `Wake` and merely recheck desktop state; sender closure is `OwnerClosed` and returns before username
    refresh. Five current-thread async regressions prove both readiness branches, closed-owner cancellation,
    live-owner task completion, and post-bootstrap bridge drain after owner closure.
  - The ordinary connected bridge remains receiver-closure-driven, and R-S11ad independently binds a launched
    `--cm-no-ui` child to its exact server parent. This slice does not claim a synchronous join from
    `Connection::Drop`; the dedicated lifetime guard cancels the task future before bootstrap completion, while the
    completed live bridge exits through its command receiver after forwarding queued close state. It closes the
    inherited unbounded waits/hot loop without inventing a blocking task supervisor or changing CM protocol behavior.
  - R-T4 now states this pre-bridge cancellation rule. Appendix C #204 and R-S11c-27t record the defect, correction,
    limitations, and remaining release/device obligations. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `1c4b559cde3115b93d97935dd4226e6e6c67ece455714c96c3391ba6f6d1dea9`, synchronized in both tracked ledgers.
- Verification evidence:
  - Exact Rust 1.75 locked/offline compilation from the reviewed vendor snapshot built the full Linux library test
    target in a fresh disposable target and passed the five focused regressions: 5 passed, 0 failed, 328 filtered.
    The pre-existing compile warnings are not promoted into failures or silently edited.
  - Exact Rust 1.75 rustfmt checked `src/server/connection.rs` and passed after the single required line wrapping.
    The formatter toolchain was mounted read-only into the container; no component was installed or fetched.
  - The extracted R-T4/R-S11c-27t shell gate passed. Its first execution also exposed that the newly written AWK
    range could reopen on a later `if headless_cm` and make a `grep|head` pipeline fail under `pipefail`; the gate
    itself was corrected to terminate the first exact region and use bounded first-match reads before being counted.
  - The independent workspace semantic verifier passed normally and its complete deliberate source-mutation matrix
    passed. Bash syntax, exact hash synchronization, `git diff --check`, and the focused semantic/order assertions
    are part of the final pre-publication rerun.
  - The repository-wide `scripts/verify.sh` entry point is not claimed green because its newly pinned exact
    devcheck image `sha256:2f0406ee5b7dcd5683d900fb8b45668abd69934e6b4bdbf4737165fc01e72398`
    is absent locally. Existing image
    `sha256:da876c1ffa017736b2f63d56f8b106956d6b4d730ebbf3e99feffda42ac0b91c` supplied focused diagnostic compile
    evidence only; it was not substituted for release provenance. No long release/APK/device run was performed.

## 2026-07-21 — shared media-worker and controlled voice-audio completion ownership

- Selection and scope:
  - The current R-S11b/R-S11c source topology remains implemented; its remaining release closure is the exact full
    R-B2/R-B10 transaction and Debian lifecycle marker, which the reusable loop prompt forbids starting without an
    explicit long-release-build request. The adjacent resource-lifetime audit therefore continued the still-open
    Android outgoing-viewer/device symptom boundary rather than claiming release completion.
  - Exact source review of `Session` I/O ownership, `Remote` video/audio/voice children, and controlled
    `Connection` peer-audio handling found one concrete exception to the 2026-07-20 “all media workers” ledger
    statement. This is a shared availability/resource-lifetime finding, not a local privilege-escalation path.
- Old path and authorship:
  - Upstream-import baseline `c2abd3b3` implemented `start_audio_thread() -> MediaSender` by spawning the decoder
    and returning only its sender, so controlled-side voice audio had always detached that worker.
  - Follow-up commit `907a3a8e` correctly introduced `OwnedMediaThread` for the outgoing viewer, but kept the old
    controlled call through an explicitly named “legacy” compatibility constructor whose `_thread` binding
    discarded the newly visible handle. That commit did not create the detached controlled behavior and did not
    modify any installed/host RustDesk, but preserving it was a partial API correction and made the tracked “all
    media workers” closure too broad. This slice removes that shortcut rather than defending it.
  - At the controlled call site, accepted format and sender were stored as separate fields; audio disable dropped
    them without a join; voice-call close deliberately retained them; graceful connection close never took them.
    `OwnedMediaThread::Drop` and `VoiceCallThread::Drop` synchronously joined, contrary to R-T4's prohibition on
    blocking completion in hard Drop. Accepted-call setup also selected global input before an await and set the
    Drop-visible owner flag only afterward; close cleared the flag before disabling input. Cancellation could
    therefore strand voice state even after decoder ownership was corrected.
- Corrected ownership model:
  - `start_audio_thread()` is now the sole constructor and returns `OwnedMediaThread`; the sender-only constructor,
    `start_owned_audio_thread()` compatibility name, `_thread` discard, and split controlled sender/format fields
    are deleted.
  - `ControlledAudioThread` combines accepted Opus format and exact decoder owner. Overlapping call requests are
    refused. Call close, audio disable, format-start failure, and connection close take this value, close channel
    admission, and await the exact decoder before replacement. Accepted calls establish Drop-visible global-input
    ownership before their first await; closing disables global input before clearing the flag.
  - Graceful viewer and controlled teardown transfer exact video/audio/voice handles to a bounded four-thread
    completion pool before awaiting it. A cancelled waiter cannot detach queued/running joins. Hard Drop closes the
    channel/signal and performs a nonblocking handoff to the same fixed pool. Pool queue exhaustion, poisoned queue
    authority, or lost completion authority aborts rather than silently detach.
  - `Connection.closed` is set only after its synchronous CM close notification, preserving the existing Drop
    fallback when cancellation lands during input/media completion. `Connection::Drop` synchronously releases its
    global voice-input authority and hands controlled audio to the nonblocking reaper.
- Evidence and honest impact:
  - Added R-T4's explicit worker-owner rule and Appendix C #203. The tracked R-D7a/R-T4 ledger now distinguishes
    this shared controlled-side correction from the earlier Android outgoing-viewer tree. It is a real defect that

    Android screen-control hang, and no device result is claimed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` now runs both media-owner regressions and gates the sole constructor, fixed completion pool,
    hard-drop handoffs, combined controlled lifetime, acceptance/close cancellation ordering, every graceful sink,

## 2026-07-21 — Android tool-preferences scratch ownership

- Exact target sequence and dependency behavior:
  - R-S11bl was committed and pushed as `c413f4e86cd05b4aac5f19bbdd9b79d4c63f50b5`, then exercised through the
    default target-local `DOUBLE_BUILD=1` transaction from a clean tree. It passed bridge generation and the full
    release native Rust/JNI build, then AGP 7.3.1 failed closed because it attempted to create
    `/home/ubuntu/.android` on the deliberately read-only root. Shell `HOME=/tmp/buildhome` did not change Java's
    account-derived `user.home`.
  - The first correction, pushed as `ba29c955ea61a374318f94ad7a24699c987256a6`, selected a fresh private
    `/tmp/android-user-home` through the current `ANDROID_USER_HOME` contract. Its clean default A/B transaction
    succeeded and produced identical signed APKs, but both passes emitted a nonfatal warning for
    `/home/ubuntu/.android/analytics.settings`. This result proved the APK path but not complete preference-state
    ownership.
  - Exact JAR inspection inside the pinned builder found the warning in
    `com.android.tools.analytics-library:shared:30.3.1`. `javap` of
    `AnalyticsPaths.getAndEnsureAndroidSettingsHome()` proved that this legacy component checks
    `ANDROID_PREFS_ROOT`, then `ANDROID_SDK_HOME`, then JVM `user.home`; it predates `ANDROID_USER_HOME`.
  - A dual-variable correction was committed and pushed as `b757d8207a8be8fc063661dfba1369428021debd` and was
    tested rather than accepted from source reasoning. Pass A reauthenticated all inputs, generated the bridge,
    completed native release compilation in 2m27s, retired LLVM, and verified the Gradle projection. AGP then
    failed closed while deriving the default debug-keystore location. Exact `com.android.tools:common:30.3.1`
    bytecode proved that `ANDROID_USER_HOME` is a final path while `ANDROID_PREFS_ROOT` is a parent to which current
    tools append `.android`; setting both to the same string therefore creates two different resolved locations,
    and `PathLocator.singlePathOf()` rejects the ambiguity. No APK was published by this failed attempt.

- Final authority model and source correction:

    root and its `.android` child as real mode-0700 current-UID directories, and proves both postconditions before
    any extracted toolchain runs.
  - Legacy analytics uses the private parent directly; current common-30.3.1 resolves the private `.android`
    child. This owns both exact pinned semantics without conflicting injection, a broad JVM `user.home` override,
    a host mount, writable container root, larger tmpfs/cgroup, persistence fallback, network, capability,
    privilege, or port.
  - `scripts/verify-android-builder-authority.py` binds the single exact root, competing-input clearing/refusal,
    freshness, both mode-0700 constructors/postconditions, and order before every tool consumer. Its final focused
    suite passed and rejected all 73 mutations, including reintroducing either competing Android home and all

    both constructors and passed its complete repository source-mutation matrix.
  - Bash/Python/HTML parsing, the independent normal workspace gate, native-codec-watch normal and self-test gates,

## 2026-07-21 — Android bounded scratch lifecycle authority

- Current checklist and selected slice:
  - The R-S11b/R-S11c source topology remains implemented. Still-open obligations are the exact clean R-B2/R-B10
    artifact transaction and Debian lifecycle marker, native Apple/iOS and real mobile-device behavior, refreshed
    independently acquired advisory authority, R-V3 external review, remaining Linux lifecycle evidence variants,
    and the accepted SHOULD-level decoder sandbox residual.
  - The selected single release blocker is R-S11bl/R-S11e-78: the Android compile container's bounded scratch
    lifecycle. Work began from clean synchronized `master`/`origin/master` at
    `fea99e583a560736771606a39f58a309ad550a2a`.

- Concrete path and root cause:
  - `scripts/build-android.sh` gives compilation one non-root, networkless, read-only-root container with a 10-GiB
    executable `/tmp` tmpfs and a 12-GiB memory/no-swap ceiling. Those bounds were retained.
  - `scripts/android-apk-build.sh` projected the writable Gradle cache before extracting every toolchain. It then
    retained the Rust installer, Android cross-std installer, Flutter, LLVM, the installed Rust toolchain, Cargo
    state, and build-home state together. The first exact build at pushed `fea99e5` exhausted that tmpfs while
    extracting LLVM before compilation.
  - Allocated-byte measurement in the exact already-present Android image showed 9,093,156,864 bytes after the four
    toolchain extractions and 9,739,079,680 after Rust installation. The independently verified Gradle seed
    projection occupies 4,694,925,312 allocated bytes. The old simultaneous live set was therefore about 14.43 GB
    before Cargo/Flutter compilation, structurally above the 10-GiB ceiling.
  - The host filesystem still had over 314 GB free, so the failure was isolated to the intentional private tmpfs.
    This is build-availability/resource-lifecycle debt, not a public listener, unbounded host write, root container,
    escape, host service/firewall mutation, exploitation, or evidence of compromise.

- Primary contract and design decision:
  - Docker documents that tmpfs is ephemeral memory-backed state, may be swapped by the kernel, and that its `size`
    is a maximum: https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/tmpfs/. Docker's resource documentation states that equal
    `--memory` and `--memory-swap` denies container swap and warns that oversized memory authority can destabilize
    a host: https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/resource_constraints/.
  - The correct model is phase ownership, not a larger tmpfs/cgroup or a host-disk fallback. Rust/cross-std installer
    payloads end immediately after installation; LLVM ends after bridge/native compilation; writable Gradle state
    begins only after LLVM ends. Installed Cargo remains because `flutter/android/app/build.gradle` executes
    `cargo metadata` during final configuration.
  - Measured staged state is 8,133,832,704 bytes after installer retirement during the Flutter/LLVM phase and
    2,352,091,136 bytes after LLVM retirement. Adding the 4,694,925,312-byte Gradle projection gives about 7.05 GB
    at the final packaging phase, without adding a mount, writable host scratch, resource grant, capability, network,
    image operation, or privilege.

- Source correction and regression boundary:
  - `scripts/android-apk-build.sh` installs Rust and Android cross-std first, removes both consumed installer roots,
    and proves both paths absent before Flutter/LLVM extraction. After bridge generation, native JNI compilation,
    and JNI/NDK-runtime projection, it removes LLVM, proves absence, clears LLVM/bindgen environment references, and
    only then invokes the single offline Gradle projection immediately before Flutter packaging.

    and `remove` as legacy, recommends `print`, `bootstrap`, and `bootout`, states that legacy load/unload return
    nonzero only for improper usage and otherwise return zero, and says remove returns without waiting for stop:
    https://manp.gs/mac/1/launchctl. Apple's launchd job guide separately confirms the system LaunchDaemon versus
    per-login LaunchAgent topology:
    https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html.
  - The authority model is exact-domain state, not command invocation: root daemon operations target
    `system/<label>`; current GUI agent operations target `gui/<numeric-effective-uid>/<label>`. A failed exact-target
    query can mean absence only after the containing domain itself printed successfully.
- Concrete defect and impact:
  - `src/platform/macos.rs` interpreted every nonzero implicit `launchctl list <label>` status as “not loaded,” then
    used legacy asynchronous `remove` and legacy `load -w`. The root scripts likewise skipped or accepted lifecycle
    work through implicit `list` and legacy `load -w`/`unload -w` even though those statuses do not prove the
    operation completed.
  - A launchd-domain/query failure could therefore be accepted as absence, and a zero legacy load/unload status
    could be accepted as successful install/uninstall. The wrappers' claimed postconditions were not authoritative.
  - This is a source-proven local macOS lifecycle finality and availability defect. It is not evidence of
    exploitation, a stopped or modified real service, host mutation, public listener, Docker root, privilege
    escalation, firewall change, or compromise.
- Implemented one coherent lifecycle correction:
  - `launchctl_query_succeeds` uses fixed `/bin/launchctl print`, suppresses expected query output, and applies the
    existing non-stdio descriptor closure before execution. `launchctl_service_loaded` first proves the containing
    domain, then queries the exact service target. `ensure_launchctl_service_removed` checks state, uses checked
    modern `bootout` only when present, and repeats the domain-aware negative proof.
  - Rust derives the LaunchAgent domain from numeric `geteuid()`, removes any existing exact GUI target, clears an
    older persistent disabled override through checked `enable`, bootstraps the plist into that exact domain, and
    requires a final successful target print. Uninstall similarly proves the exact current GUI target absent.
  - The privileged install/uninstall scripts derive `system/<service-label>`, prove system-domain reachability,
    reconcile a present daemon with checked `bootout`, verify absence, use checked `enable`/`bootstrap` for install,
    and prove absence before deleting plist/helper artifacts for uninstall. The legacy list/load/unload/remove verbs
    are absent from all corrected lifecycle paths. Existing fixed executable provenance, closed administrator-script
    environment, helper/plist trust, descriptor closure, and outer result propagation remain unchanged.

## 2026-07-22 — Android native voice-call recorder exact ownership

- Selected the explicit open Android continuation from R-S11bq after re-reading the binding loop, AGENTS.md,
  R-S11/R-S11a/R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19, Appendix C #25–#29, the current service-authority ledger, and the
  complete Android voice-call/service/Activity lifecycle. This is one Android native resource-lifetime slice; it
  does not change or claim closure of the independent R-B2/R-B10 artifact/device transaction, Linux service-child
  parent item, native Apple/installed-platform evidence, or R-V3 external review.
- Proven inherited source paths:
  - `MainService.rustSetByName("update_voice_call_state")` switched its one service-local `AudioRecordHandle`
    immediately from each controlled connection's Boolean state. Two independently valid controlled IDs were not
    aggregated, so one false event could revoke the recorder required by another; `FlutterHandler::remove_connection`
    had no matching native exact-owner retirement notification.
  - `MainActivity` constructed a second `AudioRecordHandle`. Each outgoing start/close selected the service object
    only if the asynchronous binding happened to be present and otherwise selected the Activity object. A start and
    close could therefore address different recorders, and swiping the Activity did not necessarily kill the
    process-retained foreground service.
  - Recorder creation did not prove `STATE_INITIALIZED`; start had no Boolean result; invalid buffer or allocation
    state could retain a partial recorder; and a null return from `READ_BLOCKING` re-entered the loop instead of
    terminating. These are source-proven Android native lifecycle defects and a plausible mechanism for state that
    survives until Force Stop, not an on-device causal reproduction of the reported screen-control symptom.
- Official Android contracts researched and design implications:
  - The Service API states that a running service receives `onTaskRemoved` when its app task is removed and must
    release held resources in `onDestroy`; `START_NOT_STICKY` prevents automatic recreation after termination:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Service. Implication: Activity swipe and service process
    lifetime are different owner events and must retire separate exact domains.
  - Android's bound-service guide distinguishes started-service lifetime from client binding:
    https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/bound-services. Implication: `mainService != null`
    is transport timing, never audio resource ownership.
  - Android's audio-input sharing policy does not make competing ordinary captures a reliable ownership mechanism
    and treats communication capture as privacy-sensitive:
    https://developer.android.com/media/platform/sharing-audio-input. Implication: one application coordinator owns
    the process recorder; parallel Activity/service handles are not a supported aggregation design.
  - `AudioRecord` documents construction state, recording state, stop, and release:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/AudioRecord. Implication: built-but-uninitialized and
    started-but-not-recording objects fail before ownership commit, and every partial/exact object is released.
  - MediaProjection capture requires callback-bound revocation lifecycle:
    https://developer.android.com/media/platform/av-capture. Implication: playback mode is subordinate to the exact
    current projection object, and an active old-projection recorder cannot be reused for a replacement grant.
- Intended state model:
  - One process-wide synchronized coordinator constructs the sole `AudioRecordHandle`. It records a registered set
    of voice-capable controlled IDs and a separate active subset, plus one outgoing owner consisting of the current
    positive Activity generation and canonical isolate UUID. New Activity creation invalidates the prior outgoing
    owner before Flutter runs. Rust resume is a read-only exact-current-UUID check. Kotlin accepts an exact
    previous-to-same-UUID nondecreasing-generation transfer, or the already-current replacement as an idempotent
    lost-response retry; older and cross-isolate requests cannot claim or drain a replacement. A reconciliation
    failure retires and closes only the stale original owner, never the authoritative replacement. Stale events and
    teardown therefore cannot affect a replacement. Service destruction clears controlled owners only;
    Activity/task teardown clears the exact outgoing owner only.
  - Desired recorder mode is closed and ordered: any active voice owner -> `VOICE_COMMUNICATION`; otherwise exact
    live MediaProjection -> playback; otherwise stopped. Projection reuse additionally requires object identity.
    Connection removal reaches the coordinator before UI removal. Service binding has no semantic role.
  - Recorder start commits only after initialized/recording-state proof. Buffer sizing is positive and widened before
    checked multiplication. Allocation/start/thread failures release partial state. A failed blocking read is
    terminal. Stop invalidates, calls `stop()` to unblock, joins exactly while preserving interruption, and clears
    the exact recorder/reader/mode/projection/raw-audio flag.
- LPE/security classification so far:
  - No new credible local privilege-escalation path was found in this slice. Android microphone/MediaProjection
    permissions remain OS-mediated and the change narrows process-internal resource authority. The defect is
    resource availability/lifecycle coherence, not evidence of host compromise, public listener exposure, firewall
    mutation, Docker/root use, or exploitation.
  - No host RustDesk process/service/binary/configuration/listener, firewall, UFW/nftables/iptables, host network, or
    Android device state has been inspected or changed. No container has been given root, network, a port, Docker
    socket, host PID/network namespace, or host service/config mounts.

- Selected shared-resource finding and impact:
  - The Rust audio service held one process-global `Option<String>` voice input, but every independently owned
    outgoing viewer call and accepted controlled connection could clear it on worker exit, explicit close,
    asynchronous cleanup, or `Drop`. Controlled connections duplicated ownership in `voice_calling: bool`.
  - Concurrent viewer sessions and controlled connection IDs are valid. One retiring call could therefore clear
    and restart input still required by another call, and the boolean/device/worker state could diverge. This is a
    source-proven availability/lifecycle defect, not a privilege escalation and not proof of the reported Android
    screen-control hang.
- Implemented R-S11bq/R-S11e-83:
  - `VoiceCallInputState` now couples the selected device to a checked owner count. Successful acquisition returns
    a private, non-cloneable `VoiceCallInputLease`; overflow fails without mutation, and impossible release
    underflow is fail-stop. Non-final release preserves the stream; final release alone clears and restarts it.
  - Explicit operator device selection changes the one physical stream without minting or revoking ownership. Its
    public API accepts a concrete `String`, not an `Option`, so only lease release can clear state. The ambiguous
    `set_if_present` API and all ambient global-`None` cleanup are deleted.
  - `VoiceCallThread` owns its exact input lease with its stop flag, subscription, and worker handle. Controlled
    `Connection` owns an exact lease rather than a parallel boolean, acquires before its first response await,
    refuses on acquisition failure, derives audio/overlap state from lease presence, and takes only its own lease
    on explicit close, asynchronous close, and cancellation-safe `Drop`.

    one process-global `AudioRecordHandle` directly for each individual true/false event. A false event can switch
    out while another connection remains active, and ordinary connection removal does not emit exact native owner
    retirement before removal.
  - Outgoing `MainActivity` voice events have no session owner and may cross the activity/service recorder handoff.

    and device-evidence slice; this Rust correction does not claim to solve them.

    compilation/optional-dependency selectors:

- Selection and authority reconstruction:

    viewer/login path, server connection state, connection-manager IPC DTOs, Flutter event bridge, Dart connection
    model, web bridge, Android sources, and protocol schema. The active protocol has no switch-sides request or
    response, the UI has no switch action, and the responder/orchestration code has already been deleted.

    `2bdd516` removed FRB operations and web stubs; `9d617e7` removed the Rust orchestration while deliberately
    deferring lowercase Sciter compatibility; `f8717e7` removed the protocol request/response and responder;

    `SwitchSidesResponse` path was the only setter that made `from_switch` true and formerly selected password/2FA
