## 2026-07-21 — Direct-address UI authority and numeric-ID formatter excision

- Selected the exact remaining R-G2/R-SV5 address-model slice from the Tier 4 ledger. The current R-S11 source
  topology remains closed; this slice does not modify Android foreground-service lifetime, host-service startup,
  IPC authorization, listener binding, firewall state, or any privileged operation.
- Source/history proof and impact classification:
  - `5f322d7ec217f44a737d0fea7ef03cf7d60a7238` intentionally removed numeric formatting from the desktop/mobile
    connect fields but left `formatID` in peer rendering as separate follow-on work; `9eb1c6d` later removed the
    dead numeric input formatter. Current source still retained `formatID`, `trimID`, and
    `IDTextEditingController`, plus numeric-only whitespace deletion in both autocomplete option builders.
  - The shared `connect()` choke point deleted every ASCII space before `isDirectAddress`. Consequently malformed
    input such as `192. 168.1.10` was silently changed into the different valid target `192.168.1.10`, rather than
    rejected by the Dart validator/Rust direct-address accept set. Numeric-looking persisted peer addresses were
    also presentation-rewritten by `formatID` instead of rendered as their exact route key.
  - This is a viewer target-integrity and sovereignty/coherence defect, not a demonstrated authentication bypass,
    controlled-side resource-lifetime fault, local privilege escalation, root-container path, remote code
    execution, host mutation, or evidence of compromise. The user/deep-link confirmation remains the connection
    authority; the correction ensures that authority applies to the exact address the UI received.
- Implemented the smallest complete API correction:
  - Deleted `id_formatter.dart` and replaced it with `direct_address.dart`. The new
    `DirectAddressTextEditingController.address` API and `normalizeDirectAddress` name the actual authority and
    trim only surrounding whitespace. Interior whitespace remains intact so validation fails closed instead of
    synthesizing a different target.
  - Renamed the private desktop/mobile controller, focus, editing, empty/focused, and field-builder state to the
    address model. Removed the numeric-only autocomplete normalization on both platforms. The shared `connect()`
    API now accepts `address`, normalizes it once, updates the UI without a silent catch, and validates that same
    exact value before dispatch.
  - Autocomplete tiles, peer cards, and delete confirmation now render `Peer.id` verbatim when no alias is set;
    `Peer.id` remains the audited compatibility storage field whose value is the direct address. Removed the stale
    formatter import left in `server_model.dart` after `_serverId`/`fetchID` had already been deleted.
  - Extended `address_validator_test.dart` to prove outer-whitespace normalization, preservation and rejection of

## 2026-07-20 — Android outgoing-viewer exact worker completion

- Trigger, authority boundary, and confidence:
  - The reported runtime shape was Android viewer screen control hanging after the task was swiped away and the app
    relaunched, while file transfer to the same host still worked; only Android App Info → Force Stop restored screen
    control. The requested outcome was a correct resource-lifecycle repair without weakening the deliberately
    persistent foreground service, followed by commit and push to `master`.
  - Static source tracing proves a concrete lifecycle defect that exactly permits that overlap. It is a strong
    mechanism-level explanation, not a claim that the precise device sequence was reproduced under instrumentation:
    the real-device connect → swipe-away → relaunch → screen-control sequence remains required for causal runtime
    confirmation.
  - Android `MainService.onTaskRemoved` deliberately leaves the foreground service/process alive and retires only
    outgoing sessions belonging to stopped Activity owners. That behavior is correct and remains unchanged. Incoming
    listener, `MediaProjection`, capture, accessibility, notification, and service ownership are outside this patch.
- Proven old failure path:
  - Initial Flutter outgoing-session start spawned the parent viewer I/O thread and immediately dropped its
    `JoinHandle`; the `Session.thread` slot therefore did not own the initial worker at all.
  - Reconnect replaced the stored parent handle without joining it. The old source explicitly said there was “No need
    to join the previous thread,” so a new connection round could start before the previous round had completed.
  - Each outgoing video decoder and audio decoder returned/stored only its input sender while discarding the worker
    handle. Voice capture likewise retained only a stop sender. Removing the peer from the session map and sending
    `Data::Close` requested teardown but did not prove completion of the worker tree.
  - Because Android correctly preserved the foreground-service process after task removal, a stale outgoing I/O/media
    tree could survive into the relaunched Activity/isolate. File transfer uses a separate outgoing session path, so
    its continuing to work is consistent with a stale screen-session decoder/worker tree; Force Stop necessarily
    destroys the process and all such workers. This is an availability/resource-lifetime defect, not evidence of a
    host RustDesk modification, public listener, firewall change, privilege escalation, container escape, exploitation,
    or compromise.
- Source-history attribution:
  - `git blame` on the parent tree `e79a9064154277cdfd7a6471301c4d15571b480d` attributes the unretained initial
    Flutter spawn (`src/flutter.rs:1524-1528` in that tree), reconnect handle overwrite and no-join comment
    (`src/ui_session_interface.rs:1286-1298`), video-worker spawn (`src/client.rs:2352`), audio-worker spawn
    (`src/client.rs:2500`), and voice-worker spawn (`src/client/io_loop.rs:801`) to the initial fork-baseline commit
    `c2abd3b3` dated 2026-06-19. The bounded audio-channel line was later changed, but the detached handle shape was
    not. The defect therefore predates and was not created by the recent Android owner-generation repair.
- Primary lifecycle contracts used:
  - Android Activity lifecycle and process/lifecycle separation:
    https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/activity-lifecycle.
  - Android `Service.onTaskRemoved` contract:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Service#onTaskRemoved(android.content.Intent).
  - Android native codec release contract:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/MediaCodec#release().
  - Rust `JoinHandle` completion/ownership semantics:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/thread/struct.JoinHandle.html.
  - Rust bounded synchronous-channel nonblocking admission semantics:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/mpsc/struct.SyncSender.html#method.try_send.
- Implemented the smallest coherent ownership repair:
  - `Session::start_io_thread` now retains the exact initial outgoing I/O handle. `Session::reconnect` and
    `Session::close_and_join` serialize on that one worker slot, request close first, join the previous exact worker,
    and only then permit replacement/final completion. A retired owner cannot reconnect.
  - Flutter Activity/isolate retirement, generic mobile stale-owner drain, explicit FFI session close, and test cleanup
    all converge on `close_and_join`; they do not stop Android `MainService`.
  - `OwnedMediaThread` binds each outgoing video/audio channel sender to its exact decoder worker. Teardown closes
    admission first and returns the handle for a join. The existing controlled/server-side legacy audio sender API is
    deliberately unchanged rather than broadening this outgoing-viewer slice.
  - `VoiceCallThread` binds its cancellation sender to the exact voice-capture worker. Manual close and whole-session
    teardown signal first and join the worker.
  - The outgoing `Remote` gathers video, audio, and voice handles, closes their admission/cancellation edges, and joins
    them through Tokio `spawn_blocking` before marking the connection round disconnected. No lock is held across an
    `.await`; no nested Tokio runtime or `block_on` was introduced. Drop implementations remain fail-safe completion
    sinks for exceptional paths, while normal async teardown performs joins off the executor.
  - The UUID/generation ownership layer is Android-specific. Exact outgoing I/O/media completion is in the shared

    service-owned role detached a second `start_windows_service_main_ipc` runtime. Neither retained a handle or
    reported readiness, and both could call the process finalizer independently.
  - Mandatory R-A4 invariants lived in the later `start_direct_only`, so authority-bearing local IPC could bind
    before that policy proof. The retained public owner could start without knowing whether every required local
    endpoint existed, and could neither observe nor join either IPC runtime.

    R-S11e-56 through R-S11e-58 exposed but did not create the remaining inconsistent ownership.

  authorization bypass, ordinary-user-to-root escalation, remote trigger, compromise, or involvement in the
  original Android stale-session symptom.

  - Desktop startup policy is proven before any local/public listener.
  - One fallibly spawned named native worker owns one current-thread Tokio runtime created only on that new thread.
    It prepares all required local endpoints and reports one-shot readiness only after every listener guard exists.
  - The already-installed signal owner remains live during readiness. Only after readiness may one async owner spawn
    the public listener; it observes cancellation, signals, public completion, and IPC completion.
  - Local IPC drains and returns; the async owner receives the outcome, joins the public Tokio task, transfers the
    native handle to `spawn_blocking` for exact join, and only then invokes the sole non-returning finalizer.

  - Main and Windows service-main loops preserve transaction/password drains and guard release, then return

## 2026-07-19 R-S11e-57 Non-Returning Graceful-Shutdown Finalizer Ownership Slice

- Selected binding item: the four desktop callers of `server::finish_graceful_shutdown` and the lifetime transfer
  between the main desktop runtime and detached main/protected-service/Windows service-main IPC runtimes. This slice
  does not close native supervisor execution, the exact current-commit cold R-B2 artifact transaction, real-device
  mobile evidence, or independent external crypto review.
- Proven regression and responsibility: the inherited finalizer's atomic loser branch returned immediately. That was
  safe only under the older desktop topology whose parent future parked forever. Commit
  `80f2f1d6f18aebb58e5595ed2e0ce177d50a39cc` correctly added a retained desktop listener/signal owner but then called
  that returning finalizer from the Linux/Windows main server runtime. If an IPC runtime won the atomic, the new main
  caller could return through `start_direct_only`/`start_server`/`main` and terminate the process before the IPC
  winner completed its drain. The old returning line predates R-S11e-56, but the unsafe composition and regression
  were introduced by R-S11e-56.
- Classification: deterministic shutdown-finality, service-recovery, and cleanup correctness defect. It is not a
  PAKE/authentication bypass, local privilege escalation, remote task-termination primitive, or evidence of host
  compromise.
- Primary contract: Rust's standard-library thread documentation states that termination of the main thread shuts
  down the entire program even while other threads are live; `std::process::exit` is non-returning and does not run
  other threads' stack destructors. The finalizer must therefore be a terminal ownership transfer. One atomic winner
  drains and exits. There is no successful completion value for losers to receive, so every loser waits on a
  non-polling uninhabited future until the winner exits; it may not return, start a second drain, pick a second status,
  or time out independently.
- Deadlock audit: all three IPC callers drain admitted work and drop their `LocalIpcListenerGuard` before the call;
  the direct owner has observed completion or joined the exact public-listener task before the call. A waiting loser
  therefore retains no guard/task authority required by the winner's local-IPC shutdown barrier.
- Source closure: crate-private `finish_graceful_shutdown() -> !`; an atomic loser awaits
  `pending::<std::convert::Infallible>()`, while the winner follows the existing bounded session drain, local-IPC
  barrier, input cleanup, release/acquire fatal-status selection, and `process::exit`. The unused returning
  `begin_graceful_shutdown` entry is deleted. The exact caller set is three IPC paths plus one direct owner.
- Normative/regression binding: R-S11aq, Appendix C #165, shared gate `(3b-iii-d9cg)`, Apple gate `(2b-iv-a-0f)`,
  the independent semantic validator, and its source-mutation matrix bind the non-returning signature, follower wait,
  obsolete-entry absence, exact caller set, pre-call guard/join order, and drain-before-exit order. The adjacent old
  R-S11am, R-S11ap, R-S11c-27f, and R-T9 source gates were rerun; two stale R-S11c-27f assertions were synchronized
  with already-shipped R-S11am status selection and R-S11e-55's second cfg-exclusive ctrl-c handler.
- Passing evidence: pinned `rustc 1.75.0` type-checked the exact async-never/uninhabited-future expression. In
  read-only, network-disabled, UID/GID-1000, capability-dropped, no-new-privileges containers, whole-script shell and
  Python syntax passed; the semantic positive validator passed; the complete mutation matrix passed; exact shared,
  Apple, and adjacent source gates passed; native-codec normal and mutation self-tests passed with the synchronized
  requirements digest; and `git diff --check` passed. No image was built/pulled and no port, Docker socket, host PID
  namespace, or host network namespace was exposed.
- Deliberately unavailable/unclaimed: no full application compile is newly claimed. The immediately preceding slice
  already exhausted three isolated offline layouts and stopped before RustDesk on the existing root-owned unreadable
  `pin-utils` cache; no permission, ownership, image, or root authority was changed to bypass that refusal. Native
  supervisor execution and exact artifacts remain R-R2/R-B2.
- Host boundary: no host RustDesk service/process/configuration/listener, firewall, nftables/iptables state, or network
  policy was inspected or changed.
- Publication: commit `4bed2b6c9da19cedacbfa84cc32dd4c73dcd0ee8` (`Make shutdown finalizer
  non-returning`) was pushed to `origin/master`. Independent `git ls-remote` returned that exact hash; local and
  remote tree `343812fadba040e164d85e412db55a14b762632a` matched, divergence was `0 0`, and the worktree was clean.

## 2026-07-19 R-S11e-56 Desktop Controlled-Server Lifecycle Ownership Slice

- Selected binding item: the shared Linux/macOS/Windows desktop controlled-side `start_server(true)` path's process-signal, sole public-listener task, and finalizer ownership. This slice does not close native supervisor execution, the exact current-commit cold R-B2 artifact transaction, real-device mobile evidence, or independent external crypto review.
- Proven old path: `start_server(true)` admitted main IPC and the Windows service-main IPC thread before `start_direct_only(None)`. `start_direct_only` spawned `direct_server` and discarded its Tokio `JoinHandle`, then spawned and discarded a separate signal task after the listener could already begin binding, and parked the parent future forever. Signal-constructor failure returned only from the detached task; listener clean return/unwind was unobserved and could leave a false-healthy process with no public TCP service.
- History and classification: blame traces the detached listener/park to the direct-only lift and the detached signal task to R-T9; subsequent Android generation work preserved rather than introduced that topology. The defect is deterministic controlled-service availability/recovery and admitted-session stop finality, not a PAKE bypass, remote task-kill primitive, local privilege escalation, or evidence of host compromise.
- Primary contract: Tokio 1.44.2 documents that dropping a `JoinHandle` detaches its task, while awaiting the handle observes completion and `&mut JoinHandle` is cancellation-safe in `select!`. Tokio Unix and Windows signal constructors are fallible; Tokio additionally documents that an installed Unix signal disposition is not restored when the stream is dropped. The authority model therefore requires synchronous pre-admission signal construction and one retained async owner for termination, process cancellation, listener completion, exact listener join, and transfer into the existing sole finalizer.
- Source closure: desktop `start_server(true)` now constructs cfg-specific Unix SIGTERM/SIGINT or Windows Ctrl-C streams before the server-running marker, main IPC, Windows service-main IPC, or public listener. Failure exits 1 before admission. `start_direct_only` receives that owner, retains the sole listener `JoinHandle`, and selects cancellation, signal receipt/stream loss, or listener completion. Normal signals request cancellation; every normal path joins listener destruction before `finish_graceful_shutdown`. Signal-stream loss or unexpected clean/cancelled/panicked listener completion sets R-S11am's monotonic fatal latch and uses the same drain with status 1. No nested runtime, watchdog, artificial join deadline, second finalizer, or fallback was added.
- Mobile boundary: Android still receives the exact foreground-service generation, retains its generation checks and runtime-unwind teardown, and does not consume the desktop signal owner or process-global cancellation token. iOS retains the mobile signature and its existing mobile-process lifetime.
- Normative and regression binding: R-S11ap, Appendix C #164, shared gate `(3b-iii-d9cf)`, Apple gate `(2b-iv-a-0e)`, the independent semantic validator, and its source-mutation matrix bind constructor/admission order, signal types, owner transfer, exact listener retention/join, fatal classification, finalizer order, detached-task/desktop-park absence, and Android generation preservation.
- Passing evidence: in read-only, network-disabled, UID/GID-1000, capability-dropped, no-new-privileges containers, whole-script shell syntax passed; the exact shared and Apple gate sections passed; the semantic verifier's positive pass and complete source-mutation matrix passed; `git diff --check` passed; the updated requirements digest and offline native-codec source gate passed. No image was built or pulled and no port, host PID namespace, host network namespace, or Docker socket was exposed inside a container.
- Deliberately unavailable/unclaimed: the pinned Rust 1.75 image has no installed rustfmt component. Three isolated offline compile layouts stopped before RustDesk because the unprivileged build could not read the existing root-owned cached `pin-utils` source. No cache permission/ownership, capability, image, or root authority was changed to bypass that refusal. Native compile, installed-service stop/failure injection, and exact-artifact evidence are not claimed.
- Host boundary: no host RustDesk service/process/configuration/listener, firewall, nftables/iptables state, or network policy was inspected or changed.
- Publication: commit `80f2f1d6f18aebb58e5595ed2e0ce177d50a39cc` (`Own desktop controlled-server lifecycle`) was pushed to `origin/master`. Independent `git ls-remote` returned that exact hash; local and remote tree `337d997f62578c3424ff09e7e3b0470b2e36627c` matched, divergence was `0 0`, and the worktree was clean.

## 2026-07-19 R-B2 Verifier Fixture Primary-Error Preservation Slice

- Selected binding item: verifier evidence integrity under the R-B2 cleanup contract. This is a verifier source slice; it does not close the outstanding exact current-commit cold Debian/Android/Windows artifact transaction, native Windows/Apple evidence, real-device mobile lifecycle evidence, or independent external expert review.
- Old path: `ScratchRoot.directory()` performed descriptor-owned child cleanup in `finally`, but raised a changed-edge or cleanup exception directly. If the fixture body had already failed, that cleanup exception replaced the primary failure. The repeated scratch-replacement diagnostic was therefore not trustworthy evidence of the first failure.
- Reproduction: a strict non-root container using the numeric invoking UID reached `pwd.getpwuid()` without a matching passwd entry before any managed child launch. After supplying only the principal database metadata for diagnosis, the next failure occurred at same-principal `systemctl --user` access before transient-unit creation. The old context manager masked both conditions as scratch cleanup/replacement failure.
- Boundary investigation: one explicit read-only diagnostic used an AppArmor-unconfined, network-disabled, capability-dropped, no-new-privileges container to list the existing host user-bus names and observe the `systemctl --user` rejection. It did not enter the host PID namespace, create or control a unit, mutate a service, inspect or change host RustDesk state, or inspect/change firewall/listener state. No root UID or added capability was used. This diagnostic is not counted as a passing broad self-test.
- Disposition: verifier evidence-integrity defect, not a shipped RustDesk runtime defect or privilege-escalation path. `ScratchRoot.directory()` now retains any body exception, independently accumulates exact-tree, descriptor-close, and post-cleanup authority errors, and attaches the complete cleanup failure set to the primary exception. It still refuses to repair or traverse ambiguous directory edges.
- Behavioral proof: a dedicated fixture renames the live descriptor-owned child, installs an empty replacement, injects a distinct body failure, requires that exact failure to remain primary with the exact changed-edge cleanup note, and proves both recorded directory identities and inventories remain unchanged before independent reacquisition/removal.
- Environment classification: `systemd_control_environment()` now converts a missing current-principal passwd entry into an explicit `VerificationError`; it does not accept ambient `HOME` as authority.
- Source binding: the semantic verifier requires the primary-error capture/order, all three cleanup accumulator labels, cleanup reporting, behavioral note/identity/inventory proof, fixture dispatch, explicit passwd failure classification, and the normative requirements sentence. Independent mutations must reject loss of the retained primary exception, loss of cleanup-note proof/reporting, ambient-HOME fallback, fixture-dispatch removal, requirements weakening, and the hardening-ledger closure downgrade.
- Passing publication evidence: non-root, network-disabled, capability-dropped, no-new-privileges, read-only-root containers passed Python AST parsing; normal semantic verification; the exact primary/secondary-error behavior fixture; the exact missing-passwd typed-failure fixture; the independently invoked full source-mutation matrix; shell syntax; the normal dependency inventory and its 103-check self-test; and the normal native-codec watch plus its mutation self-test. The final semantic, native-ledger, and requirements-digest gates were rerun after the final wording review.

- Linux systemd/root service, `--service`, `--server`, `_service`, `_cm`, `_pa`, `_whiteboard`, `_url`, `_uinput_*`: inspected; no confirmed LPE. Runtime service lifecycle shell construction closed by R-S11c-10i in this loop.
- Windows service/LocalSystem paths, named pipes, registry/HKLM writes, token impersonation, `CreateProcess*` paths, portable service: inspected, no confirmed LPE.
- macOS LaunchDaemon/LaunchAgent, Authorization Services, AppleScript install/update/uninstall, plist/log/support paths: inspected; local helper command provenance closed by the macOS R-S11c-5 extension; no confirmed LPE.
- Android/iOS exported components and privileged-ish platform capabilities, insofar as they can cross app/service/user boundaries.

### B. Privileged Filesystem Writes And Path Ownership

Status: IN PROGRESS.

Surfaces to map:

- Config/log/support directories: desktop config path inspected; current HEAD hardens Unix mode and Windows protected DACLs.
- File transfer receive/write paths.
- FUSE/clipboard mounts and helper-created sockets/pid files.
- Symlink, hardlink, path traversal, ownership, inherited ACL/DACL, and mode transitions.

Surfaces to map:

- Any user-controlled or OS-discovered strings that reach privileged command argv or shell.

Surfaces to map:

### E. Remote-To-Local Privilege Consequences

Status: IN PROGRESS.

Surfaces to map:

## Findings

### Confirmed Current Defects Recently Closed

1. R-S11b-3i effective whole-options reads.
   - Evidence before closure: `Config::get_option()` returned `PINNED_SETTINGS` values first, but `Config::get_options()` merged `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, persisted options, and `OVERWRITE_SETTINGS` without overlaying the pinned table. Desktop UI caches, CLI `--option`, and IPC `Data::Options(None)` consume that broad map, so those paths could disagree with the security-policy funnel and could expose stale default/stored/signed-custom values for keys that the fork treats as pinned empty or pinned fixed.
   - Impact: not a service-owned password/key-pair disclosure and not a direct local-to-root path. It was a policy-funnel correctness bug on all desktop platforms: broad local reads could misrepresent controlled-side policy, including trust-anchor/proxy-shaped keys and full-access capability pins, while single-key reads and runtime security resolvers were already pinned.
   - Required model: persisted options remain scrubbed by `is_option_can_save`, but every effective read of the controlled-side option map must overlay the compile-time policy last. Absence must not be used as the representation of a pinned-empty security key.
   - Closure: `Config::get_options()` now overlays `PINNED_SETTINGS` last; `config_it` proves both single-key and whole-map reads return pinned values and that rejected writes cannot shadow them; `common::get_key_uses_pinned_anchor_and_rejects_option_override` now asserts the whole-map trust-anchor read is pinned empty; `verify.sh` gates the overlay helper; `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and the native-codec requirements hash pin are updated.
   - Status: `CLOSED / GATED`.

2. Windows service-owned main IPC close/restart action.
   - Evidence: Windows main IPC accepts a same-session same-executable peer before frame handling; `main_channel_admits_state_mutation()` admits `Data::Close` unconditionally; the handler exits the process; a normal installed executable `--server` can reach `stop_main_window_process()` and send `Data::Close` when main IPC is occupied.
   - Impact: local same-session user can trigger exit/restart of a service-owned server child through the official executable. This is availability/control-plane authority leakage, not a confirmed credential mutation or direct root/SYSTEM code execution path.
   - Required model: service-owned main IPC state-changing actions must be admitted by both transport identity and action authority. `Data::Close` should not be accepted for a service-owned receiver from an ordinary same-session same-executable peer.
   - Closure: R-S11c-13 gates main-channel `Data::Close` by receiver authority. User-owned receivers still accept user-owned close; service-owned receivers accept close only from the owning root/LocalSystem service peer. Windows main IPC now resolves the named-pipe client token for close, and Windows `_service` stops its loop only for LocalSystem.
   - Status: `CLOSED / GATED`.

### Confirmed Current Remote Capabilities, Not LPE

1. Windows terminal shell after normal RustDesk authentication.
   - Evidence: `src/server/connection.rs` terminal authorization accepts `LoginRequest.Terminal` as an authenticated-owner capability; Windows installed-service mode rejects prelogin; `fill_terminal_user_token` obtains the current logon session user token; `src/server/terminal_service.rs` launches helper mode with that user token; `src/server/terminal_helper.rs` uses `CreateProcessAsUserW` and starts the default shell inside the helper.
   - Authority model: authenticated RustDesk owner gets a shell as the active logged-in Windows user, not LocalSystem.
   - Risk: high-power intended remote capability. If the logged-in Windows account is an admin, it is that user's shell. No inspected path upgrades the shell to LocalSystem.
   - Status: `CONFIRMED INTENDED`, not a confirmed LPE.

2. Windows authenticated RDP/port-forward.
   - Evidence: `src/server/connection.rs` accepts `AuthConnType::PortForward` under the pinned tunnel policy and normalizes target addresses. The local service-owned `share_rdp` registry-setting mutation is a different `_service` IPC request.
   - Authority model: authenticated owner can use the intended tunnel path; changing service-owned RDP policy requires local elevated `_service` IPC.
   - Status: `CONFIRMED INTENDED`, not a confirmed LPE.

3. Unix terminal shell follows the serving `--server` process authority.
   - Evidence: non-Windows terminal setup uses the self-user terminal token model and spawns the PTY from the serving process authority. On Linux, root `--service` can start `--server` as the active desktop user, or as root/service authority in root/greeter/headless cases.
   - Authority model: authenticated RustDesk owner gets a shell as the user that owns the serving server process. Current requirements treat authenticated-owner terminal access as an intended high-power capability.
   - Risk: if project policy changes to "terminal must always be active logged-in user only", root/headless/prelogin server terminal would become a policy defect. Under the current policy, no hidden local-to-root IPC path was confirmed.
   - Status: `CONFIRMED INTENDED / CONCEPTUAL POLICY RISK`, not a confirmed LPE under current requirements.

### Hardening Concerns, Not Confirmed LPE

1. Windows terminal helper pipe binding.
   - Evidence before closure: `src/server/terminal_service.rs` generated UUID pipe names and launched the helper with those names. `src/server/terminal_helper.rs` created named pipes with a restricted DACL for SYSTEM plus the target user and then accepted the first client connection.
   - Closure: R-S11c-12 makes the pipes first-instance and local-only, keeps the SYSTEM-plus-target-user DACL as a transport constraint, and accepts a connected pipe client only when `GetNamedPipeClientProcessId` equals the PID returned by `CreateProcessAsUserW` for the launched helper. The old service/helper pipe-name debug log strings are gone.
   - Status: `CLOSED / GATED`, not confirmed LPE.
   - Gate: `scripts/verify.sh` asserts the helper PID query/match, expected PID wiring for both pipes, first-instance/local-only flags, absence of old pipe-name logging, and the requirements/hardening ledger disposition.
   - Build proof: `scripts/verify.sh` passed after the closure. `WINDOWS_BUILD_SOURCE=worktree OUT_DIR=/tmp/r-s11c12-windows-build-final scripts/build-windows-vm.sh` completed both Windows VM passes and asserted R-B2 A==B determinism; canonicalized hashes: `rustdesk-setup.exe` `d2c26840e00d81d5fb2404d543792f9fd34e78ac495fe5c0c08b2858d4e787e3`, `rustdesk.msi` `81bf5d7038e63d490f8eee89088712d062eee1b28080e2605d9d8ce710521ef9`.

2. macOS privileged app-bundle verification/adoption path.
   - Evidence before closure: `src/platform/privileges_scripts/install.scpt` and `update.scpt` rejected symlinks and then ran path-based `find`, `chown -R`, `chmod -R`, and `ditto` over `/Applications/RustDesk.app` / source paths. The live install path could turn an active-user-writable app bundle into the root-launched service path during an admin-authorized script; the dormant update path could copy a caller-supplied source directory into that service root if reconnected.
   - Preconditions before closure: local attacker can mutate the app bundle or update source around the admin-authorized install/update window.
   - Impact before closure: root LaunchDaemon could execute attacker-controlled service code if the app bundle/source was attacker-mutated before being adopted as root-owned service state.
   - Closure: commit `1f2c571fdef64c6735f295672dca94e1bf86aaa8` points the root service at `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.carriez.rustdesk_service` with a root-owned support working directory; `install.scpt` no longer chowns `/Applications/RustDesk.app`, no longer trusts an app-bundle service path, and requires the helper directory/executable to be already `root:wheel`, non-symlink, non-group/world-writable, ACL-free, and executable before and immediately before `launchctl load`.
   - Status: `CLOSED / GATED`.
   - Gate: `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` and `scripts/verify.sh` now assert the helper path, helper ownership/mode/ACL checks, helper re-verification before load, absence of app-bundle root service execution, and absence of the deleted updater surface.

3. macOS launcher used non-absolute command names for some local helpers.
   - Evidence before closure: `src/platform/macos.rs` invoked `osascript`, `launchctl`, `open`, `ls`, and `ioreg` by name in local UI/CLI/helper flows, while the privileged AppleScript bodies used absolute paths internally.
   - Preconditions: attacker controls the RustDesk process environment/PATH before a local user/admin invokes install/update/uninstall/helper launch.
   - Impact: same-user command substitution or prompt spoofing risk; no confirmed root command execution because the privileged script bodies themselves used absolute command paths.
   - Closure: `src/platform/macos.rs` now uses fixed paths for `osascript`, `launchctl`, `open`, and `ioreg`, and `src/ipc.rs` uses a fixed path for the macOS reopen `open` call. Active-console identity no longer parses `ls /dev/console`; it reads `/dev/console` ownership and resolves username/home through `getpwuid_r`. `launchctl asuser` fails closed if no console UID is resolvable.
   - Status: `CLOSED / GATED`, not confirmed LPE.
   - Gate: `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` and `scripts/verify.sh` assert absence of path-selected macOS helper/reopen `Command::new("...")` in `src/platform/macos.rs` and `src/ipc.rs`, presence of fixed system paths, `/dev/console` ownership lookup, `getpwuid_r`, and the no-empty-UID launch gate.

4. macOS service-owned password authorization form is generic and not payload-bound.
   - Evidence before closure: `src/platform/macos.rs` created and verified an Authorization Services external form; `src/ipc.rs` accepted the form on `_service` and then committed a service-owned password change through the root service. The form proved admin authorization, but was not nonce/action/password-bound at the Rust IPC layer.
   - Closure: commit `a547a1f580477bba27347e9d81abdbfba37107dd` replaced the one-shot request with a begin/challenge/finish exchange. Commit `2244f4688f0fda9c0e65c67770e92637d831572e` removes the misleading digest-confirmation design entirely: the LaunchDaemon stores the proposed password in a bounded, TTL-expiring, same-peer pending request, the UI obtains an action-only Authorization Services external form for the RustDesk admin right, finish carries only request id plus authorization, and the LaunchDaemon commits only the stored pending value after noninteractive right verification.
   - Status: `CLOSED / GATED`, not confirmed LPE.
   - Gate: `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` and `scripts/verify.sh` assert the begin/challenge/finish flow, explicit right creation, same-peer bounded pending request, TTL expiry, pending-value zero-on-drop, finish-without-password, admin-auth failure cancellation, absence of digest prompt/API helpers, main IPC denial, and service-owned final commit path.

5. Dormant macOS `update.scpt` is powerful if future code re-wires it.
   - Evidence before closure: `src/platform/macos.rs::update_daemon_agent` and `src/platform/privileges_scripts/update.scpt` could admin-authorized-copy a caller-supplied source directory into `/Applications/RustDesk.app`; search found no reachable caller, and comments said the old DMG self-updater cluster was excised.
   - Closure: commit `1f2c571fdef64c6735f295672dca94e1bf86aaa8` deletes `update.scpt`, `update_daemon_agent`, `.rustdeskupdate-*` helpers, and startup cleanup of the old temp update directory. Source gates assert they stay absent.
   - Status: `CLOSED / GATED`, not current LPE.

6. Windows privileged command/package residuals.
   - The application-side EXE installer, generated command files, custom service/firewall actions, and runtime broker
     updater elevation path are closed by R-S11e-20 below. Remote SAS handling still intentionally writes and restores
     HKLM `SoftwareSASGeneration`; its separate resource/concurrency finding remains open. Enterprise MSI transforms
     remain outside the shipped package policy and must not redirect service payloads to a user-writable root.
   - Status: `INSTALLATION AUTHORITY CLOSED`; separate SAS and transform-policy residuals remain.

7. macOS privileged helper trust is ownership/mode based, not signature-explicit in the script.
   - Evidence: the install script checks the privileged helper is already root-owned, non-symlink, non-group/world-writable, ACL-free, and executable before loading the LaunchDaemon.
   - Risk: planting or modifying such a helper already requires admin/root-equivalent authority, so this is not a current LPE. A signature check would make the intended trust boundary explicit.
   - Status: `CONCEPTUAL RESIDUAL`, not confirmed LPE.

### Disproven Or Stale Findings On Current HEAD

1. Windows same-session local process to service-owned password/RDP mutation.
   - Evidence: Windows `_service` IPC admits active-session/SYSTEM current-exe peers, but `src/ipc.rs::windows_peer_is_authorized_for_service_owned_request` re-checks the actual pipe client token with `ImpersonateNamedPipeClient` and requires elevation before service-owned password or `share_rdp` changes.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN`.

2. Windows forged service-owned password commit through main IPC.
   - Evidence: service-owned commit requires the receiver to be service-owned and the main-IPC peer to be `WindowsLocalSystemPeer`; this is checked via named-pipe impersonation and SID `S-1-5-18`.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN`.

3. Windows inherited-AppData-only config ACL.
   - Evidence: current `libs/hbb_common/src/config.rs` has `windows_config_acl_sddl`, prepares config parent directories before store, hardens final files after store, applies `DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION | PROTECTED_DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION`, and tests `windows_config_acl_sddl_is_protected_owner_system_only`. `scripts/verify.sh` gates these checks.
   - Status: `STALE/DISPROVEN`.

4. Desktop `_cm` fixed-path endpoint selection.
   - Evidence: current `src/server/connection.rs` uses authenticated CM selection on Linux/macOS/Windows. Linux checks UID, expected mode, parent/process identity, and launch token; macOS checks current executable/expected mode and then performs launch-token HMAC proof before stream readiness; Windows checks the named-pipe server PID for the current executable/expected `--cm` mode and performs the same launch-token proof before any `Data::Login` or `cm_auth_token` disclosure. Windows CM launch paths pass the token environment, and Windows clipboard/privacy server clients use the same authenticated `_cm` connector. The old Flutter theme/language notification side-channel no longer opens `_cm` directly. `scripts/verify.sh` fails raw Linux/macOS/Windows `_cm` fallback reintroduction and the deleted theme/language `_cm` notification channel; `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` mirrors the macOS source assertions.
   - Status: `CLOSED/GATED`.

5. Whiteboard ambient fixed-path helper.
   - Evidence: current `src/whiteboard/client.rs` generates a per-launch token, derives `_whiteboard_<hmac-suffix>`, authenticates the endpoint before sending bind/event/close data, and uses per-connection event tokens. `src/whiteboard/server.rs` checks parent PID, current executable, mutual launch proof, and per-connection tokens. `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` gate absence of fixed `_whiteboard` listener/raw connect and legacy tuple messages.
   - Status: `STALE/DISPROVEN`.

6. macOS AppleScript argument shell injection into plist writes.
   - Evidence: Rust passes arguments to `osascript`; AppleScript uses `quoted form of` for shell interpolation; privileged script commands use absolute paths; plist XML is written as data to fixed launchd paths, not evaluated as shell.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN`.

7. macOS LaunchDaemon/LaunchAgent attacker-selected program path.
   - Evidence: current `daemon.plist` fixes `ProgramArguments` to `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.carriez.rustdesk_service`; current `agent.plist` fixes `ProgramArguments` to `/Applications/RustDesk.app/Contents/MacOS/RustDesk --server --service-owned-server`; `install.scpt` verifies the privileged helper is already root-owned, non-symlink, non-group/world-writable, ACL-free, and executable before loading the LaunchDaemon; `update.scpt` is deleted.
   - Status: `STALE/DISPROVEN` for the old app-bundle LaunchDaemon claim; closed/gated by `1f2c571fdef64c6735f295672dca94e1bf86aaa8`.

8. macOS `_service` as arbitrary local privileged bus.
   - Evidence: `_service` peer authorization requires root or fresh active console UID plus current-executable/same-bundle checks; service-channel allowlist admits only `Test` plus typed Linux/macOS service-owned password request messages; ordinary main-channel service-owned password/config writes are denied.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN`.

9. macOS service-owned password skips admin authorization.
   - Evidence: current macOS uses a begin/challenge/finish `_service` flow. The root LaunchDaemon stores the proposed password in a bounded, TTL-expiring, same-peer pending request; finish carries only request id plus the RustDesk-specific Authorization Services external form; the LaunchDaemon verifies the right noninteractively and then commits the stored value through the root-service final commit path into a service-owned main server.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN`.

10. macOS install/update/uninstall hidden remote protocol trigger.
    - Evidence: install/update/uninstall are local UI/CLI flows; no server connection handler or IPC arm dispatches privileged AppleScript flows. A remote authenticated controller could interact with visible UI like a user, but no hidden protocol action was found.
    - Status: `DISPROVEN`.

### Linux/Debian Current State

Dedicated Linux/Debian subagent completed read-only audit with no confirmed unprivileged-local-user-to-root path and no direct normal-remote-auth-to-local-privileged-operation path.

1. Linux `_service` password path.
   - Evidence: `_service` channel only admits `Test` and `RequestServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange`; Linux request verifies peer authorization and calls `/usr/bin/pkcheck --action-id com.carriez.RustDesk.set-unattended-password --process <pid,start_time,uid> --allow-user-interaction`; policy file uses `auth_admin`; final commit is root service to service-owned main IPC.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN` as unauthenticated local root escalation; this is the intended local admin/root gate.

2. Linux config/PRS at rest.
   - Evidence: Unix `store_path` uses `confy::store_path_perms(..., 0o600)` and `scripts/verify.sh` behavior-tests owner-only mode. Password storage derives and stores PRS/h1 material, not plaintext.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN` as local root escalation. Local read of protected config is endpoint compromise/connect-equivalent, not root escalation by itself.

3. Linux runtime service lifecycle shell strings.
   - Evidence before fix: `src/platform/linux.rs::run_cmds_status` used `/bin/sh -c`; `switch_service` built `cp -f ...; systemctl enable/disable/start/stop ...` shell text. Release custom app names appeared signed/release-bundled rather than runtime local-user supplied, so no ordinary-local-user exploit was confirmed.
   - Fix: `src/platform/linux.rs` now selects only trusted fixed `/usr/bin/systemctl` or `/bin/systemctl` candidates, invokes service lifecycle actions through direct argv, and migrates user config with native filesystem calls. Source config files and destination files are checked with `symlink_metadata`, the service config dir is hardened to `0700`, and copied config files are hardened to `0600`.
   - Gate: `scripts/verify.sh` R-S11c-10i runs the service lifecycle unit tests and source gate. `scripts/verify.sh` passed after the fix.
   - Status: `CLOSED/GATED`, not a confirmed prior LPE.

4. Debian package scripts.
   - Evidence before fix: `res/DEBIAN/preinst`/`postinst`/`prerm` parsed `/proc/1/exe` through `ls|awk`, called `service`/`systemctl` directly, sed-patched the installed unit, and used broad `ps|grep|awk` user-service detection plus unquoted `systemctl --machine=${serverUser}@.host --user stop rustdesk`; `res/rustdesk.service` had broad `ExecStop=pkill -f "rustdesk --"` and `KillMode=mixed`.
   - Fix: `res/DEBIAN/*` now use `deb-systemd-helper` for enable/disable/purge state and `deb-systemd-invoke` for stop/start/daemon-reload, with `init-system-helpers` declared in `build.py`. `res/rustdesk.service` no longer has `ExecStop`/`pkill` and uses `KillMode=control-group` with `TimeoutStopSec=30`. `src/platform/linux.rs` now SIGTERMs the managed `--server` child and waits eight seconds before forcing it, so local supervisor restarts do not bypass the R-T9 drain.
   - Gate: `scripts/verify.sh` R-S11c-10j/R-T9 asserts the helper-layer maintainer scripts, the `.deb` dependency, absence of raw init/systemctl/process-table/package stop leftovers, absence of legacy unit `ExecStop`/`pkill`/`KillMode=mixed`, and SIGTERM-first Linux supervisor child shutdown. `scripts/verify.sh` passed after the fix.
   - Status: `CLOSED/GATED`, not a confirmed prior arbitrary-root-code path.

5. Linux IPC parent directory and stale socket/pid handling.
   - Evidence: `src/ipc/fs.rs` opens parent dirs with `O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW`, checks type/owner/mode with `fstat`, uses `0711` for service parent and `0700` for non-service, refuses to adopt foreign-owned service parent, removes/recreates via grandparent fd, uses fd-relative `fstatat(..., AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`/`unlinkat` cleanup, and opens pid files with `O_NOFOLLOW`, regular-file ownership checks, and mode `0600`.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN` as symlink/foreign-owner local root escalation.

6. Linux systemd unit as privilege surface.
   - Evidence: `res/rustdesk.service` runs `/usr/bin/rustdesk --service` as root by design and includes confinement/resource limits.
   - Status: root service is expected; no unit-alone LPE found. The broad `ExecStop=pkill -f "rustdesk --"`/`KillMode=mixed` concern is closed by R-S11c-10j.

7. Debian maintainer scripts as unprivileged-user-to-root path.
   - Evidence: scripts operate on fixed privileged paths and systemd commands. No unprivileged-controlled root command/path input found under normal Debian permissions.
   - Status: `DISPROVEN` as ordinary local-user LPE; package-script raw service/process discovery and quoting concern closed by R-S11c-10j.

8. Linux `run_as_user` drop path.
   - Evidence before fix: used bare `Command::new("sudo")` for the root-to-user drop and for the `sudo -E` environment-preservation probe. This was argv-based, not shell injection, but helper executable provenance still came from the service process environment.
   - Fix: `src/platform/linux.rs` now resolves `sudo`, `env`, `sh`, `w`, `xrandr`, `xdg-screensaver`, and `systemctl` only from trusted fixed `/usr/bin`/`/bin` candidates that are root-owned and not group/world-writable; `sudo` and fallback `env` fail closed when no trusted fixed path exists; sudo env keys are validated for both branches; `--cm` detection uses `/proc` current-exe argv matching; X11 display fallback reads `/tmp/.X11-unix` socket metadata/passwd ownership instead of parsing `ls`.
   - Status: `CLOSED/GATED` as shell injection and privileged helper PATH-selection surface.

9. Polkit policy semantics outside code.
   - Evidence: code-side `/usr/bin/pkcheck` is fail-closed, uses process subject, and requests local interaction. The policy/rules deployment and distro-local overrides remain external configuration facts.
   - Status: `UNRESOLVED ENVIRONMENT/POLICY TRACKING`; no code-side LPE confirmed.

10. Direct remote trigger of local privileged Linux/Debian action.
    - Evidence: privileged service-owned password operation is local IPC plus local polkit; `_service` rejects all other messages; no remote protocol bridge to package lifecycle/polkit/config-root operation found in inspected files.
    - Status: `DISPROVEN` for direct remote protocol trigger. Authenticated remote desktop capabilities still act as the controlled session by design.

11. Linux `--server` tray cleanup process selection.
    - Evidence before fix: Linux `core_main.rs` entered `--server`, then invoked `Command::new("pkill").arg("-f").arg("<app> --tray")`. In installed service paths, a root `--service` can launch root or user `--server` processes depending on desktop/headless state, so `--server` startup must not rely on a PATH-selected process killer or substring process matching.
    - Fix: `src/core_main.rs` now calls `platform::stop_tray_processes()`; `src/platform/linux.rs` selects only `/proc` entries whose `exe` symlink equals the current executable and whose argv contains exact `--tray`, then sends SIGTERM. `scripts/verify.sh` gates this source shape and rejects `Command::new("pkill")` / `pkill -f` in the Linux service/tray cleanup sources.
    - Verification: `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`, `git diff --check`, focused Dockerized `cargo test --lib --features linux-pkg-config r_s11c10_process_kill`, and full `scripts/verify.sh` passed.
    - Status: `CLOSED/GATED` as Linux root/service helper command provenance and process-selection surface.

  - The begin message now carries the proposed password to the LaunchDaemon, which stores it in a bounded same-peer pending request and zeroes it on drop.
  - The finish message now carries only request id plus authorization; it cannot replace the value after admin authorization.
  - The pending request expires automatically, and UI-side authorization failure sends an empty-authorization finish to consume the pending request immediately.

## R-S11d work log — Windows installer service-root authority

- Finding:
  - Windows EXE install accepted a caller-provided install path from the Flutter desktop path picker / `install_me(path)`.
  - That path was then used as the installed service binary root for `sc create ... binpath=`, so an unelevated same-user-selected or caller-controlled directory could become the persistent LocalSystem service executable location after elevation.
  - EXE elevated command staging used predictable `{app}_{tip}.bat` / VBS paths in temp-like locations and launched `cmd.exe` by name.
  - MSI exposed install-directory selection/public property routing and kept shell fallbacks for privileged service/registry operations.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: resolves the default service install root from Program Files via `SHGetKnownFolderPath`; rejects non-default service install paths; uses the fixed service root from `install_me`, `install_service`, and `run_after_install`; resolves elevated `cmd.exe` via `GetSystemDirectoryW`; stages random command/VBS files with `create_new` and a live read-only handle that denies write/delete sharing while elevated children consume them; makes EXE `sc` service-creation errors fatal to the elevated command marker.
  - `flutter/lib/desktop/pages/install_page.dart`: removes the Windows custom install path picker and calls install with an empty path so the fixed service root is used.
  - `res/msi/**`: replaces public install-folder routing with private `App.InstallFolder` under `ProgramFiles6432Folder`; removes browse/change-folder UI path.
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp`, `res/msi/CustomActions/ServiceUtils.cpp`, `res/msi/Package/Fragments/CustomActions.wxs`: removes `sc`/`cmd.exe`/`reg` shell fallbacks from service creation/deletion and SAS registry setup; makes service create/start/stop/delete and SAS registry setup checked MSI actions; verifies stale service deletion; fixes the native `RegSetValueExW` DWORD pointer; returns MSI failure on native registry/service errors.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, `scripts/verify.sh`: add R-S11d requirement, ledger entry, and source gate.
- Verification status:
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: passed all gates (`VERIFY: all gates green`).
  - `WINDOWS_BUILD_SOURCE=worktree OUT_DIR=/tmp/r-s11d-windows-build scripts/build-windows-vm.sh`: completed.
  - Windows double-build determinism: `rustdesk-setup.exe` `070dfe4b4224cae5a26b1ce93302dda5b0840597527b363c0ba2edfbca3d4159`, `rustdesk.msi` `10f8eac78f4cb40608fd877a9d401074b2d0bfa461e603897cef6e128be18766`.
- Commit/push:
  - `c1d4affe47e089d7592331728858b0a31ea56c93` (`Harden Windows installer service authority`) pushed to `origin/master`.

## R-S11c-13 work log — service-owned IPC close authority

- Finding:
  - Service-owned main IPC treated `Data::Close` as an unconditional accepted message. On Windows, a normal same-session installed executable could reach the service-owned `--server` main IPC through transport identity and request receiver exit/restart.
  - Windows `_service` also treated `Data::Close` as a service-loop stop after transport authorization, leaving the same service-control action shape dependent on same-session/current-executable identity if a sender path were reintroduced.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc.rs`: `Data::Close` is receiver-authorized. User-owned receivers keep user-owned close; service-owned receivers require root/LocalSystem peer authority. Windows main IPC resolves the pipe client token for `Data::Close` before applying the policy table.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: Windows `_service` close now stops the service loop only when the pipe client token is LocalSystem; ordinary or unverifiable callers are rejected.
  - `src/server.rs`: removed the stale comment that normalized killing another `--server` because service restart would repair it.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `scripts/verify.sh`: document and gate the R-S11c-13 closure, including absence of an unconditional `Data::Close` bucket.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - Dockerized focused test `cargo test --lib --features linux-pkg-config ipc::test::main_channel_rejects_untyped_state_mutations --color never`: passed.
  - Direct host `cargo test` was not accepted as evidence because the host build environment hit target-directory permissions first and then missing `x11.pc`; Docker verifier supplied the clean repo environment.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: passed all gates (`VERIFY: all gates green`).
- Commit/push:

## R-S11d-1 work log — Windows Amyuni IDD helper launch provenance

- Finding:
  - The MSI `RemoveAmyuniIdd` deferred non-impersonated custom action built and checked an absolute `usbmmidd_v2\deviceinstaller64.exe` path but launched the bare helper name with `ShellExecuteW(..., exe, ..., workDir, ...)`.
  - The runtime Amyuni virtual-display helper performed the same split in Rust: it checked `current_exe()/usbmmidd_v2/deviceinstaller64.exe`, then called ANSI `ShellExecuteA` with a bare `deviceinstaller64.exe` filename and the helper directory as working directory.
  - This was a provenance defect in privileged/service contexts even though no confirmed current low-privilege-to-SYSTEM path was proven: the checked object and executed object were not structurally the same argument.
- Design:
  - The working directory is not executable identity. The privileged caller must pass the exact helper path it resolved and checked as the `lpFile`/program path.
  - This matches the Windows ShellExecute contract and Rust process guidance: relative program paths plus working-directory behavior are not a security boundary and should be replaced by an absolute program path.
- Implemented:
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp`: `RemoveAmyuniIdd` now verifies `usbmmidd_v2` is a directory, verifies the helper path is a file, logs the absolute helper path, and calls `ShellExecuteW` with `exePath`.
  - `src/virtual_display_manager.rs`: runtime Amyuni helper lookup now returns both wide-string work directory and absolute executable path, and `install_if_x86_on_x64` calls `ShellExecuteW` with `paths.exe_path`; the old ANSI bare-name `ShellExecuteA` path is removed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: add R-S11d-1 gates and disposition.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.

## R-S11d-2 work log — Windows Amyuni IDD cleanup completion authority

- Finding:
  - After R-S11d-1 bound the checked helper path to the executed helper path, the MSI `RemoveAmyuniIdd` deferred non-impersonated custom action still declared `Return="ignore"`.
  - It launched `usbmmidd_v2\deviceinstaller64.exe remove usbmmidd` asynchronously through `ShellExecuteW` and only logged launch failure, so uninstall/update could silently proceed after a privileged cleanup failure.
  - The same custom-action source also retained stale bare-`netsh` `ShellExecuteW` firewall helper examples and a commented reactivation block.
- Design:
  - Amyuni remains an optional payload: if the helper directory is absent, MSI cleanup is a no-op.
  - Once the privileged action finds the installed helper executable, cleanup has completion authority: launch failure, timeout, exit-code read failure, and nonzero helper exit are custom-action failures. The checked absolute helper path is the `CreateProcessW` application path; the working directory is not executable identity.
  - Dormant privileged shell examples are deleted rather than preserved as future reactivation templates.
- Implemented:
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp`: `RemoveAmyuniIdd` now composes a mutable command line for the checked `exePath`, starts it with `CreateProcessW(exePath, ...)`, waits on the process handle with a bounded timeout, reads the exit code, fails closed on launch/wait/exit-code/nonzero failures, and closes child handles on all paths.
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp`: removed the unused bare-`netsh` `ShellExecuteW` firewall helper functions and their commented call path.
  - `res/msi/Package/Fragments/CustomActions.wxs`: `RemoveAmyuniIdd` is now `Return="check"`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11d-2 source gates and disposition.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.

  - Windows canonicalized hashes: `rustdesk-setup.exe` `d00d523c51a58c27d58ac99403db673c710383be6716adaaeb5c10add882a75e`, `rustdesk.msi` `dcc233d5b443113e774508102493e72bffe7dc9d96a5c3e1d37fe0e90eef0e5f`.

## Residual audit leads carried forward after R-S11d-2

- Windows:
  - No current proven Windows low-privilege-to-SYSTEM path remains from the Amyuni helper launch/cleanup class after R-S11d-1/R-S11d-2.
  - Remaining Windows privileged installer/action review should continue looking for other elevated child-process and cleanup surfaces whose success is not observed, especially deferred MSI actions still marked `Return="ignore"` where the action owns privileged state.
- macOS:
  - The service-owned unattended-password Authorization Services flow now requires the RustDesk-specific admin right without claiming OS-level digest binding. The value being committed is bound by LaunchDaemon-owned pending storage: begin stores the proposed value, finish carries authorization only, and the LaunchDaemon commits only the stored pending value after right verification.
  - Explicit privileged-helper identity/signature verification remains a packaging hardening candidate, not a currently proven local privilege escalation by itself.
- Linux:
  - `src/platform/linux.rs` command provenance was closed for service/root helper paths in R-S11c-10k/R-S11c-10l, but shared helpers in `libs/hbb_common/src/platform/linux.rs` still deserve a separate command-provenance audit because common helpers historically exposed `which`/bare-command fallback patterns.
  - Debian maintainer scripts and systemd sandboxing should be reviewed as separate packaging slices for PATH-selected helpers and unnecessary service privileges.

## R-S11c-10m work log — Linux shared helper command provenance

- Finding:
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/platform/linux.rs` retained the pre-hardened command-resolution pattern after the root/service helpers in `src/platform/linux.rs` were already closed: `find_cmd_path()` fell back to `which` and then a bare command name, `run_cmds`/`run_cmds_trim_newline` exposed a public `sh -c` API, and `run_loginctl()` had a `flatpak-spawn --host` branch even though the fork's Linux target is the `.deb` + systemd model.
  - `system_message()` selected `notify-send`/`zenity`/`kdialog`/`xmessage` through PATH, and the Linux service-uninstall reopen path still used shell sequencing (`sleep ...; exec ...`) plus shell quoting.
  - The read-only explorer found no current local privilege escalation in the already-edited working tree, but confirmed the privileged/service reachability for the old `loginctl` and crash-notification helpers and recommended verifier coverage for the removed shell/PATH shapes.
- Design:
  - Shared Linux helpers that can be reached from service/root contexts do not select programs through ambient PATH, `which`, Flatpak host spawning, bare command names, generic shell strings, or shell quoting.
  - Helper program identity is a fixed absolute candidate whose executable is root-owned and not group/world-writable. Dynamic values remain argv elements, not command text.
  - The delayed reopen path is an internal argv-only mode and fails closed before taking action on malformed or out-of-range delay values.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/platform/linux.rs`: deleted `find_cmd_path`, `CMD_LOGINCTL`, `CMD_PS`, `CMD_SH`, `run_cmds`, `run_cmds_trim_newline`, and `shell_quote`; added fixed candidate sets for `loginctl` and notification helpers; added `trusted_fixed_executable`/`trusted_command_path`; removed `flatpak-spawn`; changed `run_loginctl` and `system_message` to fixed-path argv execution only.
  - `src/platform/linux.rs` and `src/core_main.rs`: replaced shell-based delayed reopen with `--reopen-after-service-stop <seconds>` and an internal receiver that rejects malformed and over-30-second values.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `scripts/verify.sh`: added R-S11c-10m disposition and gates; removed stale shared-helper shell documentation; marked the older BR-1 headless-CM finding as superseded instead of present-tense broken behavior.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.

## R-S11c-10n work log — Linux headless CM uid lookup

- Finding:
  - `src/server/connection.rs` resolved the Linux headless `--cm-no-ui` launch uid by running `Command::new("id").arg("-u").arg(&username)`.

  - The explorer confirmed the relevant privileged context is the installed service's root-owned `--server` child or a manual root `--server`; the top-level `--service` process does not run this branch. Unauthenticated remote peers cannot reach it; a CPace-authenticated peer can cause CM bootstrap but cannot choose PATH or username.
- Design:
  - Do not harden `id` with `--` or fixed paths when structured account data is already available.
  - Resolve the uid through `hbb_common::users::get_user_by_name` and carry the returned uid into the existing CM launcher shape.
  - Because NSS/passwd lookup can block, perform the lookup on a Tokio blocking worker and do not hold the desktop-manager mutex across the await.
- Implemented:
  - `src/server/connection.rs`: added Linux-only `uid_for_username(username: &str) -> ResultType<String>`, using `hbb_common::tokio::task::spawn_blocking` and `hbb_common::users::get_user_by_name(&lookup_name).map(|user| user.uid())`.
  - `src/server/connection.rs`: replaced the old `id -u` subprocess block in the `headless_cm` branch with `uid_for_username(&username).await?`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11c-10n source gates and disposition.

## R-S11c-10o work log — Linux clipboard FUSE stale unmount provenance

- Finding:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs` prepared the Linux clipboard FUSE mount directory through `/tmp` anchoring, no-follow `openat`, current-euid ownership checks, and `0755` mode enforcement, but then cleared a stale mount by running `std::process::Command::new("umount").arg(mount_point).status()`.
  - The path was fixed under `/tmp/<app>/cliprdr-{client,server}` and passed as argv, so this was not shell injection and not remotely chosen command text.
  - The read-only explorer confirmed this path is Linux-only, reachable only after authenticated file-clipboard/file-transfer capability paths, and runs with the euid of the viewer/server process. In ordinary user-owned viewer/server contexts the old defect was same-user PATH-selected execution; in root/headless service-owned `--server` contexts it was a potential local root command-provenance issue if the root server's PATH were attacker-influenced. It was not remote LPE by itself.
- Design at the time:
  - Do not replace `umount` with a fixed candidate helper or fallback chain when the Linux kernel operation is directly available.
  - Preserve the existing best-effort stale-mount cleanup shape: "not mounted" remains non-fatal, unexpected unmount failures are logged, and the following `spawn_mount2` remains the real fail-closed mount authority.
  - Keep no-follow semantics on the final path operation by using `umount2(..., UMOUNT_NOFOLLOW)`.
  - Superseded by R-S11c-10r: startup stale cleanup still tries no-follow `umount2`, but fixed-helper unmount fallback
    is now the correct non-root FUSE teardown path because RustDesk owns the fd-passing mount instead of fuser's
    `spawn_mount2` mount guard.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs`: added `fuse_mount_path_cstring` and `unmount_stale_fuse_mount`, replaced the PATH-selected `umount` subprocess with direct `libc::umount2(mount_c.as_ptr(), libc::UMOUNT_NOFOLLOW)`, treated `EINVAL`/`ENOENT` as expected "no stale mount" cleanup, and added a NUL-path regression test.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added R-S11c-10o positive/negative gates for the syscall wrapper, NUL-path test, docs/status disposition, and absence of `Command::new("umount")`; tightened R-D3a wording gates so the systemd mount syscall allowance is documented as direct FUSE syscall scope rather than helper execution.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, `libs/clipboard/README.md`, and `res/rustdesk.service`: documented the closure and deleted stale "call the umount program" / "legacy FUSE mount" wording.

## R-S11d-5 work log — Windows EXE elevated batch command provenance

- Finding:
  - R-S11d fixed the EXE install root, command-file staging, and the outer elevated `cmd.exe` path, but the generated elevated batch bodies still invoked external tools by bare name.
  - Affected elevated EXE batch fragments included `chcp`, `reg`, `netsh`, `sc`, `taskkill`, `cscript`, `XCOPY`, `timeout`, and prior-MSI `MsiExec.exe` handoffs.
  - This is UAC-boundary command provenance, not a no-interaction SYSTEM LPE: the user still has to approve RustDesk's elevated installer flow. Once consent is given, however, the privileged installer must not let the elevated shell resolve service, registry, firewall, process, shortcut, or copy tools from caller current-directory/PATH state.
- Research/design:
  - Microsoft `CreateProcessW` documentation says a command without a directory path is searched through the application directory, current directory, System32, Windows, then PATH, and calls out ambiguous process creation as a security risk.
  - Correct model for this slice: the elevated EXE batch body may still be the existing fail-closed staged command surface, but every external system tool it invokes is resolved from `GetSystemDirectoryW`, checked for existence, and quoted before formatting the batch. Built-in `cmd` operations remain built-ins.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: added `trusted_system_tool_path`, `quoted_batch_path`, and `WindowsSystemTools`.
  - `WindowsSystemTools::resolve()` binds `chcp.com`, `cscript.exe`, `msiexec.exe`, `netsh.exe`, `reg.exe`, `sc.exe`, `taskkill.exe`, `timeout.exe`, and `xcopy.exe` to checked quoted `System32` paths.
  - Threaded the tool set through broker update, bulk copy, install, uninstall, service install/uninstall, prior-MSI uninstall handoff, service creation, shortcut-script execution, registry/firewall/SAS setup, and debug timeout fragments.
  - Prior MSI uninstall strings beginning with bare `MsiExec.exe` are rewritten to the trusted `System32\msiexec.exe` path before entering the elevated batch.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11d-5 gates/status/disposition.
- Residual deliberately not folded into this slice:
  - VBS shortcut creation still stages predictable `.lnk` filenames under the user temp path before elevated copy into public/all-users destinations. With `cscript.exe` provenance closed, that is a separate shortcut staging/finalization question, not the same command-search issue. It should be audited as its own slice if a privilege/persistence boundary proof is found.

## R-S11d-6 work log — Windows EXE shortcut finalization provenance

- Finding:
  - After R-S11d-5 bound the elevated batch tools to `System32`, the EXE installer and service-install path still created predictable `.lnk` files under the caller's temp directory.
  - Elevated batch code then copied those temp-created shortcuts into protected/all-users destinations: Public Desktop, Common Programs Start Menu, Common Startup, and the Program Files install directory.
  - This is not a remote issue and still requires the user-approved elevated installer flow. The defect is local shortcut-object provenance: a caller-writable staging path must not become the authority source for elevated all-users shortcut or startup persistence.
- Research/design:
  - Microsoft's shell API exposes the protected/all-users locations through `SHGetKnownFolderPath`; those roots should be resolved structurally instead of spelled through environment variables such as `%PUBLIC%` or `%PROGRAMDATA%`.
  - Microsoft's WSH shortcut API supports creating a shortcut at the final `CreateShortcut` path. The elevated command should create the final shortcut directly, not create a temp `.lnk` and copy it later.
  - VBS command files remain the existing installer mechanism, but their script literals must fail closed for quote/CR/LF rather than silently embedding malformed paths.

  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: added `known_folder_path`, `common_programs_dir`, `common_startup_dir`, and `public_desktop_dir` around `SHGetKnownFolderPath`.

## R-S11d-7 work log — Windows MSI firewall/Amyuni completion authority

- Finding:
  - `AddFirewallRules` and `RemoveFirewallRules` were deferred non-impersonated MSI custom actions that changed privileged Windows Firewall policy, but WiX declared them `Return="ignore"` and the custom-action DLL discarded the helper result.
  - The firewall helper added inbound then outbound rules while overwriting the inbound result with the outbound result; removal issued two blind removes while overwriting the first result. MSI could therefore report success with partial or stale firewall policy.
  - `RemoveAmyuniIdd` had a checked helper fallback after R-S11d-2, but the native SetupAPI `UninstallDriver` path still returned `void`, skipped hardware-ID/class-installer/remove failures, and could not prove that the present `usbmmidd` device was absent or removed.
- Design:
  - Treat privileged MSI firewall policy and driver cleanup as completion-authoritative operations: success means final state is proven; any unproven state fails MSI unless a checked fallback proves success.
  - Firewall add must remove stale same-name rules first, create both inbound and outbound rules, and clean partial add state before returning failure.
  - Firewall remove must loop through `INetFwRules::Item`/`Remove` until absence is proven; already-absent rules are a successful no-op.
  - Amyuni native removal must return `HRESULT` plus explicit status: not-present after complete enumeration, or removed after all matching present devices were removed. Native failure may fall back to the checked AMD64 helper; missing helper after native failure is fatal. Reboot-required success is signaled to MSI.
- Implemented:
  - `res/msi/Package/Fragments/CustomActions.wxs`: `AddFirewallRules` and `RemoveFirewallRules` now use `Return="check"`.
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/Common.h`, `CustomActions.cpp`, and `FirewallRules.cpp`: firewall helper now returns `HRESULT`; the MSI entry validates the mode byte and non-empty executable path, uses `StringCchCopyW` rather than format-string copying, propagates helper failure, and fails MSI on failure.
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/FirewallRules.cpp`: add removes stale same-name rules first, requires both directions to succeed, and best-effort removes partial state before returning add failure; remove uses a bounded `Item`/`Remove` loop until absence is proven and treats `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` / `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` / `ERROR_NOT_FOUND` as absence.
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/Common.h`, `DeviceUtils.cpp`, and `CustomActions.cpp`: `UninstallDriver` now returns `HRESULT` and `DriverUninstallStatus`, scans `SPDRP_HARDWAREID` as MultiSZ, propagates enumeration/property/class-installer/remove failures, and distinguishes proven not-present from removed.
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp`: `RemoveAmyuniIdd` tries the helper only after native failure on AMD64, treats missing helper after native failure as fatal, accepts helper `ERROR_SUCCESS_REBOOT_REQUIRED` as success-with-reboot, and checks `WcaDeferredActionRequiresReboot()`.
  - `res/msi/Package/Components/RustDesk.wxs`: `RemoveAmyuniIdd` and its `.SetParam` are scheduled only for uninstall/upgrade.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added/expanded gates and disposition for R-S11d-7 and the native half of R-S11d-2.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.

## R-S11d-8 work log — Windows RDP viewer credential command provenance

- Finding:
  - `src/port_forward.rs` launched `cmdkey` and `mstsc` through ambient executable search from the viewer process.
  - The saved RDP password was passed to `cmdkey /pass:` in process arguments, and RDP credentials were moved through process-global `rdp_username` / `rdp_password` environment variables.
  - This is viewer-side, same-user credential/provenance hardening, not a service/SYSTEM local privilege-escalation path. It still violated the fork's hardened model because a same-user launch directory/PATH substitution could observe credentials or replace the intended Microsoft tools, and environment plumbing made concurrent local RDP launches race over credential values.
- Research/design:
  - `mstsc.exe` is the only external tool needed. It must be resolved through the checked `GetSystemDirectoryW` helper already used for elevated Windows installer hardening.
  - `cmdkey` is removed entirely. Saved RDP credentials are seeded with native Windows Credential Manager APIs, never by command-line password argv.
  - The helper writes a session-scoped generic credential for `TERMSRV/localhost` only when both username and password are present, snapshots any existing credential first, serializes in-process seeded launches, and restores the previous state or deletes the temporary credential after `mstsc` exits or launch fails.
  - Incomplete credentials are ignored with a warning. No complete credential means `mstsc` is launched with `/prompt`; if a seeded launch is active, additional RDP launches fail closed rather than racing over the temporary localhost credential.
- Implemented:
  - `Cargo.toml`: enabled `Win32_Security_Credentials` for the existing `windows` dependency.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: made `trusted_system_tool_path` crate-visible for the RDP helper.
  - `src/port_forward.rs`: removed `cmdkey`, bare `mstsc`, `/pass:` argv, and environment reads; added native `CredReadW`/`CredWriteW`/`CredDeleteW` snapshot/write/restore logic, a process-local credential lease, trusted `mstsc.exe` launch, and prompt-only fallback when no complete credential is available.
  - `src/ui_session_interface.rs` and `src/cli.rs`: pass RDP username/password explicitly through the port-forward call chain instead of process-global environment variables; non-RDP callers pass empty strings.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11d-8 gates/status/disposition.
- Verification before commit:

  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: passed all gates (`VERIFY: all gates green`), including the new R-S11d-8 gates.
  - Ad hoc host cargo check did not prove this slice: `openssl-sys` failed before changed Windows code was reached because the local host environment lacks OpenSSL pkg-config metadata. The committed-source Windows VM build remains the authoritative compile/reproducibility proof for this slice.
