## R-S11d-9 work log — Windows terminal default-shell command provenance

- Finding:
  - `src/server/terminal_helper.rs` selected the Windows terminal shell from a current-directory `pwsh.exe` candidate, then from a hard-coded Windows PowerShell path, then from the caller's `COMSPEC` environment variable or a bare `cmd.exe` fallback.
  - This path is remote-triggerable only after Terminal authorization. In installed-service mode, the service launches the helper/shell as the current logon user, not SYSTEM; in direct mode it uses the process owner. The issue is therefore command provenance in an already-authorized shell feature, not a service-to-SYSTEM escalation.
  - The fork should still not allow a remote-triggered terminal-open path to select its executable from current-directory or environment state.
- Design:
  - Make Windows default-shell resolution fallible.
  - Use only absolute candidates: `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`, `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\6\pwsh.exe`, `System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`, and `System32\cmd.exe`.
  - Resolve `System32` structurally with `GetSystemDirectoryW`.
  - Do not read `COMSPEC`, do not test a bare `pwsh.exe`, and do not fall back to a bare `cmd.exe`.
  - Propagate shell-resolution failure in both helper and direct terminal-open paths.
- Implemented:
  - `src/server/terminal_helper.rs`: added `trusted_system_dir`, removed the bare `pwsh.exe` candidate and `COMSPEC` fallback, returns `Result<String>`, uses `GetSystemDirectoryW`, and fails closed if no trusted shell is present.
  - `src/server/terminal_service.rs`: default shell wrapper now returns `Result<String>` and direct terminal open uses `get_default_shell()?`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11d-9 gates/status/disposition.
- Verification before commit:
  - `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check src/server/terminal_helper.rs src/server/terminal_service.rs`: passed.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.

## R-S11d-10 work log — Windows portable RuntimeBroker cleanup command provenance

- Finding:

## R-S11d-13 work log — Windows service/session-token process launch provenance

- Finding:
  - `src/platform/windows.cc` accepted a single mutable command line in `LaunchProcessWin` and called `CreateProcessAsUserW(hToken, NULL, buf, ...)`.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs` built that command line with preformatted strings for the installed service `--server` launch and for root/session-crossing `run_exe_in_session_with_env` launches.
  - This is the same command-provenance class closed for privacy broker in R-S11d-12, but on the primary service-owned/session-token process-launch helper: executable identity was left to Windows command-line module parsing.
- Authority model:
  - Any service-owned or token-switched Windows launch must bind executable identity through an explicit `lpApplicationName`.
  - The command line is argv text only; it is not the authority for which image is executed.
  - Token-switched launches must fail closed unless the executable path is absolute and already names an existing file.

  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: added Windows-target unit tests for quoting and NUL rejection.

## Reviewed finding — Linux headless root-service file authority is root filesystem authority

- Status: ACCEPTED / NOT OPEN under the current project philosophy.
- Scope: Linux packaged root service, no active console user / headless service-owned server path, authenticated peer with file-capable `Remote` or `FileTransfer` authority.
- Concrete boundary:
  - `res/rustdesk.service` runs `/usr/bin/rustdesk --service` as root.
  - On headless/no-console Linux, `src/platform/linux.rs` and `src/server/connection.rs` keep `--server` and the CM path in the service UID instead of switching to a desktop user.
  - The CM authority token proves the active RustDesk connection and file capability, but it does not express a separate policy for root filesystem exposure.
- Concrete behavior:
  - Peer-supplied file-transfer paths can reach root-context read/list/send flows and CM mutate flows.
  - The affected action class includes `ReadDir`, `ReadAllFiles`, `ReadFile`/non-Windows `Send`, `RemoveFile`, `RemoveDir`, `CreateDir`, `Rename`, and write-job base paths.
  - This is not an unauthenticated IPC bypass. It is an authenticated remote-to-root-local consequence: ordinary file-transfer authority currently means root filesystem authority in the headless root-service case.
- Reclassification basis:
  - `requirements.html` Appendix C row 10 explicitly states full-filesystem reach is intended, not a defect, after the symlink TOCTOU is fixed.
  - The Appendix C #24 disposition states a password-authenticated owner already has full control, including terminal-root and full-filesystem authority, and that no less-trusted file-transfer grant exists in this fork.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` has an explicit R-F1/R-F2 gate preserving file transfer on headless Unix: server username falls back to the process owner and the viewer's "No active console user" refusal is Windows-peer-only.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md` cavity 5 records this as an explicit headless service-user case, not an accidental CM-spawn deadlock.
- Result:
  - No code change is correct for this finding unless the project philosophy changes from "authenticated owner gets full host capability" to "file transfer is separately confined." Adding a hidden root-filesystem-deny fallback now would contradict the current spec and its verification gates.

## R-S11d-14 work log — Windows service/session token source provenance

- Finding:
  - `src/platform/windows.cc` selected service/session launch authority by enumerating process basenames in the target session.
  - User-session launches accepted a same-session `explorer.exe` process, with a `sihost.exe` username fallback.
  - Service-owned SYSTEM launches accepted a same-session `winlogon.exe` basename.
  - The selected process was opened with `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS`, and its token was opened with `TOKEN_ALL_ACCESS`.
- Authority model:
  - A process basename is not an authority proof for a LocalSystem service deciding which token to give to `CreateProcessAsUserW`.
  - User launches must use the Windows Terminal Services user-token authority for the target session.
  - Service-owned SYSTEM launches must accept only a same-session trusted System32 `winlogon.exe` token that is actually LocalSystem.
  - Token/process handle rights must be the minimum documented rights needed by the launch path, not all-access handles.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.cc`: deleted `GetProcessUserName`, `GetLogonPid`, `GetFallbackUserPid`, the `explorer.exe`/`sihost.exe` user-process fallback, and all-access process/token opens.
  - `src/platform/windows.cc`: user-session launches now obtain the primary token from `WTSQueryUserToken(dwSessionId, &hToken)` and validate the token session before use.
  - `src/platform/windows.cc`: service-owned SYSTEM launches enumerate same-session `winlogon.exe` only, validate the full process image path against `%SystemRoot%\System32\winlogon.exe`, open the token with `TOKEN_QUERY | TOKEN_DUPLICATE | TOKEN_ASSIGN_PRIMARY`, validate token session, and validate the token user SID is LocalSystem.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs` and `src/server/connection.rs`: removed the exported `EXPLORER_EXE` constant and the old Explorer-name error suppression; launch failures now report absence of a trusted logged-on user token or trusted LocalSystem session token.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added the R-S11d-14 gates/status/disposition.

## R-S11d-15 work log — Windows EXE elevated batch completion accounting

- Finding:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs::run_cmds` launched the generated elevated installer `.bat` through `runas::Command::status()`, but discarded the returned `ExitStatus`.
  - `write_cmds` created the `.undone` completion marker with ignored errors, so the marker was not a mandatory precondition for the completion proof.
  - `install_service` and `uninstall_service` converted `run_cmds` failure into a `true` return value.
- Authority model:
  - Starting elevated `cmd.exe` is not proof that privileged service/registry/firewall/shortcut/process state changes completed.
  - The elevated batch wrapper must require successful child exit and explicit completion-marker removal.
  - Service lifecycle wrappers must report failed privileged command completion as failure.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: `.undone` marker creation is now mandatory; failure to create it aborts before elevation.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: `run_cmds` now captures the elevated `ExitStatus`, records whether the marker remains, removes leftover markers before returning failure, and requires both `status.success()` and a cleared marker before returning success.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: `install_service` and `uninstall_service` now log `run_cmds` failure as errors and return `false` instead of success.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added the R-S11d-15 gates/status/disposition.

## R-S11d-16 work log — Windows MSI service-state and SAS policy persistence

- Finding:
  - The per-machine MSI defaulted `STOP_SERVICE` to `'Y'`, then used impersonated immediate custom actions to read `stop-service` from the installing user's AppData config and decide whether the deferred elevated MSI action would create/start the LocalSystem service.
  - The MSI and EXE installer paths wrote persistent HKLM `SoftwareSASGeneration=1` without recording ownership, rollback state, or the original machine-policy value.
  - Runtime SAS had a temporary set/restore shape, but it conflated an absent policy value with DWORD `0`, ignored open/read/set failures before calling `SendSAS`, and did not serialize overlapping registry mutation.
- Authority model:
  - Per-machine service presence must follow the fork's pinned service policy, not an active user's mutable profile config.
  - Installer code must not persistently rewrite machine SAS policy when it cannot prove ownership or restore the previous value.
  - Runtime SAS may temporarily enable only the service SAS permission needed for the authenticated remote action, must fail before `SendSAS` on registry errors or unsupported policy values, must preserve documented `SoftwareSASGeneration` policy categories, and must restore/delete the exact state it changed.
- Implemented:
  - MSI WiX scheduling: deleted `STOP_SERVICE` gating, deleted service-state config reads, creates/starts the service on install/repair/upgrade unless `CC_CONNECTION_TYPE="outgoing"`, and scopes service stop/delete to uninstall or upgrade cleanup.
  - MSI custom action surface: deleted `SetPropertyIsServiceRunning`, `SetPropertyServiceStop`, `SetPropertyFromConfig`, `TryDeleteStartupShortcut`, `AddRegSoftwareSASGeneration`, and the `ReadConfig.cpp` source/export/project entry.
  - EXE installer path: deleted the persistent `reg add ... SoftwareSASGeneration ... /d 1` install command.
  - Runtime SAS: `send_sas` now returns `ResultType<()>`, serializes policy mutation with `SEND_SAS_POLICY_MUTEX`, distinguishes `Absent` from `Present(u32)`, accepts only documented policy values `0/1/2/3`, preserves Ease of Access policy by temporarily changing `2` to `3`, fails before `SendSAS` on open/read/set/unsupported-value errors, restores `Present(original)` including `0`, deletes only values that were originally absent, and propagates restore errors to the caller.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added the R-S11d-16 gates/status/disposition and removed stale R-S11d assertions that required the now-deleted persistent MSI SAS writer.

## R-S11e work log — Linux polkit policy/package assurance

- Finding:
  - The Linux installed-service password path was code-side fail-closed: the `_service` request uses the local peer process subject, absolute `/usr/bin/pkcheck`, `--action-id`, `--process`, and `--allow-user-interaction`, then commits through the root service into the service-owned main server.
  - The remaining assurance gap was packaging/policy drift: source greps proved an action id and `allow_active`, but did not structurally prove that the fork ships exactly one admin-auth polkit action in every Debian package path, rejects permissive policy values, rejects repo-shipped matching `.rules` overrides, or validates the emitted `.deb` payload before hashing.
  - The older "Windows privileged-state completion follow-ups" paragraph above is now stale for its listed Windows items: R-S11d-15 closed EXE elevated batch completion, and R-S11d-16 closed MSI service-state/SAS persistence.
- Authority model:
  - Do not change the Linux IPC/password authority path and do not add a config toggle or fallback.
  - Distro-local administrator polkit overrides remain an environment fact outside app-side local privilege escalation, but the fork's own source and package must never be the permissive policy source.
  - A release build must fail before hashing if the generated `.deb` misplaces, weakens, or mutates the shipped polkit policy.
- Implemented:
  - Added `scripts/verify-polkit-policy.py`, a structured checker for `res/com.carriez.RustDesk.policy`, `build.py`, repo-shipped `.rules` files, and optional built `.deb` payloads.
  - Source policy validation now parses XML and requires exactly one action, `com.carriez.RustDesk.set-unattended-password`, with `allow_any`, `allow_inactive`, and `allow_active` all set to `auth_admin`; it rejects `yes`, `auth_self`, `auth_self_keep`, and `auth_admin_keep`.
  - Repo validation rejects any shipped `.rules` file that names the RustDesk password action and requires all three Debian packaging paths in `build.py` to create `tmpdeb/usr/share/polkit-1/actions` and copy the policy there.
  - Package validation inspects a `.deb` with `dpkg-deb --contents` and `dpkg-deb -x`, requiring one policy at `usr/share/polkit-1/actions/com.carriez.RustDesk.policy`, regular-file type, `root/root` ownership, non-writable group/world mode, matching XML semantics, and byte identity with the source policy.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` now calls the structured checker as part of the service-owned password IPC closure gate and requires the R-S11e requirements/ledger strings.
  - `scripts/build-debian.sh` now requires `python3` and `dpkg-deb`, and validates each emitted `.deb` with the same checker before recording its SHA-256.
  - `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md` now record the R-S11e disposition.
- Verification before commit:

  - `python3 scripts/verify-polkit-policy.py --repo . --deb dist/rustdesk-x86_64.deb`: passed against the existing RustDesk package artifact.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh && bash -n scripts/build-debian.sh && python3 -m py_compile scripts/verify-polkit-policy.py`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: passed all gates (`VERIFY: all gates green`), including the structured polkit assurance gate.

  - Clean committed-source Debian build: `OUT_DIR=/tmp/r-s11e-debian-build-head scripts/build-debian.sh` passed with the default R-B2 double build enabled.

### R-S11b-4d follow-up — bind peer cleanup to the exact enumerated path

- Finding:
  - The R-S11b-4d cleanup predicate correctly required `Loaded` plus `PeerConfig::default()`, but
    `batch_peers` enumerated one path and then loaded by decoded id through `PeerConfig::path(id)`.
  - A non-canonical alias such as `base64_<base64("abc")>.toml` could therefore be deleted after loading a
    different canonical `abc.toml` that happened to be a loaded default. The deleted alias file was never loaded,
    so its saved credentials, non-empty fields, corrupt bytes, or transient unreadability were not part of the
    cleanup decision.
- Authority model:
  - A filesystem cleanup operation must be justified by the exact file it may remove. Id canonicalization is a
    display/storage naming rule, not authority to delete a different path.
- Implemented:
  - `PeerConfig` now has a private exact-path load helper. Public id loads still route through the canonical
    id path, but `batch_peers` loads the enumerated path `p` and only deletes `p` when that same exact-path load
    returned a semantically default loaded config.
  - Added a regression test where a canonical default peer file and a non-canonical credential-bearing alias
    coexist; `batch_peers` must preserve the alias.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md` now require the exact-path cleanup
    shape and the alias-path regression.

### R-S11b-3i follow-up — delete forbidden hardware-codec probe IPC write surface

- Finding:
  - The shipped build policy forbids `hwcodec`/`vram`/`mediacodec`, but the feature-gated source still kept
    a main-IPC hardware-codec probe channel.
  - If that forbidden feature were enabled, `Data::HwCodecConfig(Some(_))` was admitted by the ordinary main
    IPC mutation policy and handled by writing runtime hardware-codec state, including persisted `_hwcodec`
    state on Windows/macOS.
  - This was not a shipped-release LPE because release/build gates compile hardware codecs out, but it was a
    conditional source-level authority contradiction: a forbidden feature retained a service-owned receiver
    mutation without a service-minted helper capability.
- Authority model:
  - Hardware-codec probing has no authority model in this fork because hardware codecs are outside the fork's
    build model. The correct closure is deletion, not a helper-token protocol for a feature the project refuses
    to ship.
- Implemented:
  - Deleted `Data::CheckHwcodec`, `Data::HwCodecConfig`, their main-IPC handler, the `--check-hwcodec-config`
    core entry, client/server config sync helpers, and startup callers.
  - Left the generated Flutter `main_check_hwcodec` wrapper ABI-compatible, but it now reaches a no-op.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md` now reject reintroduced hardware-codec
    IPC probe messages, helpers, process entries, and direct app-source probe callers.

## R-S11c-15 work log — Windows helper launch environment authority

- Finding:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs::run_as_user_with_env` and `run_exe_in_session_with_env` pass service-generated helper proof variables into the token-switched Windows launch path.
  - `src/platform/windows.cc::LaunchProcessWin` obtains the target token environment with `CreateEnvironmentBlock`, then `merge_environment_blocks` appended extra RustDesk variables after the inherited environment without removing same-name inherited variables and without sorting the final block.
  - The helper proof variables are the CM/whiteboard launch token and launch parent. If a target user's ambient environment already carries a same-name variable, the helper receives an ambiguous block and effective lookup behavior determines whether the service-generated proof or the ambient user value is read.
  - Microsoft documents that an application-provided Win32 environment block is a double-null-terminated `name=value` block whose strings must be sorted alphabetically by name, case-insensitively. The old merge shape was therefore both ambiguous for duplicate keys and structurally outside the documented block contract.
- Authority model:
  - Helper endpoint proof material is launcher-owned authority. It may be transported through the child environment, but it must not be shadowed, duplicated, or selected by ambient user profile state.
  - Extra launcher-owned variables override inherited same-name variables using Windows' case-insensitive environment-name model.
  - The final environment block passed to `CreateProcessAsUserW` is a single deterministic, sorted block.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.cc`: added environment-entry key parsing that handles ordinary names and drive current-directory entries.
  - `src/platform/windows.cc`: added case-insensitive key comparison through `CompareStringOrdinal(..., TRUE)`.
  - `src/platform/windows.cc`: `merge_environment_blocks` now collects base and extra entries, removes inherited same-name entries before applying extras, lets the later extra entry win if extras duplicate each other, sorts the final entries, and emits a single double-null-terminated block.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added the R-S11c-15 gates/status/disposition.
- Verification before commit:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`: passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`: passed after updating the requirements hash carried by `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: passed all gates (`VERIFY: all gates green`), including the new R-S11c-15 source gate.
  - No local lightweight Windows C++ compiler was available on this host while the pre-existing full release Windows VM build was still running; this slice is source-gated here and should receive the usual committed-source Windows build proof when a Windows build is run for this commit.
- Commit/push:

  - Local `master`, `origin/master`, and remote `refs/heads/master` all resolve to `7d9b496d6426fb723b881b313658fe5b556ef881`.

## R-S11d-17 work log — Windows portable installer source-staging authority

- Finding:
  - `libs/portable/src/main.rs` built the normal portable unpack directory under per-user LocalAppData, deleted that stable tree with raw best-effort removal, wrote embedded files into it, mapped double-click `rustdesk-*install.exe` to `--install`, and also allowed `--silent-install` to reach the embedded app from that same caller-writable unpack tree.
  - `libs/portable/src/bin_reader.rs` joined embedded archive paths onto the extraction prefix and wrote them with ordinary `create_dir_all` / `fs::write` behavior, without strict relative Windows path validation and without treating decompression/create/write/sync failures as fatal.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs::install_me` derives the install source from `current_exe`, then the elevated install batch copies the source executable's parent directory into the fixed Program Files install path. That made the portable extraction directory part of the privileged install-source chain.
- Authority model:
  - Supported portable interactive and silent install entry points must not promote a stable medium-integrity, same-user writable cache directory into Program Files after UAC consent.
  - The install source for the elevated copy must be a private protected staging tree created after elevation under the width-correct Program Files root, outside the final install directory.
  - Embedded payload names are archive authority and must be accepted only as relative Windows-safe components; write/decompression/sync/generation errors are fatal, not best-effort.
  - Cleanup must remove only manifest-known payload files and the generated RuntimeBroker copy after reparse checks. It must not recursively delete attacker-shaped trees under Program Files.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/portable/src/main.rs`: double-click `*install.exe`, external `--silent-install`, and the internal protected install arguments all route through `win::run_protected_installer`.
  - `libs/portable/src/main.rs`: the medium-integrity leg relaunches itself with `ShellExecuteExW`/`runas`, `SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS`, waits for the elevated child, reads the child exit code with `GetExitCodeProcess`, and treats a nonzero child exit as failure; the protected-main branch exits with code `1` on error.
  - `libs/portable/src/main.rs`: the elevated leg requires `current_process_is_elevated`, creates a private per-run staging directory under `FOLDERID_ProgramFiles` / `FOLDERID_ProgramFilesX86`, rejects staging equal to or below the final `Program Files\RustDesk` install directory, and rejects reparse-point staging roots.
  - `libs/portable/src/main.rs`: interactive and silent child install operations run only from protected staging, with `RUSTDESK_APPNAME`, `RUSTDESK_PROTECTED_INSTALL`, and foreground handoff set explicitly.
  - `src/ui_interface.rs`: `RUSTDESK_PROTECTED_INSTALL` hides and blocks the run-without-install escape inside the elevated install UI.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: `install_me` consumes the protected install proof before composing the privileged copy. It requires the exact `RUSTDESK_PROTECTED_INSTALL=1` marker, an already elevated child process, a regular current executable, and a regular non-reparse `Program Files\RustDesk-staging-*` source directory whose parent is the width-correct Program Files root and whose path is outside the final install root.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: the install copy helper receives the verified source directory directly instead of deriving authority from arbitrary `current_exe().parent()`.
  - `src/core_main.rs` / `src/ui_interface.rs`: silent and interactive child install failures exit nonzero, so the waiting protected packer observes rejected or failed install attempts.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: `run_cmds` now detects already-elevated installer execution and runs trusted `cmd.exe` directly instead of prompting for a second elevation; `is_elevated(None)` no longer closes the current-process pseudo-handle.
  - `libs/portable/src/bin_reader.rs`: embedded payload paths are validated as relative Windows-safe components, rejecting absolute paths, `..`, drive/ADS syntax, control characters, wildcard/reserved characters, trailing dot/space components, and Windows reserved device names.
  - `libs/portable/src/bin_reader.rs`: payload extraction now propagates decompression/read/create/write/sync/rename errors and writes through create-new temporary files before replacement.
  - `libs/portable/src/main.rs`: generated RuntimeBroker copy failure is fatal for the install source; post-extraction failures still attempt manifest cleanup, and cleanup removes only manifest-known payload files plus the generated broker after parent/target reparse checks.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`, and `scripts/verify.sh`: added the R-S11d-17 disposition, requirements hash, and gates for protected relaunch, elevated exit-code check, protected Program Files staging, silent/install routing, payload validation, synced writes, protected UI marker, no-install block, already-elevated command execution, fatal generated-file copy, and manifest cleanup.

## R-S11d-18 work log — Windows EXE elevated batch cmd-state hardening

- Investigation source:
  - Rawls reviewed the Windows installer/MSI surfaces and reported that the EXE elevated batch runner still crossed from medium-integrity caller state into elevated `cmd.exe` while preserving ambient command-processor behavior and allowing expansion-sensitive generated paths.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - The EXE install/uninstall/service-install/service-uninstall runner invoked trusted `System32\cmd.exe`, but still used bare `/C`. HKCU Command Processor `AutoRun` remained active for the elevated shell, and the generated batch/marker paths could still include expansion-sensitive characters from the caller temp directory.

  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: made installer command directory selection a fallible validated candidate list. The runner tries caller temp, ProgramData, and the existing user-accessible folder only after path-literal validation, and continues to the next safe candidate when file creation fails.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: validates each generated command-file path, tracks command-file create failures, quotes the completion-marker deletion path through the same guard, and invokes trusted `cmd.exe` as `/D /V:OFF /S /C` on both already-elevated and UAC `runas` paths.

## R-S11d-20 work log — Windows EXE elevated batch command postconditions

- Investigation source:
  - Rawls reported that after the wrapper-level completion fixes, individual EXE elevated batch commands still had mixed failure accounting: required install/update commands could fail and later marker deletion could still make the elevated batch appear complete, while cleanup commands treated absence and failed deletion too loosely.
  - Turing reviewed the remaining Windows batch surfaces and scoped this slice to EXE install/update/uninstall/service-install/service-uninstall command-body postconditions, leaving MSI `CC_CONNECTION_TYPE`, certificate cleanup, and Amyuni IDD cleanup out of scope.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - Required elevated install/update operations now either fail fast on command failure or verify the persistent target exists before the batch can delete its completion marker.
  - Cleanup operations that are allowed to be absent now verify final absence for service, registry, firewall, install-directory, and all-users shortcut state.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: added fail-fast and postcondition helpers for required batch commands, copy targets, directory existence, path absence, registry-key absence, firewall-rule absence, service absence with bounded polling, and MSI uninstall exit handling.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: broker update and install payload/broker copies now use checked copy helpers; `xcopy /C` is removed so copy failures are not deliberately continued.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: install-directory creation verifies final existence, current-exe batch text is guarded, install HKLM/HKCR registry writes and firewall additions are fail-fast, and shortcut script execution verifies the final `.lnk` exists.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: full uninstall and service-only uninstall now use absence-driven service deletion and postchecked Start Menu/Public Desktop/Common Startup/install-directory cleanup. HKCR/HKLM registry and firewall cleanup verifies final absence.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: prior MSI uninstall delegation now checks the command exit status and accepts only success, reboot-required `3010`, and product-absent `1605`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: added R-S11d-20 gates/status/disposition and updated the requirements hash.

## R-S11d-21 work log — Windows MSI service-mode package authority

    `res/msi/Package/Components/RustDesk.wxs` used `CC_CONNECTION_TYPE="outgoing"` to suppress
    `CreateStartService`, `LaunchAppTray`, and the startup tray shortcut.
  - Microsoft MSI documentation treats public properties as install-time inputs, and deferred
    non-impersonated custom actions run on the elevated/server side. Therefore service presence for this
    per-machine package must be package policy, not a caller-controlled public property or transform.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - The MSI package no longer exposes or consumes connection type as a service-mode authority. A caller can no
    longer suppress LocalSystem service creation/start by passing `CC_CONNECTION_TYPE=outgoing`.

  - `res/msi/Package/Components/RustDesk.wxs`: removed every `CC_CONNECTION_TYPE` branch from service creation,
    service parameter setting, tray launch, and startup tray shortcut conditions.

## R-S11d-22 work log — Windows EXE certificate cleanup completion authority

- Investigation source:
  - `get_uninstall` inserted `--uninstall-cert` into the elevated EXE uninstall batch as a raw command and skipped
    it if `current_exe()` failed.
  - `core_main` handled `--uninstall-cert` through `allow_err!`, so the process exited successfully after cleanup
    failure.
  - `windows.rs` declared `DeleteRustDeskTestCertsW()` as `void` and always returned `Ok(())`.
  - `windows_delete_test_cert.cc` read the certificate `Blob` into `lResult` but checked the never-updated
    `readResult`, so the fixed WDK test-certificate branch never authorized deletion.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - EXE uninstall certificate cleanup can no longer fail or be skipped while the elevated uninstall batch reports
    success. The fixed WDK test certificate and historical malformed ROOT store cleanup now have a status contract
    from native registry operations through Rust and the elevated batch.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows_delete_test_cert.cc`: replaced the raw-allocation/void-return helper with a
    status-returning implementation that enumerates stores through checked registry calls, reads the `Blob` through
    checked `RegQueryValueExW` status, deletes the fixed thumbprint only after a bounded WDK-test-cert suffix match,
    preserves malformed ROOT store cleanup through an explicit wide prefix, and avoids `KEY_ALL_ACCESS`.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: the FFI imports `DeleteRustDeskTestCertsW() -> BOOL` and converts `FALSE` into
    `Result` failure; `get_uninstall` now treats `current_exe()` failure as fatal and wraps `--uninstall-cert` with

## R-S11d-23 work log — Windows EXE Amyuni IDD cleanup completion authority

- Investigation source:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:get_uninstall` inserted `--uninstall-amyuni-idd` through a helper that returned an
    empty string if `current_exe()` failed, so EXE uninstall could skip Amyuni cleanup while continuing.
  - `src/core_main.rs` handled `--uninstall-amyuni-idd` through `allow_err!`, so the helper process returned
    success after `amyuni_idd::uninstall_driver()` failure.
  - The top-level Windows `--uninstall` dispatcher logged `platform::uninstall_me(true)` failure without exiting
    nonzero, so elevated batch failure did not necessarily reach the CLI caller.
  - `src/virtual_display_manager.rs` launched AMD64 `deviceinstaller64.exe` through `ShellExecuteW`, so runtime
    install/remove could not wait for the helper, read its exit code, bound execution completion, or distinguish
    install/update from remove/cleanup reboot-required semantics.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - EXE uninstall Amyuni cleanup can no longer be skipped, fire-and-forget, or hidden by the top-level CLI path.
    The runtime helper now observes selected helper completion; install/update rejects reboot-required because the
    caller immediately tries to use the driver, while remove accepts reboot-required as cleanup success.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: `get_uninstall` now resolves the current executable once for EXE uninstall helpers,
    treats failure as fatal, quotes the executable through the elevated-batch path guard, wraps
    `--uninstall-amyuni-idd` with `checked_batch_cmd`, and deletes the stale skip-on-error helper.
  - `src/core_main.rs`: top-level `--uninstall` exits nonzero on `uninstall_me()` failure, and
    `--uninstall-amyuni-idd` logs `uninstall_driver()` failure and exits nonzero.
  - `src/virtual_display_manager.rs`: AMD64 `deviceinstaller64.exe` launch now builds a quoted mutable command
    line, uses `CreateProcessW` with explicit application path, closes process/thread handles with RAII, waits up
    to 120 seconds, reads the child exit code, rejects nonzero exits, accepts `ERROR_SUCCESS_REBOOT_REQUIRED` only
    for remove/cleanup, and rejects that code for install/update before driver use.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: added the
    R-S11d-23 gate/status/disposition and updated the requirements hash.

  - `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check src/core_main.rs src/platform/windows.rs src/virtual_display_manager.rs`:
    passed.

## R-S11c-16 work log — Desktop service lifecycle completion authority

- Investigation source:
  - A read-only explorer independently traced the macOS service path and confirmed that `install_service()` only
    reported existing plist state, `is_installed_daemon(prompt=true)` spawned `/usr/bin/osascript` and returned
    immediately, and `uninstall_service(sync=true)` returned `true` after the closure regardless of `osascript`
    failure once resources were present.
  - `core_main` ignored `install_service()` and `uninstall_service(false, true)` return values for the explicit
    `--install-service` / `--uninstall-service` CLI arms.
  - Linux service lifecycle wrappers ignored install-time config-copy and `systemctl enable/disable` failures, and
    uninstall returned success when `systemctl stop` failed.
  - macOS service install/uninstall treated every successful `osascript.status()` call, including nonzero exit, as
    the success branch; install checked only the agent plist before discarding `launchctl load` status; uninstall
    checked only agent plist absence, discarded `launchctl remove` status, and `uninstall.scpt` masked daemon unload
    failure with `|| true` before deleting launchd plists.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - Desktop service lifecycle operations now report completion only after the operation-owned status and persistent
    state checks succeed. The explicit CLI no longer turns wrapper failure into process success. Linux and macOS no
    longer hide service lifecycle failure behind ignored status, partial postconditions, or best-effort launchd /
    systemd calls.
- Implemented:
  - `src/core_main.rs`: `--install-service` and `--uninstall-service` exit nonzero when the platform wrapper reports
    failure.
  - `src/platform/linux.rs`: `systemctl_service` logs spawn/nonzero failures; install-time config-copy and
    `systemctl enable/start/disable/stop` failures are fatal to the wrapper return; uninstall no longer runs the
    unrelated user-config migration.
  - `src/platform/macos.rs`: added checked command execution for AppleScript and launchctl calls, shared daemon/agent
    plist state helpers, checked install context, current-session LaunchAgent label removal/reload verification, and
    synchronous uninstall result propagation. Prompt-driven UI install keeps the async worker shape, but that worker
    now executes the checked install path.
  - `src/platform/privileges_scripts/install.scpt`: verifies root LaunchDaemon load by label after loading and
    unloads an existing loaded label before replacing it.
  - `src/platform/privileges_scripts/uninstall.scpt`: removes `|| true`, unloads only when the daemon label is
    loaded, verifies the label is absent, removes both plists, and verifies both plists are absent.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: added R-S11c-16 gates for the cross-desktop and macOS
    source invariants.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: added the R-S11c-16
    requirements/status disposition and updated the requirements hash to
    `27235735f69d53fe85fd5a28ccf7efef60c99995c5d857f34329b038d4563a70`.
- Verification before commit:

  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`: passed with requirements hash
    `27235735f69d53fe85fd5a28ccf7efef60c99995c5d857f34329b038d4563a70`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: passed all gates (`VERIFY: all gates green`) with full output in
    `/tmp/rustdesk_verify_r_s11c16.log`.

## R-S15 work log — Peer-derived keyboard-mode persistence removed

- Investigation source:
  - A peer/IPC explorer found that a password-correct hostile peer could use `PeerInfo.version`/`platform` to make
    the viewer select or rewrite the persisted `PeerConfig.keyboard_mode` during ordinary peer-info handling.
  - The Flutter peer-info path also called a desktop keyboard-mode helper that persisted a compatibility-selected
    mode through `sessionSetKeyboardMode`, so the same peer metadata could indirectly rewrite the saved per-peer
    preference after connection setup.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - Peer-derived keyboard-mode compatibility is now runtime-only. A peer may influence the effective compatibility
    fallback used while the current session is active, but it cannot choose or rewrite the operator-owned persisted
    `PeerConfig.keyboard_mode`.
- Implemented:
  - `src/client.rs`: removed `handle_peer_info()` keyboard-mode selection/rewrite from peer metadata and added
    regression tests proving peer info neither fills an empty saved keyboard mode nor rewrites an existing saved
    keyboard mode.
  - `flutter/lib/models/model.dart` and `flutter/lib/desktop/widgets/remote_toolbar.dart`: removed the auto-persist
    desktop keyboard-mode helper from peer-info and input-source-change flows.
  - `flutter/lib/models/input_model.dart`: kept Flutter input-source compatibility as an input-model runtime fallback
    without calling `sessionSetKeyboardMode`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gated the Rust peer-info body, the Dart peer-info path, the removed auto-persist helper, the
    runtime fallback, and both new regression tests.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: documented the completed R-S15
    keyboard-mode disposition and updated the requirements hash to

## R-S15 follow-up work log — Peer privacy-mode status no longer persists without local request authority

- Investigation source:
  - A read-only peer-message explorer found that a password-correct hostile controlled peer could send
    `Misc::BackNotification(PrivacyModeState)` to the viewer and drive `update_privacy_mode()` without proving the
    viewer had requested a privacy-mode transition.
  - The old path loaded the viewer's `PeerConfig`, wrote `config.privacy_mode.v`, optionally stored the peer-supplied
    `privacy-mode-impl-key` after compile-time allowlist validation, and saved the config. R-S15 had bounded the
    implementation string but had not authorized the peer to choose the saved boolean.
  - Impact: `PrvOnSucceeded` could poison the viewer's saved per-peer `privacy-mode=true`, causing the next default
    remote session to auto-send `TogglePrivacyMode { on: true }`; failure/off states could likewise persist `false`.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - Peer privacy-mode status is no longer local policy authority. The Rust client I/O loop records a pending
    privacy-mode request only after it actually sends a local outbound `TogglePrivacyMode` or legacy
    `OptionMessage.privacy_mode` request for a default remote-control session. A peer response may persist only if it
    matches that pending request's direction and implementation key before the request expires.
  - Unsolicited, expired, wrong-implementation, or wrong-direction privacy-mode status remains a notification path and
    does not write the viewer's saved `PeerConfig`.
- Implemented:
  - `src/client/io_loop.rs`: added `PendingPrivacyModeRequest` and `PrivacyModeResponseAdmission`; recorded pending
    requests after outbound manual/auto privacy toggles are sent; classified incoming privacy-mode status before any
    persistence; and routed `update_privacy_mode()` through `persist_privacy_mode_response_if_admitted()`.
  - `src/client/io_loop.rs` tests cover on-success/on-failure/off-success/off-failure, wrong implementation,
    wrong direction, expiry, non-default sessions, modern `TogglePrivacyMode`, and legacy `OptionMessage.privacy_mode`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: document and
    gate the pending-request authority rule.
- Verification before commit:
  - Direct local cargo could not compile because the repo `target/` directory is root-owned and this host lacks
    GTK/X11/pkg-config development packages; a temp target dir reached the expected missing GTK/X11 libraries.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - Full repo verification is run through `scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/flutter-verify.sh`, `scripts/dart-verify.sh`,
    `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`, and `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` before commit.

## R-S11c-10j follow-up work log — Debian package lifecycle completion is status-authoritative

- Investigation source:
  - Read-only Debian packaging audit found `res/DEBIAN/preinst`, `postinst`, `prerm`, and `postrm` still converted
    `deb-systemd-invoke` / `deb-systemd-helper` stop, start, daemon-reload, disable, purge, and root-config cleanup
    failures into success with `|| true`.
  - The same audit found Debian package build paths that could package stale or unchecked maintainer scripts:
    unchecked `os.system(...)` calls, `rm tmpdeb/usr/bin/rustdesk || true`, and a combined `dpkg-deb -b ...; rm -rf`
    command whose final status was cleanup rather than package-build success.
- Finding closed in this slice:
  - Debian package lifecycle helpers remain the Debian policy-aware interface, but their failures are no longer
    non-authoritative. A configured/removed/purged package cannot report success after required service lifecycle or
    root service-state cleanup failure.
  - The long Debian release build now proves the emitted `.deb` contains the exact checked `res/DEBIAN` maintainer
    scripts and rejects any built control script that masks lifecycle helper failure.
- Implemented:
  - `res/DEBIAN/preinst`: fresh install no longer stops a nonexistent old unit; upgrade checks for existing old unit
    paths and then treats stop failure as fatal.
  - `res/DEBIAN/postinst`: enable, daemon-reload, and start are checked under `set -e`.
  - `res/DEBIAN/prerm`: stop and disable happen before entry-point/unit removal and are checked; daemon-reload is
    checked after removal.
  - `res/DEBIAN/postrm`: purge helper and `/root/.config/rustdesk` cleanup are checked.
  - `build.py`: Debian package staging starts from a clean `tmpdeb`, optional binary cleanup uses checked `rm -f`,
    Debian control-script copies use `system2`, and `dpkg-deb` is split from cleanup.
  - `scripts/build-debian.sh`: extracts the emitted `.deb`, compares `preinst`/`postinst`/`prerm`/`postrm` to
    `res/DEBIAN`, and rejects masked maintainer-script lifecycle failures before hashing artifacts.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: gate and document the source and package
    authority model.

## R-X9/R-X10 follow-up work log — macOS stop-service config writer residue

- Finding:
  - `src/platform/macos.rs::uninstall_service` still sent `crate::ipc::set_option("stop-service", "Y")` after a

## R-S11b/R-S11c follow-up work log — Linux service install no longer imports user config into root

- Finding:
  - A read-only explorer found that Linux `--install-service` still called
    `copy_user_config_to_root_service_config()` before `systemctl enable/start`.
  - That helper whole-file copied active-user `{app}.toml` and `{app}2.toml` into `/root/.config/{app}`. Those
    files can carry `password`, `password_prs`, `salt`, `key_pair`, structured `socks`, and broad `options`, so
    service-owned unattended credentials/policy could be provisioned by whole-config import rather than the typed
    `_service` + polkit operation.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/linux.rs`: deleted the user-to-root config import helpers and their now-wrong tests; Linux

## R-S11d-3 follow-up work log — Windows IPC bind failure no longer kills guessed processes

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `92a65d3bbee1d744a7dfd9c236fc29b291b14600`.
  - This is a Windows runtime/service-adjacent process-control follow-up, not a reopened credential/config IPC
    finding.
- Finding:
  - When the installed/server path failed to start the main IPC listener, `src/server.rs::start_server` spawned
    `stop_main_window_process`.
  - That helper first connected to the occupied IPC endpoint and sent `Data::Close`, then on Windows fell back to
    `try_kill_rustdesk_main_window_process`.
  - The Windows fallback selected a process by app-name basename plus weak argv shape, skipped only the current
    uid/self pid, opened the selected process with `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS`, and called `NtTerminateProcess`.
  - This was not a proven privilege-escalation path: it required an IPC bind failure and the process selected was a
    same-host process matching RustDesk-like shape. The authority model was still wrong for service-capable code:
    IPC bind failure is not process-control authority, and a LocalSystem service must not terminate a guessed
    process to recover from a stale/occupied endpoint.
- Implemented:
  - `src/server.rs`: IPC start failure now logs the occupied endpoint and exits fail-closed; the close/kill helper
    is deleted.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: deleted `try_kill_rustdesk_main_window_process`, the `NtTerminateProcess` wrapper,
    the `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS` process open, and the now-unused loader imports.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: R-S11d-3 now rejects the old `stop_main_window_process`,
    `try_kill_rustdesk_main_window_process`, `NtTerminateProcess`, `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS`, and old "try kill it"
    fallback strings in the relevant source files.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded the fail-closed IPC bind
    authority model and updated the requirements hash.
- Verification:
  - Targeted checks passed: `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check --config skip_children=true src/server.rs
    src/platform/windows.rs`, `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`, `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`, and `git diff --check`.
  - Full `scripts/verify.sh` passed from committed HEAD.
  - Commit `737586323e79c61b2700deb1c658746597f04451` (`Remove Windows IPC occupant kill fallback`) was pushed to
    `origin/master`.

## R-S11c-5 follow-up work log — macOS privileged helper lifecycle installs exact bundled helper

- Baseline:

  - This closes the concrete macOS privileged-helper lifecycle gap found after the helper designated-requirement
    slice.

  - `install.scpt` verified `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.carriez.rustdesk_service`, but did not install or
    replace it from the current app bundle.
  - Fresh systems could fail service install because the helper was absent.

    beside the running app, requires it to exist as a file, and passes that path to the privileged install script.

    pinned Developer ID requirement, installs it through a root-owned temporary file into
    `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.carriez.rustdesk_service`, clears ACLs, sets `root:wheel`/`0755`, verifies the
    temp and final helper signatures, byte-compares the final helper to the bundled helper, and re-verifies the
    deployed helper immediately before launchd load.
  - `src/platform/privileges_scripts/uninstall.scpt`: unloads the daemon and removes both the deployed privileged
    helper and any install-temp helper, then verifies they are absent.

    argument passing, bundled-helper verification, root-owned temp install, byte comparison, deployed-helper

    model and updated the requirements hash.

## R-S11c-17 work log — macOS runtime service ACL inspection provenance

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `46b273bdef74adf0345ca0154f022ccde8603433`.
  - The live R-S11b/R-S11c ledger had no open original service-owned IPC item; newly found root/service trust
    command-provenance issues are tracked as new closure slices.
- Finding:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs` used `Command::new(MACOS_LS).arg("-lde").arg(path).output()` inside
    `macos_path_has_no_extended_acl`.
  - That function fed the macOS `_service` IPC installed-app and PrivilegedHelperTools trust decision after
    symlink, owner, mode, and code-signing checks.
  - `src/ipc.rs` carried a second `macos_path_has_no_extended_acl` that spawned `/bin/ls -lde` for the
    service-owned LaunchAgent plist parent/file trust check before serving the root password snapshot.
  - This was not a confirmed command-injection primitive: the command path was absolute and the checked path was
    argv-passed. The authority model was still wrong because root-side runtime trust depended on a formatter
    subprocess and parsed `ls` output for ACL state.
- Authority model:
  - Runtime macOS service trust checks inspect ACL state through libc ACL APIs on the exact no-follow path already
    passed through symlink metadata checks. Any NUL path, ACL retrieval failure, ACL validation failure, or extended
    ACL entry rejects the path; no runtime ACL decision is made by spawning `ls`.
- Research basis:
  - Apple `acl_get(3)` documents `acl_get_link_np` as the no-follow ACL retrieval API and requires freeing
    allocated ACL storage with `acl_free`.
  - Apple `acl_get_entry(3)` documents `ACL_FIRST_ENTRY` enumeration and `0` on an obtained entry.
  - Apple `acl_valid(3)` documents `acl_valid_link_np` for no-follow ACL validation in a file-system-object context.
  - Apple Libc `sys/acl.h` defines `ACL_TYPE_EXTENDED = 0x00000100`, `ACL_FIRST_ENTRY = 0`,
    `acl_t`, `acl_entry_t`, `acl_get_link_np`, `acl_get_entry`, `acl_valid_link_np`, and `acl_free`.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: removed `MACOS_LS` and replaced the `ls -lde` parser with a native macOS ACL helper using
    `CString`, `acl_get_link_np`, `acl_valid_link_np`, `acl_get_entry`, and an `acl_free` drop guard.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: deleted the duplicate `ls -lde` ACL parser and routes LaunchAgent plist trust through
    `ipc_auth::macos_path_has_no_extended_acl`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: removed the old requirement that runtime ACL
    inspection use `MACOS_LS`, added native ACL API/source-shape gates, added requirements/ledger gates, and reject
    `MACOS_LS`, `Command::new(MACOS_LS)`, `Command::new("/bin/ls")`, and `Command::new("ls")` in the Rust macOS
    runtime trust sources.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded R-S11c-17 and updated the
    requirements hash.
- Cross-check:
  - Read-only subagent `019f4efe-8893-7550-8295-abfc3a0ef90c` found no remaining Rust runtime macOS service/IPC ACL
    trust path that spawns `/bin/ls`, `ls -lde`, `Command::new(MACOS_LS)`, or PATH-selected `ls`.
  - It confirmed the then-remaining `/bin/ls -lde` use was confined to
    `src/platform/privileges_scripts/install.scpt`; that installer-shell residue is closed later by R-S11c-18.
  - It identified that the first negative verifier pass was too narrow; this slice tightened the gates to catch
    direct `Command::new("/bin/ls")` and `Command::new("ls")` spellings across the Rust macOS helper sources.
- Verification:
  - Targeted checks passed: `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check --config skip_children=true src/ipc/auth.rs`,
    `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`, `bash -n scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`, `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`,
    `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`, and `git diff --check`.
  - Full `scripts/verify.sh` passed from the edited tree.
  - Commit `61246477afff86fe26a2c38934c28c9b06c2aa14`
    (`Use native macOS ACL checks for service trust`) was pushed to `origin/master`.

## R-S11d-30 work log — Windows elevated post-install relaunch executable authority

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `58908dde67af0fea7c9dee081a9b6fd98c2a5fe8`.
  - The original R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC checklist remains closed/gated. This slice closes a separate
    Windows R-S11d trust issue discovered during the read-only residual audit: executable selection for GUI/tray
    relaunch after privileged install/service work.
- Finding:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:1575` defines the legacy Inno uninstall key
    `{54E86BC2-6C85-41F3-A9EB-1A94AC9B1F93}_is1`.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:1589` prefers that legacy key, including the Wow6432Node variant, before the current
    app-name uninstall key.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:1632` exposes that compatibility choice through `get_install_info()`.
  - Before this slice, the post-elevated relaunch helper called `get_install_info()` after EXE install, service
    install, and service uninstall batches completed. That meant legacy HKLM uninstall metadata could choose the
    post-elevated child executable even though the privileged install path had already fixed the service root to
    Program Files.
- Research basis:
  - Microsoft documents uninstall metadata under
    `HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall`.
    Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/msi/uninstall-registry-key
  - Microsoft documents `SHGetKnownFolderPath` as the API for resolving known folders by `KNOWNFOLDERID`.
    Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shlobj_core/nf-shlobj_core-shgetknownfolderpath
  - Microsoft `CreateProcessAsUserW` / process-creation guidance reinforces that callers must provide explicit,
    trusted executable paths at process-creation boundaries.
    Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessasuserw
- Authority model:
  - After privileged EXE install, service install, or service uninstall work, any GUI/tray child process is spawned
    only from the fixed Program Files executable selected by the protected install/service path, or it is not spawned.
  - Legacy uninstall registry metadata can remain compatibility/read-only install state, but cannot select a child
    executable for an elevated aftermath path.
  - Missing files, path mismatches, and spawn failures are failures, not best-effort warnings.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:2493`: EXE install relaunch passes the fixed `exe` already selected by `install_me`.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:3868` and `src/platform/windows.rs:3913`: service uninstall resolves the fixed service
    executable before the elevated batch and relaunches only that executable.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:3999`: service install relaunches only the fixed service executable resolved by
    `fixed_service_install_dir_and_exe()`.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs:4093`: deleted the old registry-selected/best-effort `run_after_run_cmds()` helper and
    replaced it with `run_after_elevated_service_cmds()`, which revalidates exact fixed executable identity, requires
    the path to be an existing file, and propagates GUI/tray spawn errors.
  - `scripts/verify.sh:457`: added gates for the new helper shape, all three fixed-executable call sites, fixed-root
    revalidation, path identity check, file-existence check, absence of `get_install_info()` in the helper body,
    absence of the old helper, and requirements/ledger disposition.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded R-S11d-30 and updated the
    requirements hash.
- Verification:
  - Targeted checks passed: `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check --config skip_children=true src/platform/windows.rs`,
    `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/verify-release.sh scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`,
    `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`, and `git diff --check`.

## R-S11d-31 work log — Windows privacy broker served-session authority

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `fa65adabc412d0de475519c374e6f0ca0486417f`.
  - The original R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC checklist remains closed/gated. This slice closes a separate
    Windows R-S11d residual found in the prior audit: the privacy broker reselected the physical console session
    instead of following the RustDesk process session actually serving the authenticated Remote connection.
- Finding:
  - The Remote privacy toggle reaches `Connection::turn_on_privacy()` through the authenticated Remote-only
    handler in `src/server/connection.rs`.
  - Before this slice, the Windows topmost-window implementation did not receive a Windows session authority from
    that call chain; it stored only the RustDesk connection id for privacy ownership.
  - In the broker launcher, `src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs` called `WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId()`, then
    passed that session id into `get_user_token(session_id, true)` and `CreateProcessAsUserW`.
  - The installed Windows service already selects the served session separately: `src/platform/windows.rs` uses
    `get_current_session(share_rdp())`, launches the service-owned `--server` into that session, and refreshes that
    server when the served session changes. Therefore the broker's physical-console lookup could disagree with the
    session being served when RDP/ICA session sharing is enabled.
  - Read-only subagent `019f4f19-c8b7-7392-b50e-b691a9722e4c` independently confirmed the same call chain and
    recommended using the current RustDesk process session, not an ambient active-session re-query.
- Research basis:
  - Microsoft documents `WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId` as returning the session attached to the physical console,
    with `0xFFFFFFFF` when no console session is attached.
    Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-wtsgetactiveconsolesessionid
  - Microsoft documents `ProcessIdToSessionId` as retrieving the Remote Desktop Services session for a specific
    process.
    Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-processidtosessionid
  - Microsoft documents `WTSQueryUserToken` as obtaining the primary token for the logged-on user in a specified
    session, requiring LocalSystem/TCB authority.
    Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wtsapi32/nf-wtsapi32-wtsqueryusertoken
  - Microsoft `CreateProcessAsUserW` guidance keeps the process-creation boundary explicit and warns about
    executable selection when the application path is not explicit.
    Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessasuserw
- Authority model:
  - The privacy broker session is the session of the RustDesk host process that is serving the authenticated Remote
    session. The broker must not reselect the physical console or accept a peer-supplied selected session.
  - If the served process session cannot be determined or is invalid, privacy-mode broker launch fails closed.
- Implemented:
  - `src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs:1`: removed the `WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId` import and imports
    `get_current_process_session_id` beside `get_user_token`.
  - `src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs:266`: broker launch now calls `privacy_broker_session_id()?`.
  - `src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs:267`: `get_user_token(session_id, true)` now uses that served process
    session id.
  - `src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs:337`: added `privacy_broker_session_id()`, which wraps
    `get_current_process_session_id()`, rejects absence, rejects `u32::MAX`, and returns the served session.
  - `scripts/verify.sh:711`: extended the existing R-S11d privacy broker provenance gate to require the served
    session helper, fail-closed errors, invalid-session rejection, served-session token call, and absence of
    `WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId` in `src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs`.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded R-S11d-31 and updated
    the requirements hash to `0bfc05068155273163f6acf886863ee8402d1fc279d897f49da1d453cd5aa601`.
- Verification:
  - Targeted checks passed: `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check --config skip_children=true src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs`,
    `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/verify-release.sh scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`,
    `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`, and `git diff --check`.

## R-S11c-10q work log -- Linux clipboard FUSE root-process denial

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `a184cb3c33299da3ee630ff677a9885c8c9a6c3d`.
  - The R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC checklist remains closed/gated. This slice closes a Linux service-adjacent
    privilege lifetime hazard found during the residual audit: a RustDesk process running as euid 0 could initialize
    the CLIPRDR file-copy FUSE path and become the FUSE mount owner.
- Finding:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs` initialized the file clipboard FUSE context by preparing the
    fixed `/tmp/<app>/cliprdr-*` mountpoint and then calling `fuser::spawn_mount2`.
  - The installed desktop path normally launches the serving `--server --service-owned-server` child as the active
    user through `run_as_user(...)`, but the no-desktop fallback uses `crate::run_me(["--server",
    "--service-owned-server"])` from the root service path.
  - At that time, `res/rustdesk.service` ran as `User=root`, kept a FUSE-only mount syscall exception, and did not drop
    `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`. That shape was intentionally narrower than upstream shell/PATH mount helpers, but before this
    slice it still allowed a root/headless RustDesk process to enter the FUSE mount path.
  - The viewer/client file-clipboard path also calls the same `fuse::init_fuse_context(true)` helper, so a
    root-launched viewer had the same root-process FUSE initializer even outside installed-service hosting.
- Research basis:
  - Linux `capabilities(7)` documents `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` as covering `mount(2)` and `umount(2)` and warns that it is
    overloaded. Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html
  - Linux `fuse(4)` / kernel FUSE docs describe the `/dev/fuse` userspace-filesystem model. Sources:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man4/fuse.4.html and
    https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/next/filesystems/fuse.html
  - `mount.fuse3(8)` documents the non-privileged FUSE helper model and the distinction between ordinary-user
    mounts and root-owned mount authority. Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/mount.fuse3.8.html
  - systemd's execution/sandboxing model confirms that service unit capabilities and syscall filters are launcher
    policy, not something the RustDesk binary can self-relax for the owner's terminal later. Source:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemd.exec.html
- Authority model:
  - The shipped non-root desktop user-server/viewer path may continue to own CLIPRDR file-copy FUSE through the
    existing FUSE/fusermount behavior.
  - A RustDesk process running as euid 0 may not initialize clipboard FUSE at all. Root/headless RustDesk keeps text
    clipboard and file transfer, but not the FUSE-backed CLIPRDR file-copy mount.
  - The eventual full cure remains a fixed-target, short-lived FUSE mount helper using an fd-passing shape so the
    long-lived root service can drop daemon-wide `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`; this slice is deliberately the root-process
    denial layer, not a false claim that the helper design is complete.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs:64`: `init_fuse_context` now calls
    `require_unprivileged_linux_fuse()?` before mountpoint selection, mountpoint setup, stale cleanup, or
    `fuser::spawn_mount2`.
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs:106`: Linux reads the effective uid with `libc::geteuid()` and
    fails closed with `CliprdrError::CliprdrInit` when the process is euid 0. Non-Linux platforms return `Ok(())`.
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs`: added a pure policy helper and regression test proving euid 0
    is rejected and nonzero euid is admitted.
  - `scripts/verify.sh:2497`: added R-S11c-10q gates for early check placement, Linux helper shape, `geteuid`, pure
    policy helper, regression test, requirements/ledger text, README note, and fuser advisory accept reason.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, `libs/clipboard/README.md`, `deny.toml`, and
    `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded the Linux clipboard FUSE root-process denial and updated the
    requirements hash to `20a255e420cea3bf22aa6d6d73d1fb86e3ce9af17c01c414f695c4e4b9da7d8d`.
- Verification:
  - Targeted checks passed: `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check --config skip_children=true
    libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs`, `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/verify-release.sh
    scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`, `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`, `sha256sum requirements.html`, and
    `git diff --check`.
  - Full `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rustdesk_fork_target scripts/verify.sh` passed from the edited tree, and then
    passed again from clean committed `HEAD` after push:
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
  - Commit `77e2a2bd0a442851ec0cd27fbd878b61573a00d0`
    (`Refuse Linux clipboard FUSE in root processes`) was pushed to `origin/master`.
- Remaining residual:
  - Superseded by R-S11c-10r for clipboard FUSE. The service unit's remaining mount/CAP_SYS_ADMIN exposure belongs to
    the authenticated owner's root-terminal semantics, not file clipboard.

## R-S11c-10r work log -- Linux clipboard FUSE fixed-helper fd passing

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `77e2a2bd0a442851ec0cd27fbd878b61573a00d0`.
  - The R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC checklist remains closed/gated. This slice closes the clipboard-specific
    FUSE mount authority tail left by R-S11c-10q.
- Finding:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs` still called `fuser::spawn_mount2` after the euid-0 refusal.
  - `fuser 0.15.1` with `default-features = false` uses its pure-Rust mount backend. That backend first opens
    `/dev/fuse` and attempts direct `mount(2)`, then falls back to `fusermount` only after permission denial. Its
    helper resolver tries bare `fusermount3` / `fusermount` before fixed `/bin/...` candidates.
  - `fuser::Session::from_fd` is the correct public API for wrapping a separately mounted `/dev/fuse` fd, but it owns
    no mount guard. Therefore RustDesk must own unmount and thread join explicitly if it bypasses `spawn_mount2`.
- Research basis:
  - systemd `SystemCallFilter` is inherited by child processes and denied syscalls normally terminate unless
    `SystemCallErrorNumber` changes that policy. Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/systemd.exec.5.html
  - Linux `capabilities(7)` lists `mount(2)`/`umount(2)` under the overloaded `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`. Source:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html
  - FUSE kernel documentation describes non-privileged FUSE mounts and the mount-owner model. Source:
    https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/next/filesystems/fuse.html
  - `fusermount3(1)` / `mount.fuse3(8)` describe the helper used for non-privileged FUSE mounts and unmounts. Sources:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/fusermount3.1.html and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/mount.fuse3.8.html
- Authority model:
  - Linux clipboard FUSE is non-root only and owner-only.
  - RustDesk does not call direct `mount(2)` for clipboard FUSE and does not let fuser choose helper executable
    identity through PATH.
  - The setuid/helper authority is constrained to fixed absolute `fusermount3`/`fusermount` candidates resolved to
    canonical helper targets. RustDesk checks both the fixed candidate parent and canonical target parent are
    root-owned and not group/world-writable, then requires the executable metadata to be root-owned, executable, and
    not group/world-writable. The helper receives only the already validated `/tmp/<app>/cliprdr-*` mountpoint after
    `--`.
  - The received `/dev/fuse` fd is accepted only through a validated `SCM_RIGHTS` control message, marked close-on-exec,
    and wrapped in `fuser::Session::from_fd(..., SessionACL::Owner)`.
  - `AutoUnmount`, `AllowOther`, and `AllowRoot` are rejected for this clipboard path because widening the kernel mount
    or depending on `/etc/fuse.conf user_allow_other` is not part of the desired local authority model.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs`: replaced `fuser::spawn_mount2` with `mount_with_fixed_fusermount`.
  - Added trusted fixed helper selection over `/usr/bin/fusermount3`, `/bin/fusermount3`, `/usr/bin/fusermount`, and
    `/bin/fusermount`, resolving the selected candidate to a checked canonical target before execution; no bare
    helper command fallback remains.
  - Added `_FUSE_COMMFD` socket passing, `recvmsg` / `SCM_RIGHTS` validation, fd close-on-exec handling, and
    `fuser::Session::from_fd(..., SessionACL::Owner)`.
  - Added `ClipboardFuseSession` / `ClipboardFuseMountGuard`, which unmount with direct no-follow `umount2` plus fixed
    helper fallback and join the FUSE thread without `unwrap`.
  - Updated stale cleanup to share the same fixed-helper fallback used by normal teardown.
  - Updated `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, `res/rustdesk.service`, `libs/clipboard/README.md`,
    `deny.toml`, `scripts/verify.sh`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`.
- Verification:
  - Targeted local checks passed: `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check --config skip_children=true
    libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs`, `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/verify-release.sh
    scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`, `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`, `git diff --check`, and
    `sha256sum requirements.html`.
  - The finalized `requirements.html` hash is
    `1bcd40f37ec8d9f84de82344158887904879b27035cc8086a93c6537413412e0`.
  - The host `cargo test -p clipboard --features unix-file-copy-paste --lib fuse` did not reach this slice because the
    ambient host lacks OpenSSL pkg-config metadata (`openssl.pc`/`libssl-dev`), so it is not counted as evidence.
  - Targeted docker tests passed: `cargo test -p clipboard --features unix-file-copy-paste --lib fuse` with 11 FUSE
    tests, including the canonical-helper relative-path regression.
  - Broader docker compile passed: `cargo check --features linux-pkg-config,unix-file-copy-paste`.
  - Full `scripts/verify.sh` passed from the edited tree:
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
  - Commit `1284f139e06f63b125e9da86bafe4116f7b5c0ad`
    (`Use fixed fusermount fd passing for clipboard FUSE`) was pushed to `origin/master`.
  - Full `scripts/verify.sh` passed again from clean committed `HEAD` after push:
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.

## R-S11c-18 work log -- macOS privileged installer ACL enforcement provenance

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `1284f139e06f63b125e9da86bafe4116f7b5c0ad`.
  - The R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC checklist remains closed/gated; no currently listed R-S11c-10 Linux probe
    remains open. This slice closes the macOS installer-side ACL provenance exception left after R-S11c-17.
- Audit findings that shaped the slice:
  - Read-only macOS agent `019f4f4f-3004-7dd3-ad5f-5375b3c1e4ce` found no reachable macOS local-to-root credential
    write or LaunchAgent snapshot bypass in current source. It identified availability/correctness hardening leads:
    accept-time macOS `_service` trust checks can run synchronous codesign work on the single-thread IPC accept loop;
    macOS begin-password-change stores a bounded pending password before Authorization Services proof; and the live
    LaunchAgent process argv proof is prefix-shaped even though the parsed root-owned plist proof is exact-length.
  - Read-only Linux/Unix agent `019f4f4e-9fb3-7bb1-837e-207143860e7c` found no direct remaining local-unprivileged-to-root
    service/helper privilege escalation. It recorded false-positive or consistency leads: fixed `/usr/bin/pkcheck`
    lacks the newer canonical-helper resolver pattern; Unix terminal chooses `$SHELL` before fixed shells but the
    shipped Linux service path does not forward attacker-controlled `SHELL`; macOS install still uses quoted
    admin-authorized AppleScript shell fragments; and some Linux helper checks are lighter than the FUSE helper trust
    checks.
- Finding:
  - `src/platform/privileges_scripts/install.scpt` still proved helper ACL-free state by running absolute
    `/bin/ls -lde` and piping the human-readable formatter output into `/usr/bin/awk 'NR > 1 {exit 1}'`.
  - This was not a demonstrated command-injection primitive: paths were AppleScript-quoted and command paths were
    absolute. It was still the wrong authority model for the privileged installer because ACL state was derived from a
    formatter/parser convention after R-S11c-17 had already moved runtime ACL trust to native ACL APIs.
- Research basis:
  - Apple documents macOS filesystem ACLs as a separate access-control mechanism evaluated before Unix mode bits in
    the normal filesystem permission decision:
    https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/FileManagement/Conceptual/FileSystemProgrammingGuide/FileSystemDetails/FileSystemDetails.html
  - Apple's `acl(3)` documentation describes the libc ACL API as the userland interface for retrieving, setting, and
    validating ACLs; that is the runtime model already used by R-S11c-17:
    https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/acl.3.html
  - Apple's shell documentation warns that command lookup through PATH is security-sensitive; this slice did not have
    PATH lookup, but it reinforces the existing project rule that privileged command identity and authority decisions
    must be explicit rather than parser-derived:
    https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/OpenSource/Conceptual/ShellScripting/CommandLInePrimer/CommandLine.html
- Authority model:
  - The admin-authorized installer may use the shell to lay down privileged service state, but it should not parse a
    display formatter to decide ACL trust.
  - The bundled helper source is verified as a non-symlink executable with the pinned helper code-signing requirement.
  - ACL-free state is an enforced postcondition on the service-owned paths RustDesk installs and owns:
    `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools` and `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.carriez.rustdesk_service`.
  - The script clears ACLs with checked `/bin/chmod -N` before verifying root:wheel ownership, non-group/world-writable
    mode, executable state, byte identity with the bundled helper, and the helper code-signing requirement.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/privileges_scripts/install.scpt`: removed both `ls -lde | awk` ACL parser uses; kept bundled helper
    file/executable/write-bit and code-signing checks; made the deployed helper verification loop clear ACLs through
    a checked `/bin/chmod -N "$service_component"` postcondition before owner/mode checks.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: now require the deployed-helper ACL postcondition,
    require the R-S11c-18 requirements/status disposition, and reject reintroduced `/bin/ls -lde` or `NR > 1 {exit 1}`
    installer ACL parser shapes.
  - `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: recorded R-S11c-18 and removed the stale runtime-row implication
    that installer ACL parsing remained only a separate exception.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/apple-conform-check.sh scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed with `requirements.html` hash

## R-S11c-19 work log -- macOS LaunchAgent live argv authority

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `17e73c63a98d2845b0581a7198188028b0c0bcb7`.
  - R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC checklist remains closed/gated. This slice closes a correctness gap in the macOS
    runtime snapshot proof left by exact root-owned plist proof versus prefix-shaped live argv proof.
- Finding:
  - `src/ipc.rs::macos_peer_is_service_owned_server_blocking` proved the live LaunchAgent role by checking only
    `process.cmd().get(1) == "--server"` and `get(2) == SERVICE_OWNED_SERVER_ARG`.
  - That accepted extra live arguments even though
    `macos_service_owned_server_launch_agent_plist_value_is_expected` already required exact `ProgramArguments`
    length and values.
  - This was not a demonstrated local-to-root path because installed-app/helper identity and trusted root-owned
    launchd plist proof were already load-bearing. It was still the wrong authority model for a root credential
    snapshot boundary.
- Research basis:
  - Apple documents per-user launch agents as launchd jobs loaded from `/Library/LaunchAgents` and user agent
    locations, with `ProgramArguments` as the tokenized program/argument array for launchd job execution:
