  - LaunchDaemon returns the root credential snapshot only to an installed signed app/trusted helper peer whose live
    command vector exactly matches the service-owned server role args and whose pid launchd reports for the trusted
    root-owned plist.
  - Extra live arguments are not part of the trusted job shape and fail closed before credential snapshot delivery.
  - `argv[0]` string equality is not made the live load-bearing proof because executable identity is already proved by
    `_service` installed-app/helper path/signing and parsed plist proof; the live helper enforces arity and role args.

  - This was not a demonstrated local unprivileged-to-root exploit in the shipped Linux systemd unit because the unit
    does not explicitly pass `SHELL`, and Terminal remains an intended full-control capability for the authenticated
    owner. It was still the wrong authority model for a root/service-adjacent process path: executable identity for
    the shell must not come from ambient environment state or an unproven fallback string.
- Research basis:
  - `getpwnam(3)` / `getpwuid(3)` define the password-database records that carry the login shell field:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/getpwnam.3.html
  - `passwd(5)` documents the shell field as the program run at login and notes that an empty shell defaults to
    `/bin/sh`; it also records `/etc/passwd` as superuser-writable:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/passwd.5.html
  - `exec(3)` documents PATH search for `exec*p` forms without a slash, reinforcing that shell identity here should
    be a slash-bearing absolute executable path and not a bare name:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/exec.3.html
  - `systemd.exec(5)` documents that system services do not automatically inherit the manager environment by default;
    environment import is explicit through unit directives:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/systemd.exec.5.html
- Authority model:
  - Terminal remains a high-power authenticated-owner capability. This slice does not narrow Terminal semantics.
  - Unix terminal shell executable identity is chosen only from project-owned fixed absolute candidates, never from
    `SHELL`, current directory, or PATH.
  - The selected candidate is canonicalized, its candidate/canonical parent directories must be root-owned and not
    group/world-writable, the canonical executable must be a root-owned regular file, not group/world-writable, and
    executable by some class. If no candidate satisfies that authority proof, terminal open fails closed.
- Implemented:
  - `src/server/terminal_service.rs`: added fixed candidate sets for Android, macOS, and other non-Windows Unix
    builds; added clean-absolute path, trusted parent, trusted executable, canonicalization, and UTF-8 conversion
    helpers; removed `SHELL`, bare fixed-shell existence checks, and unconditional `/bin/sh` success fallback.
  - Added tests covering clean absolute candidate shape, rejection of relative/parent-traversal paths, and discovery of
    a trusted candidate in the Linux verifier environment.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: added R-S11c-20 source gates requiring the trusted Unix
    resolver, root/mode/executable checks, tests, requirements/status disposition, and absence of ambient or bare shell
    fallback shapes.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded R-S11c-20 and updated the
    requirements hash.

## R-S11e-1 work log -- Linux pkcheck executable provenance

- Baseline:
  - Current pre-slice HEAD was `b1c1ae78a2d7606417df078b77102b877933e6df`.
  - R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC checklist remains closed/gated. A read-only explorer audit at this baseline found
    no remaining concrete non-Windows local privilege escalation or service-owned command-provenance defect in the
    scoped Linux/macOS helper, lifecycle, package, terminal, and clipboard surfaces.
- Finding:
  - `src/ipc.rs::linux_pkcheck_authorizes_service_owned_password_change` launched `/usr/bin/pkcheck` directly as the
    Linux service-owned password authorization checker.
  - The polkit subject/action model was already correct: the service constructs a SO_PEERCRED-derived
    `pid,start-time,uid` subject, checks the exact RustDesk action with `--allow-user-interaction`, and commits only
    through the root-service-to-service-owned-main-server path.
  - This was not a demonstrated local unprivileged-to-root exploit on normal Debian/Ubuntu systems because replacing
    `/usr/bin/pkcheck` or its parent already implies root-equivalent local compromise. It was still a weaker executable
    authority proof than the newer fixed-helper model used for service/root-adjacent commands.
- Research basis:
  - `pkcheck(1)` documents `pkcheck` as the command-line mechanism for checking whether a specified process or bus name
    is authorized for an action, with `--allow-user-interaction` allowing authentication prompts:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/polkit/docs/latest/pkcheck.1.html
  - `polkit(8)` describes polkit as an authorization API used by privileged mechanisms serving untrusted subjects, with
    mechanisms offloading decisions to the trusted polkit authority; it also defines `auth_admin` as administrative
    authentication and warns that `auth_self` is often insufficient on multi-user systems:
    https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/noble/man8/polkit.8.html
- Authority model:
  - The privileged RustDesk service may keep using polkit for Linux service-owned password authorization.
  - The executable used to query that authorization must be selected from the fixed authority path, not as an unchecked
    raw command string.
  - The fixed path is canonicalized; candidate and canonical parents must be root-owned directories that are not
    group/world-writable; the canonical helper must be a root-owned regular file that is not group/world-writable and
    has an executable mode bit. Missing or untrusted helper state fails the password-change request closed.
- Implemented:

    helpers, canonicalization, and use of `trusted_linux_pkcheck_path()` before spawning `pkcheck`.

## R-S11e-3 Linux helper canonical target provenance

- Finding closed:
  - The non-`pkcheck` Linux helper resolvers checked a fixed candidate path but returned and executed the original path
    string.
  - A fixed helper path that resolved through a symlink chain into a user-writable target directory could therefore let
    a privileged RustDesk process verify one helper target and execute a swapped target.
  - Affected app-side helper resolution included `sudo`, `env`, `w`, `xrandr`, `xdg-screensaver`, and `systemctl`.
    Shared helper resolution included `loginctl` and `notify-send` when used from privileged/root-adjacent code.
  - This is local-only under the audited call sites, but it is a local privilege-boundary issue because service/root
    RustDesk code may execute these helpers.
- Authority model:
  - Helper paths must be absolute and clean: root plus normal components only, with no relative, parent, current-dir, or
    prefix components.
  - Both the candidate parent and the canonical target parent must be root-owned directories that are not
    group/world-writable.
  - The canonical target must be a root-owned regular file that is not group/world-writable and has an executable mode
    bit.
  - The resolver returns the canonical `PathBuf`, and all helper spawns execute that canonical path. Missing or
    untrusted helper state fails closed.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/linux.rs`: converted Linux app helper resolution from boolean fixed-path checks to canonical
    `PathBuf` resolution; `sudo`/`env` call sites now execute the returned canonical paths.
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/platform/linux.rs`: applied the same canonical trusted-helper resolver to shared Linux helper
    commands.
  - Added tests for clean absolute path rejection and root/non-writable/executable metadata requirements in both
    resolver locations.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added tests/source gates for canonicalization, candidate/canonical parent trust, canonical file
    trust, executable-bit requirements, canonical-path return, and requirements/ledger disposition.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded R-S11e-3 and updated the

## R-S11d-32 Windows elevated command-file reopen identity

- Finding closed:
  - Windows EXE install/uninstall/service-install/service-uninstall generated elevated `.bat` and `.vbs` command
    files, wrote them, closed the writer, then reopened the same pathname read-only with `FILE_SHARE_READ` before
    handing the path to elevated `cmd.exe` / `cscript.exe`.
  - The read handle protected the file only after reopen. A same-owner local process watching the command directory
    could race the close/reopen gap and replace the file or modify it in place before the read lock was acquired.
  - DACL-only protection is insufficient for this object because Windows gives the owner implicit DACL-control
    authority; path-only reopen is not a stable identity proof across a local same-owner race.
- Research basis:
  - Microsoft `CreateFile` documentation states that share options remain in effect only until the handle is closed,
    and that `FILE_SHARE_READ` does not permit later write/delete opens while the handle is live:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilea
  - Microsoft object-owner documentation states that an object's owner implicitly has `WRITE_DAC` and can modify the
    DACL:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/owner-of-a-new-object
  - Microsoft `ReOpenFile` documentation confirms that reopening with a new sharing mode cannot request a sharing mode
    that conflicts with a still-open writer; that rules out a no-race downgrade from writer to read-only/no-write-share
    by keeping the same write handle open:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-reopenfile
- Authority model:
  - Before the write handle is dropped, record the file identity from the live handle and the exact bytes that were
    written.
  - After reopening the pathname read-only with `FILE_SHARE_READ`, prove that the reopened handle has the same file
    identity and the same byte length/digest.
  - Keep the verified read handle live while the elevated command consumes the path, preserving write/delete sharing
    denial after verification.
  - Replacement or in-place mutation during the close/reopen gap fails closed before elevation.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: added `InstallerCommandFileIdentity`, `installer_command_file_identity`,
    `installer_command_digest`, and `reopen_verified_installer_command_file`.
  - `write_cmds` now owns the exact command bytes, writes and syncs those bytes, captures file identity/digest/length
    from the live writer, then verifies the reopened read handle before returning the command file object.
  - Added Windows regression tests for byte-exact digesting and identity equality fields.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added R-S11d-32 source gates for the handle identity query, digest proof, verified reopen,
    write-handle capture, drift failures, tests, and requirements/ledger disposition.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded R-S11d-32 and updated the
    requirements hash to `c0018e3bfc8a7f0e4459284c5638026a93f0d13df65133889e2819e5fd3ab200`.
- Verification before commit:
  - `rustfmt --edition 2021 src/platform/windows.rs` passed.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh` passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - Full `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rustdesk_fork_target scripts/verify.sh` passed from the edited tree:
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
- Commit / post-commit verification:

    (`Bind Windows elevated command files across reopen`) was pushed to `origin/master`.
  - `HEAD` and `origin/master` both pointed to `97b70c1d4da7380746412769e2dc1d8bdadbbd95` with a clean working tree.

## R-S11e-2 macOS _service client-side server authentication

- Finding closed:
  - macOS `_service` receivers authenticated callers, but clients connected to the shared service socket path before
    proving that the peer was the installed privileged helper.
  - A same-user local fake server could win the service-socket race while the helper was absent. The service-owned
    LaunchAgent runtime-snapshot client could then accept attacker-chosen password storage/salt, and the GUI/CLI
    password-change client could send the proposed plaintext password before Authorization Services completed.
  - This is local-only, but it crosses the service credential boundary before the client authenticates the server.
- Authority model:
  - macOS `_service` client connections fail closed unless the connected server proves as uid 0 and as the trusted
    `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.carriez.rustdesk_service` helper.
  - The helper proof reuses the existing privileged-helper trust primitive: exact helper identity, root:wheel helper
    directory/file, non-group/world-writable metadata, executable bit, no symlinks, no extended ACLs, and pinned
    code-signing requirement.
  - No unauthenticated compatibility fallback is allowed.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: added `ensure_macos_service_server_is_trusted`.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: macOS `connect_with_path()` authenticates `POSTFIX_SERVICE` peers immediately after connect and
    before returning a usable `ConnectionTmpl`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: added source gates for the root uid gate, peer executable
    proof, privileged-helper trust call, connect-path wiring, and requirements/ledger disposition.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded R-S11e-2 and updated the

## R-S11b-2e/R-S11c-1f macOS service-owned password single authorized request

- Finding closed:
  - The macOS service-owned unattended-password path used a two-step begin/challenge/finish protocol where the
    plaintext candidate password was sent to the root helper before the Authorization Services external form was
    obtained and verified.
  - Even though the root helper still enforced the final authorization check before writing the root credential
    store, the protocol cached a pending plaintext password in root service state and created a request-id
    state machine that was not the correct authority shape for credential entry.
  - The operation should be a single authorized request: the user authorizes the RustDesk-specific right first,
    then the client sends the candidate password and external authorization form together to the privileged
    service.
- Authority model:
  - The active desktop/CLI process obtains the RustDesk-specific
    `com.carriez.RustDesk.set-unattended-password` right before disclosing the password to `_service`.
  - The root LaunchDaemon verifies the external form non-interactively, with a non-shared timeout-zero
    admin-only right, then writes directly to the root LaunchDaemon credential store.
  - There is no pending plaintext cache, no request-id prompt API, no generic
    `kAuthorizationRightExecute` fallback, and no main-channel or ordinary-config fallback.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc.rs`: replaced the macOS begin/challenge/finish messages with
    `Data::RequestMacosServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange { password, authorization }`.
  - The client obtains `service_owned_unattended_password_authorization()` before sending the password.
  - The service receiver validates channel, authorization-right readiness, password size, and
    `AuthorizationCreateFromExternalForm`/right verification before calling `Config::set_permanent_password`.
  - Removed the pending request map, request TTL/expiry task, password zeroing wrapper, request-id matching,
    cancellation send, and challenge/finish allowlist entries.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` gate the single-request shape, authorization-before-send
    ordering, absence of the old pending-cache/challenge API, no execute-right fallback, and main-channel denial.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` were updated for the tightened
    R-S11b-2e/R-S11c-1f closure.
- Commit:
  - Commit `fadc6aea2e4956bb5fba5c922dcd670ade23bca9`
    (`Authorize macOS service password before send`) was pushed to `origin/master`.

## R-S11e-4 macOS _service accept-loop blocking-proof offload

- Finding closed:
  - macOS receiver-side `_service` admission already required the active/root peer uid gate, installed-app peer
    proof, trusted PrivilegedHelperTools helper proof, filesystem metadata checks, ACL checks, and pinned
    code-signing requirements before any privileged service message could be honored.
  - The listener, however, ran on a current-thread Tokio runtime and performed those potentially blocking
    filesystem and code-signing checks inline before spawning the per-connection task.
  - A local connector could therefore stall service IPC accepting while proof work ran or blocked. This was a
    local availability hardening issue, not a credential-write bypass or remote issue.
- Authority model:
  - The accept loop may capture kernel-supplied peer facts and reserve bounded work, but it must not run blocking
    proof work inline.
  - The per-connection task must complete the same fail-closed proof before reading the first `_service` frame.
  - Exhausted authorization capacity drops the connection before spawning unbounded work.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: split service-scoped IPC authorization into a typed
    `ServiceScopedIpcAuthorization` snapshot and `authorize_service_scoped_ipc_authorization_snapshot`.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: added a bounded macOS `_service` authorization semaphore and moved the executable/code-signing
    proof into `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` inside the per-connection task.
  - The connection task returns before the first `stream.next().await` if the blocking task fails, uid admission
    fails, or executable/trust proof fails.
  - Linux keeps the existing synchronous service admission path, and macOS `_url` sender proof remains separate.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` gate the snapshot type, bounded authorization slot,
    `spawn_blocking` task authorizer, accept-loop ordering, no pre-spawn macOS blocking proof, and the
    requirements/ledger disposition.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` were updated for R-S11e-4.
- Commit:
  - Commit `4ddcdc2918bad532317ae2798b31fddeb653b30f`
    (`Offload macOS service IPC auth proof`) was pushed to `origin/master`.

## R-S11e-5 Linux service-owned main-server commit receiver proof

- Finding closed:
  - Linux installed-service password changes authorized the local requester through the typed `_service` polkit
    path, then sent `Data::CommitServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange` from the root service into the uid-scoped
    main IPC server selected by process/path routing.
  - The receiving main server rejected non-root commit senders, but the root service sender did not first prove
    that the connected main IPC peer was the service-launched `--server --service-owned-server` process.
  - A same-user local process running the real binary with the service-owned marker could race the uid endpoint.
    This did not bypass polkit requester authorization and was not remote, but it could receive the proposed
    service-owned password before sender-side receiver authentication.
- Research basis:
  - Linux `SO_PEERCRED` provides peer pid/uid/gid for connected Unix sockets as captured at connect/listen/socketpair
    time.
  - `/proc/<pid>/environ` is initial exec environment and is visible to same-uid contexts, so an environment marker
    is not treated as a secret. It is only a service-parent claim that must be paired with live ancestry proof.
- Authority model:
  - Requester authorization and commit receiver authentication are separate mandatory proofs.
  - The root service launches legitimate service-owned main servers with an explicit parent-service claim.
  - Before sending the password, the root service proves the connected peer by kernel peer credentials, current
    executable identity, exact command shape, the service-parent claim, and live `/proc` ancestry back to the
    current root service process.
  - Missing, stale, wrong-argv, wrong-parent, or non-descendant receivers fail closed before the password leaves
    the root service.
- Implemented:
  - `src/common.rs`: added `SERVICE_OWNED_SERVER_LAUNCH_PARENT_ENV`.
  - `src/platform/linux.rs`: added `service_owned_server_launch_env()` and propagates the parent-service claim for
    both active-user and headless/root service-owned server launches.
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: added exact argv validation and
    `authenticate_linux_service_owned_main_server`, using SO_PEERCRED-derived process identity, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`,
    `/proc/<pid>/environ`, and `linux_process_has_ancestor`.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: `commit_service_owned_unattended_password_change` authenticates the connected main server before
    sending `CommitServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` gates launch-parent propagation in both launch paths, the receiver authenticator, exact argv
    helper, live ancestor proof, commit-path ordering, regression test, and requirements/ledger disposition.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` were updated for R-S11e-5.
- Verification:
  - Fast gates passed: rustfmt check for the edited Rust files, `bash -n` for verifier scripts, `git diff --check`,
    and `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`.
  - Full edited-tree verifier passed:
    `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rustdesk_fork_target scripts/verify.sh`
    with `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
  - After commit and push, `HEAD` and `origin/master` both pointed to
    `786b61b83ead29d390572aa5a6990a95407c9456`, and the same full verifier passed again from the clean pushed
    commit.
- Commit:

    (`Authenticate Linux service password commit receiver`) was pushed to `origin/master`.

## R-S11e-6 Linux _service client-side server authentication

- Finding closed:
  - Linux service-owned unattended-password changes already used a typed `_service` request, polkit requester
    authorization inside the real root service, and a sender-side proof before the root service commits into the
    service-owned main server.
  - The GUI/CLI client still connected to the shared `/tmp/<app>-service/ipc_service` endpoint and sent
    `Data::RequestServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange(password)` before proving that the connected `_service`
    receiver was the root RustDesk service.
  - A local fake `_service` listener could receive the proposed plaintext password if it won the shared socket path
    while the legitimate root-owned service socket/parent was absent, such as after service stop, crash,
    disablement, or `/tmp` cleanup before service restart. This was local-only and did not bypass polkit or remote
    authentication, but it crossed the service-owned credential boundary before receiver authentication.
- Research basis:
  - Linux `SO_PEERCRED` returns the peer process credentials for a connected Unix-domain socket, fixed at
    connect/listen/socketpair time.
  - `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` exposes the live process command vector unless the process is a zombie.
  - The shipped Linux systemd unit is `Type=simple` with `ExecStart=/usr/bin/rustdesk --service`, so the service
    process that owns `_service` credential authority has the exact `--service` command shape.
- Authority model:
  - `_service` is mutually authenticated on Linux before any secret-bearing service request is sent.
  - The client may send a service-owned password request only after proving the connected peer is uid 0, the current
    RustDesk executable, the exact root service command shape, and root-owned non-writable executable state.
  - Missing service proof is not a compatibility condition; it is a fail-closed refusal to send the password.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: added `ensure_linux_service_server_is_trusted`, exact `--service` argv validation, and
    root-owned non-group/world-writable executable/parent predicates with regression tests.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: Linux `connect_with_path(..., POSTFIX_SERVICE)` authenticates the connected `_service` receiver
    before returning a `ConnectionTmpl`, so `connect_service()` callers cannot send first.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the Linux `_service` authenticator, root uid gate, exact argv helper, executable
    trust predicates/tests, connect-path wiring, request-before-send ordering through authenticated
    `connect_service`, and requirements/ledger disposition.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` were updated for R-S11e-6.

## R-S11c-10j Debian maintainer-script daemon-reload semantics

- Finding closed:
  - `res/DEBIAN/postinst` and `res/DEBIAN/prerm` ran `deb-systemd-invoke daemon-reload >/dev/null` under
    `set -e`.
  - The repo verifier treated that string as the expected good shape, so the release/source gate would preserve
    the same helper use in built control scripts.
  - Current Debian `init-system-helpers` documents unit-less `daemon-reload`, but the local Ubuntu
    `init-system-helpers 1.66ubuntu1` helper still rejects unit-less invocation at its top-level argument-count
    check, and Ubuntu 18.04's official `init-system-helpers 1.51` package, which matches the repo's bionic
    build baseline, documents only start/stop/restart with unit files. The package lifecycle claim was therefore
    too broad for the baseline this fork actually builds and ships.
- Research basis:
  - Debian's current `deb-systemd-invoke(1p)` describes `deb-systemd-invoke` as a policy-rc.d-aware systemctl
    wrapper for maintainer scripts and now lists `daemon-reload|daemon-reexec` as actions.
  - Ubuntu 18.04 `init-system-helpers 1.51` was inspected from the official Ubuntu archive package; its
    `deb-systemd-invoke` script requires at least an action plus unit and documents only `start|stop|restart`.
  - `systemctl --help` on this host lists `daemon-reload` as a manager-state command, not a unit start/stop
    action. The correct split is policy-aware Debian helpers for unit state/actions, and a checked systemd manager
    reload for unit-file table refresh.
- Authority model:
  - Package lifecycle completion is status-authoritative: install/remove may not mask helper failure or encode a
    helper action that is invalid on the supported baseline.
  - `deb-systemd-helper` owns Debian enable/disable/purge state, `deb-systemd-invoke` owns policy-aware unit
    start/stop, and `/bin/systemctl --system daemon-reload` owns manager reload.
  - Missing or failing manager reload is a hard maintainer-script failure, not a compatibility branch.
- Implemented:
  - `res/DEBIAN/postinst` and `res/DEBIAN/prerm`: replaced `deb-systemd-invoke daemon-reload` with the fixed
    checked `/bin/systemctl --system daemon-reload` command.
  - `scripts/verify-debian-maintainer-scripts.py`: added a reusable maintainer-script semantic gate that rejects
    `deb-systemd-invoke daemon-reload`, rejects any other raw `systemctl` use, validates the helper action set,
    and asserts the preinst/postinst/prerm/postrm lifecycle order.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: R-S11c-10j now expects the fixed manager reload command and calls the semantic gate over
    `res/DEBIAN`.
  - `scripts/build-debian.sh`: extracted `.deb` control scripts are still byte-compared to `res/DEBIAN`, and now
    also pass the same semantic gate before artifact hashing.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` were updated to remove the old
    `deb-systemd-invoke`/daemon-reload claim and record the helper/manager split.
- Verification:
  - Positive gate passed: `python3 scripts/verify-debian-maintainer-scripts.py --scripts-dir res/DEBIAN`.
  - Negative gate passed: a temporary copy with `deb-systemd-invoke daemon-reload` was rejected with
    `daemon-reload must not use deb-systemd-invoke` and `invalid deb-systemd-invoke action`.
  - Syntax/format gates passed: `python3 -m py_compile scripts/verify-debian-maintainer-scripts.py`,
    `bash -n scripts/build-debian.sh scripts/verify.sh res/DEBIAN/preinst res/DEBIAN/postinst res/DEBIAN/prerm res/DEBIAN/postrm`,
    `git diff --check`, and `git diff --cached --check`.
  - Native-codec companion gate passed after the requirements hash update:
    `bash scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`.
  - Full verifier passed before commit, and again after commit/push from the clean pushed commit:
    `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rustdesk_fork_target scripts/verify.sh`
    with `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
- Commit:
  - Commit `c8876adc8f8b49e300575dc1e05ee86a61d0077c`
    (`Fix Debian maintainer daemon reload semantics`) was pushed to `origin/master`.

## R-S11e-5 Linux service-owned main-server commit verifier hardening

- Finding closed:
  - The Linux root-service-to-main password commit path already had the correct runtime order:
    `UserMainIpcScope`, `connect(ms_timeout, "")`, `authenticate_linux_service_owned_main_server(&c)`,
    then `Data::CommitServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange(value)`.
  - The source gate still only grepped for the authenticator name in `src/ipc.rs`. That proved the helper existed
    somewhere in the file, but did not structurally prove the password-bearing commit send was after the receiver
    proof in `commit_service_owned_unattended_password_change`.
- Authority model:
  - The root service may disclose the service-owned unattended password candidate to the main IPC receiver only after
    selecting the uid-scoped main server endpoint and proving the connected peer is the service-launched
    `--server --service-owned-server` descendant of the current root service process.
  - The verifier should fail closed if the function is missing, duplicated, reordered, sends before receiver proof,
    drops the Linux cfg guard, hides send/read errors, or reads the result before the password-bearing send is awaited.
- Implemented:
  - `scripts/verify-linux-service-password-ipc.py`: added a focused structural source-order verifier for
    `commit_service_owned_unattended_password_change`. It extracts the function body, requires a unique scoped
    connect, Linux receiver-authentication call, password-bearing commit send, awaited send, and result read in that
    order, and includes negative self-tests for send-before-auth and missing-auth shapes.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: replaced the weak authenticator-name grep with the structural verifier as part of the
    R-S11b/R-S11e password IPC gate.
  - `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: tightened R-S11e-5 wording to say the gate proves structural
    commit-path ordering.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: updated the requirements hash after the requirements wording change.
- Verification:

    (`Harden Linux service password IPC verifier`) was pushed to `origin/master`.

## R-S19 voice-call close/reset authority hardening

- Finding closed:
  - Online CVE review for `CVE-2026-58056` re-focused the R-S19 audit on session-type capability
    bleed. The named FileTransfer input/screen-capture CVE was already closed in this fork, but the same
    source sweep found one remaining voice-call state edge.
  - `src/server/connection.rs` gated `VoiceCallRequest(is_connect=true)` to Remote/ViewCamera and gated
    peer-to-host audio playback on `voice_calling`, but `VoiceCallRequest(is_connect=false)` and CM
    `Data::CloseVoiceCall` called `close_voice_call()` without proving that this connection was a
    Remote/ViewCamera voice-call owner.
  - `on_close()` also reset the global voice-call input device for every connection type, so a FileTransfer
    or Terminal session teardown could still mutate cross-session voice-call input state.
- Impact:
  - Not a root/LPE path and not audio injection: narrow sessions still could not start a voice call, accept
    one, or feed audio frames.
  - It was a real R-S19 authority mismatch: voice-call close/reset is peer-triggerable state and must be
    owned by the Remote/ViewCamera session type that owns the call.
- Authority model:
  - Voice-call start, accept/refuse, peer close, CM close, and teardown reset are one capability family.
  - Only an authenticated Remote/ViewCamera connection may drive that family.
  - A close/reset is accepted only if that connection has pending or active voice-call state; unrelated
    session close is not a voice-call input-reset authority.
- Implemented:
  - `src/server/connection.rs`: added `can_drive_voice_call()`; `handle_voice_call()` now rejects
    non-voice session types; `close_voice_call()` returns `bool` and fails closed unless the connection is
    Remote/ViewCamera with pending or active state; CM close sends a peer close only when the state actually
    closed; `on_close()` resets the global voice-call input device only for an active voice-call owner.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: R-S19 now gates the voice-call authority helper, Remote/ViewCamera predicate,
    accept guard, result-bearing close, pending/active-state close condition, CM result gate, and teardown
    reset guard.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded Appendix C #83,
    the R-S19 status closure, and the updated requirements hash.

## R-S19 Linux FUSE file-content response provenance

- Finding closed:
  - The Linux `unix-file-copy-paste` FUSE context is global per side, and each FUSE node stores the
    source `conn_id` whose remote file descriptor created that node.
  - `FuseServer::read_node` sent `FileContentsRequest` to `node.conn_id`, but incoming
    `FileContentsResponse` messages entered the shared bounded queue as bare `ClipboardFile` values and
    were matched only by `stream_id`.
  - `src/clipboard_file.rs::unix_file_clip::serve_clip_messages` had the response-supplying `conn_id`,
    but dropped it when calling `fuse::handle_file_content_response`.
- Impact:
  - Not unauthenticated, not root/LPE, and not unbounded memory growth: the inbound CLIPRDR file path is already
    gated to authenticated Remote/FileTransfer sessions with clipboard and file-transfer authority, and response
    admission remains bounded.
  - A second authorized file-clipboard-capable session on the same side could interfere with another session's
    local paste read by filling the response queue, and a guessed/colliding `stream_id` could satisfy the wrong
    connection's FUSE read.
- Authority model:
  - A FUSE file-content response is valid only for the active read route whose `(conn_id, stream_id)` matches the
    connection whose file descriptor produced the FUSE node and the fresh stream id whose read path sent the
    corresponding `FileContentsRequest`.
  - `stream_id` alone is not an authority token, and a global per-side response queue is not the right authority
    boundary for concurrent sessions.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/cs.rs`: added `FuseFileContentResponse { conn_id, clip }` and
    `FuseFileContentResponseRouter`. `FuseServer::read_node` generates a fresh stream id for each read and
    registers a bounded active response route keyed by `(conn_id, stream_id)` before sending
    `FileContentsRequest`; responses that do not match that fresh active key are dropped before they can enter
    another read path.
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/mod.rs`: changed `handle_file_content_response` to require `conn_id`
    and dispatch `FuseFileContentResponse` through the keyed router with nonblocking bounded admission.
  - `src/clipboard_file.rs`: passes the serving connection id into the Linux FUSE response handler.
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/fuse/cs.rs`: regression coverage proves bounded route admission,
    wrong-connection and wrong-stream rejection, stale route removal, duplicate active-route rejection, and a real
    `read_node` request/response path where wrong-session replies are ignored before the correct response supplies
    the bytes.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the keyed router type, caller wiring, fresh per-read stream ids, active-route
    registration, bounded nonblocking admission, stale global-queue absence, and regression tests.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: recorded Appendix C #84,
    the R-S19 status closure, and the updated requirements hash.

## R-S11d-33 Windows MSI deferred install-root provenance

- Finding closed:
  - The MSI package already declared `App.InstallFolder` as a private directory under `ProgramFiles6432Folder`
    with no browse/path-edit UI, so the current package did not expose a normal low-privilege path to pick an
    arbitrary LocalSystem install root.
  - The deferred no-impersonation custom-action DLL still consumed `CustomActionData` as if that package-level
    proof were sufficient inside the privileged action. `RemoveRuntimeGeneratedFiles` only rejected empty/root
    install-folder strings before deleting a fixed runtime broker name; `RemoveAmyuniIdd` concatenated raw
    install-folder text into the AMD64 fallback helper path before `CreateProcessW`; and `CreateStartService`
    returned success when service custom-action data lacked the expected semicolon delimiter.
- Impact:
  - Not a newly proven current-package low-privilege-to-SYSTEM exploit: the live WiX authoring keeps the install
    directory private and package-owned.
  - Real privileged-state correctness issue: malformed MSI execution-script data, a future directory-setter
    regression, or a transform/custom package could make a LocalSystem action skip service creation as success
    or execute/check cleanup/helper paths without a native install-root proof.
- Authority model:
  - Every deferred LocalSystem custom action that consumes install-root, service-command, cleanup, or helper path
    data must prove the exact authority locally before touching privileged state.
  - The MSI package's private directory declaration is necessary, but the native DLL still rejects malformed,
    relative, root, non-Program-Files, reparse, or mismatched service/helper shapes before action execution.
- Implemented:
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp`: added native path normalization through `GetFullPathNameW`,
    deferred install-folder validation against `FOLDERID_ProgramFiles` / `FOLDERID_ProgramFilesX86`, parent and
    target reparse rejection, non-reparse file/directory helpers, constrained service-name validation, and exact
    quoted `<exe> --service` parsing.
  - `CreateStartService` now treats missing/extra delimiters as fatal, validates the service identifier, proves
    the executable is the matching `<service>.exe` under a trusted MSI install folder, requires the executable to
    exist and not be a reparse point, and passes the normalized command to `CreateServiceW`.
  - `RemoveRuntimeGeneratedFiles` now uses the normalized trusted install folder for broker cleanup.
  - `RemoveAmyuniIdd` now validates the install folder before helper fallback, joins `usbmmidd_v2` with an
    explicit separator, and requires the helper directory and `deviceinstaller64.exe` to be non-reparse objects
    before `CreateProcessW`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added positive gates for the Program Files directory declaration, absence of directory
    setter UI/actions, native install-root validator, service command validator, malformed-data fatal path,
    normalized service creation command, normalized runtime cleanup root, and non-reparse Amyuni helper proof.
  - `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: recorded Appendix C #85 / R-S11d-33.

## Appendix C #87 AV1/libaom runtime quarantine

- Finding closed:
  - The previous native-codec ledger treated the 2026 aom advisories as an unresolved possible
    viewer-decoder issue. Current public descriptions and upstream patches localize the reviewed aom
    advisories to encoder/control surfaces, but the source still exposed AV1 as a selectable,
    advertiseable, negotiable runtime codec.
  - AV1 appeared at several policy boundaries: encoder capability advertisement, decoder capability
    advertisement, stored `codec-preference`, desktop/mobile/toolbar codec UI, server encoder config,
    direct-service startup prose, and the local `scrap` benchmark.
  - A password-correct hostile peer could still send `Av1s` frames. Even though the broader native
    decode residual remains accepted for VP8/VP9/Opus/zstd/CLIPRDR, AV1/libaom did not need to remain a
    supported runtime path.
- Impact:
  - This was not a new unauthenticated remote path and not a root/local privilege escalation path.
  - It was a correctness/security-policy gap: a linked native codec with open severe advisories remained
    exposed through runtime negotiation and stale UI/config choices even though the fork did not need AV1.
  - The fix affects every desktop/mobile source path that shares `scrap::codec`: Debian, Windows,
    Android, and the retained macOS/iOS source-conformance paths. AV1/libaom remains linked/watchlisted
    until a later dependency-removal or native-sandbox slice.
- Authority model:
  - AV1/libaom is not a supported runtime codec. The only allowed software video runtime codecs are VP8
    and VP9 unless a future deliberate design reintroduces AV1 behind a new reviewed authority boundary.
  - A peer's `ability_av1` bit, a stale local `codec-preference=av1`, a stale server `CodecFormat::AV1`,
    or a hostile inbound `Av1s` frame is not authority to instantiate libaom.
  - VP9 is the fallback for stale AV1 encoder/preference state; inbound AV1 is dropped before a native
    decoder or recorder worker is created.
- Implemented in this slice:
  - `libs/scrap/src/common/codec.rs`: AV1 policy is fail-closed; AV1 encode/decode capability bits are
    false; stale AV1 preference falls through to the normal software policy; `EncoderCfg::AOM` is rejected
    by `Encoder::new`; AV1 decoder construction is invalid; inbound `Av1s` validates only bounded frame
    shape and then fails without calling libaom; the old AV1 benchmark/probe function and config token are
    removed.
  - `src/client.rs`: AV1 is always locally unsupported before decoder/recorder worker creation.
  - `src/server/video_service.rs`: stale AV1 encoder config maps to VP9 rather than constructing libaom.
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/config.rs`: `codec-preference` no longer accepts `av1`.
  - `flutter/lib/**`, `src/flutter_ffi.rs`, and `src/ui_session_interface.rs`: AV1 is removed from codec
    UI/session menu surfaces and from the FFI codec menu JSON.
  - `libs/scrap/examples/benchmark.rs`: local AV1/libaom benchmark instantiation is deleted.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: Appendix C #87 records
    the AV1/libaom runtime quarantine while leaving the broader native-decode residual honest.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the capability tests, decoder-disabled test, fail-closed policy function,
    config/UI/session absence, server fallback, benchmark/probe deletion, and docs/status/watch ledger.

## Appendix C #88 AV1/libaom dependency removal

- Finding closed:
  - Appendix C #87 made AV1/libaom unreachable as a runtime codec, but the native dependency still existed in
    the build graph: `vcpkg.json`, `res/vcpkg/aom`, `libs/scrap/src/common/aom.rs`, the bindgen input

  - That was correct as a short-lived quarantine but not the final design. AV1 is not a product capability in
    this fork, so a linked libaom path was a future-regression hazard even when runtime policy rejected it.
- Impact:
  - This was not a new remote path and not a local privilege escalation path.
  - It was a supply-chain/native-attack-surface correctness gap: a native codec with recent severe advisories
    remained buildable and linkable even though the fork no longer needs AV1.
  - Scope is every desktop/mobile source path that shared `scrap` and every release build path that stages
    vcpkg natives: Debian, Windows, Android, and retained Apple source-conformance checks.
- Authority model:
  - AV1 remains only a protocol/wire enum. A stale config value, peer capability bit, inbound `Av1s` frame, or

  - The retained software video codecs are VP8/VP9 through libvpx. The remaining Appendix C #2b native-decode

- Implemented in this slice:
  - Deleted `libs/scrap/src/common/aom.rs`, `libs/scrap/src/bindings/aom_ffi.h`, and `res/vcpkg/aom`.
  - Removed `aom` from `vcpkg.json`, `libs/scrap/build.rs`, `EncoderCfg`, fallback/i444 policy, vcpkg staging,
    Windows guest setup, Apple source-conformance stubs, dev-check dependencies, and operator README commands.
  - Removed `AOM_COMMIT` / `SHA512_AOM_3_12_1` from `scripts/pins.env` and narrowed R-B12(a) to retained
    libyuv distfile pinning.
  - Rewrote `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` so `aom` is a retired library, not an expected watched package.
  - Updated `requirements.html` Appendix C #88 and `HARDENING_STATUS.md` with the dependency-removal closure.
  - Strengthened `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` to fail on future source, FFI, bindgen,
    manifest, build-script, or ledger reintroduction of libaom.

## R-S11c-21 macOS privileged service template identity input

- Finding closed:
  - The macOS service install/uninstall path still rendered privileged AppleScript and launchd plist source by
    reading the live `NSBundle.bundleIdentifier` and by broad-replacing `rustdesk` / `RustDesk` in the embedded
    privileged templates.
  - The old path was `get_bundle_id()` -> `correct_app_name()` -> substituted `install.scpt` / `uninstall.scpt`
    / plist source -> fixed `/usr/bin/osascript -e` -> AppleScript `do shell script ... with administrator
    privileges`.
  - Runtime `_service` trust already required the installed app to satisfy the pinned Developer ID Team ID and
    `identifier "com.carriez.rustdesk"`, and the helper to satisfy the fixed helper path/identifier
    `com.carriez.rustdesk_service`. The privileged installer source therefore had a weaker identity-input model
    than the runtime receiver: live bundle metadata and broad text replacement could rewrite fixed service/helper
    identifiers before the root script ran.
- Impact:
  - This is not a remote trigger and not a confirmed shipped-artifact low-user-to-root path by itself; the
    ordinary signed artifact has the expected bundle identifier.
  - It is still a root-authority correctness gap in the source model: admin approval of the service installer must
    not authorize live bundle metadata, or an undifferentiated lowercase source rewrite, to alter the helper path,
    helper designated requirement, associated bundle identifier, or runtime app signing identifier.
  - Affects the macOS source-conformance path and any future macOS artifact/custom-client variant that reaches the
    privileged service installer.
- Authority model:
  - Dynamic app-name rendering is allowed only for data that is already intentionally app-name-derived: launchd
    service/server labels, app executable and working-directory paths, support/log/root-preference paths, and
    prompt text.
  - The helper executable path, helper code-signing requirement, LaunchDaemon/LaunchAgent associated bundle
    identifier, and runtime app code-signing identifier are fixed service authority:
    `com.carriez.rustdesk` / `com.carriez.rustdesk_service`.
  - If those fixed identifiers ever change, they must change as a deliberate product identity change across the
    installer templates, runtime `_service` trust constants, and source gates, not by reading a live bundle
    metadata string.
- Implemented in this slice:
  - `src/platform/macos.rs`: replaced `correct_app_name` with `render_macos_service_template`, deleted
    `get_bundle_id`, and removed all live `bundleIdentifier` use from privileged template rendering. The new
    renderer performs explicit substitutions for service/server labels, app path, support/log/root-preference
    paths, and prompts, and does not rewrite lowercase fixed identifiers.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: gate absence of `get_bundle_id`, `bundleIdentifier`,
    and the old renderer; require the explicit app-path and label substitutions; reject lowercase fixed-identifier
    rewrites; require fixed associated bundle identifiers in both launchd plists; and require this
    requirements/status disposition.
  - `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: record the privileged-template identity-input closure under
    the macOS service packaging authority model.

## R-S11d-34 Windows MSI deferred firewall/service target provenance

- Finding closed:
  - Microsoft documents deferred Windows Installer actions as running from the execution script with only limited
    session context; `CustomActionData` is the normal data path into those actions. Microsoft also documents that
    no-impersonate deferred actions can run elevated. In this repository that means the native custom-action DLL,
    not just WiX authoring, must prove the target before changing firewall, service, or process state.
  - After R-S11d-33, `CreateStartService`, `RemoveRuntimeGeneratedFiles`, and `RemoveAmyuniIdd` proved install-root
    / service-command / helper-path authority locally. `AddFirewallRules` still accepted a mode byte plus raw
    executable path and passed that path to the firewall COM helper after only non-empty validation.
  - `TryStopDeleteService` still accepted a raw service name, stopped/deleted that service, then terminated
    processes by the derived executable name. The current MSI authored those values from private package state, but
    the privileged LocalSystem action itself still lacked a full target proof if execution-script data ever drifted.
- Impact:
  - Not a newly proven low-user-to-SYSTEM exploit in the current shipped MSI: `App.InstallFolder` is private under
    `ProgramFiles6432Folder`, and the package authors the old values itself.
  - Real privileged-state correctness issue: a deferred LocalSystem action must not treat a raw path/name from
    `CustomActionData` as authority to write firewall policy, stop/delete a service, or kill processes.
- Authority model:
  - Firewall add/remove target authority is the normalized product executable under the trusted MSI Program Files
    install-folder shape. Add requires that executable to exist and not be a reparse point; remove may use the same
    normalized trusted path/rule identity without requiring the file to still exist.
  - Service stop/delete authority is the service identifier plus the exact normalized `"<exe>" --service` package
    command, and the installed service's live `ImagePath` must normalize to that same command on the opened service
    handle before stop/delete. Post-delete process cleanup is bound to the same normalized executable image path,
    not to an ambient process name.
- Implemented:
  - `res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp`: added product-executable validation, service executable/command
    validation with executable output, installed-service `ImagePath` proof, handle-bound trusted stop/delete, and
    exact image-path process cleanup. Firewall actions now pass only the normalized executable path to
    `AddFirewallRule`.
  - `res/msi/Package/Components/RustDesk.wxs`: `TryStopDeleteService.SetParam` now carries the service command
    shape instead of only the service name.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the product-executable validator, firewall normalized path, service-delete WiX data

    the old raw firewall path/name-only service-delete cleanup.
  - `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: record Appendix C #89 / R-S11d-34.

## R-B9/R-B10 legacy root Docker builder retirement

- Finding closed:
  - The tracked root `Dockerfile` was not used by the hardened release scripts, but it remained as an alternate
    build scaffold. It fetched CMake with `--no-check-certificate`, cloned vcpkg from a branch name, downloaded
    Sciter from `raw.githubusercontent.com`, installed Rust through live `sh.rustup.rs`, and delegated the build
    through root `entrypoint.sh`.
  - All translated upstream `docs/README-*.md` files still advertised the legacy root `docker build -t
    "rustdesk-builder" .` path and live rustup/Sciter download snippets.
  - This was not a runtime local privilege escalation path and not a shipped artifact path, but it contradicted
    R-B9/R-B10's one-mode build authority: release artifacts are supposed to come only from checked scripts,
    `scripts/online-fetch.sh`, digest-pinned `scripts/Dockerfile.*` images, and offline compile stages.
- Authority model:
  - The repository has one supported build scaffold family: checked scripts and pinned images under `scripts/`.
    A build path that reaches live network resources, moving channels, unchecked downloads, or a second root-level
    Docker entrypoint is not a fallback; it is obsolete source authority and must be absent.
- Implemented:
  - Deleted the root `Dockerfile` and root `entrypoint.sh`.
  - Deleted translated upstream `docs/README-*.md` files that preserved the old Docker/rustup/Sciter build path.
  - `requirements.html`: R-B9 now states that the root-level Docker builder and translated upstream README build
    paths are not supported build modes.

    build Dockerfiles rather than implying a supported root Dockerfile.

## R-S11e-7 user-owned permanent-password main IPC receiver authentication

- Finding closed:
  - Read-only Linux audit found an adjacent same-UID credential-secrecy issue in the user-owned password path:
    `set_permanent_password(v)` first asked ordinary main IPC for
    `permanent-password-user-owned-writable`, then sent `Data::SetUserOwnedPermanentPassword(v)` on the
    ordinary main IPC path if the peer answered `Y`.
  - Linux/macOS `_service` client authentication and Linux service-owned main-server commit authentication were
    already closed, but ordinary user-owned main IPC did not prove the receiver before the UI/CLI trusted the
    route answer or sent the plaintext password.
  - A same-UID local process that could win or squat the per-user socket while the legitimate user-owned daemon
    was absent/stale could learn the proposed unattended password. This is not cross-user, not remote, and not a
    service-owned root/SYSTEM commit bypass; it is local same-UID credential disclosure and route confusion.
- Authority model:
  - The service-owned path is the first-class desktop credential path when it is available; user-owned main IPC
    does not choose where an installed-service credential goes.
  - A user-owned password capability query or password-bearing user-owned write may use main IPC only after the
    connected receiver is proven as the same effective uid, current executable, exact user-owned `--server` main
    process. Service-owned markers and extra mode args are not the user-owned password receiver shape.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: added `ensure_user_owned_main_server_is_trusted`, which derives peer uid/pid from the Unix
    socket, requires the peer uid to equal the caller's effective uid, proves the peer executable against the
    current executable, and requires exact user-owned `argv[1] == "--server"` shape through
    `user_owned_main_server_argv_is_expected`. The helper is gated for Linux/macOS; Windows keeps its existing
    named-pipe server proof in `connect_with_path`.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: added `connect_user_owned_password_main` and routed both
    `user_owned_permanent_password_is_writable` and `set_user_owned_permanent_password_with_ack_async` through it
    before `ConfigRequest("permanent-password-user-owned-writable")` or
    `Data::SetUserOwnedPermanentPassword`.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: changed `can_set_permanent_password` and `set_permanent_password` to prefer
    `can_request_service_owned_unattended_password_change` before consulting user-owned main IPC.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the authenticator, same-uid/current-executable/exact-argv proof, regression test,
    authenticated password query/write connector, and service-owned-first route ordering.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record Appendix C #90 /
    R-S11e-7 and refresh the requirements hash.
- Parallel audit notes:
  - Windows read-only audit found no still-real R-S11-adjacent Windows privilege-boundary slice. MSI process
    termination, active-console session selection, and HKLM prior-MSI uninstall handling were false positives for
    the current requested local privilege-boundary scope.
  - macOS read-only audit found two later candidates, not mixed into this slice: `_service` peer proof should be
    bound to immutable endpoint identity rather than PID-only revalidation, and Authorization Services right
    normalization should occur before UI-side `AuthorizationCopyRights` acquisition on first use/stale-right cases.

## R-S11e-8 macOS service-owned password right normalization before authorization

- Finding closed:
  - macOS service-owned password changes use the custom Authorization Services right
    `com.carriez.RustDesk.set-unattended-password`. Before this slice, the UI process created the external
    authorization form before the trusted root helper had necessarily created or normalized that right.
  - On a fresh authorization database, the UI-side right check could fail before the helper received the password
    request that would create the right. With a stale or weaker preexisting right definition, the prompt could be
    acquired against that stale definition before daemon-side verification refreshed the database.
  - This was not a proven root credential-write bypass from source alone, because the LaunchDaemon still verified
    the external form noninteractively before writing the root credential. It was a policy-definition ownership and
    first-use ordering defect at the UI/root-helper boundary.
- Authority model:
  - The trusted root helper owns creation and normalization of the privileged password-change right before the UI
    asks Authorization Services for an interactive grant.
  - The readiness step carries no password. A password leaves the UI only after the client has authenticated
    `_service`, the helper has returned right-readiness true, and UI authorization succeeds.
  - The native UI-side creator must validate the exact expected right definition rather than accepting mere
    existence of the right.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc.rs`: added `MacosServiceOwnedPasswordRightReadyRequest` and
    `MacosServiceOwnedPasswordRightReadyResult(bool)`, admitted the request only on authenticated `_service`,
    rejected it on main IPC with a false readiness result, and routed the macOS password setter through
    readiness-before-authorization-before-password-send ordering.
  - `src/platform/macos.mm`: replaced the existence-only right check with exact definition validation through
    `AuthorizationRightGet`, requiring `class=user`, `group=admin`, `shared=false`, `allow-root=false`,
    `authenticate-user=true`, `session-owner=false`, `extract-password=false`, and `timeout=0` before
    `AuthorizationCopyRights` prompts.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: gate the readiness message pair, service-only
    allowlist, ordering from authenticated `_service` connect to readiness to authorization to password send,
    exact native dictionary validation, and absence of the old existence-only helper.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record Appendix C #91 /
    R-S11e-8 and refresh the requirements hash.

## R-S11e-9 macOS _service audit-token peer code identity

- Finding closed:
  - macOS `_service` client-side server authentication, receiver-side service-scoped admission, and the
    service-owned password runtime snapshot requester had the right high-level trust targets but still used the
    wrong primitive for peer code identity: socket uid plus effective pid/path revalidation, with Rust-side
    filesystem code-signing checks.
  - A pid/path proof is re-observed process metadata. It is not the immutable code identity bound to the connected
    Unix-domain socket. The offloaded receiver proof made that distinction more important because it captured a
    peer snapshot before a later blocking verifier, and the runtime snapshot path mixed installed-app trust with a
    later launchd pid/plist proof.
  - This was local IPC/service-boundary correctness hardening. It was not a demonstrated remote issue, and the
    existing service-owned password path still had uid, launchd/plist, and helper/app trust gates; the goal was to
    make the trust primitive structurally correct rather than merely working.
- Authority model:
  - macOS `_service` code identity is the socket peer's audit token. `LOCAL_PEEREPID` is useful metadata for
    diagnostics and process-shape proof, but it is not the code-signing authority.
  - The audit token must resolve to a live `SecCode` object through Security.framework, the pinned requirement must
    validate with `SecCodeCheckValidity(..., STRICT_VALIDATE)`, and the path obtained from that code object may
    then be checked as a secondary installed-location/ownership/mode/ACL proof.
  - No unauthenticated fallback, PID-only fallback, path-only fallback, or Rust runtime `/usr/bin/codesign` subprocess
    is part of the `_service` trust path.
- Implemented:
  - `Cargo.toml`: made `security-framework = "2.10"` a direct macOS dependency.
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: added `MacosPeerProcessIdentity`, captured `getpeereid` uid, `LOCAL_PEEREPID`, and
    `LOCAL_PEERTOKEN`, resolved peer code with `SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes(kSecGuestAttributeAudit)`, normalized
    leading `=` requirement strings for `SecRequirement`, and validated app/helper code requirements with strict
    Security.framework checks. Static app/helper path checks also use native `SecStaticCode`; the Rust runtime no
    longer shells out to `/usr/bin/codesign`.
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: changed macOS `_service` client-side server authentication to require a root peer whose
    audit-token code is the trusted privileged helper; changed service-scoped receiver authorization snapshots to
    carry the macOS audit-token identity into the blocking verifier before any `_service` frame is read.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: changed the service-owned password runtime snapshot requester proof to require the audit-token
    trusted installed app before launchd live-argv and root-owned plist proof are considered, and rechecks the same
    audit-token code identity after the launchd proof.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: gate the direct dependency, `LOCAL_PEERTOKEN`,
    `LOCAL_PEEREPID`, legacy `LOCAL_PEERPID` absence, audit-token identity capture, native strict validation, Rust
    `MACOS_CODESIGN` absence, and the service-client/server/snapshot wiring.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record Appendix C #92 /
    R-S11e-9 and refresh the requirements hash.

## R-S11e-10 macOS residual process launch provenance

- Finding closed:
  - The current R-S11b/R-S11c checklist is empty and remains closed/gated. A fresh adjacent launch/provenance pass
    found two macOS residual subprocess shapes outside the closed `_service` audit-token work.
  - After CPace keying, `src/server.rs` spawned `/usr/bin/caffeinate -u -t 5` solely to wake/postpone sleep for a
    remote session. The peer did not control the executable or argv, but a remote-authenticated connection should
    not need a helper process for a native user-activity declaration.
  - `src/platform/macos.rs::run_as_user_with_env` built
    `launchctl asuser <uid> /usr/bin/env KEY=VALUE ... <current_exe> ...`. The current call sites pass only
    internally generated CM/whiteboard launch tokens and parent ids, and the normal installed macOS service-owned
    server is the user LaunchAgent, not the root LaunchDaemon. Still, the helper shape mixed a root-capable
    bootstrap launcher with a generic environment-expansion executable and no key allowlist.
  - This was correctness/provenance hardening, not a newly proven ordinary-user-to-root path or remote pre-auth
    issue.
- Authority model:
  - User activity is a native macOS power-management event, not a child process.
  - Root-capable bootstrap launches may carry only launcher-owned token variables for the exact helper protocols
    that validate them. Environment keys are a positive allowlist, and the child executable remains the current
    RustDesk binary selected directly by `launchctl`.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/macos.mm`: added `MacDeclareRemoteUserActivity`, backed by
    `IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity(..., kIOPMUserActiveRemote, ...)`.
  - `build.rs`: explicitly links IOKit for the macOS Objective-C++ bridge.
  - `src/server.rs`: replaced the `caffeinate` subprocess with `crate::platform::declare_remote_user_activity()`.
  - `src/platform/macos.rs`: declared the native bridge; changed `run_as_user_with_env` to execute
    `/bin/launchctl asuser <uid> <current_exe> ...`, apply values with `Command::env`, and reject every key except
    `RUSTDESK_CM_LAUNCH_TOKEN`, `RUSTDESK_CM_LAUNCH_PARENT`, `RUSTDESK_WHITEBOARD_LAUNCH_TOKEN`, and
    `RUSTDESK_WHITEBOARD_LAUNCH_PARENT`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: gate the native IOKit helper, remote-user activity
    type, server wiring, absence of `caffeinate`, absence of the `/usr/bin/env` bridge, the launch-env allowlist,
    and the ledger/requirements entries.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record Appendix C #93 /
    R-S11e-10 and refresh the requirements hash.

## R-S11e-11 Windows service-owned password commit receiver proof

- Finding closed:
  - Windows service-owned password provisioning already required an elevated caller on `_service`, and the
    receiver-side main-channel policy rejected `CommitServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange` unless the receiver
    was service-owned and the pipe peer was LocalSystem.
  - That was not enough for confidentiality. The LocalSystem service connected to generic main IPC and serialized
    the password-bearing commit before proving that the connected main-pipe server was the service-owned server.
    A user-owned same-executable `--server` process could receive the plaintext frame and then reject it without
    writing it.
  - This is not an unauthenticated local-to-SYSTEM write. It is a sender-side receiver-identity bug for a
    service-owned secret after an authorized local password-change request.
- Authority model:
  - A secret-bearing IPC send must authenticate the receiver before serialization, not rely on the receiver to
    reject after parsing the secret.
  - For the Windows service-owned password commit, the receiver must be the current executable, running as
    LocalSystem, with the exact `--server --service-owned-server` process shape. The existing receiver-side
    LocalSystem commit gate remains defense in depth.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/mod.rs`: exposed the existing exact-argv process lookup to crate-local callers.
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: added `authenticate_windows_service_owned_main_server`, which resolves the named-pipe
    server pid, checks current executable identity, checks the process token is LocalSystem, and checks the exact
    service-owned server argv shape.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: calls the Windows authenticator immediately after connecting to main IPC and before sending
    `Data::CommitServiceOwnedUnattendedPasswordChange(value)`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the authenticator, exact-argv helper, LocalSystem receiver proof, pre-send ordering,
    retained receiver-side commit policy, and the ledger/requirements entries.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record Appendix C #94 /
    R-S11e-11 and refresh the requirements hash.

## Current no-finding pass after R-S11e-11

- Debian maintainer scripts reviewed:
  - `res/DEBIAN/preinst`, `postinst`, `prerm`, and `postrm` are short POSIX `set -e` scripts. Unit lifecycle uses
    `deb-systemd-invoke` for start/stop, `deb-systemd-helper` for enable/disable/purge, and the fixed
    `/bin/systemctl --system daemon-reload` manager reload. `scripts/verify-debian-maintainer-scripts.py` validates
    the lifecycle ordering and rejects masked helper failures or stray `systemctl` use.
  - `postrm` purge removes only fixed root-owned service config residue under `/root/.config/RustDesk` and
    `/root/.config/rustdesk` after `deb-systemd-helper purge`. `rm -rf --` on the final component removes a symlink
    itself rather than following it, and ordinary users do not control `/root/.config`. No new local-user-to-root
    path opened from this line.
- macOS privileged install/uninstall scripts reviewed:
  - `install.scpt` rejects symlinks for daemon/agent/helper/log/support/root-prefs paths, stages the bundled helper
    through `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/.com.carriez.rustdesk_service.installing`, verifies the exact helper code
    requirement, installs root:wheel 0755, clears extended ACLs, byte-compares the installed helper with the bundled
    helper, writes fixed plists with quoted `printf`, and verifies before `launchctl load`.
  - `uninstall.scpt` rejects a helper-dir symlink, unloads and verifies the LaunchDaemon, removes only fixed daemon,
    agent, installed-helper, and temp-helper paths, then verifies absence. No unquoted path, `/tmp`, user-config
    adoption, or masked privileged failure was found.
- Local IPC reviewed:
  - Main IPC has an exhaustive `Data` classification in `main_channel_admits_state_mutation`; service-owned servers
    reject ordinary option/password/storage-sync mutation, and service-owned password commits require root/LocalSystem
    peers plus sender-side receiver authentication on Linux/Windows.
  - Unix `_service` accepts only the explicit service-control messages before dispatch. Linux uses fresh active-uid
    plus executable proof; macOS uses audit-token code identity for the installed app/helper model.
  - `_cm`, `_whiteboard`, and Linux `_pa` are not only process-authenticated. CM file work is connection-token bound;
    whiteboard events require the per-launch endpoint proof plus per-connection token; Linux PulseAudio capture
    requires the owner identity/token lease and owner main-process validation before opening a source.
  - No new concrete local privilege escalation was found in this pass. Continue with other privileged packaging,
    installer, helper, runtime cleanup, and service-adjacent surfaces rather than reopening the closed R-S11b/R-S11c
    checklist without evidence.

## R-X6/R-S11c-9b desktop URL IPC handoff canonicalization

- Finding closed:
  - `flutter/lib/common.dart::listenUniLinks(handleByFlutter: false)` forwarded `uri.toString()` through
    `bind.sendUrlScheme` into Rust `_url` IPC when a secondary/connection-manager desktop process handed an
    OS-delivered `rustdesk://` URL to the main process.
  - `urlLinkToCmdArgs` later stripped embedded `?password=`, `?key=`, and relay syntax before connect, so this was
    not a connect bypass and not a root/SYSTEM escalation. The bug was earlier than connect: raw credential or
    trust-anchor material could still cross local same-user IPC before being rejected or stripped.
  - Scope: Windows/macOS desktop URL forwarding through authenticated `_url` IPC. Linux D-Bus delivery has already
    been excised. Mobile/iOS direct Flutter handling routes to `handleUriLink`/`urlLinkToCmdArgs`, not the desktop
    `_url` forwarding branch.
- Authority model:
  - A URL handoff between desktop processes is a boundary. The payload must be a freshly rendered address-only link
    derived from the same parser policy that enforces R-X6, not a raw OS-delivered URI.
  - Config/password write authorities and relay syntax remain rejected; only the supported connect authorities may
    be forwarded, and the forwarded form carries no query string or embedded secret/trust-anchor material.
- Implemented:
  - `flutter/lib/common.dart`: added `urlLinkToForwardUrl`, reused `urlLinkToCmdArgs`, allowlisted connect
    authorities, rejected empty/relay-shaped ids, and replaced raw `uri.toString()` forwarding with the canonical
    `rustdesk://<authority>/<id>` string.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the helper, listener wiring, address-only renderer, absence of raw URI forwarding,
    and ledger/requirements disposition.
  - `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: record Appendix C #95 / R-X6/R-S11c-9b.

## R-S11d-35 Windows EXE prior-MSI uninstall command reconstruction

- Source: read-only Windows installer subagent, `master` at `b6a0b84b10e278b567c594d2b667d6a601d40300`.
- Finding closed:
  - `get_uninstall` treats any prior uninstall registry string containing `msiexec.exe` as a prior-MSI handoff, but
    if `command_with_system_tool` cannot bind the prefix to trusted System32 `msiexec.exe`, it falls back to
    `checked_msi_uninstall_command(reg_uninstall_string)`.
  - That raw registry text is then spliced into the elevated EXE installer batch. `%ERRORLEVEL%` checking observes
    completion only after arbitrary command text in that registry value has already executed.
  - A prefix-only bind was also insufficient: `msiexec.exe /X {GUID} & attacker` would bind the executable but still
    preserve attacker-controlled shell tail in the argument string.
  - This is not yet a proven ordinary standard-user-to-SYSTEM path by itself because default HKLM uninstall-key ACLs
    should not be writable by a standard user. It is still an authority-confusion bug: failed provenance binding must
    not degrade into elevated execution of mutable prior-install metadata.
- Authority model:
  - The prior registry string may identify the installed MSI product code only after strict parsing. It may not
    supply an executable path, shell metacharacter, extra argv, or command tail.
  - The product code must resolve through Windows Installer to this product's `ProductName` before any elevated
    uninstall delegation is constructed.
- Implemented:
  - `Cargo.toml`: enabled `Win32_System_ApplicationInstallationAndServicing`.
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: deleted `command_with_system_tool`; added strict tokenization, braced-GUID product-code
    validation, `MsiGetProductInfoW(..., INSTALLPROPERTY_PRODUCTNAME, ...)` product-name proof, and reconstruction of
    `"<System32>\\msiexec.exe" /X {PRODUCT-CODE}` from `WindowsSystemTools`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates parser/proof/reconstruction and fails if the prefix-only binder or raw
    `checked_msi_uninstall_command(reg_uninstall_string)` fallback reappears.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record Appendix C #96 /
    R-S11d-35 and refresh the requirements hash.
- Verification:
  - `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check src/platform/windows.rs` passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `cargo metadata --locked --no-deps --format-version 1` passed.
  - `bash scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `bash scripts/verify.sh` passed with `VERIFY: all gates green`.
  - Diagnostic Windows target check `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rustdesk-win-check-target cargo check --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p rustdesk` stopped before Rust type-checking at missing `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` in `cc-rs` build scripts for `ring` and `zstd-sys`.
- Commit:
  - `b358747960612332321f4f7cb2f3f0af1ed5d3d9` (`Reconstruct prior MSI uninstall commands`) pushed to
    `origin/master`.

## R-S11e-12 macOS clipboard-file paste no-follow finalize

- Finding closed:
  - The macOS CLIPRDR file-paste worker already sanitized hostile-peer `FILEDESCRIPTOR` names and bound
    `FileContentsResponse` frames to the connection that originated the request, but its local write path still
    re-resolved peer-influenced paths under the paste destination for directory creation, temp/final file creation,
    Finder progress xattrs, cancellation cleanup, final rename, and metadata operations.
  - In the normal installed macOS model this is not a hidden remote-to-root path because the controlled server is a
    user LaunchAgent. It is still a security-correctness defect for a peer-controlled filesystem-write surface: local
    symlink/path races must be rejected by construction, not handled by a string containment check before later
    path-based filesystem calls.
- Authority model:
  - The selected paste directory is the authority anchor. After that directory is opened, peer-controlled relative
    names may only be resolved below that anchor through fd-relative component walks.
  - Created directories and files must be opened with no-follow/exclusive primitives; progress metadata and cleanup
    must stay attached to the already-open file or fd-relative relative path. Finalization must not overwrite a
    local destination and must fail closed if the fd-relative exclusive rename primitive is unavailable or rejected.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/paste_task.rs`: opens the paste target directory with an
    `openat(O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW)` component walk and stores the handle on `PasteTaskHandle`.
  - Replaced path-based parent creation with `mkdirat` plus no-follow re-open, zero-size/temp file creation with
    `openat(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW)`, progress xattr mutation with `fsetxattr`/`fremovexattr`, cancellation
    cleanup with `unlinkat`, and final rename with `renameatx_np(..., RENAME_EXCL)` plus numbered-name retries for
    real destination collisions.
  - Removed the old path-based write/finalize shapes: `std::fs::File::create`, `std::fs::create_dir_all`,
