## R-S11e-13 macOS clipboard-file paste placeholder temp authority

- Finding closed:
  - The macOS file-paste placeholder path still used global `/tmp/.rustdesk_*` placeholder names for the pasteboard
    file URL, counted all matching names in `/tmp`, and cleaned the source placeholder by ordinary path deletion.
  - This was not a newly proven remote-to-root path in the normal installed macOS model because the controlled side is
    a user LaunchAgent. It was a local same-user pasteboard/temp namespace ambiguity adjacent to R-S11e-12: another
    same-user process can observe or race pasteboard file URLs and could flood the global placeholder namespace.
- Authority model:
  - The pasteboard context owns a private temporary directory for placeholder URLs. The directory handle, not a global
    pathname pattern, is the authority for placeholder creation, counting, and source cleanup.
  - Placeholder creation must be exclusive/no-follow and owner-only. Source cleanup must use the same directory handle;
    non-placeholder cleanup paths are ignored rather than deleted as a compatibility fallback.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/pasteboard_context.rs`: creates a unique
    `rustdesk-clipboard-<euid>-<uuid>` directory under `std::env::temp_dir()` with `mkdir(0700)`, opens it with
    `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`, verifies euid ownership and owner-only mode with `fstat`, keeps an `Arc<File>`
    directory handle, creates placeholders with `openat(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC)` mode `0600`, counts
    placeholders only in the private directory and returns an error if the directory cannot be read, cleans source
    placeholders with `unlinkat`, and removes the private directory on context drop.
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/item_data_provider.rs`: no longer formats `/tmp` paths or calls
    `File::create`; it receives the private directory path/handle and calls `create_placeholder_file`.
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/paste_observer.rs`: accepts a captured paste callback so paste-result
    cleanup can carry the private placeholder authority instead of calling a global function with only string paths.
  - `libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/README.md`: documents the private per-context placeholder directory.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`: retain the touched Apple clipboard sources and gate the
    private directory, fd-relative create/unlink, scoped fail-closed counting, source cleanup authority, README,
    requirements/status disposition, and absence of global `/tmp` placeholder creation/counting or source-placeholder
    path cleanup.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record Appendix C #98 /
    R-S11e-13 and refresh the requirements hash.
- Verification:
  - `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/pasteboard_context.rs libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/item_data_provider.rs libs/clipboard/src/platform/unix/macos/paste_observer.rs` passed.

## R-S14 macOS hardened-runtime JIT entitlement minimization

- Finding closed:
  - The retained macOS Xcode source still used one `DebugProfile.entitlements` file for both Debug and Profile, and
    `Release.entitlements` also carried `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit`.
  - Apple documents that entitlement as the hardened-runtime exception for writable/executable `MAP_JIT` memory.
    Flutter's current docs classify Debug as the JIT mode and Profile/Release as AOT/precompiled modes.
  - This was not a root/LPE path and not a shipped Debian/Windows/Android artifact issue. It was still a retained
    macOS source-conformance gap: Profile/Release had an executable-memory exception that the build configuration did
    not need.
- Authority model:
  - JIT entitlement authority is build-configuration scoped.
  - Debug may carry `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit`; Profile and Release must not.
  - There is no combined Debug/Profile compatibility entitlement file and no release/Profile fallback carrying the JIT
    exception.

  - Added `flutter/macos/Runner/Profile.entitlements` with audio input, network server, and sandbox off, but no JIT
    exception.
  - Removed `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` from `flutter/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements`.
  - Updated `flutter/macos/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` so Debug, Profile, and Release point to distinct

  - Updated `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` to retain-and-check all three macOS entitlement files and exact-match

## R-S14 Android service-destroy capture-resource teardown

- Finding closed:
  - The prior Android F5/R-S14 fix stopped and cleared `MediaProjection` during service destruction, but
    `MainService.onDestroy()` did not run the same capture-resource cleanup as explicit app Stop.
  - Explicit app Stop reached `destroy()`, which stopped capture, closed `ImageReader`, detached/released
    `VirtualDisplay`, and released `Surface`; a system/OEM service destroy path only stopped the projection.
  - That left the foreground service's derived capture resources dependent on process death or projection invalidation
    instead of making service lifetime the owning authority for the full capture pipeline.
  - This is not a local-to-root or remote-auth bypass finding. It is an Android resource-lifetime hardening issue in
    the retained screen-capture grant model.
- Sources checked:
  - Android's media-projection resource-recovery guidance says the app should register a stop callback and release
    resources it holds, including the virtual display and projection surface, when projection stops.
  - `VirtualDisplay.release()` is the explicit lifecycle endpoint for a virtual display the app is done with.
  - `ImageReader.close()` frees resources associated with the reader.
  - `Surface.release()` releases the local reference and must be called when the surface is no longer used.
- Authority model:
  - The Android foreground service owns the projection token and every resource derived from it:
    `MediaProjection`, retained `VirtualDisplay`, `ImageReader`, and `Surface`.
  - Explicit app Stop and `Service.onDestroy()` must converge on one idempotent teardown sink before listener teardown.
  - `START_NOT_STICKY` remains the restart barrier: a killed service must not auto-restart into a listener or capture
    state outside a fresh authenticated session.
- Implemented:
  - `MainService.onDestroy()` now calls `releaseCaptureResources()` rather than stopping only `MediaProjection`.
  - `destroy()` uses the same `releaseCaptureResources()` sink instead of duplicating a partial teardown sequence.
  - `releaseCaptureResources()` calls `stopCapture()`, releases the retained reusable `VirtualDisplay`, and then stops
    and clears `MediaProjection`.
  - `stopCapture()` nulls `surface` after `Surface.release()` so repeated teardown through explicit Stop followed by
    `onDestroy()` is idempotent.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` gates the lifecycle callers, shared teardown sink, `stopCapture()` chain,
    retained-`VirtualDisplay` release, projection stop, nulled surface, and `START_NOT_STICKY`.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` record Appendix C #102 and refresh the
    requirements hash.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh && bash -n scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `bash scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` passed with `VERIFY: all gates green`.
  - Android arm64 release Kotlin compilation passed in the pinned offline Android builder:
    `./gradlew --project-cache-dir /tmp/gradle-project-cache :app:compileReleaseKotlin -Ptarget-platform=android-arm64 -Psplit-per-abi=true --offline --no-daemon`.
- Commit:
  - `ec0fc85323a10befe65aef3c05a8a10c864ef227` (`Harden Android capture resource teardown`) pushed to
    `origin/master`.

## R-S11d Windows runtime Amyuni helper fixed-root provenance

- Platform sweeps:
  - Windows explorer found no live Windows local privilege escalation or service/SYSTEM authority-confusion path in
    IPC, MSI custom actions, virtual display, terminal helper, portable install, or build harness surfaces.
  - Linux explorer found no live Linux/Unix local privilege escalation in service IPC, password policy, CM/file,
    terminal, clipboard FUSE, Debian scripts, or shared helper surfaces.
  - macOS explorer found no live macOS local privilege escalation, LaunchDaemon/LaunchAgent authority confusion,
    Authorization Services bypass, or code-signing/path trust gap.
- Finding closed:
  - The Windows R-S11d ledger already treated the Amyuni runtime helper path as checked installed helper authority, but
    the runtime code still derived `usbmmidd_v2\deviceinstaller64.exe` and `usbmmidd_v2\usbmmIdd.inf` from
    `current_exe().parent()` and only checked `is_dir()` / `is_file()`.
  - That was not a demonstrated default Program Files standard-user-to-SYSTEM LPE, because the normal installed service
    root is protected and the helper is launched by absolute `CreateProcessW` application path.
  - It was still a correctness gap in a privileged driver helper path: runtime helper/INF authority must be the fixed
    installed service executable root, not merely whatever directory contains the current executable, and reparse-backed
    helper/INF objects must not select driver install/remove authority.
- Authority model:
  - Runtime Amyuni driver helper authority is the fixed Windows service install root returned by
    `fixed_service_install_path("")`.
  - The running executable directory must be the fixed service install root by Windows file identity, and the
    running executable must be the fixed installed service executable for the current app name by Windows file
    identity.
  - `usbmmidd_v2`, `deviceinstaller64.exe`, and `usbmmIdd.inf` must be non-symlink, non-reparse directory/file objects
    under that root before they are used.
  - Helper path trust failures are fatal. Optional helper payload absence remains optional only after the fixed-root
    proof succeeds; malformed/inaccessible/reparse/wrong-root state does not fall through to another install path.
- Implemented:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs`: exposes `fixed_service_install_path()` inside the crate so the runtime virtual-display
    code uses the same fixed Program Files root as service install/uninstall.
  - `src/virtual_display_manager.rs`: adds runtime path validators for fixed installed executable-directory and
    executable identity, symlink/reparse rejection, trusted helper directory/file lookup, trusted INF lookup, and
    UTF-8 fail-closed INF passing into `win_device::install_driver()`.
  - `src/virtual_display_manager.rs`: changes both helper call sites from swallowed
    `if let Ok(Some(paths)) = get_deviceinstaller64_paths()` to propagated `get_deviceinstaller64_paths()?`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates fixed-root file-identity proof, non-reparse helper/INF checks, propagated helper
    trust failures, absence of lossy path/INF fallback, and the updated SetupAPI call shape.
  - `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: record the tightened R-S11d-1 /
    R-S11d-23 runtime invariant and refresh the requirements hash.

## R-S11c-10s Linux Flutter runner Rust core library load provenance

- Platform sweeps:
  - Linux/Unix explorer found no confirmed open service IPC, password/polkit, CM/FileTransfer, terminal, clipboard FUSE,
    Debian lifecycle, or shared-helper local privilege escalation. Its only residual was the already accepted
    root/headless owner-terminal and root FileTransfer policy model.
  - macOS/Android explorer found no confirmed open source issue in macOS `_service`/helper authority, installer
    AppleScript, residual process launch, macOS clipboard writes, macOS entitlements, Android exported components,
    Android MediaProjection minting, URL handoff, or clipboard platform authority. It suggested artifact-level Android
    manifest and macOS signed-helper inspection as a future package-proof slice, not a current source finding.
  - Windows explorer found no confirmed open Windows service, IPC, installer, terminal, virtual-display, portable,
    named-pipe, registry, SAS, or process-launch privilege-boundary issue and no conceptual candidate it would promote.
- Finding closed:
  - `flutter/linux/main.cc` loaded the Rust core with `dlopen("librustdesk.so", RTLD_LAZY)`.
  - Linux `dlopen(3)` documents that if the path contains no slash, the dynamic linker searches for the object rather
    than treating the string as a pathname. `ld.so(8)` documents that non-slash dependency lookup consults
    `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before `DT_RUNPATH`, except in secure-execution mode, and that `$ORIGIN` is expanded in filename
    arguments to `dlopen()`.
  - The installed `.deb` service unit does not set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so this was not promoted to a proven default
    ordinary-local-user-to-root path. It was still the wrong provenance model for a root-capable runner: the executable
    should bind to the Rust core in its own Debian bundle, not to ambient loader search state if a root invocation ever
    inherits an unsafe library path.
  - The legacy failure helper also searched `PATH` for package managers only to print installation advice. That did not
    execute package managers, but it had no place in the hardened runner path and kept ambient `PATH` parsing in the
    core-load failure branch.
- Authority model:
  - The Linux Flutter runner is a bundle entrypoint. Its Rust core authority is exactly the installed bundle's
    `lib/librustdesk.so` next to the runner, addressed as `$ORIGIN/lib/librustdesk.so`.
  - Missing bundled core, missing `rustdesk_core_main`, or unresolved core symbols are startup failures and must exit
    nonzero.
  - Load failure is diagnostic only. It must not probe `PATH`, package managers, or any fallback loader name.
- Implemented:
  - `flutter/linux/main.cc`: `RUSTDESK_LIB_PATH` is now `$ORIGIN/lib/librustdesk.so`.
  - `flutter/linux/main.cc`: `dlopen` now uses `RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL` for immediate local binding.
  - `flutter/linux/main.cc`: core-load failure now exits `main` with status `1`.
  - `flutter/linux/main.cc`: deleted `print_help_install_pkg`, `PkgMgrSearch`, `is_command_exists`, package-manager
    advice strings, `getenv("PATH")`, `strdup`/`strtok` path parsing, and the missing-library mutation of `dlerror()`
    text.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added the R-S11c-10s gate for `$ORIGIN/lib/librustdesk.so`, immediate/local `dlopen`, retained
    `$ORIGIN/lib` CMake RPATH, fail-closed startup, requirements/ledger disposition, absence of bare
    `dlopen("librustdesk.so")`, absence of `RTLD_LAZY`, and absence of package-manager/PATH advice code.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #103 for Linux Flutter runner Rust core library load provenance.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11c-10s to the Linux root-context provenance closure ledger and remaining-closure
    list.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash to
    `99168bf40dab0a86a76ee8c27b4abc00900f3bd0641b8454aec4d8f3efa1ff97`.
- Verification:
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh && bash -n scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` passed with `VERIFY: all gates green`.

## R-X6/R-S14 Android final APK manifest authority

- Finding closed:
  - The Android source manifest was mostly hardened, but the final signed APK manifest is the package authority.
    Android manifest merging can add permissions and components from libraries after source XML review.
  - The prior signed APK demonstrated the gap:
    - `file_picker` merged `android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` into the final APK even though source comments
      said READ/WRITE external storage were dropped.
    - AndroidX ProfileInstaller merged `androidx.profileinstaller.ProfileInstallReceiver` as an exported receiver
      protected by `android.permission.DUMP`.
    - `PermissionRequestTransparentActivity` and `MainService` relied on implicit default `exported=false` rather
      than an explicit source and artifact policy.
  - This was not promoted to a proven ordinary-app-to-root path. It was still the wrong package authority model for a
    hardened Android controlled side: the shipped APK should prove that only the launcher/deep-link activity is
    externally launchable and that forbidden permissions/components do not reappear through library merge.
- Authority model:
  - The final signed APK manifest, parsed after `apksigner verify`, is the authority.
  - `com.carriez.flutter_hbb.MainActivity` is the only exported component, and it must carry the intended launcher and
    `rustdesk` deep-link filters.
  - `BootReceiver`, `InputService`, `PermissionRequestTransparentActivity`, `MainService`,
    `io.flutter.plugins.urllauncher.WebViewActivity`, and `androidx.startup.InitializationProvider` must be present
    only as explicitly non-exported components.
  - Services, receivers, providers, and internal activities must not be exported. Unknown components are release
    blockers until deliberately accepted.
  - `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`, and
    `androidx.profileinstaller.ProfileInstallReceiver` are removed at manifest merge and forbidden in the final APK.
- Implemented:
  - `flutter/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: added the Android tools namespace; added `tools:node="remove"`
    declarations for `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`, and
    `androidx.profileinstaller.ProfileInstallReceiver`; made `PermissionRequestTransparentActivity` and `MainService`
    explicitly `android:exported="false"`.
  - `scripts/verify-android-apk-manifest.py`: new final-APK verifier using the pinned SDK `aapt2 dump xmltree`.
    It validates package/minSdk/targetSdk, `allowBackup=false`, approved final permission set, exact component
    inventory, MainActivity launcher/deep-link shape, explicit non-export on all internal/non-exported components,
    and absence of forbidden permissions/components.
  - `scripts/build-android.sh`: runs the verifier after `apksigner verify` and before hashing the signed APK, in both
    default double-build passes.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates source removal markers, explicit exported flags, verifier syntax, build-script wiring,
    and component/permission policy strings.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #104 for Android final APK manifest authority.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-X6/R-S14 Android final APK manifest authority.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash to
    `959294b38dbb1997148d00cdd1524ae7d16e34541d382e99046ca6ed07c4f075`.
- Verification:
  - Negative proof: running `scripts/verify-android-apk-manifest.py` against the old `dist/rustdesk-arm64.apk`
    failed on the merged `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, missing explicit exported flags for
    `PermissionRequestTransparentActivity`/`MainService`, and the exported ProfileInstaller receiver.
  - `bash -n scripts/build-android.sh scripts/android-apk-build.sh scripts/verify.sh` passed.
  - Python AST syntax check for `scripts/verify-android-apk-manifest.py` passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` passed with `VERIFY: all gates green`.
  - `scripts/build-android.sh` passed from the clean committed tree. Both signed APK passes ran
    `verify-android-apk-manifest.py` successfully, and the default double-build determinism check passed.
  - Built `.apk` hash:
    `a45c0bdb59182affd5cd03a7a0f184669d076d8a4414bdc6f08f76dd6f701be8`.
  - Direct post-build artifact verification:

## R-X6/R-S14 Android legacy JAR-signature META-INF authority

- Finding closed:
  - The Android release APK still supported `minSdkVersion 22`, so Android 5.x/6.x package-manager verification
    depended on v1/JAR signing.
  - The APK necessarily carried runtime Java resources under `META-INF/`, including R8-shrunk
    `kotlinx.coroutines` service-loader entries (`META-INF/services/k5.c0` and `META-INF/services/p5.v`).
  - `apksigner verify --verbose` warned that those entries were not protected by the JAR signature.
  - Local mutation proof confirmed the API split:
    - Changing `META-INF/services/p5.v` still verified for `--min-sdk-version 22 --max-sdk-version 23`.
    - The same modified APK failed for API 24+ because v2/v3 whole-APK verification detected signature stripping.
  - Removing `META-INF/services/**` was rejected as the wrong fix because the files are coroutine runtime
    service-loader metadata, not disposable packaging junk.
- Authority model:
  - Supported Android installs must use v2/v3 whole-APK signatures for artifact integrity.
  - v1/JAR signing must not be part of the release APK authority path.
  - Runtime `META-INF` Java resources may remain only on supported platforms where the whole APK is covered by
    v2/v3 verification.
  - Android 5.x/6.x compatibility is intentionally dropped.
- Implemented:
  - `scripts/pins.env`: changed `ANDROID_MIN_SDK` from `22` to `24`.
  - `flutter/android/app/build.gradle`: changed `minSdkVersion` from `22` to `24`.
  - `scripts/verify-android-apk-manifest.py`: added `MIN_SDK_VERSION = 24` and `TARGET_SDK_VERSION = 33`, and
    requires the final APK manifest to carry those values.
  - `scripts/build-android.sh`: passes `ANDROID_MIN_SDK` into the signing container, signs with
    `--min-sdk-version "$ANDROID_MIN_SDK"`, explicitly disables `--v1-signing-enabled`, explicitly enables v2/v3,
    runs `apksigner verify -Werr --min-sdk-version "$ANDROID_MIN_SDK" --verbose`, asserts v1 false, v2/v3 true,
    and fails if `not protected by signature` appears.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the min-SDK pin, Gradle value, final-manifest verifier value, container signing pin,
    v1/v2/v3 signing flags, warning-as-error verifier, and warning text gate.
  - `requirements.html`: updated Android SDK levels to `minSdk 24` and added Appendix C #105.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-X6/R-S14 Android legacy JAR-signature META-INF authority.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash to
    `5340aa022948ce30d0b7ab92ddbc72c711fa626ed748018872e41365acb7a252`.
- Verification:
  - Official design basis checked:
    - AOSP documents APK Signature Scheme v2 as introduced in Android 7.0 and states Android 6.0 and older ignore
      v2 signatures and verify only v1 signatures.
    - Android's `apksig` warning says a `JAR_SIG_UNPROTECTED_ZIP_ENTRY` is not covered by the JAR signature and
      unauthorized modifications to it will not be detected.
    - Android `apksigner` docs state `--min-sdk-version` controls the lowest platform level whose signatures are
      verified, and v1/v2/v3 signing defaults depend on the min/max SDK range.
  - Negative proof against the pre-change APK:
    - `scripts/verify-android-apk-manifest.py --apk dist/rustdesk-arm64.apk ...` failed with
      `uses-sdk: minSdkVersion must be 24`.
    - A locally modified `META-INF/services/p5.v` still verified for API 22/23 and failed for API 24+.
  - `bash -n scripts/build-android.sh scripts/verify.sh` passed.
  - Python AST syntax check for `scripts/verify-android-apk-manifest.py` passed without leaving a tracked artifact.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` passed with `VERIFY: all gates green`.
  - `scripts/build-android.sh` passed from the clean committed tree at
    `9e73c2086df7e80b2cc92aa4ee32b5aff30ea2eb`. Both signed APK passes verified v1 false, v2 true, v3 true,
    no `not protected by signature` warning, and `verify-android-apk-manifest.py` success.
  - Default double-build determinism passed.
  - Built `.apk` hash:
    `26d7994d91358182817623742279093b594169a958d67b64d35993b11af0f22a`.
  - Direct post-build artifact verification:
    - `apksigner verify -Werr --min-sdk-version 24 --verbose dist/rustdesk-arm64.apk` returned v1 false, v2 true,
      v3 true, no warnings.
    - `scripts/verify-android-apk-manifest.py --apk dist/rustdesk-arm64.apk --aapt2 online/android-sdk/build-tools/34.0.0/aapt2`

    - `unzip -l dist/rustdesk-arm64.apk 'META-INF/*'` still shows runtime `META-INF` resources, but no v1

## R-S11e-15 Linux pkcheck request-time peer identity binding

- Finding closed:
  - Linux service-owned unattended-password changes already used the race-resistant
    `pkcheck --process pid,start-time,uid` subject form and a fixed trusted `/usr/bin/pkcheck`.
  - The request handler still assembled that subject from split observations: socket pid/uid from
    SO_PEERCRED and a direct `/proc/<pid>/stat` start-time read in `linux_polkit_subject_for_peer`,
    after the accept-time same-executable proof had already run.
  - The old path was not promoted to a proven default local-to-root exploit because the `_service`
    connection still had the active-user/root UID gate, same-executable accept proof, packaged
    `auth_admin` polkit policy, trusted pkcheck resolver, and service-owned main-server receiver
    proof before final credential commit.
  - It was still the wrong authority shape for a privileged root mechanism authorizing an untrusted
    local IPC subject: the polkit subject should be derived from the same live identity proof that
    the IPC authority model trusts.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs`: added `PeerProcessIdentity::start_time()`.
  - `src/ipc.rs`: `linux_polkit_subject_for_peer` now calls
    `peer_process_identity(stream, crate::POSTFIX_SERVICE)` and formats `pid,start-time,uid` from
    that identity. That request-time proof revalidates SO_PEERCRED pid/uid, current executable
    match, live `/proc` uid equality, and process start time in one path.
  - Removed the now-unused `linux_proc_start_time` re-export from `src/ipc.rs`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: gates the live-identity subject, start-time accessor, identity uid, docs
    disposition, and rejects the old direct `linux_proc_start_time(peer_pid)` subject assembly.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #106.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11e-15 and refreshed the requirements hash.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `00198a612914d7fcaaf4ca27a783cb75945b0aaf94f76f1a48c258d3e0ba7970`.
- Research basis:
  - Freedesktop/Polkit documentation describes polkit as a privileged mechanism authorizing
    untrusted IPC subjects.
  - Red Hat's pkcheck guidance explicitly requires the `pid,start-time,uid` form to avoid a race.
  - Linux `proc_pid_mem`, `ptrace`, `PR_SET_DUMPABLE`, and capabilities manuals were reviewed while
    deciding not to implement same-UID `PR_SET_DUMPABLE` as this slice; it would not cure the
    at-rest same-user PRS cold-read and would not be a root-escalation fix.
- Verification:
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh` passed.
  - `bash -n scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - Direct local Cargo compile was not usable as authority on this host because `target/` is root-owned
    and the temporary-target compile lacks the host `x11.pc` system dependency.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` passed twice through the repo's Docker-backed verifier; the second pass was
    after the final import cleanup and ended with `VERIFY: all gates green`.

## R-S11c-22 Windows CM non-file clipboard authority

- Finding closed:
  - A read-only explorer audit found a residual Windows `_cm` helper authority gap outside the
    already-closed service-owned password/config-write paths.
  - In installed/root Windows server mode, `src/server/clipboard_service.rs` connected to the
    authenticated `_cm` endpoint and sent a bare `Data::ClipboardNonFile(None)` request.
  - The endpoint proof showed the caller was the launched RustDesk server/helper process, but it
    did not prove that an active Remote connection currently owned clipboard-read authority.
  - `src/ui_cm_interface.rs` handled that request by calling `check_clipboard_cm()` and returning
    text/image clipboard content without validating `(conn_id, AuthConnType, cm_auth_token)` against
    the main server registry.
  - This was not classified as a demonstrated arbitrary local-user-to-SYSTEM exploit because a peer
    still had to pass `_cm` process-shape and launch-token proof. It was a concrete helper capability
    leak: process-level helper proof was being used as data-access authority.
- Implemented:
  - `src/ipc.rs`: added Remote-only `CmAuthConnType::allows_clipboard_authority`, added a
    `clipboard` bit to `CmConnectionAuthority`, added Windows `CmClipboardAuthority`, and added the
    typed `Data::AuthorizedClipboardNonFile { id, conn_type, cm_auth_token }` request.
  - `src/server/connection.rs`: `ConnInner` now carries an optional Windows CM clipboard lease; the
    authenticated connection registry records a live `cm_clipboard` bit derived from
    `AuthConnType::Remote && can_sub_clipboard_service()`, after R-S19 capability confinement and
    before service subscription. Peer clipboard/keyboard disable updates refresh that registry bit.
    `validate_cm_connection_authority` returns clipboard authority only when the token/type match and
    the live Remote-only clipboard bit is set.
  - `src/server/service.rs`: added subscriber-scoped `cm_clipboard_authorities()` so the clipboard
    service can choose only a currently subscribed connection lease.
  - `src/server/clipboard_service.rs`: replaced the bare `ClipboardNonFile(None)` request with
    `AuthorizedClipboardNonFile` carrying a subscribed connection lease. No-subscriber state now
    reads no clipboard.
  - `src/ui_cm_interface.rs`: CM now validates `AuthorizedClipboardNonFile` through the main server
    before `check_clipboard_cm()`, rejects missing/wrong/stale/non-Remote/non-clipboard authority, and
    treats bare `ClipboardNonFile(None)` as a rejected legacy request.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added the R-S11c-22 source gate and the focused
    `cm_clipboard_authority_is_remote_only` test target.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #107 and updated Appendix C #28's helper IPC disposition.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11c-22 and refreshed the requirements hash.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `fee1be48f48ac6403aaaff740f91d85877b3ee85b3d4cf1838aa8f618f848e8c`.
- Verification:
  - `rustfmt --edition 2021 src/ipc.rs src/server/connection.rs src/server/service.rs src/server/clipboard_service.rs src/ui_cm_interface.rs` passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.

  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.

## R-S11c-10t Linux Debian package payload ownership authority

- Finding closed:
  - A direct Debian packaging audit found that `build.py` used plain `dpkg-deb -b tmpdeb rustdesk.deb`
    in its three Debian package creation paths.
  - `dpkg-deb -b` preserves the uid/gid and mode metadata already present in the staging tree.
  - In the release wrapper this was masked because the Debian build runs inside the root Docker build
    context, and the checked artifacts (`dist/rustdesk-x86_64.deb` and `rustdesk-1.4.7.deb`) already
    carried root/root ownership for the root-loaded package payload.
  - The source invariant was still wrong: a direct non-root invocation of `build.py` could produce a
    package whose `/usr/share/rustdesk/rustdesk` payload and related service/polkit trees install as
    the builder uid/gid while `postinst` links `/usr/bin/rustdesk` to that payload and systemd runs
    the service as root.
  - The boundary is the archive metadata, not the current release wrapper habit. Builder uid/gid must
    never flow into installed root-loaded authority paths.
- Implemented:
  - `build.py`: all Debian package creation paths now call
    `dpkg-deb --root-owner-group -b tmpdeb rustdesk.deb`.
  - `scripts/verify-debian-package-authority.py`: added a dedicated verifier that inspects source
    calls and reads `.deb` data/control tar members directly, requiring root-owned, type-correct,
    link-free, non-group/world-writable authority members under `/usr/share/rustdesk`,
    `/usr/share/polkit-1/actions`, and `/etc/rustdesk`, plus executable root-owned maintainer scripts.
  - `scripts/build-debian.sh`: every emitted Debian artifact is verified before hashing and before
    the release wrapper can treat it as output.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added synthetic negative and positive package tests, source gates for the
    `--root-owner-group` invariant, and release-note/status gates.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #108.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11c-10t and closed the residual Debian payload ownership item.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `923901bd25dfb61f460299fd3cbb2d7a2e079a738593e479794bd0aafff4f946`.
- Verification:

## R-S11c-23 Windows Flutter runner Rust core DLL load provenance

- Finding closed:
  - The Windows Flutter runner loaded the Rust core with bare
    `LoadLibraryA("librustdesk.dll")` before Rust-side service, IPC, or policy checks ran.
  - Microsoft's DLL search documentation says an unpackaged app normally searches the application
    directory first, then other process/system locations depending on safe-search state, current
    directory, and `PATH`; Microsoft's DLL-security guidance recommends fully qualified paths and
    restricted `LoadLibraryEx` search flags for secure loads.
  - This was not promoted to a proven default standard-user-to-SYSTEM exploit because the intended
    installed bundle has `librustdesk.dll` beside the executable under Program Files, and that directory
    is searched first under the normal unpackaged-app search order.
  - The source invariant was still wrong: a root-capable Windows runner must bind the core module to
    its own executable bundle and fail closed, not delegate pre-policy core selection to ambient DLL
    search state if the bundle is damaged, moved, or launched with attacker-influenced process search
    state.
- Implemented:
  - `flutter/windows/runner/main.cpp`: added `LoadRustDeskCoreModule()`, resolves the running executable
    with `GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr, ...)`, constructs the sibling absolute `librustdesk.dll` path, and
    loads it with `LoadLibraryExW`.
  - The load uses `LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR`, `LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_APPLICATION_DIR`, and
    `LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32`; it no longer searches current directory or `PATH` for the core DLL
    or its dependencies.
  - Startup fails closed if the executable directory cannot be resolved or the bundled core cannot load.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added the R-S11c-23 source gate for the executable-relative path, restricted
    flags, absence of the bare DLL load, and requirements/status disposition.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #109.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11c-23 closure and summary entries.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `20cf916f1782ccdedbbf4193ee90d6f3aca427900b714c866ce0ceb8bbb5d6b3`.
- Verification:
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - Pre-commit `scripts/verify.sh` passed through the repo's Docker-backed verifier and ended with
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
  - Committed-tree `scripts/verify.sh` passed through the repo's Docker-backed verifier and ended with
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.

## R-S11d-37 Windows service-owned server child executable provenance

- Finding closed:
  - R-S11d-13 had already bound Windows token-switched launches to explicit `lpApplicationName`, but
    `src/platform/windows.rs::launch_server()` still selected the service-owned
    `--server --service-owned-server` child from `std::env::current_exe()`.
  - The service-owned main-IPC receiver proof was also self-referential: it proved the named-pipe server was
    LocalSystem, exact `--server --service-owned-server` argv, and the caller's current executable, but it did
    not independently prove that the receiver executable was the fixed protected Program Files service image.
  - A read-only subagent rechecked the current tree before implementation and confirmed this was not stale:
    `CreateProcessAsUserW` already used explicit `lpApplicationName`, while the remaining child-selection,
    service-owned entrypoint, and main-IPC receiver proofs still depended on ambient current-exe identity.
  - This was not promoted to a proven default standard-user-to-SYSTEM exploit because the installer/service
    model fixes the service image under Program Files and default ACLs should protect that tree. The wrong
    invariant was authority provenance: service-owned SYSTEM children and password-bearing receivers must be
    proven against the fixed service root, not against whatever image happens to be running.
- Authority model:
  - The fixed Program Files service install root is the runtime authority for Windows service-owned children.

## R-S11c-10u Linux XDO libxdo dynamic-library provenance

- Finding closed:
  - `libs/libxdo-sys-stub/src/lib.rs` previously tried `libxdo.so.4`, `libxdo.so.3`, and
    unversioned `libxdo.so` with `Library::new(name)`.
  - That loader is reached by the Linux XDO input path: root `rustdesk --service` can spawn a root/headless
    `--server --service-owned-server`, `src/server/input_service.rs` lazily constructs `Enigo`, and
    `libs/enigo/src/linux/xdo.rs::EnigoXdo::default()` calls `libxdo_sys::xdo_new`.
  - The Linux `dlopen(3)` search rules for a no-slash name include process loader state such as
    `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, object RPATH/RUNPATH, `/etc/ld.so.cache`, and default library directories; dependencies
    of a loaded object are resolved recursively by the same linker rules.
  - `stat(2)`/Unix metadata expose file type, owner uid, and mode bits, which are enough for the source-level
    local-user boundary used here: a non-root local user cannot replace a root-owned non-group/world-writable
    system library file through root-owned non-group/world-writable directory chains.
  - This was not promoted to a proven default local-user-to-root exploit because the shipped systemd unit does
    not set attacker-controlled loader variables, and default distro library directories should not be user-writable.
    It was still a service/root-reachable native code provenance defect.
- Implemented:
  - `Cargo.toml`: added `libs/libxdo-sys-stub` to the workspace so the patched loader's tests run directly.
  - `libs/libxdo-sys-stub/src/lib.rs`: deleted the bare-name `LIB_NAMES`/`Library::new(name)` model.
  - The loader now considers only fixed absolute `/usr/lib*` and `/lib*` candidates for versioned
    `libxdo.so.4` and `libxdo.so.3`.
  - The trust predicate rejects relative paths, `/usr/local`, unversioned `libxdo.so`, shell/`ldconfig`/
    `pkg-config` discovery, writable parents, writable target files, non-root-owned parents/files, and
    non-regular targets.
  - Distro symlinks are accepted only when the fixed candidate directory chain and the canonical target
    directory chain and target file are all root-owned and not group/world-writable.
  - The final load uses `Library::open(Some(path.as_path()), RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL)` on the trusted absolute
    path. Missing or untrusted `libxdo` leaves XDO functions disabled without falling back to ambient search.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added the R-S11c-10u gate and runs the focused `libxdo-sys` unit tests.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #110.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added the R-S11c-10u closure to the Linux root-context cluster and remaining-closure
    summary.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `f6c25128d569caf1c1d8624f845d35885dfd05a9d89739333c4fea4d235360ee`.
- Verification:

## R-S11b-4d corrupt-config recovery file hardening

- Finding closed:
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/config.rs::preserve_corrupt_config()` renamed corrupt TOML files to
    `.corrupt.<nanos>` without immediately rehardening the recovery file.
  - Raw encrypted JSON recovery already attempted post-rename hardening, but the Unix branch used a
    path-based chmod shape rather than descriptor-bound `O_NOFOLLOW`/`fchmod`.
  - The ordinary writer already stores credential-bearing configs as owner-only, so this was not a direct
    ordinary-path local privilege escalation. The wrong invariant was recovery secrecy: a preexisting corrupt
    credential-bearing file with weak inherited permissions could keep those weak permissions after being
    preserved as a recovery artifact.
- Authority model:
  - Recovery preserves bytes only. It does not preserve inherited exposure.
  - Unix recovery hardening opens the preserved sibling with `O_CLOEXEC | O_NOFOLLOW`, proves the opened object
    is a regular file, changes mode through descriptor-bound `fchmod(0600)`, and re-reads metadata to prove the
    final mode.
  - Windows recovery hardening uses the existing protected config-file DACL helper, matching normal config-file
    storage semantics.
  - Other non-Unix/non-Windows targets keep the existing no-op helper because this slice only proved desktop
    filesystem authority on Unix and Windows.
- Implemented:
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/config.rs`: both TOML corrupt recovery and raw encrypted JSON recovery now call the
    shared `harden_preserved_config_file(&backup)` helper immediately after rename.
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/config.rs`: added Unix `O_NOFOLLOW` + descriptor `fchmod(0600)` implementation, Windows
    DACL delegation, and Unix regression coverage for symlink rejection.
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/config.rs`: corrupt TOML and raw encrypted JSON tests now start from a weak `0644`
    corrupt input on Unix and assert the preserved recovery file becomes `0600`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: R-S11b-4d now runs the TOML and symlink recovery tests and gates the helper shape,
    no-follow open flags, descriptor chmod, exact recovery call sites, and absence of the old path-chmod shape.
  - `requirements.html`: Appendix C #48 now states the recovery-file secrecy invariant and verifier coverage.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: R-S11b-4d now records TOML/raw recovery-file hardening as part of the credential-store
    closure.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `5d28126705c3297a7ce6be31f8150c3b29fd4bb912bf487731fddb918083219f`.
- Research basis:
  - Linux `open(2)` documents `O_NOFOLLOW` and descriptor-based open semantics:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html
  - Linux `chmod(2)` documents path chmod dereferencing behavior and descriptor `fchmod` on the file referred to
    by the open descriptor: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/chmod.2.html
  - Microsoft `SetNamedSecurityInfoW` documents the DACL-setting API used by the existing Windows protected
    config ACL helper: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/aclapi/nf-aclapi-setnamedsecurityinfow
- Verification:
  - Docker-backed focused config suite passed:
    `cargo test -p hbb_common --lib config::tests:: --color never` with 55 passed.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed.
  - Pre-commit `scripts/verify.sh` passed through the repo's Docker-backed verifier and ended with
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
  - Committed-tree `scripts/verify.sh` passed at
    `8504bdc29fc97dac9adadaac3ff6a969b6dcec52` and ended with

## R-S11c-24 Desktop Dart FFI Rust core library provenance

- Finding closed:
  - After R-S11c-10s and R-S11c-23, the native Linux and Windows Flutter runners safely preloaded the Rust core
    from executable-relative bundle paths before Rust-side service/UI dispatch.
  - `flutter/lib/models/native_model.dart` still reopened the generated FFI binding with bare
    `DynamicLibrary.open("librustdesk.so")` on Linux and bare `DynamicLibrary.open("librustdesk.dll")` on
    Windows.
  - This was not promoted to a proven default local-to-root path because Dart FFI is normally reached after the
    native runner's safe preload and after Rust-side startup dispatch. The wrong invariant was still present:
    privileged-capable desktop Dart FFI must not ask platform library search semantics to choose the second Rust
    core handle.
- Authority model:
  - Desktop Dart FFI follows the native runner bundle authority.
  - Linux derives the executable directory from `Platform.resolvedExecutable` and opens `lib/librustdesk.so`.
  - Windows derives the executable directory from `Platform.resolvedExecutable` and opens sibling
    `librustdesk.dll`.
  - Android keeps the packaged `librustdesk.so` loader name because Android's app library loader resolves that
    package library. macOS keeps `DynamicLibrary.process()` because the project already relies on a single loaded
    Rust image there to avoid duplicate global state.
- Implemented:
  - `flutter/lib/models/native_model.dart`: added `_desktopExecutableDir()` and `_openBundledRustDeskCore()`.
  - `PlatformFFI.init()` now obtains its `DynamicLibrary` from that helper instead of the old nested platform
    ternary.
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: added R-S11c-24 gates for the executable-dir helper, `Platform.resolvedExecutable`,
    executable-relative Linux/Windows paths, Android/macOS exceptions, init helper use, and absence of bare
    desktop `librustdesk` opens.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #112.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added R-S11c-24 closure.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `b72595b9d4a3bd65859450fc41e228df29862216d74c85fc0c8c409a74f9d62a`.
- Research basis:
  - Dart `DynamicLibrary.open` loads a library file from the supplied path:
    https://api.dart.dev/dart-ffi/DynamicLibrary/DynamicLibrary.open.html
  - Dart `DynamicLibrary.process` resolves currently loaded global symbols:
    https://api.dart.dev/dart-ffi/DynamicLibrary/DynamicLibrary.process.html
  - Dart/Flutter `Platform.resolvedExecutable` is the absolute symlink-resolved executable path:
    https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-io/Platform/resolvedExecutable.html

## R-S11c-10w verifier private scratch workspace authority

- Finding closed:
  - The supported host-side `scripts/verify.sh` redirected checker output through 65 distinct predictable
    `/tmp/rd_verify_*.$$`, `/tmp/r_s11b3_*.$$`, and `/tmp/r_s11c23_hits.txt` names.
  - Shell redirection opened those paths before the checked commands. A shared-host attacker could pre-create a
    symlink, causing an elevated verifier invocation to truncate or write an attacker-selected file.
- Reachability and severity:
  - `scripts/verify.sh` is a documented direct command and is the first gate in `scripts/verify-release.sh`.
  - No tracked caller invokes `verify.sh` or `verify-release.sh` through `sudo` or another elevation mechanism.
  - This was therefore a conditional build-host authority defect, not a default build-host or shipped-runtime LPE.
- Authority model:
  - One verifier invocation owns one atomically created private directory under the fixed system temporary root.
  - Every checker-generated scratch output is below that current-UID mode-`0700` directory. Inherited `TMPDIR`,
    public fixed names, PID-only names, and per-file cleanup paths are not authorities.
  - Normal, failure, and signal exits remove the one directory while preserving a non-cleanup failure status; cleanup
    failure itself is failure.
- Research basis:
  - GNU Coreutils documents the `program.$$` scheme as predictable and symlink-raceable and recommends `mktemp` for
    exclusive unpredictable creation:
    https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/mktemp-invocation.html
  - The Bash manual documents that EXIT traps run before shell termination and signal-derived status is `128+N`:
    https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bourne-Shell-Builtins.html
    https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Signals.html
- Implemented:
  - `scripts/verify.sh`: creates `/tmp/rustdesk-verify.XXXXXXXXXX` with checked `mktemp -d` under a `077` umask;
    makes the path variable readonly; verifies with Python `lstat` that it is a directory owned by the effective UID
    with exact mode `0700`; redirects all 65 migrated scratch basenames beneath it; and deletes the scattered
    per-file cleanup branches.
  - The one EXIT handler captures the incoming status, disarms EXIT/HUP/INT/TERM before cleanup, recursively removes
    only the readonly private-root path, preserves the prior status on successful cleanup, and returns failure if
    cleanup fails. HUP, INT, and TERM exit as 129, 130, and 143 before EXIT cleanup.
  - The R-S11c-10w self-gate asserts private creation, readonly binding, no-follow type/owner/mode proof, signal and
    cleanup shape, old-prefix absence, and direct public-`/tmp` redirection absence.
  - `requirements.html`: added Appendix C #115.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: added the exact R-S11c-10w closure and refreshed the requirements snapshot.
  - `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`: refreshed the requirements hash pin to
    `2f3de8f3cfb216b0bf8f54a71de59216166214c05d4ca5cb007f06e12cd32b9d`.
- Verification:
  - Migration-equivalence comparison proved the old and new scratch basename sets are both exactly 65 with no
    unmatched name.
  - A focused lifecycle test proved current-UID mode `0700`, normal status `0`, explicit failure status `7`, TERM
    status `143`, and cleanup with no leaked test workspace.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh scripts/native-codec-watch.sh scripts/dart-verify.sh` passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passed with the refreshed requirements hash.
  - Pre-commit and committed-tree `scripts/verify.sh` both passed and ended with
    `VERIFY: all gates green (KATs + handshake + policy funnel + main-crate compile + R-A6 done-set)`.
  - No `/tmp/rustdesk-verify.*` workspace remained after either full run.
  - Commit pushed to `origin/master`: `727b83da74de2c67ace8f624bc114e71ffc6f861`.

## R-S11c-10x Apple checker private host scratch authority

- Finding closed:
  - The supported host-side `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` redirected seven distinct fixed/PID-suffixed diagnostic
    basenames and one target-derived cross-check log template through public `/tmp`.
  - Shell redirection opened those host paths before the checked commands. A shared-host attacker could pre-create a
    symlink, causing an elevated checker invocation to truncate or write an attacker-selected file.
- Reachability and severity:
  - `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` is a supported direct command and is invoked by `scripts/verify-release.sh`.
  - No tracked caller invokes the Apple checker or release verifier through `sudo` or another elevation mechanism.
  - This was therefore a conditional build-host authority defect, not a default build-host or shipped-runtime LPE.
- Host/container classification:
  - `/tmp/r_s11b3_apple_trust_writers.$$`, the six `/tmp/rd_apple_*.$$` diagnostics, and
    `/tmp/apple-xcheck-$target.log` were host writes and required migration.
  - `/tmp/apple-vcpkg` and the SDK-root `/tmp` values exist only in fresh trusted-image `docker run --rm` containers;
    they are container fixture state, not host filesystem authority, and remain in that namespace.
  - The container-only fixed `/tmp/rfe` rustfmt diagnostic was not a host vulnerability, but it was unnecessary. It
    was deleted in favor of in-memory stderr capture so the checker can enforce zero direct public-temp redirections
    without carrying an exception.
- Authority model:
  - One Apple checker invocation owns one atomically created host-private directory under fixed system `/tmp`.
  - Every host diagnostic and per-target log is below that current-UID mode-`0700` directory. Inherited `TMPDIR`,
    public fixed names, PID-only names, and scattered cleanup paths are not authorities.
  - Container-only fixture directories remain inside disposable container namespaces and are not conflated with host

## R-S11d-39 Windows obsolete updater authority excision and Windows build closure

- Finding closed:
  - Normal Windows GUI startup called `try_remove_temp_update_files()`, which enumerated
    `std::env::temp_dir()` and removed every file older than one hour named `rustdesk-*.msi` or
    `rustdesk-*.exe`.
  - The supported self-updater was already absent. No tracked producer, caller, packaging script, or Flutter
    caller owned those files. The remaining `download-file-<version>` FFI query and
    `is_msi_installed()` registry helper were uncalled updater residue.
  - The operation had no producer, owner, transaction, or file-identity proof. It was invalid ambient filesystem
    deletion authority in a privileged-capable process, not a demonstrated default local-to-SYSTEM exploit.
- Primary-source basis:
  - Rust documents that `std::env::temp_dir()` may be shared among users and privileges, may itself be a
    symbolic link, and is unsuitable for predictable-name security:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/env/fn.temp_dir.html
  - Microsoft documents that non-SYSTEM temporary paths derive from environment/profile state and that
    `GetTempPath2` does not verify path existence or access; SYSTEM defaults to protected
    `C:\Windows\SystemTemp`:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-gettemppath2a
  - Microsoft documents that `DeleteFile` applied to a symbolic link deletes the link rather than the target,
    which is why the finding was not promoted to a symlink-to-target arbitrary-deletion LPE:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/symbolic-link-effects-on-file-systems-functions
- Implemented:
  - Deleted the startup call and `try_remove_temp_update_files()`.
  - Deleted the uncalled `download-file-` FFI branch, updater-only `is_msi_installed()`, Flutter
    `updateUrl` state, stale updater comments, and four exclusively owned translation keys from all 51
    language tables.
  - Preserved the live `Download new version` old-peer view-camera compatibility message and all 50 expected
    translations.
  - Added Appendix C #117, hardening item R-S11d-39, the permanent Rust/Dart absence gates, and refreshed the

## R-S11c-25 Windows terminal service principal authority

- Finding being closed:
  - The fixed-root Windows service launches `--server --service-owned-server` as LocalSystem, but Terminal user
    selection in `connection.rs` used registry-derived `platform::is_installed()` instead of that proved process
    role.
  - `get_install_info()` can prefer stale compatibility uninstall metadata. A stale nonempty legacy
    `InstallLocation` whose selected executable no longer exists makes `is_installed()` false while the supported
    LocalSystem service-owned server is running.
  - That chose `TerminalUserToken::SelfUser`, converted it to `None`, and reached the direct portable-PTY
    `spawn_command` path in `terminal_service.rs`, yielding a LocalSystem shell to a password-authenticated remote
    Terminal session.
  - Persistent terminal services recorded only `is_specified_user: bool`. Any token-bearing Windows principal
    passed reuse, including another session, another user, or the same SID after a new logon session.
  - `terminal_service::new` ignored `get_or_create_service` errors. The token fallback called `DuplicateToken`,
    closed the source token, and retained the returned impersonation token even though `CreateProcessAsUser`
    requires a primary token.
- Primary-source basis:
  - Microsoft states that `WTSQueryUserToken` obtains the logged-on user's primary token, requires a LocalSystem
    caller with `SE_TCB_NAME`, and requires the handle to be closed:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wtsapi32/nf-wtsapi32-wtsqueryusertoken
  - Microsoft states that `TOKEN_STATISTICS.AuthenticationId` identifies the represented logon session and that
    many tokens can represent one logon session:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-token_statistics
  - Microsoft states that `DuplicateToken` creates an impersonation token unusable by `CreateProcessAsUser`, and
    that conversion would require `DuplicateTokenEx`:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-duplicatetoken
  - Microsoft requires a primary token with query/duplicate/assign-primary rights for `CreateProcessAsUser` and
    runs the process in the session stored in that token:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessasuserw
- Authority model:
  - The positively proved runtime role selects the terminal principal. Service-owned LocalSystem requires the
    user token for the service-owned server process's own session; it never retargets itself to a globally active
    session. Direct non-LocalSystem mode uses the process owner. The two invalid role combinations fail closed.
  - `(token session ID, user SID, AuthenticationId)` is the reconnect logon principal, not the complete token
    authority. A persistent entry separately owns the original primary token and revalidates its TokenId and
    ModifiedId before launch; a same-principal reconnect cannot replace that token.
  - One opaque attachment lease carries the entry Arc identity and monotonically increasing generation through
    actions, output, persistence, and cleanup. Concurrent attachment is rejected; conditional Arc identity makes
    stale release/cleanup ABA-safe; canonical `ts_<UUID>` IDs reject arbitrary peer keys.
  - Preparation reserves the lease before the sole `authorized = true` edge, but the output pump has no subscriber
    until after login success is sent. Served-session logoff/principal replacement revokes the stored token and
    terminates surviving shells. LocalSystem direct PTY and LocalSystem helper execution are sink-denied.
- Implemented, pending final verification/commit:
  - `connection.rs`: explicit process-role classification; no registry selector; own-process-session token
    selection; pre-authorization lease preparation; post-login output activation; authority errors close Terminal.
  - `terminal_helper.rs`: non-Copy RAII primary-token owner; session/SID/AuthenticationId/TokenId/ModifiedId
    extraction and revalidation; LocalSystem helper refusal.
  - `terminal_service.rs`: typed reconnect principal plus immutable launch authority; canonical IDs; exclusive
    generation-bound Arc lease; ABA-safe release/cleanup; pre-login output barrier; periodic logon validation and
    shell/token revocation; exhaustive helper/direct launch dispatch; LocalSystem direct sink denial; bare service-ID
    access and boolean user classification removed.
  - `windows.rs`: invalid `ensure_primary_token` / `DuplicateToken` path removed.
  - `requirements.html`: R-S11c strengthened and Appendix C #118 added; stale terminal-selector descriptions
    corrected.
  - `HARDENING_STATUS.md`: R-S11c-25 added; `scripts/verify.sh`: behavior and structural regression gates added.
- Verification so far:
  - Containerized Rust test filter `terminal_` passed all 17 matching tests, including every Windows process-role
    combination, canonical service IDs, exact session/SID/logon-ID binding, exclusive attachment, generation
    advancement, and stale-release ABA rejection.
  - Committed Windows VM double-build, full verifier, hash-pin checks, commit, and push remain pending.

### Adversarial lifecycle and Windows-helper review

- The first uncommitted implementation was rejected before commit/build. Independent review proved that its
  per-connection authority check stopped when a persistent terminal detached, so logoff did not revoke the stored
  token or surviving shell; its preactivation rollback could delete a previously committed persistent service; its
  action handler converted authority failures into ordinary terminal errors; and its blocking `SyncSender::send`
  shutdown path could prevent revocation and lease destruction indefinitely.
- The replacement lifecycle must make authority monitoring entry-owned and attachment-independent, stage all
  reconnect mutations until checked post-response activation, preserve existing entries on preactivation rollback,
  linearize actions against an authority epoch, perform only nonblocking sink sends, launch outside the service
  mutex through an exact opening reservation, and stop process resources before bounded thread joins.
- Windows-specific review also proved inherited helper-boundary defects that must close in the same slice:
  `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` pipe handles were later used through synchronous `File` I/O; a pending overlapped connect
  could outlive its stack `OVERLAPPED` after timeout; `CreateEnvironmentBlock(..., TRUE)` inherited LocalSystem
  state and failure fell back to the service environment/current directory; pipe ACLs used the account SID rather
  than the logon SID; Win32 variable structures were read through insufficiently aligned byte buffers; and helper
  termination did not own the ConPTY shell process tree.
- Primary-source design basis added during correction:
  - `CreateEnvironmentBlock(FALSE)` excludes the caller environment, and a Unicode environment requires
    `CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT`:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/userenv/nf-userenv-createenvironmentblock
  - a null `CreateProcessAsUser` current directory inherits the caller directory:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessasusera
  - overlapped I/O must retain its `OVERLAPPED` through completion and cancellation uses `CancelIoEx`:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sync/synchronization-and-overlapped-input-and-output
  - `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` terminates every process associated with the job when its last handle
    closes, while process children inherit the job absent breakaway:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects
  - Windows access checks can bind an ACE to the token's logon SID, not merely its account SID:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/how-dacls-control-access-to-an-object
  - a `PROCESS_INFORMATION` PID cannot be reused while the retained process handle keeps that process object
    alive:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/ns-processthreadsapi-process_information
- Corrected implementation now present, still uncommitted:
  - persistent entries own attachment-independent logoff-event and one-second authority monitoring;
  - authority epoch invalidates attached leases, proxies, and opening reservations before token/session drain;
  - reconnect mutations are staged through a checked-response activation transaction, preserving an existing
    persistent service on preactivation rollback;
  - PTY/helper creation occurs outside the service lock and stale completion tears down instead of committing;
  - input/resize/shutdown no longer use blocking channel sends, and session process resources are stopped before
    join work is moved off the revocation caller;
  - attached revocation and typed action-authority failures close the network connection; ordinary operation errors
    return only a sanitized terminal error;
  - Windows helper pipes are logon-SID scoped, non-overlapped, first-instance/local-only, PID/process-object and
    token-principal checked, and restored to blocking mode only after a bounded joined connection worker;
  - token/SID/security buffers are aligned, user environment/profile creation has no service fallback, and the
    suspended helper is assigned to a kill-on-close job before resume and transferred as one RAII process-tree owner.
- Integrated containerized `terminal_` suite passes 23 tests. Shell syntax, diff whitespace, and native-codec
  requirements pin `093dbcfe79405a83f3dead6133e008a2456b5f2712611807fb3695e70f59600b` pass.
- A second independent integrated-code review, fresh full verifier, commit, committed-head Windows VM double-build,
  committed verifier, and push remain pending. The earlier precommit verifier was intentionally stopped; no
  authoritative build claim exists until the corrected source is committed and rebuilt from that commit.

### Second integrated review rejection

- The replacement remained uncommitted and was rejected again before any authoritative build. Its focused 23-test
  suite, full `scripts/verify.sh`, Dart verifier, Apple conformance matrix, formatting, shell syntax, and hash pin all
  passed, but both independent reviews found correctness defects outside those assertions.
- Win32 helper defects:
  - the inbound server pipe had only the read access implied by `PIPE_ACCESS_INBOUND`, while
    `SetNamedPipeHandleState` requires `GENERIC_WRITE` for write/read-write handles or `GENERIC_READ` plus
    `FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES` for a read-only handle;
  - `FILE_GENERIC_WRITE` in the logon-SID ACE also includes `FILE_APPEND_DATA`, whose named-pipe meaning aliases
    `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE`, overgranting instance-creation authority;
  - natural shell exit could leave the helper blocked joining a thread in synchronous pipe I/O, while a persistent
    dead session retained the job handle and prevented kill-on-close cleanup.
- Lifecycle defects:
  - authority revocation cleared opening metadata but did not signal an in-flight process/helper construction;
  - synchronous opening ran on the async connection task, delaying its authority timer by both pipe timeouts;
  - the serial monitor synchronously acquired every drained session mutex before teardown;
  - revoked persistent entries remained registered and rejected a new logon principal using the same opaque ID;
  - checked login success, option processing, activation, subscriber installation, and persistence commit were not
    one minimal coherent transition;
  - a fatal output error returned successful callback completion and could be reinvoked by `GenericService`;
  - closed-session cleanup retained only terminal ID, permitting removal of a replacement session after an ABA;
  - dead persistent sessions retained live process-tree ownership, and launch-time authority failures after the
    initial check could remain ordinary sanitized errors.
- Primary-source correction:
  - `CreateNamedPipeW` rejects unlisted `dwOpenMode` flags, so adding `FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES` to that argument is
    not valid. The corrected server design uses `PIPE_ACCESS_DUPLEX` to obtain a mode-change-capable server handle,
    while the logon SID requests and receives only individual directional data plus synchronization rights:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/namedpipeapi/nf-namedpipeapi-createnamedpipew
  - Microsoft explicitly documents the `FILE_GENERIC_WRITE` / `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE` collision and recommends
    individual named-pipe rights:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/named-pipe-security-and-access-rights
  - pending synchronous I/O is canceled by thread handle through `CancelSynchronousIo`; `ERROR_NOT_FOUND` means no
    cancellable request was found and is a documented benign race during shutdown:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ioapiset/nf-ioapiset-cancelsynchronousio
- Correction now in progress: cancellation-owned opening reservations, nonblocking ordered action dispatch,
  registry removal of exact revoked entries, mutex-independent tracked teardown, closed-session identity checks and
  detached cleanup, permanently quiescent fatal output handling, duplex server pipes with narrow logon rights, and
  real Windows runtime tests. Documentation remains provisional and no commit/build/push claim is permitted until
  this revised implementation passes review and committed-head evidence.

### Third integrated review and lifecycle redesign

- The second correction was again kept uncommitted. Final read-only review found that one successful
  `CancelSynchronousIo` did not prove a helper worker could not enter a subsequent synchronous read; helper/shell
  failures still reached the Windows runner as exit code zero; a committed session became output-visible before its
  `TerminalOpened` response; delayed close used terminal-ID absence and retained a second-generation ABA; output
  draining had no global fairness/final-output barrier; and teardown still depended on per-task thread creation.
- Win32 correction now present:
  - duplex server pipe handles retain mode-change access while the logon SID receives only directional data plus
    synchronization rights;
  - shutdown checks the latch before every framed read and repeatedly calls `CancelSynchronousIo` until both workers
    are observably finished; cancellation failure terminates the dedicated helper process while both join handles are
    still owned;
  - helper shell status is returned through `core_main` by `process::exit`, infrastructure failure is nonzero, and
    the service polls the retained process handle through a bounded reader-EOF grace before reporting `-1`;
  - the helper job handle is shared only inside the service, and revocation invokes `TerminateJobObject` outside the
    session mutex. Unexpected termination failure aborts the service, closing the sole service-owned job handle and
    activating kill-on-close.
- Terminal lifecycle correction now present:
  - action responses carry exact publication identity; output remains hidden until `TerminalOpened` is enqueued under
    the service lock;
  - natural close enqueues `TerminalClosed` and removes the exact session Arc in the same service-lock transaction;
  - orderly exit remains pending until replay, deferred output, and the disconnected reader channel drain across
    bounded polls; writer/query infrastructure failure remains immediate;
  - every poll has one 64-chunk/256-KiB global budget, stable sorted session IDs, a rotating cursor, and per-session
    quanta; services are capped at 64 committed-plus-opening sessions;
  - direct PTY launch drops the parent's slave descriptor immediately after child spawn and retains only the master,
    allowing real child exit to finish the blocking reader and complete the pending-output barrier;
  - direct reader completion starts a bounded child-status grace and re-queries the retained child on each poll, so
    a status published just after reader EOF is preserved; grace expiry reports `-1`, while writer failure remains
    immediate;
  - binary liveness is separate from attached close-status reporting: reader/writer completion immediately rejects
    reconnect and removes detached sessions even while an attached close response may wait for child status;
  - four teardown workers are created before terminal admission. A bounded permit pool covers every live/pending
    lease and opening/session; queue insertion performs no spawn or cleanup work, and permits release only after
    action/output/session-worker joins or complete rollback;
  - session entries expose an out-of-lock shutdown latch and the Windows job terminator, so authority revocation does
    not wait for the session mutex before stopping the helper tree.
- Current evidence before the next full verifier:
  - containerized Linux-visible `terminal_` suite: 47 passed, 0 failed, including a real Linux PTY producing more
    than one poll of output before natural close and controlled child tests for status re-query, grace expiry, and
    immediate writer failure;
  - isolated Rust 1.75 `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` helper check: passed;
  - whole-crate host MSVC diagnostic stopped before crate type-check at unavailable Windows OpenSSL/lib.exe native
    tooling; the native committed Windows VM test remains required;
  - the previous full `scripts/verify.sh`, Dart verifier, and Apple conformance results predate the direct-child
    status-grace correction and must be rerun before commit;
  - requirements hash is now
    `eab38b0d4fd58cbf029d10de9b9af2034914f206e750812d5b6c5ac2a8acf44e`; native-codec watch,
    verifier self-test, shell syntax, rustfmt, and diff whitespace must be rerun against that snapshot.
- Final precommit evidence:
  - independent lifecycle re-review found no concrete correctness blockers after binary transport liveness was
    separated from attached close-status reporting;
  - containerized Linux-visible `terminal_` suite: 47 passed, 0 failed;
  - fresh full `scripts/verify.sh`: all gates green, including the explicit reconnect/detached liveness assertion;
  - Apple source conformance and aarch64/x86_64 macOS plus aarch64 iOS cross-checks: passed;
  - Dart verifier: zero analysis errors and all tests/greps passed;
