## Debian shipped ELF runtime-library provenance (2026-07-12, R-S11c-10y)

Fresh discovery after the R-S11c-10s/10t closure found that the runner's executable-relative
core load did not prove the core's own dependency provenance. Evidence:

- Installed `/usr/share/rustdesk/rustdesk` has the expected `DT_RUNPATH [$ORIGIN/lib]`.
- Installed `/usr/share/rustdesk/lib/librustdesk.so` and the extracted current
  `dist/rustdesk-x86_64.deb` core both carried
  `DT_RUNPATH [$ORIGIN/../../../../tmp/tc/rustinstall/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib]`.
  From `/usr/share/rustdesk/lib`, that normalizes under public `/tmp/tc`.
- `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH LD_DEBUG=libs /usr/share/rustdesk/rustdesk --version` showed glibc using the
  core's RUNPATH for a direct dependency: it searched
  `/usr/share/rustdesk/lib/../../../../tmp/tc/rustinstall/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib`
  for `libpulse-simple.so.0` before falling through to `/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.
- The package sweep also found Flutter plugin shared libraries with absolute
  `/src/flutter/linux/flutter/ephemeral` RUNPATHs. That is not the same default public-temp LPE because
  `/src` is not normally user-writable, but it is still a shipped build-directory search path in
  root-capable package payload.
- Cause: upstream-imported `[profile.release] rpath = true` in `Cargo.toml`, combined with the Debian
  build container installing Rust under `/tmp/tc/rustinstall`; copied Flutter plugin build artifacts kept
  their build-tree RUNPATH because they are installed with `install(FILES $<TARGET_FILE:...>)`.

Primary-source semantics checked before the change:

- Cargo's release profile default has `rpath = false`; profile settings can also be overridden by
  config/environment, including `CARGO_PROFILE_<name>_RPATH`.
- rustc `-C rpath` is Unix-only and, on ELF, adds `$ORIGIN`-relative rpaths to dylib dependencies,
  including a sysroot-relative Rust libdir.
- `ld.so` expands `$ORIGIN` inside `DT_RPATH`/`DT_RUNPATH`; for no-slash dependencies it searches
  `DT_RUNPATH` for an object's direct `DT_NEEDED` entries before the cache/default directories.

Implemented source invariant:

- `Cargo.toml` pins release `rpath = false`.
- `build.py` and `scripts/build-debian.sh` force `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_RPATH=false`.
- `flutter/linux/CMakeLists.txt` makes Flutter plugin targets build with install RUNPATH and
  `INSTALL_RPATH "$ORIGIN"` before their shared objects are copied into the bundle.
- `scripts/verify-debian-package-authority.py` now validates every ELF under `/usr/share/rustdesk` inside
  each emitted Debian package: legacy `RPATH` is forbidden; the runner must have exactly `$ORIGIN/lib`;
  `libflutter_linux_gtk.so` and `*_plugin.so` may have exactly `$ORIGIN`; all other bundled ELFs,
  including `librustdesk.so`, must have no runtime search path. The self-test builds synthetic good/bad
  packages and rejects a `/tmp/rustdesk-bad` RUNPATH.
- `scripts/verify.sh`, `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` now
  track/gate R-S11c-10y. New requirements hash:
  `4327a9c1e6265b55d3333144f3460f46a7ea0e983d791e73d099676c47a5cdc6`.

Verification and committed-head artifact evidence:

- Focused verifier evidence passed: Python bytecode compilation, Debian package authority self-test (including the
  public-`/tmp` RUNPATH negative package), shell syntax, native-codec requirements pin, and `git diff --check`.
- Fresh full `scripts/verify.sh` passed all gates before commit. A direct host Cargo release build was not accepted as
  artifact evidence because the host lacks `x11.pc`; the repository's pinned Debian container is the authoritative
  Linux package environment and completed the real release build.
- Commit `8b31a7a062a34dc30e9cde9911ac723696c69d71` (`Gate Debian ELF runtime search paths`) was pushed to
  `origin/master`; local `HEAD` and `origin/master` matched and the tracked tree was clean before the authoritative
  build started.
- Default `scripts/build-debian.sh` ran from that committed source with `DOUBLE_BUILD=1`, no network,
  `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1700000000`, the pinned Ubuntu 18.04 builder, and the declared
  `flutter,unix-file-copy-paste` feature set. Both emitted packages independently passed Debian payload
  authority/RUNPATH validation, polkit validation, and maintainer-script validation.
- Package A and package B are byte-identical:
  `2ee569ad71f271eb84c77bc5492e7532f132b4fb6322ec52b2b2534757274c27`.
- Independent extraction of package A enumerated every ELF under `/usr/share/rustdesk`: the runner has exactly
  `$ORIGIN/lib`; `libflutter_linux_gtk.so` and all eight shipped `*_plugin.so` libraries have exactly `$ORIGIN`;
  `librustdesk.so` and `libapp.so` have no `RPATH` or `RUNPATH`. No legacy `RPATH`, public-temp path, Rust sysroot
  path, `/src` path, or other build-directory runtime search path remains in the shipped ELF set.

## Protected service IPC resource boundary (2026-07-12, R-S11c-26)

Fresh discovery after the R-S11c-10y closure found no new service-owned password/RDP/SAS authority bypass, but did
find a concrete protected-service resource flaw:

- `libs/hbb_common/src/bytes_codec.rs::BytesCodec::new()` defaults `max_packet_length` to `usize::MAX`.
  IPC `ConnectionTmpl::new()` used that default for service IPC, so `_service` frames were capped only by the
  30-bit wire length before UTF-8/JSON deserialization and before the service message allowlist.
- Linux/macOS `_service` accepted each transport-authorized connection into a spawned persistent loop over
  `stream.next().await`. A peer with a partial frame could hold a root/LaunchDaemon service task indefinitely,
  and one admitted connection could repeatedly run expensive receiver checks such as Linux polkit or macOS service
  proof paths.
- Windows `_service` read only one request with a timeout, but the LocalSystem service loop performed that read and
  dispatch inline and still used the uncapped IPC codec.
- The macOS password setter used the persistent Unix service connection for two exchanges: readiness first, then
  Authorization Services and the password-bearing request. Source inspection showed the actual password request did
  not depend on connection-bound state; readiness is a no-secret preflight.
- The macOS password value cap was checked only after deserialization, and Linux/Windows had no matching service-owned
  password value cap before privileged authorization, hashing, or service-to-main forwarding.

Implemented source invariant:

- `SERVICE_IPC_MAX_FRAME_BYTES` is 32 KiB. The value is tight for the typed service protocol while still covering a
  4096-byte password under worst-case JSON escaping plus a bounded macOS AuthorizationExternalForm envelope.
- `ConnectionTmpl::new_protected_service()` sets the `BytesCodec` cap before any protected service frame is read.
  Service clients and Linux/macOS/Windows service receivers use that constructor; generic IPC, CM/file-transfer raw
  blocks, PA, whiteboard, URL IPC, and port-forward framing are unchanged.
- Linux/macOS `_service` now admits an authorized connection only under a four-slot service transaction semaphore,
  reads exactly one request with `SERVICE_IPC_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, dispatches only `service_channel_admits_message`
  traffic, and closes after the response. Oversized, timed-out, malformed, or unauthorized requests fail closed.
- The macOS setter performs readiness as a separate no-secret bounded service RPC, obtains Authorization Services
  locally, then opens a fresh bounded service RPC for the password-bearing request.
- Windows `_service` uses the capped service constructor and a four-slot bounded one-shot worker. LocalSystem close
  sets a service-owned stop flag after the existing pipe-client token proof; password/RDP requests retain the elevated
  caller and service-owned commit gates.
- Linux, macOS, and Windows share `SERVICE_OWNED_PASSWORD_MAX_BYTES = 4096`, checked before polkit, Authorization
  Services verification, named-pipe elevation checks, hashing, or service-to-main password forwarding.
- `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, `scripts/verify.sh`, and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` track/gate
  R-S11c-26. The new gates include codec over-cap rejection, protected-service constructor cap, service connect/accept
  wiring, one-shot timeout shape, transaction semaphores, common password-cap wiring, and the macOS fresh-connection
  ordering.

Verification passed:

- Focused devcheck cargo tests for the service codec cap, protected-service constructor cap, protected-service password
  frame envelope, shared password value limit, service-channel allowlist, and macOS LaunchAgent plist validation.
- `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh`.
- `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`.
- `scripts/verify.sh`.

Status: verified, committed, and pushed as `ec226b4f7191a6d5d4cb25c42c3ab1c8417367a7`.

## Permanent-password provisioning ingress (2026-07-12, R-S11e-16)

Fresh cross-platform review found that the owner credential still crossed an OS process-metadata boundary before
the existing typed and authorized password operation began:

- `core_main` accepted `rustdesk --password <value>` and copied the value from the process argument vector.
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` and `requirements.html` prescribed that form for the permanent CPace owner credential.
- Linux exposes a live process command line through `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` under the default procfs visibility
  policy. The invoking `sudo` process may retain the argument while administrator authentication is pending, and
  the RustDesk process retained it while privileged authorization completed. Shell history and same-login process
  inspection are additional platform-dependent disclosures.
- Disclosure is not a low-value configuration leak: the value authenticates a remote peer as the owner. On the
  documented root/headless controlled host, successful owner authentication intentionally grants the root-capable
  Remote, Terminal, and FileTransfer authority set.

Primary sources consulted:

- Linux `proc_pid_cmdline(5)`: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_cmdline.5.html
- Linux `procfs(5)` `hidepid` policy: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/procfs.5.html
- MITRE CWE-214: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/214.html
- `rpassword` API and local 7.3.1 implementation: https://docs.rs/rpassword/latest/rpassword/

Implemented invariant:

- Bare `rustdesk --password` accepts no value and reads the new password twice from the controlling terminal with
  echo disabled. A mismatch is a nonzero failure and no setter runs.
- `rustdesk --password-stdin` is the sole noninteractive ingress. It accepts no value, refuses interactive stdin,
  reads one bounded UTF-8 line, accepts LF and CRLF, and rejects EOF-without-data, invalid UTF-8, and values over
  4096 bytes.
- An explicit empty terminal entry or empty stdin line remains the deliberate credential-removal operation. Removal
  does not require knowledge of the current password; authority is established by the existing owner/OS-admin
  operation, not by possession of the old remote credential.
- `--password <value>` and `--password-stdin <value>` fail with usage status before settings policy or the typed
  setter is reached. There is no environment-variable, compatibility, persistence, or positional fallback.
- Both input modes converge on the existing `ipc::set_permanent_password` owner-aware operation. User-owned and
  service-owned routing, receiver proof, OS-admin authorization, and credential commit behavior are unchanged.
- The deployment guide uses the hidden prompt. The noninteractive smoke path uses redirected stdin, and source gates
  reject password-valued RustDesk invocations.

Verification status at implementation time:

- Touched Rust files pass `rustfmt --check`; shell scripts pass `bash -n`; `git diff --check` passes.
- `scripts/native-codec-watch.sh` passes against requirements hash
  `8e481c65aa576818c71f760c9b8a79007186a70479ba72b5545abb34d9e3dee0`.
- Focused pinned-Rust-1.75 runtime tests pass all three `core_main::tests`; Apple source conformance passes both macOS
  architectures and the iOS source target.
- The full `scripts/verify.sh` run from clean committed source passed, including root-owned and non-root same-UID
  `--password-stdin` smoke provisioning, new-password CPace success, old-password rejection, the clipboard feature
  compile, and all hardening source gates.
- Commit `55349e5e56d346d52dc365ae44d6e8efc39bcc50` (`Remove password-valued CLI provisioning`) is pushed to
  `origin/master`; local `HEAD` and `origin/master` match and the tracked worktree is clean.

### Deferred findings preserved for subsequent single-slice closure

- **CLOSED / STALE NOTE (reconciled at R-S11e-61 audit baseline):** Windows ordinary main IPC no longer uses an
  effectively uncapped codec or unbounded persistent tasks. Commit `57bcb529` introduced the current 256 KiB main
  frame ceiling, fixed 16-transaction admission budget, two-second request/response deadline, tracked `JoinSet`
  ownership, and complete drain. LocalSystem service-main credential/control endpoints have separate fixed budgets
  and drains. The older availability note predated that consolidated closure and is not a live finding.
- **CLOSED by R-S11e-60:** Linux `_service` admission performed active-session lookup synchronously before the
  protected transaction permit, allowing a world-connectable socket peer to induce repeated root `loginctl`/D-Bus
  work. Both protected Linux endpoints now acquire their existing fixed transaction permit before identity work,
  root skips the irrelevant active-session lookup, and non-root peers must match a cached-only active UID before the
  fresh lookup that remains final authority. R-S11at, Appendix C #168, the focused Rust regression, the standalone
  semantic validator, and repository-wide mutations bind the closure. This was an availability boundary follow-up
  to R-S11c-26, not an authorization bypass.
- **CLOSED IN SOURCE by R-S11au/R-S11e-61; native signed-upgrade evidence pending R-R2/R-B2:** the review confirmed
  one narrower live defect. Exact-helper installation already copied and compared the caller-supplied bundled helper,
  but plist-only status suppressed refresh after app upgrades and runtime admitted any same-Team helper without
  byte-binding it to the helper nested in the currently installed signed app. The source closure makes the fixed
  installed app the build authority, validates outer nested code and all architectures, rejects any other installer
  input, revalidates outer-app plus deployed/bundled equality immediately before launch, requires the same equality
  in runtime helper trust, reports stale helper state as needing reinstall, and preserves uninstall for partial/stale
  artifacts. Final commit/push and native evidence are recorded in the R-S11e-61 work log below.
- **Confirmed high:** connection-manager `Data::RawMessage(Vec<u8>)` is an unconstrained authenticated-host protocol
  injection capability. The user-context CM supplies a serialized top-level protobuf `Message`; the
  connection-owning server performs no message, `AuthConnType`, capability, connection-generation, or job check and
  sends those bytes through the keyed stream. The remote viewer therefore accepts the CM-selected bytes as
  server-authenticated traffic. Concrete effects include cross-type video/audio decoder reach, clipboard integrity
  writes in eligible sessions, file-response injection, and malformed-message session termination. This is not a
  direct local root/SYSTEM execution finding and no decoder memory-corruption claim has been established, but it is
  more than availability. Correct closure requires deleting `RawMessage`, introducing narrow typed CM response
  variants carrying connection/generation/job/expected-response authority, validating each against live state and
  `AuthConnType`, and constructing the network `Message` only in the connection-owning server.
- **Confirmed medium on macOS/Windows:** CM launch proof is a server-lifetime bearer token placed in the child
  environment plus executable/`--cm` checks, not exact launched-process binding. Linux additionally verifies live
  ancestry. A compromised legitimate CM necessarily has the token on every platform; on macOS/Windows a copied token
  plus control of a qualifying genuine process is not bound to a retained child identity. Correct endpoint closure
  needs an inherited connected IPC object or exact retained process/audit-token binding. That endpoint improvement
  does not contain a compromised legitimate CM, so the typed least-authority CM vocabulary remains mandatory.

### Windows privilege-boundary findings preserved for subsequent closure

The focused Windows review at baseline `ec226b4f7191a6d5d4cb25c42c3ab1c8417367a7` confirmed the following separate
issues. None was changed as part of R-S11e-16:

1. **CLOSED by R-S11e-20 — elevated EXE install/uninstall accepted caller-authored command authority.** `run_cmds` wrote a complete
   privileged batch program into caller-selected temporary/user-accessible storage and elevates `cmd.exe` to execute
   that path (`src/platform/windows.rs:3051`, `3118`, `3264`, `3284`). Non-MSI uninstall inserts
   `std::env::current_exe()` as the executable for privileged certificate/driver cleanup (`2915`, `2918`, `2919`),
   and process cleanup selects targets by basename through `taskkill /IM` (`2731`, `4218`, `4303`). UUID staging,
   digest/file-identity revalidation, a held deny-write/delete handle, literal filtering, and fixed tools prove byte
   continuity, not operation authority. The concrete UAC-approved chain was a copied/prepared Flutter runner whose
   adjacent `librustdesk.dll` loaded before the Rust cleanup verb, followed by machine-state commands capable of
   creating the LocalSystem service. It required administrator approval and was not a promptless standard-user LPE.
   R-S11e-20 deletes this entire application installer surface and makes a fixed one-file MSI transaction the only
   setup authority; its closure record below supersedes the baseline line references and open disposition.

2. **CLOSED by R-S11e-19 — LocalSystem child ownership and service supervision.** Session transitions overwrote raw
   `h_process` without closing/reaping the prior handle (`779`, `798`). Launch replacement ignores close-delivery
   failure and waits only 100 ms (`888`, `1407`); service shutdown closes the handle and reports `SERVICE_STOPPED`
   without proving child exit (`870`, `875`). Liveness is checked only when `incoming.next()` times out (`802`,
   `832`), so continuously ready IPC suppresses it. SCM close shares the contested four-slot pipe and can be dropped
   (`743`, `816`) without negative acknowledgment. Correct closure needs an RAII job/child owner, independent
   supervision timer, in-process SCM stop event, `STOP_PENDING`, bounded graceful stop, terminate-on-timeout, reap,
   and proof the old child is gone before replacement or `SERVICE_STOPPED`. R-S11e-19 implements that complete
   authority model; the closure record below supersedes the baseline line references and open disposition.

3. **High — privileged service-child main IPC and SAS work remain unbounded.** The LocalSystem child's Windows main
   pipe still uses generic `Connection::new`, an effectively unlimited codec, one task per connection, and an
   indefinite read loop (`src/ipc.rs:695`, `734`, `780`, `3078`). R-S11c-26 bounded `_service`, not this endpoint.
   Every Ctrl+Alt+Del event also creates an OS thread and current-thread Tokio runtime before the SAS mutex serializes
   it (`src/server/input_service.rs:1564`, `1569`, `1934`; `src/platform/windows.rs:1427`, `1445`). Correct closure
   needs explicit main-endpoint frame/connection/idle/work limits or a separated privileged RPC endpoint, plus one
   fixed SAS worker or single-flight/coalescing state machine.

4. **CLOSED by R-S11e-18 — failed named-pipe impersonation restoration.** `ThreadImpersonationGuard::drop` only logged
   `RevertToSelf` failure (`src/ipc/auth.rs:183`, `189`), while `with_impersonated_client_token` returns normally
   (`2098`, `2111`). Subsequent LocalSystem service work may execute under the client's token. Restoration must be
   checked before return and inability to prove it must terminate the service, or each impersonation must occur in a
   dedicated disposable worker thread. R-S11e-18 implements process-fatal restoration proof on every return/unwind
   path; its closure record below supersedes this baseline disposition.

5. **Medium — token-switched helper environment construction silently falls back.** `CreateEnvironmentBlock` result
   is unchecked before `CreateProcessAsUserW` (`src/platform/windows.cc:359`, `362`, `376`). A null/partial block can
   inherit service context or omit a valid token-derived user environment. Environment-block creation and structural
   validation must be mandatory; launcher-owned additions may be merged only after success.

6. **Medium — privacy broker process ownership remains incomplete; installed-runtime update provenance is closed.**
   R-S11e-20 removes broker copying from setup and changes the installed-runtime updater to derive System32, require
   the exact fixed service image and Program Files destination, reject reparse source/target files, stage locally, and
   prove SHA-256 equality without shell/UAC/basename termination. Normal non-installer portable execution still has a
   separate runtime-broker copy path, and pre-commit injection/readiness failures plus the
   ResumeThread failure path can leak or strand the broker before handles enter the long-lived owner (`272`, `294`,
   `300`, `314`). Correct closure requires `GetSystemDirectoryW`, opened-object provenance checks, and immediate
   kill-on-close RAII job ownership with terminate/wait/close on every failure. This item therefore remains open only
   for normal portable execution and injected broker child lifecycle, not installed setup/update authority.

7. **CLOSED by R-S11e-20 — MSI firewall failures could report success.** COM initialization and several allocation failures left a
   separate `hr` as `S_OK`, including add/remove rule paths (`res/msi/CustomActions/FirewallRules.cpp:46`, `61`,
   `109`, `128`, `137`, `202`, `213`, `241`, `255`, `271`, `278`). Every branch must return its real failure HRESULT,
   with negative tests for COM and each allocation failure. R-S11e-20 deletes that C++ implementation and its exports,
   schedules, and source file. A file-bound WiX `fire:FirewallException` owns the inbound rule with
   `IgnoreFailure="no"`, so failure participates in the MSI transaction and rollback.

8. **CLOSED by R-S11e-20 — MSI service lifecycle completion was not transactional.** Failed start/running-state proof left a newly
   created service installed and no rollback action exists (`res/msi/CustomActions/CustomActions.cpp:1123`, `1130`,
   `1137`; `res/msi/Package/Fragments/CustomActions.wxs:12`). Deletion ignores exact-image cleanup failure; helpers do
   not check `TerminateProcess` (`CustomActions.cpp:846`, `980`, `1204`, `1207`). Prefer MSI service tables or an
   exact-command rollback action; cleanup must retain handles, check termination, bounded-wait, rescan exact image
   identity, and prove absence. R-S11e-20 deletes the custom SCM implementation and basename process killer.
   `ServiceInstall`, `ServiceControl`, and nested `util:ServiceConfig` now bind create/start/stop/remove/recovery state
   to the package-owned application component and Windows Installer rollback.

Two Windows sinks remain review questions rather than confirmed unprivileged paths: `RegRecovery` durably stores and
replays arbitrary HKLM path/key/type/value fields (`src/platform/windows.rs:4571`, `4627`;
`src/privacy_mode/win_virtual_display.rs:570`), and service-owned RDP policy chooses among legacy uninstall keys using
mutable `InstallLocation` metadata (`src/platform/windows.rs:1780`, `1551`). Their durable schemas/selectors should be
receiver-derived even if current producer authorization prevents an unprivileged exploit.

## R-S11e-17 closure — typed connection-manager file response authority (2026-07-12)

### Proven inherited path and impact

- `src/ui_cm_interface.rs` accepted a complete protobuf `Message`, serialized it, and emitted
  `Data::RawMessage(Vec<u8>)`; `src/server/connection.rs` accepted that CM value and called
  `conn.stream.send_raw(bytes)` without checking message type, file operation, job phase, generation, or
  `AuthConnType`. CM therefore selected authenticated host traffic rather than returning a file-operation result.
- The worker needed only directory, empty-directory, operation completion/error, read-job init/block/done/error/digest,
  all-files, write failure/finalization, write digest, and send-confirm semantics. The raw top-level envelope exposed
  every remote protobuf union and malformed-message termination. This was CWE-441/CWE-863 capability confusion, not
  a demonstrated local root execution path: traffic went outward to an already authenticated file-transfer peer, but
  it crossed protocol capabilities and remote parser/state boundaries the delegated file operation did not authorize.
- Peer IDs were insufficient authority. Read/write namespaces could overlap; cancellation permitted ID reuse; write
  completion removed the reservation before CM acknowledged finalization; digest checks lacked independent request
  generations; and one-shot directory/mutation responses were not operation-bound.

### Implemented authority model

- Deleted `Data::RawMessage`, all legacy CM result variants, raw protobuf directory/result blobs, raw serialized
  `FS::SendConfirm`, and CM-side top-level network-message construction.
- Added a closed serde-native `CmFileResponseKind` result vocabulary in a `CmFileResponse` envelope bound to exact
  `conn_id` and the existing random per-session `cm_auth_token`. Generic CM filesystem authority is now exact
  `FileTransfer`; Remote clipboard authority remains separate and Remote-only.
- Each `Connection` mints monotonic read/write generations and bounded one-shot request generations. Mutation results
  echo the exact typed operation kind and path. It validates authenticated FileTransfer mode, connection/token,
  generation, response kind, phase, ID/path/file number, metadata count/serialized size, and bounded error text.
- CM job IDs cannot overlap or be reused during a connection. Reads track monotonic current-file progression and an
  exact digest-confirmation phase. Writes use exclusive `Active`, `CheckingDigest`, `AwaitingPeerConfirm`, and
  `Finalizing` phases; blocks and successful completion are rejected while a digest is unresolved, peer errors remain
  terminally admissible, and final authority remains until typed CM acknowledgement. Cross-kind/stale/out-of-phase
  responses do not consume current authority. A failed helper-channel enqueue retires its pending request/job
  authority and reports failure instead of leaving an advanced phase live.
- Directory-list and transfer-manifest validation are distinct: canonical Windows drive descriptors are accepted only
  for an authorized virtual-root listing, while transfer manifests retain strict relative-name validation.
- CM returns structured file DTOs and `Connection` alone constructs peer-facing protobuf messages. Structured `_cm`
  frames have a 128 MiB decoder ceiling. Before the only split raw frame, a typed `ReadBlock` payload, the bridge
  validates FileTransfer mode/connection/token, reduces the decoder ceiling to 256 KiB, and applies a five-second
  deadline. Exact generation/current-file phase is checked before peer message construction.

### Platform disposition and proof

- Linux, Windows, macOS, and Android controlled-side file paths share the closed types and checks. iOS retains source
  coherence but has no controlled server. Desktop CM endpoint authentication and Android in-process channel admission
  remain independent prerequisite gates.
- Targeted Rust 1.75 container compile passed. `cm_file_authority_*`, `cm_file_response_authority_*`, typed directory/
  all-files result tests, and typed `ReadBlock` split-serialization tests pass.
- `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` now source-gate absence of every raw/legacy response surface
  and require the token/generation/request/phase state machine. `requirements.html` adds normative R-S11e and Appendix
  C #122; `HARDENING_STATUS.md` records R-S11e-17 closed. The requirements hash is re-pinned in the native-codec watch.

### Final committed proof

- Implementation commit: `580c063` (`Constrain CM file responses to typed authority`).
- Gate-correction commits: `f0b8485`, `faebf97`, and `9e0dfff`; these narrow stale source-extraction/string assertions
  to the implemented single-arm, normative-title, and single-token-mint shapes without weakening the checks.
- `scripts/verify.sh` passed from committed `9e0dfff`: KATs, handshake, CM authority/serialization/codec tests,
  no-follow/path tests, both Linux main-crate compile modes, completed-excision gates, and reproducibility gates.
- `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` passed from the same commit, including R-S11e-17 and the macOS/iOS cross-compile
  coherence matrix.

## R-S11e-18 closure — Windows named-pipe impersonation restoration (2026-07-12)

### Proven path and impact

- The Windows LocalSystem `_service` process impersonates connected clients to authorize elevated unattended-password
  and service-owned RDP policy requests. The Windows service-owned main IPC server impersonates the committing pipe
  client to require LocalSystem. A service-owned credential commit performs that main-pipe proof twice: once during
  pre-dispatch classification and once at the final receiver-owned commit check.
- Both processes run their IPC tasks on reusable current-thread Tokio runtimes. `_service` transactions share the
  LocalSystem service runtime thread; main IPC connections share the server's dedicated IPC thread. Impersonation is
  thread-local and no `.await` occurs inside the token query, but neither fact contains a failed restoration after the
  query returns.
- The inherited `ThreadImpersonationGuard::drop` logged `RevertToSelf` failure and returned the already computed token
  result. Windows leaves the thread in the client's context after such a failure and directs the application to
  terminate. The stale identity could therefore bleed into later requests as reduced or elevated client authority.
  This is a Windows-only cross-request principal-confusion flaw, not a proven normal-condition local-to-SYSTEM
  escalation: exploitation additionally requires an actual restoration failure.

### Closed design

- The generic callback-shaped impersonation helper is deleted. `WindowsPipeClientTokenRequirement` is a closed
  `Elevated`/`LocalSystem` vocabulary; it performs only the two required token predicates and cannot accumulate
  blocking, async, filesystem, or unrelated work inside the impersonation window.
- `windows_pipe_client_token_satisfies` captures every success/error result, explicitly invokes
  `ThreadImpersonationGuard::restore`, and returns the result only after successful restoration. Token-open errors use
  the same path. Panic/unwind retains an active guard and calls the same restoration primitive.
- `revert_thread_impersonation_or_abort` performs the single `RevertToSelf` attempt and immediately calls
  `std::process::abort` on failure. It does not log, return an error, retry through a different API, or permit the
  contaminated executor thread to survive.
- `scripts/verify.sh` parses the guard, fail-stop primitive, explicit-before-return ordering, closed token vocabulary,
  absence of the generic callback, and requirements/status disposition. `requirements.html` makes the process-fatal
  restoration invariant normative in R-S11c, updates Appendix C #25, and records the full Windows-only exposure in
  Appendix C #123. `HARDENING_STATUS.md` records R-S11e-18 closed.

### Final committed proof

- Implementation commit: `7c38462` (`Fail stop Windows pipe impersonation restoration`).
- Independent read-only call-trace review confirmed both current-thread runtime reuse paths, every elevation/
  LocalSystem call site, the lack of surrounding containment, the process-fatal Windows contract, and the closed-enum
  improvement. The reviewer made no edits.
- `scripts/verify.sh` passed from committed `7c38462`, including the R-S11e-18 structural gate, all focused security
  tests, both Linux compile modes, completed-excision gates, and reproducibility/source gates.
- `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh` passed from the same commit, including the full macOS/iOS source and cross-compile
  matrix. The gate was non-mutating.
- Final requirements hash: `defb467f61db2528b686af1bfc53e02759f952e514f0330289938d85fb49095c`.

## R-S11e-19 closure — Windows service-owned child tree supervision (2026-07-12)

### Proven inherited path and impact

- The LocalSystem SCM service retained only a raw handle for the current service-owned server child. Session-change
  paths could overwrite it without proving the old process or descendants absent, and one path committed the new
  remembered session before checking active port forwards. A deferred handoff was therefore lost permanently.
- Both handoff paths mapped port-forward query errors to zero. Child liveness was checked only after an idle
  `_service` accept timeout, so sustained service IPC could suppress supervision. Main-process exit did not account
  for descendants.
- SCM Stop/Preshutdown/Shutdown synchronously created a nested Tokio runtime and sent `_service Data::Close` through
  the same four-slot service channel. Transactions were detached. The service reported Running before listener/child
  startup, never reported StopPending, closed only its raw process handle, and reported Stopped without a process-tree
  absence proof.
- The resulting exposure was stale or overlapping privileged service-owned child trees, remote-session retention,
  and false SCM completion on Windows installed-service systems. It was not independently promoted to a demonstrated
  standard-user-to-SYSTEM execution primitive.

### Closed design

- Each launch first creates a fresh unnamed non-inheritable job and configures
  `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`. `LaunchProcessWin` uses a one-entry
  `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` in `STARTUPINFOEXW` with `EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT` and
  `bInheritHandles = FALSE`. On the Windows 11 product baseline, Windows assigns the child to the job during process
  creation before its initial thread can run; the abandoned suspended-but-unassigned process state does not exist.
- The service owns RAII job/process handles, exact PID, and served session. It independently polls the process object
  and aggregate job `ActiveProcesses`. Desired, listener, and served sessions remain distinct until handoff commits.
  Active or unknown port-forward state preserves the current tree and is re-queried; zero retires it; main-process
  death retires any surviving descendants. The latest desired session remains pending throughout deferral.
- Port-forward count and graceful-close IPC authenticate the connected fixed LocalSystem service-owned main server
  and require its pipe-server PID to equal the retained process PID. Graceful close has a bounded wait. Any remaining
  tree is terminated with `TerminateJobObject`; replacement and clean stop require a subsequent zero-active-process
  proof.
- SCM Stop/Preshutdown now latches a direct unbounded in-process signal and immediately reports StopPending. Running
  advertises only STOP and PRESHUTDOWN. `_service Data::Close`, nested runtime stop, Shutdown handling, raw handle
  overwrite, unknown-to-zero conversion, and detached service transactions are deleted. A `JoinSet` owns every
  accepted service transaction and shutdown aborts/drains it before child cleanup. Stopped is reported only after
  exact-tree absence; failure returns abnormally without a clean-stopped claim.

### Proof

- Microsoft documents `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` for Windows 10+/Server 2016+ and job assignment before the
  initial thread runs; job objects retain descendants by default, support nested jobs on the product baseline, and
  `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` terminates the associated tree when the service's final job handle closes.
- Pure `windows_service_` tests cover no-session launch, active/unknown port-forward deferral, idle handoff, dead-main
  descendant retirement, and same-session stability. `scripts/build-windows.ps1` runs that focused suite natively,
  offline and locked, before artifact compilation.
- `scripts/verify.sh` gates creation-time job assignment, job ownership/accounting/termination, exact-child IPC,
  independent liveness and handoff state, direct SCM signal/status checkpoints, tracked transaction drain, Stopped
  ordering, deleted paths, R-S11e-19, and Appendix C #124.
- Requirements hash: `6d31515fa0825dffd113607fe60484294d28207bdef9d423e2b355b64e3eaa51`.

## R-S11e-20 closure — Windows Installer sole machine-state authority (2026-07-12)

### Proven inherited authority defect

- Public application verbs implemented install, uninstall, before/after-install, certificate cleanup, Amyuni cleanup,
  and direct service installation. Flutter exposed an in-app install page and bridge. `run_cmds` generated complete
  batch/VBS programs, stored them outside the final package transaction, and UAC-elevated System32 `cmd.exe` to run
  them. Fixed tool provenance and command-file digest/identity checks proved which bytes the shell read, but did not
  prove those bytes described an authorized operation.
- Non-MSI uninstall embedded `std::env::current_exe()` as the elevated cleanup helper. The Windows Flutter runner loads
  executable-adjacent `librustdesk.dll` before Rust dispatches a cleanup verb. An administrator who approved UAC for
  a copied or attacker-prepared application directory could therefore execute that adjacent DLL elevated; the same
  command program could create the LocalSystem service. This is a concrete UAC-approved caller-image authority chain,
  not a promptless standard-user-to-SYSTEM exploit.
- Application code and MSI custom actions independently mutated Program Files payloads, registry, shortcuts, service,
  firewall, runtime files, and drivers. The MSI killed processes by basename and implemented SCM/firewall state in C++
  outside declarative rollback. Firewall COM/allocation failure and failed service start/running proof could diverge
  from reported package success.

### Closed design

- Windows Installer is the only owner of machine installation state. Application install/uninstall/helper/service
  functions and CLI arms, command-file generation, prior-uninstall-string parsing/replay, direct service mutation,
  in-app Flutter install route/page/bridge methods, and their obsolete helpers/tests/comments are deleted.
- `rustdesk-setup.exe` is recognized only by exact case-insensitive current-executable basename. Its command grammar is
  closed to no arguments, exact `--silent-install`, and one fixed internal protected marker that is rejected unless the
  process is actually elevated. Its manifest must contain exactly one root `rustdesk-installer.msi`; no application
  EXE, DLL, nested path, or extra payload is admitted. The protected leg creates no-reparse Program Files staging,
  extracts only the MSI with create-new semantics, verifies it is a regular non-reparse file, resolves System32
  `msiexec.exe` through `GetSystemDirectoryW`, invokes it directly with `/i <msi> /norestart` and optional `/qn`, waits,
  and accepts only 0 or 3010. It never extracts, executes, or loads packaged application code. Cleanup attempts every
  manifest item on every result path and aggregates failures.
- The authoritative Windows build creates the Flutter distribution, builds the MSI, canonicalizes and validates that
  MSI before embedding, creates a dedicated one-file setup payload, copies and SHA-256-checks the canonical MSI as
  `rustdesk-installer.msi`, invokes the generator with checked locked/offline Cargo, removes the payload directory in
  `finally`, and consumes only exact artifact paths. Generic `build.py --flutter` no longer creates the legacy
  `*-install.exe`; the obsolete non-Flutter and portable-pack bypasses are deleted. The offline Python media includes
  an exact `olefile` 0.47 wheel and SHA-256 pin.
- WiX binds the package-owned application file to an exact inbound TCP/21118, failure-authoritative
  `fire:FirewallException`. The same component owns declarative `ServiceInstall`, `ServiceControl`, and 5/10/30-second
  restart recovery through core WiX `ServiceConfigFailureActions`. The service is the sole persistence owner; the
  independent all-users Startup shortcut is deleted. Custom firewall, service, and basename-termination definitions,
  exports, schedules, implementations, and source files are deleted.
- Test-certificate and Amyuni cleanup are checked MSI commit actions scheduled only for explicit uninstall, not
  upgrade. Test-certificate removal accepts only the exact validated fingerprint. Amyuni cleanup is self-contained
  SetupAPI code with no `CustomActionData`, install-root, installed helper, or child-process dependency. Exact
  runtime-generated broker cleanup remains a checked deferred MSI operation before `RemoveFiles` on uninstall and
  upgrade.
- Installed-runtime broker refresh requires the exact fixed service executable, fixed no-reparse System32 source, and
  fixed no-reparse Program Files destination. Source, pending, and destination content are SHA-256 validated; refresh
  is process-serialized, writes a create-new unique pending file, and atomically commits with `ReplaceFileW` plus
  write-through or rename when absent. It never deletes the last-known-good image first, and every commit or
  `WindowInjection.dll` provenance failure propagates without a shell, UAC, caller path, or basename process kill.

### Cost and platform scope

- Windows loses the custom EXE installer, in-app install choices, arbitrary custom install path, and application CLI
  install/uninstall compatibility. Setup, repair, upgrade, and uninstall use MSI semantics and MSI-authored shortcut
  properties. The setup artifact now embeds the MSI rather than a second full Flutter payload; the standalone MSI is
  still emitted. Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS installation behavior is unchanged.
- No full Windows VM artifact build was run in this slice. The portable tests and isolated Windows-target compile prove
  bootstrapper source shape, while the repository Windows VM build remains the authoritative WiX/C++/PowerShell and
  artifact integration proof.

### Final committed proof

- Implementation commit: `015320d` (`Make MSI the sole Windows install authority`). Follow-up commits `7a87035` and
  `ef8b822` remove the final dead Flutter installer argument and correct literal matching in the structural verifier.
  `master` and `origin/master` resolve to `ef8b8226b4ebb20d9f72cdad102f0d9c65762a8b`.
- `scripts/verify.sh` passed from committed `ef8b822`, including the installer authority/excision gates, focused
  security tests, policy and handshake gates, both Linux main-crate compile modes, and reproducibility gates.
- `scripts/apple-conform-check.sh`, `scripts/dart-verify.sh`, and `scripts/flutter-verify.sh` passed from the same tree.
  Dart verification performed full FRB generation, zero-error Flutter analysis, six address-validator tests, and all
  UI security gates. Apple verification passed the macOS aarch64/x86_64 and iOS aarch64 coherence matrix.
- Portable bootstrapper tests passed 3/3 under locked offline Cargo, covering exact setup basename, exact MSI status
  policy, and closed command grammar. An isolated `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` locked/offline compile passed. Shell syntax,
  Python AST, HTML parsing, WiX XML parsing, and `git diff --check` also passed.
- Three independent read-only adversarial reviews covered MSI/native actions, setup/build behavior, and UI/docs/gates;
  their findings were incorporated before final verification. No Windows VM artifact build or release was performed.
- `requirements.html` adds normative R-S11f and Appendix C #125; `HARDENING_STATUS.md` records R-S11e-20 closed, and
  `scripts/verify.sh` permanently gates both the positive architecture and absence of deleted authority paths.
- Final requirements hash: `367cd517960457be0df6ac9b303670c1f6bf7520b702adcb9289baf7589cdb95`.

### Retained private-tree authority

- One no-network, no-pull, read-only-root Debian container with exactly `DAC_READ_SEARCH` and `CHOWN` acquires all
  directory and unique non-directory inode descriptors before mutation. It records exact inventories, edges, mount
  identity, modes, link counts, and complete internal hardlink counts; rejects mounts, special objects, external
  hardlinks, changed inventories, and changed authorities; normalizes through retained descriptors; and re-proves all
  postconditions.
- Linux `fs.protected_hardlinks` must contain exactly `1\n`. Modes strip setuid, setgid, sticky, and group/world-write
  bits while restoring owner access; the private root returns to the invoking UID/GID at mode 0700.
- The 131,072-entry limit now has a 256-descriptor reserve. Docker sets soft and hard `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to 131,328, and
  the helper establishes and re-proves the same budget before normalization or complete inode-closure acquisition.
  The first clean-clone reset test exposed the inherited 1,024-descriptor limit; the corrected test rejects the
  external hardlink for the intended reason, normalizes the hostile root-owned tree, resets it exactly, and removes
  the large private workspace through retained authority.
- Recursive private-workspace removal acquires complete hardlink closure, removes only authenticated descriptor-relative
  edges, requires every retained link count and the root link count to reach zero, synchronizes the parent, and reports
  every close failure. Deliberately concurrent same-UID namespace mutation remains outside the cooperative release
  transaction; root, kernel, and trusted storage remain trusted.

### Same-parent ext4 publication

- Publication is Linux ext4-only. Descriptor-bound `fstatfs` magic must agree with the exact runtime mount's
  `/proc/self/mountinfo` filesystem type. Descriptor-bound `FS_IOC_GETFSUUID` must return the nonzero 16-byte external
  ext4 UUID, and the journal binds that complete UUID with opaque parent, payload, and prior-destination handles.
  Folded `f_fsid` and runtime mount IDs are never durable identity.
- Untrusted file edges are acquired with `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW`, proved regular, reopened nonblocking through their exact
  retained `/proc/self/fd/N` authority, and re-proved. This closes the reproduced FIFO hang before record, source,
  release, and cleanup type validation.
- The mode-0400 v3 journal is durable in `initializing` state before payload creation. A same-parent empty mode-0700
  payload is parent-synchronized, then its persistent handle is committed in `staging` before copy. Exact synchronized
  content advances to manifest-bound `prepared`; `rollback` or `cleanup` is durable before partial deletion.
- Recovery removes an initializing record only when no payload exists. An unbound observed payload is preserved and
  rejected; a staging payload is removable only through its recorded persistent handle. First installation uses
  `RENAME_NOREPLACE`; replacement uses same-parent `RENAME_EXCHANGE`. Public verification never recovers or repairs and
  rejects any reserved `.dist-release-*` state before and after exact destination proof.
- Process-restart fixtures cover first and replacement publication at staging, prepared, rollback authorization,
  exchange, cleanup authorization, and payload removal, plus unbound payload creation, no-clobber, partial deletion,
  wrong-token canonical payload and next-record names, malformed names/records, multiple and oversized records, missing
  prior state, destination ABA, root/entry modes, hardlinks, xattrs, incomplete content, and special-file substitution.
  They do not claim physical power-loss testing.

### Independent adversarial closure

- Recovery already rejected a canonical `.next` or payload sibling whose token did not belong to the active journal,
  but neither static contracts nor behavior protected those two checks. The verifier now requires each ownership guard
  independently, mutates each away independently, and the publication fixture preserves and rejects both wrong-token
  states before proving recovery only after exact restoration.
- The path-authority proof's persistent object-handle acquisition, the normalizer's initial external-hardlink rejection,
  and its final inode owner/mode postconditions are now explicit mutation-protected contracts.
- The retained-tree helper now has one exhaustive descriptor-close collector and one primary-error-preserving reporter.
  Scratch root, retained inode, normalization, protected-hardlink, traversal, and fixture descriptor cleanup all use that
  authority. The behavioral fixture injects two close failures, proves both close attempts occur, proves an existing
  primary error remains primary with both failures attached, and proves a cleanup-only failure reports both causes.
- Linux `statfs.f_fsid` is only ext4's 64-bit fold of its 128-bit UUID and is not a canonical filesystem identity.
  Publication now requires Linux 6.9's generic descriptor-bound `FS_IOC_GETFSUUID`, rejects an unavailable, non-16-byte,
  or zero result, and records the complete external ext4 UUID. Static mutations reject removal of the ioctl and of the
  persistent path-object handle.
- The documentation verifier now reads `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
  `docs/VERSIONING.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`; checks the private-repository, ext4 UUID, journal, token,
  nonblocking-open, logical-restart, and trust-boundary contracts; rejects superseded authority text; and requires both
  tracked ledgers to contain the exact SHA-256 of the normative requirements.

### GNU-stack producer and loader authority correction

- Complete retained-bundle inventory found three legitimate `PT_GNU_STACK.p_align` conventions under the pinned
  release inputs: Dart AOT `libapp.so` emits 1, the prebuilt Flutter engine emits 0, and the GNU-linked runner, Rust
  core, and eight plugins emit 16. All 12 headers have zero offset, virtual/physical addresses, file size, and memory
  size with exact `PF_R|PF_W` and no execute bit. The earlier build stopped at sorted `libapp.so`; accepting only 1
  would therefore have exposed a second false rejection at `libflutter_linux_gtk.so`.
- The generic ELF ABI defines 0 and 1 as no alignment requirement and otherwise requires a positive power of two with
  congruent file/virtual offsets. Linux v4.15 and current `fs/binfmt_elf.c` derive GNU-stack execution only from
  `p_flags & PF_X`; glibc 2.27 and current `elf/dl-load.c` likewise consume DSO GNU-stack flags, not alignment. Flutter
  3.24.5 pins engine `a18df97ca57a249df5d8d68cd0820600223ce262`, which pins Dart
  `88c9758ef131d430d8ce595c6bfb4c90574d3ddd`; that exact Dart ELF writer deliberately returns alignment 1 for
  `PT_GNU_STACK` and describes the header as preventing executable-stack promotion. GNU BFD 2.30's backend stack
  alignment explains 16; LLVM's GNU-stack output uses 0. Alignment is producer formatting, not the NX decision.
- The corrected package policy requires exactly one unambiguous GNU-stack header; exact zero offset, virtual/physical
  addresses, file size, and memory size as this package's canonical no-content form; exact `PF_R|PF_W` with no execute
  or extra flags; and ABI-valid alignment 0, 1, or a positive power of two. It no longer confuses GNU BFD's 16-byte
  convention with the security property. The verifier now inspects every formerly ignored header field.
- Self-tests independently accept alignments 0, 1, and 16 and reject missing/duplicate headers, each nonzero
  no-content field, executable/read-only/write-only/extra-bit permissions, and non-power-of-two alignment 3. Host
  Python 3.12 and exact no-network/read-only-root Ubuntu 18.04 Python 3.6.9 tests pass; logs
  `/tmp/rustdesk-debian-stack-authority-host.log` and `/tmp/rustdesk-debian-stack-authority-pinned.log`, both SHA-256
  `82e2af6082f0a40db51ce90d350823641d784e8364452d94e59f103871a0774c`. Direct validation passes all 12 retained real
  bundle ELFs; log `/tmp/rustdesk-debian-stack-real-bundle.log`, SHA-256
  `44310f54abaa4752e0927bd514ec7a1fbfe14e8935750205e54ddd52e426c126`. A runtime probe varying only GNU-stack
  alignment across 0, 1, and 16 observed `rw-p` `[stack]` mappings in every case; log
  `/tmp/rustdesk-gnu-stack-runtime-probe.log`, SHA-256
  `511edcacba2378bdb95dc5deaa7a095d6b6c2c19d2316060cd65c9723ef579b0`.
- Normative row 119, R-S11c-10y, and the release notes now state the semantic/canonical policy. Current requirements

  `bf86c585820fa91d206ddf0efa1a8c6d8ed43e39` (`Correct Debian GNU stack artifact policy`). Complete committed-source

## 2026-07-16 — Current-release same-host smoke coexistence slice

### Selection and scope

- The earliest explicit release blocker in `HARDENING_STATUS.md` was the current runtime-smoke collision with an
  operational older RustDesk service whose historical privileged cleanup can select host-visible
  `rustdesk +--server` process text. This invocation closes only that current-release harness defect. The separate
  init-system-independent Linux service-child ownership redesign remains open for upcoming releases; no RustDesk
  lifecycle code, package, unit, service, or deployed process was changed.
- The vulnerable harness shape was direct: `scripts/smoke-server.sh` placed complete inline `bash -c` programs in
  Docker client/runtime argv and those programs contained `rustdesk --server`; every test server then used the same
  production-shaped visible argv. A host selector sees host `/proc`, including Docker client/runtime command lines,
  regardless of the container's internal PID namespace. The old operational service itself was outside repository
  control and was treated as immutable baseline, never a test fixture or cleanup target.

### Researched authority model

- Linux `execve(2)` defines the executed pathname separately from the argument vector and documents argv zero as a
  convention, not executable identity. `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` exposes the NUL-delimited argument vector and is mutable
  presentation state; `/proc/<pid>/exe` identifies the executed file object. Sources:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html,
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_cmdline.5.html, and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html.
- Docker uses private PID and network namespaces by default; a container port reaches host interfaces only when a
  publish option is supplied, while host networking removes network isolation. Sources:
  https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/ and
  https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/.
- Correct harness authority is therefore two independent proofs: (1) no smoke-created host-visible process may match
  the historical text selector, and (2) textual separation must not weaken what is tested, so every server must still
  be bound by PID/start time to the exact executable device/inode and exact role argument. A pre-existing selector
  match is admitted only as an exact stable baseline identity. The guard has no signal authority.

### Implementation

- Added `scripts/smoke-server-stage.sh` and replaced all large inline Docker shell bodies with exact mounted stage-file
  dispatch. Runtime source is read-only. Docker retains its default PID/network isolation, has no host-network,
  host-PID, privileged, or publish flags, and the bind shim still rewrites only the container listener to
  `127.0.0.1:21118`.

  `O_NOFOLLOW`, validates the opened file, and `fexecve`s that descriptor with only
  `argv = ["rd-smoke-server", "--server"]`, inheriting the existing environment. It invokes no shell and performs no
  path reopen after validation.
- Added `scripts/smoke-process-guard.py`. Before Docker it obtains two identical full-host `/proc` scans, records exact
  PID/start-time/raw-cmdline matches in a private mode-0600 no-follow single-link file, and then scans every 10 ms
  throughout all stages and once more at final drain. It admits only records exactly present in the stable baseline,
  fails on new matches, and owns no process signal operation. A separate wait binds every test server to exact start
  time, `/proc/<pid>/exe` device/inode, and NUL argv `[rd-smoke-server, --server]`.
- Source gates pin the mounted-stage count, absence of inline/host-network/host-PID/privileged/publish/sudo/pkill

  Rust compatibility: `core_main` discards argv zero, server dispatch consumes argument one, `IS_SERVER` reads

## 2026-07-16 — Linux direct service-child ownership / parent-death slice (R-S11c-27a)

### Selection and proved authority defect

- This invocation selected exactly the first coherent slice of the open upcoming-release Linux service-child
  lifecycle item: direct ownership of the live final child, a race-safe supervisor-death relationship across the
  credential-drop/exec path, and deletion of the global `--server` process sweep. Durable crash/restart records,
  pidfd-based recovery plus old-kernel fallback, the stale/corrupt/PID-reuse/file-replacement matrix, packaging for
  every init path, and non-systemd/Docker release harnesses remain explicitly open for later slices.
- The old active-user launch called generic `run_as_user()`, so the supervisor's retained `Child` could be the fixed
  `sudo` wrapper rather than the final RustDesk server. `start_os_service()` also called
  `stop_rustdesk_servers()`/`force_stop_server()`, which selected every current-executable process with exact
  `--server` argv from the global process table. That was path/argv discovery, not service ownership, and could not
  distinguish another lifecycle, portable server, build, or container authority. The existing normal child stop was
  SIGTERM-first and bounded, but was only as exact as the wrapper returned by the launch abstraction.

### Primary research and design decision

- `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` is delivered when the creating parent thread dies, is cleared for a child by credential changes,
  can be cleared by a privileged/capability-bearing exec, and requires a set-then-`getppid()` check to close the
  already-dead-parent race. `execve` preserves ordinary descriptors and replaces the process image. Rust's Unix
  `CommandExt::pre_exec` runs after `fork` and requires async-signal-safe work; Rust's built-in uid/gid setup occurs
  before registered pre-exec closures, but the stable Rust 1.75 API has no complete supplementary-group setter.
  Sources: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html,
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html, and
  https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/unix/process/trait.CommandExt.html.
- The Linux kernel documents that `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` is irreversible, inherited through fork/clone/exec, and
  prevents `execve` from gaining privilege through setuid/setgid bits, file capabilities, or an LSM relaxation. The
  dedicated service child sets it after its native identity drop and before the final exec/death binding. Source:
  https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/no_new_privs.html.
- The resulting authority is the retained, unreaped final `Child` while the supervisor lives. Normal stop targets only
  that exact child: SIGTERM, bounded wait, then `Child::kill()` and reap. Abnormal supervisor death is bound by
  `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)` because running an inherited Rust signal handler between fork and exec is not an
  async-signal-safe shutdown mechanism; the final image re-arms immediately at `core_main` entry and rejects a
  changed parent before any global initialization. `/proc/self/exe` selects the supervisor's exact executable object
  even across an installed-path replacement. The child environment is cleared and rebuilt from a fixed PATH plus
  the bounded passwd/session inputs, so root loader/environment state is not inherited.

### Implementation and current partial disposition

- `src/platform/linux.rs` now resolves the active passwd identity and supplementary groups in the parent, launches
  `/proc/self/exe --server --service-owned-server` directly, and performs only raw allocation-free
  `setgroups` → `setresgid` → `setresuid` → `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` → `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`/`getppid` operations in
  `pre_exec`. `OwnedServiceChild` contains the final RustDesk `Child`; every live replacement and shutdown path uses
  it. Root/headless children use the same direct launch, bounded environment, no-new-privileges, and parent-death
  protocol without a credential drop.
- `src/core_main.rs` re-arms and revalidates the service-owned parent relationship at the first line of desktop
  `core_main`, before global init/custom-client/config/log work. Portable/user-owned `--server` processes without the
  internal service role marker never enter this path. All `stop_rustdesk_servers()`/`force_stop_server()` definitions
  and calls are deleted; the remaining CM/Xorg/tray helper cleanup is not server lifecycle authority.
- The behavior test execs the already-built test binary as controller → supervisor → worker. The worker arms the
  production post-exec helper and reports through a private mode-0700 Unix-socket directory; the controller opens a
  pidfd, kills the exact supervisor `Child`, and proves the worker becomes poll-readable. RAII cleanup kills/reaps the
  supervisor on every panic and uses the pidfd for exact worker cleanup. This replaced an initial raw double-fork
  fixture, reducing the inventory delta from 30 to seven lexical unsafe blocks while strengthening the exec proof.
- `scripts/verify.sh` runs that behavior test and binds direct `/proc/self/exe` launch, cleared environment, native
  supplementary/primary credential order, no-new-privileges before parent binding, pre/post-exec binding, exact
  bounded child termination, and the absence of any global server sweep. R-S11c-10b now covers only the remaining
  CM/Xorg/tray helpers and actively rejects a server sweep. `HARDENING_STATUS.md` records R-S11c-27a as source
  implemented while keeping the parent lifecycle item open. The lexical unsafe inventory is now 773 across the same
  243 files/66 nonzero files, with digest
  `ee1d2580f0ec66ebd7a8f3681fb9ff69426f7a26b42805e7349ef2938b479b46`; normative requirements SHA-256 is
  `c1a17ab52a143435d628a039fa3018bc269a7fa37271bae67d798bf2db3aade0`.

### Proof before the clean-commit verifier

- Pinned Rust 1.75 dev-check container: focused exec-chain lifecycle behavior test passes; the existing exact-argv

## 2026-07-16 — Durable Linux service-child record / pidfd-first recovery slice (R-S11c-27b)

### Selection and prior authority gap

- The open lifecycle checklist was re-read from the user attachment, `/tmp/ralph_loop_prompt.md`, normative R-S11,
  R-S11a/b/c, R-S16, R-S19, Appendix C #25–#29, and the exact `HARDENING_STATUS.md` residual. R-S11c-27a had closed
  live direct-child ownership and supervisor-death binding only. The next earliest coherent blocker was durable
  crash evidence plus restart-time recovery; the parent item remains open for the complete installed/non-systemd
  behavior matrix.
- Before this slice, a crashed supervisor left no durable authority a new non-systemd supervisor could consume. A
  later PID or argv scan would reintroduce the exact wrong abstraction deleted by 27a. There was also no supervisor
  singleton, so two manually launched service supervisors could independently enter the loop and make any one-record
  protocol ambiguous.

### Primary research and authority model

- Linux `pidfd_open(2)` returns a close-on-exec descriptor for one task, is pollable for exit, and is the preferred
  existing-process acquisition primitive. `pidfd_send_signal(2)` documents the security property directly: unlike
  integer-PID `kill(2)`, the descriptor is stable across PID recycling and an exited target yields `ESRCH`. Sources:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_send_signal.2.html.
- `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 is the process start time since boot; parsing must use the final `) ` terminator because
  `comm` is parenthesized. `/proc/<pid>/exe` dereferences to the executed file object and remains identifiable with a
  ` (deleted)` pathname after unlink, so device/inode is the relevant identity and pathname text is not. Sources:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_stat.5.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html.
- The kernel documents `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` as one UUID fixed for the boot and `uuid` as fresh on every
  read. `flock(2)` exclusive nonblocking locks are attached to the open file description and release after every
  duplicate closes; `O_CLOEXEC` therefore prevents a final server image from retaining the supervisor lease.
  `openat`/`O_NOFOLLOW` binds names beneath an already validated directory descriptor. `renameat2` with
  `RENAME_NOREPLACE` makes publication atomic without destroying existing evidence. Sources:
  https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.12/admin-guide/sysctl/kernel.html,
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html,
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html, and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/renameat.2.html.
- The resulting split is intentional. Routine restart/stop remains direct `Child` authority and never consumes a PID
  record. Only a new supervisor, before IPC or child launch and while holding the singleton lease, may consume the
  durable record. Missing or proven-stale evidence signals nothing; malformed, unreadable, live-mismatched, or
  otherwise ambiguous evidence is preserved and makes `--service` exit nonzero. Availability never authorizes a
  best-effort signal.

### Implementation and current partial disposition

- `ServiceRuntime::acquire()` creates/opens `/run/rustdesk` without following links, requires the opened directory to
  be root-owned mode 0700, opens a root-owned single-link mode-0600 lease with `O_CLOEXEC`, and takes
  `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`. It reads a fresh kernel UUID as the supervisor generation. A second installed or manual
  supervisor stops before cleanup, IPC, or server launch.
- The service child receives the generation in its already-cleared bounded environment. After the actual
  privilege-drop/exec succeeds, registration captures PID, boot ID, `stat` start time, proc UID, executable
  device/inode, exact argv `[argv0, --server, --service-owned-server]`, and the one exact generation entry. Any failed
  capture or publication force-stops/reaps only the just-spawned direct child. The strict version-1 record is bounded
  to 1024 bytes and canonical decimal/UUID/order/role. Publication is a new no-follow temp inode, exact owner/mode/link
  validation, full write, file fsync, `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` (atomic `renameat` compatibility path only under
  the exclusive lease), then directory fsync. It never truncates or overwrites an existing record.
- Restart recovery opens a pidfd before inspecting a current-boot PID. Immediately before TERM it verifies boot ID,
  start time, UID, dereferenced executable device/inode, exact role, exact unique generation, and then reads start
  time again to catch an identity transition during inspection. Exit wait is bounded and poll-based on the pidfd. A
  still-live target is fully revalidated again immediately before pidfd-bound KILL and polled for a second bounded
  interval. Any mismatch or unavailable identity sends nothing further and preserves the record. Old-boot,
  pidfd-`ESRCH`, already-exited, and zombie records are reported and removed without a signal.
- On kernels returning `ENOSYS` for pidfd acquisition, the same full check runs immediately before every `kill(2)`
  and throughout both bounded waits. The source and runtime warning explicitly state that the final check-to-kill
  race cannot be removed on such a kernel; this is only a compatibility fallback. Other pidfd acquisition errors do
  not silently downgrade.
- Normal child shutdown still signals the retained unreaped `Child`. The record is removed only after reap and only
  if its strict decoded identity equals the retained record. The Linux service entry now returns `Result`; lease or
  recovery failure exits nonzero rather than looking like a clean stop. The systemd unit creates the same root-only
  runtime directory, preserves it over restart, permits the pidfd/atomic-publication syscalls, and retains whole-cgroup
  killing only as defense in depth.
- Focused pinned-container tests pass strict round-trip/malformed rejection, atomic no-replace mode-0600 publication,
  exact-match removal, corrupt-record preservation, role/generation exactness, and the prior real exec-chain
  parent-death test. The full main library compiles in the pinned dev-check container. Host-only compilation stopped
  in the external `x11` build script because this host has no `x11.pc`; no project source failed, and the repository's
  pinned container supplied the declared environment. `systemd-analyze verify res/rustdesk.service` returns zero
  (the only emitted messages concern unrelated host units/kernel IPv6 state).
- The parent lifecycle item remains open. Still required are release behavior runs for normal restart/stop, TERM
  wedge and escalation, real crash/restart, stale/corrupt/PID-reuse records, executable replace/delete, same argv with
  another executable/container inode, user/nonroot servers, and the installed privilege-drop chain; supported SysV,
  OpenRC, runit, and manual packaging/service integration; at least one Debian non-systemd run; the runtime old-kernel
  fallback exercise; and the concurrent Docker survival proof. No deployed service, package, unit, process, release,
  or prerelease operation was touched or authorized.

### Clean-commit closure for this slice

- The initial dirty-tree full verifier deliberately failed its clean-index/reset-transaction authority. It also

  normative requirements SHA-256 `91d9ec5358f705cc9648053bc93838be0ecfbe7f87ac08e5245cfc4b095138ea`.

## 2026-07-16 — Bounded direct-child graceful/forced termination slice (R-S11c-27c)

### Selection and proved lifecycle defect

- This invocation re-read the user attachment, `/tmp/ralph_loop_prompt.md`, normative R-S11/R-S11a/b/c, R-S16,
  R-S19, Appendix C #25–#29, the current hardening ledger, the direct-child and durable-recovery implementation, all
  stop/replacement call sites, and the verifier gates. It selected exactly one next coherent sub-slice of the open
  Linux service-child lifecycle item: bounded routine termination of the directly retained child plus fail-closed
  propagation before replacement. The installed/init-system and remaining hostile behavior matrix stays open.
- The pre-slice `terminate_child(mut child: OwnedServiceChild, ...)` consumed the only direct ownership before it had
  proof of exit. It bounded the SIGTERM phase for eight seconds, but after `Child::kill()` it called the blocking
  `Child::wait()` with no deadline. A wait failure was logged and discarded. `stop_server()` and every transition
  caller returned no result, and `should_start_server()` could continue to a replacement decision. Thus the routine
  lifecycle was not fully bounded and could detach the exact `Child`/record authority or proceed after uncertain
  reaping on a non-systemd supervisor.

### Primary research and authority decision

- Rust documents that `std::process::Child` has no `Drop` implementation that waits for or kills the process; losing
  the value is not cleanup. `try_wait()` is nonblocking and returns `None` while the child is still running, while a
  successful exit result waits/reaps the child. Source:
  https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Child.html.
- Linux `kill(2)` is a signal-send operation. A successful call is not an exit/reap observation, and even an existing
  target may already be a zombie that still requires `wait(2)`. `waitpid(..., WNOHANG)` returns zero when the selected
  child exists but has not changed to a waitable state. Sources:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/kill.2.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/waitpid.2.html.
- Linux also specifies that SIGKILL cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored, which makes it the correct bounded second
  stage after the graceful interval, but it still does not turn signal generation into synchronous reap proof.
  Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal.7.html.
- The resulting rule is strict: retain the exact `Option<OwnedServiceChild>` through TERM and KILL, use only bounded
  `try_wait()` loops to establish reap, remove the exact durable record only after reap, and release direct ownership
  only after record removal. If wait/reap remains uncertain, preserve the `Child` and record and return an error so
  the supervisor exits nonzero before any replacement can start. Parent exit then activates the already-proven
  PDEATHSIG containment, while the durable record remains available to the next supervisor.

### Implementation and focused proof

- `wait_child_exit()` is now fallible and reports whether the exact child was reaped inside its supplied deadline.
  `terminate_child_with_timeouts()` borrows `&mut Option<OwnedServiceChild>`, sends TERM and waits for the bounded
  graceful interval, then calls `kill()` on that same retained `Child` and waits for the bounded forced interval.
  There is no blocking `process.wait()` in production termination. Ownership is taken in exactly the two proven-reap
  branches and only after exact record removal. Wait errors, a failed KILL plus forced timeout, and a post-KILL
  unreaped deadline all retain the option/record and return a descriptive error.
- `stop_server()` and `should_start_server()` are fallible. All root/user branch transitions, restart decisions, and
  final shutdown paths use `?`; no uncertain stop reaches `start_server()`, and no uncertain final stop is logged as
  a clean service exit. Natural child-exit record removal is also propagated instead of silently logged.
- The new test execs the compiled test image as an exact retained worker in a private mode-0700 runtime directory,
  publishes its matching record, and proves the default TERM path. A second worker is sent exact-child SIGSTOP and
  `/proc/<pid>/stat` is polled until the stopped state is observed; TERM cannot complete while it is stopped, so the
  test requires the KILL/reap branch. Each path must finish inside three seconds with short injected timeouts, clear
  direct ownership, and remove the matching record. Panic cleanup retains an owned `Child` guard and kills/reaps only
  that exact test child.
- The host-only Cargo attempt stopped in the external `x11` build script because this host has no `x11.pc`; it did not
