## 2026-07-16 — Isolated supervisor-crash/restart recovery behavior (R-S11c-27d)

### Selection and proved assurance gap

- This invocation re-read the user attachment, `/tmp/ralph_loop_prompt.md`, `AGENTS.md`, normative R-S11b/R-S11c/
  R-S11i, R-S16, R-S19, Appendix C #25–#29, the complete current R-S11b/R-S11c ledger and open residual list, the
  Linux runtime-record/recovery implementation, the direct-child tests, and the verifier gate. It selected exactly
  one next coherent slice of the still-open Linux service-child parent: behavior proof for the combined supervisor
  crash/restart transition and the fail-closed hostile-record decision. Native Windows and exact-commit cold-artifact
  evidence remain separate open release work; accepted Appendix C #2b/mobile at-rest residuals were not confused
  with this release blocker.
- Before this slice, tests proved strict record encode/decode and no-replace publication, exact role/generation helper
  predicates, direct-child TERM/KILL/reap, and post-exec parent death as separate facts. No behavior test crossed the
  sequence `publish durable authority -> hold singleton lease -> supervisor crash -> exact child exit -> lease release
  -> fresh-process recovery`, and no live unrelated-process sentinel proved that a structurally valid but mismatched
  record caused neither signal nor record deletion. The production code already intended those rules, but source
  inspection and parser unit tests were not release-grade behavioral evidence for their composition.

### Primary research and authority decision

- Linux documents that `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` delivers the configured signal when the creating parent thread terminates;
  it is preserved across an ordinary `execve`, but cleared by effective-credential changes and by execution of a
  set-ID/capability-bearing binary. That supports the existing production order: credential drop, no-new-privileges,
  pre-exec arm and parent recheck, then final-image rearm. Source:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pr_set_pdeathsig.2const.html.
- `flock(2)` locks belong to an open file description and are released only when the last descriptor referring to
  that description closes. `O_CLOEXEC` on the supervisor lease therefore matters: the service child must not retain
  startup authority after exec, and a new supervisor may acquire the lease only after the old supervisor's descriptor
  is gone. Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html.
- `pidfd_send_signal(2)` targets the process referred to by the pidfd and is explicitly the race-free replacement for
  PID-only signaling when integer PIDs can be recycled. A pidfd can be monitored with `poll(2)` for process exit.
  Sources: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_send_signal.2.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html.
- `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 is the process start time after boot. `/proc/<pid>/exe` is a magic link to the executed
  file object and remains meaningful for an unlinked executable; dereferencing and comparing device/inode is the
  right identity evidence, while its textual pathname is not. Sources:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_stat.5.html,
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html, and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/symlink.7.html.
- The resulting authority model is unchanged but now behavior-pinned: only the exclusive-lease owner may consume the
  record; exited/absent exact evidence authorizes exact record removal but no signal; a live record authorizes TERM/
  KILL only after pidfd acquisition plus boot/start-time/UID/executable-object/argv/generation revalidation; malformed,
  mismatched, or unavailable live evidence authorizes neither signal nor removal. A positive exact match selects only
  the process object held by the pidfd.

### Implementation and isolated behavior proof

- The test-only `ServiceRuntime::for_test` now opens the same close-on-exec mode-0600 lock inode and calls the same
  `acquire_service_runtime_lease()` helper as production instead of cloning the runtime-directory descriptor and
  pretending it was a lease. The production `flock` block was moved into that shared helper, so the production syscall
  and error policy are unchanged and the lexical unsafe inventory remains exactly 796 blocks.
- The new `r_s11c27d_linux_service_child_crash_restart_recovery_is_exact` test uses only a unique current-UID
  mode-0700 directory under the test temporary root. A subprocess acquires the lease, launches a BusyBox `yes` applet
  whose kernel-visible argv is exactly `yes`, `--server`, `--service-owned-server`, supplies the exact generation,
  applies the production no-new-privileges/PDEATHSIG pre-exec hook, captures the production `/proc` record, and
  atomically publishes it. A second subprocess proves the live lease cannot be acquired. The parent retains a pidfd,
  kills the supervisor, observes the post-exec child exit, then launches a fresh subprocess which reacquires the
  released lease, calls production `recover_previous_child()`, and removes only the exited exact record.
- A separate exact-role live fixture supplies the noninterference proof. Structurally valid records are published with
  (1) a changed start time, modeling PID reuse; (2) a changed executable inode while argv remains byte-for-byte exact;
  and (3) a changed generation. Each production recovery attempt must fail for the named identity reason, preserve the
  exact record, and leave the live fixture observable through `Child::try_wait()`. A malformed-role record is written
  mode 0600, rejected before target admission, preserved byte-for-byte, and likewise leaves the fixture alive. Finally,
  the unmodified record must authorize pidfd-bound recovery of that exact live fixture and exact record removal.
- BusyBox was added only to `scripts/Dockerfile.devcheck` as the deterministic long-lived argv fixture; it is not a
  Rust dependency, application runtime dependency, Debian/Windows/Android/macOS payload input, or release artifact.
  The fixture uses a neutral `argv[0]=yes` because the production role predicate intentionally ignores argv zero and
  requires only exact arguments 1 and 2; its executable object, start time, UID and generation remain independently
  recorded and checked.
- `scripts/verify.sh` now runs this behavior test and binds the fixture presence, exact argv construction, live lease
  conflict, fresh recovery process, retained crashed-child pidfd, post-exec exit observation, production recovery call,
  all hostile-evidence cases, unrelated-process survival, and the ledger disposition. The combined pinned-container

## 2026-07-16 — Executable-object replacement/deletion recovery behavior (R-S11c-27e)

### Selection and conceptual privilege boundary

- This invocation re-read the user attachment, `/tmp/ralph_loop_prompt.md`, `AGENTS.md`, normative R-S11/R-S11a/
  R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19 and Appendix C #25-#29, the current R-S11b/R-S11c status, the entire open Linux
  lifecycle parent, and the production record/recovery/test paths. R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S11i source topology remains
  implemented but native Windows worktree validation and the clean cold release transaction remain open. The
  Linux lifecycle parent remains open after R-S11c-27a-d for installed lifecycle, forced PID reuse, executable
  object/package/container cases, privilege drop, non-root coexistence, pre-pidfd, non-systemd init, and Docker
  survival evidence.
- The selected single coherent next slice is the same-mount executable-object replacement/deletion case. The
  conceptual local-to-root hazard is wrong-object signaling during package replacement or pathname reuse: if a
  root supervisor treated an installed pathname or exact visible argv as ownership, it could signal a new unrelated
  process at the replacement inode, or refuse to stop the exact old service child after that child's executable name
  was removed. Existing production recovery compares dereferenced `/proc/<pid>/exe` device/inode and uses pidfds,
  which is the right model, but R-S11c-27d behavior only mutated an inode number in a record. It did not replace or
  unlink a live executable or retain a real same-path/same-role/different-inode sentinel.
- Authority decision: only the fresh exclusive-lease owner may consume the record; a signal requires one pidfd-
  selected live process plus matching boot ID, start time, UID, executable device/inode, exact role argv, and service
  generation. Rename/unlink must not revoke authority over the already-executing file object, while identical path,
  argv, generation, and file bytes at a different inode must not confer authority. Procfs link text is diagnostic
  only and is never compared as an identity.

### Primary research and design implication

- Linux `rename(2)` states that open references to the old path are unaffected and an existing destination is
  atomically replaced. Therefore package/path replacement creates a new name-to-inode binding without changing the
  old executing object. Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/rename.2.html.
- Linux `unlink(2)` removes a filesystem name while an open/referenced file remains in existence until the final
  reference closes. Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/unlink.2.html.
- `/proc/<pid>/exe` can be dereferenced to open the executed object and appends ` (deleted)` to its textual pathname
  after unlink. Procfs magic links are direct references to the kernel file handle and can reach unlinked files;
  they are not ordinary pathname-expansion authority. Sources:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/symlink.7.html.
- `pidfd_send_signal(2)` names the process referred to by the pidfd and avoids the recycled-integer-PID race; the
  pidfd is a stable process reference, not evidence that the process has the expected role. Full identity must still
  be revalidated before its use. Sources: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_send_signal.2.html.

### Implementation and current evidence

- The test-only exact-role launcher now accepts a test-owned executable path; its ordinary wrapper still selects the
  fixed BusyBox dev-check fixture. This surface exists only inside the `#[cfg(test)]` module. Production
  `try_start_server_` remains hardwired to `/proc/self/exe`, and no production caller-selectable path or fallback was
  added.
- `r_s11c27e_linux_service_child_executable_object_recovery_is_exact` creates a unique current-UID mode-0700
  runtime and two separate mode-0700 copies of BusyBox. It launches the first object with exact service argv and
  generation, captures its real production record, and atomically renames the second inode over its pathname while
  it remains live. The old process's dereferenced procfs executable metadata must still equal the original record,
  while its diagnostic procfs link ends in ` (deleted)`.
- The replacement inode is launched from that same pathname with identical argv and generation. A record carrying
  the replacement PID/start time/UID/generation but the original object's real device/inode must fail production
  recovery for executable-identity mismatch, remain exactly present, and leave both processes alive. The exact old
  record must then recover only the old object while the replacement survives.
- A third exact-role object is recorded and directly unlinked. Dereferenced procfs metadata must retain its recorded
  device/inode; exact production recovery must terminate it and remove its record while the replacement sentinel
  remains alive. Every process is created and retained by this test; cleanup has no name/PID-scan authority.
- The focused pinned Rust 1.75 dev-check test passed. `scripts/verify.sh` now has a dedicated R-S11c-27e gate binding
  atomic replacement, direct unlink, the real cross-object negative, named rejection, exact record preservation,
  sentinel survival at each decision, both exact positive recoveries, and the narrowed ledger. The final dirty-tree
  and exact clean-commit verification, full diff review, commit, push, and live-remote proof are recorded below.

### Residual and safety boundary

- This proves same-mount private-runtime executable-object semantics. It does not prove an installed package update,
  cross-mount replacement, mount-namespace alias, identical in-container pathname backed by another inode, forced
  PID reuse, the real RustDesk privilege-drop/final-image chain, or any init/package integration. Those cases remain
  open and must not inherit this slice's disposition.
- No production service path, `/run/rustdesk`, sudo/polkit action, service IPC, pre-existing PID, network listener,
  release build, release, or prerelease is used. No deployed RustDesk service was inspected or disturbed.

## 2026-07-16 — Actual-binary manual supervisor lifecycle behavior (R-S11c-27f)

### Selection, baseline defect, and conceptual privilege boundary

- This invocation re-read the user attachment, `/tmp/ralph_loop_prompt.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the normative R-S11/
  R-S11a/R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19 requirements and Appendix C #25-#29, the current hardening ledger, and the
  production Linux supervisor, owned-child, signal, record, and shutdown paths. R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S11i source
  topology remains implemented, while native Windows worktree validation and the clean cold release transaction
  remain open. The wider Linux lifecycle parent also remains open after R-S11c-27a-e.
- The selected single coherent slice is the real RustDesk binary under a manual/non-systemd root supervisor: two
  normal stop/start generations, one stopped-child bounded escalation, and simultaneous survival of a separately
  launched non-root portable `--server` sentinel. Unlike the preceding unit-level recovery cases, this exercises
  the supervisor loop, its exact child record, the real server child, signal delivery, wait/reap behavior, and the
  child's typed parked IPC through the compiled `target/debug/rustdesk` executable.
- Baseline actual-binary execution exposed a production defect. `SIGTERM` used the default terminating disposition,
  so the privileged supervisor exited with status 143 before its normal exact-child termination/reap and record
  cleanup path ran. The child happened to die because the existing `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)` relationship fired,
  but that is an emergency parent-death containment mechanism, not graceful lifecycle ownership. Reporting such a
  transition as a graceful stop could leave stale authority evidence and could conceal skipped cleanup.
- Authority decision: only the live manual supervisor owns the exact child it launched and registered. A normal
  supervisor stop must request that exact child to stop, wait/reap it, remove the exact record, and exit zero. If
  that same retained child is kernel-stopped and cannot drain, the supervisor must wait for the existing bounded
  interval and then signal/reap that exact retained child. A new supervisor produces a distinct generation. A
  separately launched non-root portable `--server` has no service-owned role marker or generation and must survive
  every service lifecycle transition. No PID/name scan or path-only match grants signal authority.

### Primary research and implementation implication

- Linux signal dispositions are process-wide; caught dispositions reset to default across `exec`, while `SIGKILL`
  and `SIGSTOP` cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored. The default action for `SIGTERM` is termination. Source:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal.7.html.
- The pinned `ctrlc` 3.4.4 crate documents that its `termination` feature extends the handler from `SIGINT` to
  `SIGTERM` and `SIGHUP` on Unix. Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ctrlc/3.4.4. Enabling that feature preserves the
  already-audited handler model instead of adding a second lexical unsafe signal implementation.
- `wait(2)`/`waitpid(2)` provide the parent operation that observes child state and releases the resources held for
  a terminated child. Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/waitpid.2.html. The existing retained
  `std::process::Child` remains the supervisor's reap authority.
- `pidfd_open(2)` and `pidfd_send_signal(2)` provide race-resistant process references for the external harness's
  stop/control operations. The pidfd names the process, while the harness separately proves the boot ID, start
  time, UID, executable device/inode, argv role, parent, and generation before using it. Sources:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_send_signal.2.html.
- `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` requests a signal when the creating parent dies. It remains useful fail-closed containment but
  does not replace an orderly TERM/request, bounded escalation, wait/reap, and exact-record cleanup sequence.
  Source: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html.

### Implementation and actual-binary runtime evidence

- `ctrlc` now enables its `termination` feature. `start_os_service` installs the repository's sole production
  `ctrlc::set_handler` before acquiring the service runtime; registration failure propagates instead of printing
  and continuing without lifecycle control. The handler only clears an `AtomicBool`, allowing the existing
  supervisor loop to reach its ordinary exact-child stop/reap path. No signal handler performs allocation, IPC,
  locking, process creation, record mutation, or direct exit.
- The competing child-side `ctrlc::set_handler` was removed. Its existing key-release operation now runs inside
  `finish_graceful_shutdown`, after local IPC shutdown and before the established successful-exit log and exit.
  This leaves the real server child's Tokio signal/drain path as its shutdown authority while preserving input
  cleanup. Since caught signal dispositions reset on `exec`, the service child does not inherit the supervisor's
  handler.
- `scripts/smoke-service-loginctl.sh` is a strict test-only fixture for one exact active root X11 seat, allowing the
  supervisor to create its real service-owned child in a disposable, networkless container. Unknown queries fail
  closed. No production option or timing knob was added.
- `scripts/smoke-service-lifecycle.sh` launches the compiled actual binary and strictly validates the mode-0600
  record, boot/start/executable/UID/generation identity, exact service-owned argv, parent relationship,
  no-new-privileges state, and typed parked IPC. Two supervisor generations stop gracefully: their exact children
  exit zero and are reaped, their records disappear, the supervisors log `Exit` and exit zero, and their child IDs
  and generations differ.
- A third exact child is stopped with `SIGSTOP` through its validated pidfd. `SIGTERM` is then sent to its validated
  supervisor pidfd. The production supervisor waits through its existing bound, reports forced termination, sends
  `SIGKILL` to and reaps that same retained child, removes the exact record, and exits zero. The final measured
  escalation interval was 8.156 seconds, within the harness's 7.5-to-20-second acceptance window.
- Throughout all three transitions, a copied binary launched as UID 4000 with supplementary groups and capabilities
  removed and no-new-privileges set runs ordinary portable `--server` without the service-owned marker. Its typed
  IPC remains responsive and its exact pidfd remains live after every graceful and forced service transition.
- The first final-shape run also exposed an evidence defect: the shared readiness helper used `return 1` in `fail()`,
  which can continue unexpectedly when a Bash function is evaluated in a conditional context. The helper now
  terminates with `exit 1`, the lifecycle harness waits for parked-log quiescence before pinning the log, the helper
  self-test passes, and the final lifecycle run produced only coherent PASS evidence:
  `SERVICE_LIFECYCLE_GRACEFUL`, `SERVICE_LIFECYCLE_RESTART`, `SERVICE_LIFECYCLE_FORCED`, and
  `PORTABLE_NONINTERFERENCE`.

### Residual and safety boundary

- This closes only actual-binary manual/non-systemd behavior in the isolated dev-check container. It does not prove
  an installed or package-managed RustDesk service, systemd/SysV/OpenRC/runit/Debian integration, installed-service
  crash/restart behavior, pre-pidfd behavior, forced PID reuse, broader malformed-record cases, the real non-root
  desktop privilege-drop/final-image chain, cross-mount or namespace/container aliasing, or independent Docker

### Pinned LLVM resource-producer research and bounded native proof

- LLVM 15.0.6 is already a byte-pinned, authenticated Windows build input for libclang; no dependency or offline
  closure expansion is needed. The official `llvmorg-15.0.6` `llvm-rc` source describes the tool as a
  platform-independent `rc.exe` replacement. Its parser stores every `VersionInfoBlock` statement in a
  `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<VersionInfoStmt>>`; `ResourceFileWriter::writeVersionInfoBlock` iterates that vector
  directly and serializes each value in insertion order. The official `tag-versioninfo.test` checks the exact emitted
  byte stream, while the icon/cursor and user-resource tests cover icon groups and file-backed numeric resources.
  The pinned Linux LLVM archive also contains `llvm-rc` and `llvm-readobj`. Two local invocations with preprocessing
  disabled and explicit UTF-8 code page produced byte-identical complete VERSIONINFO/icon/manifest resources,
  102,208 bytes with SHA-256 `6549f6a321c66597ed09b841698043c6851f3b691a9152a0baed3e55ffc8155f`.
- The first fresh networkless Windows probe used exact UUID `b9001ad2-032e-4c06-bf0d-287c8b059c38`, source-ISO
  SHA-256 `109a6c0c31644c88a19248cb41e03d99401322b9a62ddd304d8da7f766eeee0d`, and domain-XML SHA-256
  `1134c6a22dd37ed28def999243d011dc57969242c936ead0fbca571c2f5beef8`. Its XML had no network interface.
  Sixty-four fresh `C:\Program Files\LLVM\bin\llvm-rc.exe` processes emitted one exact 102,208-byte result, with the
  same `6549f6...155f` SHA-256 as the independently pinned Linux binary. The installed producer is product/file
  version `15.0.6` and SHA-256 `f1c4e01ae6214be7e1326e6290ee96b3cd7d36e690f400a16b5e33ad3aa36f29`.
  This run failed only because the diagnostic expected LLVM to label numeric type 24 as generic `ID 24`; its actual,
  correct `llvm-readobj` label is `MANIFEST (ID 24)`.
- Follow-on diagnostics removed two probe-only defects rather than weakening the producer test. UUID
  `93bda9e9-ca42-4011-884e-ae0592bd2230` was operator-interrupted while its hidden scheduled task was still running
  and is non-authoritative. A staged-boot approach then eliminated the golden logon launcher's OUTPUT-mount race.

### Linux executable-object test-fixture publication race found during Windows preflight

- The fourth broad staged verifier preflight stopped at
  `r_s11c27e_linux_service_child_executable_object_recovery_is_exact`. The preceding three broad runs passed the
  same test, but a dedicated unchanged-fixture stress run reproduced the failure on iteration 16 of 75. This time
  the third copied BusyBox child failed at `service_child_record_for_process`: the process remained live, but its
  first `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` sample was empty and therefore correctly failed the exact
  `--server --service-owned-server` predicate. The earlier broad failure occurred at the second copied child, so the
  symptom is not tied to rename or unlink behavior.
- The cause is confined to the synthetic fixture's launch/readiness boundary. When `bind_to_parent` is false, the
  fixture has no `pre_exec` closure. The fork's pinned Rust 1.75 standard-library source therefore permits its Linux
  GNU `posix_spawn` fast path and returns the resulting `Process` directly after `posix_spawnp`. By contrast, the
  real Linux service launch always calls `configure_service_child_pre_exec`; Rust 1.75 explicitly rejects the
  `posix_spawn` path when a closure is present and its fork/exec path waits for the close-on-exec error socket to
  close. Forty repeated crash/restart tests exercising the parent-bound production-shaped fixture passed before
  repair. A separate 1,000-iteration raw probe reproduced the precise boundary on its second spawn: the live
  child's first `cmdline` read returned zero bytes, then the next 10-microsecond-delayed read and all later reads
  returned exact `yes\0--server\0--service-owned-server\0`. Linux's `proc_pid_cmdline(5)` also documents that the
  file reflects the process's argv memory and is not an immutable kernel launch credential.
- The repair does not alter `service_child_record_for_process`, `inspect_service_child_identity`, recovery, or any
  production signal decision. The copied-BusyBox helper now performs a bounded five-second readiness wait for both
  the exact role argv and the exact single generation environment value, checks `Child::try_wait` on every failed
  observation, and sleeps only one millisecond between predicate checks. Exit, timeout, wrong argv, and wrong or
  duplicated generation all remain hard test failures. This establishes the synthetic subject before the
  executable replacement/deletion test begins rather than treating a transient empty proc sample as authority.
  After repair, the executable-object test passed 200 consecutive iterations and the parent-death/crash-restart
  test passed 40 consecutive iterations in the pinned `rd-devcheck` container with `--offline --locked`.

### Shared ordered Windows resource producer and Retry 13 preflight

- Production now has one shared `res/windows_resource.rs` producer included by both the root and portable build
  scripts. It parses only the canonical three-component Cargo package version, emits the fixed six version strings
  in one order together with Translation, icon, and manifest, invokes only the explicitly supplied
  `RUSTDESK_LLVM_RC` with `-no-preprocess -C65001`, captures compiler diagnostics, proves the RC input was not
  modified, and admits only a nonempty ordinary-file `.res` output before exposing it to the linker. The root and
  portable direct `winres` build-dependency edges and portable `[package.metadata.winres]` are removed; the
  transitive `winres 0.1.12` package remains because another graph consumer still requires it.
- The Windows guest binds `C:\Program Files\LLVM\bin\llvm-rc.exe` to the existing LLVM 15.0.6 SHA-256 and exact
  product/file version before either Cargo invocation. It uses the pinned `llvm-readobj` to require VERSIONINFO,
  icon, group-icon, and manifest resources; parses the compiled UTF-16 resource to require the exact six-key order
  and values; requires root/portable compiled-resource byte equality; and checks all six linked values in both the
  root `target\release\librustdesk.dll` and final setup executable. The installer source is the exact canonical MSI
  output. The PE and MSI canonicalizers now use Windows-compatible open descriptor semantics and prove their actual
  native input types; the MSI is rechecked exactly on the host. The PowerShell 5.1 COM path, strict CRLF progress
  parser, stable guest build root, networkless WiX extraction, complete offline namespace manifest, and worktree
  source scan were repaired and mutation-gated as described in the earlier diagnostic sections.
- Local preflight is green: `verify-windows-harness.py --self-test` passed 136 source mutations and four bounded
  behavioral suites; dependency inventory self-tests/text output pass with 910 Cargo packages, 244 tracked Rust
  files, and 796 lexical unsafe blocks; locked offline Cargo metadata passes; and the staged diff check passes. The
  full staged `scripts/verify.sh` run completed every later compile, behavioral, Linux lifecycle, source, version,
  canonicalization, reproducibility, and port-forward gate. Its sole failure was a stale self-test mutation that
  still searched for the deleted filesystem `find` build-script scan; log SHA-256 is
  `f47c4a052720870dc0e36ddd9ba2d49a536162adfdcaeed317d5b23495ce55b7`. The fixture now mutates the authoritative
  indexed `git ls-files` scan and reaches the clean-release transaction test. That transaction correctly refuses
  the current staged state with exact reason `index differs from HEAD`; it remains unchanged and must pass after the
  slice is committed.
- Before Retry 13, the session libvirt domain list was empty, the public output path was absent, and 428 GiB was
  available. The retained failed Retry 12 root was removed only after its exact directory identity
  `66306:104104833` was rechecked, its evidence and log hashes had been recorded above, and the live domain list was
  empty. The root-owned attached offline ISO was unlinked first, permissions were made owner-removable, and absence
  of the private run root was verified. This cleanup changes no Retry 12 conclusion or current ledger status.

### R-S11c-27g design audit — actual-binary manual supervisor crash/restart

- The next bounded slice is the still-open real-binary supervisor crash/restart case, not the installed-package or
  final cold-release matrix. The production authority path is `ServiceRuntime::acquire()` ->
  `recover_previous_child()` -> service loop. It therefore takes the root-only runtime directory and nonblocking
  exclusive lease before recovery, consumes any prior durable record before `stop_subprocess()` or a replacement
  child launch, and never uses PID/name scans for a service-owned `--server`.
- `try_start_server_()` retains the exact `Child`, launches `/proc/self/exe` with the exact service role and fresh
  generation, and makes the lease descriptor close-on-exec. The child arms `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)` after any
  optional credential change in `pre_exec`, checks the expected PPID immediately, and the final RustDesk image
  re-arms/rechecks before server startup. The Linux man-pages contract confirms that the signal is delivered when
  the creating parent thread dies, that it is cleared on effective/filesystem UID or GID changes and privileged
  exec, and otherwise survives exec. This justifies testing abrupt death of the actual supervisor rather than
  substituting a graceful signal: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html
- The exclusive `flock` belongs to the open file description and is released only when all duplicate descriptors
  close. Because the production lease fd has `O_CLOEXEC`, the ready service child does not retain it after exec; an
  abrupt supervisor exit must therefore release the lease for a new supervisor. Contract:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html
- `pidfd_open()` returns a close-on-exec descriptor for one task, returns `ESRCH` when the PID is absent, and a
  pidfd becomes poll-readable when the process exits/becomes a zombie. `pidfd_send_signal()` targets the process
  referred to by that stable descriptor rather than a recyclable numeric PID. These contracts support exact
  harness signals and bounded exit observation without weakening the production identity checks:
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html and
  https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_send_signal.2.html
- Planned behavior proof: launch the real debug `rustdesk --service`; validate its strict durable record and exact
  parked child; kill only the retained supervisor identity through a pidfd; observe the exact child cease running
  via parent-death binding while the byte-identical root-owned record remains; verify the unrelated UID-4000
  portable server is still live; launch a fresh real supervisor while that record exists; require production
  recovery to classify the old PID absent/exited without signaling, remove only that record, publish a different
  child/generation, and then complete a normal exact-child shutdown. This is partial R-S11c-27 evidence only.
- The unchanged baseline lifecycle stage passed both graceful generations, stopped-child escalation in 8.130
  seconds, and portable noninterference. The first extended run reached the expected supervisor SIGKILL and child
  pidfd exit but failed one harness-only assertion that the replacement durable record's device/inode tuple must
  differ. An `-x` trace proved production had removed the old record, published different bytes/generation, and the
  filesystem immediately reused the old inode number. Inode recycling after unlink is valid and a path inode number
  is not a monotonic generation. The invalid post-recovery inequality was removed; the test still requires the old
  record's complete metadata tuple and SHA-256 to remain unchanged after the crash and before the fresh supervisor,
  then requires a different strict record hash plus distinct child/start/generation after production recovery.
- The corrected actual-binary stage passed. The exact supervisor exited with signal status 137, its exact child pidfd
  reported exit after 3 ms, the byte-identical crash record remained until the next supervisor consumed it, the new
  generation reached typed parked IPC and then shut down gracefully, and the UID-4000 portable server survived every
  crash/recovery transition. No Rust production code, dependency, syscall, or unsafe inventory changed.
- The complete default `scripts/smoke-server.sh` integration then passed under the host historical-selector monitor.
  Its integrated lifecycle observation used prior generation `b1a5f074-744b-4204-8cb8-1204752ff107`, recovered
  generation `cc9540f3-0af1-4f23-a50d-569f815c3b91`, a 1 ms exact-child pidfd exit observation, 8.567-second

### R-S11c-27h design/runtime audit — real non-root active-seat credential drop and descriptor exec

- The selected bounded slice is the still-open actual-binary non-root active-desktop credential-drop/exec branch.
  It is not an installed package transaction or the final cold-release matrix. The trusted absolute `loginctl`
  fixture can switch one X11 seat0 from root to a real passwd-backed `rdseat` identity (UID/GID 4001 with
  supplementary GID 4101), while the existing portable server remains isolated at UID 4000. Production therefore
  takes `Desktop::refresh()` -> `ServiceChildCredentials::resolve()` -> `try_start_server_(Some(desktop))` and the
  real pre-exec credential sequence; no production test knob or substitute child executable is used.
- Primary Linux contracts used to define the proof:
  - `setgroups(2)` replaces the supplementary group list, and that list is preserved across exec:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/setgroups.2.html
  - `setresgid(2)`/`setresuid(2)` set real, effective, and saved IDs; failures must be checked even for UID 0:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/setresuid.2.html
  - when all real/effective/saved UIDs transition from zero to nonzero, Linux clears permitted, effective, and
    ambient capabilities; the bounding set is not part of that clearing rule and must not be falsely asserted zero:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html
  - `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` is irreversible, survives exec, and makes set-ID bits and file capabilities unable to
    grant exec-time privilege: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS.2const.html
  - `/proc/<pid>/exe` dereference is governed by a `PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS` check, and changing effective IDs can
    reset dumpability/proc ownership: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid.5.html
  - `/proc/self/fd/N` names an open descriptor, while close-on-exec descriptors are closed on successful exec;
    descriptor-exec interfaces naturally use close-on-exec to avoid a final-image leak:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_fd.5.html,
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html, and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/fexecve.3.html
- The unmodified runtime baseline exposed a production failure. `Command::spawn()` invokes the registered
  `pre_exec` closure before its final `execve`; after the raw UID transition, the child could not dereference the
  configured `/proc/self/exe` and each attempt failed `Permission denied (os error 13)`. This proved the previously
  documented active-seat launch claim had never crossed the real credential boundary in this harness.
- A first descriptor experiment proved that a non-close-on-exec inherited executable fd can be executed as UID
  4001, while the same `/proc/self/fd/N` path returns `EACCES` if N remains `FD_CLOEXEC`. Production now opens its
  exact `/proc/self/exe` object while privileged and verifies `FD_CLOEXEC` in the multithreaded parent. Only the
  already-forked child clears that flag through raw `fcntl(F_SETFD, 0)` after the credential drop, then execs
  `/proc/self/fd/N`. A dedicated bounded environment binding tells the final service-owned image which descriptor
  it must parse and immediately close. The root path continues to use `/proc/self/exe`. This avoids a parent-wide
  inheritable-descriptor interval, stays on the same executable object across pathname replacement, and fails closed
  on missing/invalid fd state or close failure.
- After descriptor exec succeeded, registration correctly refused to weaken executable identity when Docker's
  default root capability set could not dereference the non-root child's `/proc/<pid>/exe`. The deployed systemd
  inverse `CapabilityBoundingSet` already retains `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`; an ordinary host-root SysV/manual supervisor also
  has that authority. The isolated lifecycle now requests exactly `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE`, and the unit documents why
  it must not be removed. The subsequent same-UID typed IPC probe was also moved under a capability-free UID/GID/group

### R-S11c-27i design/runtime audit — actual-binary hostile record rejection

- The next bounded release-blocking slice is real-supervisor behavior for malformed and live-but-ambiguous durable
  service-child records. It does not claim actual forced numeric-PID reuse, installed package/service-manager
  lifecycle behavior, pre-pidfd runtime behavior, or cross-namespace identity.
- Current production authority was traced before editing. `ServiceRuntime::read_record()` opens the fixed name
  relative to the already-validated root-owned mode-0700 runtime directory with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK`,
  then requires a root-owned, mode-0600, single-linked regular file and a nonzero at-most-1024-byte body. The decoder
  requires the exact ordered version/pid/start/boot/device/inode/uid/generation/role schema, canonical decimal and
  UUID spellings, and no trailing field. `recover_previous_child()` runs before helper cleanup or IPC-listener
  startup. On a current-boot live PID, the pidfd path checks exit state and then revalidates start time, UID,
  executable device/inode, exact three-argument service role, unique generation environment binding, and a final
  unchanged start time before either signal. Any malformed record or live mismatch returns an error, leaves the
  record in place, and makes the actual `--service` process exit nonzero; only proved stale boot/absent/exited records
  are removed without signaling.
- Primary Linux contracts used for the test model:
  - `openat(2)` binds a relative lookup to an opened directory; `O_NOFOLLOW` rejects a final symlink with `ELOOP`,
    and `O_NONBLOCK` permits safe inspection before the explicit regular-file check:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/openat.2.html
  - `pidfd_open(2)` returns a close-on-exec descriptor for the task referenced by the PID, is the preferred way to
    obtain a pidfd for an existing task, and yields a pollable exit reference:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html
  - `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 is start time since boot in clock ticks. It is a necessary PID-reuse discriminator,
    but a record with a deliberately altered value is only an ambiguity simulation, not proof of forced kernel PID
    reuse: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_stat.5.html
  - dereferencing `/proc/<pid>/exe` opens the executed object and is ptrace-credential gated; an unlinked executable
    retains object identity even though link text gains ` (deleted)`:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html
  - `RENAME_NOREPLACE` refuses to overwrite an existing destination, while ordinary rename leaves already-open file
    descriptors referring to their original object: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/rename.2.html
- Intended runtime proof: while the unrelated real RustDesk portable server remains alive as UID 4000, create a
  second capability-free UID-4000 sentinel with the exact service-role argv and a controlled generation but a
  different executable. Inject one root-owned record case at a time and invoke the actual RustDesk `--service`
  image. Cover malformed canonical bytes, untrusted file mode, changed start time, changed executable identity,
  changed UID, changed generation, and a record targeting the exact RustDesk executable but its portable two-argument
  role. Every case must produce status 1, an explicit fail-closed diagnostic, byte-for-byte and metadata-identical
  record preservation, no temporary record, and continued exact sentinel liveness. The harness removes only its
  already-hash-verified fixture record between cases. Actual forced PID reuse remains separately open.
- The implemented lifecycle harness now creates records through a retained `/run/rustdesk` directory descriptor with
  `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, snapshots device/inode/owner/mode/link-count/size/mtime/ctime plus SHA-256, runs the actual
  root-owned installed-mode `rustdesk --service`, requires exact status 1 plus the core fail-closed diagnostic and a
  case-specific parser/identity reason, rechecks unchanged metadata and bytes, rejects any `.tmp` record, and only

### R-S11c-27j design/runtime audit — concurrent separate-Docker survival

- The next bounded release-blocking slice is concurrent separate-Docker noninterference for the manual service
  lifecycle harness. It does not claim installed package/service-manager behavior, actual forced numeric-PID reuse,
  pre-pidfd runtime behavior, or cross-mount/container namespace identity.
- Primary contracts used for the test model:
  - Linux PID namespaces isolate PID number spaces. Processes in sibling PID namespaces are not visible to each
    other, and PID-based syscalls operate only on PIDs visible in the caller's namespace:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/pid_namespaces.7.html
  - Docker `--pid` controls container PID namespace sharing. The default is a private container PID namespace;
    `--pid=host` or `--pid=container:<id>` would deliberately broaden visibility and is therefore forbidden for
    this sibling proof:
    https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#pid-settings---pid
- Intended authority model: the lifecycle container remains the existing networkless manual-service fixture with
  only the procfs authority it already needs for exact-child inspection. The sibling container is started separately,
  with no host or joined PID namespace, `--network none`, a read-only repository bind, a private writable `/sibling`
  control bind, and no Docker socket. The sibling is not a child of the RustDesk service supervisor and is drained
  only by the smoke harness after the lifecycle stage has completed.
- Implemented source behavior:
  - `scripts/smoke-server-stage.sh` now contains a `sibling-docker-server` mounted stage. It uses the existing
    neutral launcher to start the exact built RustDesk executable, proves `SMOKE_SERVER_IDENTITY_OK`, waits until the
    no-password server is parked, emits `SIBLING_DOCKER_READY pid=<pid> start=<start>`, and holds the same PID/start
    identity with `smoke-ready.sh --hold-running` until an exact private `stop` control file appears. On controlled
    drain it emits `SIBLING_DOCKER_SURVIVED=pass pid=<pid> start=<start>`.
  - `scripts/smoke-server.sh` now creates a private mode-0700 sibling control directory, runs
    `docker run -d --name "$SIBLING_NAME" --network none` with no `--pid`, waits for the ready file, runs the
    existing manual lifecycle stage, then requires the sibling container still to be running before writing the stop
    control file. It captures the sibling output in the private host-guard workspace rather than a command
    substitution so that container/root cleanup state is updated in the parent shell. It then removes the exact
    sibling container and emits `SIBLING_DOCKER_NONINTERFERENCE=pass cid=<cid>`.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` adds R-S11c-27j structural gates for the sibling dispatch, networkless Docker run,
    read-only source bind, private control bind, absence of any sibling `--pid`, parent-shell stop ordering, runtime
    stage status, survivor markers, and the hardening ledger entry.
  - `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` raises the mounted-stage count to 18, requires the sibling Docker block
    and mounted stage, rejects host/container PID namespace sharing, rejects missing network isolation, rejects loss
    of the survivor marker, and rejects the earlier command-substitution cleanup shape.

### R-S11c-27k design/runtime audit — forced pre-pidfd compatibility recovery

- The next bounded release-blocking slice is runtime exercise of the pre-pidfd recovery compatibility branch. It
  does not claim an actually old kernel, installed package/service-manager behavior, actual forced numeric-PID reuse,
  or cross-mount/container namespace identity.
- Primary contracts used for the authority model:
  - `pidfd_open(2)` creates a file descriptor referring to a process and is the preferred stable process reference;
    unsupported kernels report `ENOSYS`: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html
  - `pidfd_send_signal(2)` signals the process referred to by the pidfd, avoiding the separate numeric-PID lookup:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_send_signal.2.html
  - `kill(2)` accepts a numeric PID, so a userspace identity check followed by `kill` retains an irreducible final
    check-to-signal race: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/kill.2.html
- Intended authority model: pidfd remains the ordinary and stronger recovery mechanism. Only an unsupported
  `pidfd_open` result may select the compatibility branch. That branch may signal only after validating the complete
  durable child record and revalidating PID/start time/boot/executable device+inode/UID/generation/service role
  immediately before every numeric-PID signal, with identity-revalidating bounded waits. It must keep the residual
  race explicit and may never sweep by process name/path or trust a PID alone.
- Existing production path proved before editing:
  - `ServiceRuntime::recover_previous_child` reads the strict record, rejects a boot mismatch without signaling, and
    dispatches `PidFdOpen::Available` to pidfd recovery, `Unsupported` to
    `recover_previous_child_without_pidfd`, and `Absent` to stale-record removal.
  - `recover_previous_child_without_pidfd` performs the initial full identity match, emits the residual-race warning,
    sends `SIGTERM` only through `send_revalidated_service_child_pid_signal`, waits through
    `wait_revalidated_service_child_pid_exit`, and repeats the same signal/wait discipline for bounded `SIGKILL`.
  - `send_revalidated_service_child_pid_signal` calls
    `require_service_child_identity_match(record, "pre-pidfd kill fallback")` immediately before `kill(2)`.
  The security behavior was already present; the current pidfd-capable kernel made the branch unreachable in runtime
  evidence.
- Implemented source behavior:
  - `src/platform/linux.rs` adds `RD_SERVICE_SMOKE_FORCE_PRE_PIDFD`, compiled and read only under
    `debug_assertions`. The non-debug helper arm returns unconditional `false`. When selected, the ordinary pidfd-open
    helper logs the smoke diagnostic and returns the same `PidFdOpen::Unsupported` state as an unsupported kernel; it
    does not introduce a signal path or change any identity predicate.
  - `scripts/smoke-service-lifecycle.sh` starts a real RustDesk service-role child independently with neutral argv,
    generation, and harness-parent binding. It proves the live PID/start time, exact argv, executable device+inode,
    all four UID fields, generation, and parent before writing the canonical root-owned mode-0600 record. A real
    `rustdesk --service` process then receives the debug-only force, must enter the ordinary compatibility branch,
    terminate the exact prior child gracefully, and recover a fresh PID/start-time and generation. The fixture also
    requires the forced-unsupported diagnostic, residual-race diagnostic, and prior child's graceful-shutdown marker.
  - `scripts/smoke-server.sh` retains the R-S11c-27k stage status and requires the exact aggregate marker.
  - `scripts/verify.sh` and `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` bind the exact debug-only declaration, release-closed
    helper body, helper call and forced `Unsupported` return, existing signal and wait revalidation, residual-race
    warning, fixture identity proof, runtime force, result marker, ordering, stage status, and hardening-ledger entry.
    The mutation suite rejects independent removal of the critical contracts.

### R-S11c-27l design/runtime audit — installed Debian SysV lifecycle

- The next bounded release-blocking slice is the package-owned SysV adapter plus the mandatory Debian-without-systemd
  lifecycle run. It does not claim OpenRC/runit/manual integration, final-release `.deb` artifact behavior, installed
  systemd behavior, installed supervisor crash recovery over a non-root child, actual forced numeric-PID reuse, or
  cross-mount/container namespace identity.
- Existing package path proved before editing:
  - `build.py` staged only `usr/share/rustdesk/files/systemd/rustdesk.service`; the exact package inventory contained
    no `/etc/init.d/rustdesk`.
  - `res/DEBIAN/postinst` unconditionally ran `/bin/systemctl --system daemon-reload` and
    `deb-systemd-invoke start`; `preinst`/`prerm` likewise had no non-systemd stop path.
  - `res/rustdesk.service` declared `PIDFile=/run/rustdesk.pid`, but the Linux `--service` supervisor did not create
    that file. The only generic `write_pid` call was the IPC endpoint writer, whose path derives from
    `Config::ipc_path(postfix)` under `/tmp/RustDesk-...`, not `/run/rustdesk.pid`.
  - Debian non-systemd therefore had neither package persistence nor an exact supervisor identity it could stop. The
    systemd-only wording in R-R2a contradicted the later binding lifecycle requirement for SysV/OpenRC/runit/manual.
- Primary Debian contracts used for the design:
  - Debian Policy requires packages to register init scripts with `update-rc.d` and to use `invoke-rc.d` from
    maintainer scripts rather than calling `/etc/init.d/...` directly:
    https://www.debian.org/doc/debian-policy/
  - `invoke-rc.d` is the policy-aware maintainer-script interface to init systems:
    https://manpages.debian.org/bookworm/init-system-helpers/invoke-rc.d.8.en.html
  - `deb-systemd-invoke` is specifically a systemd-unit helper and is not a generic non-systemd service authority:
    https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/init-system-helpers/deb-systemd-invoke.1p.en.html
  - `update-rc.d` consumes LSB init metadata and owns SysV runlevel link registration:
    https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/init-system-helpers/update-rc.d.8.en.html
  - `start-stop-daemon` warns that a stale PID file alone can select an unintended process, refuses unsafe
    unprivileged/world-writable PID-file authority, combines match predicates, supports an init-owned PID file, and
    provides bounded TERM/KILL retry plus PID-file removal:
    https://manpages.debian.org/bookworm/dpkg/start-stop-daemon.8.en.html
  - Debian's generic `init-d-script` performs a second executable-only stop pass after the PID-file pass. That is
    unacceptable for RustDesk because it could sweep an unrelated portable installation, so this slice deliberately
    uses a short explicit LSB script with one stop call instead:
    https://manpages.debian.org/init-d-script
- Intended authority model: systemd remains the primary deployment and owns the supervisor through the exact unit
  and cgroup. SysV starts the same foreground `/usr/bin/rustdesk --service` under one init-owned, root-created PID
  file and always combines PID-file, exact executable, process name, and root UID. It sends TERM, waits 30 seconds,
  and escalates to KILL only through that same combined predicate. Maintainer scripts select the running backend with
  `/run/systemd/system`; they never probe `/proc/1`, execute an init script directly, or rediscover RustDesk by name,
  argv, or path.
- Privilege/escalation audit of the new root surface:
  - `res/rustdesk.init` fixes `PATH`, `DAEMON`, `DAEMON_ARGS`, `NAME`, and `PIDFILE` in the root-owned packaged file.
    It does not source `/etc/default`, consume caller environment as command text, use `eval`, invoke a shell with
    `-c`, or interpolate user-controlled configuration into executable/arguments.
  - `/run/rustdesk.pid` is created by `start-stop-daemon` as root, observed mode 0644/root:root/single-link on Debian
    12, under root-owned `/run`. Its PID is public but is not writable by an unprivileged local user. Every action
    combines it with `--exec /usr/bin/rustdesk --name rustdesk --user root`; PID alone has no signal authority.
  - `/usr/bin/rustdesk` is the existing root-created symlink to the root-owned packaged executable. The init script is
    a root-owned mode-0755 conffile. Package construction rejects links, hardlinks, non-root archive ownership, or
    unexpected modes for payload authority.
  - Stop has exactly one `start-stop-daemon --stop` call. There is no executable-only cleanup, `pidof`, `pgrep`,
    `pkill`, `killall`, `ps`, raw `kill`, `/proc` parser, or missing-evidence signal fallback.
  - Repeated stop checks absence of a real PID-file entry before consulting the executable. This made Debian's
    upgrade sequence idempotent after the first stop removed the PID file and dpkg temporarily removed the symlink;
    a broken symlink does not pass the absence check and still fails closed through the exact matcher.
  - Because `start-stop-daemon --background` cannot directly report a later exec failure, start requires ten
    consecutive exact status observations over one second before reporting success.
  - Systemd's false `PIDFile=` declaration was removed. `Type=simple` already owns the exact main PID, and
    `KillMode=control-group` remains the stronger additional containment layer.
- Conceptual residual: SysV `start-stop-daemon` ultimately uses the numeric PID recorded in its root-owned PID file.
  Combining exact executable object, name, and root UID rejects an unrelated reused PID and blocks unprivileged local
  control, as the behavior fixture proves. It cannot distinguish an actual stale-PID reuse into a different
  root-owned process executing the exact same installed RustDesk object with the same comm name. Creating such a
  process already requires root (outside the local-unprivileged escalation threat), but it remains a lifecycle
  correctness ambiguity. This slice does not relabel the existing actual forced numeric-PID-reuse item as closed.
- Implemented package behavior:
  - `res/rustdesk.init` is an explicit LSB init script using an init-owned PID file, stable-start observation, a
    singular bounded exact stop, idempotent missing-PID handling, status, restart/try-restart/force-reload, and no
    reload fiction.
  - `res/DEBIAN/{preinst,postinst,prerm,postrm}` bind fixed `rustdesk` service names. Postinst always registers the
    packaged init script; systemd-active systems retain the prior helper/reload/start path, while non-systemd systems
    use `invoke-rc.d`. Upgrade/removal stop through the same selected backend and purge removes both helper state and
    SysV links.
  - `build.py` and `scripts/verify-debian-package-authority.py` add `/etc/init.d/rustdesk` as an exact mode-0755
    conffile and bind its constructor copy, inventory, md5 exclusion, source mode, and mutation behavior.
  - `scripts/verify-debian-maintainer-scripts.py` now validates the init script as well as backend selection and legal

  - `scripts/smoke-debian-sysv-lifecycle.sh` and the mounted smoke stage add the release behavior path;

    artifact/update authority from supported init backends for the same supervisor.

### R-S11c-27m design/runtime audit — installed Debian systemd lifecycle

- This bounded release-blocking slice closes the installed systemd stop/restart and installed supervisor
  crash/restart checklist entries, including the production non-root active-seat child. It does not claim the final
  release `.deb`, actual forced numeric-PID reuse, cross-mount/container namespace identity, OpenRC/runit/manual
  packaging integration, exact-commit cold artifact evidence, or external expert R-V3 review. The parent R-S11c-27
  item and upcoming release remain open.
- Existing production behavior proved before adding the release test:
  - `res/rustdesk.service` is `Type=simple`, directly executes `/usr/bin/rustdesk --service`, restarts on failure,
    keeps `/run/rustdesk` across an automatic restart, uses `KillMode=control-group`, and admits the syscalls required
    by the durable-record/pidfd recovery implementation.
  - Debian maintainer scripts select systemd through `/run/systemd/system`, install the exact unit, reload the fixed
    system manager, and use `deb-systemd-invoke`; no systemd installed-lifecycle behavior test previously ran a real
    PID 1/cgroup manager.
  - The source/focused/manual/container proofs already covered direct child ownership, parent-death binding, durable
    evidence, exact recovery, normal stop, forced child reap, crash recovery, non-root descriptor exec, hostile
    records, portable noninterference, separate-Docker survival, pre-pidfd fallback, and installed SysV. The missing
    proof was their composition with real package scripts and the production systemd unit.
- Primary contracts used for the design:
  - systemd service unit semantics (`Type=simple`, `Restart=`, `KillMode=`, `RuntimeDirectory=`):
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/systemd.service.html
  - systemd container/virtualization boundary and private manager expectations:
    https://systemd.io/CONTAINER_INTERFACE/
  - Debian Policy service management and maintainer-script model:
    https://www.debian.org/doc/debian-policy/
  - Debian's systemd maintainer helper:
    https://manpages.debian.org/bookworm/init-system-helpers/deb-systemd-invoke.1p.en.html
  - cloud-init NoCloud seed behavior used only to launch the guest-side transaction:
    https://cloudinit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/datasources/nocloud.html
- Authority-model decision: do not run systemd against the host PID/cgroup namespaces and do not weaken Docker with
  `--privileged`, host PID/cgroup sharing, a writable cgroup mount, added capabilities, a Docker socket mount, host
  networking, or a published port. A disposable unprivileged KVM/QEMU guest supplies its own real PID 1 and cgroup
  tree. QEMU has `-nic none`; the pinned base is mode 0444; a throwaway qcow2 overlay receives every guest write;
  source/test payload is immutable ISO9660; no shared-directory write protocol reaches the repository.
- Immutable guest input:
  - Debian dated build `20260712-2537`, file
    `debian-12-genericcloud-amd64-20260712-2537.qcow2`.
  - Publisher-derived/independently computed SHA-512
    `6c2607f1846ee86040830c87d0b723f0967da3e884ea4673d9db4aa8eee13a4b7c663524bfa42082c16fc6919f3aa1bf425c004d07ff06c53a319ad0c42647bb`.
  - `scripts/online-fetch.sh --debian-systemd-smoke-image` is the sole network acquisition mode. It checks the
    `.harness-state` root and child as real current-user-owned mode-0700 directories before mutation; verifies HTTPS,
    hash, regular-file/link/ownership/mode authority; and stores the base mode 0444. The smoke itself has no network.
- Host boundary:
  - The orchestrator rejects UID 0 and requires unprivileged read/write access to `/dev/kvm`.
  - It rejects a symlinked/mis-owned/mis-moded/multiply-linked/wrong-hash base, a qcow2 backing file, wrong image
    format, failed `qemu-img check`, or an unexpectedly small image.
  - Runtime dependencies are copied only from the already-required `rd-devcheck` image in a separate Docker run as
    host UID/GID, `--network none`, read-only root, read-only repository, `--cap-drop ALL`, no-new-privileges, and
    `--pids-limit 64`. The resulting 100-file bundle is copied into the guest-only loader directory; it cannot alter
    the production unit or source tree.
  - The exact binary, unit, init script, maintainer scripts, guest driver, and strict loginctl fixture are hashed
    before QEMU starts and again after clean guest shutdown. QEMU receives only the overlay plus read-only seed and
    payload CD-ROMs. A 420-second hard timeout terminates a hung VM and prints bounded serial evidence.
- Guest transaction and proof:
  - Requires euid 0 only inside the overlay, PID 1 `systemd`, `/run/systemd/system`, Debian bookworm, and read-only
    payload mounts. It refuses a pre-existing RustDesk install or `policy-rc.d` suppression.
  - Creates one UID/GID-4001 active X11 seat with group 4101 and one UID-4000 portable user. The replacement
    `/usr/bin/loginctl` accepts only the production query argv and exits 64 on everything else.
  - Builds a minimal `.deb` from the exact production binary, unit, SysV conffile, and four maintainer scripts, then
    runs `dpkg -i`. The installed unit must byte-match `res/rustdesk.service`, have no drop-in, and pass
    `systemd-analyze verify`.
  - Every captured generation binds the systemd `MainPID` to root UID, installed executable inode, exact
    `/usr/bin/rustdesk --service` argv, and `system.slice/rustdesk.service`. The runtime directory must be root:root
    mode 0700.
  - Strictly parses the root-owned mode-0600 durable child record and matches boot ID, PID/start time, executable
    device/inode, UID, canonical generation, and role to procfs. The live child must have direct PPID ownership,
    exact installed inode, descriptor-exec argv, all four UID/GID fields 4001, groups 4001/4101, zero
    inheritable/permitted/effective/ambient capability sets, `NoNewPrivs: 1`, the exact bounded environment, and the
    same RustDesk service cgroup.
  - Runs a separate copy of the actual RustDesk binary as UID 4000 with neutral `--server` argv under transient
    `rustdesk-portable-smoke.service`; PID/start, four UIDs, argv, and distinct cgroup are revalidated after every
    service lifecycle event.
  - Proves package-started generation, normal systemd restart to a fresh supervisor/child/generation, deliberate
    stop with no unexpected restart and runtime-directory removal, explicit start to another fresh generation, and
    automatic failure restart after exact unit-scoped `systemctl kill --kill-whom=main --signal=KILL`.
  - The crash path requires the prior supervisor and child to disappear, a fresh MainPID/generation, `NRestarts >=
    1`, and the fresh supervisor's exact exited/stale durable-record recovery diagnostic. It does not use a raw PID
    signal or process-name scan. Package removal must reap installed processes and remove executable/unit/runtime;
    purge must remove the SysV conffile; the unrelated portable unit survives until its one explicit final stop.
- Two harness defects were exposed and corrected without changing production behavior:
  - cloud-init prefixes guest output on the serial console. The host now removes ANSI/CR framing, extracts only five
    fixed marker namespaces, rejects conflicting duplicates, and validates exact anchored marker grammars.
  - `set -o pipefail` plus `journalctl | grep -q` could false-fail after a successful early match when journalctl
    received SIGPIPE. The guest now captures journal output to a private file first and greps that stable evidence.
- Verification integration:
  - `scripts/verify-release.sh` now has an exact ordered thirteen-gate contract and runs the installed-systemd VM

  - `scripts/verify.sh` seals executable modes, image build/hash pins, safe fetch, host unprivileged/KVM boundary,

  - `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` loads the new host, guest, loginctl, and fetch sources as first-class

    portable crash-time proof, use raw numeric-PID crash injection, accept unexpected loginctl argv, alter the image
    hash, remove private state-root validation, or unwire the release gate; every mutation was rejected.

### R-S11c-27n design/runtime audit — cross-container executable identity

- This bounded slice closes the separately tracked cross-mount/container-namespace executable-identity and
  identical-in-container-path cases. It does not claim actual forced kernel numeric-PID reuse, final-release `.deb`
  artifact proof, OpenRC/runit/manually supervised packaging integration, exact-commit cold artifact evidence, or
  external expert R-V3 review. The parent R-S11c-27 item and upcoming release remain open.
- No production Rust, dependency, package definition, installed host file, host service, firewall rule, or listener
  changed. The commit changes only the disposable runtime-smoke fixtures, their sealed verifier, and the hardening
  ledger. In particular, the production Linux recovery predicate remains boot ID + `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time +
  UID + dereferenced `/proc/<pid>/exe` device/inode + exact service-owned argv/environment generation, immediately
  revalidated before pidfd-bound signaling.
- Primary contracts used for the design:
  - Linux `/proc/<pid>/exe` magic-link executable-object semantics:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html
  - Linux mount namespace isolation:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/mount_namespaces.7.html
  - Linux PID namespace visibility and signaling boundaries:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/pid_namespaces.7.html
  - Linux pidfd task identity and signaling:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_send_signal.2.html
  - Docker container filesystem/process isolation and network-none behavior:
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/ and
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/none/
- Container and host authority boundary:
  - Both runtime containers use private mount and PID namespaces, `--network none`, no published port, no Docker
    socket, no host PID namespace, no peer PID namespace, and a read-only repository bind. They receive no host
    systemd, package-manager, RustDesk-service, firewall, or process-name signaling authority.
  - The lifecycle container retains only its pre-existing narrow `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` addition, required for the root
    supervisor to inspect its deliberately non-root service child. No `--privileged`, `SYS_ADMIN`, host cgroup
    sharing, writable host executable path, or host root operation was added.
  - The sibling's container-root setup copies the already-built fixture only into that container's private
    `/usr/bin/rustdesk`. Before executing RustDesk it sets no-new-privileges and removes every inheritable,
    permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capability. The exact live status is verified through procfs.
  - The outer host process guard remains unprivileged and observational. It records the pre-smoke historical
    `rustdesk +--server` selector baseline and fails if the smoke creates a new matching host-visible argv. The
    neutral `rd-smoke-server` argv0 prevents the fixture from colliding with the operational older host selector;
    the exact service-owned role is proved separately rather than inferred from text matching.
- Executable and process identity proof:
  - Each container installs the same read-only source bytes at the identical `/usr/bin/rustdesk` pathname. The
    source SHA-256 must match in both containers, while main-installed, sibling-installed, and source device/inode
    identities must all be separated as appropriate; mount-namespace and PID-namespace inode identities must also
    differ.
  - The sibling launcher opens the installed executable with `O_NOFOLLOW`, checks it is a regular executable file,
    and descriptor-execs it with exactly `rd-smoke-server --server --service-owned-server`. It accepts no other
    optional marker.
  - The sibling guard binds readiness to retained PID/start time, dereferenced executable device/inode, exact argv,
    direct launch parent, canonical unique generation, root UID tuple, no-new-privileges, and five zero capability
    sets. A bounded environment read rejects oversized process evidence and requires the unique expected generation
    and parent entries.
  - Every main lifecycle generation must match both its strict durable record and that container's installed
    executable object. The sibling's exact PID/start/executable/generation is rechecked after the entire hostile-
    record, graceful restart, forced escalation, supervisor-crash recovery, forced pre-pidfd, non-root active-seat,

### R-S11c-27o design/runtime audit — actual forced numeric-PID reuse

- This bounded slice closes the actual forced kernel numeric-PID reuse case for service-child recovery. It does not
  claim final-release `.deb` artifact proof, OpenRC/runit/manual packaging integration, exact-commit cold artifact
  evidence, or external expert R-V3 review. The parent R-S11c-27 item and upcoming release remain open.
- No production Rust, dependency, package definition, installed host file, host service, firewall rule, host listener,
  or host RustDesk configuration changed. The commit changes only a disposable Docker smoke fixture, the mounted
  smoke dispatcher/orchestrator, the sealed verifier, and the hardening ledger.
- Primary contracts used for the design:
  - Linux kernel `/proc/sys/kernel/ns_last_pid` controls the last allocated PID in the current PID namespace:
    https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/sysctl/kernel.html
  - PID namespaces virtualize `ns_last_pid`, and writing it requires `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` or `CAP_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE` in
    the owning user namespace: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/pid_namespaces.7.html
  - `CAP_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE` specifically covers updating `/proc/sys/kernel/ns_last_pid`:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html
  - Docker `--network none` gives the container its own network stack with no external interfaces:
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/none/
- Container and host authority boundary:
  - The PID-reuse proof runs in a separate `PID_REUSE_RUN` Docker invocation with `--network none`, `--read-only`,
    `--pids-limit 128`, read-only repository bind, private tmpfs `/tmp` and `/run`, no published ports, no host PID
    namespace, no Docker socket, no host systemd, no package-manager authority, and no host RustDesk service path.
  - The container starts with `--cap-drop ALL` and adds only `SYS_ADMIN`, `CHECKPOINT_RESTORE`, and `SETPCAP`. The
    first two are required only to remount `/proc/sys` writable and set the private namespace allocator state; the
    third lets the fixture drop capability sets for the RustDesk processes. AppArmor is unconfined only for the
    container-local procfs remount. There is no `--privileged`, host networking, host PID sharing, or host process
    signaling.
  - The RustDesk children and the tested `rustdesk --service` recovery process execute under `setpriv
    --no-new-privs --inh-caps=-all --ambient-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all`. The process guard revalidates exact
    service-owned argv, parent, generation, UID, no-new-privileges, and capability state for live children. The
    capability-bearing process is the fixture shell that prepares private PID allocation, not the RustDesk process
    whose lifecycle authority is under test.
  - The fixture uses pidfd signaling only against exact PID/start identities it created for cleanup. It contains no
    `pkill`, no `os.kill`, no `kill -`, no sudo, no host PID namespace, no privileged container, and no published
    port.
- Process and stale-record proof:
  - The fixture writes `target_pid - 1` to private `/proc/sys/kernel/ns_last_pid`, reads it back, and immediately
    launches a RustDesk service-owned child through the descriptor-bound smoke launcher. That child is required to
    receive PID `50000`.
  - It writes a strict root-owned mode-0600 service-child record for that first child, then stops exactly that child
    by retained PID/start time.
  - It again forces the allocator predecessor and launches a different RustDesk service-owned child. The second
    child must receive the same numeric PID `50000`, use the same executable object, and have a different start time
    and different generation.
  - Running production `rustdesk --service` against the stale record must exit `1`, log the fail-closed lifecycle
    authority diagnostic and exact start-time mismatch, preserve the record identity/bytes, and leave the reused-PID
    child alive. The process guard then revalidates the surviving child before exact fixture cleanup removes only the
    record identity/hash it created.
- Runtime evidence: `/tmp/rustdesk-rs11c27o-pid-reuse.log`, 858 bytes, mode 0664, SHA-256

    root-owned mode-0644 single-link `/run/rustdesk.pid` containing the stopped supervisor PID. The next native
    `start` overwrites it with the new exact supervisor; the harness requires that identity replacement.

### R-A10 partial/dribbled pre-key-frame runtime closure — 2026-07-18

- Closed the exact project-test gap exposed by the R-V3 handoff without claiming external audit or artifact
  evidence. The relevant source path is: `BytesCodec` consumes a valid frame header and retains `Data(n)` while an
  incomplete body remains buffered; responder WAIT_1 wraps that retained `FramedStream::next()` in the production
  5,000 ms deadline and maps expiry to `HandshakeError::Io`; `src/server.rs::authenticate_tcp_stream` installs keys
  only on `Ok(keys)`. Before this slice, the limiter mutation API itself was a public blind increment and the server
  separately relied on callers remembering to classify the error first.
- Replaced that wrong public surface with `record_handshake_failure(source, HandshakeError) -> bool`. The private
  limiter map can now mutate only after the typed choke proves `HandshakeError::Confirmation`; timeout, EOF,
  framing, protocol, and non-confirmation PAKE aborts return `false` without touching the map. The production server
  uses that same return value for its key-confirmation security event. The old public `record_guess_failure` API and
  all call sites were deleted; the limiter-cap test now drives the typed confirmation path.
- Added `partial_prekey_frame_times_out_without_key_or_guess_charge` to the real loopback `cpace_it` suite. It sends
  the exact two-byte header declaring a valid 64-byte frame, writes one body byte, flushes, and deliberately keeps
  the raw attacker socket open. Under Tokio's paused clock, the responder remains pending for exactly the 5-second
  production WAIT_1 interval, returns `Io`, remains unkeyed, and drops the connection (the raw peer observes EOF).
  The test primes a unique TEST-NET-2 source to nine confirmation failures, accounts the actual `Io`, and proves the
  source remains allowed. The companion wrong-password test accounts the actual `Confirmation` as the tenth event
  and proves it blocks. Oversize responder/viewer, out-of-order, duplicate, and malformed wire negatives now also
  assert that no keys engage and their actual errors consume no limiter slot.
- Made the evidence drift-resistant rather than merely documentary. The R-V3 scope verifier now anchors the new
  behavioral test, the typed mutation symbol, and the exact production-server call; it rejects restoration of a
  blind public limiter increment. Its mutation suite exercises removal/renaming of the partial-frame test and
  reintroduction of the blind API. The audit handoff and hardening ledger now describe the evidence as closed only
  at project-test level and continue to say explicitly that R-V3 is outstanding.

    `{54E86BC2-6C85-41F3-A9EB-1A94AC9B1F93}_is1` record in native and manually addressed `Wow6432Node` views,
    then the app-name record in the alternate/native views, and selected the first namespace with any nonempty

    `BuildDate`, the `share_rdp` read, and the LocalSystem typed `_service` `share_rdp` write. A naturally stale
    administrator-owned legacy record could therefore make the current MSI installation appear absent or split
    service-owned RDP policy into a retired namespace.

    SYSTEM primitive: HKLM uninstall metadata is normally administrator-owned and the typed mutation already

    applications to explicit alternate-view flags; the selected design uses `KEY_WOW64_64KEY`:
