### R-S11e-24 Windows privacy-display registry recovery authority — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the pre-change Windows authority path before changing it:
  - `src/platform/windows.rs::RegRecovery` was a public serde object containing a caller-selected HKLM path, value
    name, old/new raw byte sequences, and integer registry types. `restore_reg_connectivity` opened that path with
    write authority and selected the value/type/bytes from the deserialized object.
  - `src/privacy_mode/win_virtual_display.rs` serialized the object into the generic `reg_recovery` Config option,
    while `src/core_main.rs` deserialized and replayed it at `--server` startup. The non-forced current-value check
    did not authenticate the request because the same record supplied the expected `new` bytes and type.
  - This was classified as an approved-elevation confused-deputy shape, not promoted to a demonstrated promptless
    standard-user-to-SYSTEM primitive. The supported installed service child reads the MSI-provisioned protected
    ProgramData root and has no durable config-write authority after R-S11e-22, so this persistence abstraction was
    ineffective there; a directly launched user-profile server needed deliberate elevation before the HKLM sink
    could succeed. That split made the mechanism both non-durable for the supported service and over-authoritative
    for an elevated user-profile process.
- Implemented the narrow process-local replacement required by new normative requirement R-S11j:
  - Deleted the generic config key, serde/JSON representation, startup replay, exported startup helper, arbitrary
    path/value/type fields, and integer-to-registry-type converter.
  - `RegRecovery` is crate-visible only as a type with module-private fields: one directly enumerated Connectivity
    child name and the prior raw `Recent` value. Its constructor path is the private snapshot diff; callers cannot
    choose a root, parent path, value name, registry type, or replacement target.
  - Snapshot reads now fetch only the fixed `Recent` value. A missing value is normal; every other registry read
    error propagates. Restore derives the fixed HKLM GraphicsDrivers/Connectivity parent, rejects empty, nested,
    control-bearing, or over-255-UTF-16-unit child names, opens with `KEY_SET_VALUE` only, and writes only `Recent`.
  - `PrivacyModeImpl` owns the collection in memory and consumes it once after its normal display-mode rollback.
    Every changed display child is retained and every retained restore is attempted before aggregate failure is
    returned. This also fixes the inherited multi-monitor correctness bug where nondeterministic HashMap iteration
    returned only the first changed `Recent` value.
  - Normal same-process turn-off behavior is preserved. Serialized crash recovery is intentionally not retained and
    no durable crash-recovery claim is made. Microsoft documents `SetDisplayConfig` as the supported display-topology
    API; any future durable recovery must use CCD state or a typed service-owned transaction with receiver-side
    validation, never generic configuration replay:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setdisplayconfig.

    `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, falling back to `HOME/.config`, and `Config::get_home()` independently accepted ambient
    `HOME`. That is the correct contract for an ordinary user-owned viewer/server but not for the root/service-owned
    process that enforces unattended credentials and machine policy.
  - Both exact `--service` and `--server --service-owned-server` reached those ambient helpers before this slice.
    The root/headless service-child branch called `env_clear()` and then explicitly copied the supervisor's ambient
    `HOME` into the child; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` was absent only because that particular launcher cleared it.
  - Systemd's service environment commonly masks this defect, but this fork supports init-system-independent and
    manual/sudo launch shapes. The application therefore depended on a launcher's environment policy to select the
    credential namespace. This was classified as service-policy/config-namespace confused-deputy correctness, not
    promoted to a demonstrated promptless local privilege escalation: impact also depends on which environment a
    privileged launcher preserves and the ownership of the selected filesystem target.
  - Primary contracts checked: pinned `directories-next` 2.0.0 source/docs, the XDG Base Directory specification,
    `getpwuid(3)`, and systemd's execution-environment contract:
    https://docs.rs/directories-next/2.0.0/directories_next/struct.ProjectDirs.html,
    https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/latest/,
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/getpwuid.3.html, and
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.exec.html.
- Implemented one role-confined authority model:

    The project component deliberately mirrors pinned `directories-next` Linux whitespace/lowercase mapping while
    rejecting empty, path-bearing, control-bearing, relative, or non-clean inputs.
  - Added a separate `get_effective_home_dir_trusted()` API. Review caught that the older trusted-home helper uses
    real uid (`getuid`) for caller-owned elevation paths; service-owned authority must use effective uid (`geteuid`).
    Both APIs share one passwd lookup/existing-directory implementation, preserving every old call site's semantics.

## 2026-07-19 — R-S11e-40 Linux loginctl session-query authority

- Selected exactly one coherent continuation slice after reconciling the current requirements, hardening ledger,
  call graph, and clean `master`: the shared Linux `loginctl` session-discovery boundary. The already-closed
  R-S11b/R-S11c IPC checklist was not reopened. Still-open release-wide evidence remains R-B2's exact cold
  artifact transaction, R-S11c-27's exact Debian artifact execution, native Apple/Windows evidence, real-device
  Android lifecycle/storage evidence, artifact publication/retention work, and independent R-V3 CPace review.
- Proven old path and authority model:
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/platform/linux.rs` used the private generic
    `run_loginctl(Option<Vec<&str>>)` for every session query. It retained the previously hardened fixed,
    metadata-authenticated executable and stdio-only descriptor boundary, but inherited the caller's entire
    environment, accepted arbitrary internal argv shapes, ignored non-success exit status, and decoded stdout with
    lossy UTF-8.
  - Session listing used loginctl's default formatted table. Selection searched the whole row for `seat0`, recovered
    columns repeatedly with whitespace scans, and `is_active` accepted any output containing `active`, including
    conceptually `inactive`. `is_active_and_seat0`/`is_session_locked` requested broad property output and searched
    substrings rather than parsing exactly requested rows.
  - `get_display_server_of_session(session)` asked logind about an explicit other session, but substituted the
    calling process's ambient `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` when that result was empty, tty, unspecified, or unavailable. That
    environment value describes the caller and cannot authenticate the queried session.
  - The intended model is receiver-owned and closed: trusted local logind supplies session facts through one typed,
    noninteractive query vocabulary; the executable, argv, environment, descriptors, exit status, parser, and
    fallback are all selected by the receiver. The calling process's desktop environment supplies none of another
    session's identity, seat, state, lock, or display authority.
- Primary contract research and a compatibility correction made during review:
  - The systemd 252 `loginctl(1)` manual designates `show-session` as computer-parsable, documents `--property`,
    `--no-legend`, `--no-pager`, and nonzero failure status, and warns that inherited pager configuration can become
    an elevated-command boundary:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/loginctl.html.
  - Pinned systemd 252 source emits SESSION/UID/USER/SEAT/TTY for `list-sessions`, while current systemd 260 source
    preserves the first four fields and appends LEADER/CLASS/TTY/IDLE/SINCE:
    https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v252/src/login/loginctl.c and
    https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v260/src/login/loginctl.c.
  - An intermediate draft incorrectly required only a four/five-column list and would have rejected systemd 260.
    That draft was never committed. The final parser exactly validates only the four stable authority-bearing
    SESSION/UID/USER/SEAT fields, including canonical decimal UID, and deliberately ignores version-dependent
    trailing presentation fields. Unit and source-mutation gates bind both the pinned five-field and current
    nine-field shapes. Property decisions use the documented `show-session` interface rather than table tails.
  - Rust `Command::env_clear` supplies the complete child-environment removal primitive:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Command.html#method.env_clear.
- Authority/risk assessment:
  - The inspected packaged systemd, SysV, OpenRC, runit, and manual launch paths expose no proved ordinary-user write
    into the root supervisor's environment. Normal logind output is a local OS-service result, not network input.
    Exploiting a hostile bus selector or forged output therefore requires privileged/misconfigured launch state or
    already-compromised local OS authority.
  - This is recorded as concrete cross-session deterministic-correctness and parser defects plus conceptual
    privileged session-confusion/future-deployment authority. It is defense in depth and is not claimed as a
    demonstrated promptless ordinary-user-to-root privilege escalation or evidence that this host was compromised.
- Implemented closure in `libs/hbb_common/src/platform/linux.rs:385-706`:
  - Replaced the generic optional argv helper with closed `LoginctlQuery::{ListSessions,SessionProperties}` and
    enumerated `LoginctlProperty::{Type,State,Seat,LockedHint}`. The receiver emits only exact `--no-pager`,
    list-only `--no-legend`, enumerated `--property=...`, `show-session`, and an option terminator before the
    separately supplied nonempty session identifier.
  - `configure_loginctl_environment` calls `env_clear()` before argv and the existing descriptor policy. No variable
    is re-added. `run_loginctl` now rejects every non-success exit and retains the fixed trusted executable proof.
  - Added strict UTF-8 parsers. The list parser requires all four stable leading fields and a canonical `u32` UID.
    The property parser accepts exactly one row for every requested property, reorders it to receiver-request order,
    and rejects missing, duplicate, malformed, unrequested, or control-bearing property data.
  - Active seat, state, and lock decisions compare the parsed field/value exactly. Session-Type fallback is now only
    the binary's compile-pinned X11 constant; the queried-session path contains no `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` read.
  - Updated both lifecycle loginctl fixtures to accept only the exact new production argv and return exit 64 for
    every other shape. Added R-S11z, Appendix C #148, R-S11e-40, a dedicated shell source gate, semantic source
    checks, and independent mutation cases. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `5349fee77bdc9107ccfa2fa426d05cef138451214a8c0943a11ddc491f3b4b43`, synchronized in both tracked ledgers.

    fixed systemctl image, used direct argv, applied the shared stdio-only descriptor policy, rejected spawn/nonzero
    status, and was reachable only from install/uninstall CLI paths that first required superuser authority.
  - It still inherited the privileged RustDesk process's complete environment, accepted a generic internal action
    string, supplied an unsuffixed unit whose type systemctl inferred, selected no explicit manager scope, and left
    stdin and authorization interaction ambient.

    ending alphanumeric, and otherwise containing only alphanumerics or hyphens. The receiver did not independently
    enforce that grammar before conferring unit-selection authority.

    demonstrated promptless local privilege escalation and not evidence of host compromise.

    user managers, documents `--no-pager` and `--no-ask-password`, states that enable searches unit directories and
    creates persistent symlinks, and treats exit zero as success:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/systemctl.html.
  - Official systemd 252 `systemd.unit(5)` states that `SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH` overrides the unit load path:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/systemd.unit.html.
  - Pinned systemd 252 `acquire_bus` source reads `SYSTEMCTL_FORCE_BUS`; a true value replaces the direct local
    manager path with the full D-Bus path. The corresponding bus source selects the default system bus on that path,
    for which `DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS` can supply the address:
    https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v252/src/systemctl/systemctl-util.c and
    https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v252/src/shared/bus-util.c.
  - Rust `Command::env_clear` is the complete child-environment removal primitive:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Command.html#method.env_clear.
  - The existing non-root networkless devcheck image contains systemd 252.39. Its systemctl accepted
    `--system --no-pager --no-ask-password -- definitely-not-a-systemctl-command` and reported the unknown verb,

### R-S11e-44 Linux headless connection-manager parent authority — 2026-07-19

- Reconstructed the complete old authority path before changing it:
  - The installed Linux root supervisor called `stop_headless_connection_manager_processes()` once during service
    startup and once before each root/active-user server replacement. The helper enumerated the global process table,
    accepted current-executable equality plus an exact displayed `--cm-no-ui` argv element, and issued
    `kill(pid, SIGKILL)` from the supervisor.
  - No `Child`, pidfd, start identity, generation, or parent relationship survived from observation through signal.
    A genuine installed RustDesk image is executable by an ordinary user, argv is caller-controlled presentation,
    and the check-to-signal interval could cross exec, exit, or PID reuse. This was root-originated process-table
    availability/confused-deputy and PID-race authority, not a demonstrated promptless ordinary-user-to-root
    primitive: termination does not itself grant root execution.
  - The exact service-owned/same-principal `--server` process already creates the no-UI CM, keeps its `Child` in the
    existing child collection, authenticates its fixed-endpoint IPC with the closed launch token/parent environment,
    and retains the established `EXIT_ON_IDLE` graceful-drain behavior. No global rediscovery was necessary.
- Primary kernel/runtime contracts inspected:
  - `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` delivers the configured signal when the creating parent thread dies, is inherited across an
    ordinary exec, and is cleared by specified credential/privileged-exec transitions:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pr_set_pdeathsig.2const.html.
  - `getppid()` observes a changed parent after an already-completed parent exit, so arming first and comparing
    second closes the otherwise unavoidable early-exit interval:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/getppid.2.html.
  - Rust 1.75 `CommandExt::pre_exec` requires the child hook to obey post-fork restrictions; the production hook uses
    only captured numeric data, raw `prctl`/`getppid` syscalls, and allocation-free error construction:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.75.0/std/os/unix/process/trait.CommandExt.html#method.pre_exec.
- Implemented the smallest closed ownership model:
  - Deleted the supervisor CM cleanup function, the current-image SIGKILL sweep, its direct kill wrapper, and all
    three service-loop calls. Existing same-user tray SIGTERM cleanup remains separate; global server and obsolete
    Xorg sweeps remain absent.
  - Generalized the existing Linux service-child parent-death primitive without weakening its credential ordering.
    `configure_command_kill_on_parent_death` captures the server PID in the parent and registers a raw-syscall
    `pre_exec` hook. The child first arms `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)`, then compares raw `getppid` with the captured
    parent and aborts exec with ESRCH on mismatch.
  - Added a Linux-only typed current-image launch wrapper. Only `headless_cm` selects it; GUI CM and every non-Linux
    launch retain the ordinary path. Parent-death registration precedes the existing R-S11q non-stdio descriptor
    hook. The documented parent is the creating server runtime thread, so unexpected worker loss conservatively
    retires the helper and a later connection can create a fresh generation.
  - Added an actual three-process regression: the controller launches an exact test-image launcher, the launcher
    spawns the worker through the production parent-bound helper, the worker reports its PID over a private Unix
    socket, the controller retains a pidfd, kills/reaps the launcher, and requires the worker pidfd to become
    readable. A failure-only pidfd signal prevents leaving a worker behind without weakening the assertion.
  - Added normative R-S11ad, Appendix C #152, the R-S11e-44 conformance record, dedicated shell/source gates, a
    semantic validator, and independent mutations for requirement/Appendix/ledger/gate drift, prctl operation,
    SIGKILL, getppid, captured-parent comparison, ESRCH failure, `pre_exec`, hook ordering, typed launch policy,

## 2026-07-19 — R-S11e-43 Linux obsolete Xorg process authority

- Selected exactly one coherent R-S11b/R-S11c continuation slice after rereading the normative service authority,
  display/session, package, and hardening-ledger requirements: delete obsolete Linux Xorg process authority. The
  already-closed IPC checklist was not reopened. The exact clean Debian artifact transaction remains owned by
  R-B2/R-S11c-27 and was not run.
- Proven old path and authority failure:
  - Root `stop_subprocess()` built `/etc/<app>/xorg.conf`, enumerated every visible `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, accepted
    displayed argv-zero basename `Xorg` plus that exact argument, and sent SIGKILL at service startup and both
    server-child replacement sites. No parent/child generation, executable object, start identity, UID, logind
    session, or other ownership evidence existed.
  - `Desktop::set_is_subprocess()` independently scanned all visible process command lines for that config path and
    made the exact selected desktop appear headless. This could change service restart/lifecycle decisions without
    any relationship to the selected logind session.
  - Linux `proc_pid_cmdline(5)` explicitly describes cmdline as the command line a process wants an observer to see,
    and `execve(2)` receives caller-supplied argv. A local process can therefore present the old matcher text. The
    root signal path was availability/confused-deputy authority and the desktop path was deterministic service-state
    spoofing; neither is evidence of a promptless local privilege escalation or of host compromise.

    tracking from `linux_desktop_manager.rs`. The remaining module is existing-session discovery only. An
    administrator-prestarted X server is externally owned, so there is no supported RustDesk Xorg identity for the
    service to recover, classify, or terminate.

## 2026-07-19 — R-S11e-38 cross-platform root-to-user helper authority

- Selected audit slice:
  - Re-audited every remaining repository call to `run_as_user`, `run_as_user_with_env`, `sudo -E`, and macOS
    `launchctl asuser` after the Windows dormant-launcher cleanup. The older R-S11e-35 and R-S11e-10 records were
    too broad: Windows alone enforced exact raw role/environment shapes, Linux still accepted a caller-provided
    UID/username plus arbitrary syntactically valid environment variables, and macOS still accepted arbitrary argv
    plus a four-key environment union.

    selected the deleted Unix argv/environment/user tuple. The finding is therefore conceptual/future privileged-
    launch authority, not a demonstrated promptless ordinary-user-to-root exploit.
- Primary contract proof and authority model:
  - Apple's `launchctl(1)` contract states that `asuser` adopts the target user's Mach bootstrap namespace,
    exception server, and audit session but does not modify UID/GID or import the user's environment. It was not a
    root-to-user credential drop, so an environment allowlist could not repair the abstraction:
    https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/launchctl.1.html.
  - The sudoers environment contract makes preservation depend on command-line, sudoers, and PAM/site policy;
    therefore a `sudo -E` sentinel probe does not turn the application launch into an exact receiver-owned
    environment contract: https://www.sudo.ws/docs/man/1.9.14/sudoers.man.pdf.
  - Linux installed-service topology already owns the exact credential boundary in its supervised service-server
    child before exec. The deliberate headless-root server serves the authenticated root owner and uses a same-
    principal helper. macOS service-owned server topology is the per-user LaunchAgent. Neither platform needs a
    generic root current-image launcher. Windows is the necessary exception because its installed server is
    LocalSystem and must enter the active desktop session.

## 2026-07-19 — R-S11e-39 Linux pkcheck inherited environment authority

- Selected audit slice and proved old path:
  - Continued the privileged external-process audit after the generic root-to-user launcher deletion. The remaining
    Linux service-owned unattended-password path resolves and metadata-authenticates `/usr/bin/pkcheck`, supplies
    the fixed RustDesk action and kernel-derived `pid,start-time,uid` subject, null-routes stdio, closes inherited
    non-stdio descriptors on exec, bounds execution, reaps on timeout/shutdown/error, and accepts only successful
    exit as authorization.
  - Its mutable `std::process::Command` did not call `env_clear`, so the root supervisor's complete ambient
    environment still entered the external authorization helper. This is a separate authority edge from the already
    closed executable, argv, subject, descriptor, and timeout edges.
- Primary contracts and impact classification:
  - The official `pkcheck(1)` manual describes pkcheck as a simple wrapper around the polkit D-Bus interface:
    https://polkit.pages.freedesktop.org/polkit/pkcheck.1.html.
  - The D-Bus specification states that `DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS` supplies the system-bus address and that the
    well-known local system-bus socket is used when that variable is absent:
    https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html.
  - Rust `Command::env_clear` prevents inheritance and removes all explicitly configured variables:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Command.html#method.env_clear.
  - Packaged systemd/SysV/OpenRC/runit/manual launch configurations and current service callers expose no proved
    ordinary-user-controlled write into the root supervisor environment. A hostile bus/loader value requires a
    privileged or otherwise misconfigured launcher. The finding is therefore conceptual privileged authorization-
    endpoint/future-deployment authority and defense in depth, not a demonstrated promptless ordinary-user-to-root
    primitive and not evidence that a supported deployment's polkit daemon was bypassed.
- Corrected authority model:
  - Added `configure_linux_pkcheck_environment`, which applies `Command::env_clear()` immediately after the trusted
    absolute image is chosen. The authorization command adds no environment values and then applies only exact argv,
    null stdio, R-S11p descriptor policy, and bounded fail-closed execution.
  - Kept the correction local to pkcheck. Display/session helpers whose protocols deliberately consume selected
    environment values were not refactored or broadened.
  - Added a two-hop actual-child regression. The parent launches an intermediate copy of the test image with a
    hostile `DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS`; the intermediate proves it received that ambient value, applies the exact
    production environment policy to a final copy, and the final image proves the bus selector and every other
    environment entry except its test-only role marker are absent.
  - Added normative R-S11y, Appendix C #147, R-S11e-39, an extracted shell gate, semantic verifier source checks,
    and independent mutations for removing the environment-clear primitive, adding an explicit bus selector after
    clearing, removing the production call, inverting the actual-child assertion, and renaming the shell gate,
    normative requirement, Appendix row, and hardening entry. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `5e2ff110dea6ae6af33e0094fa9452a8b2f6bc6a2363359cb70512b494f5a74f`, synchronized in both ledgers.

### R-S11e-34 macOS child inherited descriptor authority — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the complete macOS production subprocess inventory before changing it:
  - `src/platform/macos.rs` directly launched `launchctl` label queries/removal/loading and `launchctl asuser`,
    `osascript` install/uninstall scripts, app reopen through `open`, lock-state inspection through `ioreg`, and
    lock-screen control through `CGSession`. `src/ipc.rs` used `launchctl print` inside the root LaunchDaemon's
    service-owned unattended-password snapshot authorization check. `src/common.rs::run_me_with_env` launched the
    same RustDesk executable for CM/tray/whiteboard-style roles, and the feature-inert hardware-codec checker in
    `libs/scrap` launched another same-executable child. A final whole-tree launch review found the terminal shell's
    distinct `portable_pty::CommandBuilder` / `SlavePty::spawn_command` route in
    `src/server/terminal_service.rs`; it did not enter any of those ordinary `Command` call sites.
  - None of those macOS `Command` paths supplied an application-owned non-stdio descriptor contract. Darwin keeps
    descriptors across `exec` unless `FD_CLOEXEC` is set. Pinned Rust 1.75's macOS path used `posix_spawn` without
    Apple's close-by-default extension, while registering `pre_exec` selects its fork/exec path. A root/service IPC,
    credential-operation, log, directory, socket, or other kernel-object descriptor lacking close-on-exec could
    therefore enter a helper image. The LaunchDaemon authorization query and root-to-user transition make this a
    privileged-to-helper capability-boundary defect. It is not promoted to a demonstrated promptless ordinary-user-
    to-root primitive: exploitation still requires a live sensitive inheritable descriptor.
  - The pinned `portable-pty` fork performed `close_random_fds()` inside its pre-exec closure. That function
    allocated a vector, enumerated `/dev/fd` after `fork`, silently ignored enumeration and close errors, and called
    `close(2)` on every descriptor above stderr. Besides being unsafe in a multithreaded post-fork child, direct
    closure included Rust's private exec-error pipe, so a failed shell `exec` could be hidden from the parent.
  - `libs/hbb_common::platform::macos::alert` was unused but retained `osascript` 0.3 solely for a dependency-owned,
    PATH-selected helper launch outside RustDesk's command policy. The correct disposition was deletion, not a
    compatibility exception around an inaccessible launch.

  - Exact pinned Rust implementation:
    https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.75.0/library/std/src/sys/unix/process/process_unix.rs.
  - Rust 1.75 `CommandExt::pre_exec` safety contract:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.75.0/std/os/unix/process/trait.CommandExt.html#method.pre_exec.
  - Apple `getrlimit(2)`/`RLIMIT_NOFILE` contract:
    https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/getrlimit.2.html.
  - POSIX async-signal-safe function contract, including `fcntl`:
    https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/V2_chap02.html.
- Implemented one bounded stdio-only child authority:

    a value above 1,048,576. Parent-side `/dev/fd` enumeration additionally records inherited live descriptors above
    a later-lowered soft limit. The post-fork hook performs only raw `fcntl(F_GETFD/F_SETFD)`, marks every live
    descriptor above stderr close-on-exec, treats only `EBADF` as absence, and propagates every other error so
    `Command` fails before exec. The parent's descriptor table is unchanged. There is no non-stdio allowlist because
    none of the inventoried child protocols needs one.
  - Every inventoried production family applies the shared policy before `status`, `output`, or `spawn`. The
    LaunchDaemon's `launchctl print` authorization query returns false before executing the helper if policy setup

    non-stdio descriptor, accepts only `EBADF` as absence, and propagates every other failure. Rust's exec-error
    pipe therefore survives until successful `exec`. This conservative policy applies to all Unix PTY children so

### R-S11e-33 desktop fatal-signal default-disposition authority — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the complete pre-change authority path before editing it:
  - Every non-mobile release build called `register_breakdown_handler(breakdown_callback)` from shared
    `core_main`, so viewer, server, and installed-service roles all installed a process-wide `SIGSEGV` handler.
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/platform/mod.rs::breakdown_signal_handler` allocated a vector, traced and symbolized a
    backtrace, allocated/formatted names and messages, read and wrote persistent graphics/codec configuration,
    entered the logger, optionally launched a Linux desktop notification helper, invoked a closure stored in a
    mutable global, and finally called `std::process::exit(0)`.
  - The sole callback in `src/platform/mod.rs` entered input-service and native input backends to clear remapped
    keycodes and release modifiers. The Linux notification path resolved and spawned `notify-send`, `zenity`,
    `kdialog`, or `xmessage`; its standalone example kept the otherwise crash-only API live.
  - A synchronous memory-integrity signal can interrupt any thread while those allocators, locks, loggers,
    configuration writers, or native backends hold inconsistent state. Running the same facilities from the
    handler is undefined or deadlock-prone; converting the signal to success also suppresses truthful abnormal
    termination, ordinary crash/core diagnostics, and systemd `Restart=on-failure` recovery.
- Primary contracts researched:
  - POSIX `sigaction` limits defined behavior after asynchronous interruption to the async-signal-safe set and
    identifies allocator/stdio-backed operations as the canonical unsafe class:
    https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/sigaction.html.
  - POSIX process termination/default-signal behavior and `_Exit` distinguish abnormal signal termination from a
    normal status-zero exit and warn against reporting unsuccessful termination as success:
    https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/V2_chap02.html and
    https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/_exit.html.
  - POSIX `fork` and Linux `signal-safety(7)` independently reinforce that a multithreaded post-fork/signal context
    may use only async-signal-safe operations until exec:
    https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/fork.html and
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal-safety.7.html.
  - Rust `std::process::exit` runs platform exit handlers and is not a signal-safe replacement for default fatal
    disposition: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/fn.exit.html.
- Security classification:
  - This was a corrupted-process authority amplifier, availability defect, and forensic/recovery-integrity defect,
    not a demonstrated standalone local privilege escalation. Reaching the path still required a genuine fault or
    authority to signal the target process. The deleted Linux helper names, paths, and message text were fixed, so
    the audit did not prove caller-controlled command/argv injection. The severity grows when the same shared image
    runs as a service because the callback then re-enters privileged process state and can hide failure from its
    supervisor.

### R-S11e-32 Linux external-helper descriptor allowlist authority — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the remaining Linux external-program descriptor authority after R-S11e-28 through R-S11e-31:
  - The exact service roles, the enumerated sudo/reopen helpers, `pkcheck`, and same-executable children already had
    local close-on-exec policies, but the policy was owned by the root crate and did not cover helpers spawned from
    shared crates. `loginctl`, desktop notifications, `xdg-screensaver`, `xrandr`, `w`, `systemctl`, clipboard
    `fusermount`, and the Linux native-codec check could therefore inherit every ambient descriptor not already
    marked `FD_CLOEXEC`. Several are reachable from service-owned execution; the defect is an authority leak at an
    exec boundary, not evidence that any named helper actually abused an inherited descriptor.
  - Linux preserves open descriptors across `execve` unless their close-on-exec flag is set. Linux
    `close_range(..., CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)` marks a whole range without closing it in the multithreaded parent, and
    Rust requires a `CommandExt::pre_exec` closure to perform only operations safe in the post-fork/pre-exec child.
    Primary contracts reviewed:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html,
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/close_range.2.html, and
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/unix/process/trait.CommandExt.html#tymethod.pre_exec. The kernel documents
    `nr_open` as the maximum handle count, while `RLIMIT_NOFILE` is one greater than the highest valid descriptor:
    https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/sysctl/fs.html and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/getrlimit.2.html.
  - Clipboard FUSE is the only enumerated external-helper exception: `_FUSE_COMMFD` deliberately transfers one
    Unix-domain socket. The old code cleared `FD_CLOEXEC` on that socket in the multithreaded parent before spawn,
    creating a window in which an unrelated concurrent exec could inherit it. Correctness requires an exact child
    allowlist, not a process-global temporary inheritability change.
- Implemented one shared, fail-closed Linux command boundary in `hbb_common`:
  - The parent reads `/proc/sys/fs/nr_open`, derives the last valid descriptor as `nr_open - 1`, and rejects stdio entries,
    duplicates, negative values, and descriptors outside that bound before registering `pre_exec`.
  - In the child, the default policy marks every descriptor above stderr close-on-exec with
    `close_range(CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)`. Kernels without that operation use raw `fcntl(F_GETFD/F_SETFD)` across the
    validated finite range. Only after the ambient range is marked does the child clear `FD_CLOEXEC` on explicitly
    allowlisted descriptors. Errors are returned to `Command::spawn` rather than ignored.
  - The stdio-only wrapper now covers `loginctl`, desktop notification commands, both sudo/run-as-user paths,
    delayed UI/CM reopen helpers, `xdg-screensaver`, both `xrandr` families, `w`, `systemctl`, `pkcheck`, the generic
    same-executable launcher, FUSE unmount, and the feature-inert Linux native-codec check source path. The FUSE
    mount path alone passes `[child_socket.as_raw_fd()]`; the parent-side `FD_CLOEXEC` clearing window was deleted.
    The exact service-child disposition model remains local because it has a distinct policy and was not weakened.
  - Added R-S11r, Appendix C #140, R-S11e-32, a focused shell gate, semantic verifier bindings, and source-mutation
    targets for the shared algorithm, ordering, every enumerated helper family, the exact FUSE exception, removal of
    the parent window, both actual-child outcomes, and invalid allowlists. The synchronized requirements SHA-256 is
    `47ac1c117ad103df288091495c4e56b718ae2a6e91ae9720b96ed133fed67450`.
- Verification evidence:

### R-S11e-31 Linux same-executable child descriptor authority — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the launch family before changing it:
  - `src/common.rs::run_me_with_env` resolves `current_exe`, applies explicit environment additions, and directly
    spawns the same executable. It had no Linux descriptor policy. `run_me` delegates to it, so URL, tray,
    whiteboard, and connection-manager consumers shared that default.
  - This is not a viewer-only convenience boundary. In `src/server/connection.rs`, a root `--server` normally uses
    `run_as_user` for CM, but the deliberately supported headless service route has no active desktop user and takes
    the same-user `run_me_with_env(args, cm_launch_env())` branch. That root/service-owned path therefore sat
    outside the exact service-child closure in R-S11n/R-S11e-28, the enumerated sudo/reopen helper closure in
    R-S11o/R-S11e-29, and the pkcheck closure in R-S11p/R-S11e-30.
  - Linux `execve` preserves descriptors by default and closes only those carrying `FD_CLOEXEC`. The API has no
    deliberate non-stdio descriptor parameter or exception: its complete child authority is the same executable,
    argv, selected environment additions, and stdio. A sensitive file, directory, socket, namespace, or other
    kernel capability lacking close-on-exec could consequently enter the service-owned root CM image; ordinary
    user-owned consumers had the same ambient-authority defect. This is classified as a root-service-to-child
    capability leak on the headless CM route and descriptor hygiene defect elsewhere, not a demonstrated
    promptless ordinary-user-to-root primitive because exploitation requires a sensitive live inheritable
    descriptor at that launch point.
  - Primary contracts checked: Linux `execve(2)` documents that descriptors remain open by default except those
    marked close-on-exec; Linux `close_range(2)` documents `CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC` as the pre-exec marking mechanism;
    Rust `CommandExt::pre_exec` is the post-fork/pre-exec registration boundary. Sources:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html,
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/close_range.2.html, and
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/unix/process/trait.CommandExt.html#tymethod.pre_exec.
- Implemented one narrow correction:
  - On Linux only, `run_me_with_env` now calls the already-reviewed
    `platform::linux::configure_linux_helper_close_nonstdio_on_exec` before its only spawn. The existing primitive
    resolves the canonical `/proc/sys/fs/nr_open` bound in the parent and uses raw
    `close_range(CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)` with a raw `fcntl(F_GETFD/F_SETFD)` fallback in `pre_exec`.
  - Hook-configuration failure is converted to `io::ErrorKind::Other` with a bounded diagnostic and returned before
    spawn. No child is launched without the policy. Non-Linux behavior is unchanged, and the Linux child still
    receives the same argv, explicit environment additions, and stdio.
  - Added a Linux actual-child regression without root and without test-only `unsafe`. `/bin/sh` opens descriptor 9
    to a unique file and `exec`s the exact Rust test image. The intermediate image refuses to proceed unless live
    `/proc/self/fd` device/inode inspection proves that exact target arrived as fd 9. It then launches the same exact
    test through `run_me_with_env`; the final image enumerates every live descriptor and requires that no descriptor
    number resolves to the target device/inode. Comparing the kernel object rather than fd number prevents a
    close-and-reuse false result.
  - Added R-S11q, Appendix C #139, R-S11e-31, the extracted R-S11e-31 source gate, semantic verifier coverage, and
    two source mutations for removal of the production hook and inversion of the final descriptor-exclusion proof.

### R-D7a/R-T4 Android outgoing-viewer Activity/isolate ownership — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the reported lifecycle failure before changing the ownership surface:
  - Android task removal destroys or stops the Flutter `MainActivity`, but the deliberately persistent controlled-side
    `MainService` keeps the application process and Rust process-static session table alive. That persistence is
    correct for incoming controlled-side availability; it must not implicitly own outgoing viewer sessions created
    by a discarded Flutter engine.
  - The prior JNI teardown was an argument-free global `closeClientSessions()`. It could clear stale state, but it
    encoded no authority for *which* Activity/isolate was being torn down. A delayed `onDestroy()` or
    `onTaskRemoved()` from an obsolete task could therefore drain a replacement Activity's live session. A separate
    check followed by insertion/start would also leave a check/use race across the generation transition.
  - The reported asymmetry is consistent with this topology: file transfer and normal control occupy distinct
    `ConnType` peer sessions, so one path can remain usable while a stale default-control session/handler hangs;
    Android Force Stop works because it finally kills the retained process and all native static state. This is a
    source-supported causal explanation, not a completed real-device reproduction claim.
  - Primary platform contracts checked were Android's Activity lifecycle and overlapping-instance guidance,
    `Service.onTaskRemoved(Intent)`, and Flutter's engine-host cleanup contract:
    https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/activity-lifecycle,
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Service#onTaskRemoved(android.content.Intent), and
    https://api.flutter.dev/javadoc/io/flutter/embedding/android/FlutterEngineConfigurator.html.
- Replaced the global cleanup abstraction with exact owner authority:
  - Every Android `MainActivity` obtains a monotonic native generation before `super.onCreate()` can attach/run its
    Flutter engine. Dart awaits binding of that generation to the isolate-wide UUID before `runApp`; malformed,
    absent, exhausted, second-owner, or stale registration fails closed.
  - Rust stores exactly one current `(generation, isolate UUID)` binding. `session_add_existed`, `session_add`, and
    `session_start_` acquire the current owner's read admission and retain it through handler/table insertion or
    I/O-thread spawn. Generation replacement and teardown take the opposing write lock and retain it through the
    UUID-scoped drain. The lock order is owner lock then session-table/handler locks; no touched path takes them in
    reverse. Consequently an old admission either finishes before replacement and is drained, or is rejected after
    replacement; it cannot land after the replacement drain.
  - `take_all_sessions`/`close_all_sessions` and argument-free JNI/Kotlin close APIs are deleted. The new drain removes
    only handlers for the exact isolate UUID and removes/closes a peer session only when no handler remains.
    Replacement proactively drains the superseded UUID. Exact generation+UUID retirement makes delayed callbacks
    idempotent and ABA-safe.
  - `MainActivity.onStop` records the exact owner as stopped and `onStart` withdraws it. `MainService.onTaskRemoved`
    consumes only stopped owner pairs, while `MainActivity.onDestroy` closes only its own pair. Neither path stops or
    recreates `MainService`, the incoming listener, capture service, or process. A verifier assertion now requires
    exactly one `onStart` and one `onStop`, their owner bookkeeping, begin-before-`super.onCreate`, awaited
    registration/fail-closed handling before `runApp`, exact JNI signatures, UUID-scoped drain, and lock-held
    admission/retirement order.
  - This change is Android-specific. iOS retains the shared next-isolate stale-UUID cleanup and has no Android
    foreground service/task-removal split; desktop keeps its existing per-window/session ownership.
- Verification evidence:
  - `cargo test --offline --locked --lib --features flutter,linux-pkg-config
    mobile_session_lifecycle_tests` passed in the existing non-root, network-disabled `rd-devcheck` container: four

### Android mobile OS-key signed-artifact binding — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the packaging gap before changing it:
  - `MainApplication.onCreate()` obtains `MobileAtRestStorageKey.getOrCreate(applicationContext)`, passes the
    resulting 32 bytes through `FFI.setMobileAtRestStorageKey`, and only then calls `FFI.onAppStart`. The JNI
    receiver converts the byte array and installs it only through the length-checked, encrypt/decrypt-self-tested
    `hbb_common::set_mobile_at_rest_storage_key` boundary.
  - `MobileAtRestStorageKey` uses a random 32-byte process storage key, a non-exportable AndroidKeyStore AES-GCM
    wrapping key, app-private `SharedPreferences`, a synchronous durable commit, and a post-commit re-read/unwrap/
    equality check. Existing partial or corrupt envelopes return no key. Source assertions covered this model, but
    the final APK had no gate proving R8 retained the bootstrap or that the packaged AArch64 Rust library exported
    the JNI receiver. An older ignored APK demonstrably lacked the new wrapper class and key-install call while
    still containing the rest of `MainApplication`, proving source-only greps could not stand in for packaging
    evidence.
  - The prior log and ledger called the non-StrongBox fallback “TEE.” That was not a valid Android contract:
    declining to request StrongBox still permits an ordinary AndroidKeyStore key whose reported security level is
    software, trusted environment, or StrongBox depending on the device. The implementation requires OS Keystore
    protection; hardware security is defense in depth and its actual `KeyInfo` level remains a device observation.
- Implemented one bounded final-artifact verifier:
  - Added `scripts/verify-android-mobile-key-artifact.py`. It opens the certificate-verified APK without extracting
    attacker-selected paths; rejects duplicate member names, encrypted/symlink target members, noncontiguous DEX
    numbering, and oversized DEX/native inputs; and runs only digest-pinned-image `dexdump` plus image-owned
    `/usr/bin/readelf` against private temporary files.
  - It requires exactly one retained `MainApplication` and `MobileAtRestStorageKey`, proves the ordered
    `Application.onCreate` → wrapper acquisition → JNI installation → `FFI.onAppStart` calls, checks the packaged
    KeyStore/AES-GCM/generation/wrap/unwrap/durable-commit/reread method references and constants, and requires one
    AArch64 dynamic `Java_ffi_FFI_setMobileAtRestStorageKey` export in the APK's exact
    `lib/arm64-v8a/librustdesk.so`.
  - Added narrow R8 keep rules for the two security-critical bootstrap classes so their final structure remains
    inspectable. Wired the verifier beside the manifest verifier during normal signing, the final artifact recheck,
    and `build-android.sh --verify-apk`. The existing source gate now runs the verifier self-test and binds the keep
    rules, both build call sites, pinned tool paths, verify-only content path, exact class/JNI identities, and the
    corrected non-TEE wording.
  - This closes no runtime claim. Android device/emulator Keystore creation, corruption/persistence/restart behavior,

## 2026-07-18 — Mobile at-rest config wrapper OS storage key source slice

- Scope:
  - Continued the R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC hardening loop by addressing the explicit mobile residual in
    HARDENING_STATUS Appendix C #14: mobile encrypted local config was still source-wired to a RustDesk config
    keypair rather than to OS-protected app/device storage.
  - This is a source-level Android/iOS correctness slice. It does not claim Android emulator/device runtime proof,
    iOS build-host proof, or final release artifact proof.
- Pre-change authority finding:
  - `libs/hbb_common/src/lib.rs::at_rest_storage_key()` returned `Config::get_key_pair().1` for Android/iOS.
  - `Config::get_key_pair()` generates and persists the mobile keypair in RustDesk config TOML, so the at-rest
    encryption wrapper was keyed by material that lived with the protected payload. That is not a confidentiality
    boundary against a plain config-file read.
  - `get_uuid()` on mobile was coupled to the same key material path. A correct fix therefore had to separate
    public/stable device-id metadata from secret local-storage wrapping material.
- Implemented correction:
  - Added a mobile-only hbb_common injection seam:
    `set_mobile_at_rest_storage_key(&[u8])` accepts exactly `secretbox::KEYBYTES`, performs an in-process
    secretbox encrypt/decrypt self-test, and caches the key only in memory.
  - Mobile `at_rest_storage_key()` now fails closed unless that injected OS key has been installed. It no longer
    mints or reads the config keypair as the primary encryption key.
  - Mobile `get_uuid()` now uses a separate `mobile_device_id()` seam backed by the existing config keypair public
    device metadata, so `main_get_uuid` does not expose the OS storage key.
  - Android app startup now obtains/creates a 32-byte app storage key through AndroidKeyStore AES-GCM wrapping,
    prefers StrongBox when available, stores only the wrapped key and IV in app preferences, requires a successful
    durable `SharedPreferences.commit()`, validates a create/read round trip from the committed values, and injects
    the unwrapped key into Rust before `FFI.onAppStart`.
  - iOS app startup now obtains/creates a 32-byte Keychain item with
    `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, validates a create/read round trip, and injects the key into
    Rust before plugin registration.
  - Existing mobile ciphertext that can only be opened with the old config-keypair path is retained as a
    decrypt-only fallback using `Config::get_existing_key_pair()` and marks the value for rewrap. It does not
    generate a new fallback keypair and does not remain the encryption path for new writes.
  - Added a source gate in `scripts/verify.sh` that fails if the mobile at-rest key path regresses to
    `Config::get_key_pair`, if `get_uuid()` is recoupled to the at-rest key, if Android/iOS app startup does not
    inject before config-facing startup, or if legacy fallback stops being marked for rewrap.
- Verification evidence:
  - In a non-root, network-disabled, source-read-only Docker run, the focused hbb_common password-security and
    pk-fallback tests passed:
    `password_security::test::test_encryption_uses_random_nonce`,
    `password_security::test::test_decrypt_legacy_payload_starting_with_v1_marker`, and `pk_fallback`.
  - The same constrained Docker model passed `cargo check --offline --locked --lib --features linux-pkg-config`.
  - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh`, `git diff --check`, and the isolated new
    `(3b-iii-a1m) mobile at-rest wrapper uses OS-protected storage key` source gate all passed inside Docker.
- Remaining limitations / not claimed:
  - No Android emulator/device validation was run, so actual AndroidKeyStore availability, StrongBox fallback
    behavior on target devices, and Flutter/native startup ordering still need artifact/device proof.
  - No iOS build-host or simulator/device validation was run, so Keychain entitlement/runtime behavior still needs
    Apple-platform proof.

    artifact proof, final exact Debian artifact execution under R-S11c-27, independent R-V3 CPace review, or

    authorization closed.

## 2026-07-18 — R-S11o/R-S11e-29 Linux service-originated helper inherited descriptor authority

- Selected slice:
  - After R-S11e-28 closed exact Linux service-role bootstrap and exact service-child descriptor inheritance, I
    audited adjacent service-originated helper launches that still build generic `Command` values from a root/service
    context.
  - The coherent slice is Linux helper-launch fd hygiene for the sudo environment probe, `run_as_user` sudo/env
    launches, and delayed reopen helpers. This is separate from the exact retained service child and does not claim
    final Debian artifact evidence.
- Old path proven from source:
  - `src/platform/linux.rs` `SUDO_E_PRESERVES_ENV` used `Command::new(&sudo).env(...).args(...).arg(&env).output()`
    without any RustDesk-owned fd policy.
  - `src/platform/linux.rs::run_as_user` used one `Command::new(&sudo_path)...spawn()?` branch for `sudo -E` and one
    mutable `sudo.spawn()?` branch for the `sudo -- env ...` fallback, again without the descriptor pre-exec hook.
  - `schedule_reopen_after_service_stop` and `reopen_after_service_stop` spawned the current executable directly,
    with the default inherited descriptor table.
  - Linux `execve` preserves open descriptors unless `FD_CLOEXEC` is set. Sudo commonly closes descriptors above a
    configured threshold by sudoers policy, but that policy is host-configurable and cannot be treated as RustDesk's
    authority boundary. The resulting class is a privileged-launch/root-to-helper descriptor capability leak, not a
    demonstrated promptless ordinary-user-to-root primitive.
- Intended authority model:
  - Helper images may receive exactly the deliberate argv, environment, and descriptors 0–2 stdio contract. They may
    not receive root/service-open IPC, listener, config, runtime-record, directory, socket, device, or other kernel
    object capabilities through non-stdio fd inheritance. Failure to configure that policy must fail closed or skip a
    nonessential probe.
- Implementation:
  - Added `src/platform/linux.rs::configure_linux_helper_close_nonstdio_on_exec`, which resolves the canonical
    `/proc/sys/fs/nr_open` bound in the parent and registers a Linux `pre_exec` hook that marks every descriptor above
    stderr `FD_CLOEXEC` using the same `close_range(CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)`/raw `fcntl` fallback used by R-S11e-28.
  - The sudo `-E` probe now creates a mutable command, configures the hook before `output()`, logs hook/probe errors,
    and returns `false` on failure.
  - Both `run_as_user` branches configure the hook before `sudo.spawn()?`.
  - Delayed reopen scheduler and child configure the hook before `spawn()`.
  - Added R-S11o and Appendix C #137 to `requirements.html`; added R-S11e-29 to `HARDENING_STATUS.md`.

## 2026-07-18 - R-S11n/R-S11e-28 Linux service-owned inherited descriptor authority

- Slice selected:
  - Coherent Linux service-owned startup descriptor authority slice, recorded as R-S11n, R-S11e-28, and Appendix C
    #136. This follows the previous working-directory slice and does not claim overall R-S11b/R-S11c completion,
    final R-B2 reproducible artifacts, final exact Debian `.deb` lifecycle execution, R-V3 external review, or
    deferred mobile device evidence.
- Relevant defect and threat classification:
  - Linux preserves open file descriptors across `execve` unless `FD_CLOEXEC` is set. The pre-fix exact service-owned
    server path did not close launcher descriptors at service-role entry, and the supervisor-to-child pre-exec path
    did not first constrain every inherited non-stdio descriptor before credential drop.
  - A pre-fix current debug-binary probe launched the exact service-owned child with fd 198 open to a root-owned
    mode-0600 file and observed the live process retaining that descriptor:
    `PRE_FIX_INHERITED_FD=present pid=10 fd=198 target=/tmp/inherited-authority parent_fd_flags=0`.
  - This proves a real capability leak at the supported manual/supervisor boundary. It is not evidence that an
    ordinary user can force a correctly configured privileged launcher to admit an arbitrary descriptor. The issue is
    classified as a privileged-launch confused deputy and root-to-child descriptor-capability leak, not a demonstrated
    promptless local privilege escalation.
  - Primary contracts checked and consumed for the design:
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html,
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/close_range.2.html,
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html,
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/unix/process/trait.CommandExt.html, and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal-safety.7.html.
- Implemented authority model:
  - Exact Linux service-owned roles preserve only descriptors 0, 1, and 2 as the deliberate launcher I/O contract.
    Before cwd, global, custom-client, config, IPC, or network initialization, the supervisor and final service-owned
    child close every non-stdio descriptor and fail closed on an unremovable live descriptor.
  - The child pre-exec hook marks every non-stdio descriptor close-on-exec before setgroups/setresgid/setresuid. Only
    the already opened, identity-checked executable descriptor is cleared in the forked child, so `/proc/self/fd/N`
    can be executed; the final image closes that descriptor during parent-liveness proof and then performs the same
    general non-stdio close.
  - The parent descriptor table is not mutated by the pre-exec policy. The fallback paths use raw syscalls and a

### R-S11e-26 Linux service-child environment authority — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the service-child launch authority before changing it:
  - `src/platform/linux.rs::try_start_server_` accepted `Option<&Desktop>`. `Some(desktop)` simultaneously meant
    “drop to this active user” and “use this desktop snapshot,” while `None` simultaneously meant “retain the root
    service principal” and “there is no selected desktop.” This coupled two independent security decisions.
  - The root/login-screen service loop already held the refreshed, selected `Desktop`, but called
    `start_server(None, ...)` and discarded it. The root launch branch called `env_clear()` and then copied ambient
    supervisor `DISPLAY`, `XAUTHORITY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `TERM`,
    `PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC`, and `PIPEWIRE_LATENCY` into the child. `set_x11_env` also mutated the long-lived
    supervisor's process-global X11 environment as a handoff, and the terminal fallback consulted ambient
    `TERM`/`TMUX`/`STY`.
  - A manual/sudo or non-systemd privileged launcher that retained caller-selected variables could consequently
    select display, local IPC, or audio/parser endpoints consumed by the root child. This is classified as a
    privileged-launch environment confused deputy and endpoint/parser-exposure defect, not promoted to a demonstrated
    promptless standard-user-to-root primitive: practical exploitation still requires a privileged launch path that
    admits hostile environment state.
  - Primary contracts checked were Rust `Command::env_clear`, Linux `execve(2)`, and the X.Org `DISPLAY` and
    `XAUTHORITY` contracts:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Command.html#method.env_clear,
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html,
    https://www.x.org/archive/X11R6.7.0/doc/X.7.html, and
    https://www.x.org/archive/X11R7.5/doc/man/man7/Xsecurity.7.html.
- Implemented one bounded, service-owned launch model:
  - Added typed `ServiceChildPrincipal::{RootService, ActiveDesktopUser}` and made a selected `&Desktop` mandatory
    for both variants. Principal selection now controls only the credential drop; it cannot erase the session
    snapshot. Both service-loop branches pass their refreshed desktop explicitly.
  - The existing `env_clear()` remains the single inheritance boundary. Root `HOME` is independently derived from
    the effective uid's passwd record. The active-user path retains its already validated UID/GID/supplementary-group
    drop and exports only its account-derived identity/home/runtime values. X11, Wayland, and D-Bus selectors are
    copied only when nonempty and only from the selected desktop object.

    observation constrained by the existing allowlist or the fixed `xterm-256color`/`xterm` capability fallback.
  - Added normative R-S11l, Appendix C #134, the R-S11e-26 ledger entry, and a mandatory verifier gate. The gate

  - Extended the actual-binary lifecycle fixture with hostile supervisor HOME/XDG, X11, Wayland, D-Bus, terminal,

### R-S11e-27 Linux service-owned working-directory authority — 2026-07-18

- Reconstructed the inherited-path authority before changing it:
  - Rust `Command` inherits its parent's working directory unless `current_dir` is set. Linux resolves relative
    paths from cwd, inherits cwd across `fork`, and retains it across `execve`. The service supervisor normalized
    neither its own cwd nor the child command's cwd, so manual/sudo/init launch context remained an input to every
    later relative-path consumer in both processes.
  - `load_custom_client()` additionally preferred `./custom.txt` under `debug_assertions` and returned whenever the
    cwd file was readable, even if signature decoding failed. The executable-relative sidecar was then suppressed.
    This branch was absent from release builds, and an ordinary attacker cannot forge the required RustDesk Ed25519
    signature. The finding is therefore a debug/manual privileged-launch identity/namespace confused deputy and
    future-relative-path authority defect, not a demonstrated production-release exploit or promptless local
    privilege escalation. Signature authenticity and deployment-path selection are separate authorities: a valid
    signed payload can select `APP_NAME` before Linux service config and IPC namespaces are derived.
  - Every shipped manager template already normally selects `/` (systemd default, SysV `--chdir /`, OpenRC
    `directory="/"`, runit/manual `cd /`), but product correctness must not rely on every direct launcher preserving
    that convention.
  - Primary contracts checked were Rust `Command`/`current_dir`, Rust `set_current_dir`, and Linux `chdir(2)`:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/process/struct.Command.html,
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/env/fn.set_current_dir.html, and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/chdir.2.html.
- Implemented the smallest role-confined correction:
  - Deleted the debug cwd sidecar override. `load_custom_client()` now derives the optional `custom.txt` only from
    an absolute `current_exe()` path, retaining the existing macOS `../Resources` mapping. Mobile embedding's
    explicit in-memory signed payload path is unchanged.
  - Exact Linux `--service` and `--server --service-owned-server` roles set cwd to `/` after child-parent liveness
    validation and before `global_init()` or custom-client loading. Failure logs the authority error and exits 1.
    Ordinary viewer/UI/CLI and user-owned `--server` roles retain caller-owned cwd semantics.
  - `try_start_server_()` independently specifies `Command::current_dir("/")` before `env_clear()` and spawn, so
    the local child-launch API no longer carries an inherit-parent default.
  - Added R-S11m, Appendix C #135, R-S11e-27, a focused path-derivation test, a fail-closed source/order gate, and
    semantic workspace-verifier coverage. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `c452cbea6cd7850038b69de9b8dbe6dcd93e6a7f72de7710abf626eaf6d5774a`, synchronized in both ledgers.
  - Extended the actual-binary service fixture to start normal, hostile-record, recovery, forced pre-pidfd, root,
    and active-user roles from a UID-4000-owned mode-0700 directory containing malformed `custom.txt`. It reads
    exact live supervisor/child `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, requires `/`, and rejects the custom-parser diagnostic that would
    prove the hostile cwd file was consumed. The top-level smoke gate requires the exact result marker.
- Verification evidence:
  - The focused Rust regression `common::tests::custom_client_config_is_executable_relative` passed in a non-root,

## 2026-07-19 — R-S11e-42 Linux selected X11 session display authority

- Selected exactly one coherent continuation slice after reconciling the current requirements, hardening ledger,
  Linux desktop/session call graph, strict loginctl fixtures, and clean `master`: X11 DISPLAY endpoint authority and
  its associated XAUTHORITY credential hint. The already-closed IPC checklist was not reopened. Overall hardening
  remains active; the exact cold R-B2 artifact transaction, final exact Debian-artifact execution under
  R-S11c-27, native Apple/Windows evidence, real-device Android lifecycle/storage evidence, and independent R-V3
  review remain outside this source slice.
- Proven old path and authority model:
  - `Desktop::refresh` selected one exact active logind session ID, UID, username, seat, and protocol through the
    typed R-S11z boundary. `Desktop::get_display_x11` then discarded the session ID and searched loose same-UID
    process-name matches for DISPLAY. If absent, it parsed the third whitespace field of fixed-path `w` output,
    scanned the global `/tmp/.X11-unix` namespace, and finally invented `:0`; hostname and `localhost` text were
    stripped afterward.
  - The socket helper sorted Xn sockets, preferred the first socket owned by the selected user, but deliberately
    returned the last socket owned by somebody else when none matched. The positive
    `r_s11c10_x11_socket_display_discovery_reads_metadata` regression explicitly required a missing username to
    receive another owner's `:7`.
  - Xauthority discovery separately accepted the first named-process XAUTHORITY without proving that the same
    process's DISPLAY described the selected endpoint, then accepted a same-UID Xorg `-auth` argument without tying
    that Xorg server to the chosen display. Endpoint authority and a display-specific credential were therefore
    selected through independent heuristics.
  - The intended model is exact-session and fail closed: the already-selected logind object alone identifies the
    X11 endpoint. A selected-UID process may suggest only a credential file, and only when DISPLAY and XAUTHORITY
    come from the same process image and the validated local displays identify the same numeric X server. Optional
    screen suffixes do not identify different servers.
- Primary contract research and risk assessment:
  - systemd 252 `loginctl(1)` documents `show-session`, property selection, and machine-readable status behavior:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/loginctl.html.
  - The systemd 252 login1 interface exposes a read-only session `Display`; graphical session creation supplies the
    value and only the session controller may call `SetDisplay`:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/org.freedesktop.login1.html.
  - Pinned systemd source maps the D-Bus property directly to `Session.display`, saves/loads the exact value, and
    obtains the initial graphical value from PAM_XDISPLAY:
    https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v252/src/login/logind-session-dbus.c,
    https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v252/src/login/logind-session.c, and
    https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v252/src/login/pam_systemd.c.
  - The X server manual defines `/tmp/.X11-unix/Xn` only as the Unix socket for display number n. X/Xauth
    documentation makes DISPLAY the endpoint and XAUTHORITY an optional credential-file selector defaulting to
    `$HOME/.Xauthority`, whose records are display-specific:
    https://www.x.org/archive/X11R7.5/doc/man/man1/Xserver.1.html,
    https://www.x.org/archive/X11R7.0/doc/html/X.7.html, and
    https://www.x.org/archive/X11R6.7.0/doc/xauth.1.html.
  - The old behavior is classified as deterministic cross-session/cross-owner endpoint confusion and a conceptual
    privileged-local-endpoint confused-deputy path when a service child remains root. Source review did not prove a
    promptless ordinary-user-to-root exploit: the ordinary selected-user child drops to that UID, same-UID process
    state is not a stronger principal, and root code execution would still require an additional reachable X-client
    defect or privileged root-session precondition. It is not evidence that this host was compromised.
- Implemented the smallest closed authority model:
  - Added enumerated `LoginctlProperty::Display` and `get_x11_display_of_session`, which queries only the exact
    selected session through the environment-empty/status-checked helper. A strict parser accepts only local
    `:<u32>[.<u32>]` and canonicalizes decimal components. Empty, malformed, hostname-qualified, remote, or
    unavailable values produce no DISPLAY.
  - `Desktop::get_display_x11` now performs only that exact query. The same active X11 session requeries Display and
    refreshes Xauthority, so temporary absence or controller-authorized change recovers without stale state.
  - `xauthority_from_environ_for_display` reads DISPLAY and XAUTHORITY from the same process environment, validates
    both the observed and selected display as local, compares the numeric server while treating screen suffixes as
    equivalent, and accepts only a nonempty absolute control-free credential path. Discovery remains selected-UID
    only. The selected-UID GDM runtime file remains the sole explicit fallback; otherwise no override is passed and
    Xlib uses the selected account's HOME default.
  - Deleted process/w/socket/hostname/:0 endpoint inference, the fixed w candidates/resolver, cross-owner socket

## 2026-07-19 — R-S11e-45 Linux remaining current-image process-table lifecycle authority

- Selected the final remaining Linux current-image lifecycle consumer after re-reading the active requirements,
  hardening ledger, service loop, server/tray dispatch, adjacent R-S11e-43/R-S11e-44 closures, and the persistent
  scope constraints. The exact cold R-B2 release transaction, final exact Debian-artifact execution under
  R-S11c-27, native Apple/mobile evidence, and independent R-V3 review remain outside this source slice.
- Proven old authority:
  - `get_cm()` enumerated all `/proc/<pid>/exe` objects equal to the current service image and accepted an exact
    displayed `--cm` argument as connection-manager state. Any local user can execute the genuine installed image
    with caller-selected argv. Keeping that presentation alive suppressed the inherited hourly restart; making it
    disappear after observation could drive the 60-second delayed restart branch.
  - Every Linux `--server` called `stop_tray_processes()`, which rediscovered every current-image process displaying
    exact `--tray` and issued SIGTERM with the server's UID/capability authority before starting a replacement.
    Active-user children ordinarily carried same-UID authority; a root headless child could carry machine-wide
    signal authority. Executable equality plus displayed argv did not establish parentage, ownership, generation,
    or a retained process object.
  - Linux documents `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` as process-controlled presentation, `execve(2)` accepts caller-selected
    argv, and `kill(2)` applies sender UID/capability permission:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_cmdline.5.html,
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html, and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/kill.2.html.
  - The finding is concrete ordinary-user-triggerable service restart-state spoofing/availability plus conceptual
    privileged or same-principal global-signal confused-deputy authority. It is not evidence of host compromise or
    a promptless privilege escalation: affecting restart timing or terminating a selected process does not itself
    grant root execution.
- Implemented the smallest closed lifecycle model:
  - Deleted `get_cm`, the current-image enumerator/path comparator/exact-argument authority helpers, raw numeric
    signal wrapper, tray cleanup API and call, and the `cm0`/`last_restart` 60-second/one-hour branch. The branch's
    own SpotUdp/DNS rationale belonged to the already-excised rendezvous topology; the direct listener owns its
    bounded bind retry.

    `should_start_server` independently observes exit through the retained exact `Child`; explicit service shutdown
    continues to drain that exact child.
  - Linux `--server` still starts the current image with exact `--tray`. The existing `--tray` receiver performs its
    same-UID singleton check; a new candidate exits if a tray already exists, and the server signals no pre-existing
    process.

## 2026-07-20 — direct-only viewer transport-state finality

- Scope and open-checklist discipline:
  - Selected one coherent viewer-side correctness slice from the still-open cross-platform audit: prove whether the
    direct-only fork retained a relay decision after transport selection and whether that stale state could affect
    login or reconnect behavior. The exact clean R-B2 transaction, current Windows/macOS/Linux artifacts, Android
    R-B10 artifact proof, the real-device connect → swipe-away → relaunch → reconnect scenario, and external R-V3
    review remain open. This slice is not claimed to complete those items.
  - This is independent of the already-implemented Android mobile-isolate/session-owner drain. It neither diagnoses
    the operator's observed foreground-service hang as this quality-policy defect nor claims the real-device Android
    lifecycle scenario is proven.
- Proven defect and authority model:
  - `Client::_start` had already made the only permitted transport decision—direct TCP—and returned a hardcoded
    `direct=true` discriminator. `start_with_port_forward_target` keyed the stream and proactively called
    `send_login` before the outer I/O loop copied that boolean into `LoginConfigHandler.direct`.
  - `LoginConfigHandler::get_option_message` therefore observed `direct == None` during the real login-construction
    boundary and applied inherited relay caps: custom image quality above 100 fell back to 50, and Flutter custom FPS
    above 30 fell back to 30. The stale choice also survived in constructor tuples, the `Interface` trait, FPS
    control, session/reconnect FFI, authored/generated Dart, and the web bridge. Early reset retry used receiver-owned
    first-message state but was named and partly expressed as a relay retry.
  - Correct authority is final before login: the constructor returns one already-keyed direct `Stream` plus the
    fixed `TCP` display label; no later layer receives authority to reinterpret it as relay/unknown. Quality and FPS
    are consequently unconditional direct-only policies. Reset retry depends only on whether the receiver has seen
    its first peer message. A future relay would require a new transport/threat-model design rather than a dormant
    compatibility boolean.
- Privilege and security disposition:
  - The affected path is an initiator/viewer state handoff and UI/FFI API. It does not invoke a privileged helper,
    service-control endpoint, setuid executable, root-owned configuration writer, firewall tool, container runtime,
    or host network mutation. The stream remains CPace-keyed and the existing secured-stream assertions remain at
    both connection and port-forward handoffs.
  - No authentication bypass, network-egress addition, incoming-listener change, privilege escalation, remote root
    trigger, exploitation, compromise, or evidence of compromise was found in this slice. Appendix C #176 records
    it as a cross-platform correctness/state-coherence defect. Android is affected by the same viewer API and
    pre-login policy, but the defect is not Android-only and is not itself the foreground-service ownership bug.
- Source closure and regression binding:
  - Removed the discriminator and dead rendezvous feedback/update tuples at their constructor source; removed
    force/direct state from login configuration and `Interface`; simplified FPS control to its direct coefficient;
    and removed relay arguments from Rust session creation/reconnect, authored Dart, web Dart, and regenerated FRB
    ABI shape. `check_if_retry` now names its input `before_first_peer_message`, and the session supplies `!received`.
  - Added focused tests for uncapped custom quality before the I/O loop (and custom FPS under the Flutter feature)
    and opposite reset-retry outcomes across the first-peer-message boundary.
  - The supported CLI feature exposed two pre-existing compile/API failures while verifying the constructor change:

    command, added `_FUSE_COMMFD`, and spawned it without clearing the desktop process environment, fixing CWD, or
    closing stdin. `fixed_fusermount_unmount` likewise executed the fixed helper with ambient environment/CWD/stdin.

    mounts: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/fusermount3.1.html

    `/bin/mount` and `/bin/umount` children with an empty environment:

    defense and was not treated as the application authority model.

## 2026-07-20 — runtime-smoke container image/network/dependency authority

- Selected one coherent still-open harness-authority slice after re-reading the binding prompt, AGENTS.md,
  R-S11/R-S11a/R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19, Appendix C #25-#29, the live smoke scripts, and the existing
  workspace semantic/mutation validator. A suspected direct Windows-terminal pipe issue was disproved: its current
  listener already has first-instance/local-only creation, explicit SYSTEM plus exact-logon-SID directional DACLs,
  exact launched-PID binding, and principal revalidation. No source change was made there.
- Proven old smoke-harness path and impact:
  - `BUILD_RUN` and ordinary `RUN` omitted a network selection. Docker therefore attached them to the default
    bridge, providing outbound connectivity and reach to host/peer services. Lifecycle, PID-reuse, and sibling
    containers were already network-none.
  - All five run sites named mutable `rd-devcheck` without `--pull=never`; Docker's default `missing` pull policy
    permitted implicit acquisition if the tag was absent. The sole Cargo build lacked `--locked --offline`, and
    ordinary runtime stages unnecessarily mounted the mutable registry cache.
  - The old harness did not contain `-p`/`--publish`, and its bind shim rewrote only the tested
    `0.0.0.0:21118` bind to container `127.0.0.1:21118`. Docker blocks unpublished ports from outside the host by
    default. The defect was therefore ambient harness egress/host/peer reach plus implicit image/dependency
    acquisition—not public DMZ port exposure, a host RustDesk/service/config modification, privilege escalation,
    or evidence of compromise.
- Primary platform/tool contracts used:
  - Docker's none-network driver supplies only container loopback and completely isolates the networking stack:
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/none/.
  - Docker's networking overview documents default bridge attachment and outbound/peer connectivity when no
    network is selected: https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/.
  - Docker's port-publishing contract distinguishes unpublished container ports from explicit `-p` publication:
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/port-publishing/.
  - Docker run defaults image pulling to `missing`; `--pull=never` disables that fallback:
    https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/.
  - Cargo documents `--locked` as requiring the existing lock resolution and `--offline` as prohibiting network
    access: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-build.html.
- Implemented the smallest fail-closed authority model:
