    `sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal>` ID, marks it immutable, and uses only that ID at every run site.
  - Build, ordinary runtime, lifecycle, PID-reuse, and sibling launches all use `--network none` and
    `--pull=never`. No launch publishes a port, selects host networking/PID or privileged mode, or mounts the Docker
    socket. Container loopback remains available for the same-container listener/protocol/capture stages.
  - The build keeps read-write source plus explicit registry and Git caches and runs the sole Cargo build as
    `--locked --offline`. Ordinary runtime no longer receives a dependency cache; all non-build stages keep the
    source read-only. Existing lifecycle capabilities and root service semantics remain unchanged because they are
    the behavior the release smoke tests.

    forbidden host/publication/socket authority, cache separation, and locked/offline Cargo. Deliberate mutations
    cover every launch class, tag reuse, missing image validation, additional launches, port/socket authority,
    cache drift, Cargo drift, and normative/ledger/gate synchronization.

## 2026-07-20 — Windows token-switched helper environment finality

- Selected one coherent Windows LocalSystem-to-user helper-launch slice after re-reading the binding prompt,
  AGENTS.md, R-S11/R-S11a/R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19, Appendix C #25-#29, the current hardening ledger, the full
  typed helper call graph, the native process launcher, and the existing R-S11c-15/R-S11e-35 closure. The remaining
  top-level release checklist still requires exact clean R-B2 artifact execution, native mobile/Apple/Windows
  evidence, and independent R-V3 review; none is claimed here.
- Proven old path and impact:
  - The LocalSystem server launches `WindowsUserHelperLaunch::{Tray, ConnectionManager, Whiteboard}` through
    `run_user_helper` → `run_current_exe_in_current_session_with_env` →
    `launch_process_in_session_with_env(..., as_user=TRUE, ...)` → native `LaunchProcessWin`.
  - `LaunchProcessWin` called `CreateEnvironmentBlock(&lpEnvironment, hToken, TRUE)` and ignored its Boolean
    result. Microsoft's contract defines `bInherit=TRUE` as inheritance from the current process, so the target-user
    helper incorporated the LocalSystem service's ambient environment. The API's false result was not terminal.
  - CM/whiteboard then merged their two launcher-proof variables with a null base if construction failed. Tray has
    no extra variables and therefore passed null to `CreateProcessAsUserW`; Microsoft documents that a null
    environment makes the child inherit the calling process environment and that `CreateProcessAsUserW` does not
    automatically adjust the environment for its token.
  - `git blame` attributes the inherited `as_user`/environment-construction block to the initial upstream import
    `c2abd3b3`; later application-path, token-source, helper-proof, and environment-merge hardening did not alter the
    inheritance flag or make construction status authoritative. This slice closes that surviving upstream behavior
    rather than attributing it to smoke testing, Docker, or a host-side action.
  - This was a real service-to-lower-authority environment-origin defect that could disclose service-owned ambient
    configuration/secrets or select the wrong profile/config namespace. The explicit current-image path, current
    directory, retained active-user token, disabled handle inheritance, helper proof protocols, and token principal
    did not change. This is not proof of caller-selected execution, a SYSTEM shell, exploitation, host compromise,
    or any host RustDesk mutation.
- Primary platform contracts used:
  - Microsoft `CreateEnvironmentBlock`: `bInherit=TRUE` inherits the current process environment; false disables
    that inheritance; the Boolean result reports success/failure and failure is described by `GetLastError`:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/userenv/nf-userenv-createenvironmentblock.
  - Microsoft `CreateProcessAsUserW`: null `lpEnvironment` inherits the calling process environment, and the API
    does not modify an environment block for the supplied token, making preparation/passing the caller's duty:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessasuserw.
- Implemented the smallest fail-closed authority model:
  - Every `as_user` launch constructs exactly one environment for the retained target-user token with inheritance
    disabled. A false result immediately records `GetLastError`, closes the token, restores that error, and returns
    before merge, process-attribute work, or `CreateProcessAsUserW`.
  - A nominally successful null block closes the token and returns `ERROR_INVALID_DATA` at the same boundary. A
    null/caller/LocalSystem environment is no longer a token-switched-helper fallback.
  - The existing case-insensitive merge remains the right abstraction for CM/whiteboard: it removes same-name user
    profile entries before adding launcher-owned proof variables, sorts the block, and passes the exact Unicode
    result. Tray receives the successfully created unmodified target-user block.
  - The distinct `as_user=FALSE` LocalSystem service-owned child is unchanged and still receives only its explicit
    supervisor PID and creation-time variables. No new environment abstraction, dependency, token path, or process
    surface was added.
  - Added R-S11ay, Appendix C #173, and R-S11e-65. Extended the existing independent workspace semantic validator
    and source-mutation inventory rather than adding a duplicative parser. It binds the one construction site,
    non-inheritance, error preservation, abort-before-launch, null rejection, merge/use order, and
    requirement/Appendix/ledger/gate presence. Deliberate mutations cover inherited construction, inverted/ignored
    result handling, lost error capture, fallthrough after failure, null acceptance, launch-time null replacement,
    and every documentation/gate binding.
  - Requirements SHA-256 is `0987d7dc79223643010efc6aa9a7777bb3ef8948efd4816cf46da477414b78ef`,
    synchronized in `HARDENING_STATUS.md` and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`.

## 2026-07-19 — Linux protected-service permit-owned identity admission

- Selected one coherent R-S11b/R-S11c continuation after re-reading the binding prompt, AGENTS.md, the exact
  R-S11/R-S11a/R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19 and Appendix C requirements, the complete current ledger section, the
  protected Unix IPC worker, Linux peer authorization, and the root supervisor's active-desktop cache. The remaining
  top-level release checklist still requires exact clean R-B2 artifact execution, final Debian lifecycle evidence,
  native Apple/iOS and Android device evidence, and independent R-V3 review; none is claimed here.
- Proven old path and attribution:
  - Both accepted protected Linux endpoints called the service-scoped authorization snapshot before acquiring the
    generic or password transaction semaphore.
  - The snapshot unconditionally called `active_uid_fresh`; on Linux that bypasses the service-loop cache and reaches
    the fixed `loginctl`/login1 subprocess/D-Bus boundary synchronously as root.
  - The sockets deliberately accept local connection attempts before kernel-UID/executable authorization. An

    Windows, and macOS peer authenticators already require the complete role shape.

    with arbitrary extra arguments selected service-owned configuration, IPC, credential-replica, SAS, terminal, and
    helper policy. Windows bootstrap repeated a broad marker search for its machine configuration root.
  - A naive exact boolean would have introduced a downgrade: malformed marker-bearing `--server` invocations would
    be treated as ordinary servers. The design therefore needed an explicit malformed state and entry rejection.

    exact peer proofs did not tighten this current-process half. This was deterministic role/configuration confusion

    arguments: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/env/fn.args.html and

    https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html.
  - Microsoft defines the `CreateProcessW` command-line/child argument parsing boundary:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw.

    remain `Absent`. The shared boolean helper now admits only `Exact`.

    config-root selection, Windows bootstrap, or dispatch, preventing ordinary-role downgrade.
  - Windows bootstrap consumes argument-one `--service` or the shared exact-child predicate, with write authority

  - `start_os_service()` nevertheless chose `RootService` with `desktop.username == "root" ||
    desktop.is_login_wayland()`. The literal name, not the already-validated UID, decided whether the child retained
    root. `try_start_server_()` also accepted a caller-supplied `ServiceChildPrincipal` enum.
  - `ServiceChildCredentials::resolve()` correctly refuses UID 0 on the active-user path. Consequently, a UID-0
    account renamed to anything other than `root` was routed to that path and deterministically denied service. An
    internally inconsistent selected record containing username `root` plus a nonzero UID selected the no-drop root
    path instead; the active-user passwd UID/name cross-check never ran there.

    hardening change.

    name, seat ID, and object path, and defines a session's `User` property as its Unix UID:
    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/252/org.freedesktop.login1.html.
  - Linux `getuid(2)` defines `geteuid()` as returning the calling process's effective user ID:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/geteuid.2.html.
  - Linux `credentials(7)` defines user identities as integers and effective IDs as the kernel permission authority:
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/credentials.7.html.
  - Classification: concrete deterministic UID-0 service availability plus conceptual privileged child-principal
    confusion. This is not evidence of host compromise or demonstrated ordinary-user promptless LPE: the selected
    record comes from trusted local logind, and forging an inconsistent UID/name pair requires prior root or OS-service
    integrity failure.

## 2026-07-19 — R-S11e-46 Linux privileged service-to-tray boundary

- Selected one coherent continuation slice after re-reading the binding prompt, AGENTS.md, the exact R-S11/R-S11a/
  R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19 requirements, Appendix C #25–29, the full active hardening checklist, the Linux

- Proven old path and authority model:
  - `start_os_service` chooses `ServiceChildPrincipal::RootService` when the selected desktop username is root or
    when the selected desktop is the GDM Wayland login screen. The child launch correctly clears its environment,
    binds its executable/parent/descriptors, and supplies only fixed process state plus the selected desktop's
    display, Xauthority or Wayland/runtime-directory, and session-bus selectors.
  - Common Linux `--server` dispatch nevertheless always called `check_autostart_config()` and spawned the current
    image with exact `--tray`. For a root service child this created an independent root tray inside the selected
    graphical session. `run_me` did not parent-death-bind that tray, so replacing or exiting the retained server child
    did not retire it.
  - The Linux tray's Open action calls `run_me([])`. Because a child inherits its caller's effective credentials,
    the root tray could create the full no-argument GUI as root. The tray is interactive per-user desktop UI, not a
    controlled-side listener/capture/input requirement.
  - The shared Linux `platform::is_root()` compared `crate::username()` with the literal `root`. The whoami crate
    resolves the effective UID, but a passwd account name is not the privilege identity: UID 0 remains root even if
    its account name is changed or name lookup is otherwise unexpected. A security guard using the old predicate
    would therefore be incomplete.
  - Git blame attributes the unconditional common Linux server-to-tray launch to upstream import `c2abd3b3`; the
    recent fork hardening did not create this topology.
- Primary contract research and classification:
  - Freedesktop's Desktop Application Autostart specification says application autostart occurs during startup of a
    user's desktop environment after login and locates user overrides in the user's configuration home:
    https://specifications.freedesktop.org/autostart/0.5/.
  - Wayland's client API defines `wl_display` as a client connection to the compositor and resolves a relative
    `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` socket beneath `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`:
    https://wayland.freedesktop.org/docs/html/apb.html.
  - Polkit's privileged-execution security notes use a minimal safe environment, omit DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY when
    changing users, and describe retaining them for privileged GUI applications as discouraged legacy behavior:
    https://polkit.pages.freedesktop.org/polkit/pkexec.1.html.
  - X.Org's Xsecurity contract treats Xauthority cookies as display-access credentials; anyone able to read the
    cookie can access the display:
    https://www.x.org/docs/man/man.pdf (Xsecurity(5), pp. 23–25).
  - Classification: concrete promptless service-to-privileged-GUI creation plus unbound privileged-UI lifetime. It
    is not by itself proof of promptless ordinary-user-to-root code execution or evidence of host compromise; an
    additional interaction or reachable GUI/display defect would be required for that stronger claim.

    path can react to a running server.
  - The Linux `--server` arm now checks the same policy before either touching per-user autostart state or spawning
    `--tray`. Non-root portable and active-seat service-owned servers preserve the existing exact tray launch.
  - The Linux `--tray` receiver independently exits 1 for root before its same-UID process discovery and before tray
    construction. This is receiver-side defense in depth against future privileged callers.
  - Replaced account-name root detection with pure `effective_uid_is_root` plus the safe, already-dependent

## 2026-07-19 — Android stopped-Activity outgoing-session ownership resumption

- Selected one coherent continuation slice after re-reading the binding prompt, AGENTS.md, the existing Android
  `MainActivity`/`MainService`/Dart/JNI/Rust ownership path, the current R-D7a/R-T4 verifier, and the tracked Android
  evidence. This slice repairs outgoing client ownership when Android restarts a retained Activity; it does not
  change the persistent incoming controlled-side foreground service.
- Proven old failure path:
  - Each `MainActivity.onCreate()` advanced a process-native generation, and Dart later bound that generation to
    its isolate UUID before starting the UI. This correctly prevented obsolete engines and delayed teardown from
    admitting or closing replacement sessions.
  - A stopped Activity can remain in Android's back stack while another Activity instance advances the native
    generation. Returning to the older instance follows `onRestart()`/`onStart()` without another `onCreate()`.
    The old `onStart()` only removed its stopped marker; it did not reacquire native ownership. Every subsequent
    native outgoing control-session add/start from that isolate therefore failed the owner admission check, while
    unrelated controlled-side service/file paths could continue. Process death/Force Stop appeared to cure the
    failure because it discarded both native process state and the retained Activity/service state.
  - Initial Dart registration logged a false result but still called `runApp`, knowingly creating the same unusable
    UI state when native ownership had already moved.
- Primary platform contracts used:
  - Android documents that a stopped Activity object can remain resident, and returning to it invokes
    `onRestart()` followed by `onStart()` rather than `onCreate()`:
    https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/activity-lifecycle.
  - Android's service contract distinguishes retained service/task callbacks from Activity lifetime and documents
    `onTaskRemoved()` plus `START_NOT_STICKY` semantics:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Service.
  - Flutter documents that `SystemNavigator.pop()` removes the Android Activity from the navigation stack rather
    than terminating the process with `dart:io exit`:
    https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/services/SystemNavigator/pop.html.
- Implemented the smallest lifecycle repair:
  - Added a typed Kotlin/JNI/Rust `resumeClientSessionOwner(generation, UUID) -> generation-or-zero` path.
  - `MainActivity.onStart()` now asks native state to resume its bound isolate. If the UUID is already authoritative,
    native state returns the current generation without draining live sessions; this also makes an interrupted JNI
    response idempotently recoverable. If another isolate owns the process, native state allocates a fresh monotonic
    generation and drains only that displaced UUID's outgoing peer/UI sessions while holding the same owner write
    lock used by admission. Zero, future generations, and malformed UUIDs fail closed.
  - Kotlin replaces its stale generation before marking the Activity started. A failed resume forgets the stopped
    marker and finishes only the stale Activity; it does not stop or reconfigure `MainService`.
  - A false initial Dart binding now awaits `SystemNavigator.pop()` and returns before config synchronization and
    `runApp`, so native fail-closed ownership cannot become a visible but permanently unusable client UI.
  - Added a regression that creates two Activity owners, restores the first, proves its new generation is strictly
    newer, proves the displaced control session is removed/closed, proves admission changed to the restored UUID,
    proves same-UUID stale-generation resynchronization is nondestructive, and proves a future generation is
    rejected. Extended the R-D7a/R-T4 source gate to bind the Kotlin/JNI surface, lifecycle order, Dart exit-before-
    UI order, regression presence, and lock-held resume/drain order.
- Verification evidence:
  - Focused offline Rust test module completed: five tests passed, zero failed, 313 filtered out. This includes the
    restored-Activity regression plus the existing stale-isolate, owner-scoped cleanup, delayed-callback ABA, and
    admission/generation-transition tests.
  - The extracted R-D7a/R-T4 Android client-owner gate passed; `bash -n scripts/verify.sh` passed; `git diff --check`
    passed; focused `rustfmt --check src/flutter.rs` passed.
  - Focused `rustfmt --check src/flutter_ffi.rs` reported only the repository's pre-existing unrelated formatting
    difference at the older `rustdesk_set_mobile_at_rest_storage_key` signature; the new JNI region produced no
    formatting difference and no unrelated formatting edit was made.
  - The broad `scripts/verify.sh` invocation is not counted as green: its workspace self-test first required a

## 2026-07-19 — macOS privileged helper current-build binding

- Selected one coherent continuation slice after re-reading the binding prompt, AGENTS.md, the current normative
  requirements and R-S11b/R-S11c ledger, the macOS install/runtime source, and the surviving private-audit leads.
  The older Windows main-IPC “unbounded” note was closed as stale: commit `57bcb529` already supplies a 256-KiB
  frame maximum, fixed 16-transaction budget, two-second request/response deadlines, and tracked task drain. The
  narrower macOS helper provenance/version-coherence defect remained real.
- Proven old failure path:
  - `is_installed_daemon()` treated two plist files as complete state. Replacing the app could leave the prior
    root-deployed helper indefinitely reported as current, so the existing admin reinstall path was not offered.
  - Installer and runtime checks pinned path, root ownership/mode/ACL, Team ID, and helper identifier, and the
    installer byte-compared against its caller-provided sibling path. They did not bind that input or deployed bytes
    to the helper nested in the currently installed app’s recursively validated outer signature.
  - Any older valid same-Team/helper-ID binary could therefore satisfy the helper-only provenance proof. This was a
    potential downgrade to defects in an older correctly signed helper; it is not evidence that a downgrade,
    privilege escalation, compromise, host service change, or public listener occurred.
- Primary platform contracts used:
  - Apple’s Code Signing Guide documents helpers in `Contents/MacOS` as nested code sealed by the containing app and
    describes recursive nested-code validation:
    https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Security/Conceptual/CodeSigningGuide/Procedures/Procedures.html.
  - Apple’s static-code validation flags define nested-code and all-architecture checks:
    https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/static-code-validation-flags.
  - The Service Management helper-update guidance treats app/helper version coherence as an explicit lifecycle:
    https://developer.apple.com/documentation/servicemanagement/updating-helper-executables-from-earlier-versions-of-macos.
- Implemented the smallest closed current-build authority:
  - `/Applications/<App>.app` is the build authority. Runtime static validation is strict and all-architecture, and
    app-bundle validation recursively checks nested code. Deployed-helper admission additionally requires the full
    existing installed-app trust proof and exact bytes equal to its `Contents/MacOS/service`.
  - Byte equality opens both fixed files with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`, derives regular-file/length metadata from the
    retained descriptors, and compares with fixed 64-KiB streaming buffers. Whole-helper allocation and
    metadata/open symlink races are absent.
  - The admin AppleScript rejects any caller helper path except the fixed installed-app path; pins the outer app’s
    exact Team ID/bundle identifier; verifies the outer app with `--deep --strict --all-architectures`; validates all
    helper copies across every architecture; and immediately before unload/load repeats the app proof and deployed/
    bundled byte comparison. Branded app names rewrite the fixed app template consistently.
  - Service state now requires both plists plus helper equality. A stale helper returns not-current and reaches the
    existing admin-authorized reinstall transaction. Uninstall admission separately detects any managed plist,
    deployed helper, or install-temp artifact so stale/partial state cannot make cleanup unreachable.
  - Added R-S11au, Appendix C #169, R-S11e-61, a focused truth-table regression, shared/Apple source gates, and
    `verify-macos-helper-build-binding.py`. Its final 26-mutation matrix binds nested/all-architecture signatures,
    exact requirements and paths, descriptor-bound no-follow comparison, runtime trust composition, stale-state
    reinstall, partial-state uninstall, and normative/ledger/gate synchronization. Requirements SHA-256 is
    `f2752e7e462ca7d3fecb61739f446a849a2e6c2029f6e7f7b3c8573e47fc9473`, synchronized in both tracked ledgers.

## 2026-07-19 — macOS variadic file-creation ABI

- Selected the concrete Apple compilation blocker left by the preceding helper-binding slice. The current
  R-S11b/R-S11c source checklist is otherwise closed; the remaining clean exact-commit R-B2 cold release
  transaction was not run because the binding prompt excludes a long full release build without explicit approval.
- Primary ABI evidence and complete call-site audit:
  - Apple's open-source XNU `bsd/sys/fcntl.h` declares both `open` and `openat` with an ellipsis:
    https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/sys/fcntl.h.
  - Pinned `libc 0.2.171` defines Darwin `mode_t` as `u16`; its Unix declarations expose `open`/`openat` as C
    variadic functions. Rust E0617 requires a narrow integer to be cast to the compiler-specified promoted C type:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/error_codes/E0617.html. Rust's `VaArgSafe` contract explains that integers smaller
    than `c_int` undergo default promotion and cannot be passed in narrow form:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/ffi/va_list/trait.VaArgSafe.html. The Rust Reference warns that mismatched
    variadic argument types can produce undefined behavior:
    https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/external-blocks.html#variadic-functions.
  - Repository-wide review found exactly three macOS-reachable creation calls passing an explicitly narrow
    `mode_t`: the secure config transaction and the macOS clipboard paste-target and placeholder paths. The
    compiler had already diagnosed the config call as E0617 and recommended `c_uint`.
  - The portable file-transfer helper was already correct: it accepts a typed `mode_t` locally and promotes it to
    `c_uint` at `openat`. The macOS-reachable PID-file `open` call was also already correct because its unsuffixed
    `0o0600` literal is inferred as promoted `i32`. Linux-only creation calls are outside Darwin ABI scope.
    Fixed-prototype `mkdir`, `mkdirat`, and `fchmod` calls correctly retain `mode_t`.
- Implemented the smallest source correction:
  - Changed only the fourth variadic arguments of the three defective `openat(O_CREAT, ...)` calls from `mode_t`
    to `c_uint`. Numeric permissions, `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW` protections, descriptor-bound type
    checks, atomic config replacement, and cleanup behavior are unchanged.
  - Added R-S11av, Appendix C #170, and R-S11e-62. The normative rule distinguishes C-variadic-safe `i32`/`c_uint`
    call shapes from fixed-prototype `mode_t`; it does not impose a blanket filesystem mode rewrite or claim a
    runtime exploit, compromise, host mutation, or completed signed artifact.
  - Added `scripts/verify-macos-variadic-open-mode.py`, shared and Apple gate wiring, and repository-wide verifier
    integration. The focused validator binds all three corrected calls, the two already-correct call shapes,

## 2026-07-19 — Windows production-listener explicit DACL coverage

- Audited every production `new_listener(...)` consumer and the exact Windows postfix-to-DACL classifier. Main,
  user/service password, `_service`, service credential/control/SAS, and `_url` already selected explicit SDDL.
  `_cm` and token-derived `_whiteboard_<32-lowercase-hex>` instead fell through
  `windows_ipc_listener_security_attributes` to `parity_tokio_ipc::SecurityAttributes::empty()`.
- Primary platform evidence and impact classification:
  - Microsoft documents that a named pipe created with null security attributes receives a default descriptor that
    grants read access to Everyone and Anonymous:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/named-pipe-security-and-access-rights.
  - Microsoft also documents that a client may connect to a duplex pipe using read-only access:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/named-pipe-client.
  - The pinned `parity-tokio-ipc` source maps `SecurityAttributes::empty()` to null `SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES` at
    `CreateNamedPipe`. RustDesk's exact process/role/parent checks and bidirectional launch-token HMAC proofs still
    prevented helper authority use. The concrete gap was cross-user pre-authentication availability: an unrelated
    local account able to execute the installed image in exact `--server` role could enter `_cm` and repeatedly hold
    its serial one-second proof wait. This was not an authentication bypass, credential disclosure, privilege
    escalation, remote trigger, host mutation, or evidence of compromise.

    existing protected logon/session-scoped SDDL; an unknown or malformed postfix fails before endpoint creation.

    system-only credential/control/SAS policy remain unchanged.

## 2026-07-22 — protected Windows setup uses the typed Installer API

- Audited the post-UAC Windows setup leg in `libs/portable/src/main.rs`. After extracting the exact one-file
  `rustdesk-installer.msi` manifest into the already-proven Program Files staging directory, the inherited code
  derived a fully qualified, regular, non-reparse System32 `msiexec.exe`, created it through Rust `Command`, waited,
  and accepted only status 0 or 3010. The exact executable/package/argv and protected staging proofs substantially
  constrained the path.
- Primary platform evidence and impact classification:
  - Microsoft documents that child processes inherit the parent environment and current directory by default:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/inheritance.
  - Microsoft documents standard DLL-search exposure to the current directory and `PATH`:
    https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlls/dynamic-link-library-security.
  - The elevated setup originates from a user-selected process location/context, so creating a child carried an
    unnecessary environment/current-directory/standard-handle/lifetime inheritance boundary into the authorized
    per-machine transaction. Source inspection did not prove that a Windows Installer dependency actually resolved
    from attacker-controlled storage, a promptless LPE, exploitation, host compromise, or use of this path. This was
    closed as a conceptual privileged authority surface, not reported as a demonstrated vulnerability incident.
- Implemented the smallest typed in-process closure:
  - Enabled only the pinned `windows` 0.61
    `Win32_System_ApplicationInstallationAndServicing` bindings needed by the bootstrapper.
  - Deleted the System32 discovery helper and protected-leg `msiexec` spawn/wait implementation. The already
    elevated bootstrapper now calls `MsiInstallProductW` with the exact validated MSI path and the sole command-line
    property `REBOOT=ReallySuppress`.
  - Interactive invocations select `INSTALLUILEVEL_DEFAULT`; silent invocations select `INSTALLUILEVEL_NONE`.
    `MsiSetInternalUI`'s exact prior process level is held by a lexical RAII owner and restored on every normal/error
    return.
  - The Installer result is an unsigned status. Only `ERROR_SUCCESS` (0) and
    `ERROR_SUCCESS_REBOOT_REQUIRED` (3010) are accepted; `ERROR_SUCCESS_REBOOT_INITIATED` (1641) remains rejected
    because `ReallySuppress` forbids Installer-initiated restart behavior.
  - This deletes only the bootstrapper-created child. It does not claim that the Windows Installer service or the
    package's declarative/custom-action transaction has no process topology of its own.
  - Added R-S11bu, Appendix C #214, R-S11e-87 shared-gate assertions, and an independent semantic contract with
    deliberate mutations for the Cargo feature, typed call, exact property, both UI branches, prior-level capture,
    RAII ownership/restoration, child-process absence, unsigned status, rejected-status test, shared gate,
    requirement, disposition, hardening entry, and current hash scope.

## 2026-07-23 — Linux live service-child crash recovery requires stable pidfd signaling

- Candidate and authority analysis:
  - Re-read the active R-S11b/R-S11c ledger and traced the durable Linux service-child lifecycle from
    `start_os_service` through lease acquisition, record recovery, process-identity inspection, pidfd opening,
    graceful/forced signaling, stale-record removal, listener creation, and replacement-child launch. Routine
    supervisor-owned stop/restart already retains and signals the exact Rust `Child`; the remaining distinct path was
    recovery after the supervisor died while its durable-record child remained live.
  - The previous unsupported-`pidfd_open` compatibility branch repeatedly compared boot ID, PID/start time,
    executable device/inode, every UID field, exact argv role, and unique generation before raw numeric-PID
    `kill(2)`. Those checks narrowed the target but could not bind the signal across the final check-to-signal
    interval: the checked process could exit and the same integer PID could be recycled before `kill` reached the
    kernel. The source disclosed that race, but disclosure did not make root-originated `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL` correct.
  - Primary Linux authority used for the decision was the official `pidfd_open(2)` and `pidfd_send_signal(2)` API
    contract: a pidfd is a stable reference to the process originally opened, and signaling through it avoids the
    traditional PID-recycling race. The correct local authority model is therefore: crash recovery may signal a
    recorded live child only through an already-opened pidfd; metadata is evidence for accepting that descriptor,
    never a substitute signaling capability. If pidfd is unavailable, an exited/absent record may be removed without
    signaling, while a live, mismatched, or unverifiable record must be preserved and startup must fail before any
    listener or replacement child gains authority.
- Production correction:
  - `src/platform/linux.rs` deletes `send_revalidated_service_child_pid_signal` and
    `wait_revalidated_service_child_pid_exit`, including their raw numeric-PID `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL` call and bounded
    numeric-PID wait loop. The remaining `kill(pid, 0)` probe is classification-only and sends no terminating signal.
  - `PidFdOpen::Unsupported` now dispatches to `handle_previous_child_without_pidfd`. `Exited`/`Absent` removes the
    exact stale record without signaling; `Match`, `Mismatch`, and `Unavailable` preserve the record and return an
    explicit error. Existing service-entry order performs recovery before IPC listener creation or child launch.
  - The behavior is deliberately not a blanket Linux-version rejection. A routine no-record startup does not need a
    pidfd, and ordinary shutdown/restart keeps using the directly owned `Child`. Only crash recovery that would need
    to signal a still-live durable-record target requires stable pidfd authority.
  - The debug-only force hook is renamed to `RD_SERVICE_SMOKE_FORCE_PIDFD_UNAVAILABLE`. Its release-build branch is
    exactly `false`; it can only force the already-existing unsupported classification and cannot bypass identity or
    signaling rules.
- Fixture and source-proof correction:
  - `scripts/smoke-service-lifecycle.sh` replaces the old successful pre-pidfd fallback scenario with an exact-binary
    refusal scenario. It creates one canonical live child/record, forces pidfd unavailability, requires exact process
    status 1 and fail-closed diagnostics, compares complete record metadata and SHA-256 before/after, rejects a
    temporary record, and proves both the exact child and unrelated UID-4000 portable server remain alive. Only after
    those assertions does fixture cleanup remove the exact record and terminate the retained child through its
    descriptor-bound test helper. `scripts/smoke-server.sh` consumes the new
    `SERVICE_LIFECYCLE_PIDFD_UNAVAILABLE_REFUSAL` marker as R-S11c-27u.
  - The shared source gate rejects either deleted fallback symbol, requires the safe state split, release-disabled
    hook, recovery-before-listener order, runtime-fixture assertions, R-S11ca, and Appendix C #220. The independent
    semantic verifier scopes those regions and its in-memory mutation matrix separately rejects weakened status,
    metadata, byte, temporary-path, process-survival, cleanup-order, handler-state, dispatch, release-hook,
    fallback-absence, gate, requirement, Appendix, ledger, and hash-scope contracts.
  - `requirements.html` adds R-S11ca and Appendix C #220. `HARDENING_STATUS.md` marks R-S11c-27k as historical and
    superseded, records R-S11c-27u/R-S11e-93 without claiming current runtime execution, and preserves the historical

## 2026-07-23 — Linux stable-root credential ownership and nondumpable child replica (R-S11cb/R-S11e-94)

- Finding and scope:
  - Traced the complete installed-Linux password path rather than assuming the polkit process was also the storage
    authority. Root `_service_password` authorized the socket-derived caller and then invoked
    `complete_main_password_mutation` with plaintext. The active-desktop `--server --service-owned-server` child
    received that plaintext on raw `_password`; its `spawn_password_mutation` called
    `Config::set_permanent_password_persisted`, so the desktop uid/config root performed the durable machine write.
  - This contradicted R-S11b's enforcement-following-authority model. The replaceable user-session child also held
    the password-equivalent PRS without an explicit final-image nondumpable invariant. Under classic same-uid
    process-inspection rules, another process with that uid could potentially inspect that memory. This is a local
    credential-authority/confidentiality defect requiring local same-uid process authority, not evidence that memory
    was read, a password was stolen, Docker gained root, a host service/configuration/firewall changed, a public
    listener was created, exploitation happened, or a machine was compromised.
- Primary Linux contracts used:
  - `execve(2)` documents the credential-sensitive dumpability reset and the later exec behavior:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html.
  - `PR_SET_DUMPABLE(2const)` documents explicit dumpability control:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_DUMPABLE.2const.html.
  - `ptrace(2)`, `process_vm_readv(2)`, and `proc_pid_mem(5)` document the relevant ptrace-mode access checks:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/ptrace.2.html,
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/process_vm_readv.2.html, and
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_mem.5.html.
  - Direct inspection of Linux `kernel/ptrace.c` rejected the first proposed `PTRACE_TRACEME` handoff. The sole-tracer
    relationship is enforced by the attach path, while general `__ptrace_may_access` callers do not require the
    reader to be the registered tracer. Root tracing would block a second attach but would not itself close every
    same-uid `/proc/<pid>/mem` or cross-process-memory path while exec had made the child dumpable:
    https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/kernel/ptrace.c.
  - Yama's optional `ptrace_scope` policy is distribution/administrator state and cannot be an application
    invariant: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/LSM/Yama.html.
- Implemented authority model:
  - The stable root supervisor is the sole durable writer. It persists submitted plaintext, reads the resulting root
    PRS tri-state, and sends the exact child only a canonical PRS-or-empty `SensitivePassword` replica under the same
    operation UUID. The child applies only `set_permanent_password_prs_for_runtime`; it never persists the machine
    credential. Canonical validation requires empty or base64 for exactly 32 decoded bytes, and wipes decoded,
    re-encoded, and replaced replica allocations.
  - A separate raw `_service_credential` socket gives startup a bodyless UUID-bound request and exact 44-byte-or-empty
    PRS response. It has an independent capacity-two semaphore acquired before `/proc` identity work. Root proves
    and re-proves the exact child before reading/sending credential state. The unprivileged child does not attempt to
    read protected root `/proc` metadata: it requires kernel socket credentials for uid 0 and a positive peer PID,
    then proves that PID is both its launch-parent marker and actual direct parent. The root independently proves the
    child's exact argv, direct parent, and current generation. The snapshot is installed before any child
    local/public listener, and explicit empty root state suppresses stale user-profile storage. Unavailable,
    malformed, wrong-operation, wrong-peer, or undecryptable state fails startup closed.
  - Root-to-child and child-to-root proofs now require the direct parent PID and current root runtime generation,
    rather than accepting live ancestry alone. Any failure after root durable persistence to extract the PRS or
    converge exact `Applied` child state latches failure and stops the generation for a fresh root-snapshot restart.
  - The rejected ptrace draft is not the production boundary. Final review also rejected making the primary package
    executable mode 0711: doing so would make every ordinary user-launched RustDesk process nondumpable and break the
    existing same-uid `/proc/<peer>/exe` proofs between ordinary RustDesk processes. The corrected package keeps the
    primary UI/service image root/root mode 0755 and adds a separate byte-identical root/root mode-0711
    `rustdesk-service-child` image solely for active-user child exec. Root opens both while privileged, requires the
    fixed primary path, protected child parent, exact ownership/modes/length/bytes, and pins the selected child inode;
    an already execute-only root-owned manual image may use its current inode directly. Root also requires
    `/proc/sys/fs/suid_dumpable` to contain exactly `0`. Linux then preserves nondumpability through the
    unreadable-executable exec transition. The final image first requires initial `PR_GET_DUMPABLE == 0`, reasserts
    `PR_SET_DUMPABLE(0)`, verifies the final state, writes one readiness marker, and stops. Root publishes the exact
    durable child record while stopped and only then sends `SIGCONT`. Root-principal children share the explicit
    nondumpable marker/stop publication boundary. The systemd unit permits neither `ptrace` nor `@debug`; retained
    root `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` is used only for exact nondumpable-child `/proc` proof. The unsupervised recovery fixture is
    debug-only, release-false, and cannot be inherited through the real supervisor's cleared environment.
- Regression enforcement and current confined evidence:

## 2026-07-23 — Linux nondumpable CM/PA exact-parent authority (R-S11cc/R-S11e-95)

- Finding and scope:
  - R-S11cb deliberately moved the active-user installed-service child to a dedicated root-owned mode-0711 image
    and required that final image to remain nondumpable. Its connection manager executes that same image and is
    likewise nondumpable. The retained Linux `_cm` admission path nevertheless tried to reconstruct
    `PeerProcessIdentity` by reading the other same-uid process's `/proc/<pid>/exe`, `cmdline`, and `environ`.
  - Linux gates the `/proc/<pid>/exe` symbolic link through ptrace access checks. The confidentiality boundary added
    by R-S11cb could therefore reject the legitimate nondumpable server/CM pair. Control and audio depend on that CM
    path, while an independent file-transfer path can remain usable, matching the observed split symptom. This was a
    hardening-induced local compatibility and authority-model defect, not evidence of exploitation, a remote
    authentication bypass, Docker root access, a host service/configuration/firewall change, a public listener, or
    machine compromise.
- Primary Linux contracts used:
  - `proc_pid_exe(5)` documents the ptrace read-mode check on `/proc/<pid>/exe`:
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html.
  - `unix(7)` documents Linux peer credentials on connected Unix-domain sockets:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html.
  - `proc_pid_stat(5)` documents the process parent and start-time fields:
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_stat.5.html.
  - `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(2const)` and `execve(2)` define the parent-death and exec behavior used by the existing
    parent-bound child launcher:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html and
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html.
- Implemented authority model:
  - Linux CM/PA flows now use `LinuxProcessIdentity`, containing exactly PID, UID, and process start time. The socket
    supplies PID/UID; `/proc/<pid>/stat` supplies a PID-reuse-resistant start identity. Executable, argv,
    environment, and launch-token fields are deliberately absent from the serialized identity and are not read
    across the nondumpable boundary.
  - The server accepts `_cm` only when the kernel-reported peer is the exact live direct child of the current server
    and has the expected uid. The CM independently requires its launch-parent marker to equal its current kernel
    parent and requires its protected main-IPC peer to equal that parent's PID/UID/start-time identity before
    requesting per-connection authority.
  - The launch-token HMAC remains mutual and is now bound to the exact closed CM role, `--cm` or `--cm-no-ui`; a
    proof generated for one role cannot authorize the other. All Linux CM launches, graphical and headless, now use
    the existing parent-death launcher. Its pre-exec hook arms `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)` and rechecks the captured
    parent, so an orphaned fixed-endpoint CM cannot outlive the server whose authority it carries.
  - The per-connection PulseAudio lease retains only the minimal kernel identity. The server records the exact CM
    child for active audio subscribers and rechecks both process generation and direct parent before minting
    capture authority. The CM-side `_pa` path accepts an external owner only when it is the exact launch parent and
    the exact authenticated main-IPC peer, then validates the random per-connection token through that peer. The
    same-process user-owned voice-call path remains exact-self bound.
  - Incumbent `_cm` probing now requires exact direct-parent identity plus mutual role-bound HMAC. `_pa` probing
    requires exact minimal identity. No same-uid fallback, private-procfs fallback, body-before-proof path, or
    generic configuration authority was introduced.
- Regression enforcement and final confined evidence:
  - Added `scripts/verify-linux-nondumpable-cm.py`, which binds the three-field identity closure, kernel socket
    credentials and start time, exact parent proofs in both directions, role-domain-separated mutual HMAC,

    focused Rust regressions, R-S11cc, Appendix C #222, hardening-ledger identity, and shared-gate wiring. Its
    adversarial self-test rejected all 17 deliberate weakenings.

## 2026-07-23 — Linux nondumpable whiteboard exact-parent authority (R-S11cd/R-S11e-96)

- Finding and scope:
  - The R-S11cb installed-service child deliberately executes through a dedicated root-owned mode-0711 image and
    remains nondumpable. A whiteboard overlay launched by that server executes the same image and inherits the same
    confidentiality boundary.
  - The retained helper-side `_whiteboard_<hmac>` admission first required the socket peer to equal its recorded
    launch-parent PID, then called `ensure_peer_executable_matches_current_by_pid_opt` and the server-role argv
    reader before reaching the mutual launch-token proof. On Linux, `/proc/<pid>/exe` dereference is ptrace-gated.
    The new confidentiality boundary could therefore make the legitimate overlay reject its own nondumpable parent.
  - This is a source-proven hardening-induced local overlay availability and helper-authority incompatibility. It is
    not evidence of exploitation, remote authentication bypass, Docker root access, a host RustDesk
    service/configuration/firewall change, a public listener, or machine compromise. It is separate from the
    originally reported Android stale-background-service symptom.
- Primary Linux contracts and confined reproduction:
  - `proc_pid_exe(5)` documents the `PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS` check on `/proc/<pid>/exe`:
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html.
  - `ptrace(2)` documents denial for a nondumpable target without `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`:
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/ptrace.2.html.
  - `unix(7)` documents `SO_PEERCRED` PID/UID/GID credentials captured for a connected Unix-domain socket:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html.
  - `proc_pid_stat(5)` documents the kernel parent and process start-time fields used without executable, argv, or
    environment recovery:
    https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_stat.5.html.
  - `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(2const)` documents the parent-death behavior reused by the corrected launch:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html.
  - A capability-free reproduction in an already-present container as numeric UID/GID 1000 observed the same-UID
    child `/proc/<pid>/exe`, `cmdline`, and `stat` before `PR_SET_DUMPABLE(0)`. After the transition, `exe` changed
    to `EACCES` while `cmdline` and `stat` remained readable. That directly demonstrates why the old executable
    proof rejects the intended nondumpable topology and why PID/UID/start-time parent identity remains usable.
- Implemented authority model:
  - Linux whiteboard admission now rejects a zero launch parent, requires that immutable launch-parent PID to equal
    the helper's current kernel parent, derives the parent's minimal PID/UID/start-time identity, and requires the
    connected Unix-stream peer credentials plus live start time to equal that exact identity. It answers no HMAC
    challenge before this convergence succeeds.
  - The Linux branch no longer reads the parent's executable, argv, environment, launch token, or other
    ptrace-gated metadata. macOS and Windows retain their existing exact parent PID, current executable, and

## 2026-07-23 — R-S11ce/R-S11e-97: unprivileged Linux clients authenticate the root service without root procfs

- Scope selected from the still-open R-S11b/R-S11c evidence loop:
  - This invocation audited client-side authentication of the installed Linux uid-0 service on the framed
    `_service` liveness endpoint and the raw `_service_password` endpoint.
  - It did not inspect, execute, stop, restart, reconfigure, replace, or otherwise interact with the host RustDesk
    binary/process/service, any host listener, UFW/nftables/iptables, Docker networking, Android/device state, or
    the host's live IPC paths.
- Source finding and security disposition:
  - In parent commit `23a07fa67423345dbd9d37d58cda3f2b195926b3`, both unprivileged client paths first
    connected to the root service socket and obtained its kernel peer identity, but then attempted to read
    `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, dereference `/proc/<pid>/exe`, require exact `--service` argv, and prove root-owned
    executable metadata.
  - That contradicted the already-recorded R-S11i Linux authority model. An ordinary active-user process cannot
    rely on reading ptrace-gated process metadata from the uid-0 service, so the proof could reject the legitimate
    installed service before a generic liveness request or raw password header/body was sent.
  - The extra procfs checks did not provide a meaningful boundary against a process already capable of presenting
    uid 0 on the connected Unix socket. This was a source-level, hardening-induced local availability and password
    provisioning incompatibility. It is not evidence of exploitation, credential disclosure, Docker obtaining
    root, a changed host service/configuration/firewall, a public listener, or machine compromise.
- Primary Linux contracts:
  - `unix(7)` documents `SO_PEERCRED` as the connected Unix-domain socket peer credentials in effect at
    connect/listen/socketpair time:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html.
  - `proc_pid_exe(5)` documents that dereferencing `/proc/<pid>/exe` is governed by
    `PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS`:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html.
  - `ptrace(2)` documents the ptrace access-mode checks underlying protected procfs process metadata:
    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/ptrace.2.html.
- Implemented authority model:
  - `src/ipc/auth.rs` now has one `validate_linux_root_service_peer` decision: kernel peer UID must be present and
    exactly zero, and kernel peer PID must be present and positive.
  - Thin framed and raw wrappers obtain those values from the already-connected stream and call the common
    decision. `src/ipc.rs` invokes the framed wrapper for generic service IPC and the raw wrapper for
    `_service_password` before any endpoint request/header/body is sent.
  - The obsolete Linux root-service argv, executable, file-metadata, parent-metadata, and two client-proof helpers
    were deleted. No compatibility alias or fallback remains.
  - The fixed service pathname and separately hardened root-owned mode-0711 service IPC parent remain intact. A
    non-root pathname squatter fails the connected peer-UID check. A root process able to present uid 0 is already
    inside the root authority boundary.
  - The opposite-direction controls were intentionally not weakened: the root password receiver still proves the
    active/root caller and exact polkit subject before reading a body, and `_service_credential` retains its exact
    direct-parent/current-generation mutual proof.
- Requirements and regression enforcement:

    `93211ba414c616db371c4d2e4cb26f29184bd14825568db2cd0341d72e738678` in
    `requirements.html`, `HARDENING_STATUS.md`, and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`.

## 2026-07-23 — R-D7a/R-T4/R-S11br: exact Android owner policy and the shared verifier agree

- Scope and finding:
  - This invocation returned to the reported Android outgoing-viewer swipe/relaunch lifecycle and audited the
    relationship between the current exact-owner source, the release gates, and the hardening ledger. Runtime
    source was not changed.
  - `src/flutter.rs` correctly implements `AndroidClientOwnerState::resume` as a read-only reconciliation. It
    accepts only a nonzero, non-future generation for the exact current Flutter-isolate UUID and returns the
    authoritative current generation. `resume_android_client_owner` takes the owner read lock and has no
    replacement or session-drain authority.
  - The focused R-S11br verifier and the regression
    `stale_android_activity_cannot_reclaim_the_replacement_owner` correctly bind that policy. A stale Activity
    cannot replace the current isolate, close its sessions, or acquire its owner admission.
  - The older shared R-D7a block in `scripts/verify.sh` still required the deleted regression
    `resumed_android_activity_reclaims_owner_without_reusing_a_stale_generation` and required resume to take the
    write lock, mint replacement authority, drain the displaced UUID, and drop the lock. Those exact assertions
    were absent from the current source, so the broad gate necessarily failed against the secure implementation.
  - The top R-D7a/R-T4 narrative in `HARDENING_STATUS.md` retained the same superseded policy, saying an older
    Activity could allocate a generation and drain a different current owner. The later R-S11br row correctly
    documented the opposite policy. This was a release-gate and binding-ledger contradiction, not a new runtime
    resource defect.
- Historical and platform proof:
  - Git history attributes the mutable takeover implementation and the stale shared-gate assertions to
    `63a1275` (`Resume Android client ownership on restart`).
  - Commit `5868c069a56efaaa0a3c18acc45afbe4512d4893` (`Make Android voice-call audio ownership exact`) intentionally
    changed Rust resume to the current read-only exact-UUID model, added stale-Activity refusal, and updated the
    focused verifier, Kotlin owner state, normative R-S11br requirement, and later hardening row. It missed the
    older shared block and top summary.
  - Android's Activity and Service contracts support treating these as independent lifetimes: a stopped Activity
    can remain resident, Activity destruction is not guaranteed before process death, and a started foreground
    service can keep the application process important. `Service.onTaskRemoved` is a service callback for task
    removal, not an authority-transfer guarantee between arbitrary Activity instances:
    https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/activity-lifecycle,
    https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/process-lifecycle, and
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Service#onTaskRemoved(android.content.Intent).
  - The manifest uses `singleTop`, which does not establish a process-wide single-Activity authority invariant.
    A previous instance that is not at the top can coexist with a replacement; therefore an older Activity must
    fail closed rather than take the replacement isolate's owner.
- Implemented conformance correction:
  - `scripts/verify.sh` now requires `stale_android_activity_cannot_reclaim_the_replacement_owner`.
  - Its exact embedded lifecycle/admission block now requires the resume entry to use

## 2026-07-23 — R-S14/R-S19: exact Android connection type owns capture demand

- Scope selected from the Android resource-ownership follow-up:
  - The parent Android lifecycle/resource topology A–H was already source-closed. This pass re-read the controlled
    connection admission and last-connection teardown path end to end, specifically looking for authority that
    was reconstructed or dropped while crossing Rust, serialized `Client` state, JNI, and the persistent Android
    foreground service.
  - The traced path was `src/server/connection.rs` authorization and `Data::Login` construction,
    `src/ipc.rs::CmAuthConnType`, both `ConnectionManager::add_connection` callers and
    `remove_connection` in `src/ui_cm_interface.rs`, JNI serialization through
    `scrap::android::call_main_service_set_by_name`, and `MainService.rustSetByName("add_connection")`.
  - This was a source/build audit only. It did not inspect or interact with the host RustDesk binary, process,
    service, configuration, IPC path, listener, firewall, UFW/nftables/iptables state, Docker networking, or a
    physical/emulated Android device.
- Exact source finding:
  - The server already resolved every admitted connection to one closed
    `CmAuthConnType::{Remote,FileTransfer,ViewCamera,Terminal,PortForward}` and included that exact enum in
    `Data::Login`.
  - `ConnectionManager::add_connection` discarded the enum while constructing its serialized `Client`.
    Android `MainService` reconstructed the resource class from `is_file_transfer`, `is_view_camera`,
    `is_terminal`, and `port_forward`; Rust's last-live-capture predicate independently reconstructed it from
    three booleans. Both screen-capture predicates omitted PortForward.
  - A password-authenticated port-forward connection could therefore request or reuse a retained
    MediaProjection on Android and could make native teardown retain the capture pipeline after the last actual
    Remote desktop connection disconnected. The parallel fields were valid presentation data, but they were not
    a sound replacement for the already-validated authority enum.
  - This is an R-S14 resource-binding and R-S19 capability-coherence defect. It is not a password/PAKE bypass,
    privilege escalation, public-listener change, container escape, source proof of exploitation, or evidence
    that any host was modified or compromised.
- Correct ownership model implemented:
  - `Client` now carries the exact `ipc::CmAuthConnType`; both desktop IPC and Android in-process login paths pass
    the already-validated enum without reconstructing it.
  - Native Android capture retention is exactly `authorized && !disconnected && conn_type == Remote`.
    FileTransfer, ViewCamera, Terminal, and PortForward are all explicit negative cases in the Rust regression.
  - `ControlledConnectionType.kt` is the one closed Android decoder for the five canonical serde tags. Unknown,
    missing, case-varied, or future unhandled values fail before notification, voice-call ownership, or capture
    demand. There is no permissive default.
  - Android desktop capture is exact Remote-only. Voice-call ownership is exact Remote/ViewCamera-only. File
    notification presentation remains exact FileTransfer-only. `MainService` no longer reads the four parallel
    fields to decide either capture or voice resources.
  - The persistent foreground service remains deliberately persistent. Android documents that a started service
    has a lifecycle independent of the Activity that created it:
    https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services. MediaProjection separately requires callback
    registration before virtual-display creation and exact cleanup when the projection stops:
    https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/projection/MediaProjection.html. The resulting design is
    a persistent service/listener with exact per-connection resource demand, not service termination as a
    recovery mechanism.
- Requirements and regression enforcement:
  - R-S14 now requires the validated `AuthConnType` to cross Rust-to-Android intact, forbids reconstructing Remote
    from parallel presentation fields, and explicitly excludes all four non-Remote modes. Appendix C #205 and the
    R-S14 hardening row record the incomplete earlier classifier and the exact correction without overclaiming
    device evidence.
  - The synchronized requirements SHA-256 is

  - The earlier exact-connection-type fix still allowed an old connection-manager task to compute and deliver a
    detached global `stop_capture` after a newer Remote connection had already requested capture. That ordering
    could leave the persistent service alive with a valid newer Remote session but false capture demand, matching
    the reported screen-control hang/file-transfer success/Force-Stop recovery shape without proving the exact
    device instance.

    change only their exact ID and derive capture demand from the complete set under the same monitor. Capture and
    voice retirement are attempted independently and capture is always reconciled afterward. There is no detached
    global capture-stop command.

    callbacks. JNI refuses callbacks from zero, stopped, or replaced generations before entering Java. Listener
    start binds a generation only after proving that the JNI caller is the exact currently retained `MainService`
    object; exact-generation compare-and-exchange stop prevents delayed destruction of an obsolete service from
    stopping a replacement.

    references. NDK initialization receives only the retained global `applicationContext`, never a JNI local
    reference or a Service object. Exact-object release cannot clear a replacement callback owner.

  Docker client/daemon and cached image namespace, the live source/cache bind mounts, and every containerized

    `ubuntu:24.04` tag; the WiX restore selects mutable `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0`. The former also
    performs a live root `apt-get` inside the producer.
  - No launch currently publishes a port, mounts the Docker socket, or requests a host network/PID/IPC/UTS
    namespace. Its network is intentional outbound acquisition. The concrete defect is root/build-host/cache
    authority and mutable execution identity, not evidence that a host listener was published, a container
    escaped, host root was acquired, or host RustDesk/service/firewall/network state was changed.
  - Every ordinary launch also receives all of `online` writable, and the Gradle warmer receives the live
    repository writable. That separate output/publication authority remains open after the container-execution
    floor and must not be conflated with this slice.
- Implemented source model:
  - One fixed root-owned Docker client, one fixed local Unix endpoint, and one current-user-private empty client
    configuration; reject host/root invocation and caller Docker authority.
  - Every ordinary acquisition producer uses an already present immutable image ID, `--pull=never`, explicit
    bridge networking with no publication or host namespace, a read-only root, the invoking numeric UID:GID,
    all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, and fixed PID/memory/no-swap/CPU/tmpfs ceilings.
  - Mutable compatibility tags and live package installation are not execution authority. A producer whose
    required image has no audited immutable pin must fail closed and require an already captured digest-verified
    output rather than execute the mutable image.
- Primary-source design basis:

    explicit form and `readonly` removes write access, and that containers have no default resource constraints.

    that `-p`/`-P` publish ports. It warns that a published port without a host IP binds all interfaces and can
    bypass UFW; host networking shares the host network namespace.

    bridge egress but forbids every publication and host-namespace form.

  Gradle/Dart code executing in the intentionally networked `stage_gradle` producer.

    `scripts/android-apk-build.sh` from that writable mount.

    `.dart_tool`, plugin metadata, and generated bridge paths. The bind therefore granted the networked producer
    write authority over the whole live checkout, not merely the intended cache outputs.

    with residue possible under the former image-default-root path. No residue was removed or changed.
  - The exact commit tree contains zero symlink, submodule, or special entries. This is source-integrity /
    build-host authority and historical root-owned generated residue, not evidence that a committed input was
    changed, a container escaped, host root was acquired, a listener was exposed, host
    RustDesk/service/firewall/network state changed, exploitation occurred, or the host was compromised.
- Implemented source model:
  - Fix the root-owned Git/tar tools and command path. Use one closed-environment Git funnel with private HOME,
    no system/global configuration, no hooks, no ambient attributes, and no filesystem monitor.
  - Require a clean committed tree, capture its exact commit/tree, reject nonregular/nonexecutable entries, and
    archive that commit into the existing private online-fetch workspace.

    writable copy at `/src`; mount and execute the Android inner program separately from the read-only authority.

    commit/tree/clean/archive identity; then safely retire the exact writable tree.

  the complete `online` offline-input closure and the two legitimate durable outputs, Gradle User Home and the

    package installation therefore also granted write/delete authority over Cargo/Pub state, NDK/vcpkg/native
    trees, toolchain archives, builder archives, and every unrelated offline input.
  - Numeric non-root execution limited the producer to the invoking user's authority but did not make that broad
    bind admissible. This is source-proven input/output-publication authority, not evidence that cached input was
    changed, a container escaped, host root was acquired, a listener was exposed, host RustDesk/service/firewall/
    network state changed, exploitation occurred, or the host was compromised.
- Implemented output model:
  - Normalize the canonical online root to current-user-owned mode 0700 and hold an exclusive transaction lock
    over stale-state recovery, completeness checking, preparation, producer execution, publication, and retirement.
  - Clone the existing current-user-owned SDK into unpredictable private same-filesystem staging, create a separate
    empty Gradle home, and bind the transaction to exact root/source/output inode identities plus a full SDK digest
    in a bounded fsynced mode-0600 state record outside the producer mounts.
  - Mount `/online` read-only with recursive submount inclusion disabled. Give the producer only the exact staged
    `/outputs/android-sdk` and `/outputs/gradle-home` writable mounts; reject these internal path variables in every

    occurred, or the host was compromised.

    It locks the private online root, verifies the pinned Rust 1.75 archive before and after execution, recovers
    exact stale transactions, and validates an existing final tool with the same non-mutating semantic gate.

    fsynced state record. The producer receives `/online` only as

    Cargo home, target, and home remain in bounded scratch.

    and only the fixed FRB `uuid` feature. Producer, Rust-input, output, and publication verdicts are independent.

    hardlinks, foreign ownership, writable published state, unstable reads, bounds violations, unexpected Cargo
    root inventory/metadata, and non-x86-64/non-ELF output. It requires canonical Cargo 1.75 metadata binding the
    exact registry package/version/bin/features/profile/target/compiler record.
  - Fsync precedes descriptor-relative `RENAME_NOREPLACE`; a final failure rolls the exact inode back. Restart
    recovery classifies only exact unpublished/published arrangements, preserves ambiguity, and retires reconciled
    staging through exact directory-mode restoration plus external-inode-closure removal.

    https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/renameat2.2.html and

## 2026-07-24 — Ordinary main-IPC credential mirror excision (R-S11b-4e)

- Audited boundary: the desktop GUI/main-IPC client versus the daemon process that owns and enforces the
  controlled-side permanent password, including the UI status calls that ran after raw password mutation.
- Source-proven residue before this slice:
  - `MainConfigKey::PermanentPasswordStorageAndSalt` returned the daemon's locally persisted
    `config.password` plus `config.salt` as a newline-delimited ordinary main-IPC string.
  - The GUI parsed that string, called public `Config::set_permanent_password_storage_for_sync`, reconstructed
    and persisted `password_prs`, and invoked that mirror from password-status presentation and after successful
    raw password mutation.
  - `config.password` plus its salt reconstruct the connect-equivalent CPace PRS. The receiver admitted this
    request only when its main server was user-owned and rejected it for a service-owned receiver, so the review
    did not prove a cross-UID disclosure, local-to-root escalation, authentication bypass, exploitation event,
    Android lifecycle defect, or host compromise. It nevertheless violated R-S11's ordinary-main nonsecret
    protocol model, duplicated live credential state into an independent GUI config, and retained a generic
    persistent credential-import API after mutation had moved to the proved raw protocol.
- Corrected authority model:
  - Deleted the main-protocol credential variant/handler, newline payload, string facade/parser, synchronous and
    asynchronous mirror clients, post-mutation mirror, authority predicate, public persistent sync writer,
    private apply/transaction helpers, and the tests that existed only to preserve mirroring.
  - Desktop presentation now requests only `LocalPermanentPasswordSet`, derived by the receiver from its own
    effective credential state. `is_permanent_password_set` likewise returns the daemon status without importing
    or rewriting client-side credential state. Android and iOS retain their in-process `Config` status path.
  - User-owned password mutation remains solely on the raw operation/ACK protocol. The separate Linux raw-PRS
    replica and macOS/Windows storage-envelope replica channels remain purpose-specific, mutually authenticated,
    generation-bound, and nonpersistent in the service child; their credential reads are not ordinary main IPC.
  - The main-config-handler source gates are now scoped to that exact dispatch arm. They reject direct local
    storage/salt, PRS, and key-pair reads there without falsely banning those APIs from the distinct service
    replica implementations.
- Requirements and proof model:
  - Added R-S11b-4e and Appendix C #237, corrected Appendix #234 and the older R-S11b-4 ledger statement, and
    synchronized the requirements SHA-256
    `b9d7bf518b013e043f850530fe74a2f4b475803ee68f41a1352bb553d704a996` in both tracked ledgers.
  - Shared and Apple gates reject the retired enum, facade/parser/clients, authority predicates, persistent
    writer, credential string payload, and direct secret reads in the main config handler; require the
    receiver-derived replacement and ledger/spec bindings; and preserve the purpose-specific runtime replica.
  - The focused Rust regression accepts `local-permanent-password-set` and rejects the retired storage/salt key.
    Its gate uses the exact real module path `ipc::test::...`; the initially written `ipc::tests::...` filter was
    caught during review because Cargo would otherwise succeed after running zero matching tests.
  - The independent semantic validator checks the complete source/UI/gate/spec/ledger contract. Its full
    in-memory source-mutation inventory passes after rejecting deliberate reintroduction of the writer, main
    variant, mirror client, direct handler secret read, client-local status fallback, weakened negative test,
    zero-test Cargo filter, disabled shared/Apple enum and handler gates, stale Appendix #234 text, missing
    Appendix #237, and deferred ledger.
- Confined evidence:
  - Exact Rust 1.75 locked/offline `hbb_common` library tests pass all 138 tests after deletion of eight

## 2026-07-24 — Single-key, receiver-effective ordinary main-IPC option mutation (R-S11b-3n)

- Audited boundary: one desktop UI/CLI option edit crossing ordinary main IPC into a user-owned daemon, plus
  the Flutter/web bridge surface that exposed the same option mutation vocabulary.
- Source-proven defect before this slice:
  - `ui_interface::set_option` cloned the complete cached `OPTIONS` map and changed one entry.
    `ipc::set_options` serialized that snapshot as `MainIpcRequest::SetOptions(MainStatusOptions)`.
  - The receiver merged the request by first deleting every allowlisted key from its current options and then
    extending with the caller's snapshot. A stale or concurrent caller could therefore overwrite unrelated
    receiver changes even though the initiating action addressed one key.
  - `OptionsSet(Applied)` returned no effective value. The caller replaced its complete cache with the requested
    snapshot even if `Config::is_option_can_save` rejected/purged a key or `Config::get_option` overlaid a pinned
    value. The caller cache could diverge from the state the receiver would actually read.
  - The unused JSON `main_set_options` Flutter FFI and authored web `mainSetOptions` method retained a generic
    batch mutation shape. Repository-wide authored-source review found no Dart caller, while fresh bridge
    generation later proved deletion did not break the shipped binding graph.
  - Service-owned receivers already rejected the old operation before mutation. This defect therefore does not
    prove a cross-principal write, local privilege escalation, credential disclosure, exploitation event,
    Android lifecycle/resource defect, host compromise, or any change to the host RustDesk installation.
- Corrected authority model:
  - Replaced the batch request with `SetOption(MainStatusOption)`. The typed enum key preserves the existing
    explicit allowlist, and both client and receiver validate the per-value byte bound.
  - After the unchanged service-owned authority rejection and bounded mutation-slot acquisition, the receiver
    invokes exactly `Config::set_option` for the requested key, reads the effective value through
    `Config::get_option`, and returns `OptionSet { result, effective }`.
  - The client accepts only `Applied` with an effective entry whose typed key equals the requested key. It has no
    local persistence or whole-options snapshot fallback. The UI updates/removes only that cache entry using the
    receiver-derived value; unrelated cache entries remain untouched.
  - Deleted the whole-map receiver merge, IPC batch client, UI whole-map setter, unused JSON Flutter FFI, and
    authored web batch method. The `--option` CLI now prints an IPC rejection/unavailability error and exits
    nonzero instead of discarding it.
  - `MainStatusOptions` remains only for bounded, allowlisted status snapshots. In-process
    `Config::set_options` remains a separate filtered config primitive and is not reachable from ordinary main
    IPC after this slice.
- Requirements and verifier closure:
  - R-S16 now requires exactly one key/value per ordinary mutation, the exact receiver sink, an effective-value
    read through the pinned funnel, key-correlated acknowledgement, one-entry caller-cache update, and no batch
    JSON/FFI bridge. R-S11b now names the current `SetOption` protocol.
  - Added R-S11b-3n and Appendix C #238 with the non-escalation/Android/host-state scope above. The synchronized
    requirements SHA-256 is
    `30d66306566cacc376188aa7d14c39514bbe2be5051c86e0c6c4c0fe26b17020` in
    `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` and the hardening ledger.
  - Shared and Apple gates bind the typed single-key request/response, service-owned rejection, exact
    `Config::set_option` sink, receiver-effective `Config::get_option` read, client no-fallback/key correlation,
    exact UI cache update, focused protocol regression, deleted batch surfaces, ledger, and Appendix row.
  - The Dart gate rejects the batch symbol family in authored sources and in newly generated
    `generated_bridge.dart`/Freezed output.
  - The independent semantic validator checks those control-flow and source/spec/ledger contracts directly.
    Fifteen new deliberate mutations cover the request type, exact receiver sink, effective response, client key
    correlation, UI cache value, Flutter and web batch reintroduction, CLI failure finality, shared/Apple/Dart
    gates, normative requirement, Appendix row, ledger, and focused regression.
- Confined evidence:
  - Python compilation and Bash syntax passed. The independent workspace verifier passed normally, and its
    complete source-mutation inventory passed after every new and pre-existing deliberate weakening was rejected
    for its intended semantic label.
  - Exact Rust 1.75 locked/offline compilation ran the six `ipc::test::main_` regressions: service-owned mutation
    rejection, nonsecret config keys, single-key/receiver-effective wire protocol, global-frame rejection,
    allowlist/value bounds, and duplicate-key rejection. Result: 6 passed, 0 failed, 343 filtered out.
  - The full pinned `scripts/dart-verify.sh` transaction verified canonical offline-input digest

    reported zero Flutter analyzer errors, passed the focused Flutter tests, completed the shipped
