## 2026-07-24 — Audit-integrity correction: an earlier source search accidentally launched host RustDesk

- Read-only process inventory during the resumed privilege-boundary audit
  found a shell and child process owned by this Codex session:
  - shell PID `221880`, parent Codex PID `32209`, UID/GID `1000:1000`;
  - child PID `221881`, argv exactly `/usr/bin/rustdesk`, UID/GID
    `1000:1000`;
  - both started on 2026-07-23 at 01:44:03 local time and remained live when
    inspected.
- The shell command was intended to run `rg` over source and ledger text, but
  its double-quoted pattern included literal Markdown backticks around
  `/usr/bin/rustdesk`. Bash interpreted the first backtick pair as command
  substitution and executed the host path before `rg` could start. The host
  path resolves to `/usr/share/rustdesk/rustdesk`; the long-running child kept
  the command substitution and parent shell blocked.
- This is directly attributable to this Codex session. It was not Docker,
  root, `sudo`, a build, a RustDesk upgrade, or an in-place binary/configuration
  edit. The inspected process identity does not by itself prove whether the
  extra user-owned application process affected any reported connection
  symptom, and no unsupported causal claim is made.
- No process was signaled, stopped, restarted, or otherwise changed during the
  discovery. The user was told the exact process identities and that
  termination requires explicit authorization.
- Any earlier interval-wide statement that no host RustDesk application was
  executed must be read subject to this correction. The narrower claims that
  the Cargo-vendor transaction did not use host RustDesk as part of its
  implementation, did not use root, did not publish a port, and did not alter
  the host RustDesk binary/service/configuration/firewall remain supported.

## 2026-07-26 — R-S11dd/R-S11e-122 runtime-smoke host/build authority

- Scope and proven source gap:
  - `scripts/smoke-server.sh` selected `docker` through `PATH` and inherited
    caller Docker host/context/configuration state. Docker documents that
    `DOCKER_CONTEXT` can override `DOCKER_HOST` and the configured context can
    select the daemon:
    https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/.
  - The top-level host orchestrator executed
    `scripts/smoke-process-guard.py` directly and used its historical
    selector/baseline/monitor modes to enumerate the host `/proc` process table
    for the duration of a smoke run.
  - `BUILD_RUN` accepted the image-default UID 0 and mounted the live checkout
    read-write. Docker documents the default-root user at
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/#user and writable bind-mount
    host-file authority at
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/bind-mounts/#considerations-and-constraints.
  - These were excessive daemon-selection, host-process-inspection, and
    source/build authorities. Source review found no publication/host-network
    option or Docker-socket mount in these launches and supplies no evidence
    that a remote daemon was selected, a host process or source file changed,
    Docker escaped, root was acquired, a listener/port was exposed, host
    RustDesk/service/configuration/firewall/network state changed,
    exploitation occurred, or the host was compromised.
- Implemented source authority model:
  - The orchestrator refuses host UID or primary GID 0 and admits only the
    exact non-symlink root-owned mode-0755 single-link `/usr/bin/docker`
    client and a non-symlink root-owned single-link local
    `/var/run/docker.sock`. The socket device/inode/owner/group/mode/link
    identity is stable-bound for the run.
  - Caller Docker host, context, configuration, TLS, API, platform, trust, and
    custom-header inputs are rejected. One `/usr/bin/env -i` command array
    supplies the fixed Unix endpoint plus a fresh mode-0700 private
    configuration containing exact mode-0600 `{}`. The client/socket/config,
    private authority root, and private target are checked around operations;
    cleanup preserves changed authority instead of broadly deleting it.
  - Every Docker operation routes through `smoke_docker`, except the bounded
    `docker wait` child, which invokes the same fixed command array with
    identical pre/post authority checks.
  - The compile container is the invoking numeric UID:GID with all
    capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, read-only root, no pull/network,
    explicit PID/memory/no-swap/CPU/tmpfs ceilings, live source read-only, and
    a fresh current-user-private writable target. The two established
    locked/offline Cargo caches retain their build-input role.

    source and the private target read-only. Root/capability service fixtures
    remain container-only and retain no host namespace, Docker socket,
    network, publication, writable source, or writable build-output authority.
    Their actual runtime execution remains open R-B2 evidence and was not
    inferred from source.

## 2026-07-26 — R-S11de/R-S11e-123 Dart/FRB Docker authority

- Scope and source-proven gap:
  - This coherent slice covers only the host-side Docker client, daemon,
    configuration, numeric-identity, and private-workspace metadata authority
    used by `scripts/dart-verify.sh`, `scripts/frb-codegen.sh`, and their
    common immutable-builder provenance call.
  - At parent `80cf32130024623954d5a55bad2c7ec9f0e36085`, both launchers
    required and invoked `docker` through caller `PATH`. Their direct
    launches inherited all caller Docker routing and configuration state.
    `require_pinned_builder_image` invoked
    `scripts/offline-image-provenance.py` through PATH-selected `python3`;
    although that helper selects `/usr/bin/docker`, its Docker subprocesses
    inherited the caller environment.
  - Docker's CLI reference documents that `DOCKER_CONTEXT` overrides
    `DOCKER_HOST`, both participate in daemon selection, and client
    configuration can inject default proxy variables into containers:
    https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/.
    Docker's daemon-access documentation shows contexts selecting a remote
    daemon over SSH:
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/protect-access/.
    Therefore immutable image IDs and otherwise-correct run flags did not
    prove which client/daemon interpreted those flags or which configuration
    influenced the client.
  - This was real build-verdict and daemon/configuration-selection authority
    debt. Source review and this correction provide no evidence that a
    malicious client or remote daemon was used, any image/source changed,
    Docker escaped, host root was acquired, a listener/public port was
    exposed, host RustDesk/service/configuration/firewall/network state
    changed, exploitation occurred, or the host was compromised.

- Intended and implemented authority model:
  - Each verifier process independently initializes one opt-in Docker
    authority below its own exact current-user/current-group mode-0700
    private workspace; the outer Dart verifier and nested FRB verifier never
    share Docker configuration state.
  - Initialization refuses effective UID or primary GID zero and rejects
    inherited `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`,
    certificate/TLS, API version, default platform, content-trust/server, and
    custom-header inputs.
  - Numeric identity and authority metadata are read with absolute
    `/usr/bin/id` and `/usr/bin/stat`, including the shared private-online
    snapshot mode check used by Dart verification.
  - The only admitted client is the executable, non-symlink, root:root,
    mode-0755, single-link `/usr/bin/docker`. The only admitted endpoint is
    the non-symlink, root-owned, single-link Unix socket at
    `/var/run/docker.sock`. Client and socket device/inode/owner/group/mode/
    link identities are captured.
  - The caller-private parent receives one new mode-0700 `docker-config`.
    `config.json` is created under `umask 077` with no-clobber redirection and
    must immediately be current UID:GID, mode 0600, one link, and exact
    canonical `{}\n`. Parent, config directory/file, client, socket, and
    configuration bytes are reproved before and after every wrapper
    operation.
  - Direct launches use `/usr/bin/env -i`, fixed `PATH`, private `HOME`,
    `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock`, private `DOCKER_CONFIG`,
    absolute `/usr/bin/docker`, and redundant explicit `--host` and
    `--config`. Provenance uses absolute `/usr/bin/python3 -I -S` and the
    helper's existing absolute Docker client under the same empty
    environment.
  - Cleanup first reproves the whole Docker authority, then removes only the
    exact `config.json` and `docker-config` with nonrecursive `rm`/`rmdir`.
    Changed identity or bytes preserve the private workspace and fail with
    status 125 instead of becoming input to recursive cleanup.
  - Both callers create and capture their workspace before provenance,
    initialize their independent authority before provenance and launch,
    route their sole direct launch through `local_docker`, and use absolute

## 2026-07-26 — R-S11dk/R-S11e-129 Debian artifact-builder Docker authority

- Invocation baseline and open checklist:
  - Began from clean synchronized `master`
    `9236d84bcbfb7493c495596918e2b52a2c7a1864`.
  - The R-S11b/R-S11c service-owned IPC source topology remains implemented,
    while a clean committed cold R-B2/R-B10 release transaction remains open.
  - R-S11dj explicitly left two broader Docker boundaries open: the Debian
    artifact builder and the final Debian systemd-lifecycle child. This
    invocation selects only the earlier artifact-builder boundary; the
    lifecycle child remains a separate follow-on.

- Source-proven old path:
  - `scripts/build-debian.sh` captured UID/GID through ambient `id` only after
    sourcing repository shell and did not refuse host UID or primary GID zero.
  - It accepted unset or fixed `DOCKER_HOST`, rejected only context and four
    certificate/TLS inputs, constructed a bespoke empty Docker config without
    identity-binding it, and exported that process-global configuration.
  - Because the shared local authority was not initialized,
    `require_pinned_builder_image` used its ambient provenance fallback.
  - The sole compiler operation invoked direct `"$DOCKER_BIN" run`, so the
    fixed pathname and inner confinement did not prove daemon/config authority.
  - Recursive workspace cleanup did not first reprove and remove the Docker
    config leaf/directory and could therefore consume changed authority.

- Primary research and design implication:
  - Docker CLI reference:
    https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/
    documents host, context, configuration, certificate/TLS, API-version,
    platform, content-trust/server, and custom-header inputs; context
    precedence; explicit `--config` precedence; and config-driven proxy
    injection into containers.
  - Docker context documentation:
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/contexts/
    documents context-carried endpoint and TLS selection, including remote
    daemons.
  - Docker Engine security guidance:
    https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/
    documents the powerful host authority behind control of a rootful daemon.
  - Intended model: refuse root before repository code; create a private
    unpredictable workspace; initialize the shared fixed local Docker
    authority before release classification/provenance/launch; route
    provenance and the sole compiler through its empty-environment wrappers;
    reprove authority with online-input state; and exactly remove authority
    before recursive workspace cleanup, preserving changed objects on failure.

- Current implementation and final pre-publication evidence:
  - `scripts/build-debian.sh` now fixes `PATH`, captures identity with absolute
    `/usr/bin/id`, refuses UID/GID zero before sourcing, initializes
    `debian-builder` shared authority beneath every direct/release private
    workspace, uses `local_docker` for the sole compiler, rechecks shared
    authority with the online snapshot, and removes exact Docker authority
    before workspace recursion.
  - Bespoke `DOCKER_BIN`, partial ambient-input checks, config assertion/export,
    direct launch, PATH-selected Docker prerequisite, and later ambient `id`
    reads are removed.
  - Full-diff review found one integration error before publication: the shared
    `local_docker` wrapper intentionally gives the client an empty environment,
    so the prior bare `-e SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` form would have unset the pinned
    reproducibility epoch inside the compiler. The builder now supplies the
    nonsecret pinned value explicitly as
    `-e "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"`; focused and independent
    mutations bind that exact transfer.
  - `scripts/verify-debian-builder-authority.py` now binds the caller and the
    full shared client/socket/config/provenance/cleanup implementation. Its
    normal contract and all 62 deliberate mutations pass.
  - `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` now owns the complete Debian model,
    focused gate, R-S11dk, Appendix C #264, R-S11e-129, and shared gate wording.
    Its normal contract and complete confined in-memory repository
    `--source-mutations-only` catalog pass after the final production and
    normative state.
  - The complete catalog drove three verifier-only accounting corrections
    before its clean pass: it required the focused gate's exact
    API/platform/trust-input label to be independently owned, aligned that

## 2026-07-26 — Windows golden exact libvirt-domain authority (R-S11dr/R-S11e-136)

- Selected one coherent continuation after R-S11dq:
  - Audited only `scripts/provision-windows-vm.sh`, its focused/independent
    verification contracts, and the directly corresponding requirements and
    evidence ledger.
  - Traced the live source plus `git blame` and `git log -S`. The destructive
    pre-launch name-collision workaround originates at `599fd4d0`
    (`Undefine any stale golden domain before virt-install`); the surrounding
    name-addressed launch/control path descends from the original June 2026
    golden provisioner.
  - Read the official libvirt domain-format and `virsh` manuals. A domain name
    is host-unique metadata; the RFC 4122 UUID is the global domain identifier;
    `virsh` accepts UUID domain arguments; `destroy` immediately terminates the
    addressed domain without deleting storage; and inactive
    `undefine --nvram` removes its persistent configuration and NVRAM.

- Finding and classification:
  - Before every launch, the old provisioner suppressed the results of
    name-addressed `destroy` and `undefine --nvram` against the predictable
    `${HARNESS_PREFIX}-win-golden` name, then invoked `virt-install` without an
    explicit UUID.
  - Boot-key injection and state queries reused the mutable name. Boot-key
    errors and the background client's final status were ignored. A failed
    `domstate` query could enter the old non-running branch. Successful
    marker/hash acceptance left a persistent definition for the now-deleted
    generic name-prefix cleanup authority.
  - Classification: mutable-name destructive ownership, identity ambiguity,
    suppressed control failures, incomplete process-group ownership, and
    non-terminal creator cleanup. This is not evidence that the provisioner
    ran, another domain was destroyed, the host RustDesk service was changed,
    root was acquired, a listener was exposed, or the host was compromised.

- Authority model and source closure:
  - Validate the fixed name grammar and generate one kernel-random version-4
    UUID. Require complete, successful name/UUID enumeration to prove both
    absent before creating the golden disk and again immediately before
    launch. A pre-existing name or UUID is a fail-loud reconciliation
    condition and is never adopted or destroyed.
  - Record creation intent immediately before

- Finding and classification:
  - `RUN_ROOT` is created privately but its device/inode identity is not
    retained. Successful cleanup therefore authorizes recursive mutation and
    deletion from the pathname alone; a renamed/replaced terminal edge is not

    substituted edge or a nested mount can redirect or widen the deletion
    boundary, and the deliberately suppressed `chmod` errors erase useful
    failure classification.

    authority is still open. If `windows_helper_authority_close` then fails,
    cleanup changes the build verdict to failure only after the transaction's
    source/input/result/diagnostic evidence has already been destroyed.

    authority ordering, and failure-evidence preservation debt. The builder

  - Record the exact device/inode identity immediately after `mktemp` creates
    each real current-principal mode-0700 run root.

    domain, and Windows-helper Docker/configuration authority before attempting
    any terminal run-state deletion. Any inconclusive earlier retirement

  - Verification is source/mutation plus bounded filesystem behavior inside

## 2026-07-27 continuation — Linux `_pa` protocol/resource finality

- Audit scope and existing authority:
  - Traced `src/ipc.rs::start_pa`,
    `validate_pulse_audio_start_authority`, `_pa` connection construction,
    the `ConnectionTmpl` codec/read/write APIs,
    `src/server/audio_service.rs::pa_impl::run`, subscriber-bound
    `PaCaptureAuthority`, endpoint identity proof, and the surrounding
    `GenericService` retry behavior.
  - The existing authorization chain remains conjunctive and source-proven:
    the client proves the `_pa` endpoint before token disclosure; the token is
    freshly minted from active subscriber IDs; the accepted owner is either
    the exact current-process identity or the exact live direct-child CM
    identity; nonlocal validation connects to the serialized owner's
    UID-scoped main endpoint and proves its exact identity; and source
    resolution/PulseAudio open occur only after token validation.
  - Classification: no reviewed source path showed an unauthenticated process
    starting capture. This slice is not evidence of exploitation, compromise,
    root acquisition, public listener exposure, or host RustDesk/service/
    configuration/firewall/network mutation.

- Proven gap:
  - The first unauthenticated `_pa` frame was
    `Data::PulseAudioStart { owner, token, source }`, so the endpoint compiled
    and deserialized the full cross-purpose local IPC union before authority
    validation.
  - Both the accepted and connecting `_pa` streams used the generic
    `ConnectionTmpl::new`/`BytesCodec::new()` default with
    `max_packet_length == usize::MAX`. Although reserve growth is internally
    chunked, a same-UID local client could continue accumulating an unbounded
    frame before the token check.
  - The helper ignored `psimple::Simple::read` failures and could spin; its
    raw frame write had no deadline. The audio service ignored the
    token-bearing request's send failure and used
    `if let Ok(data) = next_raw().await`, which hid immediate peer resets and
    could hot-loop while subscribers remained. A stalled peer could block the
    task indefinitely, preventing timely observation of subscriber removal or
    `RESTARTING`.

- Implemented source design:
  - Added the dedicated one-variant, unknown-field-denying
    `LinuxPulseAudioIpcRequest::StartCapture { owner, token, source }` and
    removed `PulseAudioStart` from `Data`.
  - Added an 8-KiB purpose-specific codec ceiling, exact empty-or-3,840-byte
    audio-frame shape, and one-second I/O deadline constants. Both `_pa`
    accepted and connecting streams install the cap before the request.
  - Added purpose-specific typed request read/write methods, a shape- and
    deadline-bound raw frame writer, and a frame reader whose one-second
    timeout is a cancellation wake while EOF/codec/shape failure is terminal.
  - The receiver validates the typed owner/token request before source
    resolution, terminates PulseAudio read failure, and terminates stalled or
    failed writes. The audio service propagates request-send and frame-read
    errors into existing bounded service retry/backoff and wakes periodically
    to recheck `sp.ok()`/`RESTARTING`.
  - Added the exact-wire/unknown-field/cross-purpose/typed-duplex/codec/frame/
    timeout/reset Rust regression; expanded the focused Linux nondumpable
    CM/PA/whiteboard mutation checker; added a direct independent workspace
    semantic contract and mutations; expanded the shared R-S11c-7 gate; and
    added R-S11dy, Appendix C #278, and R-S11e-143.

- Re-read the persistent Ralph objective, `/tmp/ralph_loop_prompt.md`, the
  repository rules, current clean synchronized `master`, normative
  R-S11/R-S11a/R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S16/R-S19 and Appendix C #25–#29, and the
  current R-S11b/R-S11c ledger before selecting a slice.
- Current checklist: all named R-S11b/R-S11c source slices are recorded
  implemented/closed; the parent clean committed cold R-B2 artifact/native
  proof remains pending. The controlling prompt forbids starting the long
  release build without an explicit request, so this invocation continues the
  required fresh source audit instead of relabeling an already-closed item.
- Selected boundary: the desktop `_whiteboard_<hmac>` helper on Linux, macOS,
  and Windows. Existing endpoint authority remains strong: a per-launch token
  derives the endpoint name and mutual HMAC proof, the helper admits the exact
  launch parent/process role, and post-admission drawing state is bound to
  per-Remote-connection tokens.
- Proven current gap:
  - `src/ipc.rs` still places all four whiteboard handshake messages and all
    four post-admission commands in the cross-purpose `Data` union.
  - `src/whiteboard/server.rs` wraps the accepted stream with unbounded
    `Connection::new`, then spawns an untracked task whose `conn.next()`
    deserializes that entire union indefinitely and silently ignores unrelated
    variants.
  - `src/whiteboard/client.rs` connects through the same unbounded generic
    codec, uses an unbounded local command channel, ignores every post-proof
    transport write failure, gives those writes no deadline, and retains an
    otherwise-unneeded local sender that prevents channel closure from waking
    the worker.
  - The helper accepts an unbounded number of connection-token binds and may
    leave the overlay/event loop alive after terminal transport loss when its
    active map happens to be empty.
- Classification: the endpoint proof prevents the reviewed arbitrary local
  caller from exercising whiteboard authority, so this is not evidence of an
  authorization bypass, privilege escalation, public listener, exploitation,
  or host/service/firewall/network mutation. It is a concrete local
  parser/memory/lifecycle/future-reactivation defect and contradicts R-S11's
  already-binding independent-message/cap/budget/finality requirement.
- Intended authority/resource model: the exact launch parent and helper use
  three closed, directional, unknown-field-denying protocols (owner handshake,
  helper handshake, and post-proof command), all outside `Data` and behind a
  purpose-specific codec cap before the first frame. Handshake and command I/O
  is deadline-bound; malformed/cross-phase/reset errors are terminal. The
  parent owns one bounded lossy event queue and propagates transport failure;
  the helper owns exactly one authenticated stream, a bounded active-token
  state, and terminal overlay shutdown with no detached stream task.

## 2026-07-27 — Mobile outgoing-session owner/connection lifecycle correction

- Scope and source-proven defect:
  - Re-read the active Ralph objective and repository rules, then traced the
    Android viewer path from `MainActivity` owner registration through Dart
    route/model disposal, the generated Flutter bridge, Rust session tables,
    outgoing worker ownership, rendering/input submodels, and file transfer.
  - Android's persistent `MainService` is intentional and remains unchanged.
    The defect was a separate identity collapse: one isolate-wide UUID was
    registered as the Activity owner and also reused as every successive
    outgoing connection ID. Flutter does not await asynchronous
    `State.dispose()`, while the process-static native session table and global
    Dart `FFI` model survive task swipe/relaunch.
  - A delayed old route close could therefore select a replacement
    same-peer/type connection under the reused UUID. A delayed event stream
    could observe the replacement after the shared `closed` flag was cleared.
    Reused input/relative-mouse models retained old-session state, pending file
    completers and dialogs were not retired at connection rotation, and an old
    file event-loop callback could rearm its timer.
  - This is a source-proven mobile outgoing-session ownership/availability
    mechanism consistent with “file transfer works while screen control hangs
    until Force Stop.” It is not claimed as physical-device causal
    reproduction, compromise, host-service failure, or a controlled-side
    foreground-service defect.

- Corrected ownership and resource model:
  - One mobile `clientOwnerId` now lasts for the Activity/isolate while every
    `FFI.start()` mints a fresh connection `sessionId`. Authored add/attach/start
    FFI carries both identities.
  - Native handlers store the client-owner association. Android holds exact
    owner admission through insertion/start and verifies that the connection
    belongs to that owner. Before a new mobile connection is inserted, native
    code removes and joins every previous mobile connection except an exact
    identical owner/session pair. Activity/task teardown drains by stored owner
    association; exact route teardown closes only its captured connection ID.
  - Mobile pages retain the exact ID returned by their own start. State that
    belongs to the exact old native handler is persisted before that captured
    ID is closed; a replacement cannot be selected by the old close, and
    post-await Dart cleanup may clear shared state only if the ID is still
    current. Event, frame, decoded-image, cursor, and file delivery recheck the
    captured ID; stale decoded images are disposed.
  - Pre-rotation model reset cancels pending file fetches/completers, dismisses
    old dialogs, retires event-loop generation, clears chat/terminal/render
    caches, and releases side buttons and relative-mouse state against the
    exact retired connection without permanently disposing observers required
    by the replacement. This shared mobile correction also benefits iOS;
    Android alone adds Activity-owner admission and persistent-service
    amplification.
  - The final residual audit also closed same-process ABA/resource paths outside
    the original close call: a timed-out file completer removes itself only if
    it is still the identical map value, async cursor/window-coordinate and
    directory reads stage results locally and publish only after an exact
    session check, and remote/camera keyboard, lifecycle, menu, metrics, stream,
    breadcrumb-timer, and scroll-controller resources are bound to and retired
    with their owning route/session. The behavioral Dart regression exercises
    the same-path file-timeout/replacement race rather than merely grepping for
    its implementation.
  - Line-by-line review found one further native display-resource defect before
    publication. Post-drain reconciliation always excluded a mandatory session
    ID, so an idempotent/retry replacement drain could omit the preserved
    handler while deciding which display captures remained in use. The helper
    now accepts an optional exclusion: live display switching supplies the
    exact active handler, while exact-session removal, replacement drain, and
    Activity-owner drain reconcile against every remaining handler. Focused
    and independent method-scoped contracts reject restoring an exclusion on
    either drain.
  - R-S11eb/R-S11e-146 and Appendix C #281 make the identity/resource
    lifecycle normative. The active requirements SHA-256 is
    `2f2cf27cfd7f8aca3a0898f67014cd5ca395c421f5b2fdee259fe4c9d63622aa`

## 2026-07-27 — R-S11ec outgoing clipboard exact-network-round ownership

- Source diagnosis and scope:
  - `src/client.rs` explicitly documented that peer-first close left
    `has_sessions_running(DEFAULT_CONN)` true because Flutter's UI handler
    outlived the network I/O round. The stop path therefore skipped cleanup.
    Desktop and Android clipboard-worker `JoinHandle`s were discarded; the
    Windows file-clipboard context used the same stale UI-registry predicate.
  - This proves cross-platform outgoing clipboard lifecycle debt. Android's
    persistent process amplifies it across task swipe/relaunch. It does not
    prove that clipboard polling was the exact cause of the reported
    screen-control hang, and it does not implicate or justify stopping the
    controlled-side persistent `MainService`.
- Implemented ownership correction:
  - Every default outgoing network round acquires a monotonic exact clipboard
    lease at I/O-loop entry and releases it through RAII on every exit. The
    exact lease is passed into peer-message handling before clipboard startup.
  - Shared clipboard state owns the active lease set, stop token, sole worker
    `JoinHandle`, serialized drain transition, and pending replacement start.
    A stale or non-last release cannot retire another round. The exact last
    release closes listener admission and transfers the retained handle to the
    existing fixed bounded off-runtime completion pool.
  - A replacement arriving during drain stays admitted and starts only after
    the old exact handle joins. Zero-owner completion finalizes Linux FUSE and
    Windows `ContextSend`; a retained replacement instead starts its worker.
    The UI-registry liveness facade and process-global clipboard `running`
    Boolean are absent. iOS does not compile this worker.
- Counted confined evidence on the final source state:
  - The focused Android/mobile ownership verifier passed and rejected all
    `185` deliberate mutations, including exact lease acquisition/release,
    network-round-to-peer-handler handoff, monotonic/ABA behavior, retained
    worker authority, stop publication, serialized replacement, completion
    callback, requirement/ledger bindings, and both shared execution gates.
  - The independent workspace semantic baseline passed. Its complete
    in-memory source-mutation mode then passed uninterrupted from mutation one
    through the end after the final ledger update.
  - The complete `scripts/dart-verify.sh` transaction passed in immutable
    Debian builder image
    `sha256:607278bc16cf12eadaa41f8fa63a5a160a34b1a980be8cb2a772c4c3b7d3fdb2`

## 2026-07-27 — R-S11ed/R-S11e-148 delayed OS-password exact-round ownership

- Source diagnosis and scope:
  - `src/client.rs` previously cloned the mutable `Session` into an unretained
    native thread for OS-password automation. That thread emitted activation
    mouse events around three 50-ms sleeps, waited another 1.2 seconds, and
    then emitted the optional password plus Return.
  - Each delayed event called `Interface::send` through the cloned session.
    Because reconnect replaces `Session::sender`, a helper admitted by an old
    connection round could wake after replacement and resolve the new round's
    sender. The network-round owner joined its I/O task but did not own this
    detached helper, so normal reconnect ordering did not close the lifetime
    gap.
  - This is source-proven shared native-viewer lifecycle debt affecting the
    common Rust path used by Android, iOS, and desktop Flutter. Android's
    persistent process amplifies the stale lifetime; the web bridge bypasses
    this Rust path. It is not proof that this mechanism caused the reported
    screen-control hang and is not a controlled-side `MainService` defect.

- Implemented ownership correction:
  - The UI-side session now admits a typed `Data::InputOsPassword` request
    through the sender installed for the current outgoing round. Only the
    connected `Remote` that receives that request may start its sequence.
  - Before spawning, the current `Remote` synchronously constructs the
    immutable mouse/key message bundle while its handler is current. Each
    `Remote` retains the sole `OwnedInputOsPasswordTask`. Replacing a sequence
    aborts and awaits the prior exact task before spawning another. Every
    normal I/O-round exit invokes the same abort-and-await shutdown before
    `ConnectionRoundOwner::finish`; exceptional `Remote` drop aborts the
    retained task.
  - The async sequence captures only the prepared bundle and exact
    `Remote::sender`; its type contains no `Session`, `Interface`, handler, or
    other capability that can resolve mutable connection state. It never calls
    mutable `Session::send` after admission, so even an exceptional teardown
    cannot retarget an old event to a replacement channel. The original
    activation ordering, key-modifier mapping, three 50-ms delays, 1.2-second
    delay, optional-password behavior, and Return event are preserved.
  - Closed exact-channel delivery logs a noncredential diagnostic and stops
    the sequence. The implementation uses the existing Tokio runtime and
    async sleeps; it adds no nested runtime, blocking helper thread,
    `spawn_blocking`, dependency, or Android service-lifetime change.

- Counted confined evidence on the final source state:
  - The focused Android/mobile ownership verifier passed and rejected all
    `207` deliberate mutations. Its new mutations cover typed UI admission,
    typed I/O-loop handling, retained sole-handle ownership, exact sender
    capture, activation/password ordering, async delays, channel-close
    termination, abort-and-await replacement/final shutdown, exceptional drop
    abort, logged joined-task failure without process abort, behavior-test
    presence, requirements/appendix/ledger bindings, and shared gate wiring.
  - The independent workspace semantic baseline passed. Its complete
    in-memory source-mutation catalog also passed uninterrupted after the
    exact new diagnostics were bound.
  - The complete `scripts/dart-verify.sh` transaction passed in immutable
    Debian builder image
    `sha256:607278bc16cf12eadaa41f8fa63a5a160a34b1a980be8cb2a772c4c3b7d3fdb2`
    as UID/GID 1000:1000, with `--pull=never`, no network, read-only container
    root, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, finite PID/memory/no-swap/
    CPU/tmpfs limits, and disposable private source/offline-input snapshots.
    The exact offline closure digest was
    `a94e73ae80a235e7544d862558fccd8f22b045abc2324b61ff98391ba411b918`.
    Full Flutter bridge regeneration succeeded; Flutter analysis reported
    zero errors; all four focused Flutter test files passed; the shipped

    `client::tests::clipboard_leases_track_exact_network_rounds_without_stale_stop`

    The final Dart/source sweeps passed, Cargo.lock and the source worktree

  - The new behavior regression uses a mock interface that panics if delayed

    synthetic forty-character commit rather than a real clean detached Git
    source, injected caller-owned `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_CONFIG` even
    though the current targets reject all ambient Docker client inputs, and
    omitted the current local-Docker initialization/assertion/removal state.

    syntax, whereas both current targets use
    `type=bind,source=...,target=/online,readonly`. Android was sent through
    `--verify-apk`, so it did not exercise the normal signing preflight and
    build consumer it purported to cover.

    shipped RustDesk runtime defect, credential/IPC defect, privilege
    escalation, exploitation, compromise, root acquisition, public exposure,
    container escape, Android lifecycle cause, or host
    RustDesk/service/firewall/network change.

    Android inner build program, Android exact-source validator, and
    private-tree cleanup helper into one current-principal mode-0700 private
    repository. It initializes a real SHA-1 Git repository under closed Git
    configuration, commits only the fixture source, detaches `HEAD`, and
    supplies the resulting full lowercase commit. Runtime inputs are
    untracked, while the production target scripts still perform their own
    exact clean-source proofs.
  - The output destination is never created and is checked absent before and

## 2026-07-28 — R-S11ei/R-S11e-153 exact-owner bounded Android controlled input

- Source-proven defect and scope:
  - Android's controlled-side `InputService` retained one default Java
    `Timer` for the process lifetime and never cancelled it. Its thread was
    non-daemon; delayed long-press, recents, and wheel-drain tasks therefore
    survived for as long as the persistent accessibility process.
  - Wheel gestures accumulated in an unbounded
    `LinkedList<GestureDescription>` and advanced after an elapsed delay,
    rather than after Android reported completion or cancellation. Repeated
    left-down or wheel-button-down input could schedule multiple tasks while
    retaining only one replaceable task pointer.
  - Pre-API-33 key input allocated and posted through a fresh main `Handler`
    per event. Neither that work nor any delayed action carried a connection
    owner.
  - Rust validated only the current `MainService` generation, then erased the
    authenticated connection ID at JNI. Kotlin returned `void`; authorization
    or type replacement, exact disconnect, service-generation teardown, and
    queue refusal could not be returned to or acted upon by the owning Rust
    connection.
  - Android task swipe intentionally preserves the foreground/accessibility
    process; Force Stop destroys it. The source therefore proves real
    Android process-persistent controlled-input/resource debt.
  - This path is used when the Android device itself is being controlled. It
    is not the outgoing Android viewer path used to control a desktop host,
    so this finding is not claimed as the cause of the reported
    viewer-to-host screen-control hang. It is not evidence of an
    authorization bypass, exploitation, compromise, root acquisition, public
    exposure, container escape, or host RustDesk/service/firewall/network
    modification.

- Corrected authority and resource model:
  - `ControlledInputOwner` is exactly
    `(positive MainService generation, positive authenticated connection ID)`.
    The serialized `MainService` constructs it only while controlled
    admission is open, its native generation is positive, and the exact ID
    remains in the authorized `Remote` capture/input owner set.
  - Pointer and key JNI carry the exact connection ID, validate both
    generation and ID, call Boolean-returning Kotlin methods, and return that
    result to the connection. False admission or JNI failure closes only the
    exact Rust connection; there is no latest/global-owner retry or silent
    success.
  - `InputService` retains a set of live exact owners. Mouse/touch continuation
    state has one exact owner and one typed sequence kind. A different owner,
    mixed kind, duplicate down, or mismatched continuation is refused.
  - Authorization/type replacement and exact disconnect retire that exact
    owner's queued and delayed work. Service teardown first closes admission,
    clears capture owners, retires the exact generation, and then releases
    capture resources. The persistent foreground and accessibility services
    remain alive; killing the service/process is not used as cleanup.
  - A live API-26+ pointer continuation which was actually OS-admitted is
    ended before local state is reset. A staged down with no admitted stroke
    is discarded and cannot be turned into a manufactured click. An already
    OS-admitted finite wheel gesture may finish or be cancelled, but its
    callback cannot admit retired queued work.
  - `ExactOwnerBoundedQueue` uses `ArrayDeque`, rejects invalid owners and
    overflow, preserves FIFO order, and removes by full owner equality. Wheel
    and key pending capacities are 32 and 64. There is one retained main
    `Handler`, one posted drain per queue, and at most one in-flight wheel
    gesture. Android completion/cancellation exclusively advances wheel
    admission; key drain processes one event per main-loop turn and rechecks
    exact liveness.
  - Long-press and recents each retain one owner/sequence-bound callback.
    Sequences advance monotonically and refuse rather than wrap. Post failure
    removes that owner's pending queue before refusal. The process-lifetime
    `Timer`, `TimerTask`, unbounded wheel queue, delay polling, and per-key
    handler allocation are deleted.

## 2026-07-28 — R-S11eh/R-S11e-152 bounded exact-subscriber audio egress

- Source-proven defect and scope:
  - `src/server/connection.rs` gave each controlled connection one general
    `mpsc::UnboundedSender<(Instant, Arc<Message>)>` for non-video service
    traffic. `AudioFrame` and `Misc::AudioFormat` used that queue. The
    one-second stale-frame check ran only after dequeue, so a stalled sole
    stream writer could retain generated audio indefinitely before reaching
    the check.
  - The shared non-iOS outgoing viewer voice-call subscription was also
    unbounded. The interim R-S11bp blocking worker drained it into the
    viewer's separate unbounded `Data` command queue. That removed idle
    polling but only moved the unbounded accumulation point.
  - Android's intentionally persistent process can amplify the lifetime of
    retained queues, but this is shared Rust viewer/controlled-side resource
    debt, not an Android-only defect and not proof of the reported
    one-host screen-control symptom.
  - The defect provides a local resource-availability failure mode. It does
    not grant credentials, root, service-owned IPC authority, host access,
    container escape, listener authority, or firewall/network control. No
    privilege-escalation path was found in this slice. The relevant security
    consequence is boundedness/finality under a stalled or slow peer.

- Corrected ownership and data-plane model:
  - Every exact audio subscriber now owns one `AudioEgressState` containing
    at most one pending format and one latest frame, plus a capacity-one Tokio
    wake channel. Producer sends are synchronous and nonblocking; a full wake
    coalesces.
  - A frame replaces only the pending frame. A new format replaces the
    pending format and retires a pending old-generation frame. The receiver
    always drains format before frame. No lock is held across `.await`.
  - Closing the receiver first closes the wake channel and synchronously
    clears both retained messages. A concurrent or later sender observes the
    closed wake and clears state again, so receiver retirement does not
    require another producer send to release retained audio.
  - `ConnInner` classifies exactly `AudioFrame` and `AudioFormat` before its
    video/general routes. Controlled connections install the bounded audio
    sender and drain it in a separate branch of the existing connection
    select through the sole stream writer. The one-second stale-frame refusal
    remains in that bounded branch; the general queue no longer handles
    audio.
  - Shared non-iOS outgoing voice calls now use `VoiceCallAudio`, which owns
    the exact service subscription, the non-cloneable input lease, and the
    bounded receiver. The connection round's existing Tokio select receives
    that mailbox and writes directly through its sole peer writer. The
    detached voice thread, stop flag/channel, polling/blocking helper,
    intermediate `Data` forwarding, unbounded audio subscription, and
    voice-specific reaper handoff are deleted.
  - Stop, round teardown, and hard `Drop` unsubscribe the exact synthetic
    connection before releasing its input lease. iOS, which has no local
    audio service for this path, has an explicit permanently-pending disabled
    select branch so the shared source remains platform-coherent without
    creating a worker/runtime/fallback.
  - No dependency, listener, service, Android foreground-service lifetime,
    recorder coordinator, incoming controlled-voice authority, host
    configuration, or privileged helper behavior changed.

- Counted confined evidence on the final pre-publication source state:
  - Pinned Rust 1.75 compiled the library test target from the repository's
    authenticated offline vendor closure in immutable development image
    `sha256:da876c1ffa017736b2f63d56f8b106956d6b4d730ebbf3e99feffda42ac0b91c`.

## 2026-07-28 — R-S11eg/R-S11e-151 controlled video-frame acknowledgement ownership

- Source-proven defect:
  - `src/server/video_service.rs` retained one process-global unbounded Tokio
    acknowledgement channel and one pending connection-ID set keyed only by
    numeric display index.
  - Monitor display 0 and camera display 0 therefore shared the same channel
    receiver and overwrote the same display entry despite being distinct
    controlled sources. Their capture loops could steal each other's
    acknowledgements, prematurely complete, or wait until timeout.
  - The old waiter counted any distinct dequeued connection ID rather than
    requiring that ID to be a target of the current frame. Duplicate and
    unrelated events accumulated in the unbounded queue.
  - Displayless `VideoReceived` and disconnect wake searched an overwritten
    display-only map. Process-global notifier entries survived capture-loop
    retirement.
  - Every 300-ms wait was an ordinary function annotated with
    `#[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]`, constructing and destroying a
    Tokio runtime on the dedicated synchronous capture thread.
  - This is source-proven cross-source frame-pacing integrity, availability,
    and resource-lifecycle debt shared by controlled desktop builds and
    Android's controlled service path. It is not proof of the reported Android
    screen-control hang, a screen/camera authorization bypass, exploitation,
    compromise, privilege escalation, public exposure, container escape, or a
    host RustDesk/service/firewall/network modification.

- Corrected ownership model:
  - Each live controller is keyed by exact
    `(VideoSource, display_idx)` and owns one
    `VideoFrameAckState` containing only the current pending and acknowledged
    connection-ID sets.
  - The process index retains only `Weak` state references, admits at most 64
    live controller generations, rejects an already-live stream key, prunes
    retired weak entries, and removes a registration only when the dropping
    controller's exact `Arc` still owns that key.
  - `GenericService::send_video_frame_with_targets` snapshots current
    subscriber IDs under the service write lock, installs that exact round
    before enqueueing the frame to any subscriber, and therefore closes the
    fast-local-dequeue-before-ownership race.
  - Explicit dequeue acknowledgement now carries connection-bound source,
    display, and connection ID. The legacy displayless peer acknowledgement
    and disconnect wake carry the connection-bound source and visit only live
    controllers for that source.
  - An acknowledgement changes state only when its connection ID is pending
    in the current local round, and each ID inserts at most once. Unrelated,
    duplicate, wrong-source, wrong-display, retired-controller, and
    over-capacity state does not widen the round.
  - Waiting uses one standard condition variable on the already-synchronous
    capture thread. It retains the 300-ms privacy/cancellation polling cadence
    and existing three-second pacing bound without a Tokio runtime, async
    mutex, channel backlog, detached worker, new listener, dependency, or
    protocol field.
  - The legacy displayless wire acknowledgement has no display or frame
    generation token. This slice therefore does not claim wire-level proof
    that a delayed acknowledgement belongs to a particular encoded frame; it
    confines that compatibility signal to a pending exact connection in its
    connection-bound source. A protocol-generation change would be a separate
    compatibility slice, not silently inferred here.

- Privilege and authority audit:
  - The new state machine is downstream of existing authenticated controlled
    connection admission. It does not create, grant, widen, persist, or
    deserialize a screen/input/camera capability.
  - A callback cannot manufacture another connection's ownership because the
    internal connection ID is supplied by the live `Connection`; the
    acknowledgement state accepts only IDs already snapshotted from that
    service's subscribers. Camera and monitor sources remain distinct even at
    the same display index.
  - Controller registration and retirement are exact in-memory lifetime
    operations. The weak registry is not a process-lifetime authority owner,
    and an old controller drop cannot remove a replacement generation.
  - No filesystem, credential, Unix ownership, group, capability, namespace,
    IPC endpoint, port, service manager, firewall, Docker socket, or device
    authority is introduced or exercised by the product change.
  - Production lock acquisition uses the repository's permitted poisoning-is-
    fatal `unwrap()` exception. No lock is held across `.await`; the new path
    creates no nested runtime and performs no async blocking.

## 2026-07-27 — R-S11ef / R-S11e-150 exact controlled-screenshot ownership

- Source-proven defect selected as the next coherent Ralph-loop slice:
  - R-S19 had separated monitor and camera screenshot capture by
    `(VideoSource, display_idx)`, but that pair was still the complete key of
    one process-global pending-request map. Two authorized controllers asking
    for the same source/display could not coexist: the later request silently
    destroyed the first request ID and response channel, leaving the first
    controller without a terminal response.
  - The stored request had no internal connection identity. Connection
    retirement therefore could not cancel pending or already-collected work,
    and a later connection reusing a numeric ID could not be distinguished by
    exact channel authority during cleanup.
  - Texture/VRAM fallback removed the singleton and later reinserted it. A
    request arriving during that interval could be overwritten by the older
    fallback work.
  - Every response spawned an unretained native PNG thread. Repeated requests
    therefore created process-detached work without one bounded admission or
    join owner.
  - This is controlled-side response-integrity, availability, and native
    resource-lifecycle debt shared by desktop controlled builds and Android's
    controlled service path. It does not establish the cause of the reported
    Android screen-control hang and is not an authorization bypass, privilege
    escalation, container escape, host modification, compromise, or public
    exposure.

- Corrected ownership and resource model:
  - Every admitted request ID must be nonempty, at most 128 bytes, and free of
    control characters. Admission records the internal connection ID and the
    exact Tokio response channel in addition to source/display.
  - `PendingScreenshots` retains at most 64 exact connection owners. Each
    owner has at most one in-flight request and one replaceable pending
    successor. Requests from different controllers coexist; only the pending
    successor from the same exact channel is replaced.
  - A matching frame collects every non-in-flight exact owner at that
    source/display. They share the captured pixels and one encoded PNG.
    Completion, retry, cancellation, and publication double-check numeric ID
    and `Sender::same_channel`; work from a retired/replaced channel cannot
    mutate or publish into its replacement.
  - `Connection::drop` synchronously retires both pending and in-flight
    screenshot authority for its exact channel. Poisoned-lock cancellation is
    logged instead of panicking in `Drop`.
  - Texture fallback requeues an exact request once only when no newer pending
    successor exists. It never overwrites the successor.
  - One process-lifetime retained `ScreenshotEncoder` worker owns a
    `sync_channel` with capacity two. Capture uses nonblocking `try_send`;
    startup failure, queue saturation, and unexpected worker retirement send
    explicit errors and complete only the exact still-current owners. The old
    per-response detached-thread shape is absent.
  - Dimensions are nonzero and bounded to 16,384 per side and
    8,192-by-8,192 total pixels; dimension multiplication is checked; RGBA
    length must equal checked width × height × 4. `BoundedScreenshotPng`
    refuses a write before its buffer crosses 32 MiB, and a post-encode bound
    remains as defense in depth.
  - No dependency, runtime, listener, Android service-lifetime, permission,
    root, or host configuration path was added.

  - The complete `scripts/dart-verify.sh` transaction passed in immutable

## 2026-07-28 — R-S11ee/R-S11e-149 exact-session screenshot ownership

- Source-proven defect:
  - `src/client/screenshot.rs` retained the most recent peer PNG in one
    process-global `Mutex<Screenshot>`.
  - `session_handle_screenshot` accepted a Flutter UI-session UUID but ignored
    it. Any live session could therefore save, copy, or discard whichever
    peer's response most recently replaced the singleton, and removing the
    owning `SessionHandler` did not destroy the bytes.
  - Every request used the UI-session UUID itself as its wire request ID.
    `pending_screenshot_sids: HashSet<String>` could not distinguish two
    successive requests from the same UI session, so a late response could
    satisfy a replacement request and an old file-picker callback could
    consume newer bytes.
  - Android's intentionally persistent process amplified the lifetime across
    task swipe/relaunch, but the defective Rust/Flutter path was shared by
    Android, iOS, and desktop Flutter. Simultaneous desktop sessions could
    collide without a process restart.
  - This is cross-session peer-data/resource ownership and stale-callback
    debt. It is not source proof of the reported screen-control hang, a
    controlled-side `MainService` defect, a local-to-root path, privilege
    escalation, exploitation, compromise, public exposure, container escape,
    or any host RustDesk/service/firewall/network change.

- Corrected ownership model:
  - The global cache, lock, type, and setter are deleted. The screenshot action
    helper receives a value-owned `bytes::Bytes`.
  - Each exact live Flutter `SessionHandler` owns at most one
    `OwnedScreenshot { request_id, data }`. Starting a request clears only that
    handler's prior value; handler removal destroys the bytes.
  - The current outgoing `Remote` owns a bounded
    `PendingScreenshotRequests` map. It retires any prior request for the same
    UI session, mints a checked monotonic `<ui-session>:<sequence>` wire ID,
    retains at most eight total mappings, and drops the map with the round.
  - A peer response is admitted only by removing its exact current mapping.
    Late, duplicate, replaced, oversized-with-stale-ID, and unrequested
    responses cannot publish into a session.
  - The targeted Flutter event carries the exact request ID. Save, copy, and
    discard carry both UI-session and request IDs. Only a double match
    atomically takes the bytes once; a stale mismatch leaves the current value
    untouched.
  - The established screenshot encoding, write, clipboard, discard, and
    mobile no-op clipboard behavior remain otherwise unchanged. No dependency,
    Android service-lifetime change, new thread/runtime, listener, or
    privilege path was added.

## R-S11e-167 Android shared serialization-gate diagnosis (2026-07-29)

- The product invariant is present:
  `MainService.rustSetByName` is exactly preceded by `@Keep` and
  `@Synchronized`; add/remove connection owner mutation and capture
  reconciliation occur inside that method.
- The focused Android ownership verifier already requires the exact
  `@Keep\n    @Synchronized\n    fun rustSetByName` sequence and its mutation
  removes `@Synchronized`. The independent workspace validator has the same
  exact current assertion and deliberate product mutation.
- The shared shell gate alone is defective. It uses:
  `grep -qA2 '@Synchronized' "$r_s14_kt" | grep -qF 'fun rustSetByName'`.
  GNU grep's `-q` suppresses selected output, including context output, so the
  downstream grep receives no bytes and deterministically fails even when the
  exact synchronized declaration is present. The neighboring generic
  `grep -qF '@Synchronized'` succeeds but cannot repair the empty pipeline.
- The minimal correction will replace both weak/redundant checks with one
  direct `awk` adjacency predicate over an exact annotation-only line followed
  by the `rustSetByName` declaration. The independent workspace validator will
  bind that shared assertion, forbid the retired quiet context pipeline, add a
  deliberate mutation, and bind the R-S11e-167 ledger.
- This is verifier alignment only. No Kotlin/product behavior, service
  persistence, capture/input resource ownership, APK/device state, host
  process/service/network/firewall/listener state, or release output is being

## R-S11ek/R-S11e-169 Android controlled-audio service-generation finding (2026-07-29)

- The fresh read-only Android source audit found a real adjacent
  process-persistent lifecycle defect:
  - native controlled callbacks and `InputService` already retain the exact
    monotonic `MainService`/server generation;
  - `VoiceCallAudioCoordinator` discarded that generation at its final
    process-wide audio boundary;
  - controlled connection and active-voice owners were only `Set<Int>`;
  - the playback `MediaProjection` had no service-generation owner; and
  - obsolete `MainService` teardown invoked a global
    `clearControlledConnections()` and unowned projection clear.
- Consequently, a delayed obsolete-service teardown could clear a replacement
  generation's live controlled voice or playback resource. Reuse of the same
  numeric connection ID is an ABA case because the old and replacement
  resources were indistinguishable at this boundary. Android Force Stop
  destroys the process and masks this class of stale ownership, while ordinary
  task removal intentionally retains the foreground/accessibility process.
- This is Android-only source-proven process-persistent resource,
  availability, and lifecycle debt. It is not proof of the separately reported
  outgoing Android-viewer-to-host screen-control hang, an authorization bypass,
  exploitation, root acquisition, privilege escalation, compromise, public
  exposure, container escape, or a host RustDesk/service/firewall/listener/
  network modification.
- Exact authority model:
  - controlled-resource admission starts closed;
  - only the positive exact generation returned by
    `FFI.startServer(this, ...)` may be installed;
  - a current active begin is idempotent and preserves its resources;
  - a newer generation atomically retires the predecessor's controlled
    connection/activity sets and playback projection before recorder
    reconciliation;
  - a cleared or superseded generation cannot be reactivated;
  - every controlled register/update/unregister/clear and projection update
    carries and matches the exact active generation; and
  - the separate outgoing session/generation voice owner survives controlled
    service replacement.
- Scoped implementation in progress:
  - `VoiceCallOwnerState.kt` owns the monotonic/active service generation and
    rejects stale or retired operations;
  - `VoiceCallAudioCoordinator.kt` serializes that transaction and stores the
    playback projection with its generation;
  - `MainService.kt` stays closed until the audio coordinator accepts the
    exact native generation and propagates that generation at all call sites;
  - `android-voice-call-owner-state-test.kt` covers monotonic replacement,
    same-ID ABA, stale update/clear, idempotent current begin, retired
    generation refusal, and controlled/outgoing overlap;
  - focused/shared/independent validators and R-S11ek, Appendix C #290, and
    R-S11e-169 are being updated to bind the complete source transaction.
- Explicitly out of scope and not claimed fixed by this slice: Android raw-video
  JNI flag ownership, companion-service status publication, a current APK or
  physical-device reproduction, exact cold R-B2/R-B10 artifacts, independent
  reproduction where separately required, and external review.
- No root/sudo, host service/process/network/firewall/port inspection or
  mutation, privileged container, device/socket mount, Docker port, Android
  service/capture/peer execution, APK/device action, or release build has
  occurred. The Ralph loop remains active.

## Newly exposed Android SDK self-test umask debt (2026-07-29)

- The first canonical wrapper created its private log by exporting
  `umask 0077` before invoking `scripts/verify.sh`. The verifier exited `1`
  before container execution with exactly one failed gate:
  `R-S11cr exact Android SDK output authority:
  transaction-self-test-failed`.
- Preserved failed log:
  `/tmp/ralph-verify-805b45a00b2ae320b69612623819d5a8f5bd02ba-exact.log`;
  mode `0600`; size `14,997` bytes; SHA-256
  `21fbd1965bee6c2e77e3ad046cd7135edcbd17c38a952bd87f7b1877dcc9deb1`.
- Source diagnosis:
  - `extract_packages()` creates the raw output root with
    `root.mkdir(mode=0o755)` but does not explicitly normalize that root;
  - the same function explicitly `chmod(0o755)`s its child directories;
  - `compare_output(..., profile="raw")` correctly requires the root to be
    `0755`;
  - under `umask 0077`, the raw root becomes `0700` and the transaction
    self-test fails with
    `Android SDK output mode differs from its profile: .`.
- A networkless, non-root, read-only-repository container reproduced the
  boundary exactly:
  - `umask 0022`: self-test exits `0`;
  - `umask 0077`: self-test exits `1` with the same root-mode diagnostic.
- The production acquisition container ordinarily uses the normal `0022`
  process mask, and the exact canonical rerun under that normal mask passed
  the unmodified transaction self-test and every later gate. This makes the
  first failure an invocation-exposed self-test/transaction umask-sensitivity
  defect, not an Android audio-generation regression and not permission to
  discard the failure.
- This is the next source-led Ralph-loop candidate. The likely minimal
  direction is explicit root-mode normalization after creation plus a
  deliberate restrictive-umask behavior fixture and focused/shared/independent
  mutation binding. It is not yet claimed fixed.

- No host root/sudo, host RustDesk/service/process/firewall/port/listener
  inspection or mutation, public listener, Docker port, host device/socket
  mount, APK/device action, Android service/capture/peer execution, online
  acquisition, or cold release build occurred. The canonical verifier's
  checked-in shell/Python authority fixtures execute in its ordinary
  host-side orchestration process while product compile/tests execute in its
  confined containers; no privilege escalation or host runtime was exercised.
  The Ralph loop remains active.

  - the parent previously sampled `$!` and `/proc/$pid/stat` immediately;

    the startup race.

    admission bound;

## R-S11el/R-S11e-172 exact Android listener-generation rebuild ownership (2026-07-29)

- Scope and diagnosis:
  - Android intentionally keeps its controlled-side listener alive in the
    foreground `MainService` when the Flutter task is removed. The retained
    foreground service is not itself the bug and was not removed.
  - The live R-T13 `ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback` called the
    generationless JNI `rebuildDirectServerListener()`, which unconditionally
    incremented a process-global rebuild epoch independent of the exact
    service/listener generation.
  - Android may deliver an already-queued network callback after the owning
    Service has begun destruction. A stale Service A callback could therefore
    advance the independent epoch after replacement Service B had started,
    causing B's listener to drop and rebind even though A no longer owned it.
  - A Kotlin-only generation comparison would not close the race: validation
    and epoch advancement must linearize with begin and exact stop in native
    state. This is process-persistent Android listener-availability/lifecycle
    ownership debt. It is not claimed as a physical-device causal
    reproduction of the originally reported outgoing viewer screen-control
    hang, an authorization bypass, compromise, root acquisition, public
    exposure, container escape, or host RustDesk/service/firewall/listener/
    network modification.

- Final state-machine design:
  - `AndroidListenerLifecycle { generation, rebuild_epoch, active }` is held
    behind one Android `Mutex`.
  - Successful begin checked-adds and allocates exactly one nonzero generation,
    resets its rebuild epoch, and marks that ownership active.
  - Exact stop succeeds only for the active matching generation and marks it
    inactive. It does not allocate or consume another generation ID. A delayed
    obsolete Service stop cannot deactivate a replacement generation.
  - Exact network rebuild checks active ownership and matching generation and
    checked-adds the epoch while holding the same lock. A stale callback cannot
    validate A and then advance B's epoch.
  - The exact lifecycle snapshot returns an epoch only for an active matching
    generation. The accept loop therefore exits on exact deactivation or a
    newer begin, and rebinds only when the epoch changes while the same
    generation remains active.
  - Generation-allocation exhaustion and rebuild-epoch exhaustion fail closed
    by deactivating current ownership. Zero/stale operations do not mutate
    current state. The obsolete `ANDROID_SERVER_GENERATION`,
    `LISTENER_REBUILD_EPOCH`, and generationless JNI/API surface are absent.
  - The first implementation draft made stop consume a generation by
    checked-add. Review found a terminal-state defect: at `u64::MAX`, stop
    could not advance and could leave the listener classified active. That
    draft was not accepted. The explicit `active` bit and non-allocating exact
    stop are the corrected design; exhaustion tests bind both terminal cases.
  - Kotlin retains the exact positive generation returned from
    `startServer(this, ...)` in a `@Volatile Long`, passes it through the
    Boolean JNI rebuild call, and logs rejected stale callbacks distinctly.
    `onDestroy()` releases controlled capture/voice/input resources, then
    deactivates its exact listener generation before draining the handler and
    unregistering the network callback.
  - JNI rejects non-positive signed generation values before conversion. Pure
    Rust tests cover current rebuild, wrong-stop preservation,
    stop/replacement, same-process stale-callback ABA, zero inputs, generation
    exhaustion, and rebuild-epoch exhaustion.

- Tracked contract and verifier integration:
  - R-S11el and Appendix C #293 make exact service-generation rebuild
    ownership normative in `requirements.html`.
  - `scripts/verify-android-listener-generation.py` is the focused independent
    gate and rejects 34 deliberate production/JNI/Kotlin/requirement/ledger/
    shared-gate regressions.
  - The shared Android ownership gate incorporates this boundary and rejects
    385 deliberate mutations.
  - `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` binds the focused verifier, its
    mutation catalog, the shared gate, and the tracked requirement/ledger.
  - Stale comments describing exact stop as a generation bump or
    “supersession” were corrected after the first complete catalog. The final
    comments precisely distinguish exact deactivation from supersession by a
    newer begin.
  - Synchronized normative requirements SHA-256 is
    `16795a46a1a70a6f10505ce474c8a94b99e4f3707d0a74ebb45345d793e56a7c`.

- Confined compilation and behavior evidence:

### R-S11en/R-S11e-175 authored-tree Android MainService status and explicit-stop ownership

- Source/history proof:
  - The inherited `MainService` companion published `_isReady` and `_isStart`
    without a service generation. A delayed predecessor projection callback
    or teardown could therefore change process-visible status belonging to a
    replacement service.
  - The inherited `MainActivity` binding used `BIND_AUTO_CREATE`. Its
    `stop_service` call invoked a public `MainService.destroy()` method, which
    called `stopSelf()` but did not retire the Activity binding. The Activity
    could report success while the binding postponed the service's
    `onDestroy()`, which is the sole owner of controlled-capture release,
    exact listener deactivation, callback-owner release, network-callback
    removal, and wake-lock release.
  - `git blame` traces the companion publication and duplicate destroy path to
    the original upstream import `c2abd3b3`; the binding wrapper is inherited
    from `790754c6`. This is not a Docker-created lifecycle or a host-service
    change.
  - Android's official service guide states that a service which is both
    started and bound is not destroyed after stop until every client unbinds:
    `https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services`.
    `Context.stopService` documents the same `BIND_AUTO_CREATE` finality:
    `https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/Context#stopService(android.content.Intent)`.

- Corrected ownership model:
  - `MainServiceStatusOwner` is the single private, synchronized,
    process-visible status authority. Its immutable snapshot carries the exact
    positive native service generation and MediaProjection readiness.
  - A current-generation begin is idempotent and preserves readiness. A newer
    generation resets readiness. Zero, regressed, retired, and superseded
    generations are refused. Only the exact active generation may publish
    readiness or retire the snapshot.
  - `MainService` begins status only after `FFI.startServer` returns a positive
    exact generation, uses that generation for projection install/release/stop
    publication, and retires it during `onDestroy`. Companion `_isReady`,
    `_isStart`, and their getters are absent.
  - The unread `RdClipboardManager` process-global capture-status replica and
    its writers were deleted instead of wrapping dead state in another owner.
  - Passive Activity attachment uses binding flags `0` and therefore cannot
    recreate a missing service. `BIND_AUTO_CREATE` remains only for explicit
    initialization when no service snapshot is published.
  - One idempotent Activity unbind helper owns binding retirement. Explicit
    Stop calls `Context.stopService` for the explicit service intent and then
    unbinds the Activity client. `MainService.onDestroy` remains the single
    resource teardown. The public `destroy()` and its duplicate `stopSelf()`
    path are absent.
  - The published snapshot is observation only. Capture, listener,
    authorization, connection, voice, and input resources retain their
    existing exact service-generation owners.

### Selected follow-up: Android task-removal versus Activity-resume owner claim

- The next coherent slice was selected only after re-inventorying the
  purpose-specific IPC endpoints and the process-persistent Android outgoing
  session surfaces. The named service-control, SAS, PulseAudio, whiteboard,
  desktop-URL, connection-manager, clipboard, media-worker, reconnect-round,
  screenshot, audio, input, listener, raw-video, status, and explicit-stop
  source slices are already closed and gated. Their exact cold release,
  installed/native/device, independent-reproduction, and external-review
  evidence classes remain open and are not being relabeled as source work.
- A new source-proven Android outgoing-owner race remains in
  `MainActivity.stoppedClientSessionOwners` and
  `MainService.onTaskRemoved()`:
  1. `MainActivity.onStop()` records its exact generation/session owner.
  2. `MainService.onTaskRemoved()` calls
     `takeStoppedClientSessionOwners()`, which copies and clears that map.
  3. Native voice/session retirement occurs only after the synchronized map
     operation has returned.
  4. The same stopped Activity may enter `onStart()` in that check/use gap.
     Because its marker has already disappeared, it resumes the exact native
     owner successfully.
  5. The service then unregisters and closes that same exact owner after the
     Activity has become visible, leaving the Activity with retired native
     admission.
- This is a classic split check/use lifecycle transition. Exact generation
  identity prevents an obsolete callback from selecting a *replacement*
  Activity, but it does not prevent task removal from retiring the very same
  generation after that generation has concurrently resumed.
- Android's official lifecycle documentation states that a stopped Activity
  instance can return through `onRestart()`/`onStart()` and that
  `onStart()`/`onStop()` may occur multiple times. The `Service.onTaskRemoved`
  contract is a separate running-service callback when the user removes an
  application task. Those independent component callbacks provide no
  repository-level atomicity for the map-copy/native-close sequence:
  - https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/activity-lifecycle
  - https://developer.android.com/guide/components/activities/state-changes
  - https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Service#onTaskRemoved(android.content.Intent)
- Correct authority model selected for implementation:
  - Each stopped exact owner is in one of two explicit process states:
    `STOPPED` or `RETIRING`.
  - Activity resume atomically claims a `STOPPED` record before native resume.
    If it wins, task removal cannot claim or close that owner.
  - Task removal atomically changes `STOPPED` to `RETIRING` before releasing
    the state lock. An Activity that observes `RETIRING` must fail closed and
    finish; it may not call native resume.
  - Native voice/session retirement runs outside the Kotlin state lock, so a
    potentially bounded worker join is not hidden under that monitor.
