    Wrong-session, stale-generation, duplicate, and replacement callbacks
    cannot remove another owner.
  - The persistent incoming `MainService`, listener, MediaProjection, capture,
    and controlled connection resources remain running and are not used as a
    cleanup mechanism.
- This mechanism is Android-specific. It is consistent with a process-lifetime
  owner becoming incoherent until process death, but it is not claimed as a
  physical-device causal reproduction of the reported one-host
  screen-control symptom; a current APK/device sequence remains required.
- No source has yet been edited for this slice. No root/sudo, host
  RustDesk/service/configuration, firewall/UFW/nftables/iptables,
  listener/port, Android service/capture/peer, APK/device, VM/libvirt, Docker
  execution, online acquisition, or public-network action occurred during the
  proof and selection phase.

### Rejected R-S11eo candidate: Android callbacks are serialized in this process

- The proposed task-removal versus Activity-resume race above was re-audited
  before publication and is not a real callback interleaving in this
  application. Android's official processes-and-threads contract states that
  components of one application run in the same process and main thread by
  default, and that lifecycle callbacks for components in that process are
  dispatched on that thread:
  `https://developer.android.com/guide/components/processes-and-threads`.
- The repository manifest declares both `.MainActivity` and `.MainService`
  without `android:process`; the `<application>` likewise has no process
  override. `MainService.onTaskRemoved()` and `MainActivity.onStart()` are
  therefore serialized on the same application main thread. The latter cannot
  run after the stopped-owner map clear but before the synchronous JNI
  close/join returns from the former.
- Android's Activity contract still permits a stopped instance to return
  through `onRestart()`/`onStart()`, and the service contract still delivers
  `onTaskRemoved()` when a running service's application task is removed.
  Those facts do not imply concurrent delivery. The missing threading proof
  was decisive.
- The native owner audit independently showed that, once
  `close_android_client_owner` retires the exact generation/UUID,
  `resume_android_client_owner` refuses it because the active native
  `session_id` is absent. A later serialized `onStart()` therefore fails
  closed even after task-removal cleanup.
- A draft `STOPPED`/`RETIRING` Kotlin state machine, fixture, R-S11eo/#297
  requirement text, ledger text, and focused/shared/independent gate changes
  had been authored but not committed. They were all removed with
  `apply_patch` after this contradiction was established. `git diff
  --exit-code`, `git diff --check`, and `git status --short --branch` then
  proved the repository and index exactly clean at published
  `cb6efb3634ee5878ef696cc4ebbe040c47bfcba9`.
- No commit or push was made for the rejected candidate. It is not being
  relabeled as a security or availability fix, and no R-S11eo/R-S11e-176 or
  Appendix C #297 entry remains in the tracked tree.
- The preliminary confined verifier/Kotlin/Gradle runs performed while the
  candidate was under review are historical harness evidence only; they do
  not validate a retained product change. They used the previously recorded
  non-root, networkless, read-only-source/offline-input container boundary.
- No root/sudo, host RustDesk/service/process/configuration,
  firewall/UFW/nftables/iptables, listener/port, APK/device, VM/libvirt, or
  host namespace action occurred. The only online reads in this correction
  were the official Android developer documentation pages named above. The
  broader Ralph loop remains active.

## 2026-07-30 — R-S11eo/R-S11e-176 mobile outgoing-session preparation finality

### Source-proven mechanism

- The retained correction is distinct from the rejected same-main-thread
  Android callback race above. The outgoing Flutter viewer synchronously
  invoked `sessionAddSync` for every new mobile route.
- Native `session_add` deliberately removes prior mobile sessions and calls
  `close_and_join` on each exact predecessor I/O worker. That worker owns and
  drains its media children. Exact joining is required finality and must not
  be detached, timed out, or weakened.
- flutter_rust_bridge 1.80.1 implements `SyncReturn` by running the Rust
  closure inline. Ordinary bridge functions use its fixed normal worker pool.
  The exact predecessor join therefore ran on Flutter's main Dart isolate and
  could freeze the outgoing mobile UI while correctly waiting for native
  finality.
- Mobile add errors were printed and converted into a live-looking UUID. The
  non-web event stream had no `onError` or `onDone`, and native
  `session_start_` installed the event handler before attempting
  `start_io_thread` without rollback on false/error. A route could remain on
  “Connecting...” with no live I/O worker.
- Android's intentionally process-persistent service/process lifetime
  amplifies retained outgoing state after task swipe, but the synchronous
  authored mobile path is shared by Android and iOS. The missing stream
  finality handling was shared non-web Flutter code. This is source evidence
  for a real outgoing availability/resource-finality defect; it is not
  physical-device reproduction of the reported one-host symptom and is not a
  defect in the controlled-side persistent `MainService`.

### Corrected resource model

- `session_add_mobile` is one typed, concrete `Result<()>` normal bridge
  operation. Generated FRB output proves
  `Future<void> sessionAddMobile(...)` dispatches with
  `_platform.executeNormal(FlutterRustBridgeTask(` and does not use
  `_platform.executeSync`. A native mutex serializes the complete
  predecessor close/join plus replacement insertion transaction.
- The synchronous add and existing-session attach entries reject Android/iOS
  before mutation. The exact native join remains synchronous inside the
  bridge worker; no nested runtime, detached cleanup, deadline, or dependency
  was added.
- `MobileSessionStartQueue` retains exactly one running request and one
  replaceable pending request. New pending work supersedes and completes the
  prior pending request. Exact pending cancellation does not interrupt an
  admitted native finality transaction; an exact running close receives and
  awaits that running request's completion even when a newer successor is
  pending.
- Each admitted request carries its exact generated session UUID. After
  asynchronous add it rechecks current ownership; a stale request closes only
  its captured native UUID. Both stale-entry and persisted-current close paths
  cancel/await exact preparation before their final close, eliminating the
  close-before-add gap.
- The quality-monitor option read moved after successful native insertion, so
  asynchronous add did not create a new option-read race.
- `session_start_` now handles false and error admission as one exact
  transaction rollback: remove the exact session handler, drop its stream,
  and close/join the exact session when it was the last handler. It does not
  forge the normal `"close"` stream marker before returning the bridge error.
  The Rust regression blocks that exact failed worker, proves rollback waits,
  and proves an unrelated replacement UUID remains present and unclosed.
- `SessionStreamFinality` distinguishes an expected exact native close marker
  from unexpected stream error/end. Unexpected finality is admitted once,
  rejects stale UUIDs, retires the exact native session, dismisses loading,
  and shows a bounded nonsecret Connection Error.

## 2026-07-30 — R-S11ep/R-S11e-177 macOS raw runtime-PRS credential IPC

### Finding and authority correction

- Current-tree review found a direct contradiction between the existing
  normative R-S11i raw-only credential-replica contract and the macOS
  implementation. The LaunchDaemon returned
  `PermanentPasswordSnapshotResult { storage, salt }` as a serde/JSON framed
  generic `_service` response. The LaunchAgent decrypted that durable storage
  envelope only to install a nonpersistent PRS.
- Existing installed-app audit-token proof, exact live
  `--server --service-owned-server` argv, launchd PID/path, and root-owned
  parsed LaunchAgent plist proof constrained the recipient. The finding was
  therefore protocol-separation, least-disclosure, and secret-memory-ownership
  debt, not evidence of exploitation, unauthorized disclosure, root
  acquisition, public exposure, or host modification.
- The corrected surface removes the generic credential request/response and
  storage/salt handler. Generic macOS `_service` retains only nonsecret
  liveness and Authorization Services right-readiness control.
- macOS now shares the canonical raw `_service_credential` wire protocol with
  Linux. The endpoint is mandatory and root-scoped, has independent fixed
  transaction and Security.framework-proof capacities, and is rejected by
  both generic IPC constructors.
- The root listener snapshots the accepted socket's uid, effective-pid
  metadata, and `LOCAL_PEERTOKEN` before spawning accepted work. A bounded,
  exactly owned Security.framework worker proves the installed-app peer before
  even the bodyless UUID request is read. After that request, a second exact
  proof binds the same connected peer to trusted installed-app code, exact
  live argv, launchd-reported PID/path, and the root-owned exact LaunchAgent
  plist before a password-equivalent value is disclosed.
- The root authority derives the typed canonical PRS-or-empty locally and
  returns only the operation-bound empty-or-44-byte raw replica through the
  fixed wiping `SensitivePassword` transport. No durable storage envelope,
  salt, serde/JSON value, `Bytes`/`Framed` value, or generic service response
  crosses the endpoint.
- The LaunchAgent client first requires the exact service-owned-server process
  role. It connects to uid 0's raw credential path under one absolute
  deadline, proves the connected root privileged helper from its audit token
  and trusted installed location before sending the bodyless request, checks
  the response UUID and canonical PRS shape, and installs only the
  nonpersistent runtime PRS overlay. Refresh failure clears that overlay
  directly rather than invoking the retired storage-envelope runtime API.

## 2026-07-30 — Android outgoing-viewer lifecycle drain and persistent-process coherence

### Reported symptom and source-proven finding

- The reported Android sequence was: connect as a viewer, swipe the UI task
  away while the deliberately persistent RustDesk foreground service keeps the
  application process alive, reopen the UI, and observe that screen control can
  hang for one host while file transfer or a different target still works.
  Android App Info → Force Stop, which terminates the retained process and
  service, restores screen control.
- This audit did not operate the Android device or reproduce that sequence.
  Source analysis therefore does not claim that the corrected lifecycle defect
  was the exact cause of that incident or identify a particular decoder,
  network session, or worker as the one observed on the device.
- Source did prove a real Android-specific availability/resource-finality
  defect. `MainActivity.onCreate`, Activity teardown/failure paths, and
  `MainService.onTaskRemoved` synchronously crossed JNI into begin/retire
  operations. Those operations removed the exact outgoing owner and called
  `Session::close_and_join` while holding the Android owner transition lock.
  The join waits for the outgoing I/O worker and its native video/audio/voice
  children. Android Activity and Service callbacks share the application main
  thread by default; a correct but slow drain could therefore freeze component
  lifecycle delivery and the next Activity in the retained process.
- File transfer succeeding did not disprove a stale or blocked screen-control
  session: the protocol/session trees and worker finality paths are distinct.
  Force Stop helping is consistent with process-lifetime state being discarded,
  but remains corroborating behavior rather than causal proof.
- The defect is source-proven on Android because of its direct component
  lifecycle JNI path. iOS retains the existing off-UI synchronous mobile-add
  drain and has no Android lifecycle coordinator. No matching installed iOS,
  macOS, Windows, or Linux runtime failure is claimed.

### Corrected ownership and finality model

- Lifecycle callbacks now perform only the exact authority transition:
  generation/UUID admission is advanced or validated, exact handlers and peer
  sessions are removed from live admission, and the complete owned
  `ClientOwnerDrain` is transferred with nonblocking `try_send` to one retained
  process-lifetime coordinator worker. The callback returns without waiting for
  close/join finality.
- The public JNI/Kotlin operation is named `retireClientSessions`; its return
  count means removed from live admission, not already joined. Existing
  persistent `MainService` listener/capture ownership was not weakened or
  removed.
- The coordinator owns one named retained `JoinHandle`, one bounded queue slot,
  and checked monotonic issued/completed tickets under one mutex/condition
  variable. A request owns every removed handler/session. Its worker emits the
  exact close events, joins each exact I/O/media tree, performs the existing
  mobile key release, advances only the next exact ticket, and wakes waiters.
- One slot is sufficient because replacement admission is ticket-gated: after
  a live tree is transferred, another live tree cannot be inserted until that
  inherited drain finishes. Additional Activity transitions may replace
  generation authority, but cannot manufacture another admitted peer tree.
- Android's asynchronous serialized mobile-add path waits the captured exact
  predecessor ticket and then revalidates generation/UUID authority before
  insertion. The ordinary Android `session_add` replacement path removes its
  predecessor under owner admission, releases the owner read guard before
  `close_and_join`, and reacquires/revalidates the exact owner before inserting
  the successor; the reacquired guard is retained through insertion.
- Review of the first draft found that it still held the owner read guard while
  joining a prior mobile tree. That would have made a component callback
  waiting for the write guard indirectly wait on the same worker finality and
  would have falsified the nonblocking guarantee. The final source splits that
  lock/finality region and adds a second executable blocked-worker regression
  specifically for this case.
- Coordinator creation/loss, queue failure, ticket exhaustion, worker panic,
  progress-lock/condition-variable poisoning, or out-of-order completion
  fail-stops the process. Cleanup is neither detached nor reported complete
  without exact finality. No timeout, per-retirement thread, unbounded queue, or
  fallback state reset was added.

- Requirement R-S11eq and Appendix C #299 specify the Android
  component-thread boundary, exact ticket/owner model, prohibition on retaining
  owner admission across predecessor finality, fail-stop transfer behavior,
  renamed JNI/Kotlin surface, and both blocked-worker proofs.
- `scripts/verify-android-client-lifecycle-drain.py` is a focused independent
  source interpreter for this slice. Its baseline passed and all 39 deliberate

  `--source-mutations-only` catalog passed against the final exact source.

  `1843750ba46d5dd61b531d378ed349c87719a81b2abb34ffdfaadbd1423aa9fe`;

## 2026-07-30 — Desktop lock-screen mechanism authority and dormant launcher deletion

### Source-proven path and finding

- The two controlled-side product actions are the authenticated Remote
  `LockScreen` special-key edge in `Connection::handle_input` and the
  configured lock-on-disconnect action in `Connection::on_close`. Both
  converge on `handle_owned_lock_screen` and
  `lock_screen_with_key_handler`; there are exactly two product consumers.
- The compile-time selector's live Linux branch emits an owned physical
  Meta+L chord. Its live macOS branch emits an owned physical
  Control-Command-Q chord. Only the Windows branch called a platform
  function. The generic final `else` previously obscured that exact target
  split.
- Separate public Linux and macOS platform functions remained compiled even
  though whole-tree current-source and history review found no product caller:
  Linux resolved and spawned `xdg-screensaver lock`; macOS executed the private
  `CGSession -suspend` image. They were dormant conceptual command/API surface,
  not runtime fallbacks. Earlier R-S11r/R-S11t/R-S11e-3/R-S11e-32/
  R-S11e-34/R-S11c-10k inventories had incorrectly described them alongside
  reachable child-image paths.
- Windows called the native `LockWorkStation` function but discarded its
  Boolean result. A real initiation failure was therefore reported as success
  to the owned input path.
- This is stale compiled authority surface, inaccurate reachability accounting,
  and Windows result-visibility debt. No execution of either deleted helper,
  privilege escalation, exploitation, unauthorized access, public exposure,
  host modification, or causal relationship to an observed RustDesk
  connection incident is claimed.

### Primary-source design research

- The freedesktop xdg-screensaver manual at
  `https://portland.freedesktop.org/doc/xdg-screensaver.html` defines `lock`,
  limits the tool to use inside a desktop session, and explicitly discourages
  root invocation. A process launcher was therefore not a correct generic
  cross-context lock abstraction, quite apart from being product-unreachable.
- Apple Support's current Mac keyboard-shortcuts documentation at
  `https://support.apple.com/en-us/102650` documents Control-Command-Q as the
  screen-lock shortcut. The existing owned-input path already used that exact
  mechanism.
- Microsoft Learn's `LockWorkStation` contract at
  `https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-lockworkstation`
  specifies a nonzero BOOL only when asynchronous initiation succeeds, zero on
  failure, and `GetLastError` for extended failure information. It also limits
  the call to the interactive desktop and expressly says nonzero does not
  prove final locked state.
- The Rust Reference's conditional-compilation contract and the pinned
  `cfg-if` macro behavior support the source-level conclusion that one matching
  platform branch is emitted. The separately defined Linux/macOS platform
  functions were not fallback branches.

### Corrected mechanism model

- `src/platform/linux.rs` deletes `XDG_SCREENSAVER_PATHS`, its resolver, the
  public `lock_screen` function, command construction, descriptor-policy call,
  and spawn. The fixed-command inventory now contains only the retained xrandr
  and systemctl sets.
- `src/platform/macos.rs` deletes the public `lock_screen` function and the
  entire `CGSession` command/output path.
- `src/server/input_service.rs` names all three compile-time branches
  explicitly. Linux and macOS retain only their connection-owned physical
  chord dispatches. Windows calls `crate::platform::lock_workstation()?`; no
  generic platform lock name, compatibility alias, external-helper fallback,
  shell, or second mechanism remains in those platform modules.
- `src/platform/windows.rs` names the operation by its actual native authority
  as `lock_workstation() -> ResultType<()>`, checks `LockWorkStation() ==
  FALSE`, captures `GetLastError`, and returns an error through the existing
  owned input path. Success is described only as asynchronous initiation.
- A focused Linux unit regression invokes the production selector through an
  owned event sink and proves exactly four events: Meta down, physical-map L
  down, physical-map L up, Meta up.

### Normative and verifier bindings

- R-S11er and Appendix C #300 specify the three explicit mechanisms, both
  dormant-helper deletions, Windows failure propagation, Linux behavior proof,
  and the prohibition on inferring native Windows/macOS or release evidence.

  then-present dormant helpers from reachable child paths.

## 2026-07-30 — Windows viewer keyboard interception authority and dormant Sciter hook deletion

### Source-proven path, history, and finding

- `src/platform/windows.cc` retained a TigerVNC-derived
  `WH_KEYBOARD_LL` implementation with one process-global hook thread, mutable
  target/default `HWND` values, a selected-system-key `PostMessage` relay,
  `win_down` and `stop_system_key_propagate` ambient booleans, and native
  enable/disable/toggle/state entry points. Rust wrappers in
  `src/platform/windows.rs` exposed that complete surface.
- History review proved that the sole product enable call was the deprecated
  Sciter frame initialization in `src/ui.rs` at the imported baseline
  `c2abd3b`. Commit `0d2c882` deleted the Sciter UI and that caller. Current
  Flutter had no enable call, yet Remote/ViewCamera pointer enter/exit and
  Remote disposal continued to call `hostStopSystemKeyPropagate`; those calls
  changed only the dormant Boolean. `keyboard::legacy_keyboard_mode` and
  `Session::send_mouse` continued to read `get_win_key_state`, although only
  the never-started hook callback could update that state.
- The live Flutter viewer already has a separate keyboard path:
  `change_grab_status` serializes `Run`/`Wait` ownership in
  `GrabOwnerState.owner: Option<u128>` using the full per-window session UUID,
  stale owners cannot release a replacement, and the rdev event stream updates
  `MODIFIERS_STATE` for both left and right Meta before conversion.
- This was live-looking dead behavior, redundant global input-interception
  surface, and a misleading modifier-state fallback. It is not evidence that
  the dormant hook ran, captured a key, enabled privilege escalation,
  modified the host, caused an Android or connection incident, or represented
  a compromise.
- The controlled-side privacy-mode hook in
  `src/privacy_mode/win_input.rs` is a distinct Remote-only local-input
  suppression mechanism with its own R-S19a lifecycle. It remained present
  and positively bound by the new gates; it was not confused with or deleted
  as the retired viewer path.

### Primary-source design research

- Microsoft Learn's `SetWindowsHookEx` contract at
  `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowshookexw`
  identifies `WH_KEYBOARD_LL` as a global-only hook and warns that global hooks
  affect applications on the same desktop and consume shared resources.
- Microsoft Learn's `LowLevelKeyboardProc` contract at
  `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/lowlevelkeyboardproc`
  requires the installing thread to pump messages, states that the callback
  runs before asynchronous key state is updated, documents timeout-driven
  silent hook removal on newer Windows, and recommends raw input for most
  monitoring use cases.
- Flutter's Windows architecture documentation at
  `https://docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/windows/building` describes
  the Windows runner as the owner of the Win32 window and message loop. The
  retained Sciter-target `HWND` relay was therefore not an appropriate hidden
  compatibility layer for the Flutter runner.
- Inspection of `libs/enigo/src/win/win_impl.rs` established an important
  final detail: `Enigo::Key::Meta` maps to `VK_LWIN`, while
  `Enigo::Key::RWin` maps separately to `VK_RWIN`. Direct fallback therefore
  must query both keys before merging the owned rdev event state.

### Corrected authority and lifecycle model

- `src/platform/windows.cc` deletes the complete dormant viewer hook, hook
  thread, target/default window state, posted-key relay, ambient booleans, and
  native functions. It retains the unrelated platform code that followed it.
- `src/platform/windows.rs` deletes the corresponding native declarations and
  `enable_lowlevel_keyboard`, `disable_lowlevel_keyboard`,
  `stop_system_key_propagate`, and `get_win_key_state` wrappers. No
  compatibility alias or constant-result replacement remains.
- `src/flutter_ffi.rs` deletes `host_stop_system_key_propagate`.
  `remote_page.dart` and `view_camera_page.dart` delete every call and the
  pointer regions that existed only to toggle the dormant state; Remote
  disposal deletes its toggle-only fallback. `flutter/lib/web/bridge.dart`
  deletes the web stub. Freshly generated FRB output therefore has no such
  operation.
- Viewer interception remains solely under the existing exact-session rdev
  grab owner. Legacy-key modifier fallback queries both Enigo `Meta` and
  `RWin`, merges those point-in-time OS states with tracked left/right Meta
  event state before the Win+L special-key decision, and later merges the full
  modifier set for outbound events. The viewer mouse path likewise queries
  both Windows keys and merges the tracked modifier state before sending.
- No second hook, ambient Boolean, Sciter `HWND`, posted-key relay, FFI toggle,
  Dart toggle, or empty compatibility wrapper remains.

### Normative and verifier bindings

- R-S11es specifies the exact-session rdev owner, both direct Win-key queries,
  tracked modifier ordering, complete native/Rust/FFI/Dart deletion, and
  privacy-hook separation. Appendix C #301 records the historical defect and
  bounded disposition without making an exploitation or incident-causality
  claim.
- `HARDENING_STATUS.md` records R-S11es/R-S11e-180 as source implemented and
  confined integration/semantic/mutation green while explicitly leaving

- `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` independently interprets those

## 2026-07-30 — Windows dormant fixed-temp diagnostic append authority

### Current-source proof, history, and classification

- `src/platform/windows.cc` defined an upstream-imported
  `void flog(char const *fmt, ...)` helper. Its complete effect was to call
  `fopen("C:\\Windows\\temp\\test_rustdesk.log", "at")`, silently return if
  the pathname could not be opened, format caller-controlled diagnostic text
  through `vfprintf`, and close the stream.
- The only other whole-tree occurrence was an already-commented
  `flog("%s %s\n", currentname, inputname)` call in
  `inputDesktopSelected`. Exact searches found no live C/C++ caller, header,
  Rust declaration, generated/native binding, Flutter FFI operation, export
  definition, build-map reference, script, test, or supported diagnostic-file
  feature.
- `git blame` and `git log -S` attribute both the helper and commented call to
  upstream-import commit `c2abd3b`; neither acquired a live caller afterward.
  `build.rs` still compiles `src/platform/windows.cc` for Windows, so retaining
  the dead function preserved source/API surface in the privileged-capable
  native translation unit. Current source does not prove that dead-section
  elimination retained it in any final artifact or that it ever executed.
- Adjacent native functions initially examined as possible residue were
  proved live and left unchanged:
  `get_session_user_info` and `get_available_session_ids` have Rust callers in
  `src/platform/windows.rs`, and `AddRecentDocument` backs the live
  `add_recent_document` wrapper.
- This is dormant conceptual pathname/file-write authority and misleading
  debugging residue. It is not evidence that the helper ran, that a particular
  installation's `C:\Windows\Temp` ACL was unsafe, that an unprivileged party
  could create a redirect there, that privilege escalation, exploitation, or
  host modification occurred, or that this path explains any Android,
  RustDesk-host, screen-control, file-transfer, firewall, listener, or network
  symptom.

### Primary-source design research

- Microsoft Learn's MSVC `fopen`/`_wfopen` contract at
  `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/fopen-wfopen?view=msvc-170`
  documents that `"a"` opens the named file for writes at end of file and
  creates it when absent. That is pathname-based append behavior; it does not
  establish that an existing or created object is an application-owned,
  identity-checked diagnostic sink.
- Microsoft Learn's `GetTempPath2` contract at
  `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-gettemppath2a`
  documents privilege-aware temp-directory selection. For a SYSTEM process,
  its normal result is the protected `C:\Windows\SystemTemp` default, and
  Microsoft explicitly identifies prevention of common path-redirection
  problems as the reason for that design. The API also warns that callers
  still must verify path existence and adequate access.
- Microsoft Learn's `CreateFile` contract at
  `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilea`
  documents the distinction created by
  `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT`: without it, opening an existing symbolic
  link normally returns a handle to the target. The dormant C-runtime helper
  performed no equivalent reparse/object-identity check. This supports the
  conceptual design finding; it does not prove that a usable redirect existed
  on any specific machine.

### Correct authority model and implementation

- Diagnostic file output is permitted only through an explicitly supported,
  lifecycle-owned sink whose producer and object authority are defined. This
  fork has no supported caller or native diagnostic-file feature for `flog`,
  so the helper owns no file authority.
- `src/platform/windows.cc` deletes the entire helper and its commented call.
  No alternate temp directory, environment-selected pathname, compatibility
  alias, constant stub, feature flag, guard, or replacement file logger was
  added.
- The unrelated `<cstdio>` include remains because the live
  `alloc_console_and_redirect` path still calls
  `freopen("CONOUT$", "w", stdout)`. No adjacent live session or
  recent-document native API was deleted or modified.
- Normative R-S11et and Appendix C #302 bind the complete deletion, primary
  authority rationale, bounded non-incident classification, exact source
  absences, and still-open native/release evidence. The requirements SHA-256
  is
  `bf704ac9bf2f5a70a33c96dc170f9872a9e440f27279c79358e778b2f79548f1`;
  both `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md` and the active trailing hash ledger in
  `HARDENING_STATUS.md` record that exact value.

### Verifier construction and confined evidence

- `scripts/verify.sh` adds the extracted R-S11e-181 shared source gate. It
  rejects any `flog(` definition/call or `test_rustdesk.log` pathname in the
  native source and requires the independent semantic validator, R-S11et,

- `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` independently checks:

  - `// flog(` commented-call absence;
  - catch-all `flog(` absence;
  - `test_rustdesk.log` absence;

  - the normative helper/path/GetTempPath2/no-replacement contract;

- Seven deliberate mutation families restore a minimal native helper, restore

- In immutable Rust 1.75 devcheck image
  `sha256:da876c1ffa017736b2f63d56f8b106956d6b4d730ebbf3e99feffda42ac0b91c`,

## 2026-07-31 — R-S11eu/R-S11e-182 exact-generation Android video-worker and screen-state ownership

### User report, scope, and causal boundary

- The user reported two operational symptoms in binaries which they stated
  predate the entire current nineteen-day development loop:
  - an Android outgoing viewer could retain a process-persistent background
    service across task swipe, then hang screen control for one controlled host
    until Android App Info `Force Stop` killed the process; file transfer still
    worked and another controlled host could still connect;
  - a Windows outgoing viewer could develop up to approximately ten seconds of
    display delay after losing focus while input/control remained responsive;
    reconnecting cleared the display delay.
- Those reports establish a cross-platform display/freshness investigation
  requirement; they do not prove one common cause. No installed Android,
  Windows, or Debian artifact was read, replaced, launched, or instrumented in
  this slice. The reported operational binaries predate the source changes
  below, so those source changes cannot have caused the already-installed
  behavior, but source review alone also cannot prove that they fix it.
- This slice therefore remains narrowly classified as controlled-side Android
  process-persistent state/worker ownership debt discovered during that
  investigation. It is not a causal reproduction or closure of the outgoing
  viewer focus/background delay. R-S11eb separately owns outgoing viewer
  replacement and final drain; the explicit cross-platform performance mandate
  remains open in `HARDENING_STATUS.md`.

### Source findings and corrected ownership model

- Before this slice, Android raw-video and screen-state operations could cross
  MainService lifetime boundaries through process-global state and ambient
  reads:
  - the process-global raw frame buffer and screen geometry were not uniformly
    owned by the exact positive MainService generation;
  - stale video workers could observe, drain, or mutate state belonging to a
    replacement service generation;
  - video/display/capturer construction did not carry one exact generation
    through every consumer;
  - generic Java name-based state access remained in the screen/half-scale path;
  - encoder bitrate calculation could consult ambient Android display scale
    instead of the scale captured with the generation-owned display.
- `GenerationOwnedScreenSize` now combines monotonic exact-generation ownership
  with the optional screen geometry. Begin, update, read, and retirement reject
  zero, stale, retired, or replaced generations; stale retirement cannot clear
  a replacement generation.
- `GenerationOwnedFrameRaw` and the JNI raw-video entry points now bind frame
  enablement, publication, consumption, and retirement to the exact positive
  MainService generation. A stale worker cannot drain or disable its
  replacement's raw buffer.
- Android `Display`, `CapturerInfo`, capturer reads, display service, connection
  display enumeration, `Server`, and `VideoService` retain and forward the
  exact generation. Android controlled-server construction rejects a missing or
  zero generation. Android `CLIENT_SERVER` remains a separate outgoing
  voice-audio-only server with no controlled display/video generation.
- Kotlin `MainService` publishes screen geometry through the typed
  `FFI.updateScreenInfo(generation, width, height, scale)` operation and exposes
  a typed serialized `rustSetHalfScale(Boolean)` callback. The retired generic
  screen getter/setter/refresh path is absent.
- The Android display scale is captured with its generation-owned display and
  retained in VPX configuration and the live encoder. `base_bitrate` is again a
  pure resolution calculation; the validated scale-square adjustment is applied
  from the retained encoder scale, not from mutable ambient MainService state.
- Callbacks into MainService reject zero or non-current generations before
  entering the typed Java operation, and fallible half-scale mutation propagates
  failure instead of silently discarding it.

## 2026-07-31 — R-S11ev/R-S11e-183 shared outgoing-viewer video mailbox

### Source/history finding and bounded correction

- Commit `edc8a3b9e4bdd48995741568ccae95b648d94293` changed the shared
  `MediaData` decoder channel to capacity eight but left non-key video frames
  in a separate 120-frame `ArrayQueue`. The producer retained a frame before
  nonblocking admission of its separate `MediaData::VideoQueue` wake token.
  Channel-full therefore dropped the token while preserving the frame; the
  decoder popped one frame per surviving token. Equal producer/consumer rates
  after a stall could preserve that tokenless backlog indefinitely.
- The source mechanism is directly consistent with responsive control and
  delayed display, with reconnect destroying the incoherent queue/token pair.
  At one frame per second, the eight-entry token offset is consistent with
  roughly eight seconds of display lag. Exact operational Windows/Android
  artifact identities and a device reproduction are absent, so this is not
  recorded as proof of the observed cause or closure of the broader
  focus/background latency report.
- R-S11ev removes the split frame/token protocol. Each display now owns one
  mutex/condition-variable mailbox whose ordered `VecDeque` retains frames and
  controls directly. Frame and control counts are independently bounded to
  eight. Checked generations own independent-frame replacement, overflow,
  refresh, stale/decode-error retirement, reset, and the pre-publication
  current-generation check. Viewer receipt through completed decode has a
  one-second freshness budget.
- Sender/receiver close or Drop clears retained work, rejects producers, wakes
  the decoder, and preserves the prior exact-worker join/reaper authority.
  Counter underflow and generation exhaustion fail closed. The direct
  `crossbeam-queue` dependency is removed from this crate; its transitive lock
  record remains for other dependencies.

## 2026-07-31 — R-S11ew/R-S11e-184 exact Flutter software-RGBA publication

### Source finding and bounded correction

- The inherited software-render handoff stored one `RgbaData { data, valid }`
  per display across all Flutter UI sessions. While `valid` remained true,
  every newer decoded frame returned before replacement or notification. A
  throttled, backgrounded, or suspended Dart consumer could therefore retain
  the oldest unconsumed image indefinitely while decode and input/control
  continued. Event-stream replacement did not replay that ready publication.
- The display-only acknowledgement also had no UI-session or publication
  identity. A late async completion or another UI session could clear
  successor/peer work. The exported `session_get_rgba` returned a pointer into
  a Rust `Vec` after releasing its lock, and Dart held the pointer-backed
  `Uint8List` across asynchronous image decode while teardown could retire the
  allocation.
- R-S11ew replaces that state with exact `(SessionID, display)` mailboxes and
  positive, checked, nonreused handler-wide publication tokens. Each mailbox
  holds one stable published frame, at most one latest-wins pending semantic
  frame, and empty reusable capacity. Exact-token acknowledgement drains or
  promotes only the newest pending frame under a new token. Stale/duplicate
  tokens do nothing; exhaustion and event-delivery failure fail closed.
- Stream rebind replays every ready exact display/token or visibly fails the
  session start. Session/owner/display retirement removes only exact obsolete
  mailboxes. No live eligible software consumer means no retained frame. The
  display-only generic trait operations, raw C pointer symbol, and
  size-then-pointer protocol are deleted.
- Dart now copies the exact publication through the generated bridge while
  Rust holds the mailbox read lock, then owns those bytes through asynchronous
  image decode. The common one-consumer decoder-to-mailbox path still swaps
  buffer ownership without a copy. The bridge boundary adds a software-render
  copy and is explicitly awaiting device/fallback allocation and throughput
  profiling; this is a correctness choice, not a performance verdict.

### Confined evidence

- Fresh production-style Flutter Rust Bridge generation completed from the
  exact working source with pinned Rust 1.75, Flutter 3.24.5, LLVM 15.0.6,
  FRB 1.80.1, sealed Pub/Cargo inputs, and no network. The generated signatures
  bind `sessionCopyRgba(session, display, publication) -> Uint8List?`,
  exact-token acknowledgement, and the two-field RGBA event. The generator
  repeated its existing nonfatal `Dart_Handle` typedef-redefinition diagnostic;
  success is not relabeled as a clean native bridge verdict.
- The complete pinned Linux Flutter-feature graph compiled, and all five
  `r_s11ew_` Rust behaviors passed: stable publication/latest-only promotion;
  exact session/display isolation; no-consumer nonretention; exact display
  retirement; and publication-exhaustion failure.
- Targeted analysis of the touched Dart model/bridge files reported no errors,
  one pre-existing warning, and fifteen pre-existing informational diagnostics.
  This is not a clean whole-app analyzer claim.
- The focused semantic verifier rejected all 36 deliberate mutations. The
  existing Android outgoing-owner verifier rejected all 438 mutations after
  incorporating the legitimate replay rollback and exact mailbox retirement.
  The independent semantic baseline passed.
- The complete unsliced independent source-mutation catalog was restarted from
  mutation one after each verifier correction and ultimately passed beginning
  to end. Earlier attempts exposed three verifier-authority defects: mismatched
  diagnostic identity for duplicated exact-key anchors, mismatched pending-slot
  labels, and a stale Android drain mutation fixture which omitted exact RGBA

## 2026-07-31 — R-S11ex/R-S11e-185 exact desktop Flutter texture lifecycle

### Source finding and bounded correction

- The inherited desktop Flutter texture model launched pixelbuffer and GPU
  creation through detached `Future.then` continuations. Destroy inspected
  fields populated by those continuations, so a destroy requested before
  initialization completed could return without owning the late work.
  Display switching removed an owner before its arbitrary 100-millisecond
  delayed teardown completed, and page disposal did not await texture
  retirement before closing the native UI session.
- Tab-to-window transfer intentionally reuses a connection UUID and replaces
  the native UI handler, but desktop `clientOwnerId` had been that same UUID.
  Late work from the retired view could therefore not be distinguished from
  its replacement and could register or unregister the replacement renderer.
- Every desktop `FFI` view now receives a fresh UI-owner UUID independent of
  the connection UUID. Pixelbuffer and GPU registration carry both values
  through authored Dart, fresh generated bridge output, Rust FFI, and native
  renderer admission. A same-session native regression proves that a retired
  owner can neither replace nor clear the replacement owner's pixelbuffer.
- One explicit Dart lifecycle now owns initialization, publication, matching
  unpublication, and one exact release future. Retirement is visible before
  its first wait, drains late initialization, forbids late publication,
  reports callback failures, and makes repeated retirement share exact
  finality. A per-display serialized slot waits for predecessor retirement
  before creating a replacement and bounds synchronous construction failure.
- Both desktop page disposers synchronously invalidate the texture model and
  await its complete drain before native UI/session close. Fixed-delay
  ownership is absent. A retiring texture clears a Dart UI texture ID only
  when that exact ID is still installed, and does so in `finally` so a native
  unregistration exception cannot leave the retired UI ID displayed.

## 2026-07-31 — R-S11ex/R-S11e-185 repository-owned native RGBA renderer lifecycle

### Source finding and bounded correction

- Follow-on read-only review of the exact pinned
  `flutter_texture_rgba_renderer` revision
  `42797e0f03141dc2b585f76c64a13974508058b4` found native ownership debt
  beyond the already-published app-side lifecycle correction. Windows used
  asynchronous unregister while destroying callback state before completion
  and then unregistered again from the texture destructor. macOS unregistered
  but retained its renderer-map entry. Linux used process-global raw-pointer
  state, leaked the plugin-owned `GObject` reference, and had no buffer/mutex
  finalizer.
- Windows and Linux also retained the oldest unconsumed native frame while
  discarding newer producer frames; macOS replaced its data but emitted
  redundant availability notifications. That is source-proven
  bounded-presentation-freshness debt consistent with focus throttling, not
  proof that it caused the reported operational delay.
- The exact upstream Apache-2.0 package is now a provenance-bound,
  non-publishable path dependency at
  `flutter/third_party/texture_rgba_renderer`. The upstream license and macOS
  podspec are byte-identical; the two CMake files differ only by the added
  derivation notice. The Pub lock and acquisition validators now expect seven
  Git dependencies rather than treating the upstream RGBA checkout as
  executable dependency authority.
- Windows reserves an empty exact-key owner slot before callback registration,
  installs the registered texture through a no-throw `shared_ptr` move, retires
  and extracts the exact node on close, and retains both texture and Dart
  result through unregister completion. Callback-setup failure restores the
  retired node for retry. The texture destructor has no second unregister and
  exceptions cannot cross the Rust C ABI.
- Linux owns one renderer map per plugin, removes and retires before
  synchronous unregister, releases the exact plugin-owned reference, drains
  on plugin disposal, and finalizes both buffers and the mutex. Pending and
  presented buffers have separate dimensions, so failed frame notification
  discards only pending bytes/metadata and cannot return a valid prior pointer
  with zero dimensions.
- macOS removes the exact dictionary entry, serializes frame admission and
  retirement, invalidates registry/data state before unregister, copies
  stride-aware rows, keeps one latest pending pixel buffer, and coalesces
  availability until raster consumption.
- All three implementations validate typed arguments, dimensions, stride
  alignment, overflow, and source length, copy into plugin-owned storage, keep
  at most one latest pending frame, and reject publication after retirement.
  The separate GPU texture plugin is not corrected or claimed by this slice.

## R-S11ez/R-S11e-187 — cancel pending native texture publication at retirement

### Source finding and authority model

- Linux `texture_rgba_retire()` and Windows `TextureRgba::Retire()` initially
  set only a retired Boolean. Their copy callbacks tested pending-frame state
  first, so one pre-close queued frame could still be promoted after retirement
  began. The focused verifier required that unsafe Linux order. macOS already
  clears its texture identity, pixel data, and pending marker under one serial
  queue.
- This is source-proven close/replacement resource-finality debt, not evidence
  of use-after-free, exploitation, host changes, public exposure, renderer
  execution, or the reported focus-delay cause.
- Retirement now serially refuses new admission, detaches and cancels only the
  unconsumed pending frame and metadata, and makes the copy callback fail before
  pending promotion. Previously presented storage remains owned until registrar
  unregister/finalization; retirement does not prematurely free it.

### Native callback evidence

- A new Linux native regression includes the production plugin translation unit,
  links Flutter's real Linux embedder library, creates the actual
  `FlPixelBufferTexture` subclass, and dispatches notifications through an
  interface-conforming fake `FlTextureRegistrar`.
- The unchanged pre-fix implementation compiled but the test failed because a
  pending frame crossed retirement and no retirement diagnostic was returned.
  The corrected implementation's warnings-fatal native run passes: stride
  packing, latest-pending replacement, notification coalescing,
  failed-notification rollback with prior-frame preservation, retirement
  cancellation, continued presented-frame ownership through finalization,
  retired-callback failure, and later frame rejection.
- A second regression compiles and executes the exact production
  Windows `texture_rgba.cpp` on Linux against a minimal test-only implementation
  of the Flutter registrar/pixel-buffer interfaces it consumes. It passes the
  corresponding latest-frame, coalescing, notification-failure, retirement,
  presented-buffer-lifetime, null retired-callback, and later-admission cases.
  This is portable execution of the Windows callback core, not native Windows
  headers, ABI, compiler, engine, registrar, renderer, or package evidence.
- Earlier isolated AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer invocations emitted
  passes, one test per container. The sanitizer environment is not reliable evidence:

  a fresh final-tree rerun reproduced the same failure with the Linux test alone and

## R-S11fa/R-S11e-188 — exact viewer presentation-resume recovery

### Source finding and recovery authority

- The outgoing peer session correctly survives ordinary mobile backgrounding and
  desktop focus loss, while Android's controlled-side foreground `MainService`
  correctly survives Activity task removal. None of the four outgoing viewer pages
  had a corresponding display-plane recovery edge. Mobile RemoteDesktop resumed
  only clipboard synchronization, mobile ViewCamera ignored application lifecycle,
  and desktop RemoteDesktop/ViewCamera restored input or wake state without
  invalidating delayed video work or requesting a new independently decodable
  frame. Retained desktop tabs also lacked selected-page recovery ownership.

  display-only lag while file transfer and input remain responsive. It is not a
  reproduction or causal claim about the older operational artifacts, not a reason
  to remove the persistent Android controlled-side service, and not evidence that
  a host service, listener, firewall, network, container, or machine was changed.
- Each RemoteDesktop/ViewCamera page now owns one `PresentationRecovery` state.
  Mobile non-resumed states, desktop blur/minimize, and desktop deselection mark
  one recovery pending. Initial and duplicate resume events do nothing. Desktop
  tab owners propagate the actual selected key to every retained page; hidden tabs
  retain recovery until selected. The first selected exact-current page invokes
  the existing `sessionRefreshVideo` path, whose native sink invalidates the local
  video mailbox generation/GOP before sending a display-specific or legacy peer
  refresh. It neither reconnects nor changes service/listener ownership.

## R-S11fb/R-S11e-189 — bounded controlled-video egress and exact writer completion

### Source finding and ownership correction

- Controlled capture pacing previously treated dequeue by the connection task as
  progress even though the ordinary keyed send then entered the separate bounded
  512-command sole-writer FIFO. A slow/non-reading display plane could therefore
  accumulate obsolete already-sealed frames while input and file-transfer planes
  remained responsive; reconnect destroyed the backlog. This is a shared-source
  mechanism consistent with the report, not a reproduction or causal claim about
  unidentified older Android, Windows, or Debian artifacts.
- Each controlled connection now owns one bounded video mailbox: one wake token,
  one latest display switch, at most 32 display slots, and one frame-or-refresh
  outcome per display. Frame identity carries immutable monitor/camera source,
  display, and checked monotonic generation. Fresh/switch-cleared displays suppress
  deltas until an independently decodable frame; replacement that would break a
  GOP retires the exact affected rounds and requests exact-display refresh. Ready
  displays recur round-robin, display switch precedes successor video, and no
  mailbox lock crosses a wait.
- The existing keyed sole-writer FIFO remains the only transport writer and nonce
  owner. A tracked video command carries one non-cloneable one-shot completed by
  that exact command's `SinkExt::send` result. At most one tracked video write is
  pending per connection; only exact `Ok(())` advances the matching source/display/
  generation/connection round. Teardown closes receiver admission and retires the
  trusted exact connection ID; stale service-subscriber enqueue after closure
  returns its new identity for retirement.
- Displayless peer acknowledgement fields were unused in this fork, could not bind
  display or generation, and had no sender. Their protobuf tags are reserved and
  local exact writer completion owns pacing. Writer completion proves neither peer
  receipt nor decode/publication/presentation and does not eliminate or measure
  kernel/TCP buffering.

### Privilege and authority result

  privileged operation, service action, installer path, shell helper, listener, socket,

  `no-new-privileges`, bounded CPU/memory/PIDs, private tmpfs, no port/device/Docker-socket
  mount, and no host namespace.

### Source finding and correction

- Rust previously loaded `FlutterRgbaRendererPluginOnRgba` as a void function. A missing
  symbol skipped the call but still consumed `render_notified`; Windows/Linux/macOS native
  admission results were discarded; and the caller ignored `StreamSink::add` failure.
  A failed native publication or failed exact-session UI enqueue could therefore suppress
  later first-image notification until an independent reset or reconnect.
- A new `FlutterRgbaRendererPluginTryOnRgba` symbol returns canonical C `int` one/zero.
  Rust loads only the new symbol and fails closed when absent. The old void symbol remains
  as a compatibility delegate, so a new executable never interprets an old void ABI's
  indeterminate return value. Windows propagates the production texture core result and
  maps validation/exception to zero; Linux propagates the production mark result; macOS
  propagates its serialized Swift owner result while its registry notification remains a
  void platform API.
- Rust commits the first-image bit only after both native acceptance and exact UI-stream
  enqueue. Native rejection does not invoke the UI closure; UI rejection leaves retry
  pending; later dual acceptance commits once; a missing stream consumes nothing. No
  timer, queue, reconnect, background service, session owner, or control/file/input path
  changes.

## 2026-08-01 — R-S11fd/R-S11e-191 macOS launchd service-record authority

### Source proof and classification

- The root LaunchDaemon's raw `_service_credential` handler authenticates the accepted
  Unix peer from its socket audit token, proves the installed app code identity, checks
  exact live `--server --service-owned-server` argv, parses the exact root-owned
  LaunchAgent plist, and then calls `launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>` as the final
  launchd-ownership corroboration before releasing the root PRS runtime replica.
- `src/ipc.rs::macos_launchctl_print_value` flattened that nested diagnostic output:
  it trimmed every line, split the first `=`, compared keys case-insensitively, and
  returned the first `pid` or `path` at any depth. The caller first converted stdout
  through `String::from_utf8_lossy`, accepted those two independent first matches, and
  did not reject duplicate, unbalanced, or trailing records.
- The socket audit-token signing/path proof, exact live argv, and trusted parsed root
  plist remained independently load-bearing. This is therefore a conceptual privileged
  service-record ambiguity and deterministic correctness defect, not a demonstrated
  promptless local-to-root primitive, proof of exploitation, or evidence of a host,
  service, firewall, network, container, or installed-artifact change.

### Research and intended authority

- Apple documents explicit launchd service targets and `launchctl print` as an
  inspection path, while its current Service Management sample exposes registration
  status and does not offer a public typed PID/plist service-record API suitable as a
  drop-in replacement. The diagnostic query remains only fail-closed corroboration;
  it is not promoted to a typed or independently sufficient trust source.
- The privileged receiver may return the replica only when strict UTF-8 begins with the
  exact requested target header and one balanced outer dictionary contains exactly one
  top-level canonical nonzero peer PID and exactly one top-level already-trusted plist
  path. Nested fields never count; duplicates, imbalance, trailing records, lossy text,
  PID-only/path-only matches, or parser fallback reject. The audit-token, argv, and root
  plist proofs remain mandatory before and after this diagnostic step.

### Implemented source and gates

- `src/ipc.rs` replaces the depthless parser with
  `macos_launchctl_service_identity`, strict UTF-8, exact target/header and balanced-depth
  parsing, exactly-once top-level `pid`/`path`, canonical PID text, and exact tuple
  comparison. The launchctl child uses `/` and a cleared environment containing only
  fixed `LC_ALL=C`; the existing non-stdio descriptor policy remains.
- Five pure regressions cover exact acceptance, nested substitution, duplicate
  top-level authority, wrong target/trailing data, invalid UTF-8, and noncanonical PID.
- `scripts/verify-macos-service-credential-ipc.py`, the shared and Apple gates, and
  `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` bind the parser, command environment, exact
  caller decision, behavior names, R-S11fd/R-S11e-191, and Appendix C #312 with focused
  and independent deliberate mutations.
- `requirements.html` and `HARDENING_STATUS.md` record the exact source scope and keep
  native signed macOS launchd/Security.framework execution plus exact artifact/cold
  release evidence open. Verification and publication results are pending at this point
  in the work log and will not be retroactively described as already run.

## 2026-08-01 — R-S11fe/R-S11e-192 bounded macOS launchd proof-child resources

### Finding and unchanged authority model

- The preceding R-S11fd correction made the root LaunchDaemon's final
  `/bin/launchctl print gui/<uid>/<label>` parser strict, but the fixed child still
  ran through `std::process::Command::output()`. Rust 1.75 documents that API as
  waiting for completion while capturing stdout and stderr. The call therefore
  retained growable stdout and unused stderr buffers without an explicit byte
  ceiling inside the one-second exactly owned proof worker.
- This was bounded-resource and fail-closed availability/finality debt, not new
  caller-selected execution authority. The executable, argv, UID and label target,
  working directory, environment, and descriptor policy were fixed. Socket
  audit-token/code-signing identity, exact live argv, trusted parsed root-owned
  LaunchAgent plist, strict R-S11fd record parsing, and final code revalidation all
  remained independently mandatory. No exploitation, promptless local-to-root path,
  compromise, or host modification was demonstrated.

### Source correction

- `src/ipc.rs` transfers the outer Tokio absolute deadline into the exactly owned
  blocking worker. The launchctl child receives null stdin and stderr and one piped
  stdout descriptor made nonblocking with `fcntl(F_GETFL/F_SETFL | O_NONBLOCK)`.
- One synchronous owner drains through an 8 KiB stack buffer into a vector which can
  never exceed the fixed production ceiling of 256 KiB. It polls the same direct
  child and sleeps for at most two milliseconds between non-ready checks. A child
  deadline reserves 50 milliseconds inside the outer proof deadline for termination,
  reap, and worker join.
- Zero limit, pre-spawn elapsed deadline, missing stdout pipe, nonblocking setup
  failure, read failure, status-poll failure, byte overflow, or child deadline
  expiry fails closed through the same termination-and-reap owner. Only stdout EOF
  plus a successful exit status reaches the strict R-S11fd parser. Cleanup failure
  is retained in the diagnostic, while the pre-existing process-fatal outer exact-
  worker-ownership backstop prevents detached continuation.
- The helper remains deliberately scoped to the fixed OS child. It is not presented
  as a general process-tree sandbox and grants no caller-selected image, argv, limit,
  deadline, parser, or credential fallback. No thread, async task, nested runtime,
  queue, detached reader, dependency, or listener was added.

  `/usr/bin/printf` is accepted exactly at its 12-byte test ceiling;
  `/usr/bin/yes` exceeds a 4 KiB ceiling and is terminated before its one-second
  deadline; and `/bin/sleep 5` is terminated at a 50 ms absolute deadline. The final
  locked/offline Rust 1.75 run compiled the full library test target from the audited
  read-only Cargo vendor closure and passed 3/3 tests with 410 filtered in 0.05 seconds.

## 2026-08-01 — R-S11ff/R-S11e-193 exact outgoing-viewer refresh admission

### User report, source finding, and evidence classification

- The motivating operational report remains: after Android task removal, reopening the
  app could leave outgoing screen presentation hanging while file transfer still worked;
  Android Force Stop plus reopen restored presentation. A comparable Windows-client
  focus-loss case could accumulate up to roughly ten seconds of display delay while
  control input remained prompt; reconnect restored display presentation. The Android,
  Windows, and Debian artifacts in that report predate this source slice by weeks.
- Read-only source tracing found a concrete shared client-flow defect, but did not prove
  it was the sole or actual cause of those operational symptoms. Presentation recovery,
  manual refresh, renderer changes, and decoder/backlog recovery all ended at
  `Session::refresh_video`, which placed a peer refresh message on the same unbounded
  generic UI-command queue as unrelated work. Local video generation invalidation did
  not happen until the network loop eventually dequeued that command. Flutter's FFI
  returned void, silently ignored a missing session, and carried only the connection
  UUID rather than the exact UI-owner UUID. Native decoder/backlog call sites ignored
  refresh-admission failure.
- The implemented classification is therefore exact, bounded source-path closure
  consistent with delayed recovery—not an operational reproduction, proof of causation,
  or claim that the reported Android/Windows issue is fixed. No host RustDesk process,
  service, listener, installed binary, firewall, network state, configuration, Android
  device, Windows client, Debian endpoint, renderer, capture source, or peer was used.

### Implemented exact-round flow

- Every ordinary outgoing viewer round owns a `ViewerVideoRefreshReceiver`. Its fixed
  pending state is either one all-display request or a FIFO of at most 16 distinct
  display identities, plus one capacity-one Tokio wake. Duplicates coalesce without
  bypassing closure observation, all-display supersedes pending display identities,
  admission is synchronous/nonblocking, and capacity or closed-round conditions are
  explicit errors.
- The already-owned I/O worker is spawned behind a capacity-one standard-library start
  gate. Successful spawn ownership publishes the exact round sender before gate release;
  spawn failure, close before publication, or a disconnected start gate cannot report
  admission. Reconnect removes predecessor admission before joining it and publishing a
  successor. Final close removes admission before predecessor finality.
- Final manual review found a narrower retirement race after the first complete catalog:
  activation released the sender-slot lock after publishing the sender but before
  releasing the worker gate, while `close()` published retirement before acquiring that
  lock. Close could therefore land in that interval and still allow the worker to start
  before the existing connection-round cancellation stopped it. That earlier behavior
  and 3,450-entry catalog evidence were superseded. Activation now holds the sender-slot
  write guard through `start.send(receiver)`, while close acquires the same write guard
  before publishing round retirement and `close_requested`. Publication/gate release and
  retirement now linearize wholly in one order.
- The network loop selects the refresh receiver independently of the generic UI queue,
  invalidates the exact display or all live video generations before its sole writer
  sends the peer request, and closes the round on send failure. A refresh found on the
  generic queue is a fail-closed contract violation. The broader generic command queue
  remains unbounded and is not claimed fixed.
- Flutter's authored helper and every lifecycle, toolbar, recording, and transferred-
  session caller carry `clientOwnerId`. Empty display inventory is an error. The concrete
  result-bearing FFI validates the protocol display range and holds the session registry
  plus exact UI-owner guard through nonblocking admission. Native display admission holds
  the live peer-inventory guard through exact-round sender selection. Decoder/backlog
  recovery treats failed admission as terminal instead of waiting indefinitely for an
  unrequested keyframe.

  Debian builder image

## 2026-08-01 — R-S10/R-S11e-16 constant-time permanent-password confirmation

### Source finding and classification

- The fresh privileged credential-path audit found one live secret comparison in
  `prompt_unattended_password`: the hidden `rustdesk --password` confirmation used
  `password == confirmation`. `SensitivePassword` implemented `PartialEq` with ordinary
  Rust byte-slice equality and also implemented `Eq`. Neither the language/API contract
  nor that generic trait surface guaranteed the content-independent comparison required by
  R-S10; future call sites could also regain `==` without naming secret-comparison intent.
- This was not evidence of host compromise, a demonstrated local privilege escalation, a
  network exposure, or the reported Android/Windows session-display fault. The comparison
  occurs between two values entered by the same local operator before the existing
  user-owned/service-owned credential routing and receiver authorization. It is classified
  as a source-level secret-handling and API-safety defect in the privileged R-S11e-16
  provisioning ingress.

### Implemented authority model

- `SensitivePassword` now exposes only the purpose-named
  `constant_time_eq(&SensitivePassword)` operation for equality. It delegates to the
  vendored sodiumoxide wrapper around libsodium `sodium_memcmp`. Generic `PartialEq` and
  `Eq` implementations are deleted, so ordinary `==` cannot compare password bodies.
- The hidden terminal confirmation calls that explicit method and still erases the
  confirmation before returning either success or mismatch. Existing validation, the
  4096-byte ceiling, exact CLI shape, noninteractive stdin path, credential routing, raw
  protocol, and receiver authority are unchanged.
- A focused Rust regression covers equal bytes, a same-length last-byte mismatch, and an
  unequal-length mismatch. The shared verifier and embedded Apple structural analyzer pin
  the exact call and libsodium primitive, forbid both generic equality traits and the old
  call, and require the behavior regression. The Apple analyzer rejects deliberate
  call-site, primitive, and trait-restoration mutations.
- The independent workspace verifier binds product source, shared and Apple gates, R-S10's
  exact `MUST` wording, Appendix C #121, the hardening ledger, its own single dispatch, and
  ten deliberate mutations spanning those surfaces. The requirements identity is
  `c4d4b802d3821b27fc73020c888983c7f0e189e06c65b9b0d00603047d4700f8`.

### Counted confined verification

  live installed-ownership routing, Linux service credential bootstrap/replica/finality state

  ordinary-IPC credential writer, service-owned user-profile fallback, caller-selected
  privileged action, relative privileged executable, or ambient privileged command environment
  was proved. One apparent double-lock was explicitly disproved against numbered source; it was
  overlap in a combined diagnostic display, not repository code.

  defect: it is unbounded, high-frequency input/control/file commands share it, and UI/CLI send
  paths discard send errors. A correct replacement needs count and byte bounds, explicit
  overflow finality, exact-round cancellation, and preserved command ordering. A count-only
  Tokio-channel substitution would be a shortcut because one post-key frame may be up to the

  review; doing another broad speculative redesign without current native reproduction would
  compound the operator's stated risk.

  FFI admission await a peer result would change coalescing, request identity, version
  compatibility, server topology validation, timeout ownership, and presentation-recovery
  semantics. A wire ACK that merely confirms a service option write would not prove fresh-frame
  presentation and therefore must not be introduced as cosmetic certainty.
- No repository byte, host RustDesk state, process, listener, service, configuration, firewall,
  network state, installed binary, or container image was changed. The worktree remained clean.

## 2026-08-01 — Windows exact-token child environment audit

### Proven composition defect

- The privileged Windows process-creation audit traced `launch_windows_service_server` through
  `launch_process_in_session_with_env` into native `LaunchProcessWin`, then separately reviewed
  the retained token sources, explicit application/current-directory construction, atomic job
  assignment, terminal-helper suspended launch/resume path, and disposable named-pipe client
  impersonation worker. No second live impersonation site, missing `RevertToSelf`, caller-selected
  service image, inherited handle, pre-job execution window, or ignored null process result was
  found in those reviewed paths.
- One concrete cross-change defect was proved in `LaunchProcessWin`. The 2026-07-09 helper-proof
  environment merge made the `as_user=FALSE` Windows service child pass a non-null custom block
  containing its supervisor PID and creation-time proof variables. The 2026-07-20 environment-
  finality correction constructed a non-inherited token environment only inside `if (as_user)`.
  Those changes composed into a near-empty two-entry environment for the LocalSystem service
  child. Without extra variables, the same branch would instead have passed null and inherited
  the supervisor's ambient environment. Neither behavior derives launch context from the exact
  token selected for `CreateProcessAsUserW`.
- Microsoft documents that `CreateEnvironmentBlock` with a non-null token retrieves that token's
  environment, `bInherit=FALSE` excludes the current process environment, and a null
  `CreateProcessAsUserW` environment inherits the calling process environment. The trusted
  winlogon token already carries the documented `TOKEN_QUERY | TOKEN_DUPLICATE` rights required
  for a primary-token environment query. The corrected policy is therefore one non-inherited
  block for every selected token, followed by case-insensitive replacement of launcher-owned
  proof variables.

### Implemented closure and evidence boundary

- `LaunchProcessWin` now treats environment construction and nominal-null rejection as
  unconditional post-token-selection gates. The user-helper behavior is unchanged. The
  `as_user=FALSE` service child now starts from its exact LocalSystem token environment; its two
  supervisor identity entries still replace same-name values, and caller ambient state is not
  inherited. Construction failure remains terminal before job attributes or process creation.
- The focused shared gate now extracts the exact native launcher and rejects any restored
  `if (as_user)` environment gate. The semantic validator requires one exact-token construction
  site and correct failure/null/merge/launch ordering. A deliberate valid nested-`if` mutation
  preserves the old ordering markers while making construction conditional, proving that the
  new unconditionality assertion—not an incidental assertion—rejects that regression.
- In immutable image
  `sha256:da876c1ffa017736b2f63d56f8b106956d6b4d730ebbf3e99feffda42ac0b91c`,
  Bash syntax, Python compilation, the normal semantic validator, and the complete in-memory
  source-mutation matrix passed with read-only source, numeric UID/GID 1000:1000, no network,
  no pull, read-only root, all capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges`, and bounded
  CPU/memory/PIDs/tmpfs. The first complete mutation attempt correctly refused credit because
  the mutation was killed by an older ordering assertion; the mutation was changed to preserve
  ordering and target only unconditionality, and the complete matrix then exited zero.
- The pinned Linux image contains no Windows SDK/MinGW headers, so no native Windows compile or

  `RuntimeBroker_rustdesk.exe` directly from
  `src/privacy_mode/win_topmost_window.rs::PrivacyModeImpl::start`.

## 2026-08-01 — outgoing viewer generic command-plane resource/finality audit

### Proven residual and bounded design

- The operator explicitly warned that the accumulated change volume without current real
  Android/Windows/controlled-peer testing is risky. This slice therefore makes a narrow source
  claim only. Read-only tracing found the generic outgoing viewer command plane still used one
  `mpsc::UnboundedSender<Data>`/`UnboundedReceiver<Data>` pair across interactive input,
  clipboard, delayed OS-password events, automatic FPS/record state, file operations, lifecycle
  close, CLI, and desktop port-forward managers. GUI and CLI send paths discarded admission
  errors, and the connected receiver treated producer loss as a non-terminal no-op. This was a
  concrete unbounded-allocation and connection-finality defect; it is not proof that the queue
  filled operationally or caused the reported display-only focus/background latency.
- Each outgoing round now owns one `ViewerCommandSender`/`ViewerCommandReceiver`. A 256-command
  Tokio FIFO provides the count limit. One shared semaphore accounts fixed `Data` size plus
  dynamic string or serialized protobuf payload bytes across every clone, with an aggregate
  budget of two 32 MiB post-key session packets plus fixed-capacity overhead and an individual
  dynamic payload ceiling of the session frame limit minus the secretbox MAC. This is logical
  retained-command/payload accounting, not a claim of byte-exact allocator heap measurement.
  Admission is synchronous and nonblocking. A mutex linearizes admission with one exact-round
  terminal state; no lock crosses an await. An out-of-band watch wakes the receiver and lets
  clean close supersede/drain a full FIFO. Oversize, count exhaustion, byte exhaustion, or
  accounting failure retires the entire round rather than dropping one ordered key/file/control
  command and continuing incoherently. Receiver loss rejects stale clones; producer loss is an
  explicit terminal receive outcome.
- The bounded type was integrated into the GUI session slot, non-Flutter clipboard context,
  delayed OS-password producer, automatic FPS/record publication, chained file deletion, initial
  clipboard publication, `Remote`, CLI, and port-forward managers. The network owner reports a
  command-plane failure, attempts a bounded close reason, and retires the connection. A generic
  protobuf peer-send failure is terminal instead of logging and continuing. The CLI now consumes
  and sends its command messages instead of retaining an unused unbounded receiver. A compiled
  source regression rejects restoration of the old unbounded `Data` sender, receiver, or factory
  in the four command-plane source files.

## 2026-08-02 — R-S11fh controlled-side file-response exact local writer finality

### Source trace and authority result

- Read-only tracing confirmed the remaining R-S11fg boundary: the common controlled-side
  digest/block/done/error producer returned an exact `WriterReceipt`, but the connection loop
  bound it as `_receipt` and resumed its transfer tick. Every other controlled `FileResponse`
  passed through `Connection::send`, whose ordinary stream send discarded failure. Queue
  admission was therefore not owned through completion of the exact socket-sink write.
- The controlled connection now owns one bounded `ControlledFileWriteTracker`. Every current
  protobuf `FileResponse` variant is classified at the sole send funnel; the exact round reserves
  count and retained-byte authority before keyed `send_with_receipt`, owns the receipt until
  completion, and treats admission/writer/cancellation/timeout/accounting failure as terminal.
  Admission failure is consumed before the next `select!`, preventing an unbiased scheduler from
  processing later traffic on the poisoned writer.
  The common producer's exact receipt is retained and its transfer tick is suppressed while that
  one transfer-data write is pending. Round teardown explicitly retires every remaining owner.
- Ownership is bounded to 256 receipts and two maximum post-key packets with checked arithmetic,
  checked monotonic identities, collision refusal, and a 30-second absolute completion deadline.
  The existing connection `tokio::select!` polls the receipt set directly. No new task, thread,
  runtime, dependency, lock-held await, blocking producer send, busy poll, unbounded queue,
  writer barrier/flush, reconnect path, fallback, protocol field, or wire acknowledgement was
  introduced. Ordinary non-file messages retain their previous send path.
- Exact receipt success proves only that this encrypted frame reached the local socket sink. It
  does not prove remote receipt, authentication/decoding on a real connection, acceptance,
  persistence, file-operation success, UI state, or end-to-end completion. Existing authenticated
