## 2026-08-02 — R-S11fi incoming viewer file-block persistence failure

### Source trace and result

- Read-only tracing found a concrete shared viewer finality error in
  `src/client/io_loop.rs`: authenticated `FileResponse::Block` handling awaited
  `TransferJob::write` and discarded every returned error behind a `to-do`. A failed no-follow
  open, decompression, seek/synchronization, or asynchronous write could therefore leave the exact
  receive job plus partial `.download`/`.digest` state active. Later blocks and peer `Done` could
  continue on state whose local persistence had already failed.
- One result-bearing `write_viewer_file_block` helper now owns the complete incoming transition.
  A block for no active exact job remains inert. Success preserves the existing generic-job status
  update. Failure removes the exact job, performs the existing handle-relative/no-follow partial
  artifact cleanup, returns the exact peer job/file identity plus local error, records it in the
  existing round-owned `file_flow_failure`, and terminates the round. Later block/`Done` traffic is
  therefore unreachable on that poisoned connection state. No per-job cancel, tombstone,
  compatibility branch, new task/thread/runtime/timer/dependency, reconnect fallback, protocol
  field, or cosmetic acknowledgement was added.
- Final source review found a Windows-relevant ownership defect in the first implementation: a
  failed mid-stream receive job could still own its open `.download` handle when cleanup tried to
  delete the artifact. Unix permits unlink of an open file, but Windows normally rejects it.
  `TransferJob::remove_download_file` now takes mutable access, drops its exact `data_stream`, and
  only then enters no-follow artifact cleanup. Its viewer-cancel and controlled-manager
  error/cancel call sites use the same central order.
- The first deterministic regression stages real sidecars, opens and retains the production
  receive stream with a valid block, then sends an out-of-range authenticated block and proves
  exact error identity, exact job retirement, and removal of both artifacts. The Unix regression
  stages a rejected symlink at the real `.download` target and a real digest sidecar, exercises the
  no-follow open failure, and proves job retirement, both artifact removals, and that cleanup did
  not follow the rejected target.
- `requirements.html` R-S11fi and Appendix C #317 normatively bind this transition, including
  receive-handle-close-before-cleanup order and explicit open release blockers. The requirements
  identity is
  `855fc6fe45e399bf60606c2554a271da3ef758f940ec45646a6e9230224dfb99`, recorded identically in
  `HARDENING_STATUS.md` and `docs/NATIVE-CODEC-WATCH.md`.

## 2026-08-02 — R-S11fj viewer download-digest inspection finality

### Scope and source finding

- The inspected path is the shared outgoing viewer on Android, iOS, Windows, Linux, and macOS:
  authenticated controlled-peer `FileResponse::Digest` → exact local download job/current file →
  overwrite/resume inspection → confirmation response.
- The inherited download branch looked up a job by peer digest ID, cast the signed file number
  directly to `usize`, mutated the job digest, and then called
  `fs::is_write_need_confirmation`. Any metadata or pre-epoch `SystemTime` conversion error was
  printed as `error receiving digest` and discarded. The peer remained waiting for a confirmation
  that would never arrive while unrelated connection traffic could remain healthy; an inconsistent
  active-file digest was silently ignored.
- `git blame` and `git log -S` trace the discarded-error branch to initial upstream import
  `c2abd3b`, not to the recent hardening loop. The controlled-side sibling already returned a typed
  digest-inspection error to its connection-round owner. This is source-proven file-flow finality
  debt, not an operational reproduction or evidence of host compromise/service modification.

- New synchronous `inspect_viewer_download_digest` validates the exact job ID, exact current file,
  checked nonnegative and in-range file index, and filesystem destination before deriving the path
  or inspecting local overwrite/resume state. It mutates the job digest only after inspection
  succeeds.
- A digest with no active matching job remains inert because the round has no local authority for
  it. Any mismatch, invalid index/destination, or local inspection error for an active job is
  recorded through the existing round-owned `file_flow_failure` and makes the peer-message handler
  return false, terminating the exact connection round. The old print-and-continue branch is gone.
- Existing resumable sidecars are not destroyed merely because read-only digest inspection failed;
  a future fresh connection retains the existing explicit resume authority. No retry, detached
  task, timer, reconnect workaround, fallback, cleanup policy, dependency, wire field, or cosmetic
  acknowledgement was added.

  hardening period contained 296 commits and touched 468 files. Generated outputs, the normative

  refusal; it does not exercise capture → video TCP → viewer decode → native renderer → focus or

  retained one tracked writer send, but production `src/server/connection.rs` then calls
  `notify_video_frame_fetched` after that local writer's `Ok(())`. The exact writer result comes

  `poll_flush` as an immediate successful no-op. The receipt proves only local socket/kernel

  `FramedStream`s, sends a tracked authenticated frame, and waits for the local writer receipt

  merely patched around the observed Android task-swipe/Force-Stop symptom. The user later reported
  the same display-only delay on a Windows viewer after focus loss: control remained responsive,
  displayed video could lag by as much as roughly ten seconds, and reconnect cleared the delay.
  The operational Windows client and Debian controlled-side artifacts were described as weeks older
  than this long-running development branch. Those reports are requirements and diagnostic clues,
  not reproduction evidence for the exact current source.
- The preceding R-S11fk slice proved that the existing tracked writer receipt ended at local
  kernel-TCP acceptance, before authenticated peer read. This implementation slice changes the
  production video protocol and pacing boundary. It does not claim to identify the sole cause of an
  older operational artifact's delay, and it does not claim that the cumulative branch is safe to
  deploy without current native artifact testing.
- Exactly 14 tracked files are in scope: protocol/shared source, server generation/controller/
  connection state, viewer negotiation/receipt source, shared and generated-bridge gates,
  requirements, hardening/native-watch ledgers, and the two semantic verifiers. No host RustDesk
  binary, process, service, configuration, listener, firewall, or installed application is in scope.

### Production model implemented

- `VIDEO_FRAME_RECEIPT_VERSION` is exactly 1. The protobuf contract adds a nonzero service-lifetime
  `VideoFrame.generation`, exact `VideoFrameReceipt { display, generation }`, video-only capability
  advertisement in `LoginRequest`, controlled-side capability echo in `PeerInfo`, and one typed
  top-level receipt union. Previously retired displayless/generationless tags remain reserved.
- The shared video service advances one checked generation for its whole lifetime, installs the
  exact source/display/connection controller round under its service lock, stamps that generation
  onto the encoded frame, and only then admits it to connection mailboxes. Zero, reused, or
  non-monotonic generations fail closed rather than aliasing an older round.
- Remote Desktop and View Camera sessions require exact capability version 1 and fail visibly on
  mismatch. File transfer, port forwarding, terminal, and other non-video sessions neither
  negotiate nor require the capability. There is no fallback that treats local writer completion
  as peer progress for an unnegotiated video peer.
- On the viewer, the receipt is created only after keyed frame reassembly/authentication/decryption/
  parse and after codec, size, display, and generation validation. It is sent before first-frame UI
  work, decoder admission, publication, renderer scheduling, focus, or presentation. A bounded
  per-display tracker rejects zero and non-monotonic identities and resets only when the network
  connection itself is replaced.
- On the controlled side, Monitor versus Camera comes only from authenticated `AuthConnType`.
  Capture progress for a generation occurs exactly once and only when both its sole-writer result
  and matching authenticated peer receipt have occurred, in either observation order. Zero, stale,
  duplicate, future, wrong-display, wrong-source/session, pre-login, or retired receipts are inert.
- Each connection retains at most one transmitted-but-unreceipted video frame. While it is pending,
  newer captured frames remain in the already bounded latest-candidate GOP-aware mailbox; existing
  independent-frame suppression, display-capacity limits, and exact connection retirement remain
  enforced. This is a network-parse receipt, deliberately not a decode/render/presentation receipt,
  so focus/background rendering cannot block transport liveness.

## 2026-08-02 — R-S11fl shared controlled-video capture pacing

### Trigger, risk statement, and source finding

- The user explicitly warned that the accumulated branch had substantial change volume without
  real Android/Windows/Debian end-to-end exercise and that testing on this DMZ host must never
  expose a listener beyond `127.0.0.1` or interfere with the already running host RustDesk service.
  This slice therefore remains `PARTIAL / RELEASE-BLOCKING`; none of the source/unit/cross-compile
  results below is represented as deployment or operational validation.
- Source tracing after exact peer receipts were introduced found a separate inherited shared-capture
  barrier. One `VideoFrameController` per source/display required every targeted connection to
  acknowledge a generation before the shared capture loop advanced, with 300-millisecond polls for
  up to three seconds. With two viewers, one backgrounded, congested, suspended, or non-reading
  peer could repeatedly hold a healthy viewer despite that healthy viewer returning exact
  authenticated receipts. The current official upstream `src/server/video_service.rs` retained
  the same all-target barrier at inspection time. This proves a source defect and provenance; it
  does not prove that the mechanism caused any unidentified older operational artifact.

### Production model implemented

- Each captured generation now owns one bounded connection map whose exact target states are
  `Pending`, `Retired`, or `Acknowledged`, plus one monotonic historical `progressed` bit.
  Any first valid exact authenticated peer receipt releases the shared source/display capture loop.
  Removing the acknowledging connection cannot erase that historical progress; if every target
  disconnects, the obsolete wait releases; and a one-viewer round remains paced by that viewer.
- Local frame-candidate supersession changes an exact pending target to `Retired` but deliberately
  does not count as peer progress. Connected but entirely stalled viewers therefore cannot turn
  bounded candidate replacement into a full-speed capture/encode spin. Each connection retains the
  existing one-transmitted-unreceipted-frame and constant-space GOP-safe successor limits.
- An already-pending explicit refresh interrupts the obsolete acknowledgement wait through the
  existing 300-millisecond polling boundary. No protocol field, queue, task, thread, runtime,
  recurring timer, dependency, local-writer fallback, presentation acknowledgement, or reconnect
  workaround was added.

## 2026-08-02 — R-S11fl blocked shared-capture wait execution

### Scope and authority model

- The user correctly warned that the accumulated hardening changes carry release risk where source
  and deterministic tests are not backed by native lifecycle execution. This slice did not add
  another product behavior change. It closed one concrete test gap in the newest shared-video
  pacing state machine while retaining Android/Windows/Debian native execution, renderer behavior,
  timestamps, latency budgets, and release artifacts as explicit blockers.
- The required invariant is narrow: after one source/display generation targets two exact
  connections, the capture wait remains blocked while neither has acknowledged; one exact peer
  receipt must wake the actual condition-variable wait promptly even if the other peer remains
  pending. No local supersession, unrelated connection, stale generation, or timeout is allowed to
  stand in for that receipt.

### Test and gate correction

- The existing R-S11fl tests used `Duration::ZERO`. They proved state predicates but did not execute
  the blocking/wake behavior used by the synchronous capture thread.
- `src/server/video_service.rs` now contains
  `r_s11fl_blocked_capture_wait_wakes_on_one_exact_peer_receipt`. It uses rendezvous channels to
  start one real waiter, observes a test-only atomic marker set immediately before the actual
  condition-variable wait, proves no result arrives during the pre-receipt interval, delivers the
  exact source/display/generation/connection receipt for one of two targets, requires the
  five-second wait to wake within one second, and joins the waiter. This is test-only code;
  production Rust is unchanged.
- `scripts/verify-android-voice-call-ownership.py` requires the new behavior proof and deliberately
  deletes it and removes or neutralizes the actual-blocking proof in the focused mutation catalog.
  `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py` independently requires those source proofs, requires the
  focused verifier's mutations, and directly mutates the same proofs in its complete catalog.

### Counted confined evidence

- Pinned Rust 1.75.0 compiled the exact read-only checkout from the authenticated read-only
  `online/cargo-vendor` closure in immutable image
  `sha256:da876c1ffa017736b2f63d56f8b106956d6b4d730ebbf3e99feffda42ac0b91c`.
  The container used numeric UID/GID 1000:1000, `--pull=never`, `--network=none`, no published port,
  a read-only root and source/vendor/toolchain inputs, all capabilities dropped,
  `no-new-privileges`, bounded PID/memory/CPU/descriptors, no Docker socket/device/host namespace,

## 2026-08-02 — R-S11fm desktop texture activation finality

### Source finding and authority model

- Read-only tracing found a concrete desktop presentation-owner mismatch. The pixelbuffer texture
  constructor started `DesktopTextureLifecycle` asynchronously and discarded completion, while
  `LatestDesktopTextureSlot` treated synchronous construction as a successful current owner.
  Native creation rejection (`-1`), zero pointer, initialization exception, or publication
  exception could therefore release partial state inside the lifecycle while leaving the same
  failed/released object latched as the display slot's current owner. Same-display demand is
  deliberately idempotent, so focus/resume alone did not recreate it; a display transition, view
  replacement, or reconnect could mask the stale slot.
- This is source proof for the Windows/Linux/macOS Flutter software-texture path. It is not evidence
  that the reported older operational artifacts hit this interleaving, not a native renderer or
  focus reproduction, and not an Android presentation-path finding.
- The exact authority model is one transaction: the display slot constructs and owns one candidate,
  starts its idempotent result-bearing activation, awaits initialization and publication, and may
  treat it as current only after success. Failure must report the applicable lifecycle error,
  complete exact partial-owner retirement, and remove only that candidate. Stable failure latches
  one demand transition to prevent allocation spin; a distinct newer demand observed during the
  pending failure receives one fresh attempt after predecessor finality.

### Implementation and proof surface

- `RetirableDesktopTexture.activate()` now returns `Future<bool>`.
  `DesktopTextureLifecycle` shares one exact activation future and reports success only after
  publication. Explicit-false initialization is reported; all failure/retirement paths retain the
  prior exact cleanup, unpublication, release, and late-publication exclusion semantics.
- `_PixelbufferTexture` no longer starts detached work in its constructor. The serialized display
  slot awaits exact candidate activation, retires and identity-clears a failed candidate, and uses
  a monotonic demand revision to distinguish stable failure from a newer false/true transition.
  No timer, reconnect, task, thread, queue, runtime, dependency, protocol, service, or native plugin
  implementation changed.
- Deterministic Dart coverage adds explicit-false initialization, asynchronous activation failure
  with exact retirement/bounded retry, and a newer display demand arriving during failed activation.
  The existing exception/publication/retirement/construction/predecessor-finality cases remain.
- The focused verifier is being extended to bind the exact activation API/result, slot wait,
  stable-failure latch, demand revision, exact failed-owner retirement, test names, R-S11fm,
  Appendix C #321, ledger, and deliberate mutations. The independent verifier additionally reads
  and mutates the exact lifecycle, render, and test sources rather than trusting the focused
  verifier alone.

## 2026-08-03 — R-S11fo exact viewer decoder-endpoint finality audit

### Source/history finding and authority model

- Read-only source and history tracing found a shared viewer finality defect introduced with the
  R-S11ev mailbox work in commit `57a48ea`. `VideoMailboxReceiver::drop` correctly closes the exact
  mailbox when its decoder worker exits, but every important sender-side observer lost or ignored that
  fact: `pending_frames()` reduced closure to numeric zero, UI refresh ignored failed
  `begin_refresh()`, peer-frame `Closed` was logged and discarded after the exact ingress receipt, and
  the impossible post-create missing-owner branch returned success. The authenticated connection
  could therefore preserve responsive input/file/network planes around a dead display plane until a
  reconnect destroyed the round.
- This is source proof of a cross-platform Android/iOS/Windows/Linux/macOS defect and is consistent
  with a reconnect repairing a frozen display. It is not evidence that the user's operational Android
  or Windows artifacts reached this edge, and it is not causal proof for the reported background/focus
  delay.
- The correct authority is the exact authenticated viewer round plus its owned per-display mailbox and
  decoder worker. Once that receiver is gone, no caller may observe a healthy empty queue, acknowledge
  local refresh success, or continue the same round. The existing round teardown is the sole recovery
  owner: it closes admissions, drains and joins exact workers, and lets a later round create fresh
  receipt/mailbox/decoder/GOP state. No blind decoder respawn was added.

### Implemented closure

- `VideoMailboxSender::pending_frames` now returns `Option<usize>`: live empty is `Some(0)` and exact
  receiver loss is `None`. `OwnedVideoThread` preserves that liveness value instead of mapping
  absent/closed state to zero.
- Peer-frame `Closed` and impossible missing ownership terminate the round visibly. All-display and
  single-display UI refresh terminate if an existing decoder cannot accept invalidation. Queue
  maximum, per-display FPS trend, recovery re-observation, and the refresh race all terminate on
  closure. Initial refresh before any display worker exists remains allowed; normal keyframe wait and
  bounded backlog recovery remain nonterminal.
- No protocol field, transport, listener, reconnect workaround, detached task/thread, timer, polling
  loop, queue, runtime, dependency, service, privilege boundary, or native renderer implementation
  changed.

## 2026-08-03 — R-S11fp exact desktop pending-texture re-notification

### Source finding and bounded claim

- Read-only tracing found the same presentation-liveness gap in the repository-owned Windows,
  Linux, and macOS software-RGBA texture backends. Once a frame was pending, successor decoded
  frames correctly replaced its pixels without another Flutter availability notification. That
  latest-wins coalescing is bounded and correct while the first notification remains actionable,
  but RustDesk treated that notification as a durable presentation receipt.
- The pinned Flutter 3.24.5 engine source at commit
  `a18df97ca57a249df5d8d68cd0820600223ce262` marks an external texture and schedules an engine frame
  per availability call; it does not acknowledge presentation of RustDesk's newest pending bytes.
  RustDesk's existing exact-owner presentation recovery requested a fresh peer keyframe after
  focus/resume/reselection but did not re-notify an already-pending native texture. A fresh keyframe
  could therefore replace pending bytes without scheduling a new engine frame, while reconnecting
  recreated the texture and its first notification.
- This is source proof of a desktop defect and a plausible mechanism for display-only focus delay
  with responsive control. It is not live causal proof for the user's operational Windows artifact,
  and it does not describe or close Android's separate software-RGBA publication path.

### Implemented authority and failure semantics

- The versioned in-tree native ABI now exports
  `FlutterRgbaRendererPluginTryNotifyPending`. Windows serializes on the texture mutex and returns
  the exact registrar result; Linux does the same under its GLib mutex; macOS serializes with frame
  publication and retirement on the texture queue. Idle live textures succeed without a spurious
  registrar call. Null, invalid/unregistered, retired, missing-registrar, and registrar-refusal
  states fail. A failed re-notification does not consume the pending pixels.
- Rust loads the exact new symbol fail-closed and selects the same old-peer/single-display or exact
  multi-display native pointer used by decoded-frame publication. Exact-current UI-owner recovery
  keeps the session-handler read guard, re-notifies the pending texture, propagates failure, and only
  then admits the existing peer refresh. An absent or not-yet-published texture remains a valid
  pre-first-frame state and proceeds to ordinary first-frame notification.
- No protocol field, transport, listener, reconnect branch, timer, poller, display link, queue,
  detached task/thread, runtime, dependency, service, privilege surface, or duplicate state owner was
  added. Mobile compilation excludes the desktop notifier path.

### Counted confined behavior and source evidence

## 2026-08-03 — R-S11fq Linux service-child terminal authority

### Privileged source finding

- Read-only tracing disproved R-S11e-26's recorded claim that terminal choice was a bounded
  desktop-uid observation or fixed fallback. `src/platform/linux.rs::get_all_term_values` enumerated
  every numeric `/proc` entry owned by the selected desktop uid, read complete `cmdline` and
  `environ` files for shell-looking processes, retained arbitrary distinct nonempty `TERM` values,
  and allowed `get_cur_term` to export the first candidate when `xterm-256color` was absent. The
  desktop user controlled the process population and values; there was no string, process,
  candidate, or total-read bound.
- The nominally fixed fallback was not ambient-free. The exact pinned `terminfo 0.8.0`
  `Database::from_name("xterm-256color")` ran inside the supervisor. Its vendored source consults
  `TERMINFO`, otherwise `HOME/.terminfo`, then `TERMINFO_DIRS` and `PREFIX`, before fixed system
  locations; it opens, wholly reads, and parses the selected file. The ncurses terminfo contract
  independently documents the same environment-directed database search.
- This was a privileged-launch parser/confused-deputy surface plus active-user-controlled
  enumeration/read/allocation work and child-environment authority. It is not evidence of
  exploitation or a demonstrated promptless local privilege escalation: the root parser path
  still requires a privileged launcher to retain hostile variables, and an active-user session's
  child is normally privilege-dropped to that user.

### Corrected authority model and implementation

## 2026-08-03 — R-S11fr exact software-RGBA recovery and asynchronous commit order

### Read-only presentation-lifecycle finding

- The existing exact `(SessionID, display)` software-RGBA mailbox intentionally retained one
  immutable published frame and at most one latest pending frame. While the published token was
  outstanding, producers replaced only the pending slot and emitted no second Flutter event.
  Focus/background recovery re-notified a desktop native texture and requested peer video, but did
  not rotate or re-deliver the software publication. Android/iOS compile out the native notifier,
  and a desktop software fallback has no native texture to notify. A suspended Dart decode could
  therefore strand every newly decoded/key frame in the pending slot until reconnect retired the
  mailbox.
- The Dart session listener starts an unawaited asynchronous body per event. Pixel decode and
  first-image canvas/cursor initialization contain several awaits, but the old commit checks proved
  only that the session UUID remained current. Two publications from the same live session could
  complete in reverse order and let the older image overwrite the newer image.
- These are source-proven shared software-presentation liveness/order defects and plausible
  reconnect-masked mechanisms. They do not establish that either defect caused the user's older
  Android/Windows/Debian operational symptoms. The controlled service's deliberate persistence is
  not removed or restarted by this correction.

### Corrected ownership model

- Recovery now re-arms a live exact software mailbox before native texture re-notification and peer
  refresh. Re-arm obtains a fresh checked positive Dart-compatible token, immediately makes the
  predecessor token stale, promotes only the newest pending frame when present, otherwise republishes
  the stable current bytes, and emits the exact display/token to the exact current event stream.
  Exhaustion or missing/refused delivery retires only that mailbox and fails visibly. No mailbox is
  an idle no-op, preserving native-only behavior.
- The existing handler/mailbox locks continue to linearize producer replacement, old acknowledgement,
  re-arm, display/session retirement, and UI-owner replacement. No timer, poller, replay queue, task,
  thread, Tokio runtime, reconnect branch, dependency, or protocol field was added.
- Dart now owns a synchronous revision-bearing exact publication admission. Positive publications
  strictly increase within one native session across displays; an exact new session may start at a
  lower counter. Admission is rechecked before/after decode, after every asynchronous first-image
  initialization step, and immediately before commit. Stale completions dispose their `ui.Image`.
  Reject, failure, and success paths acknowledge the exact native token once through the existing
  idempotent endpoint. Image clear/close retires publication order before disposing the image.

## Linux selected-session observation hardening (R-S11ft / R-S11e-207)

### Source finding and bounded correction

- The privileged Linux service refreshed desktop state on its outer loop, but the old path also
  globally scanned process command lines for Xwayland and could nest ten retries over six process
  patterns and four separate environment-key scans. Candidate count and complete `cmdline` /
  `environ` contents were not bounded, and selectors could be assembled from different process
  records. This is source-proven cross-principal availability, observation-consistency, and
  selector-integrity debt; it is not evidence of exploitation, a promptless LPE, a listener, a
  firewall change, or the cause of the user's older Android/Windows display-delay observation.
- Each outer service iteration now performs at most one selected-UID typed snapshot. Numeric process
  entries, selected processes, environment candidates, aggregate bytes, `cmdline` bytes/arguments,
  `environ` bytes, and selector values have explicit limit-plus-one-enforced ceilings. Bytes returned
  before a later read error still consume the aggregate budget.
- Numeric process directories are opened no-follow and directory-only; the closed `cmdline` and
  `environ` members are opened handle-relative no-follow. Process ownership is checked before and
  after environment observation. Complete terminal delimiters, strict UTF-8, unique selectors,
  canonical DISPLAY syntax, control-free Wayland/D-Bus selectors, and same-record/display-bound
  absolute Xauthority are required.
- Classification is exact and typed, including the real RustDesk image with an actual `--tray` argv
  element. The old regex scanner, repeated environment scans, and inner retry/sleep are deleted; the
  existing outer service loop remains the sole retry owner.
- Separate root/user retained-child identities now include selected session ID, username, UID,
  protocol, and all four explicit environment selectors. A newly complete Wayland or D-Bus selector
  therefore replaces the exact retained child instead of leaving a child stranded with stale or
  incomplete startup state.

## 2026-08-04 — R-S11fw Linux X11 capture shared-memory authority

- Direct source review of `libs/scrap/src/x11/capturer.rs` found the inherited X11 capturer creating
  its live raw-screen System V IPC segment with `IPC_CREAT | 0o777`, retaining it until capturer
  drop, and issuing an unchecked `xcb_shm_attach`. The source comment explicitly stated that
  everyone could do anything. An early `shmat` failure also occurred before any RAII cleanup owner
  existed. This granted every local account kernel read/write permission over a live screen buffer
  and left protocol/early-error cleanup incomplete. It is source evidence of confidentiality,
  integrity, and cleanup exposure, not evidence that another account attached or that this host was
  exploited/modified.
- The correction creates only an exact owner-read/write 0600 `IPC_PRIVATE` segment after checked
  nonzero size arithmetic, establishes one RAII owner before a read-only local `shmat`, waits for
  `xcb_shm_attach_checked` completion through `xcb_request_check`, and only then calls `IPC_RMID`.
  Consequently the segment is deletion-pending for its remaining useful lifetime. A failed removal
  transition checks the X-server detach and fails construction; RAII detaches/removes exact local
  state and reports cleanup failures. There is no permissive or unchecked fallback.
- Linux man-pages `shmctl(2)` and `shmat(2)` were used as the kernel authority for permission bits,
  attach permission, attachment counts, and `IPC_RMID` lifetime. The XCB SHM API/header and MIT-SHM
  protocol were used for checked-request/error retrieval, server write access for `GetImage`, and
  attach/removal order. These sources support the fix's authority model; they do not establish
  runtime compatibility with this repository's product on a real X server.

## 2026-08-04 — R-S11fx Linux X11 MIT-SHM GetImage frame finality

- Adjacent review after R-S11fw found an inherited failure-finality defect in
  `libs/scrap/src/x11/capturer.rs`: `Capturer::get_image` called
  `xcb_shm_get_image_unchecked`, supplied `NULL` for the reply function's protocol-error output,
  ignored whether the reply pointer was null, freed it, and returned no result. `frame()` then
  unconditionally constructed and compared a slice over the existing shared buffer. An X-server
  rejection, connection failure, or missing reply could therefore be flattened into admission of
  stale or otherwise unconfirmed frame bytes. This is source evidence of Linux X11 capture
  finality/freshness debt, not causal proof for the reported Android/Windows focus-delay symptom.
- The official XCB SHM API and generated header establish that the unsuffixed reply-producing
  `xcb_shm_get_image` is the checked request, that `_unchecked` routes errors to the event queue,
  that checked reply errors require a non-null `e` output, and that the returned reply must be
  freed. The MIT-SHM protocol and Xorg `ProcShmGetImage` implementation establish that GetImage
  writes into the shared segment, validates geometry/format/capacity, and reports the number of
  bytes written in reply `size`. The inspected pinned image header (libxcb 1.15) matched the
  declared ABI. This research justifies checked error receipt and exact reply-size admission; it
  does not substitute for executing the product against a real X server.
- The correction changes the FFI binding to `xcb_shm_get_image`, makes `get_image` return
  `io::Result<()>`, supplies a real protocol-error output, snapshots all diagnostic/reply fields
  before release, and frees both XCB allocations on every outcome. One pure classifier rejects, in
  order, protocol error (preserving error/major/minor/resource fields), connection failure, missing
  reply, and a reply size unequal to the exact allocated capture buffer. `frame()` propagates that
  result before constructing, comparing, or returning the shared slice. No retry, reconnect,
  timer, queue, background service, or unrelated X11 enumeration behavior was added.
- The final exact formatted snapshot passed the pinned Rust 1.75 Rustfmt check and a fresh
  locked/offline empty-target `scrap` build. Four serialized scoped tests passed, zero failed, and
  thirteen were filtered: the two prior kernel SHM tests plus exact GetImage success, size
  mismatch, protocol error fields, connection failure, and missing-reply branches. The focused
  verifier passed baseline and all deliberate mutations. The final complete independent
  `--source-mutations-only` catalog exited zero with `verify-verifier-workspace: ok`.
- Pre-verdict failures were retained rather than hidden. Initial compile invocations stopped before
  compilation because a login shell hid Cargo, Rustup tried to write its read-only state, and the
  first corrected direct invocation lacked the vendor source map; the pinned direct-toolchain plus
  canonical sealed vendor configuration then compiled and passed. Two independent mutation runs
  correctly rejected the unsafe source mutation but stopped because one fixture expected the wrong
  diagnostic label and another ambiguously targeted both a live assertion and its inert self-test
  literal. Both fixture defects were corrected and neither incomplete run was counted. Initial
  Rustfmt attempts found the image component absent, then missing standalone compiler libraries,
  then insufficient tmpfs while duplicating the compiler; direct execution from the extracted
  pinned archive finally ran and exposed two formatting changes, which were applied before all
  final tests and mutation gates were rerun.
- All execution used immutable/networkless containers as numeric UID:GID 1000, read-only source and
  inputs, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, bounded private tmpfs, and no port, host network
  or namespace, device, display, Docker socket, or privileged flag. No root/sudo, host RustDesk
  executable/process/service/configuration, listener, display, firewall, UFW/nftables/iptables, or
  network state was used, inspected, or changed.
- Requirements R-S11fx, Appendix C #332, hardening R-S11e-210, shared/focused/independent verifier
  wiring, and requirements hash
  `bbf1b995e0152da6ddb4645ff6aac1fd326c57f6499ccb79324f99ff8616518b` bind the slice.
  Real Xorg/Xvfb request/reply execution, actual capture-to-codec-to-render behavior,
  focus/background recovery, timestamps and latency budgets, cross-version sessions, installed
  service behavior, exact current artifacts, cold release reproduction, independent reproduction,

## 2026-08-04 — R-S11fy stale canonical Pub-cache replacement authority

- Review of `scripts/online-fetch.sh::stage_pub_cache` and
  `scripts/online-pub-cache-output.py` found a fail-closed availability dead end. An occupied
  `online/pub-cache` was treated as final: if its structural check or either networkless
  enforced-lockfile replay failed, acquisition stopped before constructing a current candidate.
  Historical canonical inputs may be root-owned and immutable, while the acquisition process is
  intentionally unprivileged. Deleting/chmodding the old tree was outside authority and a direct
  cross-parent exchange/archive was not viable without write permission on the moved directory.
  This is evidence of input-refresh authority debt, not of malicious cache contents, root use,
  container escape, or host RustDesk/service/network mutation.
- The first transaction design recorded and validated both trees but attempted
  `RENAME_EXCHANGE` directly between `staging/output` and `online/pub-cache`. Its first confined
  self-test failed with `EACCES` when the old directory was sealed 0500. A minimal control proved
  `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` itself worked in the same container. Linux `rename(2)` documents
  the relevant rule: moving a directory across parents needs write permission on that directory
  to update its `..` entry. A second minimal control proved that exchanging two sealed/writable
  directory names under one parent succeeds. The cross-parent-old design was discarded before any
  real cache or persistent harness state was touched.
- State v2 now binds exact online, staging, candidate, displaced tree, retired-record root, names,
  identities, candidate/displaced digests, and source/Flutter provenance before namespace
  mutation. A strict, exact-digest candidate is synchronized and moved with descriptor-relative
  `RENAME_NOREPLACE` to one recorded reserved sibling under `online`; both source and destination
  parents are fsynced. A same-parent `RENAME_EXCHANGE` then atomically swaps that sibling with
  `pub-cache`. Only the exact new live candidate is descriptor-sealed to 0500 and fully revalidated.
  The displaced tree remains byte-, inode-, owner-, and mode-preserved at the reserved sibling; it
  is never chmodded, chowned, recursively removed, normalized, or moved across parents. Only the
  current-user-owned journal envelope is no-clobber archived under the same-filesystem private
  `.harness-state/retired-online-inputs` root.
- Recovery recognizes only exact prepared, promoted, exchanged-but-unsealed, and completed
  three-name inode topologies. It validates candidate and displaced digests before finishing a
  recorded promotion or exchange and rejects/preserves every other arrangement. Rollback restores
  the old live name first through the same-parent exchange, then restores/demotes only the exact
  candidate. An unselected candidate created while an old cache remains live may be retired without
  granting replacement authority. Existing exact canonical inputs remain unchanged.
- The executable helper self-test passed ordinary replacement of a sealed old directory,
  promotion-crash recovery, exchange-before-seal recovery, rollback after sealing the candidate,
  old identity/digest preservation, exact candidate finality, and journal-only archival. The

  independent workspace baseline passed, and the final complete
  `scripts/verify-verifier-workspace.py --source-mutations-only` run exited zero with
  `verify-verifier-workspace: ok` on the frozen source bytes.

  `sha256:da876c1ffa017736b2f63d56f8b106956d6b4d730ebbf3e99feffda42ac0b91c`
  as numeric UID:GID 1000, `--network=none`, read-only root/source, dropped capabilities,
  no-new-privileges, bounded CPU/memory/PIDs, private tmpfs, and no port, host network/namespace,

## 2026-08-06 — exact Linux full-peer literal-loopback evidence correction

### Current checklist and selected slice

- The current R-S11b/R-S11c ledger says every enumerated source authority item is implemented and
  every listed R-S11c-10 root/service discovery or shell path is closed. Its remaining parent
  obligations are the explicitly deferred long clean cold release and native/installed evidence;
  no new privileged product API or authority rewrite was justified in this loop.
- The selected earliest bounded release-evidence slice is R-S11gc/R-S11e-216. It changes only the
  Linux full-peer evidence harness, focused/independent verifier bindings, and synchronized
  requirements/ledger records. It changes no production Rust, Flutter application behavior,
  listener policy, IPC authorization, password semantics, service code, package, or dependency.

### Source-proven contradiction and authority model

- `libs/hbb_common/src/tcp.rs:824-829` deliberately implements the production IPv4 listener with
  `Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED`; `src/direct_service.rs:954-971` calls it and runs the product socket
  assertion. The sixth exact full-peer attempt at commit
  `05f9d6e9e5d35aca7564222714f21d4f67cc56f2` therefore reached typed `user-server` and correctly
  produced `0.0.0.0:21118`, while the harness required literal `127.0.0.1:21118` without applying
  its repository's existing external loopback confinement. The run stopped before viewer start.
- The sixth run also provides the previously missing R-S11gd executable evidence: the exact shipped
  release runner's authenticated `--password-stdin` command printed `Done!`, exited zero, and the
  same server transitioned from typed `parked` to typed `user-server`. Its source identity is tree
  `18ee30b23dc11d4fbe7d51aa54fd8c360517d4d7` and deterministic archive SHA-256
  `eb63f001feedd6476b185624938e641dc386a6aa61e4841999fe561fddcae8ce`.
- `scripts/smoke-bind-loopback.c:27-38` already implements the narrow external evidence boundary:
  only `AF_INET` + `INADDR_ANY` + port 21118 becomes `INADDR_LOOPBACK`; every other bind is passed
  to the real function unchanged. Docker's official `none`-driver documentation independently
  confirms that only loopback is created in that network namespace. The glibc documentation
  confirms `LD_PRELOAD` is dynamic-loader symbol interposition and discourages it for hardened
  production runtime configuration, reinforcing the design decision that this object remains an
  explicit manifested evidence-only input and never a product/release configuration.
- Intended authority: compile the existing shim from the exact committed snapshot, hash it in the
  immutable runtime manifest, apply it only to the controlled server process tree, prove that exact
  mapped path before credential provisioning, and keep ambient/exported preload plus the separate
  password CLI and viewer preload-free. A green result may prove the full media/session pipeline

### Implemented proof surface and execution boundary

  principal, re-reads and validates logon type, exact builder identity, and the unchanged declared run level,

## 2026-08-08 — removal of the main verifier's remaining UID-0 IPC fixture exception

### Finding and selected proof decomposition

- Read-only source tracing found that the ordinary Cargo graph in `scripts/verify.sh` was already
  numeric-nonroot/networkless, but two special IPC filesystem tests still launched `--user 0:0`
  with `CAP_CHOWN` and `CAP_FOWNER`. Those containers created foreign-owned directories and ACLs by
  `chown`, then exercised the root-service reject-and-recreate path. The exception published no port,
  mounted no Docker socket, and did not touch the host RustDesk service, but it was unnecessary root
  build-host authority and violated the requested container boundary.
- The replacement decomposes the proof without weakening product behavior. The ordinary non-root
  module test binds the complete production predicate: foreign owner, effective UID 0, and the
  protected service postfix. A distinct nonzero UID/GID owns and ACL-tags two real fixture directories
  beneath a mode-0733 grandparent owned by the invoking UID. The invoking UID then runs the exact
  production descriptor-relative known-entry scrub, `unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR)`, and `mkdirat` helper.
  No `chown`, UID 0, added capability, listener, product instance, or network is needed.
- Real execution exposed two initially incorrect emulation assumptions, and neither failed run was
  counted. First, a mode-0733 grandparent cannot be opened `O_RDONLY` by the foreign UID; the helper
  now uses `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`, which permits descriptor-relative creation without adding
  directory-read authority. Second, a non-root actor cannot unlink entries inside the foreign-owned
  child merely because it owns the grandparent. The exact POSIX ACL therefore includes sorted named
  `rwx` entries for both principals: the foreign entry is the persistence grant whose destruction is
  under test, while the actor entry is the narrow surrogate for production root's directory-write
  authority. The code still knows and removes only the two canonical stale names. A mode-0644
  one-byte unknown marker lets the non-root actor prove content preservation; it remains unknown to
  the implementation and forces `ENOTEMPTY` in the fail-closed case.

## Follow-up — Windows response-bound secondary-window destruction candidate

- Source tracing proved the already-recorded production defect rather than inferring it from the user's older
  operational symptom. Windows sent Dart `onDestroy` without a method-result owner and erased the manager-owned
  `FlutterWindow`/engine from `WM_DESTROY`; production remote, camera, and terminal handlers await session/tab
  cleanup before returning. Linux already waits for that response and defers native retirement to a later idle
  turn. The review also found a second concrete Windows edge: erasing the C++ owner in `WM_DESTROY` left
  `GWLP_USERDATA` pointing at freed memory while Windows could still deliver terminal `WM_NCDESTROY`.
- The current source candidate makes close admission idempotently pending before its close callback, invokes
  `onDestroy` with one exactly-once result completion covering success/error/not-implemented, reports non-success,
  and captures only immutable HWND/ID values. Completion posts one collision-resistant registered message; it does
  not delete the owner inside the result callback. `WM_DESTROY` lets Flutter handle the message and records terminal
  state without owner erasure. `WM_NCDESTROY` completes Flutter/default handling, clears and verifies the
  exact `GWLP_USERDATA` pointer, closes HWND/channel admission, records exact native finality, and returns without
  erasing the owner. Only after synchronous `DestroyWindow` returns to the registered-message handler does that
  handler erase the manager entry. Destructor-initiated destruction has no such erasure step and cannot recursively
  mutate a map owner already being destroyed; failure to clear the exact user-data owner withholds finality and
  fails closed by retaining the manager entry.
- The existing zero-interface Windows presentation transaction now asks the real production-class secondary window
  to close, holds its Dart response for at least 1000 measured monotonic milliseconds, submits a fresh blue frame
  while held, and requires the exact HWND plus composed blue pixels to remain live. It then requires the Dart cleanup
  receipt before HWND and manager retirement, primary close, typed-zero process exit, strict result publication,
  guest shutdown, and exact cleanup. This is deliberately a narrow engine/session and HWND/object lifetime witness,
  not a real RustDesk peer or release-readiness claim.

### Sixth clean transaction: service starts, then rejects generic-to-object-specific DACL mapping

- Clean commit `97f1fe07089c57822927fb8cdadd91f6ffa336d0`, tree
  `58308811f564fcf91f319ddd1870c581a267b96a`, ran as
  `87dd072c-bc28-4c43-9eeb-52abb3869ded-A`. Source/offline identities and the zero-interface/loopback-VNC domain
  gates passed. Native Rust suites, Flutter release, the callback-core executable, locked WiX/MSI and setup builds,
  redirected-input regression, and release CPace probe all passed. Setup still returned Windows Installer 1603.
- The Application log extracted read-only from the powered-off CoW guest records a new exact failure, error 1920:
  `RustDesk Service` failed to start. The System log records the exact quoted Program Files image plus only
  `--service`. The service's own retained log proves that its protected ordinary and SAS IPC listeners started and
  then records `run_service failed: Windows sensitive IPC kernel DACL does not match its creation descriptor` for
  `_service_password`. The same sequence repeated under Windows Installer's bounded start retries. No credential
  assertion ran and no positive installed-SCM result is claimed.
- Source tracing found a comparison defect rather than a principal-policy defect. `windows_restricted_ipc_sddl`
  authored NETWORK deny, LocalSystem, and server ACEs with generic `GA`; `CreateNamedPipeW` maps generic rights to
  object-specific rights when it creates the kernel object. The code serialized the unmapped creation descriptor,

### Authority model and evidence ceiling

- Microsoft documents that `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` assigns the child to the listed job(s) at process
  creation on Windows 10+/Server 2016+, that `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` terminates associated processes
  when the final job handle closes, that process handles remain valid after process termination, and that
  `TerminateProcess` is asynchronous and must be followed by a wait when finality matters. The source already uses
  these primitives. The native harness must use a handle plus creation time rather than PID alone, and every forced
  exit must be bounded and observed through the signaled exact process object.
- An unnamed production job deliberately cannot be reopened by the observer. Therefore the native receipt may claim
  exact observed process-generation cleanup/replacement and successful authenticated CM IPC, but not direct external
  inspection of the server's private job handle or its limit flags. Source/mutation gates continue to bind atomic
  job-list assignment and kill-on-close configuration; native owner-death behavior supplies the complementary
  execution evidence.
- This slice will not claim graphical control, focus/minimize recovery, the reported display-only latency defect,
  concurrent CM selection, sustained soak, macOS, Android/iOS, exact cold release equality, independent reproduction,
  or external review unless those paths are separately and actually executed.

## 2026-08-12 — Windows harness storage-exhaustion incident and bounded lifecycle correction

### Read-only measurement and attribution

- The user's terabyte-scale suspicion was confirmed. `.harness-state` measured exactly
  `1,657,673,850,880` bytes. Sixteen retained `windows-build-*` roots measured
  `1,152,846,229,504` bytes in aggregate. They were created between 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-12, commonly at
  intervals of roughly 30–90 minutes, and individually occupied approximately 48–98 GB.
- Representative private-tree accounting showed an approximately 35-GiB `golden.qcow2` in every retained root,
  8–17 GB pass-A trees in most roots, and an approximately 38-GiB `online-snapshot` in many roots. Source tracing
  confirmed that `snapshot_golden` attempted `FICLONE` and otherwise copied all golden bytes, while the normal
  online path copied the canonical closure beneath each run root. Cleanup deleted the run root only after green
  completion; every ordinary failure retained all bulk state. No atomic singleton, retained-root refusal, or free-
  space floor prevented repeated allocation.
- Docker was measured separately, without deletion: images 246.7 GB, container writable layers 178.9 GB, volumes
  79.96 GB, and build cache 275.9 GB. Approximately 151 GB of container writable storage belonged to the user's
  live `haggai_computer` container and is not attributed to this Windows harness. No Docker object was modified.
- No root or sudo was used. This audit did not inspect or mutate host RustDesk, its service/configuration, firewall,
  routes, or network settings. It did not create a public listener. The finding is a repository harness lifecycle
  defect and is not evidence of compromise or product-runtime failure.

### Corrected authority and resource lifecycle

- The build now atomically owns one fixed current-UID mode-0700 directory lease. A concurrent invocation, any
  retained `windows-build-*` root, or unfinished bounded-evidence/shared-snapshot transaction fails before another
  bulk allocation. Existing historical roots are not automatically deleted. The 16 roots measured above remain
  present and deliberately block a new builder main path until separately authorized identity-bound reconciliation.
- Provisioning seals only the same current-principal single-link golden inode from mode 0600/0400 to exact 0400
  after its completion receipt and pinned SHA-256 pass. Builds sample the canonical golden no-follow and bind
  device, inode, mode, uid, gid, link count, byte size, nanosecond mtime/ctime, and full SHA-256 across a stable read.
  A run creates only a symbolic edge to that file and places a disposable CoW overlay over the relative edge. The
  complete identity is checked before overlay creation, between build passes, and before publication. Per-run
  reflink/full-copy fallback is removed.
- The canonical online closure now creates at most one private digest-addressed shared snapshot. Creation is under
  the singleton lease in an identity-bound private transaction, verified before publication, committed with Linux
  `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`, state-directory fsynced, transaction exact-retired, and published closure verified.

## 2026-08-21 — R-S11hf/R-S11e-244 bounded exact-generation global Dart event dispatch

- Read-only source tracing proved an inherited process-global event-ownership and resource defect in both native and
  web Flutter paths. Native `PlatformFFI._startListenEvent` detached one async closure per Rust event, awaited the
  registered-handler probe, and only then read the mutable fallback callback. An event admitted for an old session
  could therefore migrate into a replacement callback, while slow handlers overlapped without a finite owner for
  ordering, retained futures, or retained message strings. Web independently discarded registered/global handler
  completion, and named-handler replacement/unregister did not retire admitted old work. Blame attributes these paths
  to upstream import `c2abd3b3` (2026-06-19), not to this hardening slice. This is a source-proven, plausible
  cleanup-mediated stale-state mechanism across Flutter clients; it is not proof that the unidentified weeks-old
  Android, Windows, or Debian artifacts contained or exercised these bytes, and it is not a causation claim for the
  reported display-only latency.
- `flutter/lib/models/global_event_dispatcher.dart` now captures an exact named-handler binding list or exact fallback
  generation synchronously at admission. Registered and low-rate/control routes share one retained serial drain with
  one running plus at most 64 pending entries, a 16,777,216-UTF-16-code-unit message ceiling, a 67,108,864-byte
  aggregate retained charge, exact 256 + 2*code-units + 16*captured-handler accounting per entry, and at most 256
  registered bindings. Replacement and exact teardown retire only the old generation's pending work; already-invoked
  work may settle but cannot migrate or overlap replacement work. Malformed/oversize/capacity/handler/stream failure is
  visible to the exact owning route and cannot terminate a later generation.

  around all web global JSON would have placed `cursor_position`, `cursor_data`, and `cursor_id` behind a second

  cursor presentation. The final route-aware design parses and hands those three exact names synchronously to the
  existing exact-owner `LatestFrameQueue` lanes through the future-free `submitObserved` admission; raw cursor JSON
  does not enter the control FIFO. Second, the initial `FutureOr<void>` callback result was rejected after type review:
  Dart `void` cannot soundly distinguish a synchronous result from a returned future. The final callback ABI is
  unambiguous: synchronous completion is `null`, asynchronous completion is a non-null `Future<void>`, and a non-null
  result from a configured synchronous route is terminal. Focused and independent mutations bind both typedefs and
  this refusal.
- `flutter/lib/models/latest_frame_queue.dart` retains its existing exact-owner one-running/one-latest semantics while
  sharing admission between completion-bearing `submit` and future-free `submitObserved`. Observed failure is reported
  by the lane itself, queue retirement remains exact and idempotent, and diagnostic callback failure is surfaced
  without corrupting lane finality. `flutter/lib/models/model.dart` stores the exact fallback generation/session,
  retires that capability on exact session teardown, hands web cursor state synchronously to the latest-state lane,
  and keeps low-rate/control/topology work awaited and serial. Native and web `PlatformFFI` implementations use the
  shared dispatcher while preserving native registered-first/fallback routing and web registered/global ABI
  separation. Android's intentionally persistent foreground service and process lifetime are unchanged.

## 2026-08-24T09:35:55+03:00 — R-S11hn lossless whiteboard IPC/event-loop lifecycle ownership

- Read-only source tracing proved that the dedicated whiteboard helper's sole overlay terminal event lived at the
  end of the post-authenticated `handle_new_stream` path. Missing or invalid launch environment, invalid parent,
  listener construction failure, listener end/error, and comparable pre-stream returns could therefore end the IPC
  runtime without ending the overlay event loop. Windows and macOS started the IPC thread before their event-loop
  constructors published the global proxy, so an early direct event would also have been lossy. One terminal edge
  used an unbounded channel, all platforms used a raw detached thread, and its exact join handle was discarded. This
  was local helper lifecycle/finality and orphan-process debt, not evidence of compromise, exploitation, public
  exposure, privilege escalation, host RustDesk/service/firewall/network modification, or causation for the
  separately reported Android/Windows display-only delay.
- The correction gives the process generation one locked level-triggered `(proxy, terminal latch)` owner.
  Termination before proxy installation remains latched; the later installation consumes its supplied exact proxy
  to attempt one immediate Exit without retaining it. Installation first retains the exact proxy; the first terminal
  finalizer takes it for one Exit and repeated finalization is inert. Event-loop retirement clears only the retained
  proxy and cannot reset terminal history. Locks are released before synchronous terminal event delivery. A
  synchronous worker entrypoint installs its function-scoped finalizer as its first action before calling the
  runtime-backed function, so even Tokio runtime construction panic and every later startup/stream return converge
  on the same terminal owner. The authenticated handler observes cancellation but no longer owns process finality.
- `WhiteboardIpcWorker` owns one Tokio one-shot stop sender and the exact named, fallibly constructed thread handle.
  Linux joins it on application-construction failure and after event-loop return; the shared Windows/macOS owner
  joins whenever its event loop returns or fails. Spawn and join failure are visible. The unbounded channel, raw
  detached spawn, direct platform-global proxy mutation, inner-handler-only Exit, and obsolete cleanup callback are
  absent. The correction adds no retry, reconnect, polling loop, second listener/runtime/worker, service/activity
  kill, Android foreground-service weakening, port, network behavior, dependency, privilege transition, or alternate
  command route.

- Source-proven defect: macOS raw `_service_credential` returns the root LaunchDaemon's password-equivalent PRS as a
  nonpersistent runtime replica to the per-user service-owned `--server`. The listener captured a service-scoped UID,
  effective PID, and full `LOCAL_PEERTOKEN` before task transfer, but its generic proof returned only a Boolean. After
  the bodyless request, a new last-owner identity was derived and checked for installed app, exact service-owned server
  argv, and exact LaunchAgent PID/plist ownership, but that proof also returned only a Boolean. The action therefore did
  not bind the secret response to the accepted socket generation, retain/replay complete argv across `launchctl`, or
  fresh-check endpoint/UID/PID/full token immediately before PRS load/send. Existing signed-code, finite-role, launchd,
  raw-wire, and client root-helper checks constrained the old path; this is source-proven secret-response requester-
  generation/finality debt, not evidence of disclosure, exploitation, deployed-artifact causation, or host-state
  modification.

  complete argv equal to exactly `--server` plus `SERVICE_OWNED_SERVER_ARG`. It retains full argv while bounded

## 2026-09-01 — R-S11ic retained Windows service-main supervisor authority

- Outcome: the Windows service-main credential and control receivers no longer collapse their requester proof to a
  detached Boolean before a protected operation. Admission now returns distinct
  `WindowsServiceCredentialRequester` and `WindowsServiceControlRequester` capabilities. Their shared private state
  owns the exact opened supervisor process object, a freshly inspected immutable executable/complete-argv identity,
  and the accepted complete LocalSystem token proof. The exact endpoint capability remains owned across bounded
  request parsing and exposes only that endpoint's protected actions.
- Final authority: admission independently obtains the named-pipe last-message token proof and the retained process
  generation's live token proof, requires exact equality and LocalSystem, binds fresh PID/creation time to the
  launch-provided supervisor identity, requires the fixed installed service image and exact `--service` role, and
  checks process liveness plus stable pipe PID. Immediately before every credential quiesce/apply/query/resume or
  privileged session-count read, the consuming capability replays pipe PID, retained process liveness and creation
  time, fresh complete process identity equality, fixed image, exact role, both live token proofs against the accepted
  proof, stable pipe PID, and final liveness; the protected operation is its final action.
- Shutdown ordering: `prepare_shutdown` performs complete requester revalidation before producing an action-specific
  `WindowsServiceShutdownRequester`. The handler owns that capability across the bounded `ShutdownAccepted` response
  write. A failed acknowledgement performs no shutdown. After a successful acknowledgement, `commit` repeats the
  complete proof and only then requests graceful shutdown; a failed replay performs no shutdown. The existing
  truthful acknowledgement-before-latch protocol is preserved without detaching requester authority.
- Scope and behavior: no request/response variant, listener, port, retry, reconnect, timer, poller, task class,
  runtime, dependency, service restart, lifecycle transition, credential operation, privilege, or network behavior
  was added. The old `authorize_windows_service_main_ipc_connection`,
  `windows_pipe_client_token_is_local_system`, and `WindowsPipeClientTokenRequirement` Boolean surfaces were removed.

  Win32 named-pipe, process-handle, creation-time, token, and zero-time liveness APIs. It is not proof that a client
  pipe handle was never inherited or duplicated and does not claim exclusive authorship of every frame. Exact-current

## 2026-09-07 — R-S11ir/R-S11e-281 Windows RDP-sharing client transaction ownership

- Scope: source-only correction of the Windows Flutter client's request to the existing service-owned `share_rdp`
  policy transaction. The source-proven pre-change route was Dart `shareRdp` -> FRB worker
  `main_set_share_rdp` -> shared `set_share_rdp` -> an internal per-call `#[tokio::main(current_thread)]` helper ->
  the already typed `SetShareRdp`/`ShareRdpSet` exchange. Each call built and destroyed a Tokio runtime; concurrent
  bridge calls could overlap; shared/FFI code erased the returned error; and Dart had no in-flight latch or visible
  refusal path. The LocalSystem receiver still required the exact elevated, fixed installed, no-argument UI process
  generation and retained that requester through final HKLM revalidation. This was client resource/admission/result
  finality debt, not a newly discovered service authorization bypass, privilege escalation, registry-write bypass,
  public exposure, or evidence that an operational artifact executed the path.
- Correct ownership: one lazy process-lifetime `WindowsShareRdpClientOwner` caches startup success or failure, owns
  one named native thread and one fallibly built current-thread Tokio runtime, publishes readiness, joins failed
  startup, and retains the live `JoinHandle` in a mutex-protected `Option`. Its one-slot Tokio channel uses
  `try_send`; the sole runner awaits requests serially without per-request spawn. The caller waits at most eight
  seconds on that request's private completion channel. Only `accepted: true` succeeds; refusal, missing/unexpected
  response, transport failure, queue-full, queue-closed, deadline uncertainty, and completion disconnect remain
  explicit. Caller timeout does not cancel admitted work. Shared and Flutter FFI return the result; Dart latches
  synchronously before await, disables both row and checkbox, surfaces failure, and clears the latch only in a
  mounted `finally` block.
- Final review found and closed a subtler resource edge before publication. The first version reaped a worker found
  finished before submission, but a queue closure between that check and `try_send`, or completion disconnect after
  admission, returned failure while retaining the now-observably terminal handle for only a later caller to reap.
  `reap_unavailable_worker` now consumes the handle without a racy `is_finished` precheck, drops the mutex, joins the
  exact generation, and returns purpose-distinct stopped/panic errors to the closed-admission or disconnected-result
  caller. No observed failed generation is intentionally detached or retained indefinitely. Six focused mutations
  and 13 independent cross-surface mutations make this edge load-bearing.

  value, requester capability, identity/token proof, elevation transition, service action, process launch, helper,

## 2026-09-08 — R-S11is/R-S11e-282 exact-command CM file-response admission finality

- Scope and source-proven old path: this source-only slice covers the authorized connection-manager filesystem response
  producer shared by desktop Windows/Linux/macOS and Android's in-process CM listener. `CmFileResponder::send` called
  the already-bounded `CmEgressSender::send`, logged refusal, and returned `()`. `handle_fs`, every response-producing
  directory/operation helper, read initialization, and the periodic read tick could therefore continue after losing an
  exact result. Desktop and Android erased the handler result. Desktop read-tick failure was log-and-continue, and an
  `AuthorizedFS(WriteBlock)` whose following raw frame could not be read became `None` and resumed after frame
  synchronization was lost. Most concretely, `start_read_job` tried to publish `ReadJobInit` and then unconditionally
  assigned the connection and inserted the live job. This was exact file-result and resource-finality debt, not proof
  that an unidentified deployed Android/Windows/Debian artifact exercised it, not the reported screen-delay
  reproduction, and not evidence of compromise, public exposure, privilege escalation, or host mutation.
- Intended ownership and correction: the exact authorized filesystem command or read tick owns admission of its exact
  `CmFileResponse` to the bounded mailbox for the exact connection/session/generation/request/job. Admission success is
  local ownership transfer, not peer completion. Refusal is terminal for that exact session path; it cannot be retried,
  redirected, defaulted to success, or followed by later CM work. `CmFileResponder::send` now returns the exact
  `CmEgressAdmissionError`; `handle_fs` and every response producer propagate it across directory and recursive
  enumeration, create/remove/rename, write rejection/finalization/digest, and read initialization/digest/block/done/error.
  Desktop command, desktop tick, and Android listener break their exact path on first refusal. Incomplete raw write-block
  framing is terminal. `start_read_job` admits successful `ReadJobInit` before assigning and inserting the job. Read
  initialization returns an optional typed digest to the tick owner, which admits it before later read progress. A
  filesystem effect already completed before response refusal is neither rolled back nor misreported; session teardown
  is the only sound disposition once its result cannot be represented.

- Scope and source-proven old path: the Windows desktop connection manager used `IpcTaskRunner::running` both as task

  returned first, causing an immediate same-thread retry with no await, backoff, or changed state. Each refused
  `register_cliprdr_controlled` attempt had already advanced the checked process-lifetime route generation and allocated
  a bounded channel before acquiring the registry lock and discovering the duplicate. The adjacent conditional
  `MonitorReady` write was log-only. Deeper review found two same-ID ownership gaps: Login inserted/replaced the bare-ID
  `CLIENTS` entry before the next runner call attempted route admission, and active route-lease destruction preceded
  terminal bare-ID client cleanup. A colliding candidate could replace then remove an incumbent client; a terminating
  owner could release route exclusion before its client cleanup. The result match also ignored `Ok(None)`, which the IPC
  decoder returns for non-UTF-8 or invalid JSON, and allowed later frames after malformed input. These were source-proven

## 2026-09-09 — R-S11iu/R-S11e-284 exact-generation CM client-registry ownership

- Scope and source-proven old path: `src/ui_cm_interface.rs` kept process-lifetime desktop and Android CM clients in a
  bare-ID `RwLock<HashMap<i32, Client>>`. Admission unconditionally replaced an entry by server-assigned ID; desktop and
  Android task cleanup, chat, and voice mutation later selected only that ID. The Android listener retained only
  `current_id` and allowed another Login on the same task. Rust-to-Flutter remove/chat events and Dart remove/chat/voice
  consumers also carried or matched only the ID. MainService mirrored controlled capture/input/voice/notification state
  by the same bare ID. An older draining task could consequently mutate or retire a newer same-ID entry and Android
  resource owner. This is source-proven identity/lifecycle-finality debt on both desktop and Android, not evidence of a
  deployed collision, authorization or privilege bypass, compromise, public exposure, host/service/firewall/network
  mutation, or causation of the separately reported Android task-swipe or Windows focus/minimize display-only latency.
- Correct shared ownership: `CmClientRegistry` owns the client map and a checked monotonic process-lifetime generation.
  One locked admission transaction rejects nonpositive IDs, an older source generation, an active same-source collision,
  and generation exhaustion before commit. It stamps a private source generation and serialized registry generation,
  then inserts once. Desktop CM managers use source generation zero and fail closed on an active same-ID collision. A
  strictly newer Android MainService generation may supersede an older active source; the new owner atomically commits,
  then nonblockingly closes the displaced egress task before UI publication. A disconnected same-source card remains
  replaceable. The generated `CmClientOwner(id, generation)` stays with the exact stream/task through terminal cleanup.
  Exact-owner checks precede registry mutation, clipboard cleanup, UI events, idle exit, chat, and voice updates. The
  public user-selected bare-ID helper can remove only an already-disconnected current card. No registry lock crosses an
  await, JNI, UI, clipboard callback, or egress send.
- Android persistence and controlled resources: the persistent foreground MainService behavior is intentionally
  preserved. Android channel creation rejects service generation zero and makes the existing exact MainService
  generation the Rust registry's source authority. Serialized add/remove/chat/voice state carries the signed registry
  generation through Rust JSON, Kotlin `Long`, and Dart `int`. `ControlledCaptureOwnerState` maps each connection ID to
  one monotonically newer registry generation and exact capture classification. `ControlledInputOwner` now contains
  service, connection, and registry generations, so the bounded queues and delayed pointer/key actions cannot inherit
  predecessor work. Controlled voice registration/activity uses a connection-to-registry-generation map. Replacement
  retires predecessor input, voice/recorder demand, and notification state before publishing the new effects; stale or
  duplicate add, remove, and voice callbacks return before side effects. Dart rejects lower-generation adds before UI
  mutation, replaces the client and tab together for a newer generation, and filters remove/chat/voice by exact current
  generation. Activity/task removal is not used as cleanup and Force-Stop is not treated as a solution.
