# 2026-10-04 — X11 root pixel layout and padded MIT-SHM capture

- The inherited display iterator used GetGeometry depth 16/32 to choose a format and replaced
  every failed/other depth with BGRA. The capturer allocated `width * height * bytes_per_pixel`,
  which omits X11 scanline padding, and the public buffer inferred stride from the returned byte
  length. This could mislabel pixel bytes or under-allocate a 16-bit odd-width MIT-SHM image.
- The X11 protocol specification distinguishes depth from bits-per-pixel, gives each ZPixmap
  depth its own format and scanline pad, and defines image byte order and root visual color masks:
  https://www.x.org/releases/X11R7.7/doc/xproto/x11protocol.html#server_information.
  The XCB generated declarations for format/depth/visual iterators and records were checked at
  https://xcb.freedesktop.org/manual/xproto_8h_source.html before adding the FFI records.
- Source `65919cdc36a9b08160865d5fff6f7b9c6663ac64`, tree
  `ec09be8f6192832ad23ed3899f94e01dbccf9d27`, selects only exact supported TrueColor
  layouts from the setup pixmap format, image byte order, and matching root visual. Missing,
  duplicate, inconsistent, or unsupported metadata fails; no geometry-depth/BGRA fallback
  remains. The row size is padded from the selected format and must match the actual MIT-SHM
  GetImage size, depth, and visual before pixels are exposed. Empty or >u32 frame sizes fail.
- The focused zero-NIC VM completed in 44 seconds. Its 24-bit and 16-bit Xvfb instances drew
  and captured an actual red pixel using the production MIT-SHM code. The 641-pixel 16-bit root
  returned 1,284-byte rows (not 1,282), and the public pixel buffer reported that stride.
  The fixture also checks unsupported format classification but does not fabricate a hostile
  server. Raw serial: `.harness-state/verifier-vm/evidence/x11-layout-final-65919cdc.serial.log`,
  75,520 bytes, SHA-256 `ca11a40fcf2abe411bcd2ba67296615fb53d549788afd2e474666a0e7575a0e1`;
  outer SHA-256 `6b9dac3600e99e8f0fe24cd113d0c229fca3a5b7b038814ec701fb30484cb910`.
  Host listeners were invariant, no pre-existing process drift appeared, guest and VM owners
  joined, and no `run.*` scratch remains.
- This establishes component capture layout for the exercised Xvfb cases, not hostile-X-server
  setup parser safety, full-product display presentation, the Android/Windows delay cause,
  installed service behavior, or local-privilege-escalation closure. R-S11b/R-S11c native and
  release obligations remain open.

# 2026-10-04 — X11 setup-record bounds before monitor enumeration

- The current pre-change `DisplayIter::new` called `xcb_setup_roots_iterator` on the unvalidated
  `xcb_get_setup` pointer; `next_screen` and `root_format` advanced XCB's nested format, depth,
  and visual cursors from server-provided counts without bounding records by the setup reply's
  declared total length. A service-owned X11 capture path may meet a user-controlled X server,
  so malformed setup is a potential out-of-bounds read/availability path across that boundary.
  This is a source-level risk, not a demonstrated promptless local privilege escalation.
- The X11 wire spec defines an eight-byte prefix, four-byte-unit body length, fixed forty-byte
  success header, padded vendor string, eight-byte FORMAT, forty-byte SCREEN, eight-byte DEPTH,
  and twenty-four-byte VISUALTYPE records:
  https://www.x.org/releases/X11R7.7/doc/xproto/x11protocol.html#server_response .
  The inspected upstream libxcb `read_setup` allocates exactly prefix plus declared body before exposing setup, and
  `_xcb_in_read_block` completes the requested read or reports error:
  https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/lib/libxcb/-/blob/master/src/xcb_conn.c and
  https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/lib/libxcb/-/blob/master/src/xcb_in.c .
- Source `7dea168655fe9641113e93cd74ca6940a4987809` replaces the nested generated XCB
  cursors with one checked parser and owned root-layout records. The prefix is checked before
  the full header is read; every variable-length record is checked before dereference, and a
  non-exact final offset fails. No RandR monitor query occurs after malformed setup.
- The focused zero-NIC verifier VM passed in 41 seconds. Its real two-screen Xvfb/XCB setup
  was altered after XCB received it to exercise shortened total length, vendor overflow,
  format/root/depth/visual count overrun, and trailing data, sixteen times each. The old
  generated root cursor still admitted the shortened-length case from the intact allocation;
  the corrected production iterator rejected every case with no monitor query. Real 24-bit
  and 641-pixel 16-bit MIT-SHM capture continued to yield a drawn red pixel and 1,284-byte
  padded 16-bit rows. Source-bound raw serial
  `.harness-state/verifier-vm/evidence/x11-setup-7dea1686.serial.log` is 75,479 bytes,
  SHA-256 `652423d1834471ba16f6510d23204b401b690eb200a5baaa750a5af6f260660a`.
  Outer SHA-256 is `b7a6263d3abee555776131e78bf21d2a5727ceaf9b11a600ee387ccc7a7c895e`.
  Host listeners were unchanged, process drift zero, owners joined, scratch self-retired.
- The first run of this slice failed at a Rust 1.75 fixture compile error (`cast_mut` on an
  already-mutable pointer), before any native case executed. Its serial was retained, the
  stopped exact run was retired under the admission lock after owner/mount/file-use checks,
  and no run/overlay remains. It is not counted as a product failure or pass.
- This is post-read XCB setup injection, not a raw malicious-server wire test, an installed
  root service, a full-product display path, Android/Windows delay causation, or LPE closure.
  Native installed, cross-platform, sustained, release-artifact, and external-review work

## 2026-10-04 — desktop CM raw `WriteBlock` receiver bound; focused execution blocked

- Current code inspection found an independent receiver defect at `src/ui_cm_interface.rs` `IpcTaskRunner::run_with_authority_validator`: after a validated file-capable login and matching `Data::AuthorizedFS` token, the `WriteBlock` branch awaited `self.stream.next_raw()` without a deadline and without switching the connection's 128-MiB aggregate frame ceiling to the 256-KiB file-block ceiling. `src/ipc.rs` `ConnectionTmpl::next_raw` itself has no deadline; `BytesCodec::decode_head` only enforces the currently engaged cap. The controlled `src/server/connection.rs` response half already used a five-second deadline and the block cap, but that is not authority for the CM receiver to assume the sending peer will complete. A stalled authenticated server generation could retain a CM task; an oversized raw frame could be accepted up to the aggregate cap. This is a bounded-resource/transport-finality finding, not evidence of exploitation or a demonstrated local privilege escalation.
- Source commit `06f5f092177cd3341d0c985bb23970d881116224` was pushed. It gives both halves one protocol timeout constant, engages the 256-KiB cap before the CM raw read, uses the five-second receiver deadline, closes the task on timeout/transport error, and restores the aggregate cap only on successful completion. Two Tokio regressions drive the real `IpcTaskRunner` over a framed duplex stream with an admitted file login: exact 256-KiB read reaches the file handler, 256-KiB-plus-one retires while the peer remains open, and a withheld raw block must retire within the receiver deadline. ## 2026-10-05 — Android controlled-CM add waits for exact Service acknowledgment

- Source review found that Rust committed an incoming Android CM client before calling a void `MainService.rustSetByName("add_connection", ...)` JNI callback. Its implementation passes an actual error allocation to the caller rather than freeing it when an error output is supplied. Official libxcb-1.15/src/xcbext.h specifies checked flag1, the extension/request descriptor and two valid preceding iovecs; Xorg xorg-server-21.1.13/Xext/shm.c enforces exact QueryVersion request size. The fixture therefore sends one selected real QueryVersion with one extra word via that ABI; Xvfb supplies actual BadLength16, with normal XCB reply/error pointers untouched. 2026-10-14 — Direct hostname resolver source audit, R-SV5/R-SV10.
Previous turn was progress: current master1bb8bff3 is pushed/clean; actual Flutter19
and parser3 passed at6f42d76c. Their source/behavior is unchanged and is not rerun.
The next source path is real: client499 passes validated hostname:port to
socket_client79/FramedStream::new tcp466, which awaits lookup_host before its
per-address TCP timeout. Vendored Tokio1.44.2 addr164–190 parses IP literals as
ready values, otherwise calls std::net::ToSocketAddrs on spawn_blocking. Rust1.75
sys_common/net181–194 sets SOCK_STREAM hints and calls libc getaddrinfo.
Primary source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/1.75.0/library/std/src/sys_common/net.rs.
The admitted Debian builder uses Ubuntu18.04/libc2.27. Its upstream getaddrinfo
sysdeps/posix/getaddrinfo.c2187–2261 enters sorting for naddrs>1 and creates a
datagram source-route probe even if DNS transport was TCP. resolv/res_send.c858–905
creates DNS datagram sockets. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bminor/glibc/glibc-2.27/sysdeps/posix/getaddrinfo.c
and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bminor/glibc/glibc-2.27/resolv/res_send.c.
resolv.conf options use-vc forces DNS TCP but does not replace getaddrinfo sorting:
https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/resolv.conf.5.html.

Proven source: xrandr_command.rs run_with_limits spawns with piped stdout, then pidfd_open failure returns before draining; CommandChild::drop selects natural Child::wait with pidfd=None and held child.stdout. A writer can fill the pipe and block forever. Closing a pipe alone still does not establish safe command admission or retire a hung writer that handles EPIPE, so redesign launch acquisition rather than wrap the running-child optional-handle state in a guard. Model: an anonymous CLOEXEC Unix socketpair exchanges exactly one child PID and one permit before exec. A joined launch thread runs Command::spawn, because pre_exec awaits the permit while std spawn awaits exec completion. The parent holds descriptor identity, obtains pidfd while the child cannot execute its program, then permits exec and returns Child plus mandatory pidfd together. On failed acquisition or unwind, shutdown of the gate's write half refuses execution and the exact launch thread/any returned child join before return; after pidfd acquisition, only that fd may signal. Running CommandChild has no optional pidfd or natural-wait operating branch. Descriptor policy and trusted argv construction remain unchanged.

Primary research: Rust 1.75 process_unix.rs lines 144-166 proves spawn waits/reaps after a pre_exec error; its pre_exec region forbids allocation/destructor/lock traffic. Socketpair/send/shutdown are local unexposed controls, MSG_NOSIGNAL prevents control-channel SIGPIPE, and all control FDs must remain above stdio and CLOEXEC. Tracing loading callbacks exposed a prerequisite: mobile TerminalPage obtains a per-peer FFI from TerminalConnectionManager, distinct from gFFI, so blindly applying the global-mobile closeView path would refuse its legitimate cancellation. Exact route-view authority is still required. Inspecting that manager exposed a real ownership defect: releaseConnection(peerId) reads and decrements whichever FFI/count currently occupies the key; both page disposers supplied only the peer ID. A closed predecessor may be replaced before its old page disposes, allowing the late old release to decrement or close the new connection. The two separate owner/count maps also allowed count ownership to diverge. Choose this one coherent prerequisite slice; do not apply the unsafe loading/credential migration.

Replace those parallel maps with TerminalConnectionPool<FFI>, whose entry owns one immutable object and its count. Retain/release require identity; installation of the same still-current object cannot reset its count. Last release removes the entry and returns its exact owner before any external cleanup. Both desktop/mobile disposers pass _ffi; the peer-only release API is gone. Reuse validates the exact live Get registration. Closed-predecessor replacement unregisters only its known owned registration before fresh creation, because Get.put does not overwrite an ordinary existing registration; unknown/failed retirement refuses admission. Last release deletes only its retired FFI's registration before closing that object, without post-close pool mutation, and explicitly reports close errors by type. Native close completion, reentry and UI/engine teardown finality remain OPEN.

Source decision uses the actual canonical Get4.7.2 package selected in flutter/pubspec.lock, matching hosted SHA c79eeb4339f1f3deffd9ec912f8a923834bec55f7b49c9e882b8fef2c139d425. Read local get_instance/src extension/implementation and public exports: Get.delete's async facade directly invokes public synchronous GetInstance.delete; plain FFI has no GetLifeCycleBase deletion hook. Use that synchronous API for checked registration retirement before native start/close. The fetched older4.6.5 web source is not treated as pinned evidence. No package/cache bytes are modified or newly accepted as a whole-closure proof.

Concrete defect: src/client/io_loop.rs's upload and download automatic-resume branches cast
FileTransferDigest.transferred_size (uint64) to the inferred uint32 OffsetBlk value. At 2^32
bytes this becomes zero; 2^32+2 becomes two. Confirmation can therefore select a different byte
position and accounting than the requested resume. This is a source-established correctness
defect, not a newly reproduced exploit, data-loss report or native authority closure.

TransferJob::confirm_with_offset now accepts the original u64, checks representability before
any job mutation, creates the existing wire request and calls the existing exact-job/file
confirmation receiver before returning it for publication. Both automatic-resume branches use
that API; existing skip/error retirement remains. An unrepresentable offset explicitly fails,
preserving unclaimed partial files. The wire schema and IPC fields remain unchanged; supporting
larger resume positions requires a coordinated protocol decision. Primary source:
https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/proto3/#binary-wire-compatible-changes-conditionally-safe
explains why simply widening integer fields may cause older readers to truncate high bits.

prepared, UNCOMPILED and UNEXECUTED. No source-wording test is substituted for them.

Authority model: one FFI-owned MobileConnectionView binds a record to its exact ModalRoute
and captured session UUID. Every closing callback captures that record at publication;
binding a replacement or exact disposal revokes predecessor authority before unmount.
Foreign/unbound/stale/hidden records cannot pop the selected route. A legitimate terminal
uses its per-peer FFI, with no global-owner fallback. Its still-visible route may close
after native retirement. Closing retires the record first, drains only that route's own
local history and completes its pop future, while preserving every other route. System
UI restoration is unawaited/type-only on failure; root-navigation state changes only for
the actual global Navigator. Desktop registration/window checks remain at their receiver.

and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flutter/flutter/3.24.5/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/navigator.dart

During caller/verification review, classify a concrete sham boundary: the r_t5_dropped_next
case uses biased select with ready(()) first, so its read is never polled. It cannot support
the advertised pending/partial-read cancellation guarantee. Source comments and R-T14 falsely
say a cancelled framed read consumes zero kernel bytes. Framed may already have read into
its persistent buffer; the actual security property is no lost frame or partial nonce advance.
The previous20-case CPace pass includes only an unpolled-read observation for this one case;
retain other19 results but narrow that cancellation claim. Primary pinned sources re-read:
tokio-util0.7.15 codec/framed.rs documents next as retaining the underlying stream reference,
and tokio1.44.2 macros/select.rs documents biased polling order. Replace the weak test with
actual gated/observed TCP reads, retaining the same production Framed/codec owner through
partial-header, complete-header and partial-ciphertext cancellation, then exact two-frame
authenticated recovery. Correct only R-T5/R-T14 and source comments; no crypto/runtime change.

without observing them, while retaining the actual wire suite. Keep full-core integration
pending its original admission and do independent required verification/specification work.

New coherent slice: file enumeration admits unsupported filesystem objects as regular files.
Relevant source path: fs.rs read_dir_entries_with_usage uses no-follow metadata but classifies
every non-directory, non-link as File at lines269-283. Recursive enumeration includes that File
and new_read_with_budget publishes it; open_data_stream later performs read-only File::open.
A FIFO has no regular-file contents/length and a blocking read-only open can wait for a writer;
a Unix filesystem socket is also not a regular transfer source. Direct recursive roots already
reject unsupported types, so descendant classification contradicts that existing contract.
Primary sources: Rust std/fs FileType/Metadata documents is_file as regular-file classification;
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/struct.FileType.html and Linux fifo(7)
https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/fifo.7.html document writer rendezvous on blocking open.

production misrouting; do not manufacture an LPE claim or mix it into this slice.
This correction does not close replacement races between enumeration and later source open,
installed/root-service behavior, platform acceptance or measured transfer-hang/resource finality.

Next coherent slice: send-source acquisition after enumeration. Relevant current paths at
fs.rs open_data_stream(~3530) and set_stream_offset's Send branch(~3850) call File::open on a
pathname after the file list was admitted. A local replacement FIFO can block that open;
initialization can also install a directory/device handle. The initializer additionally opens
before read()'s existing Send-role check, so a misrouted Receive job can acquire a read source.
No production wrong-vector route/LPE has been demonstrated; classify that role gap precisely.

Intended model: only Send jobs may initialize a source, and every newly opened send source
must be a regular file as proved from the exact retained object before publication, digest,
seek or progress. Unix opens use O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY, so a substituted FIFO does not rendezvous
with a writer and a terminal cannot become the controlling terminal. Windows additionally
requires FILE_TYPE_DISK from GetFileType. One private open helper serves initial and first
resume acquisition; active resume continues using its original retained file. Keep source-link
resolution/full-filesystem semantics: R-S8 explicitly requires no-follow on writes, not a new
source confinement mode. Do not reuse the receive no-follow/owner/nlink helper as a shortcut
that silently forbids previously supported explicit source file/parent links. These acquisition
checks do not close namespace/content replacement by another regular file, pre-open device
side effects, network-filesystem stalls, installed privilege or other-platform native acceptance.

Primary source research: pinned Tokio1.44.2 fs/open_options.rs custom_flags delegates to
std flags and open uses asyncify; fs/file.rs implements native raw-handle borrowing. Linux
open(2)/fifo(7) document FIFO writer rendezvous, nonblocking open and O_NOCTTY, and O_NONBLOCK
does not promise bounded regular/network-filesystem I/O. Microsoft GetFileType documents disk,
pipe/socket, character and unknown/error classes; all non-disk classes fail closed.

Relevant source path: Connection::create_and_start_read_job enumerates a complete list, sends
Dir and publishes the job; fs read initialization opens the current entry before its digest.
Waiting only for Dir would race the first open. The deterministic replay therefore requests two
regular files, consumes the actual list and first digest, replaces the announced second source
with a real FIFO while the first waits for confirmation, and only then confirms the first file.
It requires exact150001-byte first-file contents in at least2blocks, one correlated Error for
file1 with the actual regular-file refusal, no digest/data/Done for that second entry, restores
the exact fixture bytes and requires a later CM directory barrier with exactly the two regular
entries. Existing same-keyed-connection150001-byte digest/Done/barrier recovery follows. The
original seven unsupported-type refusals and seven-artifact hash checks remain mandatory.
No product hook, sleep-based filesystem-order assumption, new policy or protocol is introduced.
Std read_dir docs explicitly do not promise order, so choose entry1 from the announced list:
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/fn.read_dir.html ; FIFO semantics:
https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/fifo.7.html . Source reconstruction and wire ownership,
not a canned log marker, determine the expected outcome.

admitted objects; a replacement remains foreign even after a primary operation

primary or cleanup half; foreign or displaced bytes/inode changed; exact sibling
sidecar not retired; uncertainty marker changed/absent; damaged survivor; or an
accepted late block/Done. Official Linux rename/open semantics establish that
renaming a pathname leaves an already-open file description attached to its
original object, so the fixture creates a real identity mismatch rather than
simulating an error: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/rename.2.html and
https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html, read 2026-10-15.

Source research found an adjacent concrete error path: the plugin forwards
callback errors to Flutter MethodChannel. Exact official Flutter3.24.5 source
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flutter/flutter/3.24.5/packages/flutter/lib/src/services/platform_channel.dart
lines539-553 serializes PlatformException fields verbatim and all other exceptions
with error.toString(). It does not itself log ordinary handler errors in this
version. FormatException can return its malformed JSON source; callers may later
display/log that reply. Do not call this automatic framework logging or a proven
privilege escalation. The plugin also starts _windowMethodCallHandler without
awaiting its future, so event errors escape the response owner's lifetime.

Chosen boundary: the one existing DesktopMultiWindow.setMethodHandler adapter
owns envelope extraction, application dispatch and the awaited event path until
its response. Failure yields one fixed PlatformException code/message with null
details and a type-only diagnostic. Never serialize an original exception, code,
details, input, sender or method name. Valid payload/sender/result and explicit
handler removal retain their existing protocol. This does not change native
peer authority, credentials, session admission or close semantics.

Source trace: every _openDirectoryPath response checks only session identity before
directory/selection publication. Older same-session requests and refreshes can
therefore publish after a newer destination. resetForSession retains the same
caller-visible session in the isolated model and currently has no separate request
retirement identity. Automatic job completion calls refreshAll, so assigning one
unconditional latest-request counter to both navigation and background refresh
would let background work cancel the user's pending destination. Duplicate paths
are already refused by FileFetcher; a refused duplicate must not retire its live
incumbent. Initialization also has asynchronous saved-path/fallback continuations
and an independent initDirAndHome publisher before tryCompleteTask.

Home correlation is a distinct protocol issue. goToHomeDirectory clears remote
home and opens the empty path; FileFetcher maps normal reads by requested path.
ReadDir has only path/include_hidden; FileDirectory has id/path/entries, with id
reserved for jobs and zero for ordinary listings. CM resolves an empty directory
to Config::get_home, and connection.rs sends the actual resolved directory path.
The Dart waiter keyed by the empty string cannot consume that resolved-path reply,
while initDirAndHome can already publish it. The server's initial authenticated
post-CM-login read may also use a saved directory, so replacing Home with the cached
initial path would change its meaning. Do not add a guessed-response fallback or
guard only one publisher. A coherent correction needs exact request correlation
through native/wire directory queries plus a current navigation/view owner and
initialization retirement; it must preserve the existing bounded response/dispatch
ownership, tombstones and explicit failure semantics until the protocol is changed.

Modifier source trace: InputModel.handleKeyDownEventModifiers stores right Alt
in the left slot. Its key-up family flag clears even while the other side remains
tracked. ToReleaseRawKeys.updateKeyDown/updateKeyUp selects a family through
aggregate pressed-state flags, then selects the changed key; a chord can suppress
other families, and an already-released key can fail to retire its record.
The exact logical identity must select the bounded release slot, independently
of aggregate state. Modern release flags must preserve another tracked side.

Trace beyond the byte counter found an independent lifecycle defect. The desktop
IpcTaskRunner queued-response branch in src/ui_cm_interface.rs:1898–1925 awaits
its JSON send and optional raw-block send without a deadline. ConnectionTmpl's
src/ipc.rs:7812–7853/8140 sends have frame ceilings but no internal deadline. A
native peer that stops reading can therefore strand the authenticated runner,
registry owner, read source and queued responses inside that selected branch.

Intended model: one private desktop CM response-send operation owns JSON plus its
optional raw payload under one fixed five-second initiating deadline. Any error or
timeout is terminal for the exact runner/stream; do not reuse partially written
framing, retry/reconnect, infer delivery or roll back completed filesystem effects.

guarantees. Pinned Tokio1.44.2 source confirms timeout drops the awaited future and
cannot preempt a non-yielding poll:

Linux socket buffering/peek semantics reviewed at
https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/socket.7.html and

### 2026-10-16 — CM pre-bootstrap owner cancellation and positive readiness

Previous goal turn is progress: native socket backpressure A/B accepted and pushed
91e10766/c16ec444. R-S11b/c still lacks complete installed principal, helper/process,

Relevant source path: Connection::drop closes cm_ipc_owner before its remaining
fields (including the command sender) are destroyed. The pre-bootstrap owner
wrapper at src/server/connection.rs:8459 previously used biased selection with
the worker before owner_closed. A ready worker could therefore be polled after
owner closure; command-channel liveness is not that exact owner proof. The same
wrapper treated either outcome of bootstrap_complete as established readiness.
Intended model: until a positive bootstrap acknowledgement, an already-ready owner
closure prevents a new worker poll. Positive readiness alone permits the existing
six-second terminal drain, retaining the exact worker result. Closure of the
readiness sender grants no connected-state authority. A poll already admitted
while the owner was live is not made synchronously preemptible by this change.

Pinned Tokio1.44.2 select source confirms biased top-to-bottom polling:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tokio-rs/tokio/tokio-1.44.2/tokio/src/macros/select.rs
Root futures0.3.30 resolves futures-util0.3.31; its Fuse retires the completed
one-shot future to Pending rather than repolling a consumed receiver:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/futures-rs/0.3.31/futures-util/src/future/future/fuse.rs

Correction keeps the same API and one owned pinned worker. A fused bootstrap signal
is selected first, success enters established drain, closed signal retires itself,
then pre-bootstrap owner closure precedes worker polling. Existing bounded drain
and genuine worker results remain. No new runtime, task, timer setting, retry,
process launch or compatibility branch is added to production.

Caller audit found a concrete independent path before expanding async work:
Client::handle_cliprdr_msg calls serve_clip_messages(Client,...), while the
controlled Connection dispatch calls it with Host after the existing capability
gate. src/clipboard_file.rs's FileContentsResponse arm unconditionally called
init_fuse_context(true) before dispatching to the actual side. A delayed or
unsolicited content reply with no context could therefore prepare the viewer's
mount namespace, even for Host. Its FormatDataResponse arm likewise initialized
the viewer side regardless of the typed caller and left non-success flags in an
empty TODO branch before continuing initialization. The library response router
already needs an existing context and exact pending conn/stream route; no new
context is needed to receive file contents. Server clipboard service startup
owns the separate Host context; client clipboard leases retire Client state.

Intended model: file-content replies carry no bootstrap authority and can only
complete an existing exact route. Failed metadata replies do not initialize;
successful metadata uses the existing target-side initialization protocol under
the caller's already validated session/capability. The API already carries a
typed ClipboardSide; use it rather than a hardcoded bool. No second mode, new
runtime/task, retry, credential/policy path or network behavior is introduced.
The broader blocking FormatDataResponse/startup/teardown and global-context owner
integration remains open; this correction does not claim to solve async placement.

Microsoft's primary protocol contract specifies FileContentsResponse as the reply
to a request with the same stream ID, supporting the pending-response model:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rdpeclip/df87c178-ab02-471a-acde-bb921aa1af85
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rdpeclip/cbc851d3-4e68-45f4-9292-26872a9209f2
The no-bootstrap consequence is the fork's authority/lifetime inference, not a
claim that the protocol document describes FUSE mounting. Failed format-data
handling and initialization errors are explicit; the empty TODO branches retire.

Current relevant API: socket_client.rs79 delegates an opaque ToSocketAddrs
target to FramedStream::new(tcp.rs463). That framing constructor performs
lookup_host and loops all returned addresses before constructing the framed
socket. Its name hides both system resolution and candidate policy; it also
discards socket/bind/connect failures and the TCP_NODELAY error. The actual
viewer already enters through connect_tcp_local. Two examples and the native
DNS diagnostic bypass that facade using the generic framing constructor.

Intended boundary: a framing/socket constructor accepts one explicit SocketAddr
and performs only that one socket connection. Address resolution and candidate
selection are explicit connector work; hostname callers enter that existing
facade. The next resolver owner can then own configuration, DNS transport,
deadline and cancellation without retaining a hidden lookup below it. There
will be no string-accepting compatibility constructor or DNS fallback in the
framing layer. Propagate exact socket/option errors rather than silently
discarding them. This necessary API separation is not the complete DNS fix:
the connector's existing blocking lookup remains visibly OPEN until replaced.
Do not add a timeout around it and claim native work is retired.

Relevant path at90155e23: window_channel.cc94/125/138 builds the outbound map in InvokeMethod,
InvokeMethodSelfVoid and InvokeMethodSelf. Each fl_value_set call creates a new key, while the
sender also creates a new integer. fl_value_set retains references to both arguments; dropping the
map releases its own references and leaves the original two keys and integer unowned per invocation.
The payload is borrowed and must remain caller-owned. Use fl_value_set_string for borrowed payload,
and fl_value_set_string_take for the newly created sender value. Same two wire fields and values,
no authority, action, credential, retry, callback, public API or transport change.

Primary API/source reviewed: https://api.flutter.dev/linux-embedder/fl__value_8h.html and
https://api.flutter.dev/linux-embedder/fl__value_8cc_source.html show retaining set versus owning
set_take/string_take; final FlValue destruction uses g_free. GLib free contract:
https://docs.gtk.org/glib/func.free.html ; Linux RTLD_NEXT forwarding:
https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/dlsym.3.html . Existing normative instructions/specification
are byte-identical to the previously read/count-frozen90155e23 versions; root AGENTS reread.

nonce nonreuse and its sequence/replay limits; the primitive does not establish application
parser safety or whole-process lifetime. No new native failure, exploit or LPE closure is claimed.

FileFetcher._readLocal:2169 releases its pending slot, then always reads sessionId on late success,
even after cancelPending/timeout already completed the exact caller. A dead/throwing owner getter
therefore becomes an error in the returned completion future; Future.then's sibling onError handles
upstream failure, not an exception from onValue. A live caller can receive timeout rather than
the actual owner error. No exploitation or current native weak-parent-GC reproduction is claimed.
The selected correction will use the exact pending owner's terminal state before consulting the
session callback, and explicitly deliver live continuation errors through that caller's result.

Concrete path: video_qos.rs user_network_delay starts each per-user update from self.fps
and clamps that estimate with self.highest_fps(), both aggregate values. A different pending
or low-limit viewer can therefore lower a healthy viewer's stored estimate. on_connection_close
removes the departed owner without immediately recalculating the remaining shared rate.
Authenticated Remote/ViewCamera resource publication/retirement owns these calls at
connection.rs14545-14553/14639-14650. No credential or privileged authority change is needed.
Design: each connection's completed samples update its own retained rate estimate, bounded by
that connection's requested limits. Existing conservative shared minimum, pending cap, startup
cap, quality adaptation and output limits still derive the actual capture rate. Retirement
immediately recomputes from remaining live owners. No timer, retry, reconnect, worker or API.
Three new production VideoQoS regressions precede the fix: pending-peer estimate isolation,
custom/automatic-limit isolation with shared limits preserved, and immediate rate recomputation
on departure without a new frame/sample. Existing four probe/history/recovery controls remain.

change. Controlled RTT inputs establish controller behavior only, not presented-pixel latency.

Concrete path: WebmRecorder::drop record.rs343-353 finalizes its owned Writer<File>
and then resolves ctx2.filename again to remove a short/unwritten recording. A
renamed file or replaced parent can therefore make cleanup unlink another entry.
HwRecorder carries the same time/path cleanup policy. Source findings alone are
not an installed-root exploit claim. Official Rust File/remove_file semantics:
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/struct.File.html
https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/fn.remove_file.html

threshold. R-T4 requires owned cleanup; it does not require deleting recordings.
Preserving valid short recordings is consistent with recording functionality.

RecorderContext producers pass tx=None. Delete that dead event API, not replace it
with another unused callback. The actual output factory needs only borrowed output
metadata, not the upstream context or a notification capability.

Source: video_service.rs:1243/1348 encoder timestamps use capture-loop elapsed milliseconds;
client.rs:1316 starts Recorder independently during that stream. record.rs:265 forwards
absolute signed pts through an unchecked u64 cast/multiply; no per-file origin exists.
check_pts uses None-as-zero, opens files before key admission, mutates pts before native
acceptance, and rolls back into a new file on a nonkey frame. Filenames have only millisecond
clock uniqueness. Native writer owns one immutable video track, so codec/size/clock epochs
must close the preceding owner and begin a decodable new file, with first key at time zero.

Intended model: Recorder privately owns active backend/context and last accepted source pts;
empty/initial-nonkey input creates no file. Any size/codec/clock reset retires that epoch,
then skips frames until a key, including within one batch. A fresh unique filename belongs
to each epoch. WebM owns the first accepted key's signed source origin and maps checked
relative milliseconds to native nanoseconds. Arbitrary signed origins are valid; an
unrepresentable relative interval returns failure and closes admission. Backend/context
mutation is not a public escape. Keep existing hardware local-elapsed mux semantics;
hardware/native complete timing acceptance stays OPEN (its source uses Instant::elapsed,
not a fixed frame counter). No additional dependency or consumer pin changes are needed.

Before product edits, add native zero/nonzero/negative origin, rollback/key wait, fast
rotation, overflow and initial-empty/nonkey transactions, keeping all18 accepted controls.
A bounded test-only EBML reader observes actual finalized native container timestamps
using Segment TimestampScale plus signed block-relative ticks; the zero-origin case is
an independent positive control. Actual native VP8 key/inter packets, not fake flags.
No clock backdating. Primary Matroska element/block specifications and Rust checked_sub

Primary pinned-source research identified the abstraction error: futures-util
0.3.31 SplitSink/SplitStream share a BiLock of the entire Framed. Dropping its
sink on write failure or abort could return admission while the retained reader
still owned encoded output storage. tokio-util0.7.15 Framed parts preserve codec,
read buffer and prefetched readability; Tokio1.44.2 io::split shares only I/O.
ReadFrame::from(buffer) derives readable state from original capacity: this is why
the correction uses Framed::from_parts rather than FramedRead::new followed by
buffer mutation. Rust field-drop order and bytes1.11.1 is_unique provide the owner
and observer designs. Exact primary URLs/design implications are in the capsule.

## 2026-10-18 — file modification-time domain; native Linux component correction

One bounded slice addresses the unsigned timestamp cast in native receive
publication, independently of the parked pre-I/O identity races. The previous
finish_recv_write_no_follow converted the protobuf u64 modified_time using
`modified_time as _`. Real FileEntry admission accepted u64::MAX, and the native
receive claim successfully replaced an existing destination with its staged
content at mtime -1 Unix second. This is a reproduced metadata correctness defect;
this slice does not establish a new local privilege escalation or installed
authorization bypass.

The model validates metadata before state admission and revalidates at the native
publication sink before changing staged mtime, removing the digest or renaming.
Pinned filetime0.2.23 and Rust1.75 primary-source review shows that a signed-seconds
conversion alone is insufficient for Windows epoch/tick arithmetic. Product
a69b64b897f2c1df31cbc692d58fd0bab3642fac/tree17afb832512f340f7298b332264118ef1c7bad00
uses checked UNIX_EPOCH/SystemTime addition, checks the Unix backend's native
time_t domain, and constructs FileTime from that representable SystemTime.
The same helper is used for every manifest timestamp before its path inspection
or state changes and at the native sink after the already-published guard.
No clamping, wrapping, fallback, new dependency, runtime, listener or privilege.
Filesystem-specific range/rounding fidelity remains a separate OPEN obligation.

## 2026-10-18 — receive resume-length admission; Linux native A/B accepted

The previous turn made progress by correcting the timestamp wrap and preserving
its native evidence. This turn fixes a distinct shared-library resume defect:
inspect_write_destination offered an overlong partial's complete length as a
resume offset, while ReceiveWriteClaim::resume checked only offset <= available,
not available <= the admitted final size. Real confirmation could therefore
claim an oversized partial and advance job state even when final publication's
size check could not accept it. This is metadata/state correctness evidence,
not a reproduced local privilege escalation or installed unauthorized effect.

The admitted file list owns the final size. Pinned Rust1.75 fs/io source review
confirms that seeking neither truncates a file nor validates its declared final
length, and opened-file metadata does not promise immunity to later concurrent
mutation. Product ad57ba2ab7a2e1a17d682e02f6ab1643688cd210,
tree7819e62f04b0ea9d05b90f6efaf6de2b9b5a6172, adds one shared length validator.
Read-only inspection calls it before advertising a matching resumable prefix.
The private resume API now receives the admitted list size explicitly and checks
the retained partial handle before clone/seek or stream ownership publication;
cached peer digest size cannot widen that bound. Failure retires only the lease
and preserves the partial/digest/destination and job confirmation/progress.
18 production insertions/3 deletions; no truncation, clamp, fallback, new
dependency/runtime/listener or privilege. Existing final size validation remains.

Pushed master b335deff15553aa3472ee24766b14e90a84bf9db, tree 8a7a130ade50c9e8a3cff36326f4afd876bd70b5. The Rust facade and existing supported Result exports propagate failures. Texture-render notifications follow successful persistence and effective readback. Observed failure and authority model:
The old explicit PeerConfig::remove called fs::remove_file(Self::path(id)); the final symlink itself was already an entry unlink, but parent/ancestor symlinks and pathname replacement redirected the authority. Preparation only extracts that exact old implementation behind a private before-unlink scheduling hook. Every other Config byte and the original result mapping are unchanged. Production always supplies a no-op hook.
Linux now opens one existing directory component at a time relative to an owned directory descriptor with O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC, rejects parent/prefix traversal components, and retains the final descriptor. It verifies a real directory owned by effective UID with no group/other write bits, then uses unlinkat flags0 relative to that retained parent. The errno is captured before descriptor destruction. RAII closes intermediate and final descriptors. Missing parents/names remain idempotent and create nothing. There is no mkdir, chmod, chown, canonicalize-and-reopen, full peer load, credential migration, async wait, new global lock or pathname-based Linux fallback. Final symlink entries remain removable without target mutation; directories and other failures remain explicit errors. O_PATH preserves legitimate write+search-only directory operation without requiring directory-read permission.
Public Rust/FFI signatures, all Flutter/API callers and the exact other-platform removal implementation are unchanged. Full Config is 244264 bytes / SHA-256 68691cb4563e7eb2acf8e5b2a19f5c33a48020ce0d9b3136173083fb981b61d2. Test source is 113308 bytes / SHA-256 f09be49ef6532b5741e9c20d35e37404e806a8ec8e3dae13528d65680f5e5d53 and byte-identical between preparation and corrected execution. Before and after:

Source defect and authority: LocalConfig fields at config.rs:4140–4152 and UserDefaultConfig.options at 4282 used deserialize_default callbacks which return Ok(default) after a present field type error. Fresh transaction reads in LocalConfig::update and UserDefaultConfig::set_option therefore admitted a partial record and could discard unrelated stored data; display refresh published an empty map. The record must decode all present known fields as their declared types before it can authorize a settings commit. The production correction deletes exactly six deserialize_with attributes, retaining serde(default) for absence. It adds no API, helper, dependency, lock, runtime, permission repair or recovery path. The remaining config.rs bytes are exactly the baseline. APIs, callers, controlled credentials/policy and string normalization are untouched.

Primary-source research: https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html specifies default only for an absent field and explains the deserialize_with override; https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html describes the normal typed visitor errors. The existing fixed-error read boundary retains those errors after removing the overrides. Actual pinned Rust 1.75/Serde/TOML behavior, rather than those documentation statements alone, supplies the comparison below.

## Ordinary option durable-source authority and Unix regular-file reads (9fbb652a)

Continuation audit: the previous goal turn made progress by deleting redundant native-settings setter replicas at ff0a5ab3 and recording their current 103-case/179-row evidence at 0ce335e2. This turn began at that exact clean/pushed head and reproduced its completed 2,090-path snapshot. The broad goal remains active. Relevant source path and authority: Config2.options at config.rs:1078 used an error-swallowing field decoder, its initial load at 1341 used generic recovery, and Config::set_option at 3155 decided idempotence and built its next record solely from CONFIG2 cache. The sole production Config2 writer could replace a corrupt/unreadable file from cached data, lose a completed external edit, skip a required durable change when cache matched, or attempt a write even though the file already satisfied the action. The main receiver at src/ipc.rs:4786 calls that same Result-returning setter; its action/key/role authorization and failure propagation are unchanged. A one-key commit must first validate the current owned record under the existing cache write lock, mutate only the selected key, store only a durable change, then publish the confirmed record. Failed reads must preserve both source and cache; only genuine absence/omitted fields supply defaults. The shared Unix reader also needed an opened-object admission: blocking fs::read on a FIFO cannot be the new transaction's preflight.

Production change 9fbb652a9d27fb2da5005853fab933e217a35150 / tree 935bbf5e15e98e67d090264e754267203941b2e6 has exactly four changed regions: Config2 known-field decoding, read-only initial Config2 load, shared Unix descriptor read, and the one-key Config::set_option transaction. Current config.rs is 245,958 bytes / SHA 87fe756e628de66297e4921e3fd3489e150f90ba0ce17cd0902e2eb77671de1b (prior 245,124 / 0dee7ba4c66cf2ad7077a00d2a051f4ccd3117870526fee24db83d1765573aba). Restoring those four regions recovers every other prior byte. The setter mutates an owned fresh record without cloning cache, preserves the existing lock and policy gate, conditionally persists and only then adopts cache. The options field defaults only when absent; malformed present map/value shapes are errors. Initial failure logs a fixed error and defaults only in memory without recovery. Unix opens O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY, checks the retained descriptor's is_file before reading, and lets the same file own metadata/read/drop. Windows reader bytes are exactly unchanged. No API, dependency, runtime, unwrap/expect, new lock, privileged operation or credential path is added.

Primary-source research: https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html and https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html distinguish absent-field defaults from typed visitor errors. https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html documents nonblocking FIFO open, regular-file behavior and O_NOCTTY; https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/unix/fs/trait.OpenOptionsExt.html supplies the Rust custom_flags interface. The descriptor check follows the opened object rather than a pathname precheck. These design implications are supported by the actual Linux observations below; they are not substituted for runtime evidence on other target OSes.

Source finding: libs/hbb_common/src/fs.rs unix_require_edge_absent_after_removal (old line 1391) only checked a retained-parent name for ENOENT. unix_remove_file_no_follow, unix_remove_symlink_at and unix_remove_directory_handle all returned that result immediately after unlinkat. No parent synchronization occurred. Public remove_file, remove_directory and remove_empty_directory_tree propagated this success, so recursion could continue removing its parent even if a native directory durability barrier was unavailable. Linux primary references https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html and https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/unlink.2.html distinguish directory-entry synchronization from the already-visible name deletion. This is a demonstrated completion/durability error, not an established LPE.

## 2026-10-21 — Linux filesystem descriptor lifetime after leader-thread exit

Completed one R-S0/R-S8 functionality slice; the overall hardening goal stays ACTIVE.
Initial clean source: f7c5be377ec84d0e54a63ea67206bdb8113be683.
Native preparation: 4c8bb2aa038fab27b52c9c9e890c4d4243bdf266.

(tree eb03360650a69d6e055909c8545aebb8fb63fd25), clean and pushed to origin/master.

The exact production change is two descriptor-prefix substitutions in
libs/hbb_common/src/fs.rs: DirectoryContext::descriptor_path and
TransferJob::open_send_file use /proc/thread-self/fd rather than /proc/self/fd.
Every other fs.rs byte is unchanged. The retained directory continues to own enumeration,
entry classification and child lookup; its original pathname remains presentation data.
The send helper still metadata-opens O_PATH, admits only a regular inode, reopens the
held object for reading and proves readable dev/ino identity. It adds no caller-path retry,
new permission route, generic authority, runtime, dependency, configuration change or
fallback. Both initial send and first-resume source use this helper, but this slice's
leader-exit behavioral fixture exercises initial reads, not resume.

Linux proc_pid_fd(5) documents unavailability of the process descriptor directory after
main-thread termination with workers alive. proc_thread-self(5) identifies the accessing
live thread. The native fixture tests that kernel distinction, rather than assuming the
two path strings are equivalent. A real custom-main child starts one worker and exits its
actual leader through raw SYS_exit at a controlled unlocked boundary; an alive-leader
child is the control. The worker independently verifies retained probe dev/ino through
the live alias and ordinary pathname readability. It then drives real public read_dir
and TransferJob initialization/read APIs with exact bytes for regular and symlink sources.
Its sole explicitly owned test runtime is constructed from synchronous test code.
The parent owns and joins both exact children (five-second per-child budget) and retires
its private fixture after their joins. No host application, root test, service, device,
or foreign process participates.

rejected as the accepted A/B baseline; it is not classified as a product descriptor leak.

A leader's descriptor directory can become empty after that task exits even though a surviving worker retains live sockets. The checker then rejects a valid listener because it sees an empty surface. This is an actual component functional defect; it does not establish an exploitable LPE or application-level reachability.

Authority/lifetime model: the synchronous query observes the accessing worker's owned descriptor-table view, independently of the leader's lifetime, while retaining the existing open-description pin, inode/alias deduplication, socket query semantics and failure result. The inaccurate /proc/self-always-exists explanation is replaced with the precise incomplete-inspection refusal statement. No fallback or permissive policy is added, and no unrelated procfs paths are blanket-rewritten.

Primary research: Linux man-pages proc_pid_fd(5), https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_fd.5.html, documents the leader-lifetime limit of that directory's contents. Linux man-pages proc_pid_task(5), https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_thread-self.5.html, identifies thread-self as the accessing task. These support choosing the caller's directory; native evidence below tests the actual kernel behavior. Android source shares the change, but Android runtime is not claimed.

Relevant clipboard path and model: src/clipboard.rs::clipboard_listener::linux::native_authority pins an O_PATH object, checks regular type and maximum length, reopens that exact retained file description for reading, verifies type/device/inode again, and parses bounded Xauthority records under one startup budget. Its retained pin belongs to the current synchronous thread, yet the reopen used /proc/self/fd, whose leader-backed contents can disappear while another thread remains alive. The correct local surface is /proc/thread-self/fd: the same worker that acquired the pin resolves it. Production changes exactly that one path literal, without changing OpenOptions flags, type/identity/length checks, permissions, parsing, missing-file semantics, deadline/error behavior, regular-symlink support or the no-pathname-retry/no-cookie-fallback model.

The stable Linux man-pages proc_pid_fd(5) and proc_pid_task(5) documentation previously reviewed explains the leader-directory lifetime and current-task alias:

## 2026-10-21 — bounded Linux configuration-directory lease admission

Previous goal turn: progress, with pushed CM/file ledger compression and exact isolated count/provenance. Current initial source2805211ba1c957254e3bfea42f8ab6c7e3ebb11a clean/equal origin. Initial settings audit finds LocalConfig::update holds only process-local LOCAL_CONFIG across its fresh read and later whole-file replacement; cross-process lost updates remain OPEN, as already recorded. No partial cross-process fix or parked UI/global writer work was attempted. While tracing storage, established an earlier precise availability defect: config/linux_directory.rs Lease::open used flock(fd,LOCK_EX) without a deadline. This can indefinitely block any Linux configuration writer traversing that retained directory lease.

Primary research: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html. LOCK_EX may wait on an incompatible lock; LOCK_NB reports EWOULDBLOCK. Independently opened file descriptions conflict even within one process, and closing the retained description releases its lock. Flock is advisory, not caller authentication or privileged action authority. Chosen correction preserves the exact metadata/name/owner checks and retained inode, uses LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, immediately propagates non-contention errors, waits only on WouldBlock within a one-second monotonic admission budget, and requests synchronous sleeps of at most10ms/remaining budget. Persistent contention returns io::ErrorKind::TimedOut. No forced unlock, lease deletion/replacement, journal recovery or namespace write without acquisition, mutation retry, alternate path, dependency, runtime or production worker is added. OS scheduling is not a hard realtime guarantee; this does not bound unrelated open/metadata/fsync calls or total path-walk duration.

## 2026-10-21 — integer quality/FPS default readback agrees with peer inheritance

Previous goal turn was progress:6801848f separated historical Linux authority evidence from
current acceptance and removed repeated ledger narration. This turn completes one coherent
product correction in display defaults, with an actual same-test-source native A/B.

Current R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S11i acceptance remains OPEN for all15 credential actions: exact-current
installed authorized/refused principals, protected effects, persistence/runtime-only behavior and
restart, identity/role/generation/descriptor/token races, malformed/replayed input, shutdown,
uncertainty, finality and resource cleanup. R-S0 requires immunity plus complete functionality;
R-F5 actual presentation/input-visible recovery and multi-hour freshness remains OPEN.

Relevant live path and intended semantics:
flutter/lib/common/widgets/setting_widgets.dart::customImageQualitySetting serializes double
quality/FPS values and consumes the native effective readback. UserDefaultConfig::set_option
returns candidate.get(key) after its existing checked transaction. Its get_num_string reader
previously validated f64 then formatted that floating value directly. Actual
PeerConfig::default_custom_image_quality parses/casts to an integer, while default_options
inherits custom-fps as text; src/client.rs::get_option_message parses that field as the integer
OptionMessage FPS and uses30 when parsing fails. Per-session dialog.rs already applies toInt
before typed quality/FPS requests. A default acknowledgement such as25.9 therefore differs
from the quality consumer's25, while inherited FPS25.9 is not an integer and falls back to30.

The shared default read must report the integer consumed by those paths. The existing reader
abstraction formatted too early: product10c83463 makes its private generic get_num return the
validated numeric type, then formats bounded quality/FPS after their i32 conversion.
The two other numeric default fields retain their original integer parsing and formatting.
Existing parse/range/fallback/precedence and checked one-key transaction semantics remain.
This does not reject decimal-form integers supplied by Dart, add a second parser, silently
migrate stored strings on read, or change any credential/receiver authority.
Primary semantics checked:
https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/operator-expr.html#numeric-cast
https://api.dart.dev/dart-core/num/toInt.html
Both conversions truncate toward zero; validation already excludes NaN/infinity and bounds
positive values far inside i32 before conversion. Native tests below establish actual results.

Selected path: scripts/vm-transient-storage.py run_qemu cancellation handler only sets cancelled and forwards through the child's pidfd. After QMP cont the old code immediately enters child.wait() without a timeout or cancellation observation, so a child ignoring TERM prevents the finalizer from initiating its own KILL/join. Outer cleanup waits its timeout owner before resource retirement; outer timeout has a ten-second kill-after window. This is a demonstrated orchestration/lifecycle defect, not a newly demonstrated product LPE or evidence that historical storage swings had this exact cause.

Authority/lifetime design: only the supervisor's retained pidfd for its direct, waitable child authorizes signals. Continue paused-start hard-file admission and the existing QMP protocol. After continuation use native pidfd poll with100ms sampling of the cancellation flag. On cancellation raise into the existing exact-child finalizer, send TERM, wait five seconds, then pidfd KILL and exact wait; publish joined-child output accounting only after finality. Five seconds starts escalation before the outer ten-second kill window. Exact join is deliberately retained; a scheduling or uninterruptible kernel wait is not guaranteed a fixed completion deadline, and uncertain ownership/retirement remains fail-closed. No profile, memory/scratch/file/headroom, launch command/privilege or storage-selection change.

## Connected QMP startup cancellation — native wake and exact child drain (2026-10-21; finald00c754b)

Previous goal turn classified PROGRESS: code59f691bb/final7a073387 replaced indefinite post-cont child.wait with pidfd cancellation observation; native old/corrected behavior and immutable capsule/audit are authoritative. Current all15 installed/native R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S11i credential-action acceptances, required authorized settings effects, principal/generation/descriptor/token races, complete R-S0 immunity/functionality, R-F5 real presented-frame/input-visible impairment recovery and multi-hour behavior, release/reproduction/review remain OPEN. All explicit user parks remain OPEN/PARKED; no fresh parent/peer/bootstrap/prerequisite producer resumed.

Initial7a0733875249200245339089ad0c11ef08b2bfe4 clean and origin/master-equal. Source proof: vm-transient-storage.py run_qemu retains its QMP socket10-second timeout and incoming.readline65537; flag-only cancel forwards TERM but has no wake for buffered connected I/O. Its exact-child5-second finalizer starts only after that read exits, potentially later than the outer10-second kill-after window. Correct prior post-cont cancellation does not cover this earlier wait. This is a demonstrated shared harness lifecycle gap, not a product LPE finding or proof of the historical storage-swing cause.

Primary-source research, with target-native falsification rather than inferred completion:
https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/socket.html#socket.socket.recv explains retry after an interrupted system call whose Python signal handler returns without raising. Flag-only cancellation must not be assumed to end recv.
https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/socket.html#socket.socket.shutdown specifies SHUT_RDWR disabling further sends/receives.
https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/shutdown.2.html (Linux man-pages kernel/libc interface documentation) identifies ENOTCONN as no connected socket; only that expected state is tolerated.
Design implication: wake only our own retained exact socket with shutdown, preserve descriptor release in its normal context, forward only through retained child pidfd, and enter existing exact-child finalizer. Do not close/reuse a descriptor or acquire buffered-reader locks from the signal handler. Do not introduce a synthetic asynchronous cancellation exception that could interrupt a finalizer. Check cancellation before command send and before/after response read. Unexpected shutdown OSError is explicitly re-raised, not silently swallowed; since the socket context closes before the child finalizer, closed qmp descriptors are skipped. Capsule wording “No asynchronous exception is intentionally raised from cancellation” describes absence of a synthetic cancellation exception; native unexpected shutdown errors do propagate as the recorded code requires.

One concrete controller defect. In src/server/video_qos.rs::VideoQoS::user_network_delay, the quick/ordinary capacity-probe counters advanced on healthy completed delay samples before the existing sending_fps < previous_fps branch blocked the immediate FPS increase. A different viewer's requested low rate or pending probe could therefore leave both counters partly satisfied while the actual shared stream ran below this viewer's learned rate. Removing the restriction reused those low-rate samples to trigger an early probe. This is a controller correctness defect; no new local privilege-escalation mechanism or actual pixel-delay effect is claimed.

Authority and design. Each live viewer keeps its own learned rate and both probe streaks. Feedback while the shared sending FPS is below that viewer's previous learned FPS cannot establish capacity at that learned rate. The existing restriction branch therefore continues capping the computed estimate at its prior value and clears both quick_increase_fps_count and increase_fps_count. Only new unrestricted feedback rebuilds them. No message, API, role, configuration knob, dependency, runtime, compatibility path or alternate authority is introduced. The correction preserves learned rates, requested limits, pending/startup/shared caps, delay and RTT history, quality target/adaptation and connection owners.

Previous goal turn: PROGRESS, the direct-only verification-contract correction was committed and pushed. This turn completes one product slice under R-S7/resource correctness.

Source path: libs/hbb_common/src/fs/file_block.rs decoded bounded compressed input into vec![0; SIZE + 1]. That fixed Rust allocation could abort instead of returning the function's io::Result error. The unchanged receiver at libs/hbb_common/src/fs.rs:3894 propagates a decoder error before the block's filesystem/progress effects. No new filesystem/connection/admin authority is introduced. This is a reproduced allocation-error correctness defect, not a demonstrated local privilege escalation.

Model: retain the fixed 128-KiB-plus-one buffer, input/output/history limits and raw-input borrowing. try_reserve_exact obtains output capacity before resize initializes it; refusal returns io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::OutOfMemory), with no formatted diagnostic allocation, retry, fallback or dependency. Production changes are confined to that four-line reservation sequence. Rust 1.75.0 GlobalAlloc and Vec sources were reviewed:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/1.75.0/library/core/src/alloc/global.rs
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/1.75.0/library/alloc/src/vec/mod.rs

## PROGRESS — bounded QoS bitrate-growth arithmetic (2026-10-22)

Previous goal turn: PROGRESS, the file-block output allocation correction was implemented, reproduced against the old native behavior and accepted in its focused component lane. This turn completes one separate video QoS arithmetic slice. The initial feedback review found that fresh replies already retire pending-probe state; that correct behavior was left intact.

Relevant path: Encoder::bitrate() feeds VideoQoS::store_bitrate through src/server/video_service.rs and src/server/video_qos_apply.rs. VideoQoS::adjust_ratio in src/server/video_qos.rs added 150 to a u32 bitrate before floating-point conversion. The same ceiling could round above its intended budget, or round to the current ratio and be ignored by the strict greater-than-current guard. These are controlled-input component defects; no real codec/device is claimed to have emitted the extreme values, and they are not attributed as the cause of reported display lag or a local privilege escalation.

Model: calculate the existing 150-kbps ceiling in f64, exactly representing the u32 bitrate plus 150. Narrow the positive finite ceiling to f32 and step down one representable value if nearest rounding exceeds it. A ceiling equal to the current ratio still limits growth. The private positive/finite ratio invariant bounds the ceiling, so its positive bit pattern cannot underflow on that decrement. Zero bitrate, the existing BR_SPEED applicability threshold, quality limits and congestion reductions retain their policy. No connection/privilege authority, dependency, worker, timer, transport, retry or state owner is added. Rust's documented numeric widening/narrowing and overflow semantics were reviewed:
https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/operator-expr.html#numeric-cast

Error return releases the borrow without running compression; the next call reuses that context. No resize, unsafe production operation, new dependency, level/format change, alternate authority, raw fallback or automatic retry is introduced. Source path established before production editing:
VideoQoS::bitrate_store held one u32; its context-free store_bitrate replaced it.
video_service.rs startup and video_qos_apply.rs confirmation both wrote their
encoder bitrate into that one global value. adjust_ratio used it for the one
global quality ratio's 150-kbps growth calculation. Two live 2000-kbps encoders
were therefore represented by only the last 2000, not their 4000 total.
Display removal or same-name replacement removed/replaced DisplayData but did
not retire the global stored value. These are source/arithmetic findings, not
observed original native failures or an LPE claim.

The intended owner is the exact retained display registration. DisplayData now
owns its confirmed bitrate; set_display_bitrate(name, generation, bitrate) is
private to the server scope, validates the retained opaque generation and returns
false on stale/missing registration. Startup and quality confirmation explicitly
return SWITCH on refusal; confirmation cannot publish a new ratio after refusal.
The context-free public setter and global stored field are deleted, with no alias,
fallback, separate queue, thread/runtime, dependency or optional mode.
Current caller guards already validated exact generation; this is not a claim that
a production stale-caller authorization bypass was reproduced. The new mutator also
makes that invariant explicit at its receiver.

The shared controller calculates the sum from live registrations, so removal and
replacement automatically retire their contribution. u128 covers a supported
usize-sized registry of u32 values without addition overflow. The existing u32
status getter alone clamps the representation; adaptation receives the wide sum.
The common 150-kbps formula, downward f32 ceiling conversion and existing quality/
congestion policy remain, with explicit floating conversion of the wide denominator.
This is configured metadata/controller accounting, not measured real encoder output
or a new congestion-control protocol.

Research/design background:
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8836.html#section-2, section 2(6), recommends
coordination of streams sharing a bottleneck. It discusses RTP; no RFC compliance
or transfer of its native evidence to this TCP implementation is claimed.
The pinned WebRTC individual-entry/sum example is
https://webrtc.googlesource.com/src/+/2e00abc98e599c6a4e23da0b8d64017ce2eebe7f/api/video/video_bitrate_allocation.cc .
Design inference: the already-global ratio should use the same live encoder set
it controls, rather than its most recently reported member. No external library,
algorithm or dependency pin is imported.

Concrete defect and model: try_decompress_with_limit returns io::Result and is shared by post-key clipboard/cursor/compressed-terminal consumers, but its Rust1.75 Read::read_to_end path grows a Vec through infallible reserve. The public decoder API must return a checked output-allocation error while retaining normal codec/limit semantics. Replace only that read/growth loop with8192-byte stack reads, explicit Interrupted retry, fallible amortized Vec::try_reserve before each append, and OutOfMemory mapping. Do not reserve the full64MiB/caller ceiling upfront. Existing max-plus-one detection, independent64MiB history bound, public APIs, callers, error types and file-block production bytes remain unchanged. No dependency, thread/runtime, fallback, secret/authority path or production unwrap/expect was added.

The old CM chat bridge accepted only a numeric connection ID. Native send_chat selected
the currently indexed sender, so an old command could select a replacement connection.
The receiver now requires the expected registry generation, checks exact current ownership,
pending admission and disconnected state under one read guard, retains that sender and
releases the guard before sending. There is no bare-ID fallback in chat; the existing
helper remains live for other commands. The generation is mandatory in the native FFI and
the existing unimplemented web signature. No new web CM mode or dependency was added.

The Dart CM producer checks its selected peer, numeric ID, positive generation and live
state before mutating the message/history or touching the bridge. It retains its parent
during submission. Both actual send entrypoints now share sendDraft; locally refused
messages retain their exact draft, while locally accepted sends clear the composer.
The production toolbar bypasses the pinned library's unconditional post-callback clear.
Existing optimistic submission is retained; this is not remote-delivery acknowledgement.

Source path: Session::add_port_forward in src/ui_session_interface.rs excluded port0 from range validation; PeerConfig::add_port_forward in libs/hbb_common/src/config.rs had no local-port validation; add_owned_port_forward admitted local0 regardless of the exact Session kind. PreparedPortForwardListener::bind in src/port_forward.rs interprets local0 as ephemeral RDP startup and enters run_rdp before listener admission. The ordinary Flutter port formatter accepts digit0 and forwards it to the Rust request. Further caller review found the separate feature-cli path: src/cli_command.rs accepts an options string, src/main.rs parses signed i32 ports without bounds, and cli::start_one_port_forward calls the one-off listener directly, bypassing the supervisor. Correct owner model: ordinary saved and one-off mappings require explicit local1..65535; an RDP session owns only its internally requested ephemeral0. Public producer validation precedes queue admission; saved-writer validation precedes load/write; the receiver compares local-port kind with its exact Session before target/budget/bind/launch effects. The separate one-off function is named listen_one_off and validates before reaper bootstrap, admission or OS-thread creation; its CLI caller follows the new name and the old production API is absent. The existing closed-control source guard follows that name. Removal remains unrestricted by the new add guard, allowing explicit cleanup of an old invalid0 entry while preserving a sibling. No new dependency, mode, credential route, compatibility alias or permissive fallback is added.

Evidence uses canonical sealed no-NIC Linux VMs and guest-only numeric-nonroot/capless/NNP/network-none containers, exact production producer/writer methods, actor/reaper, target validation, prepared native exclusive binds and the complete one-off owner-thread/join implementation. The three initial tests cover five producer ports, five writer ports, four ordinary/RDP-by-fixed/ephemeral owner cases and explicit legacy removal. The fourth test executes four one-off invalid/healthy cases, observes actual bound sockets, and waits for exact owner-thread shutdown plus rebinding.

## Receive next-file digest handshake — native library A/B

Completed the selected functional correction at 9a4ff02e23c56cd7034e5b278b357b1695e6393d, pushed to origin/master with a clean worktree. Preparation: 6d54a854b4f6ef3c1c0ca88baf18ff23219f5b12. Source path and failure: TransferJob::read advances the sender at EOF and its next initialization requests a digest decision before any next-file block. Receive write advances on the next block. The viewer inspect_viewer_download_digest and CM CheckDigest both formerly required digest.file_num == current receive index. Thus a normal multi-file overwrite handshake rejects file 1's digest while the receiver still holds file 0. This was already a functional gap in the equality model, not a newly established privilege escalation or proof that the last size-binding change caused it.

The common receiver owns the manifest, exact job ID/current file and retained destination claim. Its typed async admit_receive_digest validates receive role, job identity, current or immediately succeeding admitted index and exact listed size before side effects. For a valid successor it uses the existing finish_current_write_file path to require exact bytes, own flush/sync and complete the prior retained claim, then advances index, resets confirmation/wait/skipped state and replaces the digest. Incomplete/malformed requests cannot advance. Final Done remains exact and whole-list-bound. The scalar setter and duplicated facade equality guards are removed, with both viewer and CM awaiting the shared admission before inspection. Connection, nonce, generation and AuthConnType ownership remain prerequisites at their existing receivers; a digest is not independently privileged action authority.

API preparation moves the existing ID/index checks into the complete typed digest method while preserving strict equality and the original role/size setter body. Native baseline POLhTOe4Uj therefore reproduces that existing transition failure; it is not described as a pristine unchanged-product artifact. All three real-file sender/receiver sequences reject file 1's digest, 45 tests pass and one fails. Eleven negative-request observations preserve staged bytes, stream/claim, cache, index/confirmation and counters. Concrete defect: both viewer and CM previously called admit_receive_digest, which changed the cached incoming digest, before inspecting the destination. The correct owner is one TransferJob operation over its admitted manifest, exact job/index, bound destination and retained predecessor claim. inspect_receive_digest validates receive role, ID, current/immediate-successor index and declared size, derives the path, and completes only a full preceding claim. It then awaits the existing leased regular-file/no-follow inspector on the existing Tokio blocking pool. Only complete success, including lease retirement, publishes the incoming digest cache. The worker owns bounded path/request data and no reference to that cache. A next-file inspection failure preserves a predecessor already committed; no rollback/deletion of that file is attempted. Both receiver facades await this operation; their local inspection code and the admission-only helper are removed. The standalone read-only inspector's bytes remain exact. ## 2026-10-25 — Linux peer removal requires durable directory acknowledgement

Completed a new coherent correction; the preceding goal turn was progress. All fifteen installed credential actions remain OPEN. Whole-peer writers and all other user-parked work were not resumed.

Source audit found PeerConfig::remove acknowledging unlink/ENOENT plus name absence without synchronizing its retained O_PATH parent. Linux fsync documentation requires explicit directory synchronization for directory-entry durability (https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html); open(2) distinguishes O_PATH location handles from ordinary I/O access (https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/open.2.html). The existing result-bearing Rust facade and Flutter failure handling already propagate errors and suppress success feedback; this was source review, not native UI execution.

The pinned sodiumoxide 0.2.7 decoder allocates from input length before parsing.
Production 6193e94bf1c14f7eabd01af06001f9cabf08720c now admits only explicit empty clear or exactly
(32 + 2) / 3 * 4 = 44 encoded bytes before decoding. Existing sodiumoxide Original
alphabet/padding, decoded-size/canonical checks and temporary wiping remain.

runtime-replica publication. Invalid lengths use the fixed value-error category;
no rejected credential bytes are printed. No new dependency, wire/storage format,
cryptographic primitive, authority route, fallback or harness change is introduced.

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sodiumoxide/sodiumoxide/0.2.7/src/base64.rs :
  decode allocates decoded_len(input.len()) before parsing; bound the fixed representation first.
- https://doc.libsodium.org/helpers : retain the established Original decoder and complete parsing.
- https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648.html : padded groups and canonical pad bits require
  44 encoded bytes for the existing 32-byte PRS, without weakening remaining canonical checks.
