## 2026-10-25 UTC — permanent-credential envelope allocation bound

Completed one coherent configuration-library correction. Base add61bef594c7c04162fc0ec5d63e774ef2105c5 (tree e809f2f0210ca2c1a138993a0c2ad5bd6d7aecc2); regression preparation 388fa445f34633132f3f350f711bfd58af632253; product e5aedb22c93bb603552153b5c2999fce1579469d; ledger/final pushed master 27526c3fc01a1e3d49020a7cf3516911383e1ac1, tree 61033abbf9f784517a198d41a249f4a00a5ba929. Final worktree is clean and all nine stashes remain intact.

Source finding and decision:
- libs/hbb_common/src/config/permanent_password.rs previously stripped the current 01 prefix and passed any nonempty suffix to sodiumoxide Base64 decoding. The pinned 0.2.7 decoder allocates from encoded length before checking the alphabet. The optional-value correction c356cae5 removed failed-result copying but did not bound this current-prefix path.
- The fixed credential is 32 raw bytes / 44 padded Base64 bytes. The largest supported plaintext is the two-byte hash prefix plus that value (46 bytes). The current secretbox envelope adds one format byte, NONCEBYTES (24) and MACBYTES (16): 87 ciphertext bytes, 116 Base64 bytes, 118 bytes including 01. Required older zero-nonce ciphertext is smaller.
- The decoder now derives that ceiling from existing constants and refuses larger suffixes before Base64 allocation or storage-key acquisition. Typed PRS/hash readers and configuration validation share the result. Refusal leaves existing stored fields intact and grants no credential/action authority. No encryption, wire, key-selection, dependency or authorized-write format changes.
- Primary research: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sodiumoxide/sodiumoxide/0.2.7/src/base64.rs (allocation order); https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox (combined-mode overhead); https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/helpers (padded Base64 size). Local writer/caller, both native ciphertext layouts, constants and Cargo.lock were inspected before implementation.

Research: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/sigaction.2.html and https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/waitpid.2.html establish process-wide signal disposition and the wait/zombie implications of explicit SIGCHLD ignoring and SA_NOCLDWAIT. Source and model: src/server/video_qos.rs::user_network_delay already classifies excess delay >=150 ms as congestion. Its 150–199 ms quality floor and 300–599 ms delay-product branches could nevertheless raise an already reduced learned rate. A shared low-rate restriction did not prevent that increase when the affected viewer itself owned the low rate. Congested feedback cannot demonstrate higher sending capacity. No API, dependency, codec, timer threshold, authentication or service authority changes.

Research: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8836.html#section-2 calls for minimizing self-induced interactive-media latency, reacting to delay buildup and recovering capacity after a bottleneck clears. This supports the design direction; the RFC does not prescribe this application's 150-ms threshold or implementation.

## 2026-10-26 — viewer FPS requests during decode congestion

Previous goal turn: PROGRESS (server rate-control correction with native A/B). This turn continues the user's requested video/recovery pivot. Linux process-identity finalization, camera/media supplier and all other user parks remain OPEN. The broad goal is still active and incomplete.

Source audit traced the viewer's bounded generation/GOP mailbox, receive-time freshness checks, server per-display egress and exact writer/peer-receipt conjunction. That review does not establish a new cause of the retained real-viewer latency failure. It did identify a separate concrete defect in src/client/io_loop.rs::Remote::fps_control: decode backlog can set should_decrease even when limited_fps exceeds the previous locally admitted request. The method then sends and caches that larger value. For example, previous 3 FPS, estimated decode capacity 10 FPS and six queued frames produces a 9-FPS request.

Correct model: a congestion-triggered automatic request may hold or lower the previously admitted limit, not raise it. Before initial publication, the user-requested cap bounds it. Existing initial publication, true reductions, healthy-feedback increase, fresh-GOP recovery and failed-send cache finality remain. last_auto_fps records LOCAL queue admission, not a remote-applied acknowledgement. No authority, protocol, dependency, queue capacity, timing threshold or settings API changes.

Research used RFC 8836 section 2 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8836.html#section-2), previously read in the same video-recovery investigation: avoid self-induced real-time latency and recover useful capacity when congestion clears. This is supporting design guidance, not an RFC mandate for the fork's particular decode-control formula.

Source path before correction: src/server/connection.rs::Connection::try_port_forward_loop at 9e713178:8505 selected peer input and then awaited timeout(PORT_FORWARD_SEND_TIMEOUT, forward.send(...)) inside the selected branch. The timeout constant was and remains 120000 ms. Cancellation and CM reception were sibling branches and could not run during that awaited send. Some(item) also disabled the CM branch on receiver EOF. This is a concrete responsiveness defect; no new privilege escalation is claimed.

The existing connection and CM mailbox own termination. The correction retains one pinned relay future while an outer select receives cancellation and CM messages. Terminal events drop that exact relay; nonterminal messages preserve the same future and pending bytes. No tasks, dependency, target authority, session kind, cipher route, timeout value or alternate operation mode were added. Existing Connection cleanup still follows the relay return. See src/server/connection.rs:8505 at product commit 63e00bd0ba7a944752945c57fdf44187303d2546.

Research: [Tokio select tutorial](https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial/select) and [select API](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/macro.select.html) explain branch cancellation and resuming a persistent pinned future. [SinkExt::send](https://docs.rs/futures-util/0.3.31/futures_util/sink/trait.SinkExt.html#method.send) includes flushing. Design implication: terminal controls must remain outside the whole awaited relay operation, while unrelated control messages must not reconstruct an unfinished send.

## 2026-10-26 — Bounded reverse tunnel progress during local backpressure (PROGRESS)

Continued the active goal after the verified tunnel-shutdown correction. The current R-S11b/R-S11c/R-S11i ledger still leaves all fifteen credential-action installed/native acceptances open. This invocation completed one tunnel data-flow slice; it did not resume password timing, video, full-parent/installed service, or other user-parked work.

Source proof: at 2c58d21d, src/port_forward.rs::run_forward (line 660) and src/server/connection.rs::try_port_forward_loop (line 8505) awaited a local socket write inside a selected data branch. While that write was pending, neither method could poll the same local socket for reverse data. The unchanged real-keyed writer still uses its existing bounded admission; this slice does not establish bulk keyed-peer behavior.

Authority/lifetime: the existing mapping/connection owner retains both halves of the local framed socket and one stack-pinned optional write. Peer input is disabled while that write owns the sink; reverse local reads remain active. Completion returns the sink before admitting the next peer frame. No background task, payload queue, dependency, target-selection route, capability or cipher mode was added. Data selection uses default fairness; viewer cancellation and controlled cancellation/CM control remain outside the whole relay with priority. Read EOF is recorded, then retires the relay only after an already-admitted local write completes. This prevents truncating that write when read progress exposes EOF earlier.

Primary research: [futures-util split API](https://docs.rs/futures-util/0.3.31/futures_util/stream/trait.StreamExt.html#method.split) and [the pinned 0.3.31 implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/futures-rs/0.3.31/futures-util/src/stream/stream/split.rs) support independent read/sink polling; the BiLock guard ends at each poll return, including Pending. [Option::as_pin_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html#method.as_pin_mut) and [Pin::set](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/pin/struct.Pin.html#method.set) provide projection and in-place retirement without moving an active write. Exact production method compilation ran on pinned Rust 1.75.0.

Current source path: src/clipboard.rs used clipboard_content_for_native for desktop sanitation, native format conversion and Android sanitation. The uncompressed branch called content.to_vec() before checking the 64 MiB ceiling or RGBA dimensions/length. Invalid content therefore acquired a payload-sized copy before rejection; a valid-copy allocation failure could abort rather than reach the existing error-return path. The required ownership model is that the converter validates borrowed incoming bytes before admitting their owned copy; the copy must return allocation failure, while valid data and the existing bounded compressed-data path remain correct. No alternate authority path or fallback is added.

Startup audit: read core_main exact-role admission, trusted effective-home initialization
and logger ordering; Config::get_home/log_path service-root selection; native logger call
sites; and pinned flexi_logger 0.27.4 writer, rotation, cleanup and handle lifetime.
R-S11k binds the exact Linux service role's storage to its effective account before
logging. This review established no new HOME/XDG escalation and no installed filesystem
authority claim. The direct-mode logger's lazy initial state also means the dependency's
handle-drop warning alone did not establish a current live defect; no speculative lifetime
patch was made. Pre-key summary functions in src/server.rs already aggregate the specified
events under R-T0/R-T12; their rate behavior was not changed or re-executed.

The concrete correction addresses daily-only file rotation. Age alone cannot constrain a
busy day's current file. The production builder now uses
Criterion::AgeOrSize(Age::Day, 4 * 1024 * 1024), retaining timestamp names and 31 archives.
The 4 MiB threshold limits ordinary records' accumulated file size while keeping the
existing quiet-day rotation and archive-count policy. It is deliberately not advertised
as a strict disk quota: a single record can cross the threshold, cleanup is asynchronous,
and old oversized archives retire under existing retention rather than being truncated.
No source-path authority, log privacy, flood counter, filter, format, write-mode,
initialization or caller-handle behavior was changed.

Research: https://docs.rs/flexi_logger/latest/flexi_logger/enum.Criterion.html and
https://docs.rs/flexi_logger/latest/flexi_logger/struct.Logger.html describe the API;
the actual pinned 0.27.4 code in online/inputs/cargo-vendor was independently read.
state.rs checks current_size > max_size before a following write; list_and_cleanup.rs
implements KeepLogFiles and shutdown joins the cleanup thread. The attempted versioned
documentation URL was unavailable; conclusions about 0.27.4 rely on the pinned source
and native execution, not an assumed current-doc implementation.

- flutter/lib/models/input_model.dart:279–295 owns each gesture with session/client and pointer/device/view. At :1514–1530 the old non-Android path rounded each event delta toward zero and then replaced its floating scale anchor, losing the remainder. Repeated sub-unit deltas could therefore emit no zoom at all.
- Official Flutter docs https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes/trackpad-gestures and https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/gestures/PointerPanZoomUpdateEvent-class.html identify scale as cumulative zoom. The fix replaces the floating anchor with cumulative integer scaleUnits initialized to zero, quantizes (event.scale - 1.0) * 1000, and sends the difference from the prior quantized total. It avoids repeated floating accumulation and preserves the existing signed thousandth-unit encoding.
- Current gesture authority, retirement, Android routing, end-of-gesture zero, scroll/fling behavior and native sinks are unchanged. src/flutter.rs:3490 reads the integer; src/ui_session_interface.rs:1427 carries it in TouchScaleUpdate; src/server/input_service.rs:1765 invokes handle_scale only on Windows. That source review is not native execution.
- Five behavioral cases were added to the existing trackpad test file and required inventory. The existing modifier-release profile now requires 98 named cases across four suites: 19 modifier, 31 physical-mouse, 36 trackpad and 12 side-button. Existing regression bodies remain unchanged; all product source at the preparation equals the base. Finding: ChatModel.setOverlayState discarded every returned GetX subscription through BlockableOverlayState.addMiddleBlockedListener. Rebinding retained old overlay callbacks and accumulated duplicate subscriptions. An old overlay could mark the current chat's window-focus state false; disposal left that subscription active. Authority/lifetime: the model owns exactly its current overlay subscription. Same-overlay rebinding is idempotent. Replacement and disposal pause then cancel the old subscription; disposed models refuse new bindings. The fire-and-forget listener wrapper and an unreachable focus-toggle branch are removed. Pinned GetX 4.7.2 get_stream.dart defers subscription removal during delivery and LightSubscription.cancel does not await that removal; pause therefore revokes delivery immediately. The four regressions exercise listener count, old-overlay publication, replacement within an in-progress event, and disposal within an event. Research: https://api.dart.dev/dart-async/StreamSubscription/cancel.html plus exact pinned GetX source hashes in the capsule.

## 2026-10-26 — Owned delayed chat focus (PROGRESS)

Previous goal turn classified PROGRESS: overlay subscriptions were corrected and verified. Current slice fixes the separate pending focus timer. The current authority checklist was reread: all fifteen R-S11ia–R-S11io installed/native credential actions and their shared restart, race, persistence, cleanup and independent-review acceptance remain OPEN.

Source finding: ChatModel.requestChatInputFocus created an unretained 100 ms Timer on each call. Its callback only checked node listeners and focus eligibility; hiding/closing/rebinding the view and disposal could not revoke it. A still-mounted closing view could therefore regain actual Flutter primary focus. Multiple requests retained independent deadlines. The CM close transition waits for platform window operations, so retirement belongs before those awaits.

Model: one pending timer belongs to ChatModel. New requests cancel earlier ones; overlay unblock or replacement, hiding, session close, final disposal and CM close initiation cancel pending focus. Final disposal refuses later requests; ordinary close preserves reusable-model reopening. Completion clears the timer before checking existing node eligibility. Close revokes before overlay cleanup; all retirement calls are synchronous and idempotent. Product diff is one file, flutter/lib/models/chat_model.dart, with 17 insertions and one deletion. No new dependency or alternate mode.

Research: https://api.dart.dev/dart-async/Timer/cancel.html establishes cancellation and repeated-cancel semantics. https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/FocusNode/requestFocus.html documents deferred/microtask focus notification, reflected by timed widget pumps and actual hasPrimaryFocus observations. The repository window_manager.setSizeAlignment implementation was read to establish its awaited resize/position sequence. This uses native Flutter focus objects, not a timer-call counter. CM platform-window and screen-retriever responses remain controlled doubles.

Source before correction: flutter/lib/models/file_model.dart JobController.resumeJob captured a session and action ID, awaited _requests.resumeJob, then resolved the numeric ID again and unconditionally assigned inProgress. The desktop Resume button is displayed for paused rows. src/flutter_ffi.rs session_resume_job resolves a viewer session; src/client/file_trait.rs resume_job acknowledges enqueue of Data::ResumeJob only. Design: the current session's exact paused transfer object owns this resume. After the awaited enqueue reply, that same object must still occupy the action ID. Only its remaining paused state may become inProgress; terminal events take precedence. Nonpaused/nontransfer admission and removed/replaced owners return false. Bridge errors still propagate and leave the paused job retryable. No new lifetime store, dependency or mode is introduced.

Finding and correction: libs/hbb_common/src/compress.rs used zstd 0.13.1 Compressor::new inside a thread-local Result cache. The constructor's Default calls zstd-safe 7.1.0 CCtx::create, which panics when ZSTD_createCCtx returns NULL before the Result path is available. The cache now holds Option<CCtx> and uses try_create, mapping None to OutOfMemory. It applies the same compression level and empty dictionary before insertion and retains the same compress2 operation. Each thread owns its successful context; failed initialization leaves no cached failure or partial context. Existing output reservation/packing, decoder limits, API and callers are unchanged. File read and cursor producers already propagate errors; terminal output reports its typed error and Android clipboard logs refusal. No new privileged operation or alternate authority path was added.

- https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/ld/Options.html#index-wrap — exact undefined-symbol substitution with healthy __real calls.

Relevant path and ownership:
DesktopHomePage.initState called periodic_immediate, which scheduled an independent initial
Future.delayed and repeated async callbacks without waiting for their returned futures. The
page awaited mainGetError and mainGetBoolOption(stop-service), then updated page state without
mounted checks. dispose cancelled only its timer. This establishes a source-level possibility
of overlapping reads and retired-page publication; the old native page was not reproduced.
The replacement uses one page-owned ServerStatusRefreshLoop with a one-second interval after
settlement. Mounted checks occur at entry and after both awaits before later reads/publication.
dispose synchronously closes admission and initiates the loop's draining future; it does not
block Flutter's synchronous disposal, cancel native IPC or claim a native cancellation deadline.
The only privileged operations remain the unchanged existing authorized service paths; these
polls read status and do not grant new authority.

The shared loop previously invoked _runTurn before assigning _activeTurn. A close called from
readiness or refresh could therefore return while that accepted callback remained pending.
The awaited readiness path also omitted a post-await closed check. The correction records a
Future.microtask turn before either callback can execute, checks closed on entry and again
after readiness, retains the original active future through settlement and prevents rearming.
A callback that itself awaits close on its own turn would await itself; the reentrant tests
initiate close and observe completion from outside the callback. No such self-await is added.
ServerModel's transaction and 500 ms process-owned schedule are unchanged, as are all other
periodic_immediate users.

Primary research before implementation:
https://api.dart.dev/dart-async/Timer/Timer.periodic.html
https://api.dart.dev/dart-async/Future/Future.microtask.html
https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/State/dispose.html
Design implications: repeating callbacks do not join their async body; microtask creation can
publish ownership before callback reentrancy while flattening its result; retired State must
release scheduling and refuse late setState.

Source finding at the base: RelativeMouseModel.setRelativeMouseMode incremented _enableRequestId only on enable. _resetState, disable, resetForSession and dispose did not invalidate a pending enable. updatePointerLockCenter returned void for both valid geometry and refusal; the Windows/Linux completion chain always reached enable after a normal return. A late frame reply could update shared coordinates and recenter before the existing final enable-token check; a late frame error could disable a newer enabled mode. Keyboard/camera admission was checked before, but not after, the deferred query. InputModel's public geometry wrapper also returned void.

Intended authority: a deferred setup belongs to the captured mode generation, connection UUID and window. Retirement invalidates that generation synchronously. An unavailable or invalid geometry result is an explicit failure, and neither stale success nor stale failure may mutate a replacement. Current Windows/Linux keyboard/camera permission must still permit enable at completion. A disposed model cannot admit another enable.

Implementation: RelativeMouseModel._isCurrentMode combines disposal, mode generation and session identity. _resetState advances the generation before clearing state; setRelativeMouseMode refuses disposed owners. Geometry returns Future<bool>, preserves its captured window identity across the real WindowController getFrame await, rejects nonfinite/nonpositive rectangles, refuses stale replies/errors before publication or cleanup, and returns true only after successful coordinate preparation. The InputModel wrapper propagates the result. Relative mouse callers recenter only after success; Windows/Linux completion rechecks exact mode/session and keyboard/camera permission before and after recenter. Cursor retry work also checks its captured mode/session before each native request. Setup exceptions use the existing complete disable cleanup instead of merely clearing fields. No dependency, platform mode or fallback was added.

Primary research: https://api.dart.dev/dart-async/Future-class.html explains interleaving across awaits and error propagation; https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/services/MethodChannel/invokeMethod.html specifies result/platform-error/missing-plugin completion; https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/Rect/isFinite.html defines the finite-coordinate check. ## 2026-10-27 — Android receiver modifier state; Rust behavior corrected, native Android OPEN

User steering remains a pivot away from earlier work. R-S15 cleanup stash d1d4dfc74506280b04a31ce5368c85968c473845 and all prior parks are preserved. This slice follows peer-search focus at 592205e6 and addresses a different product aspect. No live instruction file, requirements.html, host RustDesk, haggai_computer, foreign listener owner, service or firewall was changed. No subagents or full-parent/parked platform fixtures ran.

Finding and intended model:
- In src/server/connection.rs's Android KeyEvent branch, the old is_press expression included !key.is_some() and then tested is_press inside if let Some(key). Every recognized physical modifier therefore took removal rather than insertion. The branch then replaced the supplied modifier vector with its empty held set, also erasing explicit Legacy modifiers and CapsLock/NumLock metadata.
- Each Connection now owns a HashSet<ControlKey> restricted by decoding to the eight Shift/Control/Alt/Meta sides. Map/Translate Android codes and explicit Legacy ControlKey transitions name the same held key. Down inserts; up removes; repeat is idempotent. A complete press tap contributes current-event metadata but cannot insert or remove a persistent hold. Existing supplied modifiers and locks are retained; held/tap additions are deduplicated.
- Removed the now-unused map_key_to_control_key helper and import. The old rdev intermediate representation is unnecessary for Android wire codes and its pinned mapping omitted MetaRight 118. No new product dependency or alternate operation mode was added.
- R-S11g/R-S19 Remote admission, raw and final size/shape/modifier validation, exact Android server/connection generation, JNI handoff and queue refusal remain in place. These statements are source disposition, not runtime authority-boundary closure. State initialization remains connection-owned Default; no global modifier state was introduced.

Primary research:
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/KeyEvent documents Android keycodes, side/aggregate modifier bits, lock metadata and normalizeMetaState. It supports the eight-code table and also identifies native conversion acceptance still needed.
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustdesk-org/rdev/f9b60b1dd0f3300a1b797d7a74c116683cd232c8/src/keycodes/android.rs is the root-lock-pinned mapping; MetaRight is absent. The receiver correction does not fix all viewer producer mappings.

## 2026-10-27 — User-directed pivot: connection-tab selection after close (PROGRESS)

No live instruction file was changed.

Selected coherent slice: desktop connection-tab selection. Source review found DesktopTabController.remove initialized its destination to zero and decremented the selected index whenever the last tab was removed, even if that tab was in the background. The RemoteTabPage.onSelected caller uses the selected key for remote presentation and native current-session selection; its onRemoveId does not overwrite selection. The model therefore must preserve the active connection across background closes, using current state when an asynchronous close completes. Closing the active tab selects its immediate right neighbor or the left neighbor when last. The correction replaces the old six-line calculation with three lines in flutter/lib/desktop/widgets/tabbar_widget.dart. Other closure, retirement, selection dispatch and timer behavior is unchanged.

Primary research: Flutter's exact pinned 3.24.5 PageController/PageView source at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flutter/flutter/3.24.5/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/page_view.dart and official constructor contract https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/PageView/PageView.html. jumpToPage uses a numeric index and does not check its range; tests must observe the displayed page as well as controller state and callback identity. No new dependency or product API was added.

The old jumpTo accepted indices past the current list and queued a 100-ms callback
capturing a numerical index. That callback could override a newer selection, address
a removed index, execute in a replacement view or expire before remount. The page
cache compared only counts and mutated a previously supplied child list; same-count
replacement could retain a wrong page. The corrected controller admits only a valid
selection. Its mounted reactive view synchronizes after layout, checking mounted
state, controller/state identity, current index/count and exact selected TabInfo.
Every PageView receives a fresh child list keyed by exact TabInfo identity: surviving
tabs retain State, replacement tabs get fresh State even for the same peer key.
The timer, mutable count-only cache and CM-specific branch are deleted.
Product diff is 38 added / 42 removed lines in tabbar_widget.dart; no dependency added.

## 2026-10-27 — Bound automatic reconnect scheduling after extended failure

The preceding verification cleanup is progress. On continuation, all fifteen

ledger, shared FfiModel error/retry/reset paths, native retry classification,

defect is live: showMsgBox doubles _reconnects without a ceiling before each later

The decision is one fixed 30-second maximum requested retry delay, preserving the
first five backoff intervals and manual retry. It bounds polling delay during a

or introducing a runtime policy. Dart Timer construction supplies that delay to
the current Zone; WidgetTester.pump advances its fake clock. Primary references:
https://api.dart.dev/dart-async/Timer/Timer.html
https://api.dart.dev/dart-async/ZoneSpecification/createTimer.html
https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/flutter_test/WidgetTester/pump.html

## 2026-10-27 — Reject invalid saved floating-window coordinates

The preceding reconnect slice is verified progress. Current R-S11b/R-S11c review
still leaves all fifteen installed credential actions open; all explicit parks
remain in force. This slice addresses R-S0 application correctness, not a new
local privilege-escalation finding. Requirements and live instructions are unchanged.

Source path: main.dart loads draggablePositions before runApp on mobile and before
constructing desktop Remote/ViewCamera windows. overlay.dart DraggableKeyPosition
reads the local Flutter preference through flutter_ffi.rs and LocalConfig. That
map returns strings without coordinate validation. The loader calls double.parse
on two comma-separated fields: malformed numbers throw before UI creation, while
NaN and infinity are accepted as positions. Existing callers already supply an
initial location when the saved position is unset.

The contract is one position consisting of two finite coordinates. An invalid
saved value has the existing unset meaning; valid positions retain their values
for the existing layout/adjustment code. Loading performs no write or authority
operation. Storage errors are not converted into missing data. Official Dart
documentation confirms that tryParse alone still accepts NaN and infinity:
https://api.dart.dev/dart-core/double/tryParse.html
https://api.dart.dev/dart-core/num/isFinite.html

`ListSearchActionListener.onKeyEvent` accepted every non-null character without
checking modifiers. Its file-manager onSearch/onNext callbacks clear or replace
selection (`file_manager_page.dart` around 1140–1184), so command key events could

and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flutter/engine/3.24.5/shell/platform/windows/keyboard_unittests.cc
(AltGrModifiedKey). No new platform fallback or dependency is introduced.

### 2026-10-27 — independent, bounded native tunnel-owner reaping

R-T17's shared reaper synchronously joined each handoff in FIFO order. The live CLI
one-off launcher hands its owner over while its listener remains open; that join
therefore withheld completion of unrelated finished supervisors. Its queue cap also
excluded the join already in progress, admitting 33 retained owners instead of 32.

The replacement in 506a5800 retains unfinished handles and joins only finished
owners. A private owned permit spans handoff, queue, pending storage and native join.
It is released before completion publication, so an awakened caller can reuse the
capacity. Idle receive blocks; pending work is checked every 50 ms. Receiver closure
drains pending owners. Overflow, disconnected handoff and bootstrap failure keep
fail-stop semantics; an unsuccessful handoff retains its request until abort.
No caller/runtime thread performs the OS join and no new worker thread is created
per request. The outer session, mapping/connection limits, relay and authentication
paths are unchanged.

Rust 1.75 documents is_finished followed by join as the nonblocking join pattern;
join remains the native completion/synchronization boundary:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/1.75.0/library/std/src/thread/mod.rs
The pinned Tokio 1.44.2 owned semaphore permit releases its slot on drop:

## User pivot: mobile virtual joystick callback lifetime (2026-10-27)

The user directs another aspect. Peer sorting remains OPEN/PARKED: source review
only, no product or test changes and no runtime claim. Do not resume it automatically.
All earlier parks remain. The new slice starts from d835e61f8f9c54b2f640faa58ea0608bfe461b7f.

Source finding: VirtualJoystick in floating_mouse_widgets.dart starts a 120-ms hold
timer, then uses common.dart periodic_immediate. That helper schedules a separate
zero-delay Future and returns only the periodic Timer. Disposal cancels the hold
and periodic timers but leaves the queued Future and nonzero offset. Its callback
can therefore invoke the movement adapter after the widget has been removed.
This is a candidate UI lifetime defect, not demonstrated remote input or privilege
escalation. An absent onPanCancel is not evidence of this defect: the pinned
Flutter 3.24.5 monodrag recognizer sends an accepted pointer cancellation through
onEnd. No cancellation-handler patch is proposed.

Intended ownership: this mounted joystick owns every scheduled movement callback;
removal retires future movement while preserving normal hold, release, cancellation
and fresh-drag behavior. The focused eight-case --virtual-joystick profile mounts
the actual widget, exercises both absolute/relative adapters, and holds ready
zero-delay callbacks until after removal. Gesture dispatch and other timers remain
real Flutter test-framework operations; native movement adapters are explicit
doubles. The profile uses the existing bounded-RAM Flutter workload and fresh
bindings. Baseline execution precedes any product change.

## Mobile virtual mouse button press ownership — investigation (2026-10-27)

Continuation from clean/pushed fa609666d8091ef8134a1ae2aa24b3e2a9c89ff0.
The previous turn is concrete product/runtime progress; the broader goal and
all fifteen installed credential actions remain OPEN. All user parks, including
peer sorting, remain in force.

Relevant source: FloatingLeftRightButton starts a 200-ms timer, sets the global
isSpecialHoldDragActive flag, awaits CursorModel.syncCursorPosition, then calls
InputModel.tapDown. Pointer up/cancel independently sends tapUp before that await
may complete. Disposal cancels only the timer, with no matched release. The two
buttons share one global Boolean; releasing one clears the other's hold state.
InputModel.tapDown/tapUp resolve the mutable current session independently, while
FFI.start on mobile reuses its model objects with a fresh UUID after mobileReset.
The native session_send_mouse sink looks up the UUID provided by the bridge.
These are source findings, not a runtime or privilege-escalation claim.

Intended ownership: each virtual button press retains its pointer, button and
session through preparation, down admission and matching release. Release before
admission prevents down; an admitted down drains an ordered release to the original
session even if its widget retires. Independent buttons retain independent holds;
the pending work and admission must remain bounded. Rendered baseline preparation
adds seventeen cases using the production widgets and InputModel, fresh bindings,
controlled cursor-sync/native-send futures and preference/native-input doubles.
The --virtual-mouse-buttons profile reuses the existing bounded RAM workload;
its additional resource-mapping control is included in both exact count receipts.
No product changes precede the baseline.

Primary references: api.flutter.dev/flutter/gestures/PointerEvent/pointer.html,
api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/Listener/onPointerCancel.html,
api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/State/dispose.html and
api.dart.dev/dart-async/Future-class.html. Pointer identity belongs to one contact;
disposal is terminal and asynchronous ordering/error ownership must be explicit.

baseline. Rust Vec try_reserve/try_reserve_exact documentation confirms the spare
capacity distinction: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html.

### 2026-10-27 — decoded playback PCM freshness investigation

The preceding document correction is complete progress. All fifteen installed
credential actions and the overall goal remain open; wallpaper and every earlier
user park remain parked. This slice concerns the non-Linux portable PCM output
buffer, not the parked Linux PulseAudio stalled-call cancellation work.

Source path: AudioHandler::handle_frame decodes and converts PCM, then calls
AudioBuffer::append_pcm. The compressed mailbox rejects packets older than one
second, but the decoded ring retains only f32 values. Its three-second sample
capacity and twelve-second occupancy adjustment do not expire an old tail after
output stalls. fill_output can subsequently publish those samples unchanged.

The intended owner is the existing output attempt's single PCM mutex. Retained
PCM must carry its own admission age; incoming PCM must not renew older samples.
At callback dequeue, expire blocks older than one second, preserve complete
interleaved frames, keep silence/nonblocking contention behavior, and allow fresh
PCM to recover without recreating the output. Sample and timestamp storage must
both be bounded and reserved fallibly before output activation. This is a local
PCM-queue deadline, not capture-to-speaker, device, or R-F5 acceptance.

Before product changes, one four-case real-clock regression exercises the exact
production ring and output-fill function: stopped callbacks, new PCM after a gap,
a partly consumed stereo block, and producer-lock contention followed by resume.
It retains fresh stereo ordering and post-expiry recovery controls. The focused
audio-buffer export becomes 25 tests; its shared module increases the mailbox
inventory to 49. No extra VM profile or larger resource admission is introduced.
The baseline must execute in the established bounded-RAM audio-buffer VM lane.

Research: the Opus 1.3.1 decoder contract defines ordered stateful decoding,
interleaved stereo, and packet duration. Rust VecDeque documents fallible exact
reservation and FIFO ownership; neither count bounds nor capacity reserve imply
freshness. References: https://www.opus-codec.org/docs/opus_api-1.3.1/group__opus__decoder.html
and https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.VecDeque.html.

implementations in `flutter/lib/common/widgets/overlay.dart` require the previous
and current frames to have a keyboard before adjusting the panel, so the first

only the width of a one-line TextPainter, so a hard line break can hide the actual

the longest complete-grapheme suffix that fits one line, prefixes truncation with

## 2026-10-28 — retained bounded Flutter result-file admission

The preceding goal turn completed the direct-address catalogue deletion and its
component verification. At `ee8575b2`, `parse_result` separately lstats a result
pathname and opens it, checks only the pre-open file size/link count, and allocates
an entire line before enforcing its length. A replaced pathname can therefore
select different bytes, a changed/link-shared file can be accepted, and a long
line can exceed its intended allocation bound before refusal. These are verifier
input defects, not a demonstrated RustDesk privilege escalation or evidence that
any retained product run was forged.

The intended owner is one no-follow, nonblocking opened regular-file descriptor.
Its initial metadata bounds admission and subsequent reads; successful EOF must
match that admitted length and unchanged size/link/modification metadata. Line
allocation is bounded before decoding. The existing test inventory, failure,
skip, completion and source-isolation requirements remain in force. Python 3.11's
[descriptor APIs](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/os.html#os.open) and
[bounded readline](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/io.html#io.IOBase.readline)
support this design. The Dart [JSON reporter contract](https://github.com/dart-lang/test/blob/master/pkgs/test/doc/json_reporter.md)
permits interleaved events and late errors; no new event-order restriction is
part of this file-admission correction.

The regression uses real temporary files inside the isolated guest, with metadata
observation hooks scheduling replacement, growth, truncation, a second hard link

The new slice is Windows absolute pointer normalization. At `fa342297`,
`libs/enigo/src/win/win_impl.rs::mouse_move_to` subtracts the virtual origin and
multiplies by 65535 in i32 before dividing by an unchecked desktop extent.
`src/server/input_service.rs::handle_mouse_simulation_` passes the absolute
MouseEvent coordinates to that method. The source path can overflow or divide
by zero; catch_unwind is not a valid coordinate conversion and optimized builds
can wrap. Even ordinary coordinates target a pixel boundary and can round into
the preceding pixel. This is a concrete correctness finding, not an LPE claim.

Primary research: Microsoft's [MOUSEINPUT contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-mouseinput)
uses normalized 0–65535 coordinates with VIRTUALDESK selecting the whole desktop;
the [virtual screen](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/gdi/the-virtual-screen)
may have a negative origin. The [UI Automation implementation](https://source.dot.net/UIAutomationClientSideProviders/MS/Internal/AutomationProxies/Input.cs.html)
explains the 65536-wide pixel bins and boundary-rounding problem. The intended
conversion uses widened arithmetic, validates extent and membership, and selects
an integer inside the requested pixel's bin. Both axes must admit before SendInput.
This preserves negative coordinates and refuses malformed/stale-outside requests
without native input. Monitor topology/DPI races and actual Windows cursor effects
still require a target-native run.

and adds five direct production-function tests: negative-origin controls, exhaustive
pixel round trips across small/ordinary/large extents, invalid extents, out-of-range
coordinates and extreme origins. A focused Linux VM compiles that module with
optimization and overflow checks disabled. Its 2 GiB guest, 6 GiB bounded RAM scratch
and 4 GiB file ceiling use the shared admission/monitor/joined-cleanup orchestration.

pixels, widens both operands before subtracting, and rejects offsets outside

pixel centre can still select the previous pixel. Both axes are checked before

## 2026-10-28 — viewer recording error/status regression preparation

Source finding: `VideoHandler::handle_frame` (`src/client.rs:1337`) discards
`Recorder::write_frame` errors. The recorder logs and latches failure, but
`Remote::update_record_state` publishes `record_status=true` when it queues the
start control, and has no worker-output failure input. `RecordingModel` consumes
that event directly. The viewer can therefore retain active recording state
after a known output failure. The controlled-side `Recorder::write_message`
wrapper (`libs/scrap/src/common/record.rs:144`) also discards the result; it is
outside this first viewer regression. This is a source-established propagation
gap, not a newly executed reproduction or demonstrated local escalation.

The intended owner is the exact recording attempt within the live viewer
connection and its decoder workers. A known output failure must retire that
attempt, report its outcome and preserve ordinary video decoding. A late result
must not stop a later attempt or a replacement connection. Start/stop/error and
checked finalization need one coherent state transition; blindly enqueueing
`RecordScreen(false)` from a worker would not establish that ownership.
[Rust's File contract](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/struct.File.html) explicitly
distinguishes drop from checked I/O completion;
[Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.Write.html#method.write_all) preserves
write/flush errors for callers. The lower native mux checks remain necessary,
but cannot report their outcome after a caller discards it.

command path, CPace-keyed guest-loopback streams, native VP8 encoder/decoder,

directory invalid; the other case supplies a writable directory. The selected
path/auto-record preferences are controlled test inputs and restored afterward.
The existing test UI observer records status and errors; its first-publication
gate drains before a second frame, so the oracle requires two decoded callbacks.

caught fixture panics. The writable control checks the native WebM header and

## 2026-10-28 — wire-capture acceptance and obsolete capture stage

Previous turn: progress, with the overlapping credential-response catalogue
deleted and its exact comparison/count retained. This slice corrects R-A9's

R-A9 at the initial retained source `28a6ce56` claimed that capture could establish
random indistinguishability and absence of offline guessing. Its required property
remains binding, but that observation cannot establish it. Primary research:
[NIST SP 800-22](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/22/r1/upd1/final) distinguishes
statistical observations from cryptanalysis; the design implication here is that
random-looking packets do not prove cryptographic security.
[Pinned CPace draft 21, security considerations](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-irtf-cfrg-cpace-21.html#section-10)
separates the protocol proof and application responsibilities; the fork's R-S6,
R-A10 and R-V3 conformance/independent-review obligations remain unchanged.
[libsodium secretbox](https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox)
defines authenticated recovery under matching key/nonce, providing a concrete
record-level observation rather than an appearance-based claim.

The R-A9 observer must own the complete correct peer flow, capture readiness and
completion, ordered records, test-session authentication and expected payload
recovery, recipient delivery and terminal cleanup. A separate confined plaintext
control must falsify the observer; missing/truncated/stale/wrong/undecodable
capture or missing transmission/delivery cannot pass. Specified public framing
and pre-key CPace fields are distinguished from protected application records.
Only synthetic credentials are used; operational secrets are excluded. R-A5's
engaged key separation and R-P10 nonce obligations remain distinct. R-A5's
capture wording and acceptance item 3 now agree with this contract. No progress
history, run receipt or implementation status is added to the specification.

## 2026-10-28 — popup anchors in navigator coordinates

The preceding turn made authoritative progress by deleting the unused copied
popup controls. This slice exercises the remaining menu implementation. The
R-S11b/c installed-native matrix and all fifteen credential actions remain OPEN;
the current user-directed UI work does not resume parked credential, parent-build,

The live peer-card, connection-page and desktop file-manager callers construct
`RelativeRect.fromLTRB(x, y, x, y)` from global pointer coordinates. Its right
and bottom arguments are distances from the container edges, not another copy
of the pointer. The copied menu's RTL layout therefore mirrors the anchor; it
also receives the wrong coordinate system under offset/scaled navigators.
Flutter's primary contracts distinguish these spaces:
https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/rendering/RelativeRect-class.html ,
https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/rendering/RelativeRect/RelativeRect.fromSize.html ,
https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/rendering/RenderBox/globalToLocal.html .

The shared helper derives the selected navigator's overlay, converts the global
point with `globalToLocal`, then forms a zero-size anchor with `fromSize` and
that overlay's actual size. Pointer callbacks retain `Offset` values; conversion
occurs when opening the menu. The peer caller retains its invocation's point,
awaits its menu items and requires mounting before deriving the overlay. The
breadcrumb converts its local bottom edge as a point, including its transform.
All five custom-popup calls and the file-manager standard upload popup adopt
the helper. The connection-page call is split across lines and was included by
whitespace-aware reference review; its final adoption follows the component run
without changing any executed helper/menu/test byte.

Source trace: `ConnectPasswordDialog` is the sole production `PasswordWidget`
caller. `DialogTextField` already gives its password field framework autofocus,
but `PasswordWidget.initState` schedules an unconditional second request after
50 ms. A user-selected control can therefore lose focus after navigation.
The separate Android repeat-focus option has no caller. The intended model is
one framework-owned initial focus request, followed by user-directed focus;
the widget retains and disposes its own node. Flutter 3.24.5's
[EditableText implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flutter/flutter/3.24.5/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/editable_text.dart)
uses one mounted post-frame autofocus request, and the
[Focus contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flutter/flutter/3.24.5/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/focus_scope.dart)
selects initial focus only when its scope lacks one. No timer override is required.
